# Membrum audit — 2026-11-23

- **Date:** 2026-11-23
- **Plugin version:** 0.12.5 (`plugins/membrum/version.json`)
- **Commit:** `4a14376d`

## 1. Executive summary

This audit covers the Membrum drum synthesizer at the commit above: the plugin code under `plugins/membrum/` (processor, controller, voice pool, per-voice DSP, state codec, presets, editor, tests, documentation) and the KrateDSP headers it consumes. `tools/membrum-fit` is out of scope except where it duplicates the plugin's parameter mapping. Candidate findings came from three sources: a static read of the code along 23 dimensions; a measurement lane of 8 steps (repo lints, Release build, the sharded test gate, pluginval at strictness 5, audio probes through the real processor, kit-quality probes over the 20 factory kits, clang-tidy, the portability check); and a literature check of 136 physical claims made by the code, its comments and the manual. Each candidate then went to three independent skeptics, each told to refute it from a different angle: whether the code really does what the finding says, whether the behaviour is intended or guarded elsewhere, and whether it has the claimed consequence (for physics findings: the code, the literature, and intent plus audibility). A finding that no skeptic refuted is CONFIRMED, one refutation makes it PLAUSIBLE, and two or more make it REFUTED. A completeness critic then reviewed the whole result, commissioned follow-up finders for the gaps it saw, and sent doubtful refutations to a tie-break. 259 findings survive: 6 critical, 48 high, 71 medium and 134 low. The existing gates see none of them: at this commit the build has no warnings, the 642-case test gate is green, pluginval passes, clang-tidy reports 0 warnings and the portability check is clear. The only red item in the lane is the `uidesc-inventory --check` lint (MB-195).

**Headline defects.** The 6 critical and 48 high findings fall into the eleven groups below. Findings from different dimensions that describe one root cause keep their own ids and are listed together. Every finding named here is CONFIRMED unless marked otherwise.

1. **Preset loads race the audio thread.** A kit or pad preset loaded from the browser, and a host `setState`, rewrite the voice pool, the allocator, the pad configs and the coupling engine on the message thread while `process()` runs. A probe reproduces the crash.
   Critical: MB-001.
2. **Saving a preset from the editor changes the sound.** The controller builds the saved blob from its parameters, and two sound fields have no parameter. Every pad's `noiseLayerGain` is saved as 0 and loads back as 0.1, and the body-damping "auto" sentinel is saved as an explicit 0.5 override. After a save and reload of the default kit the snare wire is 36 dB down and untouched pads decay 5-16x shorter. The Ruinae audit's R-202 / R-203 fix unified the browser load path but left the save providers, and the second apply of every load, in place (MB-152). No test compares a controller save with the processor's own state (MB-139).
   Critical: MB-087, MB-162. High: MB-030, MB-043, MB-139, MB-152, MB-166.
3. **Pitch envelope, tension glide and Material Morph barely move the sounding modes.** On the block renderers that every host uses, the modal bank's coefficient smoothing advances once per block, so the bank moves only about 1 % of the way to a new target per block (a time constant of 2 ms times the block size in samples). The 808-style pitch sweep does not happen at normal buffer sizes, and the sound depends on the buffer size. The earlier H-3 fix is not effective. With Material Morph on, the morph refresh also overwrites the pitch-envelope and tension scaling (MB-028). The claim that the pitch envelope retunes the String waveguide is contradicted (MB-210). The SC-009 pitch-glide test passes because it runs only the per-sample renderer, which no host uses (MB-141).
   Critical: MB-008, MB-026. High: MB-028, MB-141, MB-151, MB-159, MB-210, MB-237.
4. **Voices that never retire, and voices the pool drops or cuts.**
   - A Feedback-exciter voice never retires: the per-sample path never flushes silent modes, so the voice slot and its CPU are lost for good. Critical: MB-027. High: MB-009, MB-018, MB-038.
   - Retirement reads the shared modal bank's mode count, which the String body never updates. A String voice is cut after 256 host blocks while still ringing, or never retires after a body swap or kit switch. High: MB-106, MB-160.
   - Allocator slots leak when a voice finishes before its MIDI note-off; with the Quietest policy polyphony collapses to one voice. High: MB-050, MB-105.
   - Quietest stealing drops simultaneous hits, because a voice triggered earlier in the same block still has level 0. High: MB-049.
   - Auto-release tests a per-host-block peak, so voice length depends on the buffer size; at blocks of 1-16 samples hits are killed at their onset. High: MB-052.
5. **Note timing ignores `sampleOffset`.** Every hit starts at the block start, so timing and flams depend on the host buffer size. No test checks note timing or block-size invariance (MB-141, also in group 3).
   High: MB-051.
6. **Allocation and long work on the audio thread at note-on.** An exciter or body type swap at note-on allocates and frees heap memory (30 % of default-kit hits), and an FMImpulse swap runs FFT wavetable generation (about 190 us). The strike-normalisation probe renders 30 ms of scalar modal bank for almost every hit, so one note-on costs up to 1.4-3.5 ms. The tests meant to catch this cannot: the allocation count is read while its scope is still open and is always 0 (MB-136), and the SC-007 zero-allocation tests force every pad to Impulse + Membrane (MB-137).
   High: MB-002, MB-003, MB-020, MB-136, MB-137.
7. **Cross-pad coupling does not do what its controls and the manual describe.** Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance do nothing, because the coupling matrix they recompute is never read by the audio path (MB-004, MB-167). The engine rings resonators tuned to the struck voice's own partials, not to the unstruck pads, so "the kick makes the snare wires buzz" does not exist (MB-232, MB-258). Global Coupling goes silent after a sample-rate change, an offline bounce or a project reload, because `setupProcessing` re-prepares the engine and leaves its amount at 0 (MB-067).
   High: MB-004, MB-067, MB-167, MB-232, MB-258.
8. **Decay is a dead knob on almost every factory pad.** When both body-damping overrides are set, the per-pad Decay knob, its global proxy and the decay macros do not change a modal body's ring time, and Material loses its damping role. The factory kits store explicit overrides on almost every pad (MB-109 counts 429 of 459). The "auto" state has no parameter representation: the damping knobs show 50 % for a value that is never applied, and the first touch shortens the decay several-fold (MB-074).
   High: MB-029, MB-074, MB-109 (PLAUSIBLE).
9. **Exciter and filter level defects.**
   - Feedback exciter: the unnormalised modal bank is driven into its soft-clip rail, giving a square wave pinned at ±0.707 x velocity for 1-3 s on every body, whatever the Feedback Amount. High: MB-017.
   - Friction exciter: the velocity response is inverted. Soft hits drive the body into the hard-clip rail while a full-velocity hit sits at the -6 dBFS budget. High: MB-019.
   - FMImpulse exciter: strike normalisation is measured at velocity 1.0 only, so on Bell bodies a velocity-100 hit lands up to 11.3 dB over the body budget and reaches the limiter. High: MB-260.
   - Tone-shaper filter: cutoff and filter type glide in from the voice slot's previous note, so the attack of a filtered pad depends on slot history. A hat at LP 317 Hz plays 46 dB louder on a fresh slot than on a warm one. High: MB-042, MB-265.
10. **Selected-pad proxies, macros and editor controls.**
    - The Simple-view macro knobs and the Coupling Amount knob always edit pad 1, whichever pad is selected. High: MB-071.
    - Host automation recorded on a selected-pad proxy replays onto whichever pad is selected at playback. High: MB-072, MB-163.
    - Macro deltas never reach the controller: knobs show pre-macro values, the next direct edit wipes the delta, and controller-side saves drop it. High: MB-073.
    - Macros do not return to the original sound at neutral. Punch below neutral collapses an un-enveloped pad's pitch to 20 Hz, and Brightness 0.5 -> 1 -> 0.5 leaves the filter cutoff at 0.8 instead of 1.0. High: MB-081, MB-173.
    - The polyphony slider has no control listener, so dragging it never changes Max Polyphony. High: MB-096.
    - XY morph pad edits on the Y axis (Morph End) never update the controller's parameter, so kit and pad preset saves lose them. High: MB-097.
11. **String waveguide tuning.** The String body reads its loop delay with linear interpolation. The code comment's claim that this gives an exact fractional delay and a flat loop gain is contradicted by the literature.
    High: MB-208.

Several of these fixes touch code that other plugins share: `ModalResonatorBank` (Innexus, Seraphis), `WaveguideString` and `SympatheticResonance` (Innexus), and `XYMorphPad` (Disrumpo and others). The findings say where a Membrum-local fix leaves the other plugins' output unchanged.

Across all severities the largest categories are physical-model deviations (59 in the three `physics-*` categories, 5 of them high), test gaps (20, 4 of them high), factory-kit sameness (16) and documentation that describes an older engine (`spec-conformance`, 12).

**Relation to prior audits.** `plugins/membrum/docs/correctness-audit.md` (Finding 1-23), `plugins/membrum/AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md` (H-n / M-n / L-n / N-1) and the Ruinae audit's Membrum items (R-202, R-203 in `specs/ruinae-audit/report.md`) are history and are left unchanged. This audit re-checked them against today's code and reports whatever is still present or only partly fixed under its own ids, MB-nnn, which never reuse a prior id; section 7 maps prior ids to MB ids.

**Sections of this report**

- **2 Statistics**: counts per pipeline stage, verdict, severity and category.
- **3 Measurement lane**: the 8 steps with their results and log paths, and every probe measurement (the baseline for re-measuring after the fixes).
- **4 Kit quality**: the 20 factory kits (flagged pads, near-duplicate pairs, cross-kit spread, velocity response) and the parameter-audibility table.
- **5 Physical-model review**: all 136 claims with verdict, correct form and sources, confirmed ones included.
- **6 Findings**: every surviving finding, critical to low, CONFIRMED before PLAUSIBLE, with evidence, suggested fix and verifier notes.
- **7 Prior-audit status**: prior finding ids that are still present, still open or partly fixed, with the MB id that tracks each.
- **8 Inventory cross-reference**: the inventory tables and their mismatch lists.
- **Appendix A** Refuted findings, **Appendix B** Unverified findings, **Appendix C** Critic gaps.

The fix plan is `fix-plan.md`, next to this report.

### lints

> Ran all 16 repo lint scripts plus check-au-plist.js membrum and uidesc-inventory.js --check, one after another, each to its own log under f:/tmp/membrum-audit/. Every lint exited 0 and printed a clean result (lint-odr: "OK — 1005 definitions scanned, no cross-file name collisions."; lint-layers: "OK — no layer-dependency violations in 5-layer DSP tree."; lint-plugin-editor-baseline: "OK - 9 plugins carry the update check and the version label"; lint-finite-bitmask: "clean"; check-au-plist: "OK   membrum: AUv2 plist version matches version.json and kAUcomponentVersion"). The other lints each print one line and exit 0, and I did not read those lines individually. The exception is uidesc-inventory --check, which exited 1 with "UIDESC DEFECTS {"overlap":160}". All 160 overlaps are a FieldsetContainer against its own contained children (SelectedPadSimple, SelectedPadAdvanced and EditorDefault templates). No non-FieldsetContainer overlap appears, and there are no out-of-bounds, lost-binding or stacked-pair defects. plugins/membrum/tests has no uidesc_overlaps_allowed.json, so the tool's --allow mechanism, which Disrumpo uses, is not set up for Membrum. I did not check whether CI runs this check for Membrum. Individual logs are f:/tmp/membrum-audit/lint-lint-&lt;name&gt;.log, lint-au-plist.log and lint-uidesc-inventory.log.

**Verdict:** ran = yes, ok = **false** (one red check: `uidesc-inventory.js --check`).
**Log:** `f:/tmp/membrum-audit/lint-uidesc-inventory.log` (per-lint logs `f:/tmp/membrum-audit/lint-lint-<name>.log`, `lint-au-plist.log`).

| Kind | File | Line | Text |
|---|---|---|---|
| lint | `plugins/membrum/resources/editor.uidesc` | - | uidesc-inventory.js --check exit 1: UIDESC DEFECTS {"overlap":160}. Every overlap is a FieldsetContainer reported against its own children, e.g. "overlap [SelectedPadSimple]: FieldsetContainer Macros at 4,28,388,104 / ArcKnob MacroTightness at 8,52,56,56"; "overlap [SelectedPadAdvanced]: FieldsetContainer Source at 4,166,388,96 / COptionMenu BodyModel at 216,182,100,20". No allow file exists (plugins/membrum/tests/uidesc_overlaps_allowed.json is absent), so the check cannot pass as it stands. |

### probes

> I wrote a probe TU with 39 hidden [.][audit-probe] cases that renders through the real Processor, VoicePool, DrumVoice and Controller. I built it three times, capped to 2 nodes, and each build had zero warnings. Each run was sharded with run-gate --share 4 and was GATE GREEN in about 4.4 s wall clock. The runs produced 580 PROBE lines.
>
> All three extra-focus leads were measured.
> (1) Save paths diverge: CONFIRMED (bad). A kit-preset save followed by a reload loses noiseLayerGain on every pad: slot 57 goes from 1.0/6.2/3.5 to 0.1 on 32/32 pads. On the default kit the reload also turns the B1/B3 sentinel -1 into an explicit 0.5 (22 pads B1, 16 pads B3).
> - Default-kit snare 38: energy above 3 kHz drops from -7.84 to -42.35 dB and peak from -9.52 to -13.89 dBFS.
> - Default-kit kick: decay60 drops from 0.97 to 0.19 s.
> - Tom 41: 1.54 to 0.23 s.
> - Closed hat: 0.32 to 0.02 s.
> - Factory kits carry explicit damping, so only slot 57 is lost there. Acoustic Studio Kit snare loses 35.5 dB of wire.
> - The pad-preset save has the same defect: snare 6.2 becomes 0.1, and tom B1 -1 becomes 0.5, giving decay 1.54 to 0.23 s.
>
> (2) Double apply: each kit-browser load sends 2119 begin/perform/endEdit triples (2112 per-pad, 7 global), and the next block makes 162 recomputeCouplingMatrix calls.
> - For in-range factory kits the two routes agree.
> - Out-of-range slots 0-33 diverge: the message path keeps decay 1.7 and material -0.3, while the edit path clamps them to 1.0 and 0.0.
> - A stale edit batch arriving after a second kit message produces a hybrid kit for one block: snare max diff 0.477. It resolves once the second kit's edits arrive.
>
> (3) Field maps: no drift. 56 offsets map one-to-one, and the pad-preset round trip skips only enabled and pan, as FR-061 requires. applyPadSnapshot leaves slots 0-27 and 30-33 unclamped, and NaN/Inf in those slots is stored verbatim and written back by getState.
>
> Other bad results:
> - Note events ignore sampleOffset: onset lands at the block start, and output differs by up to -8.8 dBFS between block sizes.
> - The pitch envelope refreshes once per block: a 20 ms 160->50 Hz linear sweep is wrong by 233 cents at bs 64 and 2012 cents at bs 1024.
> - Hi-hat choke does nothing on a fresh instance, because the choke table is 0,0 until a setState.
> - A Feedback-exciter voice never retires after its output is digitally silent (a CPU leak).
> - The Brightness macro 0.5->1->0.5 leaves the cutoff at 0.8 instead of 1.0.
> - Projects saved by released v0.9.x (blob v1) and v0.10.x (v2) are rejected (git tags).
>
> Suspicious:
> - A note-off shortens hits by 10-25x: kick 0.97 to 0.10 s, tom 1.54 to 0.06 s.
> - Steal and retrigger fades are 2.3-2.6x the pre-steal slope.
> - Neutral modeStretch 1.0 still stretches Plate/Shell/Bell partials by up to +59 cents at partial 8.
> - The String body is not normalised to -6 dBFS: its peak is -0.02 dBFS.
> - Mid-note automation changes only pan; 62 of 63 per-pad parameters latch at note-on.
> - The processor-level kick pitch depends on sample rate, while the DrumVoice alone is sample-rate invariant.
> - Friction and modeInject do not sustain, contrary to CLAUDE.md.
> - Coupling at maximum clears the silence flag on every block.
> - Macros override the user's direct edits on return to 0.5.
>
> OK: velocity curves, the -1 dBTP limiter and master gain (exact -24/-6/+12 dB), pan law, multi-bus (aux is a pre-master send; a null aux buffer does not crash), coupling runaway, proxy == per-pad (0 of 62 differ), getState idempotence for all 20 factory kits, malformed-blob rejection, no modes at or above Nyquist, and no NaN anywhere.
>
> Cleanup: CMakeLists.txt reverted, plugins/membrum/tests/audit/ deleted, and git status --porcelain plugins/membrum is empty. The build dir still holds a membrum_tests.exe linked with the probe cases until the next build.

**Verdict:** ran = yes, tree clean = yes; 46 measurements: **15 bad**, **15 suspicious**, 16 ok.

### quality

> I wrote a temporary probe file with 93 hidden [.][audit-probe] cases (one per factory kit, one cross-kit case, one per parameter, plus a choke-table check). Each case drives a real Membrum::Processor at 48 kHz with block size 256 and 16 output buses. The build was clean with zero warnings (-m:2). The sharded run was green: 93 cases, 10.7 s wall, 7 workers, --share 4. I merged the PROBE lines and CSV parts, copied them to specs/membrum-audit/probes/, then reverted CMakeLists.txt and deleted tests/audit/. git status --porcelain plugins/membrum is empty. The membrum_tests.exe in build/ still contains the probe cases until its next rebuild.
>
> KITS (640 pad rows, 517 enabled): no pad is silent, no pad produces NaN, and no pad has a DC offset. In 21 pads of 10 kits a single velocity-100 hit already peaks at the bus limiter ceiling (-7.00 dBFS = master -6 dB minus 1 dBTP). These are mostly Unnatural-kit pads with the Friction, Feedback, FM or Bell exciters, plus Latin Perc 46, LinnDrum 40 and World Metal 55. Orchestral notes 49 and 54 ring past 4 s with no modeInject, Friction or Feedback to explain it. A note-off at 100 ms cuts 180 of the 185 pads that decay for 0.5 s or more to under half their natural decay (median ratio 0.21). For example, Orchestral 54 drops from >4 s to 0.14 s. The cause is VoicePool::noteOff, which gates the amp envelope and damps the bank. The voice_pool.h comment still says note-off is bookkeeping only.
>
> SAMENESS: 19 near-duplicate pairs across 9 kits, all within one PadCategory. Several are bit-identical pads (bandDist 0.00): Tabla 53/66 and 36/42, and Experimental FX 42/44. Hand Drums and Latin Perc share identical notes 36 and 38. Across kits, notes 36/38/42/45/49 differ by 16.5-23.2 dB mean bandDist. No two kits are closer than 6.7 dB (Rock Big Room and Vintage Wood; 808 and 909). By the bands-plus-centroid-plus-decay metric, the kits are distinct from each other. Velocity: no pad meets the flat-response flag, but several get darker when hit harder, which is the opposite of the expected direction (centroid ratio hi/lo 0.25-0.9 on 10 of 60).
>
> PARAMETERS (71): 65 ok, 4 suspicious, 2 bad. Global Snare Buzz (271) and Tom Resonance (272) are bit-identical in their coupling context: CouplingMatrix::effectiveGain_ is computed but never read by the audio path. Per-pad couplingAmount (36) only gates on > 0 and is otherwise inaudible. couplingDelay (273) is inaudible, and global coupling at 1.0 changes level by 0.0 dB. modeInject (23) and fmRatio (32) have a 12.1-12.2 dB jump between adjacent steps on the hat. Every per-pad parameter except pan applies only at the next note-on.
>
> Side measurements:
> - The default snare's decay knob is bit-identical (the B1/B3 overrides in default_kit.h:130-131), and its material and morph are near-dead.
> - On a fresh instance the choke table is 0,0,0 for notes 42/44/46 while the configs say 1,1,1. DefaultKit::apply never syncs chokeGroups_; a getState/setState round trip fixes it.
> - PadCategory classifies only 2 of 517 enabled pads as Snare. Note 38/40 pads come out 9 Kick, 16 Perc, 4 Tom, 1 Snare, because the Snare rule needs the NoiseBurst exciter.
> - The filter-envelope amount moves level by at most 0.2 dB and centroid by at most 1 % even with cutoff at 0.4.
>
> I did not probe the three extra-focus state leads in this lane: it is the kit-quality and audibility lane, and the state-codec probes are another finder's job.

**Verdict:** ran = yes, tree clean = yes; 49 measurements: **4 bad**, **26 suspicious**, 19 ok.

## 4. Kit quality

Source: the `quality` step of the measurement lane (section 3). All numbers below come from
[`probes/quality-results.txt`](probes/quality-results.txt) and the three CSV files it wrote; the probe source is
[`probes/audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt`](probes/audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt).

**Full per-row data** (the tables below are summaries):

| File | Rows | Content |
|---|---|---|
| [`probes/kit-pads.csv`](probes/kit-pads.csv) | 640 (20 kits x 32 pads) | every pad of every kit: exciter, body, PadCategory, peak, rms500, dc, nonFinite, decay, decay with note-off at 100 ms, centroid, limiter margin, master dB, noiseLayerGain, flags, modeInject, the 24 band levels |
| [`probes/kit-pairs.csv`](probes/kit-pairs.csv) | every within-kit pair of sounding enabled pads | bandDist, centroid ratio, decay ratio, near-duplicate flag, same-category flag |
| [`probes/param-audibility.csv`](probes/param-audibility.csv) | 213 (71 parameters x 3 base pads) | per-step rms500 / centroid / decay, the max changes, bit-identity, the max adjacent-step jump, live-while-ringing, verdict |

The same directory also holds the inputs of later verification probes (limiter, note-off, retune, velocity-centroid, filter-glide:
`audit_limiter_probe.cpp.txt`, `limiter-*.csv`, `limiter-probe-summary.txt`, `audit_noteoff_probe.cpp.txt`, `noteoff-probe.csv`,
`audit_retune_probe.cpp.txt`, `retune-probe-results.txt`, `audit_velocity_centroid_probes.cpp.txt`, `velocity-centroid-results.txt`,
`audit_filter_glide_probe.cpp.txt`, `filter-glide.csv`, `factory-filter-pads.csv`, `svf-glide-times.txt`). They are not part of
this section's baseline; the findings that use them cite them directly.

### 4.1 Probe definitions

Harness: a real `Membrum::Processor`, 48 kHz, block size 256, 16 stereo output buses wired (aux active only for the output-bus
probe). Each kit is loaded from `resources/presets/Kit Presets/<Category>/<name>.vstpreset` (component chunk ->
`Processor::setState`). Between hits the probe runs `setActive(false)` / `setState(kit)` / `setActive(true)`, so every hit starts
from silence with a reset bus limiter. Note-on velocity is 100/127 unless stated. A render stops early once no voice is active and
16 blocks are below 1e-8. Parameter sweeps use a fresh Processor with the default kit per render; the context and the probed value
are sent through `IParameterChanges` in the note-on block.

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| mono | (L + R) / 2; the pan probe uses L |
| peak dBFS | max \|L\|, \|R\| over the render |
| rms500 dBFS | RMS of mono over the first 500 ms |
| dc | mean of mono over the whole render; flagged when \|dc\| > 1e-3 (-60 dBFS) |
| nonFinite | count of non-finite samples in L and R |
| decay | 10 ms RMS frames; the time after which the envelope stays 60 dB under its maximum; ">cap" when still above at the end (cap 4 s in the kit table, 3 s in parameter sweeps) |
| centroid Hz | magnitude-weighted spectral centroid of the first 200 ms (Hann 4096, hop 1024, zero-padded edge frames, DC skipped) |
| bands | 24 log-spaced bands, 40 Hz to 16 kHz, power averaged over the first 1 s (Hann 8192, hop 2048), in dB normalised to the loudest band, floored at -80 dB |
| bandDist(a, b) | RMS over the 24 bands of (a - b), in dB. This is the distance used for sameness, cross-kit spread and nearest kit |
| Kit flags | silent = enabled and peak < -60 dBFS; limiter = peak - (kit master dB - 1) >= -0.5 dB (one hit already reaches the -1 dBTP bus limiter; the factory kits run at master -6 dB, so the ceiling is -7 dBFS); dc; nan; long ring = decay > 4 s, "unexplained" when the pad has no modeInject > 0, Friction or Feedback exciter |
| Near-duplicate pair | bandDist < 3 dB AND centroid ratio <= 1.10 AND decay ratio <= 1.20 (silent pads excluded); "same category" = both pads in the same `PadCategory` |
| Cross-kit spread (per note) | the same note in all 20 kits: mean pairwise bandDist (flag < 3 dB); centroid sd = standard deviation of log2(centroid), in octaves; decay sd = exp(standard deviation of ln(decay)), a ratio |
| Nearest kit | for each kit, the other kit with the lowest mean bandDist over notes 36/38/42/45/49 present in both (flag < 3 dB) |
| Velocity response | notes 36/38/42 of every kit, vel 40/127 vs 127/127, 1 s render; rms500 diff, peak diff, centroid ratio hi/lo; flagged flat when rms500 diff < 6 dB AND centroid change < 5 % |
| Parameter sweep | steps 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 (discrete parameters: every step), base pads 36 / 38 / 42. Per base pad: level = max - min rms500 dB (floor -100), centroid % = max/min - 1, decay % = max/min - 1 (non-silent steps), bandDist = max pairwise, bit-identical over the whole range. **bad** = bit-identical on all 3 base pads; **suspicious** = every metric < 1 dB / 5 % / 5 % / 1 dB on all 3, or (continuous parameters only) an adjacent-step rms500 jump > 12 dB between two non-silent steps. live = changing the value (to 0 and to 1) at 299 ms while tom 41 rings, in the same context, alters the output after the change |

### 4.2 The 20 factory kits

Overall: 640 pad rows, **459 enabled** (the step summary and its PadCategory probe say "517 enabled"; `kit-pads.csv` has 459 rows
with `enabled = 1` and the PadCategory counts 76 + 2 + 83 + 75 + 223 also sum to 459, so 517 is a typo in the step summary).

a single velocity-100 hit, 2 ring past 4 s unexplained (Orchestral 49, 54) and 2 ring past 4 s by the intended Friction sustain
(Modular West Coast 37, Experimental FX 39; the latter is also on the limiter).

Notes on the kit table:

- **Limiter pads.** The 21 limiter pads peak at -7.00 to -7.16 dBFS, a margin of -0.00 to -0.16 dB to the -7 dBFS bus ceiling.
  The step's reading is that the per-voice strike normalisation to `kBodyHeadroom` does not bound the sustaining exciters
  (Friction, Feedback) or the FM / Bell bodies, so the -1 dBTP bus limiter (`processor.cpp:717`) shapes single hits on these pads.
- **Note-off truncation.** Of the 185 enabled pads whose natural decay is >= 0.5 s, a note-off 100 ms after the note-on cuts 180
  to under half of that decay (median ratio 0.21). Examples: Acoustic Studio tom 41 1.37 s -> 0.17 s, Orchestral 54 > 4 s -> 0.14 s.
  Per-pad values are in the `decayS` and `decayNoteOff100msS` columns of `kit-pads.csv`.
- **Identical pads.** bandDist 0.00 within a kit: Tabla 36/42 and 53/66, Experimental FX 42/44. Most other near-duplicates are hat
  42 vs pedal hat 44 (808, 909, Jazz Brushes, LinnDrum, Vintage Wood: bandDist 0.28-1.60).
- **Hand Drums vs Latin Perc.** The step says notes 36 and 38 "render identically in the two Percussive kits". The raw rows say
  something slightly different. Hand Drums **42** and Latin Perc **36** are the same pad: Impulse/Membrane, peak -18.93, rms500
  -38.39, decay 0.24 s, centroid 1258.0 Hz in `kit-pads.csv`, and 30.11 / 26.05 / x0.533 in the velocity probe. Hand Drums 38 and
  Latin Perc 38 are near-identical: centroid 741.5 Hz and decay 0.31 s in both, peak -18.40 vs -18.17, same velocity row. Hand
  Drums 36 is a different pad (velocity 16.93 / 17.79 / x1.029).
- **Inverted velocity brightness.** The step reports 10 of 60 notes getting darker when hit harder. The velocity rows in
  `quality-results.txt` have **12** of 60 with a centroid ratio below 1. These are the bold entries above: Acoustic Studio 36 and
  38, Orchestral 38, Rock 38, Vintage Wood 38, 909 38, Hand Drums 38 and 42, Latin Perc 36 and 38, Drone 36, Ghost Bones 38.
  The step's own list ("velocity:inverted brightness" in section 3) names all 12, so the count of 10 is the error, not the list.
- **Weak velocity range, no flat flag.** Four pads move less than 6 dB in rms500 between velocity 40 and 127, but their timbre
  changes, so none trips the flat flag: ExpFX 36 (-0.63 dB, quieter when hit harder, centroid x6.07), LinnDrum 36 (4.88), Chaos 36
  (5.31) and World Metal 36 (5.91, peak diff 0.00 dB, so both velocities reach the same peak).

The same note in all 20 factory kits (20 sounding for each note), velocity 100/127, 4 s. Verdict ok when the mean pairwise
bandDist is >= 3 dB.

| Note | Mean pairwise bandDist dB | Centroid sd (octaves) | Decay sd (x ratio) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 36 | 16.53 | 1.27 | 2.13 | ok |
| 38 | 22.35 | 1.46 | 2.76 | ok |
| 42 | 23.24 | 1.85 | 2.50 | ok |
| 45 | 19.55 | 1.27 | 2.21 | ok |
| 49 | 22.52 | 1.62 | 2.50 | ok |

No kit pair is under the 3 dB nearest-kit flag. The closest pairs are Rock Big Room / Vintage Wood (6.70 dB) and 808 / 909
(6.73 dB). By this bands + centroid + decay metric the 20 kits are distinct from each other. The sameness problems are within
kits (section 4.2), not between them.

Other sweep facts:

- **Pan (offset 64).** The pan probe's 123 dB "jump" was a metric artefact: the features are measured on L, which goes silent at
  hard right. The step corrected the verdict to ok.
- **Output bus.** ok: the main bus is unchanged by design, and aux routing is correct on 48 of 48.
- **Parameters that act on a ringing voice.** Only pan (64), masterGain, globalCoupling and couplingDelay. Every other per-pad
  offset (62 of them) takes effect at the next note-on, because `VoicePool::applyPadConfigToSlot` runs only at note-on
  (`voice_pool.cpp:232`).
- **PadCategory.** Over the 459 enabled factory pads the split is Kick 76 / Snare 2 / Tom 83 / HatCymbal 75 / Perc 223. Notes 38 and
  40 (the snare slots) classify as Kick 9, Perc 16, Tom 4, Snare 1. The Snare rule (`pad_category.h:41-43`) requires the NoiseBurst
  exciter, and the redesigned snares use Impulse plus the noise layer.

## 5. Physical-model review

Method: every physical claim the code makes (in comments, constants, mapping laws, tests and the manual) was checked against textbooks, peer-reviewed papers and, where a number was at stake, a numerical probe; confirmed claims are listed as well, so nobody has to re-check them.

### 5.1 Claims 1-46

Columns: **Verdict** is confirmed / nuanced / oversimplified / unsupported / contradicted. **Evidence** is the quality of the evidence behind the verdict. **Correct form** is what the literature gives, in one line. **MB-id** is the audit finding the claim became ("-" when it did not; a related finding filed from a later claim is named in brackets). Full source lists follow in "Sources for claims 1-46".

Tally: 46 claims; 6 confirmed, 9 nuanced, 7 oversimplified, 5 unsupported, 19 contradicted. 24 became findings (MB-id above).

#### Sources for claims 1-46

**Claim 1. Membrane mode ratios and (m,n) labels are the Bessel-zero ratios j_mn/j_01 of an ideal circular membrane** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:30-60, 108-115 (used at plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:100-109)`)

- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, March 1992. *paper*, <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>. Establishes: Eq. (1): f_mn = j_mn/(2 pi a) sqrt(T/sigma), where j_mn is the nth root of J_m. Fig. 2 tabulates the relative frequencies of the first 14 ideal-membrane modes: (0,1) 1.000, (1,1) 1.594, (2,1) 2.136, (0,2) 2.296, (3,1) 2.653, (1,2) 2.916, (4,1) 3.156, (2,2) 3.501, (0,3) 3.600, (5,1) 3.652, (3,2) 4.060, (6,1) 4.154.
- N. H. Fletcher, T. D. Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., Springer 1998, ch. 3 (membranes) and ch. 18 (drums). *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: Ideal circular membrane modes are J_m(k_mn r) cos(m theta), with frequencies set by the Bessel zeros (the source of Rossing's Fig. 2).

**Claim 2. Strike-position weighting is |J_m(j_mn r0/a)|, the radial mode shape at the strike point, with r0/a = 0.9*strikePos** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:111-118 (cull at dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:790-797, gain at 835)`)

- S. Bilbao, 'Modal Synthesis', CCRMA online book section, 2006. *textbook*, <https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~bilbao/booktop/node14.html>. Establishes: Initial conditions or excitation are expanded onto the (usually orthogonal) set of modal functions through inner products, which give the weights. The output is the modal functions projected onto an observation state, in the simplest case a delta at a chosen location.
- J. Woodhouse, Euphonics, '3.6 Tuned drums'. *docs*, <https://euphonics.org/3-6-tuned-drums/>. Establishes: Mode shapes vary as cos n theta or sin n theta times J_n. A centre strike excites the untuned axisymmetric modes, and the tuned modes all have a nodal line through the centre, so players do not strike a kettledrum near the centre.
- N. H. Fletcher, T. D. Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., Springer 1998. *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: The response of a struck membrane is a normal-mode superposition. Each mode's amplitude is set by the mode shape at the excitation point divided by its modal mass (norm).

**Claim 3. evaluateBesselJ (20-term power series in float) stays under 1 % error for strike arguments up to j_mn*0.9 ~ 17.6** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:117-160 (comment 123-127, kMaxTerms = 20 at 152); called at plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:117`)

- Measurement: membrane_probe.js (float emulation of evaluateBesselJ vs a 200-term double series of J_m). *docs*, no URL. Establishes: Worst |J| error 0.357 at strikePos 1.0 (mode 46, m=1, x=17.654: 0.533 vs 0.176). 4 modes above 0.01 and 1 mode above 0.1. The error first exceeds 0.01 at strikePos 0.91. The 20-term double series also gives 0.529, so the error is truncation.
- M. Abramowitz, I. Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, 1964, eq. 9.1.10 (ascending series for J_m) and section 9.12 (recurrence / computation). *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: The ascending series converges for all x, but needs terms well past k ~ x/2. Backward recurrence is the standard stable method for large x.

**Claim 4. Air loading tunes the (m,1) modes to Rossing's timpani series 1 : 1.50 : 2.00 : 2.44 : 2.90 and leaves all other modes at pure Bessel** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:62-105 (applied at plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:100-109)`)

- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992. *paper*, <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>. Establishes: (1,1):(2,1):(3,1) are nearly 1:1.5:2, and (4,1), (5,1) are typically 2.44 and 2.90 times (1,1) (ref. 7, Rossing & Kvistad 1976). The modes with one to five nodal diameters give partials near 2:3:4:5:6. Air loading lowers the low-frequency modes. Kettle air stiffness raises the axisymmetric modes, especially (0,1). Reducing the kettle volume raises (0,1), (0,2), (0,3) and lowers (1,1)-(4,1).
- The Well-Tempered Timpani, ch. 3 'Air loading' (summarising Rossing et al. 1976-2000). *docs*, <https://wtt.pauken.org/chapter-3/air-loading-2>. Establishes: Air loading considerably decreases the frequency of the lower modes, while the loading is small for higher modes. Kettle air stiffness raises the concentric (0,n) modes somewhat.
- J. Woodhouse, Euphonics, '3.6 Tuned drums'. *docs*, <https://euphonics.org/3-6-tuned-drums/>. Establishes: Added air mass reduces all natural frequencies, differently for each mode, and does not by itself create harmonic relations. The kettle adjusts it so that a few modes fall near harmonic ratios.

**Claim 5. Air Loading is described as a low-mode frequency depression that makes the drum deeper** (`plugins/membrum/MANUAL.md:177, 239-248; plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:121-125, 285-291; plugins/membrum/src/dsp/voice_common_params.h:45-48; plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:62-86`)

- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992. *paper*, <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>. Establishes: Air loading lowers the low-frequency modes. In two-headed drums, coupling through the enclosed air or the shell forms mode pairs: snare (1,1) at 275 and 344 Hz, and bass drum coupling splits (0,1) and (1,1). The 1:1.5:2:2.44:2.90 series is a kettledrum result.
- The Well-Tempered Timpani, ch. 3 'Air loading'. *docs*, <https://wtt.pauken.org/chapter-3/air-loading-2>. Establishes: Air loading lowers the natural frequencies from those of an ideal membrane, most strongly for the lower modes.

**Claim 6. Mode Scatter models natural head imperfection and reproduces the (0,1)/(1,1) mode splitting of a real snare head** (`dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:654-656, 784, 809-810 (comments at plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:121-125, plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h:74-77, 132-135, 163-165)`)

- J. Woodhouse, Euphonics, '3.6 Tuned drums'. *docs*, <https://euphonics.org/3-6-tuned-drums/>. Establishes: Any real drum departs from perfect circular symmetry, so the cos/sin mode pairs are normally slightly separated in frequency and show up as double peaks in a frequency response.
- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992. *paper*, <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>. Establishes: Coupling between the two heads forms mode pairs: snare (0,1)-like and (1,1)-like pairs, (1,1) at 275 and 344 Hz. Bass-drum head coupling splits (0,1) and (1,1).

**Claim 7. Membrane inharmonicity (Stretch) uses the stiff-string law sqrt(1 + B n^2) with n = sorted mode index + 1, on by default via material** (`dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:776-807 (membrane stretch source: plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:129-138)`)

- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992. *paper*, <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>. Establishes: Bending stiffness of the membrane, like the stiffness of piano strings, raises the frequencies of the higher overtones. Air loading is mainly responsible for the harmonic relationship, and the other effects only fine-tune.
- S. Bilbao, Numerical Sound Synthesis, Wiley 2009, ch. 11-12 (stiff membrane / thin plate: u_tt = c^2 Lap u - kappa^2 Lap^2 u). *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: Stiff-membrane dispersion omega^2 = c^2 |k|^2 + kappa^2 |k|^4: the stiffness correction depends on the spatial wavenumber |k| = j_mn/a, not on a mode count.

**Claim 8. Plate/NoiseBody mode ratios follow free circular plate (Kirchhoff/Leissa) physics** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h:4-35, 70-101 (generator tools/gen-plate-chladni.js:19-25,36-40; consumers plate_mapper.h:39-43, noise_body_mapper.h:95-106)`)

- A.W. Leissa, Vibration of Plates, NASA SP-160, 1969, sec. 2.1.3 / Table 2.5 (completely free circular plate). *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: Free circular plate lambda^2 at nu=0.33: (2,0) 5.253, (0,1) 9.084, (3,0) 12.23, (1,1) 20.52, (2,1) 35.25, (0,2) 38.55. My Bessel solver reproduces these to 0.1 %.
- Dong & Liu, 'An Absolute Acoustic Readout of Plate Wave Speed for Bullion Authentication...', arXiv:2610.29194, 2026, Appendix (solver validated against both of Leissa's free-plate tables). *paper*, <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.29194>. Establishes: Reprints Leissa's Table 2.5 next to an independent solver: (2,0) 5.251/5.253, (0,1) 9.076/9.084, (3,0) 12.222/12.230, (1,1) 20.517/20.520, (2,1) 35.241/35.250, (0,2) 38.514/38.550. These are identical to my computed values.
- Brezas, Kaselouris, Orphanos, Bakarezos, Dimitriou, Papadogiannis, 'Experimental and computational vibroacoustic study of cymbals', Forum Acusticum 2023 (EAA), DOI 10.61782/fa.2023.0309. *paper*, <https://dael.euracoustics.org/confs/fa2023/data/articles/000309.pdf>. Establishes: Table 1, ESPI on an 8-inch MS63 brass cymbal: (2,0) 210 Hz, (3,0) 555, (4,0) 1040, (5,0) 1520, (3,1) 1630, (4,1) 1740, (2,1) 1760, (5,1) 2030 Hz. As ratios to (2,0): 2.64, 4.95, 7.24, 7.76, 8.29, 8.38, 9.67.
- T.D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of percussion instruments: Recent progress', Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 22(3), 2001, sec. 6.1. *paper*, <https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ast/22/3/22_3_177/_pdf>. Establishes: Over 100 modes recorded on a 46-cm crash cymbal, labelled (m,n) with m nodal diameters and n nodal circles, i.e. the free-plate mode families.

**Claim 9. Exponent P = 1.7 is 'the measured-cymbal Chladni exponent reported by Rossing & Peterson'** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h:26-33 (also tools/gen-plate-chladni.js:7-9,19-20)`)

- C. Wilbur & T.D. Rossing, 'Vibrational modes of cymbals and Chladni's law', ASA 132nd meeting, 5pMU8, 1996 (abstract). *paper*, <https://www.auditory.org/asamtgs/asa96haw/5pMU/5pMU8.html>. Establishes: Gives the modified law f[m,n] = C_n (m+2n)^(P_n) with per-family empirical constants, fitted to about 300 modes of a 16-inch cymbal, and Perrin's f = C(m+bn)^P. No numeric exponents.
- Chladni's law (Wikipedia), citing Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, p. 680, and Rossing & Fletcher, Principles of Vibration and Sound, pp. 73-74. *docs*, <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chladni%27s_law>. Establishes: f = C(m+2n)^p. p is about 2 for flat circular plates and 1.4-2.4 for cymbals, handbells and church bells, and can vary within one object by mode family.
- Brezas et al., 'Experimental and computational vibroacoustic study of cymbals', Forum Acusticum 2023. *paper*, <https://dael.euracoustics.org/confs/fa2023/data/articles/000309.pdf>. Establishes: (m,0) ESPI ratios 2.64 / 4.95 / 7.24 for m = 3/4/5, i.e. p of about 2.4 / 2.3 / 2.2, not 1.7.

**Claim 10. Strike-position weighting cos(m*theta)*cos(n*pi*rho) is the free-plate mode shape at the strike point** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h:103-129 (consumers plate_mapper.h:45-53 with a 0.05 floor, noise_body_mapper.h:108-113 with a 0.03 floor)`)

- A.W. Leissa, Vibration of Plates, NASA SP-160, 1969, sec. 2.1.3 (free circular plate mode shapes). *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: Free-plate mode shape W = [J_n(kr) + C_n I_n(kr)] cos(n theta), with C_n set by the free-edge moment condition. The radial function is a Bessel/modified-Bessel combination, not a cosine.
- T.D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of percussion instruments: Recent progress', Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 22(3), 2001, sec. 6.1. *paper*, <https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ast/22/3/22_3_177/_pdf>. Establishes: 'In the n = 0 modes, the center of the cymbal vibrates very little, and this nodal region expands as m increases.' Physically the (m,0) modes are weak for strikes near the centre.
- S. Bilbao, Modal synthesis (CCRMA online notes). *textbook*, <https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~bilbao/booktop/node14.html>. Establishes: A point excitation drives each mode in proportion to the mode shape (the projection) at the excitation location.

**Claim 11. modeStretch 1.0 is 'physical / no stretch' for the plate table** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_mapper.h:58-62 (also noise_body_mapper.h:118-120; dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:783, 799-807; voice_common_params.h:23; pad_config.h:212; membrane_mapper.h:129-138; tests/unit/bodies/test_plate_body.cpp:135-137)`)

- N.H. Fletcher & T.D. Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., 1998, ch. 2 (stiff strings) and ch. 3 (plates). *textbook*, <https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-21603-4>. Establishes: f_n = n f_1 sqrt(1 + B n^2) is the stiff-string inharmonicity law over harmonic numbers n. Plate modes follow f proportional to lambda_mn^2 from bending stiffness, with their own eigenvalue ordering.
- A.W. Leissa, Vibration of Plates, NASA SP-160, 1969. *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: Plate frequencies follow omega = lambda^2 sqrt(D/(rho h a^4)). The dispersion is already contained in lambda_mn.

**Claim 12. A linear fixed-ratio modal bank models cymbals and gongs** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h:210-271 (Cymbal template), 186-208 (Hat), 274-294 (Perc on the Plate body); bodies/noise_body_mapper.h:115-182`)

- T.D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of percussion instruments: Recent progress', Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 22(3), 2001, sec. 6.1-6.2. *paper*, <https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ast/22/3/22_3_177/_pdf>. Establishes: Three features of cymbal sound: the strike sound in the first ms, peaks at 700-1000 Hz building over 10-20 ms, and a strong 3-5 kHz aftersound a second later ('shimmer'). Energy converts from low-frequency to high-frequency modes. The route to chaos goes harmonics, then subharmonics, then chaos.
- N.H. Fletcher & T.D. Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., 1998, ch. 20 (cymbals, gongs). *textbook*, <https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-21603-4>. Establishes: Cymbal and gong modes are inharmonic and show dynamic nonlinearity (pitch glide, energy cascade, chaos) at amplitudes comparable to the plate thickness.

**Claim 13. Shell partial ratios are the free-free Euler-Bernoulli beam eigenvalue ratios (roots of cos(bL)cosh(bL)=1)** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_modes.h:32-59`)

- Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed. (1998), Ch. 2 (transverse vibrations of a free-free bar). *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: Free-free bar frequencies satisfy cos(bL)cosh(bL)=1, which gives overtone ratios 1 : 2.756 : 5.404 : 8.933 : 13.34 : 18.64.
- J. Woodhouse, Euphonics, 3.2.1 Bending beams and free-free modes. *textbook*, <https://euphonics.org/3-2-1-bending-beams-and-free-free-modes/>. Establishes: Eq. 17: cos kL cosh kL = 1, with roots kL ~ (n+1/2)pi that improve at higher n; omega_n ~ [(n+1/2)pi/L]^2 sqrt(E h^2 / 12 rho).
- This audit: numerical root solve (node, bisection, 200 iterations per root). *docs*, no URL. Establishes: Exact ratios 1, 2.757, 5.404, 8.933, 13.344, 18.638, 24.814, 31.872 ... 465.947; worst table deviation 0.73 cents.

**Claim 14. Default ("physical") Mode Stretch still warps the shell and bell ratios off their published series** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_mapper.h:60-62 (also bell_mapper.h:55-57; dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:783, 806-807; contrast membrane_mapper.h:136-138)`)

- Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments (1998), Ch. 2 and Ch. 21. *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: The free-bar ratios (1, 2.756, 5.404, ...) and the tuned-bell partials are the stiffness-inclusive eigenvalue series. No additional stiff-string factor applies to them.
- Hibbert et al., 'Partial Frequencies and Chladni's Law in Church Bells', Open Journal of Acoustics 4 (2014) 70-77. *paper*, <https://file.scirp.org/pdf/OJA_2014060315140205.pdf>. Establishes: Upper rim partials are measured to cents relative to the nominal across 2752 bells; tuning residuals are tens of cents at most.
- This audit: evaluation of the bank's warp at B = 1.111e-3. *docs*, no URL. Establishes: The per-mode cent shifts at default, relative to the fundamental: shell mode 2 +2.9 c, mode 4 +14.3 c, mode 6 +33 c, mode 8 +58.5 c, mode 12 +127.5 c, mode 32 +657 c; bell (relative to the nominal) hum -22.8 c, prime -19.9 c, tierce -15.1 c, quint -8.5 c, superquint +10 c, octave nominal +22 c, idx 9 +67.5 c, idx 15 +193 c.
- plugins/membrum/AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md line 64 (remediation note). *docs*, no URL. Establishes: 'Accepted consequence (user-approved): widening B_max changes the DEFAULT timbre of all Membrum bodies, because the mappers feed a non-zero stretch at the unity default (... plate/shell/bell/noisebody stretchNorm=0.333).'

**Claim 15. A free-free beam stands in for a drum shell (cylindrical shell)** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_mapper.h:11-20, 44-47`)

- T.D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3) 40-47 (1992), reporting Rossing, Bork, Zhao & Fystrom, JASA (1992). *paper*, <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>. Establishes: 'The lowest modes of the free drum shell are the cylindrical shell modes having m nodes parallel to the axis and n circular nodes.' Fig. 4, snare shell: (4,0) 415 Hz, (4,1) 611 Hz, (5,0) 658 Hz, (5,1) 835 Hz; complete drum, shell-dominated: (4,0) 874 Hz, (5,0) 1064 Hz; complete drum (0,1) at 183 Hz.
- Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments (1998), Ch. 2-3 (rings, cylindrical shells). *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: Thin-ring flexural frequencies scale as n(n^2-1)/sqrt(n^2+1) (n >= 2); for cylinders, axial modes add (m,n) families. I relied on print knowledge here and did not open this source in this audit.

**Claim 16. Shell strike amplitude uses the free-free bar mode shape (end antinodes)** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_modes.h:61-110 (stale comments: shell_modes.h:75-76, shell_mapper.h:15-20)`)

- Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments (1998), Ch. 2, free-free bar mode shapes. *textbook*, no URL. Establishes: The free-free eigenfunction is the cosh/cos/sinh/sin combination with antinodes at the free ends; mode 1 has nodes at 0.224L and 0.776L.
- This audit: numerical evaluation of computeShellAmplitude's formula (node script). *docs*, no URL. Establishes: End values ±1.0000; nodes at 0.2242 / 0.7759 (mode 1), 0.1321 / 0.5000 / 0.8679 (mode 2), 0.0945 / 0.3558 / 0.6442 / 0.9056 (mode 3).

**Claim 17. Bell principal partials hum/prime/tierce/quint/nominal = 0.5 : 1 : 1.2 : 1.5 : 2 (relative to the prime)** (`plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/bell_modes.h:56-60 (first five entries); bell_mapper.h:38-41`)

- Strike tone (Wikipedia), table citing Fletcher & Rossing 2008. *docs*, <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_tone>. Establishes: Ideal/actual ratios to the prime: hum 0.500/0.500, prime 1/1, tierce 1.200/1.183, quint 1.500/1.506, nominal 2.000/2.000, with (m,n) labels (2,0), (2,1#), (3,1), (3,1#), (4,1).
