**Evidence.** controller_state_codec.cpp:91 `// Wire coupling (sound[58] -> offset 65). snapIndex 57 = noiseLayerGain.` (no row for 57); :161-162 `snap.sound[slot.snapIndex] = readParam(...)` covers 42/43; :267 `if (isSentinelSlot && snap.sound[slot.snapIndex] < 0.0) continue;`; controller.cpp:227 `.name = "Body Damping b1" ... .defaultValue = 0.5`; state_codec.cpp:243 `cfg.noiseLayerGain = std::clamp(static_cast<float>(snap.sound[57]), 0.1f, 16.0f);`; membrane_mapper.h:73 `law.b1 = 0.2f + n * 49.8f;` and :77 `law.b3 = n * 1.0e-3f;`; controller_state.cpp:111 `auto kit = Membrum::ControllerState::buildSnapshot(*this, selectedPadIndex_);`

**Suggested fix.** Keep a controller-side mirror of the fields that have no parameter (per-pad noiseLayerGain and a per-pad "B1/B3 overridden" flag, or the raw B1/B3 double including -1). Fill it from every load path (setComponentState, kit and pad load providers) and read it in buildPadSnapshotFromParams. Simpler alternative: ask the processor for its blob (an IMessage request and reply) when saving. Test: processor getState, then controller setComponentState, then kitPresetStateProvider, then processor setState, then getState; the bytes must equal the first getState. Run it on the default kit (covers slot 57 and the sentinel) and on one factory kit. Do the same for a pad preset with padPresetStateProvider and LoadPadPreset.

**Verifier notes:**
- Could not refute (no probe): the save callbacks are wired to the providers (controller.cpp:739-741, 759-761); kLateSlots has 24 rows covering snapIndex 34..56 and 58; only toPadSnapshot writes `snap.sound[57] = cfg.noiseLayerGain` (state_codec.cpp:147); the T60 arithmetic (ln(1000)/25.1 ≈ 0.275 s) is correct.
- Confirmed: a grep finds no noiseLayerGain ParamID or controller mirror (only processor/state/dsp files and a plugin_ids.h comment); the provider tests (test_kit_uimode_roundtrip.cpp:53/101, test_pad_preset.cpp:87/125/282, test_coupling_state.cpp:245) are controller-side only; factory kits come from tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp, so the damage hits user-saved presets and factory kits re-saved from the editor. Severity kept.
- Confirmed: PresetManager uses the state provider whenever processor_ is null (preset_manager.cpp:309, 361, 417, 449); the gain multiplies the noise output directly (drum_voice.h:549/861/1051); default-kit toms have an explicit B3 = 0.15, so only their b1 is corrupted, matching the lost-ring claim; only test_pad_preset.cpp:245 calls padPresetStateProvider.

### High (48)

#### MB-002 — An exciter or body type swap at note-on allocates and frees heap memory on the audio thread. The default kit allocates on 30% of hits; FMImpulse runs FFT wavetable generation.

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** rt-safety · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Also flagged by:** shared-dsp-contracts

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciter_bank.h:53-57, 198-252](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciter_bank.h#L53) (prepare at 235); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h:177-213](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h#L177) (prepare at 212)

**Problem.** Voice slots are shared across pads. When a slot's new pad has a different exciter or body than its previous pad, ExciterBank::trigger() / BodyBank::configureForNoteOn() run applyPendingSwap() inside DrumVoice::noteOn: the trigger at drum_voice.h:343 (and earlier in the strike probe, :1338), and configureForNoteOn at :244. applyPendingSwap does active_.emplace<T>() and then T::prepare() on the audio thread:
- ImpulseExciter / MalletExciter: ImpactExciter::prepare calls combDelay_.prepare(sr, 0.055f) (impact_exciter.h:66), which calls DelayLine buffer_.resize (delay_line.h:316).
- FMImpulseExciter::prepare calls FMOperator::prepare twice. Each runs generateMipmappedFromHarmonics: FFT::prepare, two std::vector temporaries and one IFFT per mipmap level (fm_operator.h:101-113, wavetable_generator.h:82-88). The file's own note says this is "NOT real-time safe".
- StringBody: WaveguideString::prepare runs two DelayLine::prepare calls (waveguide_string.h:105-110).

The emplace also frees the outgoing alternative's vectors on the audio thread. The comment at fm_impulse_exciter.h:17-19 ("prepare() is only called from DrumVoice::prepare()") is false.

**Why wrong.** The audio thread must not allocate, free or run FFT setup. The static_asserts at exciter_bank.h:194-196 and body_bank.h:173-175 only prove nothrow default construction, not freedom from allocation. Allocation-free swaps need every alternative prepared up front, for example one prepared instance per type per voice, or the comb / delay buffers sized in DrumVoice::prepare and handed to the alternative.

**Consequence.** Heap lock contention and page faults on the audio thread at ordinary note-ons in any kit that mixes exciter types (every factory kit). An FMImpulse swap costs 550-800 us inside one noteOn at 48 kHz. This gives xruns and crackles under load, worst on macOS AU and with small buffers.

**Evidence.** exciter_bank.h:235 `std::visit([sr, vid](auto& e) noexcept { e.prepare(sr, vid); }, active_);` inside applyPendingSwap. body_bank.h:212 same for bodies. fm_operator.h:109 `generateMipmappedFromHarmonics(sineTable_, harmonics, 1);`. wavetable_generator.h:83-88 `FFT fft; fft.prepare(kDefaultTableSize); ... std::vector<Complex> spectrum(numBins); std::vector<float> buffer(kDefaultTableSize);`.

PROBE probe.cpp (scratchpad rtprobe, global operator new counter, real headers and libs, 48 kHz, FTZ on):
- Allocations inside DrumVoice::noteOn: X->Impulse and X->Mallet 1 alloc / 16423 B; X->FMImpulse 4 allocs / 32940 B with noteOn 548-795 us; Membrane / Plate / Shell / Bell / NoiseBody -> String 2 allocs / 32846 B. Other swaps 0.
- VoicePool with the default kit, maxPoly 8, random pads: 2250 noteOns, 672 of them allocated (30%); processBlock 0 allocations.

**Suggested fix.** Make every exciter and body alternative allocation-free after DrumVoice::prepare. Options:
- hold the shared resources (ImpactExciter comb buffer, the FMOperator sine table, the WaveguideString delay lines) as DrumVoice / bank members, sized in prepare, with the alternative receiving a pointer;
- or keep all 7 + 6 alternatives prepared side by side and switch an index;
- for FMOperator, generate one static sine WavetableData once per process instead of per operator.

Tests to fix:
- test_allocation_matrix.cpp:104-111 deliberately runs the first, swapping noteOn untracked on the wrong premise that emplace never allocates. Track that first noteOn for every A->B pair.
- Add a VoicePool fuzz with a mixed-type kit (DefaultKit::apply). test_polyphony_allocation_matrix.cpp:74-75 sets every pad to Impulse+Membrane, so it never swaps.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed from source: trigger() swaps whenever pendingType_ != currentType_ (exciter_bank.h:53-57) and applyPendingSwap emplaces then prepares (:198-252, :235; body_bank.h:177-213, :212), reached from drum_voice.h:244, :343 and :1338, with pad_config_apply.h:32-33 setting the pending types. The allocating prepares are impact_exciter.h:66 -> delay_line.h:316, fm_impulse_exciter.h:35-36 -> fm_operator.h:109 -> wavetable_generator.h:83-88, and string_body.h:34 -> waveguide_string.h:109-110. test_allocation_matrix.cpp:104-110 skips the swap; quoted counts not re-run but consistent.
- Could not refute: the "(no heap)" comment at exciter_bank.h:200 holds only for the emplace; delay_line.h:84 itself says prepare allocates; spec 137 FR-072 (specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:257) requires an allocation-free noteOn, and spec.md:578 marks it MET on the strength of a test that skips exactly the allocating call.
- Confirmed: the default kit mixes Impulse/Membrane, Mallet/Membrane, NoiseBurst/NoiseBody, Mallet/Plate and Clap/NoiseBody (default_kit.h:47-316), so ordinary note-ons swap (e.g. NoiseBurst->Impulse); emplace does not allocate but the prepare after it does. Breaks a non-negotiable project rule.

#### MB-003 — The strike-normalisation probe renders 30 ms of scalar modal bank on the audio thread for almost every hit. One noteOn costs up to 1.4-3.5 ms and blocks miss their deadline.

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** rt-safety · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Also flagged by:** exciters, bodies-modal, voice-signal-path, test-gaps, prior-audit-regressions, gestalt-voice

**Corroborated by research:** Physics (contradicted): the probe does not render "the real excitation": the mallet size hint is applied after the probe, several exciter parameters are missing from the cache key, and random draws differ between probe and note. A measured normalisation is only as good as how closely the probe matches the note it scales: apply every per-note exciter setting (mallet size hint, pitch-envelope start) BEFORE probing, key the cache on every exciter parameter that changes the strike (FM ratio, friction pressure, feedback amount, mallet hint), and make the probe deterministic (a fixed probe seed, or the analytic or expected peak rather than one noise realisation). Sources (evidence quality moderate): J.O. Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, "Modal Expansion" [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Modal_Expansion.html — the output of a linear modal bank is the sum of each mode's response to the excitation; a peak measured with a different excitation spectrum, such as a longer contact pulse, does not bound or equal the peak of the actual note.

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:302-304, 394-404, 1273-1299, 1322-1363, 1394-1412, 1717-1728](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L302)

**Problem.** The primary probe (measuredStrikeOutputGain, :302-304 then :1394-1412):
- runs on every StrikeNormKey miss;
- runs probeStrikePeakExcited: 0.030*sr samples through bank.processSample;
- processSample does a per-sample scalar smoothCoefficients pass plus a scalar processSampleCore over every mode (modal_resonator_bank.h:374-377, 906-914, 919-960), not the SIMD block kernel;
- also runs the live exciter and click layer.

Why it almost always misses: the cache key lives in the DrumVoice (strikeNormKey_, :1728), but voice slots are shared across pads (VoicePool assigns any free slot, voice_pool.cpp:232-233) and are swapped into shadows. Pad A and pad B alternating on the same slot miss every time.

The secondary shell probe (:394-404, probeStrikePeak, 20 ms) is not cached at all. It runs on every noteOn of a pad with shell coupling enabled.

The cost scales with the sample rate (window in seconds) and the mode count (64 for NoiseBody, 48 for Membrane / Plate). It is unbounded per block: every coincident hit pays it.

**Why wrong.** The audio thread needs a bounded, small per-event cost. A 30 ms offline-style render per note-on is unbounded work. With several coincident hits (kick + snare + hat on a beat) it exceeds the whole block budget. The cache cannot work as designed while it is keyed per voice slot instead of per pad.

**Consequence.** Audible dropouts and crackles on busy patterns, at high sample rates or small buffers. They appear first at 96 / 192 kHz, where the probe length grows with the sample rate but the block budget does not.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:1329 `const int probeLen = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(0.030f * sr));`, loop :1344-1353 calling `bank.processSample(exc)`. :1407 `if (!(key == strikeNormKey_))` with strikeNormKey_ a DrumVoice member at :1728. :402-403 `secondaryBank_.setOutputGain(measuredStrikeOutputGain(secondaryBank_));` uncached ("Not cached", comment :400-401).

PROBE probe.cpp (scratchpad rtprobe, FTZ on, NoiseBurst exciter), noteOn cost on a cache MISS vs a HIT:

| Body | 48 kHz miss avg | 48 kHz hit avg | 192 kHz miss avg | 192 kHz hit avg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Membrane | 331 us | 8.7 us | 1266 us | 9.6 us |
| Plate | 345 us | 7.1 us | 1516 us | 10.4 us |
| Bell | 131 us | 3.2 us | 585 us | 5.3 us |
| NoiseBody | 402 us | 7.4 us | 2067 us (max 2893) | 13.3 us |

VoicePool with the default kit, maxPoly 8, a hit every ~8 ms and 3 coincident hits every 4th hit, 6000 blocks:

| Rate / block | noteOns > 100 us | worst noteOn | worst block | budget | blocks over budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 48 kHz / 128 | 1639 of 2250 | 2361 us | 5249 us | 2667 us | not recorded |
| 96 kHz / 64 | 519 of 694 | 1368 us | not recorded | 667 us | 281 |
| 192 kHz / 128 | not recorded | 3478 us | not recorded | 667 us | 354 |

Single uncontended core.

**Suggested fix.** Move the probe off the audio thread. Compute the normalisation gain per PAD on the message / setup thread (or in a low-priority worker) whenever a pad's mapper inputs change, store it in PadConfig-side state (an atomic float per pad), and have noteOn read it. As an interim step:
- key the cache per pad (a 32-entry table in VoicePool) instead of per voice;
- use the SIMD processBlock for the probe;
- cache the secondary-bank gain too.

Test: a [rt-safety] case that times VoicePool::noteOn on a mixed default kit with round-robin pads, asserting the 99th-percentile noteOn stays below a small fraction of a 64-sample block at 96 kHz. Tag it [wallclock] or put it in the CPU lane.

**Verifier notes:**
- Could not refute: the probe runs from noteOn (drum_voice.h:302-304 -> :1394-1412 -> :1322-1363) for 0.030*sr samples (:1329: 1440 at 48 kHz, 5760 at 192 kHz) with the live exciter and click layer; it takes the scalar path (modal_resonator_bank.h:374-377, :421-425, :906-914, :919-966), as the SIMD kernel is used only by processBlock and processSampleNoSmooth. The cache is a DrumVoice member (:1717-1729) and the Oldest policy's findIdleVoiceOldest (voice_allocator.h:567-581) rotates slots across pads; the secondary probe (:394-404, :1273-1299) is uncached.
- Confirmed: beginning a fast release swaps main and shadow DrumVoice objects (voice_pool.cpp:922), so the cached key moves with the voice; the comment at :300-301 and the N-1 design text (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:406-407) promise a once-per-pad probe that the code does not deliver; INVESTIGATION-snare-body-2026-07-01.md:84 required keeping the measurement off the audio thread or bounding its cost, and neither happened. No test pins the noteOn cost.
- Confirmed from source and from the measurement logs (scratchpad rtprobe run2.log, run3.log; Release /O2 against the real voice_pool.cpp). At 48 kHz / 128 only 1 block went over budget, so dropouts concentrate at high sample rates and small buffers, as claimed; probe3's VoicePool numbers also include the separate exciter-swap allocations (MB-002), which add cost but do not explain the 300-2000 us measured in isolation. High stands.

#### MB-004 — Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance do nothing: the CouplingMatrix they recompute is never read by the audio path. Per-pad Coupling Amount is only an on/off gate.

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** dead-parameter · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Also flagged by:** coupling, param-plumbing-macros, duplication-drift, parallel-paths, spec-conformance

**Corroborated by measurement:** Quality probe param:global=271:snareBuzz: "bit-identical on 36, 38, 42; live=no", verdict bad. Grep couplingMatrix_|getEffectiveGain|effectiveGain over plugins/membrum/src: only coupling_matrix.h, processor.cpp:138 (recomputeFromTier1) and processor.h:81 `couplingMatrixForTest()`. processor.cpp:703 `float coupling = couplingEngine_.process(delayed);`

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:131-143, 411-424, 185-228](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L131)

**Problem.** kSnareBuzzId and kTomResonanceId only store their atomic and call recomputeCouplingMatrix(). That fills couplingMatrix_.effectiveGain_. No audio code reads couplingMatrix_: its only reader is the test accessor couplingMatrixForTest (processor.h:81). The coupling the user hears is SympatheticResonance, driven by the mono bus sum (processor.cpp:693-707) and by resonators registered at note-on. Registration is gated only by `couplingAmount > 0.0f` (voice_pool.cpp:243-248), so per-pad Coupling Amount values between 0 and 1 have no level effect. Meanwhile the processor calls recomputeCouplingMatrix (a 32x32 loop) on the audio thread for every exciter, body, pitch-env-time, coupling-amount and Complexity edit. On a kit-browser load that is about 160 times in one block, because of the performEdit replay (extra-focus lead 2). All of that work is wasted.

**Why wrong.** A registered, automatable parameter with a knob in the editor (editor.uidesc:402-407; controller.cpp:517, 523) must change the sound. MANUAL.md:77-78 documents a "matrix [global + snare buzz + tom resonance + per-pad amt]" stage that does not exist in the signal path. Commit 40d9aac6 claims "the category-driven coupling math was always doing the useful work". Git history shows effectiveGain was only ever read by the removed matrix UI publisher, never by the audio path.

**Consequence.** Two visible coupling knobs are dead, and per-pad Coupling Amount is binary. Users tuning snare-buzz / tom sympathy hear no change. Audio-thread CPU is also wasted on every related edit and about 160x per preset load.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:411-417 `case kSnareBuzzId: ... snareBuzz_.store(clamped...); recomputeCouplingMatrix();` and the same for kTomResonanceId :418-424. processor.cpp:138 `couplingMatrix_.recomputeFromTier1(` is the only non-test use (grep for couplingMatrix_ in plugins/membrum/src: processor.cpp:138, processor.h:81 test accessor, processor.h:145 declaration). coupling_matrix.h:79-87 getEffectiveGain / effectiveGainArray have no production caller (grep). voice_pool.cpp:243-244 `if (couplingEngine_ != nullptr && padConfigs_[...].couplingAmount > 0.0f)` is the only use of couplingAmount. `git show 17a7d681:.../processor.cpp` shows no audio-path read of effectiveGain either.

**Suggested fix.** Either wire the matrix into the engine or remove the dead knobs. To wire it: at noteOn pass a per-source gain, sum over dst of effectiveGain[src][dst] times the receivers' coupling, into SympatheticResonance::noteOn (or scale the excitation per voice before the bus sum feeds the engine). Otherwise remove Snare Buzz / Tom Resonance, the matrix and the recompute calls, and make Coupling Amount scale level. Test: render kick-then-snare with snareBuzz 0 and with snareBuzz 1. The coupling-return energy must differ by at least X dB (today it is bit-identical). Add the same test for Tom Resonance and for couplingAmount 0.2 vs 1.0.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed from source: recomputeCouplingMatrix (processor.cpp:131-143) writes only couplingMatrix_, whose only reader is processor.h:81; the CouplingMatrixEdit / Snapshot handlers named at processor.h:68-70 are a stale comment; the audible path (processor.cpp:693-707) is scaled only by setAmount(globalCoupling) (:408), and SympatheticResonance::noteOn (sympathetic_resonance.h:179) takes no per-pair gain; the recompute runs at processor.cpp:187, 198, 206, 215, 227, 415, 422 and from applyKitSnapshot (:988, :1012) without changing the sound. High fits.
- Confirmed: snareBuzz_ / tomResonance_ are read only in recomputeCouplingMatrix (:139-140) and getState (:887-889); MANUAL.md:431-432 and :376 document effects the code does not have; commit 40d9aac6 and CHANGELOG.md:465-467 contradict the code; no spec or prior-audit ruling covers it. The recompute is a bounded 32x32 loop, so it wastes work but does not break real-time safety; severity left as stated.
- Confirmed: the controller only registers, formats and snapshots both IDs (controller.cpp:517, 523; controller_state_codec.cpp:345-346, 379-380); "SC-002 kick triggers audible snare buzz" (test_coupling_integration.cpp:240-285) varies the GLOBAL coupling with snareBuzz fixed at 0.5, and the receiver-exclusion test (:861-880) reads only the matrix. This verifier judges the CPU part overstated (~160k flops per load, tens of microseconds, no allocation), calls the rt-safety dimension a mislabel, and argued that medium fits better than high.

#### MB-009 — Feedback-exciter voices never retire: the slow path never calls flushSilentModes, so getNumActiveModes() never reaches 0

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-voice-path · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Also flagged by:** shared-dsp-contracts

**Corroborated by measurement:** Probe lifecycle:Feedback exciter never retires: "-240 dBFS / 1 / not set (output < -100 dBFS after 3.8-7.1 s)" (peak in last 1 s / active voices / silence flag). drum_voice.h:620 `const bool useSlowPath = feedbackExciter;`; drum_voice.h:1030 `body.processSampleNoSmooth(sharedBank, exc)`; modal_resonator_bank.h:399-412 processSampleNoSmooth has no flushSilentModes call.

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:620-669, 989-1067](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L620)

**Problem.** Retirement and the 256-block safety net both require `sharedBank.getNumActiveModes() == 0` (drum_voice.h:645-665). numActiveModes_ only falls inside ModalResonatorBank::flushSilentModes() (modal_resonator_bank.h:461-474), which processBlock() calls (:446, :457). The Feedback exciter forces processBlockSlow (drum_voice.h:610-624). That path drives the bank only through processSampleNoSmooth (:1030, the body *_body.h processSampleNoSmooth wrappers), and processSampleNoSmooth never flushes. bankSilent therefore stays false forever, silentBlockCount_ is reset every block, and active_ is never cleared, even after the output has decayed to exact zero.

**Why wrong.** A voice must retire when its body has decayed (the STK / Chromaphone idiom the code cites at :631-637). The safety net exists exactly so that no voice stays Active forever (:652-659), but it is gated on the same bankSilent flag.

**Consequence.** Every hit on a Feedback pad occupies a voice slot permanently, until it is stolen or choked or the kit changes. It keeps running the per-sample slow path over 44 modes on silence (a CPU leak per hit). VoicePool calls noteOff() on it every block, its meta stays Active, the processor's main-bus silence flag is never set, and the active-voice meter and steal decisions count dead voices.

**Evidence.** Measured (probe retirement(), Membrane default PadConfig, 44.1 kHz, block 256, no noteOff, 30 s). Retire times: Impulse 6.13 s, Mallet 6.14 s, NoiseBurst 4.59 s, Friction 4.65 s, FMImpulse 5.29 s, Clap 5.46 s. Feedback: "NEVER(>30s) activeModes=44 lastBlockPeak=0". Code: `const bool bankSilent = sharedBank.getNumActiveModes() == 0;` (:645); slow loop `const float bodyOut = body.processSampleNoSmooth(sharedBank, exc);` (:1030) with no flush. processSampleNoSmooth (modal_resonator_bank.h:399-412) has no flushSilentModes call.

**Suggested fix.** At the end of processBlockSlow, call bodyBank_.getSharedBank().flushSilentModes(), and also secondaryBank_.flushSilentModes() when it is active. flushSilentModes is public. Test: Feedback + Membrane default pad, noteOn(1), render 10 s at block 256 with no noteOff, then REQUIRE(!voice.isActive()). Add the same case at VoicePool level: getActiveVoiceCount() == 0.

**Verifier notes:**
- Traced and real: the slow path forwards through every body wrapper (membrane_body.h:54-57, plate_body.h:51-54, shell_body.h:47-50, bell_body.h:47-50, noise_body.h:91-94) to processSampleNoSmooth, which never flushes; numActiveModes_ is lowered only at modal_resonator_bank.h:471 and reset at :760/:841; voice_pool.cpp:352-396 frees a slot only when isActive() goes false and its noteOff (:380-384) cannot touch the mode counter. Matches the measurement (Feedback never retired, activeModes=44, peak 0; the other six retired in 4.6-6.1 s). Steal and choke still reclaim the slot, so high stands.
- Could not refute: the comments at drum_voice.h:633 and :1089 wrongly assume processBlock runs on every path; no test pins Feedback retirement (test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp:293 checks only right after noteOn); not intended (the design exceptions cover Friction sustain and modeInject, and feedback_exciter.h:187 shows the exciter deactivates itself); not a repeat of the prior audit's flushSilentModes item.
- Confirmed: grepping the tests for Feedback with retire / isActive / getActiveVoiceCount finds nothing; the generator uses ExciterType::Feedback 10 times. Audible impact is small (stealing a silent voice makes no sound) but it is a voice and CPU leak of up to 16 slow-path voices that defeats the safety net. The String body (string_body.h:71-75) is an exception that does not change the verdict. High stands.

#### MB-017 — Feedback-exciter pads drive the unnormalised modal bank into its soft-clip rail: the output is a square wave pinned at ±0.707×velocity for 1-3 s, on every body, at every velocity, whatever the Feedback Amount

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-exciter · **Dimension:** exciters

**Corroborated by measurement:** Quality kit:pads-on-limiter (21 pads): "-7.00..-7.16 dBFS / -0.00..-0.16 dB" (peak / margin to ceiling). Probe level:body headroom: "String -0.02" vs ~-6. drum_voice.h:1329 `const int probeLen = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(0.030f * sr));`.

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:269-276](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L269)

**Problem.** With the Feedback exciter selected, noteOn sets bank.setOutputGain(1.0f) and setOutputSoftClipThreshold(0.707f) (drum_voice.h:272-276), and the strike normalisation is skipped. The bank's raw resonant output is many times above 0.707, so applyOutputStage (modal_resonator_bank.h:894-900, softClip(x/t)*t) saturates on every sample. Even the 0.0011-peak exciter at velocity 0.1 (feedback_exciter.h:105-126) saturates it. The voice output is then the clip rail times the amp envelope.

**Why wrong.** A drum voice needs headroom-normalised, velocity-dependent timbre. The comment at drum_voice.h:264-268 says the loop's gain budget is "calibrated against the clipped output", but the bank never leaves the clip. SC-008 (peak <= 0 dBFS) holds only because of the rail, not because the loop is stable. Feedback Amount (feedback_exciter.h:100-111) cannot change a signal that is already saturated.

**Consequence.** Every Feedback pad (factory "Feedback-Plate Drone" and others) sounds like a fixed-level clipped square or fuzz for 1-3 s. Velocity changes only the level (peak = 0.707 x v exactly), never the timbre. Feedback Amount is effectively dead, and the -3 dBFS square at full scale dominates any kit it plays in.

**Evidence.** Voice probe (fbprobe.cpp, DrumVoice + applyPadConfigToVoice, 44.1 kHz, v=0.8, click 0, noise 0), RMS/mean per 200 ms window:
- Membrane decay 0.2: [0.0s 0.565] [0.4s 0.565] [0.8s 0.562] [1.2s 0.538]; samples @10000 = -0.5656 -0.5656 -0.5656 (flat).
- Plate decay 0.5 is still 0.554 RMS at 2.8 s. Bell, Shell and NoiseBody (0.339 = rail x 0.6 modalMix x 0.8) behave the same.
- feedbackAmount 0 vs 1: 0.565 vs 0.565 RMS in the first 1.2 s.
- Velocity sweep: peak 0.0707 / 0.2121 / 0.3535 / 0.4949 / 0.7070 at v 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0, exactly 0.707 x v.
- vprobe: Feedback click 0, RMS 0.7065 vs peak 0.707 at 44.1, 96 and 192 kHz.

**Suggested fix.** Normalise the Feedback path like the others: measure the loop's strike peak or use a fixed calibrated input gain so the bank runs below the clip threshold, and keep the soft clip only as a safety net. Then retune feedbackAmount so it sets the sustain or loop gain audibly. Test: a Feedback pad on each body at v=0.8, where crest factor (peak/RMS) over 0.2-1.0 s must be > 3 dB (today 0 dB), and Feedback Amount 0 vs 1 must differ in RMS by > 3 dB.

**Verifier notes:**
- Could not refute the mechanism (traced, not run): Feedback skips the measuredStrikeOutputGain normalisation (drum_voice.h:286-306); per-mode input gain is the raw mode amplitude (modal_resonator_bank.h:829-839); softClip returns exactly ±1 beyond ±3 (dsp_utils.h:107-108), so a raw sum above ~2.12 is pinned at ±0.707; velocity reaches the output only through the amp envelope (drum_voice.h:436, :1061). The bank's own comment (modal_resonator_bank.h:147-151) describes this pinned failure mode, which Phase 11 removed for every exciter except Feedback; the only Feedback Amount test (test_dead_exciter_params.cpp:102-113) asserts a mean-abs difference above 1e-4.
- Mechanism confirmed; the audit's probe-results.txt (lines 138, 143) shows peak(v1.0) - peak(v0.25) = 12.04 dB = 20log10(4), i.e. peak linear in velocity; spec 137 research.md:96 expects the energy limiter to stop the clipping, which it cannot (feedback_exciter.h:154-156). This verifier argued for a downgrade: only one of seven exciters is affected, MANUAL.md:225 sells it as "chaotic runaway-resonance percussion", and "every body" overclaims because String runs a WaveguideString.
- Confirmed with an own probe (scratchpad fbprobe.cpp against KrateDSP.lib): Membrane v=0.8 RMS 0.565 with 0.0 dB crest (a square at 0.707*0.8), Plate 0.420 RMS at 2.8 s, Mallet at the same settings 7-27 dB crest; velocity sweep exactly 0.707*v with 0.0-1.1 dB crest even at v=0.1; Feedback Amount 0 vs 1 identical through 0.8 s and different only in the tail (1.6 s: 0.333 vs 0.371), so "effectively dead" is a slight overstatement. String not probed; factory kits assign Feedback (membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1408, 1579, 3465, 3586, 3695, 6054, 6256, 6292, 6388).

#### MB-018 — Feedback-exciter voices never retire after note-off (the slow path never flushes silent modes): a permanent voice-slot and CPU leak

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-path · **Dimension:** exciters · **Also flagged by:** bodies-modal, voice-signal-path, layers-shaper, prior-audit-regressions

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:644-669, 989-1041](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L644)

**Problem.** Retirement needs sharedBank.getNumActiveModes() == 0 (drum_voice.h:645-651, and the 256-block net at 660-665 also requires bankSilent). Only ModalResonatorBank::processBlock decrements numActiveModes_, through flushSilentModes. The Feedback exciter forces processBlockSlow (drum_voice.h:610-611), which drives the bank only through prepareBlockSmoothing + processSampleNoSmooth (drum_voice.h:1002, 1030). No flushSilentModes call is in the plugin (grep), so the active-mode count never falls.

**Why wrong.** Every renderer must retire a voice once its body is silent and the envelope has released. The comment at 631-637 relies on "flushSilentModes() (called inside ModalResonatorBank::processBlock)", which the slow path never calls.

**Consequence.** Every Feedback-pad hit holds its voice slot and a per-sample slow-path modal render (up to 32-64 modes) until the voice is stolen, even though the output is digital silence. With maxPolyphony 4-16, a few Feedback hits fill the pool and every later note steals. CPU grows with each Feedback hit, and processBlock keeps the slot meta Active, so the host meters show active voices that are silent.

**Evidence.** Retirement probe (retire.cpp, decay 0.2, v=0.8, noteOff at 0.1 s, 256-sample blocks, 44.1 kHz): exciters 0-4 and 6 retire at 0.37 s on Membrane and Shell; "exciter 5 body 0: retired at NEVER within 20 s (last block peak 0.00e+00)", the same for Shell. Code: drum_voice.h:1002 `sharedBank.prepareBlockSmoothing();` and :1030 `body.processSampleNoSmooth(sharedBank, exc)`; no flushSilentModes in plugins/membrum/src.

**Suggested fix.** Call sharedBank.flushSilentModes() (and the secondary bank's) once per block at the end of processBlockSlow, or give the bank's per-sample path an end-of-block flush hook. Test: for each exciter type, noteOn, noteOff at 0.1 s, then voice.isActive() must be false within 5 s (today it is true for Feedback after 20 s).

**Verifier notes:**
- Traced and holds: the slow path calls only prepareBlockSmoothing (modal_resonator_bank.h:386-389) and processSampleNoSmooth (:399-412), neither of which touches active_ or numActiveModes_; computeModeCoefficients (:759-841) recounts every non-culled mode as active, so a retune cannot lower the count either; the comments at drum_voice.h:449, 633, 1089 wrongly assume processBlock runs. Audible damage is limited (stealing a silent voice is harmless), but the CPU and slot leak of up to maxPolyphony voices is real.
- Confirmed: noteOff (drum_voice.h:442-452) only gates the envelope and damps the bank, so envFinished becomes true while bankSilent stays false and the slot never returns to the allocator (voice_pool.cpp:386-396); the prior audit fixed M-6 and the tension glide on this same path (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:39-50, 275) but never retirement; factory kits use Feedback on ordinary pads (membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1407-1408, 6255-6256, 6291-6292).
- Confirmed: the leak is bounded by maxPolyphony because stealing reclaims slots, but each Feedback hit permanently costs a slot plus a 32-64-mode per-sample render; later hits are needlessly stolen (5 ms fast-release crossfades) and the meters stay high; the generator references Feedback 21 times. High stands.

#### MB-019 — Friction exciter has an inverted velocity response: soft hits drive the body into the hardClip rail while a full-velocity hit sits at the -6 dBFS budget

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** exciter · **Dimension:** exciters

**Corroborated by research:** Physics (contradicted): the Friction exciter is said to produce stick-slip from the STK power-law bow table. The bow table itself is the standard STK/Smith memoryless friction curve (prior audit: verbatim STK BowTable up to the 0.01/0.98 clamp), but stick-slip is a limit cycle of the COUPLED system: the junction input is the differential velocity between the bow and the string/body velocity at the contact point (Smith: v_Delta+ = v_b - (v_s,r+ + v_s,l+)), and the outgoing waves feed back into the resonator. McIntyre, Schumacher & Woodhouse (1983) model self-sustained oscillation as a nonlinear friction element in a feedback loop with the resonator's reflection function. With the feedback forced to 0 the table is a static nonlinearity of a monotonic bow-velocity ramp: no stick and no slip can occur, and jitter of 0.001-0.003 cannot create them. Sources (evidence quality strong): J. O. Smith III, "The Bow-String Scattering Junction", Physical Audio Signal Processing [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Bow_String_Scattering_Junction.html — Delta = v_b - v_s with v_s the sum of the travelling waves meeting at the bow; reflection coefficient rho(Delta+) = r/(1+r), r = 0.25 R_b(Delta)/R_s; outgoing waves v_s,r- = v_s,l+ + rho*Delta+, so the friction force depends on the string velocity at the bow point. M. E. McIntyre, R. T. Schumacher, J. Woodhouse, "On the oscillations of musical instruments", JASA 74(5), 1325-1345, 1983 [paper] — bowed/blown self-oscillation arises from a nonlinear excitation element (friction curve) coupled in a feedback loop to a linear resonator described by its reflection function; the oscillation is a property of the loop, not of the nonlinearity alone.

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/friction_exciter.h:79-95, 118-125](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/friction_exciter.h#L79)

**Problem.** Velocity raises bow speed (ceiling maxVelocity x speed = v x (0.2+0.6v)) and moves the bandpass from 400 Hz up to 8 kHz (line 86). The bow is driven with zero body feedback (line 124, core_.process(0.0f)), so deltaV = bowVelocity. The STK table (bow_exciter.h:315-323, refl = clamp(1/(|dv x slope|+0.75)^4)) then gives a SMALLER force for a larger deltaV, and the high bandpass rejects the slow bow-force ramp. The exciter output falls 23 dB from v=0.1 to v=1.0. The strike normalisation probes at velocity 1.0 (drum_voice.h:1338), so it calibrates the weakest case, and every softer hit is boosted past kBodyHeadroom.

**Why wrong.** A velocity response must be monotonic: a harder strike must not be quieter (spec 136 SC-005: amplitude difference > 6 dB, 30 vs 127). Normalising at v=1 assumes the exciter's peak grows with velocity, as it does for Impact, FM, NoiseBurst and Clap. Also, CLAUDE.md says "Friction sustains without note-off", but the exciter stops itself at 41 ms (measured last non-zero sample at 41.0 ms); any sustain is body ring.

**Consequence.** Friction pads with click mix 0 (factory Singing Bowl, Guiro, Tanpura and string/membrane drones set clickLayerMix = 0, e.g. membrum_preset_generator.cpp:5200, :5653) hit the voice hardClip rail at velocities 0.2-0.7, a distorted soft playing level. With the default click 0.5, the click dominates the hard hits and the playable range from v=0.2 to v=1 is only 8 dB (Impulse: about 40 dB).

**Evidence.** Exciter probe (probe.cpp, ExciterBank alone, 44.1 kHz), Friction peak: v0.1 0.0187, v0.2 0.0175, v0.3 0.0119, v0.5 0.0065, v0.7 0.0035, v1.0 0.0013. Voice probe (vprobe.cpp, level 1, click 0): Membrane v0.1 0.700, v0.2..0.7 1.000 (rail), v1.0 0.500; Bell v0.2..0.5 1.000, v1.0 0.532; Plate v0.2..0.5 1.000, v1.0 0.500. With click 0.5: Membrane v0.2 -13.4 dB vs v1.0 -5.4 dB. Impulse reference: v0.1 -45.6 dB, v1.0 -6.0 dB.

**Suggested fix.** Remap Friction velocity so force rises with velocity: for example scale the output by velocity, keep the bandpass under the bow-force spectrum, or derive the output from the bow-force derivative. Alternatively normalise by the exciter's peak at the hit's own velocity. Test: a Friction pad (click 0) on Membrane and Bell, where voice peak must increase monotonically over v = 0.1..1.0 and stay below the rail.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed by tracing (friction_exciter.h:79-86, :124; bow_exciter.h:153, :292-296, :315-323; plateau force ≈ 0.008 at v=1 vs ≈ 0.025 at v=0.1) and two own probes: exciter peaks match the finding exactly, and the voice (level 1, click 0) hits the 1.000 rail at v=0.2-0.7 on Membrane, Bell and Plate while v=1.0 sits at ~0.5; with click 0.5 the response is also non-monotonic (v=0.5 quieter than v=0.3). ExciterBank::process (exciter_bank.h:65-70) adds no velocity scaling and the normalisation probes at v=1 (drum_voice.h:1336-1340, :1380-1386).
- Confirmed (standalone clang -O2: peaks match, last non-zero sample at 41.0 ms for every velocity); voice peak ≈ 0.5 x v x exc(v)/exc(1), so mid velocities exceed the rail. Spec 137 FR-016 (specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:192) requires velocity to drive amplitude and spectrum; the tests check only the centroid (test_friction_exciter.cpp:38-58, test_velocity_mapping); the prior audit only confirmed the STK BowTable formula (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:317); the 41 ms auto-release is documented in friction_exciter.h:7-9.
- Confirmed (WSL g++, real FrictionExciter): a 23.3 dB inverted range at Friction Pressure 0 and 0.5; FrictionExciter never calls setResonatorEnergy, so the bow energy limiter (bow_exciter.h:209-217) never acts; a linear modal model normalised at v=1 shows mid velocities overshooting the -6 dBFS budget by 6-9.5 dB; the only velocity test that includes Friction (test_velocity_mapping.cpp:62-78) checks centroid only; Friction appears 21 times in the generator.

#### MB-020 — Exciter type swap allocates and runs FFT wavetable generation on the audio thread (about 190 us per FMImpulse swap); the allocation tests deliberately avoid the case

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** rt-safety · **Dimension:** exciters · **Also flagged by:** spec-conformance, gestalt-voice

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciter_bank.h:198-235](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciter_bank.h#L198)

**Problem.** ExciterBank::trigger (called from DrumVoice::noteOn and from the strike probe, drum_voice.h:343, 1338) runs applyPendingSwap, which default-emplaces the new alternative and calls e.prepare(sr, vid) on the audio thread. FMImpulseExciter::prepare calls FMOperator::prepare twice, and each runs generateMipmappedFromHarmonics (fm_operator.h:103-113). That builds a new FFT and std::vector buffers and runs 11 inverse FFTs (wavetable_generator.h:83-88, 236-288). Impulse and Mallet prepare call DelayLine::prepare, which does buffer_.resize (impact_exciter.h:66, delay_line.h:316). The old alternative's vector is freed on the audio thread. generateMipmappedFromHarmonics is not noexcept, so bad_alloc inside the noexcept prepare would terminate.

**Why wrong.** Root CLAUDE.md: no allocation on the audio thread. fm_operator.h:101 says prepare() is "NOT real-time safe", and fm_impulse_exciter.h:17-19 falsely claims prepare is only called from DrumVoice::prepare. MANUAL.md:505 claims "Zero allocations on the audio thread ... ExciterBank and BodyBank pre-allocate every variant up front".

**Consequence.** The first hit of a pad on a slot whose previous pad used a different exciter allocates. A kit or preset switch, or a roll alternating pads with different exciters across slots, takes the heap lock and costs 190 us per FM swap (about 7% of a 128-sample block at 48 kHz per voice). Several FM pads hit together after a kit load can drop out. test_allocation_matrix.cpp:104-111 runs the swapping noteOn outside the AllocationScope with the false premise that emplace never allocates, and test_per_pad_dispatch.cpp:360-366 forces uniform exciter types "because ... swaps ... trigger ... heap allocations".

**Evidence.** swapcost.cpp (operator new counter, 48 kHz): "Clap -> FMImpulse swap: 189.0 us, 4 heap allocs" (pffft aligned mallocs not counted), "Clap -> Impulse swap: 1.0 us, 1 heap allocs", "Clap -> Mallet ... 1 heap allocs", "Clap -> Friction swap: 29.8 us". A retrigger of the same type costs 0.04-0.16 us. sizeof(ExciterBank) = 180880 bytes.

**Suggested fix.** Hold one prepared instance of every exciter alternative per voice (a tuple or array of the 7, as the MANUAL describes), or share one FM sine table prepared at setup and give FMOperator a non-owning table pointer. The swap then only changes an index and calls trigger. Test: an allocation-scope test where each noteOn switches the exciter type (all 7x7 transitions) and asserts 0 allocations, with the test_allocation_matrix warm-up removed.

**Verifier notes:**
- Traced and holds (timings and counts not re-run): setExciterType only records pendingType_ (drum_voice.h:1134, exciter_bank.h:48-51); trigger swaps (exciter_bank.h:53-58) and prepares on the audio thread (:233-235); fm_impulse_exciter.h:35-36 -> fm_operator.h:103-109 -> wavetable_generator.h:82-100 builds an FFT and vectors per call; a throwing allocation inside the noexcept chain would call std::terminate. impact_exciter.h / delay_line.h were not opened by this verifier, but the FMImpulse path alone confirms the violation.
- Confirmed: wavetable_generator.h:236-288 builds local FFT objects and std::vector buffers (241, 259, 265, 287, 288); the "no heap" comment (exciter_bank.h:200) and MANUAL.md:505 are false; test_allocation_matrix.cpp:104-108 and test_per_pad_dispatch.cpp:360-368 sidestep the case; no prior ruling in the Membrum audit files accepts it. High is appropriate.
- Confirmed: pad_config_apply.h:32 sets the exciter type on the pooled slot at note-on, and the comment at drum_voice.h:1312-1317 admits the swap allocates; with slots shared across 32 pads this is routine in a mixed kit, not only after a kit load; 189 us is ~7% of a 128-sample block at 48 kHz per FM swap, plus unbounded heap-lock latency on every swap type. High stands.

#### MB-028 — With Material Morph enabled, the pitch envelope (and tension glide) is fully overwritten every chunk or sample

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** body-model · **Dimension:** bodies-modal · **Also flagged by:** voice-signal-path (x2), layers-shaper, parameter-audibility, shared-dsp-contracts, prior-audit-regressions

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:734-770, 960-977, 506-519, 1638-1652](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L734)

**Problem.** Every renderer runs the pitch or tension retune first: updateModalFundamentalOnBank, which scales cachedMapperResult_ by pitchHz/natural and calls updateModes. It then runs the morph refresh: refreshBodyForMaterialOnBank sets cachedMapperResult_ = mapModalBody(t, p, 0.0f) and calls pushCachedModes, an updateModes with the UNSCALED natural frequencies. updateModes replaces all targets, so the last call wins. The bank targets therefore sit at the natural pitch on every chunk (fast path 734-770), block (slow path 960-977) and sample (process() 506-519).

**Why wrong.** Pitch envelope and Material Morph are independent per-pad features. The morph refresh must keep the current pitch ratio, as the tension and pitch paths do.

**Consequence.** On any pad with morphEnabled the pitch envelope and the Membrane tension glide are silently dead, on all three renderers. Factory pads affected (both features set): experimentalKit pad 4 (membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1437-1442, 230->160 Hz glide), jazzBrushesKit pad 2 (:1718/:1732) and modularWestCoastKit pad 2 (:3506-3512, which also sets tensionModAmt 0.30).

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:745 `retuneFundamental(pitchHz);` then :769 `refreshBodyForMaterialOnBank(bodyBank_.getSharedBank(), m);`; :1650-1651 `cachedMapperResult_ = mapModalBody(t, p, /*pitchHz*/ 0.0f); pushCachedModes(sharedBank);`; :1658-1664 pushCachedModes passes cachedMapperResult_.frequencies unscaled to updateModes. process(): :509 updateBodyFundamental then :518 refreshBodyForMaterial (same order). Slow path: :964 then :976. Generator scan (node over tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp) found pads with both morphEnabled = 1 and tsPitchEnvTime > 0: experimentalKit pad 4, jazzBrushesKit pad 2, modularWestCoastKit pad 2.

**Suggested fix.** In refreshBodyForMaterialOnBank, store the unscaled mapper result in cachedMapperResult_. Then push it through updateModalFundamentalOnBank(sharedBank, lastPitchHz_) instead of pushCachedModes when the pitch env or tension is active. Or reorder: morph refresh first, then the pitch/tension retune. Either way, keep the current pitch*tension ratio applied.

Test: a Membrane pad with pitch env 400->100 Hz over 100 ms plus morph 0.2->0.8 over 300 ms, rendered via process() and via processBlock. The sounding f0 at 100 ms must be within 10 % of 100 Hz, and must differ from the same render with the pitch env off.

**Verifier notes:**
- Traced on all three renderers (fast :734-770, slow :960-977, process() :506-519); updateModes (modal_resonator_bank.h:294-305) replaces every target, MembraneMapper::map ignores pitchHz (membrane_mapper.h:89), and morphActive = materialMorph.isEnabled() (drum_voice.h:609, material_morph.h:65), so the overwrite runs every chunk for the whole note; the tension branch is overwritten the same way; only String escapes (:1644-1648). Factory scan not re-verified; the mechanism alone confirms the defect.
- Confirmed: makeBodyParams (:1520-1541) carries no pitch; the comment at :1601-1606 says cachedMapperResult_ is meant to be scaled by the pitch path, so the features are meant to compose; no test covers both together (test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp tests them separately, M-1 at :191-231); membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1437-1443 sets both on one factory pad. High stands.
- Confirmed with no mitigation: isPitchEnvActive() is just pitchEnvTimeMs_ > 0 (tone_shaper.h:310-313), so the retune and its undoing repeat every chunk, and the noteOn seed (:318-321) is undone by the first chunk's morph push; membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1430-1443 confirms experimentalKit pad 4 is a Plate with a 230->160 Hz envelope and morphEnabled = 1.0. High stands.

#### MB-029 — With both damping overrides set (every factory pad), the per-pad Decay knob, its global proxy and the decay macros do not change a modal body's ring time, and Material loses its damping role

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** dead-parameter · **Dimension:** bodies-modal · **Also flagged by:** parameter-audibility

**Corroborated by measurement:** quality probe `param:offset=4:decay` on the default snare: "IDENT (36: 5.9 dB/466% decay; 42: 17.1 dB/471%)", with the note that default_kit.h:130-131 sets bodyDampingB1 = 0.60 / B3 = 0.40 on the snare, so the mapper ignores decay. Sameness: "Tabla 36 vs 42: 0.00/1.027/1.000" and "ExpFX 42 vs 44: 0.00/1.000/1.000".

**Corroborated by research (physics, contradicted):** the "Metallic" endpoint (b3 -> 0, frequency-independent damping) contradicts the linear-in-frequency internal-friction law for metals. Per-mode decay for metals is b(f) = pi·tan(phi)·f (Wildes & Richards after Zener), Chaigne & Doutaut (1997) add a quadratic viscoelastic term, and the constant (fluid) term "is usually small". The coded law keeps only the minor constant term and drops the dominant linear one; a real cymbal, bell or steel plate loses its upper partials much faster than its fundamental. Sources (strong): Klatzky, Pai & Krotkov, *Perception of Material from Contact Sounds*, Presence 9(4):399-410, 2000 (https://www.cs.ubc.ca/labs/lci/papers/docs2000/pai-KlaPai00.pdf); Sterling & Lin, I3D 2016 (https://gamma.cs.unc.edu/gpdsynth/data/gpdsynth.pdf), which finds a power-law damping model fits recorded objects better than Rayleigh a1 + a2·omega².

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:64-80](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L64-L80)

**Problem.** `dampingLawFromParams` builds the legacy law from decayTime (Decay, Material, Size, Decay Skew bias) and brightness (Material). It then REPLACES b1 when `bodyDampingB1 >= 0` and b3 when `bodyDampingB3 >= 0`. With both set, the Decay-derived law is discarded completely. Every modal mapper uses this function: membrane :177, plate :95, shell :93, bell :90, noise_body :149. The preset generator writes explicit bodyDampingB1 = bodyDampingB3 = 0.40 as the default for every pad (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:131-136); its comment says the sentinel "cannot survive the controller". So no factory pad uses the sentinel.

**Why wrong.** Decay is a primary per-pad control. It is shown as the global "Resonance" proxy (controller.cpp:288) and driven by the Tightness / Body Size macros (macro_mapper.cpp:136-137, 173-175). It must change the body's ring time. Material is documented as setting brightness and damping (FR-032/033). The override should scale or offset the Decay-derived law instead of replacing it; alternatively, the editor must show that Decay is inert while overrides are on.

**Consequence.** On every non-String factory pad, sweeping Decay 0 -> 1 changes nothing in the body's ring time:
- At b1 = b3 = 0.40 the fundamental of a 158 Hz membrane has T60 0.229 s at decay 0, 0.5 and 1.
- The sentinel path gives 0.96 / 2.64 / 5.91 s.
- 1 kHz modes: 0.016 s vs 0.26-0.33 s.

Plate, Shell and Bell use Material only for brightness and decayTime, so their Material knob becomes timbrally dead except for Membrane's stretch term. Decay still reaches the String body, ModeInject's decay and NoiseBody's noise decay, so the knob seems to work only on some pads.

**Evidence.** membrane_mapper.h:69-79: `auto law = ...dampingLawFromLegacy(legacyDecayTime, legacyBrightness); if (params.bodyDampingB1 >= 0.0f) {... law.b1 = 0.2f + n * 49.8f;} if (params.bodyDampingB3 >= 0.0f) {... law.b3 = n * 1.0e-3f;}`. Generator :135-136 `double bodyDampingB1 = 0.40; double bodyDampingB3 = 0.40;`. state_codec.cpp:216-221 loads them as explicit overrides. Computed from the code's damping law (membrane, material 0.5, size 0.5), T60 of f0 at decay 0 / 0.5 / 1:
- sentinel: 0.962 / 2.643 / 5.913 s;
- 0.40/0.40: 0.229 / 0.229 / 0.229 s.

**Suggested fix.** Make the overrides relative, for example b1 = legacyB1 · 2^(k·(n-0.5)) and b3 = legacyB3 + n·1e-3. Or make the factory and controller default the sentinel by adding an "Auto" state the controller can represent (a separate bool param, or reserve normalized 0 to mean auto), then regenerate the factory kits. Test: for a factory kit pad (loaded via `State::applyPadSnapshot`), render at Decay 0.2 and 0.8; the measured T60 of the fundamental must differ by at least 2x.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute: `dampingLawFromLegacy` (modal_resonator_bank.h:133-139) returns only b1 = 1/decayTime, b3 = (1-brightness)·4e-5, and membrane_mapper.h:71-78 overwrites both, so nothing from decayTime (membrane_mapper.h:146-152) or brightness (:121) survives; all modal mappers route through it (bell :90, plate :95, shell :93, noise_body :150, membrane :177). `decay_` otherwise reaches only `params_.decay` (drum_voice.h:185, :1525) and the modeInject decay (:331); String's `setDecay` (string_body.h:50, body_bank.h:142) is unaffected. Re-derived 0.962 s (sentinel, decay 0) and 0.229 s (override) from the code. The override precedence is commented as intended (membrane_mapper.h:35-39, pad_config.h:280-281) and B1/B3 knobs are visible (editor.uidesc:244-246), but that does not cure the inert Decay.
- Confirmed from source; the "every factory pad" claim rests on the generator source (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:131-136 and every per-pad recipe from :517 on writes explicit values), not on decoding the shipped .vstpreset files. The controller registers B1/B3 at default 0.5 (controller.cpp:227-228), so the knob's "default position" is itself an override; MANUAL.md:237's promise that Decay and Material work "when the Phase 8A knobs are at their default position" therefore never applies to shipped content. Only dsp/default_kit.h keeps the sentinel on some fields (default_kit.h:171-174), and it is not a factory .vstpreset.
- Could not refute: decayRate_k = b1 + b3·f² (modal_resonator_bank.h:367-368) depends only on b1/b3; Tightness and Body Size change only `cfg.decay` / `material` (macro_mapper.cpp:132-139, 165-177), so both macros lose their ring-time effect; reproduced 0.229 s (override) and 2.64 s (sentinel, Decay 0.5) by hand. Pad 18 sets only B3 and keeps the explicit 0.40 B1 default.

#### MB-030 — Extra-focus lead (1), damping part confirmed: controller-side kit and pad preset saves turn every sentinel pad into an explicit 0.5/0.5 override, cutting the default kick and tom ring to a fraction

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** lifecycle-state · **Dimension:** bodies-modal

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp:157-162](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp#L157-L162)

**Problem.** `buildPadSnapshotFromParams` writes sound[42] and sound[43] (kLateSlots :70-71) from the controller parameter value. The controller registers kPadBodyDampingB1/B3 with defaultValue 0.5 (controller.cpp:227-228), and the replay skips sentinel slots on load (controller_state_codec.cpp:264-267, 312-316). The processor's -1 sentinel therefore never reaches a controller-built blob. `State::applyPadSnapshot` loads 0.5 as an explicit override (state_codec.cpp:216-221). This finding reports the body-side consequence only; the noiseLayerGain half is MB-043.

**Why wrong.** A preset saved from the browser must reproduce the processor's state (host getState uses `State::toPadSnapshot`, which keeps -1). The default kit deliberately leaves the tom b1 at the sentinel: default_kit.h:170-174 says "an override here would clobber the long fundamental".

**Consequence.** Fundamental T60 before (sentinel) and after a save-and-reload through the kit or pad preset browser, using the code's own damping law:
- Default-kit tom (mat 0.4, size 0.5, decay 0.5, b3 0.15): 1.115 s -> 0.239 s.
- Default-kit kick (mat 0.3, size 0.8, decay 0.3): 1.483 s -> 0.245 s.
- Default pad (mat 0.5, size 0.5, decay 0.3): about 1.79 s -> 0.18 s at f0; 1 kHz modes about 0.30 s -> 0.013 s.

The kit audibly turns short and dead after a save and reload, and Decay becomes inert on every pad (see MB-029).

**Evidence.** controller_state_codec.cpp:157-162 `for (const auto& slot : kLateSlots) { snap.sound[slot.snapIndex] = readParam(ctrl, ...); }` with :70-71 `{.offset = kPadBodyDampingB1, .snapIndex = 42}, {.offset = kPadBodyDampingB3, .snapIndex = 43}`; controller.cpp:227-228 defaultValue 0.5; pad_config.h:282-283 `bodyDampingB1 = -1.0f; bodyDampingB3 = -1.0f;`; state_codec.cpp:216-221. T60 numbers from a node evaluation of `dampingLawFromLegacy` / `dampingLawFromParams` (membrane_mapper.h:64-80, modal_resonator_bank.h:133-139, decayRate = b1 + b3·f²): tom 1.115 -> 0.239 s; kick 1.483 -> 0.245 s.

**Suggested fix.** Give the controller a representable "auto" state for B1/B3: either a per-pad bool "Damping Override" param, or mirror the processor's per-pad sentinel set by every load path. `buildPadSnapshotFromParams` must then write -1 for auto pads. Test: processor default kit -> getState bytes A; controller `setComponentState(A)` -> `kitPresetStateProvider` -> blob -> processor setState -> getState bytes B. Assert sound[42] and sound[43] for pads 0, 5 and 7 are -1 in B, and A == B byte for byte.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute: kit save (controller_state.cpp:105-118 -> `buildSnapshot`, controller_state_codec.cpp:358-362) and pad save (controller_state.cpp:196-215) both go through `buildPadSnapshotFromParams`, which writes the late slots from `getParamNormalized` (:159-163) and can never write -1; the processor's `toPadSnapshot` keeps the sentinel (state_codec.cpp:124-125) and `applyPadSnapshot` treats only negatives as sentinel (:213-222). Re-derived the after-save T60s (tom 0.239 s, kick 0.245 s); did not re-derive the "before" values.
- Confirmed: browser providers are wired at controller.cpp:739-741 / :759-761; reload gives b1 = 25.1 s⁻¹ (membrane_mapper.h:71-74), capping fundamental T60 at about 0.275 s. docs/tom-depth-implementation-plan.md:167 and :413 call the tom sentinel load-bearing; the kick sets neither B1 nor B3. The retune notes' "sentinel can't survive the param system" (06-orchestralKit-fix-plan.md:71, 12-latinPercKit.md:109) concern the offline generator, not the browser save. Tests only cover the load direction (test_kit_browser_load.cpp:210-211, test_pad_preset.cpp:554-555).
- Confirmed: hand-derived the default pad (b1 about 3.35 -> 25.1 s⁻¹ plus about 12.5 s⁻¹ of b3 term at 158 Hz, roughly 10x shorter) and the tom (legacy b1 about 2.45 s⁻¹). Generator-built factory presets are not affected; any user kit or pad preset saved from the browser is. High severity justified.

#### MB-038 — Voices with the Feedback exciter never retire: the slow path never flushes silent modes, so getNumActiveModes() never reaches 0

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-management · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1002-1062, 644-669](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1002-L1062)

**Problem.** `processBlockSlow` drives the body per sample with `processSampleNoSmooth` (1030, via membrane_body.h:54-58 -> modal_resonator_bank.h:399-412). That path never calls `flushSilentModes()`; only `processBlock` does (modal_resonator_bank.h:446, 457). `numActiveModes_` therefore stays at the count `setModes` gave at note-on. `bankSilent` (645) is never true, so neither the normal retirement (647) nor the 256-block safety net (660-665) can fire. `active_` stays true forever, even after note-off, once the body is digitally silent.

**Why wrong.** Retirement is defined as bank silent plus envelope finished (drum_voice.h:631-651), and the comment at 633-634 assumes `flushSilentModes` runs "inside ModalResonatorBank::processBlock". The Feedback route never goes through `processBlock`, so it violates that contract and becomes an immortal voice (the CPU-leak hazard).

**Consequence.** Every Feedback-exciter hit holds its pool slot forever. voice_pool.cpp:469-519 renders it every block on the most expensive per-sample path and calls `noteOff()` on it every quiet block (508-512). It frees the slot only when `isActive()` is false (514-519), which never happens. After a few Feedback hits the polyphony is full of silent zombies: every new note steals, the CPU stays at the full per-voice slow-path cost, `getActiveVoiceCount` and the meters show phantom voices, and the processor's silence flags are never set. Factory kits use Feedback on several pads (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1408, 1579, 3465, 3586, 3695, 6054, 6256, 6292, 6388).

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:1030 `const float bodyOut = body.processSampleNoSmooth(sharedBank, exc);` with no flush anywhere in 933-1084; modal_resonator_bank.h:399-412 (no flush) vs :446 `flushSilentModes();`. Probe vo_probe.cpp A (noteOff at 0.1 s, 512-sample blocks, 30 s): "Feedback body=Membrane: retiredAt=never active=1 bankActiveModes=44 energy=0 lastBlockPeak=0"; "body=Plate: bankActiveModes=48 energy=0, active". Control (Impulse/Membrane, same schedule): retired at 0.383 s.

**Suggested fix.** After the per-sample loop in `processBlockSlow`, call `sharedBank.flushSilentModes()`, and `secondaryBank_.flushSilentModes()` when the secondary bank is active (both are public). Test: Feedback x {Membrane, Plate} voice, noteOn, noteOff at 100 ms, render 5 s in 512-sample blocks, then `REQUIRE(!voice.isActive())`. Add the same check at VoicePool level: `getActiveVoiceCount()==0` and `isAnyVoiceActive()==false`.

**Verifier notes**
- Defect holds: the slow path is chosen exactly for `ExciterType::Feedback` (drum_voice.h:610-624); `numActiveModes_` only decreases in `flushSilentModes` (modal_resonator_bank.h:471) and is otherwise recounted from amplitude/Nyquist in `computeModeCoefficients` (760, 841), so a retune cannot reach 0 either. String (waveguide) may be unaffected; every modal body is. The quoted vo_probe.cpp was not found on disk; the verdict rests on the source trace. No test checks Feedback retirement (test_feedback_exciter.cpp:118 checks only the exciter's `isActive`).
- Confirmed: `prepareBlockSmoothing()` (1002) is only `smoothCoefficients()` (modal_resonator_bank.h:386-389); all modal body wrappers forward to `processSampleNoSmooth`, which returns after `applyOutputStage` without flushing; no other `flushSilentModes` caller exists in plugins/membrum/src. Intended sustain cases are modeInject and Friction, not Feedback; test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp only checks `isActive()` fresh and after noteOn (258, 293).
- Confirmed (wrappers: membrane_body.h:54-57, plate_body.h:51-54, shell_body.h:47-50, bell_body.h:47-50, noise_body.h:91-94; `flushSilentModes` appears in plugins/membrum only in comments at drum_voice.h:449, 633, 1089). Audible damage is small because a zombie is silent and Oldest/Quietest stealing mostly displaces zombies; the cost is CPU (up to 16 voices x 44-48 modes per sample), phantom meters and a pool that never reports idle.

#### MB-042 — Tone-shaper SVF glides its cutoff and filter type over 5 ms from the slot's previous note: the attack of a filtered pad depends on voice-slot history

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** layers-shaper · **Dimension:** layers-shaper

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:79-83, 348-353, 134-156](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h#L79-L83)

**Problem.** `prepare()` enables SVF smoothing (5 ms, svf.h:153). `setFilterCutoff` and `setFilterType` then only set targets (svf.h:188-194 and 204-211), and they are called at every noteOn through `applyPadConfigToVoice`. `ToneShaper::noteOn` calls `filter_.resetIntegrators()` only, not `snapToTarget()` or `reset()`, so g, k and the LP/HP/BP mix coefficients start from whatever the previous note on that voice slot left. On a fresh slot that is the `prepare()` state, a 20 kHz lowpass. The comment at 329-331 notes the `snapToTarget()` recommendation and skips it.

**Why wrong.** A drum hit must render the same regardless of which pad last used the voice slot; voice allocation is invisible to the user. The noteOn comment's own goal is to wipe per-note state from the previous voice on the slot, and the coefficient smoother is part of that state.

**Consequence.** The first ~5-15 ms of every filtered pad varies by about 8 dB with allocation history. A fresh slot leaks the strike transient unfiltered through a 20 kHz LP, and after a different pad the attack crossfades from that pad's filter type. Flams and rolls hit unevenly, and HP/BP pads leak their attack: an HP at 14 kHz and one at 19.8 kHz measure identically at -36.3 dBFS RMS, dominated by the LP-to-HP glide.

**Evidence.** Probe test 4 (LP 300 Hz, click on, 0-5 ms): fresh slot peak 0.2863 / RMS 0.16555; same pad second hit 0.2118 / 0.13612; LP pad after an HP pad 0.1527 / 0.06635. Control 4b with the filter bypassed: 0.2856/0.16558 vs 0.2819/0.16429. Test 8: HP norm 0.95 (14159 Hz) RMS 0.015280, norm 0.999 (19862 Hz) RMS 0.015281. Code: tone_shaper.h:348 `filter_.resetIntegrators();` with no snap; :83 `filter_.enableSmoothing(true);`.

**Suggested fix.** In `ToneShaper::noteOn`, after resetting the filter envelope, set the first cutoff target (`filterCutoffHz_ * exp2(3*amt*env0)`) and call `filter_.snapToTarget()`, or `filter_.reset()`, which also zeroes the integrators. Test: an LP 300 Hz pad rendered on a fresh voice, after an HP pad on the same voice, and as a repeat hit must give the same 0-5 ms peak and RMS within 0.5 dB. A bypassed-filter control shows the rest of the voice is already repeatable.

**Verifier notes**
- Holds: `setMode` calls `computeMixTargets()` so the m0/m1/m2 mix is smoothed too (svf.h:188-195), advanced per sample (svf.h:365-368, 521-525); setters run at note-on via pad_config_apply.h:78-85; the first-sample forced update (tone_shaper.h:449-455) also only sets a target. `ToneShaper::reset()` (which snaps) is reached only from `DrumVoice::resetForKitSwitch` (drum_voice.h:477). A bypassed pad (tone_shaper.h:427-429) never advances the smoother, so stale coefficients persist. Probe numbers fit the mechanism (about 8 dB spread in the first 5 ms).
- Confirmed and not intended: `resetIntegrators` deliberately leaves g/k/m* alone (svf.h:289-298), a rationale that applies within one voice, not across unrelated pads; Membrum's own exciters snap their SVFs on trigger (noise_burst_exciter.h:61/107, clap_exciter.h:65/115, feedback_exciter.h:56/118, friction_exciter.h:50/88). No membrum test references this behaviour. Probe not rerun.
- Confirmed: smoothCoeff = 1-exp(-1/(0.005·sr)) (svf.h:529-536), about 95 % settled after 15 ms; `prepare()` snaps to a 20 kHz LP (tone_shaper.h:489, svf.h:169-175). tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp has 180 FilterCutoff/tsFilter references, so factory kits use the filter widely. Fresh-slot LP hit equals the bypassed control (attack effectively unfiltered); after an HP pad -7.9 dB; settled repeat -1.7 dB.

#### MB-043 — noiseLayerGain has no parameter and is lost on every controller-side preset save: the default-kit snare wire drops by 36 dB

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** layers-shaper · **Dimension:** layers-shaper · **Also flagged by:** gain-staging-master

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp:91, 116-181](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp#L91)

**Problem.** The per-pad noise-layer gain multiplier (`PadConfig::noiseLayerGain`, sound slot 57; applied at drum_voice.h:549/861/1051) has no ParamID, so the editor cannot show or edit it. `buildPadSnapshotFromParams` never writes sound[57] (kLateSlots skips it, comment at :91), so it stays at the value-initialised 0.0 (state_codec.h:60, 100). On load, `State::applyPadSnapshot` and `applyPadPresetSnapshot` clamp it to [0.1, 16] (state_codec.cpp:243, 326). Kit and pad presets saved from the browser therefore reload every pad at 0.1. The default kit and the generator depend on values above 1 (default_kit.h:120 snare 6.2, :262 3.5, :336 2.2). This confirms extra-focus lead 1 for the noise layer and measures its audible effect.

**Why wrong.** A kit or pad preset saved by the user must reload with the same sound as the host state (getState writes slot 57 from PadConfig, state_codec.cpp:147). A field that the save path cannot represent is data loss.

**Consequence.** Saving the default kit (or any factory kit) as a user preset and reloading it removes the snare wires, the cymbal wash and part of every pad's noise layer. A default pad (gain 1.0) loses 20 dB of noise layer.

**Evidence.** Probe test 12 (default kit, 500 ms, block 256, noise part = render minus mix-0 render): pad 2 snare gain 6.20 -> 0.1: noise part -33.6 -> -69.4 dBFS (total -26.4 -> -27.3); pad 13 crash gain 3.50: -34.3 -> -65.3 dBFS; pad 0 kick gain 1.00: -44.4 -> -64.4 dBFS. Code: controller_state_codec.cpp:91 `// Wire coupling (sound[58] -> offset 65). snapIndex 57 = noiseLayerGain.` (no entry); state_codec.cpp:243 `cfg.noiseLayerGain = std::clamp(static_cast<float>(snap.sound[57]), 0.1f, 16.0f);`.

**Suggested fix.** Give the controller a per-pad copy of noiseLayerGain, either as a hidden per-pad parameter or as controller-side state filled by setComponentState and by the kit/pad load providers, and write it into sound[57] in `buildPadSnapshotFromParams`. Better still, drive every route from one slot table (lead 3). Test: kit-preset save, then load into a Processor, then getState must be byte-identical to the processor's getState before the save; the same for a pad preset.

**Verifier notes**
- Traced end to end: providers at controller.cpp:739-741 / :759-761; kLateSlots (:58-93) jumps from snapIndex 56 to 58; `std::array<double,59> sound{}` (state_codec.h:60, :100) saves 0.0; load clamps to 0.1 (state_codec.cpp:243, :326) while host getState keeps the real value (:147). Gain is live in audio (pad_config.h:261, pad_config_apply.h:46, drum_voice.h:549/861/1051). Measured drops match the arithmetic (6.2 -> 0.1 = 35.8 dB; 1.0 -> 0.1 = 20 dB). Existing tests build the blob with sound[57] already set, so only the load side is covered.
- Confirmed; probe not rerun. No mitigation: the lead-2 re-apply carries ParamIDs only and noiseLayerGain has none; controller_state.cpp:146-149 / :243-246 cover only the load direction. PLAN-wire-coupling-2026-07-13.md:142 ("state-only, no param") records the no-ParamID decision, not acceptance of losing the value on save. test_kit_uimode_roundtrip.cpp uses `kitPresetStateProvider` but goes controller to controller.
- Confirmed by the audit's own lane (specs/membrum-audit/probes/probe-results.txt): getState -> setComponentState -> kitPresetStateProvider -> setState -> getState is not byte-identical in any kit; slot 57 differs on all 32 pads (lines 408, 414, 420); default-kit snare energy above 3 kHz -7.84 -> -42.35 dB (line 422), Acoustic Studio snare -12.83 -> -48.37 dB (line 410), 808 snare at gain 1.0 -23.13 -> -42.35 dB (line 416), crash RMS -31.61 -> -34.16 dB (line 413); the pad-preset path loses it the same way (line 426). The "every pad loses 20 dB" claim is true for the field but barely audible on pads with a low noise mix.

#### MB-049 — Quietest stealing drops simultaneous hits: a voice triggered earlier in the same block has currentLevel 0, so the next note-on steals it

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-management · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Also flagged by:** gestalt-processor

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:158-179, 252-257, 848-872](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L158-L179)

**Problem.** In Quietest mode with a full pool, noteOn picks a victim with `selectQuietestActiveSlot()` before the allocator runs (158-179). A new voice's `meta_.currentLevel` is set to 0 at note-on (256) and updated only after the voice renders a block (375/486), so it always counts as the quietest. When several notes arrive in one block (any chord, made more likely because sampleOffset is ignored), each later note steals the voice the previous note in the same block just started. The pre-steal also runs before the allocator checks for a same-note retrigger (196, voice_allocator.h:239-243): retriggering a ringing pad kills an unrelated voice and then retriggers the pad on its own slot anyway. When `selectQuietestActiveSlot` returns -1, the allocation mode is not updated, so the allocator steals using whatever mode was set last.

**Why wrong.** FR-122 asks for the quietest sounding voice to be stolen. A voice that has not rendered a sample has no measured level and is the most recent hit, not the quietest one. A retrigger needs no new slot (the allocator reuses the pad's own slot), so stealing another voice for it is never needed.

**Consequence.** Measured with a probe driving VoicePool directly (maxPoly 4, Quietest, 48 kHz, 512-sample blocks, four cymbals ringing): after kick+snare+hat in one block only the hat is left; the kick and snare were each faded out from their first sample. In a second probe a snare retrigger with a full pool killed the ringing ride (51) and dropped the active count from 4 to 3. In a busy groove this loses downbeats and cuts cymbals for no reason.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:158-159 `const bool poolFull = std::cmp_greater_equal(allocator_.getActiveVoiceCount(), maxPolyphony_);`; :161-179 Quietest pre-steal before `allocator_.noteOn` at :196; :256 `meta_[slot].currentLevel = 0.0f;`; :862-864 picks the lowest level. Probe (scratchpad vp_probe/probe.cpp) S1: before `s0:A/n49 s1:A/n51 s2:A/n57 s3:A/n59`, after kick+snare+hat in one block `s0:A/n49 s1:A/n42 s2:A/n57 s3:A/n59` (36 and 38 gone). S2: after the snare retrigger `alloc=3 metaActive=3 ... s1:F/n51` (the ride was killed).

**Suggested fix.** Give a just-allocated voice a level of +infinity-equivalent (FLT_MAX), or exclude slots whose `noteOnSampleCount == sampleCounter_` from `selectQuietestActiveSlot`. Run the Quietest pre-steal only when the allocator would actually steal: skip it if the note is already playing (allocator `getVoiceNote` or meta `originatingNote`) or an idle slot exists. Always set an allocation mode. Tests: (a) maxPoly 4 full, three note-ons in one block, then all three new notes are Active; (b) full pool plus a retrigger of a ringing pad, then the active count is unchanged and no other slot is FastReleasing.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute either mechanism: the victim gets `beginFastRelease` (:171) so its first sample is already inside the 5 ms fade; the processor does not split blocks at note sampleOffset (sampleOffset appears only in the parameter queue, processor.cpp:164-165); `VoiceAllocator::retriggerNote` (voice_allocator.h:843-869) reuses the note's own slot, so the pre-steal victim dies for nothing. Tests miss it: test_voice_pool_stealing_policies.cpp:142-195 renders 16 blocks before one stealer, :197-217 sends one extra note-on. Default policy is Oldest (voice_pool.h:361), so only Quietest users are hit; high kept. Probe not rerun.
- Could not refute: `Processor::processEvents` (processor.cpp:565-598) calls `voicePool_.noteOn` for every event before the single processBlock (620-666). Spec 138 FR-122 (spec.md:170) and acceptance scenario 2 (spec.md:77) require stealing the voice with the lowest instantaneous amp-envelope level; MANUAL.md:415 sells Quietest as protecting long tails, which this defeats. Prior findings.json (line 692) mentions the level-0 re-targeting only in passing.
- Confirmed: voices below 1e-3 are already auto-released (:380-384), so the level-0 just-started voice is always the victim; a stolen just-started voice is snapshotted into the shadow slot before it renders, so only ~5 ms of its attack is heard (a kick in a chord becomes a tick). The tiebreak test at :197-217 actually requires the level-0 tie. At 512-sample blocks (~10.7 ms) any flam or chord falls into one block; maxPolyphony 4-8 is in the intended range.

#### MB-050 — Allocator slots leak when a voice finishes before its MIDI note-off; with Quietest, polyphony collapses to one voice

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-management · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Also flagged by:** voice-management-midi, spec-conformance, gestalt-processor

**Corroborated by measurement:** probe `lifecycle:note-off shortens hits`: "kick 0.97->0.10 s, snare 0.16->0.09, tom 0.06 vs 1.54 s, crash 1.85->0.20 s". Quality `noteoff:truncation`: "180 of 185 / 0.21". voice_pool.cpp:296 `VP_VOICES[slot].noteOff();`; drum_voice.h:446 `ampEnvelope_.gate(false);` and :451 `bodyBank_.getSharedBank().damp(kNoteOffDampScale);`.

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:283-300, 386-396, 514-519](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L283-L300)

**Problem.** When `DrumVoice::isActive()` turns false while meta is Active, processBlock calls `allocator_.voiceFinished(slot)` without calling `allocator_.noteOff` first. The allocator ignores `voiceFinished` for any slot that is not Releasing (voice_allocator.h:288-293). If the MIDI note-off has not arrived yet (a held note, or a note longer than the pad's ring), the allocator slot stays Active. The later note-off skips the voice because meta is already Free (293-294) and moves the allocator slot to Releasing (299). Nothing ever calls `voiceFinished` for it again, so `allocator_.getActiveVoiceCount()` stays inflated. Self-triggered auto-release (380-384) never informs the allocator either.

**Why wrong.** The pool's own comments (1048-1053) say the allocator must be noteOff'd before `voiceFinished`, otherwise "the allocator would still believe the slot is Active". The choke and Quietest paths do this (172-173, 1056-1057), but the natural-finish path does not. `poolFull` (158) then reports a full pool while no voice is sounding.

**Consequence.** Probe: maxPoly 4, held notes on pads 42/44/37/39 that finished after 448-2848 ms, then late note-offs. Result: `alloc=4 metaActive=0`, every allocator slot stuck at Releasing. With Quietest from then on, each new hit kills the only real voice: crash hit, then the kick killed the crash, then the snare killed the kick (1 active voice at maxPoly 4). With Oldest/Priority the leaked Releasing slots are recycled through the Steal path (forced `beginFastRelease` plus a 219 KiB swap per note). Pads hit with long notes (a 1/4 note at 120 bpm = 500 ms is longer than the measured 448 ms clap and 565 ms closed-hat lifetimes), audition holds and held e-drum notes all trigger it.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:386-396 `meta_[slot].state = VoiceSlotState::Free; ... allocator_.voiceFinished(static_cast<std::size_t>(slot));` (no allocator noteOff); :514-519 same; voice_allocator.h:288-293 `if (state != VoiceState::Releasing) return;`; voice_pool.cpp:293-299 noteOff skips Free metas, then `allocator_.noteOff(midiNote)`. Probe S3: `[after 4 finished+late-noteoff] alloc=4 metaActive=0 : s0:F/n42/alloc2 ...`; `[kick hit] alloc=4 metaActive=1 : s0:A/n36`; `[snare hit] alloc=4 metaActive=1 : s0:A/n38`.

**Suggested fix.** On natural finish (both overloads) call `(void)allocator_.noteOff(meta_[slot].originatingNote)` before `voiceFinished`, restricted to that slot (or add an allocator API that idles one slot). Do the same when auto-release fires. Test: hold a short pad until meta Free, send the late note-off, and assert `allocator.getActiveVoiceCount()==0`. Then with Quietest and maxPoly 4, play 4 overlapping notes and assert all 4 are Active.

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed from source: auto-release (380-384, 508-512) only calls the voice's own noteOff; natural finish (386-396, 514-519) calls `voiceFinished` on a slot the allocator still holds Active, so `activeVoiceCount_` is not decremented (voice_allocator.h:301 never reached); after the late note-off moves it to Releasing (voice_allocator.h:258-268) the only `voiceFinished` callers (173, 395, 518, 1057) never revisit it. `selectQuietestActiveSlot` (848-872) sees only meta-Active slots, so the one real voice is the victim (findIdleVoice, voice_allocator.h:922-935, 539-614). Ordinary DAW input with long notes triggers it; high kept.
- Confirmed: the processor forwards every note-off for pitches 36..67 (processor.cpp:551, 580, 592), so a note held past the ring reaches this path in a real host.
