With Oldest/Priority, `findStealVictimSingle` (voice_allocator.h:630-636) prefers Releasing slots, so leaked slots are recycled through a Steal (forced `beginFastRelease`, voice_pool.cpp:221): wasteful but mostly inaudible. The intended pattern (noteOff then voiceFinished, 1048-1057, 172-173) is skipped only here.
- Confirmed, but this verifier argued for medium: Quietest is not the default (voice_pool.h:361) though 2 of 20 factory kits select it (modularWestCoastKit, generator:3733-3734, maxPoly 12; droneSustainKit, 6220-6221, maxPoly 8); collapse needs maxPoly-1 distinct pads whose note-off arrived after retirement (the leak grows with distinct pads, since a leaked slot is reused on its own pad's retrigger, voice_allocator.h:830-869); typical 1/16 DAW notes and e-drum modules send the note-off before the ring ends. `setMaxPolyphony` (578-587) only trims slots above the new count; the leak persists until reset or kit switch (279-280). The recorded final severity stays high.

#### MB-051 — Note events ignore sampleOffset: every hit starts at the block start, so timing and flams depend on the host buffer size

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** midi-timing · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi

**Corroborated by measurement:** probe `timing:sampleOffset`: "1 / 0 / -99 / -510" (first non-zero sample minus offset, for offsets 0/1/100/511). `timing:block-size invariance`: "bs64 -20.9 dBFS, bs512 -9.8, bs2048 -8.8, bs16384 -10.0; onsets quantised to block start". processor.cpp:583-584 `voicePool_.noteOn(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(pitch), event.noteOn.velocity);` with no offset.

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:559-599, 601-622](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L559-L599)

**Problem.** `processEvents` never reads `Event::sampleOffset`, and `VoicePool::noteOn`/`noteOff` take no offset (voice_pool.h:113-118). All events are applied before the single `VoicePool::processBlock` call for the whole block, so every note in a block starts at sample 0. Two consequences follow. A same-pad hit pair in one block becomes allocator retrigger, then Steal (forced 5 ms fade from sample 0), then NoteOn, so both attacks overlap at sample 0. A note-on plus note-off of the same pad in one block gates and damps the voice before its first sample. `process()` also returns at `numSamples == 0` before `processEvents` (613-614), so events sent in a zero-length flush block are dropped.

**Why wrong.** VST3 events carry sampleOffset so that an instrument starts each note at that sample. A drum machine has to be sample-accurate: flams and rolls only exist in the gaps between hits. The task's timing hazards list exactly this. No test passes a non-zero offset, as the specs-and-tests map noted.

**Consequence.** Timing error up to one block (512 samples = 10.7 ms, 1024 = 21 ms at 48 kHz). Grooves are quantised to the buffer grid and jitter differently at each buffer size, and offline renders change with the host block size. A 20 ms flam collapses into one doubled attack whenever both hits fall in one block. A note-off in the same block as its note-on (short MIDI notes) mutes the hit at its onset.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:573-585 `case Event::kNoteOnEvent: ... voicePool_.noteOn(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(pitch), event.noteOn.velocity);` (no sampleOffset); :613-614 `if (data.numSamples == 0) return kResultOk;` runs before :621 `processEvents(data.inputEvents);`; :636 / :663 one processBlock per host block; voice_pool.cpp:128 `void VoicePool::noteOn(std::uint8_t midiNote, float velocity)`; voice_allocator.h:239-243 same-note retrigger emits Steal+NoteOn on the same slot.

**Suggested fix.** Split the render at event boundaries: iterate events by sampleOffset and render `VoicePool::processBlock` from the current position to each event's offset, applying the event in between (main and aux pointers advanced by the offset). Also process events when `numSamples == 0`. Test: a note-on at sampleOffset 300 in a 512 block puts the first non-zero output sample at index >= 300; rendering the same MIDI at block sizes 64 and 1024 gives onset times that match within 1 sample.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute: sampleOffset is read only at processor.cpp:164-165 (parameter queues); voice_pool.h:113/118 have no offset and both processBlock overloads (:126, :133) render the whole block. The voice_pool.h:115-117 "bookkeeping only" comment is stale: `VoicePool::noteOff` (voice_pool.cpp:283-299) gates the amp envelope and fires `damp()`, so same-block note-on/off does mute the hit. Only non-zero offset in tests is a noteOff at kBlockSize/2 (test_editor_asan_lifecycle.cpp:210).
- Confirmed; specs/138 FR-152 covers only parameter sample-accuracy, and nothing documents block-start event quantisation as a design decision. Correction: a few tests do pass a non-zero offset (test_editor_asan_lifecycle.cpp:210; test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:182/744 helpers), but none asserts onset timing.
- Confirmed: a same-pad pair in one block goes retrigger -> Steal -> `beginFastRelease(force=true)` -> NoteOn on the same slot (voice_pool.cpp:203-233), so the first hit survives only as a 5 ms tail. Overstated detail: a 20 ms flam collapses only at blocks of 1024+ samples at 48 kHz; at 512 only flams under ~10.7 ms do. Zero-length blocks with note events are rare in hosts. High kept.

#### MB-052 — Auto-release uses a per-host-block peak, so voice length depends on buffer size; at 1-16 sample blocks hits are killed at onset

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-management · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi · **Also flagged by:** gain-staging-master

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:350, 367-384, 478-512](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L350)

**Problem.** After rendering each host block, the pool calls `DrumVoice::noteOff()` if the block's absolute peak is below 1e-3. With small blocks this fires at a zero crossing of a still-loud low tone. It also fires on the first block of a hit, because the amp envelope restarts from 0 (drum_voice.h:435) with a 0.5 ms attack. It repeats on every quiet block, compounding `damp(0.997)`. The decision is block-size dependent by construction. The peak is taken after level_ (prior audit L-11, still open) and before pan.

**Why wrong.** A voice's lifetime must not depend on how the host partitions the buffer. A silence detector needs a window in samples (or an envelope follower), not one host block, and must not fire before the attack has run.

**Consequence.** Probe, held tom 45 (no note-off), 48 kHz. At velocity 0.25: bs=1 retires at 16 ms (0-50 ms RMS -62.4 vs -35.8 dBFS at bs=512, so the hit is nearly silent); bs=16 retires at 396 ms (300-600 ms -77.7 vs -52.4); bs=32 at 583 ms; bs=512 at 928 ms. At velocity 0.8: bs=16 retires at 760 ms vs 1397 ms at 512, and bs=1 at 15 ms. Low-latency e-drum setups (16-32 sample buffers) and hosts that split blocks at events get shorter, darker tails, and offline renders depend on block size.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:350 `constexpr float kSilenceThreshold = 1.0e-3f;`; :380-384 `if (peak < kSilenceThreshold && meta_[slot].state == VoiceSlotState::Active) { VP_VOICES[slot].noteOff(); }`; :508-512 same in the multi-bus overload. Probe S5 table: `bs=1 0-50ms -62.4 ... retired@16 ms`, `bs=16 ... 300-600 -77.7 retired@396 ms`, `bs=512 ... 300-600 -52.4 600-1000 -68.4 retired@928 ms`; at velocity 0.8 `bs=16 retired@760 ms` vs `bs=512 retired@1397 ms`.

**Suggested fix.** Replace the per-block test with a per-voice peak-hold or one-pole envelope follower over a fixed time window (for example a 20-50 ms hold), armed only after an onset grace period (for example 10 ms after noteOn). Fire noteOff at most once. Ideally key it on the pre-level signal (closes L-11). Test: render the same held hit at bs 1, 16, 64 and 512 and assert equal retirement time within one window and tail RMS within 1 dB.

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed: the peak window is exactly `numSamples` (clamped only to `maxBlockSize_`, :317); no grace period, hold window or "already released" latch; meta stays Active until `!isActive()` (386-396), so noteOff and `damp()` (modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516, which scales `radius_` and `radiusTarget_` in place) repeat every quiet block. A 16-sample window centred on a zero crossing of a 100 Hz tom reads about 0.10·A, so release can start ~20 dB early. No block-size invariance test exists. Probe not rerun; mechanism and direction of the numbers fully supported.
- Confirmed: processor.cpp:636 / :663 pass the host block straight through with no fixed internal subdivision; at bs=1 the auto-noteOff is guaranteed to fire almost at once on a low mode's zero crossing. The 331-349 comment explains only the threshold value and the infinite-ring fix, not block size; only test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp touches the threshold, with fixed blocks.
- Confirmed: noteOff damp calls run at the block rate (about 3000/s at bs=16 vs about 94/s at bs=512), so post-noteOff decay depends on block size; at sub-24-sample first blocks noteOff fires during the 0.5 ms attack (drum_voice.h:159) and the 300 ms release (:162) starts from a tiny level (-62 dBFS at bs=1). Effect small at 256-512 buffers, audible at 16-64. High kept.

#### MB-067 — setupProcessing re-prepares the coupling engine and leaves its amount at 0: Global Coupling goes silent after a sample-rate change, an offline bounce or a project reload

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** coupling · **Dimension:** coupling

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:1080-1084](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L1080-L1084), with [dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h:113-132, 152-160, 312-322, 370-372](dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h#L113-L132)

**Problem.** `Processor::setupProcessing` calls `couplingEngine_.prepare(sampleRate_)` and never calls `couplingEngine_.setAmount(globalCoupling_)` again. `SympatheticResonance::prepare` runs `amountSmoother_.snapTo(0.0f)`, which sets both current and target to 0, but leaves `couplingGain_` at its old non-zero value. From then on `process()` scales the input by `amountSmoother_.process()`, which stays at the 0 target. `isBypassed()` also stays false, because `couplingGain_ != 0`. The coupling engine contributes nothing until the Global Coupling parameter is written again, by a parameter change or a kit load.

**Why wrong.** Engine contract (sympathetic_resonance.h:110-111): "prepare... Must be called before process()". The amount is set separately through `setAmount` (:152-160), and prepare silently drops it. Every VST3 host calls setupProcessing again on a sample-rate change and before an offline render (processMode kOffline). Many hosts also call setState before setupProcessing on project load. The stored `globalCoupling_` atomic (processor.h:148), which getState saves, no longer matches what the engine does.

**Consequence.** 13 or more of the 20 factory kits set globalCoupling between 0.18 and 0.85 (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1661, 2283, 2516, 2911, 3735, 4243, ...). In those kits the sympathetic resonance disappears after a host sample-rate change, in an offline export (which then sounds different from realtime playback), and after a project reload whenever the host calls setState before setupProcessing. The knob still shows the value. Because `isBypassed()` is false, the per-sample coupling loop still runs over all 64 resonators every block for zero output, and the main bus never reports silence (processor.cpp:739-741).

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:1081 `couplingEngine_.prepare(sampleRate_);` with no setAmount afterwards (1080-1090). The only setAmount calls are processor.cpp:408 (param kGlobalCouplingId) and :978 (applyKitSnapshot). sympathetic_resonance.h:124-125 `amountSmoother_.configure(5.0f, sampleRate_); amountSmoother_.snapTo(0.0f);`, and prepare never assigns `couplingGain_`. :319-322 `float smoothedAmount = amountSmoother_.process(); float scaledInput = input * smoothedAmount;`. :371 `return amountSmoother_.getCurrentValue() == 0.0f && couplingGain_ == 0.0f;`. smoother.h:261-270 `snapTo` sets `current_ = target_ = value`. The test at test_coupling_phase9_verification.cpp:294 checks only `CHECK(peak > 0.0f)`, which the dry kick already satisfies. Static reading only; no probe was run.

**Suggested fix.** After `couplingEngine_.prepare(sampleRate_)` in setupProcessing, re-apply `couplingEngine_.setAmount(globalCoupling_.load())`. Also fix the shared engine so `prepare()` keeps the configured amount: retarget the smoother to `couplingGain_` instead of 0, or reset `couplingGain_` together with it. Innexus also consumes this engine, so gate its suites too. Regression test (processor level): set kGlobalCouplingId = 1, then setActive(false), setupProcessing(96 kHz), setActive(true), play a kick and a tom, and compare against a coupling-0 render: the RMS difference must exceed a threshold. Run the same case in the order setState(kit with coupling 0.5) -> setupProcessing -> process. The existing T061 test (test_coupling_phase9_verification.cpp:213-326) checks only peak > 0 of the dry kick, so it cannot catch this.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute: setActive (processor.cpp:1093-1127) never touches the engine; `reset()` (sympathetic_resonance.h:135-140) clears both values but `prepare()` does not; `OnePoleSmoother::process()` (smoother.h:195-200) returns 0 every sample after the snap. setState-before-setupProcessing: `applyKitSnapshot` sets the amount, then the re-prepare snaps it to 0. getState (processor.cpp:885) still reports the old amount.
- Confirmed: a sample-rate change (setActive false -> setupProcessing -> setActive true) wipes the amount in every host; T061 sets coupling = 1, changes the rate and asserts only peak > 0 (:294, :325). FR-006 (test comment :204-209) requires the re-prepare to work after a rate change; nothing documents the loss as intended.
- Confirmed, but this verifier argued for medium: `Processor::setState` calls `applyKitSnapshot` directly (905-915); the controller's setComponentState sends no performEdit, so nothing restores the amount until the knob moves or a kit loads; the generator sets non-zero globalCoupling in 15 places, and voice_pool.cpp:243-247 keeps registering resonators, so the wasted CPU is real. The lost layer is subtle: `setAmount` maps 0..1 to a -46..-26 dB send (:156-157) and the energy limiter caps it at -20 dBFS. The recorded final severity stays high.

#### MB-071 — Simple-view macro knobs and the Coupling Amount knob always edit pad 1, whichever pad is selected

**Severity:** high (filed as critical; downgraded on verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** param-plumbing · **Dimension:** param-plumbing-macros · **Also flagged by:** parameter-audibility, duplication-drift, parallel-paths

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/resources/editor.uidesc:39-43, 93, 137-145, 241](plugins/membrum/resources/editor.uidesc#L39-L43)

**Problem.** The five macro ArcKnobs (Tightness, Brightness, Body Size, Punch, Complexity) are bound to tags 1037-1041, and the Coupling Amount knob to tag 1036. With kPadBaseId 1000 and stride 128, these are pad 0's PER-PAD parameter IDs, not selected-pad proxies. Nothing remaps them. kProxyMappings (controller.cpp:84-155) has no row for kPadCouplingAmount or any kPadMacro* offset. `Processor::processParameterChanges` (processor.cpp:173-229) decodes 1037 as padIdx 0, offset 37 and applies the macro to pad 0. No setTag, sub-controller or tag remap exists in src/ (grep). The uidesc comment at :92 ("pad 0 offset 36 = selected-pad proxy") and controller_param_format.cpp:429 ("Selected-pad proxies are the pad-0 slot") describe a mechanism that does not exist.

**Why wrong.** Spec 141 FR-020 and US1 scenarios 3-4 require the macros on the SELECTED pad, with pad 1's macros preserved when pad 2 is selected. The Material/Size/Decay knobs beside them do follow the selection through the proxies, so the panel mixes two targets.

**Consequence.** With the snare (pad 2) or any other pad selected, turning Tightness/Brightness/Body Size/Punch/Complexity rewrites the KICK's (pad 1) material/decay/size/cutoff/pitch-env/couplingAmount, and the selected pad does not change. The knobs keep showing pad 1's macro values after a pad switch. The same applies to Coupling Amount in the Advanced view. The user silently edits the wrong drum, and pad 1 accumulates the deltas.

**Evidence.** editor.uidesc:39 `<control-tag name="MacroTightness" tag="1037"/>` ... :43 `tag="1041"`; :93 `<control-tag name="CouplingAmount" tag="1036"/>`; :137 `ArcKnob control-tag="MacroTightness"`; :241 `ArcKnob control-tag="CouplingAmount"`. controller.cpp:84-155 kProxyMappings ends at kWireCouplingId with no macro or couplingAmount row. processor.cpp:217-223 `else if (padOff >= kPadMacroTightness && padOff <= kPadMacroComplexity) { voicePool_.setPadConfigField(padIdx, padOff, fValue); macroMapper_.apply(padIdx, ...)`. A grep for setTag/getTagForName in src finds nothing.

**Suggested fix.** Add global proxy IDs for the five macros and couplingAmount (new IDs below 1000, rows in kProxyMappings, and processor proxy cases that route to `selectedPadIndex_` and run `macroMapper_.apply` / `recomputeCouplingMatrix`), and bind the uidesc to those IDs. Do not swap types on existing IDs. Test: a controller and processor with selected pad 5; performEdit on the Tightness control's tag; assert that pad 5's `cfg.macroTightness` and `cfg.decay` changed and pad 0's did not. Also fix test_param_reachability_in_editor.cpp:303-310, which counts pad-0 anchored tags as reachable for every pad and so encodes the bug as intended.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute (pad_config.h:19, :25, :82, :89, :349 decode 1036-1041 as pad 0 offsets 36-41; `setParamNormalized` at controller.cpp:861-891 and `syncGlobalProxyFromPad` at :961-985 touch only kProxyMappings rows; no sub-controller in the uidesc). Downgraded critical -> high: no crash, no unsafe audio, no state corruption beyond the wrong pad's values, and the edit can be undone.
- Confirmed: `createView` (controller.cpp:1008) returns a plain `VST3Editor`, and `verifyView` (:1274-1446) only caches OutputBus, PitchEnv, Morph and ADSR views without rewriting tags. Spec 141 US1 scenarios 3-4 (spec.md:63-64) and FR-020 (:222) put the macros on the selected-pad panel; the only defences (uidesc :92 comment, test_param_reachability_in_editor.cpp:12-14 and :303-304) assume routing the controller does not implement. The suggested fix (new IDs below 1000, no type swap at existing IDs) is sound.
- Confirmed: `MacroMapper::apply` (macro_mapper.cpp:63-96) layers deltas onto pad 0's material, decay, decaySkew (:127-144), cutoff and related fields; processor.cpp:208-215 does the same for couplingAmount into `recomputeCouplingMatrix`. SC-001 (spec.md:326) says "adjust the five macros on a selected pad". Downgrade reasons: default selection is pad 0, so it shows only after selecting another pad; the incremental mapper removes exactly the delta it added when the knob returns (macro_mapper.cpp:80-84).

#### MB-072 — Host automation recorded on any selected-pad proxy replays onto whichever pad is selected at playback

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** param-plumbing · **Dimension:** param-plumbing-macros

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:267-522, 395-401](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L267-L522)

**Problem.** All 60 global proxies (Material, Size, Decay, Exciter, Body, tone shaper, noise and click, damping, pan, ...) are registered kCanAutomate (controller.cpp:281-295, 299-321, 378-381, 594-670). The editor binds every per-pad control to these proxies, so DAW automation is recorded on the proxy ID. On playback the processor writes that value to `selectedPadIndex_`, the pad selected at that moment. kSelectedPadId itself is kCanAutomate (controller.cpp:500-503), and every grid click performEdits it (controller.cpp:1056-1063), so it lands in automation and undo too. When the selection changes, `syncGlobalProxyFromPad` updates the proxies with the base setter only (controller.cpp:961-971). The host is never told that "Material" now holds a different value, so the host's lane and current value disagree with the plugin's. The per-pad parameters the proxy actually changes are also written with the base setter (controller.cpp:868-871), so the host never records or displays the real target.

**Why wrong.** A VST3 automatable parameter must have stable meaning: the same ID must not address a different DSP field depending on UI state. Inside one block, processParameterChanges processes queues in host order (processor.cpp:151-167), so a kSelectedPadId change and a proxy change in the same block apply to either pad depending on queue order.

**Consequence.** Common workflow: draw a Decay ride on the snare, then click the kick to edit it. On playback the snare's Decay automation now rewrites the kick, and the snare stays static. Automation written over several pad selections smears across pads. Re-opening a project with a different saved selection changes which drum the automation plays.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:267-268 `case kMaterialId: voicePool_.setPadConfigField(selectedPadIndex_, kPadMaterial, fValue);` and the same pattern for every proxy through :521. :395-400 `case kSelectedPadId: ... selectedPadIndex_ = std::clamp(static_cast<int>(std::lround(clamped * 31.0f)), 0, 31);`. controller.cpp:500-503 `RangeParameter(STR16("Selected Pad"), kSelectedPadId, ..., 31, ParameterInfo::kCanAutomate)`. controller.cpp:969 `EditControllerEx1::setParamNormalized(mapping.globalId, padValue);` (no performEdit).

**Suggested fix.** Mark the selected-pad proxies and kSelectedPadId kIsReadOnly or without kCanAutomate (or kIsHidden for kSelectedPadId). Have the controller performEdit the PER-PAD ID on a proxy gesture (begin, perform and end on `padParamId(selectedPadIndex_, offset)`) and drop the processor-side proxy routing, so automation is pad-stable. Keep the proxies only as UI binding targets. Test: record a proxy performEdit with pad 2 selected, change the selection to pad 1 with no further edits, then replay the recorded value through processParameterChanges; assert that pad 2's field changes and pad 1's does not.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute: editor.uidesc:29-35 binds controls to proxy IDs 100-104, 200, 201, so the host records the proxy ID; grepping src/ finds no performEdit on `padParamId(selectedPadIndex_, ...)` on this path (performEdit sites are :1060-1063, :1114, kUiModeId, view callbacks, controller_state.cpp:167 / :265). The processor comment at processor.cpp:262-265 ("In a DAW, the controller forwards these as per-pad params") is false. Prior correctness-audit.md covers only the stale grid highlight (Finding 6) and kUiModeId.
- Confirmed: the proxy pattern is deliberate (specs/139-membrum-phase4-pads research.md R2, quickstart.md:17-19) to keep the generic editor usable, but no spec, manual or prior audit addresses its automation behaviour, and the code departs from the spec: FR-091 says selection-change proxy updates are "issued one-at-a-time via performEdit/endEdit", and tasks.md T016 says a global change does "performEdit + setParamNormalized + endEdit on the corresponding per-pad param".
- Confirmed including impact: the knob gesture goes through `VST3Editor`'s standard performEdit on the proxy ID (ArcKnobs at uidesc:149-153, 231-235); FR-091 (specs/139-membrum-phase4-pads/spec.md:321) contradicts the base-setter sync. Reachable in any VST3 host with automation: record a ride with the snare selected, click the kick in read mode, and the lane writes the kick.

#### MB-073 — Macro deltas never reach the controller, so knobs show pre-macro values, the next direct edit wipes the delta, and controller-side saves drop it

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** param-plumbing · **Dimension:** param-plumbing-macros

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/macro_mapper.cpp:63-96, 127-219](plugins/membrum/src/processor/macro_mapper.cpp#L63-L96)

**Problem.** `MacroMapper::apply` runs only in the processor (processor.cpp:217-223). It adds deltas to cfg.material, decay, decaySkew, tsFilterCutoff, modeInjectAmount, size, modeStretch, tsPitchEnvStart, tsPitchEnvTime, noiseBurstDuration, couplingAmount and nonlinearCoupling. The controller is never told, so its per-pad and proxy values for those fields stay at the pre-macro values. Three failures follow:
- (a) Moving a macro and then touching, for example, the Material proxy sends the controller's pre-macro value plus the user's change, and `setPadConfigField` overwrites cfg.material absolutely (voice_pool.cpp:613). The macro delta is silently erased while the macro knob still shows its offset.
- (b) A kit-preset save (`kitPresetStateProvider`, controller_state.cpp:105-118, via `buildPadSnapshotFromParams`, controller_state_codec.cpp:117-181) stores pre-macro fields plus non-neutral macro values. On load, `applyKitSnapshot` only syncs the cache (processor.cpp:999-1002), so the macro effect is lost while the macro knobs still show it. Host getState saves the post-macro cfg, so the two save paths diverge (same family as extra-focus lead 1).
- (c) After a pad-preset load the pad keeps its macros (FR-061) but takes the preset's fields (processor.cpp:1014-1017). Returning a macro to 0.5 then subtracts a delta that was never added.

In addition, every applier clamp01s after adding the delta while the cache stores the unclamped macro (:132-134), so a sweep to an extreme and back is lossy. Example: material 0.9, Tightness 0.5 -> 1.0 adds +0.15 and clamps to 1.0; back to 0.5 subtracts 0.15 and gives 0.85.

**Why wrong.** Spec 141 SC-006 says macros at 0.5 are neutral and leave the parameters where the preset placed them. A macro is meant to be a reversible offset that both sides of the VST3 boundary agree on, and a save from either path must reproduce the sound.

**Consequence.** The audible sound, the displayed knobs and the saved preset disagree. Users lose macro tweaks when they save kits from the browser or touch a related knob. Pads drift after macro sweeps that hit a clamp.

**Evidence.** macro_mapper.cpp:132-134 `cfg.material = clamp01(cfg.material + (linDelta(m, ...) - linDelta(mOld, ...)));` and :91-95 cache = live macro. processor.cpp:1000-1002 `macroMapper_.invalidateCache(); for (...) macroMapper_.syncCacheFromCfg(p, ...)`. controller_state_codec.cpp:137-141 reads controller params for the sound slots and :174-178 reads the macros. A grep finds no macro handling in src/controller other than the tables.

**Suggested fix.** Store the macro as a pure offset applied at noteOn (base field + macro offset, never baked into cfg). This removes the cache, the order dependence, the clamp loss and the save divergence. Alternatively, make the controller compute the same deltas and performEdit the derived per-pad params. Tests: (1) macro move, then controller kit save, then processor load, then getState must equal getState before the save; (2) material 0.9, Tightness to 1 and back to 0.5, then cfg.material == 0.9; (3) macro move, then performEdit Material proxy +0.01, and the macro contribution remains.

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed; (b) is the strongest part, the clamp loss in (c) is real, and (a) is partly the intended design. No processor-to-controller report exists (only controller-to-processor messages at controller.cpp:1076/1094, controller_state.cpp:150/247). On reload, the controller's follow-up performEdits (controller_state.cpp:163-172) send the macros first (codec 210-214), the cache already matches so `apply` returns at :77, and the field writes restore pre-macro values. Clamp example verified with `kTightnessMaterialSpan = 0.30` (macro_mapper.h:101).
- Core claim (b) holds; (a) and (c) are mostly the documented design (spec 141 spec.md:35, 189 and research.md:85-100 define macros as forward-only drivers). The Phase 8G comment (controller_state_codec.cpp:197-209) assumes the snapshot carries "post-macro values", which holds for getState blobs, not controller-provider blobs. No test covers macro move -> controller save -> processor load (test_kit_uimode_roundtrip, test_pad_preset, test_coupling_state do not exercise MacroMapper). `kTightnessDecaySkewSpan = 1.0` makes the clamp loss common.
- Confirmed every consequence: spec 141 FR-102 (spec.md:308) deliberately forbids controller-side recomputation, but spec.md:35 says "editing a macro moves the underlying parameters", so the stale controller values are a real state mismatch. (a) Tightness 0.5 -> 1.0 adds 0.15 to material; the first Material touch drops it by 0.15 at once (voice_pool.cpp:613 plain assignment) while the macro knob reads 1.0. (b) For Tightness 1.0 the lost deltas are material +0.15, decay -0.25 normalized, decaySkew +0.5 (spans at macro_mapper.h:101-103).

#### MB-074 — The body-damping B1/B3 "derive" sentinel has no parameter representation: the knobs show 50% for a value never applied, and the first touch shortens decay several-fold

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** param-plumbing · **Dimension:** param-plumbing-macros

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:221-228, 620-625](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L221-L228)

**Problem.** PadConfig defaults bodyDampingB1/B3 to the -1 sentinel (pad_config.h:282-283), and DefaultKit leaves B1 at the sentinel on some templates (default_kit.h:171-174). The controller registers both per-pad params and both proxies at 0.5. The controller replay skips sentinel slots (controller_state_codec.cpp:263-268), so after setComponentState the knob keeps 0.5 while the DSP derives the law. Any touch writes an explicit override: b1 = 0.2 + n·49.8 and b3 = n·1e-3 (membrane_mapper.h:71-78). At n = 0.5 that is b1 = 25.1 s⁻¹ and b3 = 5e-4. The derived law is b1 = 1/decayTime and b3 = (1-brightness)·4e-5 (modal_resonator_bank.h:133-138, :123). For a default Membrane pad (decay 0.3, material 0.5), decayTime is about 0.30 s by the mapper formula, so b1 is about 3.3 and b3 = 2e-5. The registration comment ("b3 norm 0.5 -> 4e-5 s ... equivalent to legacy brightness=0.5") is wrong by 12.5x. No control returns a pad to "derived", and the controller kit and pad saves write the displayed 0.5 as an explicit override (lead 1).

**Why wrong.** A knob must display the value the DSP uses, and moving it by a small amount must change the sound by a small amount. A sentinel that cannot be expressed as a parameter needs an explicit mode switch (an "Auto" toggle or a reserved 0 = derive position).

**Consequence.** A 1% nudge of Body Damping b1 on an untouched pad drops the body's 1/e time from about 0.30 s to 40 ms (about 7.5x shorter). A nudge of b3 raises high-mode damping about 25x (at 1 kHz the rate goes from about 20 to 500 s⁻¹). The display claims nothing changed in between (50% -> 51%). Every controller-side save does the same to every untouched pad.

**Evidence.** controller.cpp:223 `//   b3 norm 0.5 -> 4e-5 s (Hz convention; equivalent to legacy brightness=0.5)`; :227 `{.offset = kPadBodyDampingB1, ... .defaultValue = 0.5 }`; :621-622 `RangeParameter(STR16("Body Damping b1"), kBodyDampingB1Id, nullptr, 0.0, 1.0, 0.5, ...)`. membrane_mapper.h:73 `law.b1 = 0.2f + n * 49.8f;` and :77 `law.b3 = n * 1.0e-3f;`. modal_resonator_bank.h:138 `.b1 = 1.0f / decayTime, .b3 = (1.0f - brightness) * kLegacyMaxB3`, :123 `kLegacyMaxB3 = 4.0e-5f`. controller_state_codec.cpp:267 `if (isSentinelSlot && snap.sound[slot.snapIndex] < 0.0) continue;`.

**Suggested fix.** Add a per-pad "Damping: Auto/Manual" parameter, or reserve normalized 0 as the "derive" position and remap the override over (0, 1]. Initialise the controller param from the processor's derived law when in Auto, and fix the comment. Test: a fresh processor with pad 0 at the sentinel; performEdit kBodyDampingB1Id = getParamNormalized + 0.01; assert the rendered T60 changes by less than 10%. Today it changes about 7x.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute; T60 not rendered, so the 7-10x figures come from the mapper formulas. The default kit leaves B1 at -1 for Kick, Tom (default_kit.h:171-174), Hat and Perc, and B3 for Hat and Perc; only Snare (:130-131), Cymbal (:249-250) and Clap (:323-324) are explicit. The display is a plain percent with no Auto state (controller_param_format.cpp:335-341, 413-422); the proxy forwards to `setPadConfigField` (processor.cpp:461-465, voice_pool.cpp:678-679). Only a blob can carry a negative value (state_codec.cpp:216-219, 333-336). Tom nudge shortens decay about 10x.
- Confirmed: worked example b1 3.35 -> 25.6 s⁻¹ at n = 0.51 (about 7.6x), b3 2e-5 -> 5e-4 (25x). Double-click reset writes an explicit 0.5; no macro touches damping. MANUAL.md:237 ("Decay and Material still work ... when the Phase 8A knobs are at their default position") misdescribes the jump rather than documenting it, since returning to 0.5 still gives an explicit b1 = 25.1. A touch on a default-kit tom cuts exactly the long fundamental default_kit.h:172-173 protects.
- Confirmed: about 20 of the 32 default-kit pads (default_kit.h:408-439) keep B1 at -1; the knobs are in the Physics row (editor.uidesc:244/246). Tom (material 0.4, decay 0.5, size 0.6): decayTime 0.412 s, b1 2.43 -> 25.1 (about 10x). The controller-side save writes every untouched sentinel pad as an explicit 0.5 (controller_state_codec.cpp:159-163), overlapping lead 1. High kept.

#### MB-081 — Punch macro below neutral collapses an un-enveloped pad's pitch to 20 Hz; Punch and Brightness do not return to the original sound at neutral

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** param-plumbing · **Dimension:** parameter-audibility

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/macro_mapper.cpp:151-153, 185-192](plugins/membrum/src/processor/macro_mapper.cpp#L151-L153)

**Problem.** `applyPunch` adds -(linDelta(m)-linDelta(mOld)) to tsPitchEnvTime and expDelta to tsPitchEnvStart, then clamps each to [0,1]. On a pad whose pitch envelope is off (start = end = time = 0, the PadConfig default and 309/459 factory pads), any Punch below 0.5 gives tsPitchEnvTime = (0.5-m)·0.4 > 0, which turns the envelope on (tone_shaper.h:310-312), while start is clamped at 0 and end stays 0. Both map to 20·100^0 = 20 Hz (pad_config_apply.h:101-107). The pitch envelope is absolute Hz (tone_shaper.h:380-388), and the body is retuned by pitchHz/naturalFundamentalHz_ (drum_voice.h:1613-1619), so the whole modal set is moved to a 20 Hz fundamental. Separately, the clamp is applied to the field while the cache keeps the unclamped macro. Sweeping Punch 0.5 -> 1 -> 0.5 gives time = clamp(0-0.2) = 0, then 0+0.2 = 0.2, and start 0+0.5-0.5 = 0: the pad ends at neutral Punch with a 100 ms envelope pinned at 20 Hz. Brightness does the same with the default cutoff 1.0: 0.5 -> 1 -> 0.5 gives cutoff clamp(1.2) = 1, then 0.8 = 20·1000^0.8 = 5.0 kHz lowpass.

**Why wrong.** Spec 141 SC-006 says macros at 0.5 are neutral and leave the underlying parameters where the preset placed them. A macro must be reversible and must not produce a degenerate state. "Less punch" should shorten or soften the attack, not detune a 158 Hz membrane by 3 octaves.

**Consequence.** Nudging Punch down by 1 % on any kick, snare, hat or perc pad without a pitch envelope (a 2 ms envelope at 20 Hz) turns it into a sub-20 Hz thud. Sweeping Punch or Brightness and returning to centre leaves the pad changed: pitch stuck at 20 Hz, or a 5 kHz lowpass engaged. The processor saves this through getState (`toPadSnapshot` of cfg), the per-pad knobs in the controller do not show it, and only a preset reload undoes it.

**Evidence.** macro_mapper.cpp:185-192: `cfg.tsPitchEnvStart = clamp01(cfg.tsPitchEnvStart + (expDelta(m, kPunchPitchEnvDepthSpan) - expDelta(mOld, ...)))` and `cfg.tsPitchEnvTime = clamp01(cfg.tsPitchEnvTime - (linDelta(m, kPunchPitchEnvTimeSpan) - linDelta(mOld, ...)))`; macro_mapper.h:115-116 spans 0.50 / 0.40; :151-153 Brightness cutoff span 0.40. pad_config.h:202-204 defaults start/end/time 0. Kit scan: peStart mode 0.0000 x309, peTime 0 on 313/459 pads, fCut 1.0 on 374/459. No round-trip test in test_macro_mapper.cpp (case list read).

**Suggested fix.** Store each macro's contribution separately (base field + macro offset, clamped only at the point of use, i.e. effective = clamp(base + delta(m))) instead of mutating cfg incrementally. For Punch, only scale an envelope that already exists (gate the time and start deltas on tsPitchEnvTime > 0), or define Punch on other targets (click mix/contact, exciter hardness). Tests: (1) Punch 0.5 -> 0 -> 0.5 and 0.5 -> 1 -> 0.5 restore every cfg field bit-for-bit; (2) Punch 0.45 on a default pad leaves the rendered f0 within 1 semitone of the Size-derived f0.

**Verifier notes**
- Holds: with the cache at 0.5 (macro_mapper.h:77-81), Punch < 0.5 turns the envelope on (tone_shaper.h:354-358, 310-312); `PitchSegmentEnvelope::process` (pitch_segment_envelope.h:103-133) holds endValue_ = 20 Hz; drum_voice.h:734-745 retunes every chunk through `updateModalFundamentalOnBank` (1607-1625). apply() mutates cfg and caches the unclamped macro (macro_mapper.cpp:85-95). The controller does not mirror macro deltas (only controller.cpp:210 registration, formatting, codec). test_macro_mapper.cpp's only Punch case (line 121) sets 1.0.
- Could not refute: no guard or clamp on the retune ratio (drum_voice.h:1587-1626); String is retuned through `setStringFrequency(20)`. Brightness 0.5 -> 0 -> 0.5 also leaves modeInjectAmount = 0.15, so the pad now rings undamped. The mapper's own comments (macro_mapper.cpp:80-84, 119-124) and spec 141 FR-021 / SC-006 promise neutral-at-0.5, which the clamp drift contradicts.
- Confirmed: at Punch 0.49, time = 0.004 (about 2 ms, pad_config_apply.h:107) and start clamps to 0, so start and end are 20 Hz; a 158 Hz membrane drops about 3 octaves and a ~1500 Hz NoiseBody hat by a factor of 75. Only the kick (default_kit.h:59-61) and toms (:475-477) have a pitch envelope. Brightness return lands at 20·1000^0.8 = 5.02 kHz (pad_config_apply.h:84). Reachable with one drag of the Punch knob (editor.uidesc:42 tag 1040, :142-143); test_macro_preset_load_regression.cpp never tests 0.5 -> x -> 0.5.

#### MB-096 — PolyphonySlider has no control listener, so dragging it never changes Max Polyphony and it never follows the parameter

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** ui-wiring · **Dimension:** ui-wiring

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:1156-1164](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L1156)

**Problem.** createCustomView builds `new UI::PolyphonySliderView(viewRect, kMaxPolyphonyId)` and returns it without `setListener(editor)`. PolyphonySliderView's constructor passes a null listener (polyphony_slider.h:29 `CControl(size, nullptr, tag)`). For a custom view, UIDescription only applies the attributes of the uidesc class ("CView"; uidescription.cpp:682-687 -> uiviewfactory.cpp:219-235). The CView creator does not apply control-tag or a listener. VST3Editor::verifyView binds a ParameterChangeListener only when `control->getListener() == this` (vst3editor.cpp:1047).

**Why wrong.** CControl::valueChanged only notifies `listener` and the sub-listeners (ccontrol.cpp:247-252). With no listener, the VST3Editor never gets valueChanged and never calls setParamNormalized + performEdit for kMaxPolyphonyId. CControl::beginEdit/endEdit still reach the host through CFrame (ccontrol.cpp:195-196, 211-212), so the host sees an empty gesture with no value. No ParameterChangeListener exists either, so host automation, kit-preset loads (which replay maxPolyphony) and setComponentState never update the slider after construction. Disrumpo solves the same case with an explicit `morphPad->setListener(editor)` (disrumpo controller.cpp:1204).

**Consequence.** The only Max Polyphony control in the editor (editor.uidesc:391) is dead. The bar moves and reads "Max Polyphony: N", but the processor keeps its old voice count. After any preset or project load the bar shows the value from when the editor opened, not the real one. Users cannot change polyphony from the UI, and the readout misleads them.

**Evidence.** controller.cpp:1160 `auto* view = new UI::PolyphonySliderView(viewRect, kMaxPolyphonyId);` with no setListener; polyphony_slider.h:29 `: CControl(size, nullptr, tag)`, :153-154 `setValueNormalized(quant); valueChanged();`; ccontrol.cpp:249 `if (listener) listener->valueChanged (this);`; vst3editor.cpp:1047 `if (control && control->getTag () != -1 && control->getListener () == this)`; uidescription.cpp:687 applyCustomViewAttributeValues(result, viewClass) with class="CView" (editor.uidesc:391).

**Suggested fix.** In createCustomView call `view->setListener(editor)` (use the VST3Editor* argument that is currently unnamed), so VST3Editor::verifyView attaches its ParameterChangeListener. Alternatively, wire valueChanged to beginEdit/performEdit/setParamNormalized on the controller and push setParamNormalized(kMaxPolyphonyId) into the view. Test: open the editor (shared_editor_views_probe harness), find the PolyphonySliderView, simulate a mouse-down/up at 75 % width, and assert the controller's kMaxPolyphonyId moved and the recorded performEdit carries it. Then call setParamNormalized(kMaxPolyphonyId, x) and assert the view's getValueNormalized()==x.

**Verifier notes.**
- Full path traced: controller.cpp:1156-1163 never calls setListener (the comment at 1158, "Tagged so VST3Editor routes valueChanged()", is wrong); uidescription.cpp:682-687 + uiviewfactory.cpp:219-235 apply only the "CView" creator, so controlcreator.cpp's listener assignment (:75, :81-98) never runs; Membrum's verifyView (controller.cpp:1237-1406) has no PolyphonySliderView branch and no setListener exists anywhere in plugins/membrum/src.
- Correction that makes it worse: CFrame::beginEdit/endEdit reach VST3Editor::beginEdit/endEdit, which are empty no-ops (vst3editor.cpp:691-701), so the host gets no gesture at all, not an empty one.
- The view is seeded once (controller.cpp:1161-1162) and never updated; automation, preset loads and setComponentState never reach it.
- The only covering test (tests/unit/controller/test_voice_management_ui.cpp:159-174) just greps the uidesc for control-tag="MaxPolyphony" and never exercises the binding.
- High fits: the only polyphony control in the editor is dead and shows a stale value; the parameter stays reachable via host automation and presets (processor.cpp:242).

#### MB-097 — XYMorphPad Y-axis (Morph End) edits use performEdit only and never update the controller's parameter, so kit and pad preset saves lose them

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** ui-wiring · **Dimension:** ui-wiring

**Location:** [plugins/shared/src/ui/xy_morph_pad.h:305-309, 374-377, 424-428, 445-448, 267-269](plugins/shared/src/ui/xy_morph_pad.h#L305)

**Problem.** The X axis goes through CControl::valueChanged, so VST3Editor calls setParamNormalized + performEdit. The Y axis (secondary param kMorphEndId, wired by Membrum at controller.cpp:1362-1363) calls only `controller_->performEdit(secondaryParamId_, morphY_)`. EditController::performEdit only forwards to the component handler. It does not call setParamNormalized, so Membrum's override never runs: no forward to the selected pad's per-pad kPadMorphEnd, and the global kMorphEndId value is not updated either.

**Why wrong.** The processor gets the edit (it forwards global 242 to the selected pad itself), but the controller does not. Every controller-side consumer then sees the old value. kitPresetStateProvider and padPresetStateProvider build the blob from controller parameter values (controller_state.cpp:111, 201-202). syncGlobalProxyFromPad copies the stale per-pad value back to the proxy. Membrum's other custom editors already do performEdit AND setParamNormalized for this reason: PitchEnvelopeDisplay (controller.cpp:1296-1297), ADSRDisplay (1432-1433) and the overlay (1604-1605).

**Consequence.** A user drags the morph pad vertically, hears the new Morph End, and saves a kit or pad preset. The preset stores the previous Morph End, so the edit is lost on reload. Switching to another pad and back puts the stale value in the proxy. A later Simple<->Advanced rebuild places the XY cursor at the old Y. A host that does not echo performEdit (most hosts) shows the old value in its generic UI.

**Evidence.** xy_morph_pad.h:305-309 `controller_->beginEdit(secondaryParamId_); controller_->performEdit(secondaryParamId_, static_cast<double>(morphY_));` (no setParamNormalized anywhere in the file); controller.cpp:1362-1363 `xyPad->setController(this); xyPad->setSecondaryParamId(kMorphEndId);`; controller.cpp:862-871 proxy forwarding only inside setParamNormalized; controller_state.cpp:111 `buildSnapshot(*this, selectedPadIndex_)` reads controller params.

**Suggested fix.** In Membrum's verifyView, do not rely on setController(this) alone. Either give XYMorphPad a secondary-param callback, as PitchEnvelopeDisplay has (setParameterCallback with performEdit + setParamNormalized), or have XYMorphPad call `controller_->setParamNormalized(secondaryParamId_, y)` next to each performEdit (shared fix; check Disrumpo and the other consumers). Test: drive XYMorphPad mouse events in a controller test and assert that getParamNormalized(kMorphEndId) and getParamNormalized(padParamId(sel, kPadMorphEnd)) equal the dragged Y. Then save via padPresetStateProvider and assert that blob slot MorphEnd equals Y.

**Verifier notes.**
- Every Y-axis site (double-click 258-269, mouse-down 305-309, drag 374-377, mouse-up 391-392, wheel 424-428, Escape 445-448) calls only beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit; the header comment at line 11 says Y is "Controlled via direct performEdit()".
- EditController::performEdit (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vsteditcontroller.cpp:186-193) only forwards to componentHandler; Membrum does not override performEdit, so the proxy forward (controller.cpp:861-871, mapping row :116) never runs.
- The processor applies kMorphEndId (processor.cpp:370-371) but writes no outputParameterChanges, so nothing syncs the controller back.
- Both save providers read controller params (controller_state_codec.cpp:107, 116-181, 330, 361), so the saved Morph End is stale; verifyView reads getParamNormalized(kMorphEndId) (controller.cpp:1366), so a template rebuild places the cursor at the old Y.
- Limits: audio and host getState (processor-built) keep the dragged value; Morph End is audible only with Material Morph enabled. The preset data loss stands, so severity stays high.
- No test drives the XY pad's Y axis (test_param_reachability_in_editor.cpp:189 only lists kMorphEndId).

#### MB-105 — VoiceAllocator misuse: voiceFinished() on a still-Active allocator slot is ignored, and with the Quietest policy the pool collapses to one voice

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** shared-dsp-contract · **Dimension:** shared-dsp-contracts · **Also flagged by:** prior-audit-regressions, gestalt-processor

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:380-396, 508-519, 158-178](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L380) (callee: [dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_allocator.h:258-302, 439-441](dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/voice_allocator.h#L258))

**Problem.** A voice can finish on its own without a MIDI note-off. The pool's auto-release calls DrumVoice::noteOff() at peak < 1e-3 (cpp:508-512) but never calls allocator_.noteOff(). When the voice later finishes, the natural-finish branch calls allocator_.voiceFinished(slot) while the allocator slot is still Active. VoiceAllocator ignores voiceFinished for any slot that is not Releasing. When the MIDI note-off later arrives, allocator.noteOff() moves the slot to Releasing. Nothing ever calls voiceFinished again, because meta is already Free. The slot stays Releasing for good and is still counted in activeVoiceCount_.

**Why wrong.** voice_allocator.h:283-293 documents the contract: 'Transitions voice from Releasing to Idle. Ignored for non-Releasing voices'. The caller must call noteOff before voiceFinished. The pool does this correctly on the choke path (cpp:1056-1057) and the Quietest pre-steal path (cpp:172-173), but not on the natural-finish path. poolFull (cpp:158-159) then reads the inflated allocator count.

**Consequence.** Any note held longer than the pad's decay leaves its slot stuck. With the Quietest policy, poolFull stays true while meta shows free slots. Every new hit then fast-releases the only sounding voice: effective polyphony becomes 1, and tails are cut on every hit. Measured (maxPolyphony 4, Quietest; four notes held 10 s and then released):
- Hit 40 takes slot 0.
- Hit 41 steals 40 ('slots: [0 note=41 st=1] ...', metaActive=1).
- Hit 42 steals 41 ('shadow slot 0 FastReleasing originatingNote=41').

Control: the same sequence with the note-offs sent before the voices die keeps 40, 41 and 42 together (metaActive=3). With Oldest, the stuck slots are taken as steal victims, so each later hit issues a Steal on an idle slot and fast-releases an idle voice into the shadow (wasted work).

**Evidence.** voice_allocator.h:288-293 'if (state != VoiceState::Releasing) return;'; :439-440 getActiveVoiceCount returns activeVoiceCount_, decremented only in voiceFinished and steal. voice_pool.cpp:514-519 'else if (meta_[slot].state == VoiceSlotState::Active) { ... allocator_.voiceFinished(slot); }' with no allocator noteOff; :508-511 the auto-release calls only VP_VOICES[slot].noteOff(); :158-159 poolFull = allocator_.getActiveVoiceCount() >= maxPolyphony_. Probe C:/Users/scab/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/af40cef86e602ebb/69f67fe4-9e20-4f6f-a325-fd4459c6f76b/scratchpad/contract_probe_mb/vp.cpp (+ vp_oldest.cpp, vp_control.cpp), output quoted in the consequence.

**Suggested fix.** On the natural-finish branch of both processBlock overloads (cpp:386-396 and 514-519), call allocator_.noteOff(meta_[slot].originatingNote) before voiceFinished(slot), as the choke path does. Alternatively, call it when the auto-release fires. Test (voice_pool): maxPolyphony 4, Quietest, four held notes rendered past their decay, then note-offs, then three new hits; assert that all three are Active and no shadow is FastReleasing. Add the same test for Oldest.

**Verifier notes.**
- Mechanism traced: auto-release (cpp:380-384, :508-512) gates only the voice; voiceFinished on an Active slot returns early (voice_allocator.h:293) so activeVoiceCount_ (:301) is not decremented; the later VoicePool::noteOff (cpp:283-300) moves the slot Active -> Releasing (voice_allocator.h:265-268) and nothing ever calls voiceFinished for it again.
- Only a same-note retrigger (findVoicePlayingNote :830-840), resetAllVoicesForKitSwitch (cpp:279) or a shrinking setVoiceCount reconciles allocator and meta.
- Quietest: selectQuietestActiveSlot (cpp:848-871) picks a real sounding voice and fast-releases it (cpp:161-178), so the FR-025 Releasing-victim preference (voice_allocator.h:630-636) is never reached. Probe re-run by a verifier (vp.exe vs vp_control.exe) reproduced metaActive=1 vs 3.
- Oldest (the default, voice_pool.h:361): findStealVictimSingle (voice_allocator.h:630-637) takes the stuck slots, so each Steal fast-releases an idle voice (cpp:221): wasted work, plus reduced polyphony while the stuck slot is still Active.
- Processor forwards host note-offs straight to the pool (processor.cpp:580, 592); nothing upstream guards. Two factory kits set stealingPolicy = 1 (Quietest), e.g. tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:3734.
- One verifier could not find the quoted probe output on disk, but the source alone establishes the defect; another re-ran the probe and confirmed it.

#### MB-106 — String body: the shared bank's stale active-mode count after a body swap means a String voice never retires; on a fresh voice it is cut after 256 host blocks while still ringing

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** shared-dsp-contract · **Dimension:** shared-dsp-contracts

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h:177-213](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h#L177) (and drum_voice.h:644-669; string_body.h:38-41, 82-89; callee modal_resonator_bank.h:222-236, 461-480)

**Problem.** BodyBank::applyPendingSwap() calls sharedBank_.reset(), which zeroes oscillator states and snaps coefficients. reset() does NOT clear active_[] or numActiveModes_, and StringBody never runs the shared bank (its processBlock only drives the WaveguideString), so flushSilentModes() never runs either. DrumVoice retirement nevertheless keys on sharedBank.getNumActiveModes():
- A voice slot whose previous note was modal keeps that count, e.g. 44, forever: a String note there never retires.
- On a fresh slot the count is 0 from the first block. bankSilent is then true immediately, and the 256-BLOCK safety net cuts the string while it rings, after a time that depends on the host block size.

**Why wrong.** modal_resonator_bank.h:221-236: reset() only clears states and snaps smoothing; numActiveModes_ is maintained solely by computeModeCoefficients (:760) and flushSilentModes (:471). A body that bypasses the bank must not use the bank's mode count as its lifetime signal. Either the swap must clear the mode set (setModes with 0 partials), or retirement must ask the active body (StringBody: waveguide energy).

**Consequence.** Measured (48 kHz, noteOff at 0.5 s):
- String on a fresh voice, block 64: retired at 0.343 s, while the output was still above -60 dB at that moment (cut at 256 x 64 samples).
- Fresh voice, block 512: retired at 0.789 s.
- String after a Membrane note on the same voice: not retired after 20 s at blocks 64 and 512 (bankActiveModes=44), a permanent CPU leak and stuck Active slot.

getPartialInfo (drum_voice.h:1250-1258) also feeds the coupling engine the previous body's stale mode frequencies for String voices.

**Evidence.** body_bank.h:181 sharedBank_.reset(); then emplace and prepare; modal_resonator_bank.h:222-236 reset() has no numActiveModes_/active_ write; string_body.h:38 reset(ModalResonatorBank& /*sharedBank*/) ignores the bank, :82-89 processBlock loops string_.process only. drum_voice.h:645 bankSilent = sharedBank.getNumActiveModes() == 0; :660-664 safety net counts processBlock calls. Probe C:/Users/scab/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/af40cef86e602ebb/69f67fe4-9e20-4f6f-a325-fd4459c6f76b/scratchpad/contract_probe_mb/st.cpp: 'String after a Membrane note (same voice) block=64 retired_at=-1.000 s bankActiveModes=44'; 'String on a fresh voice block=64 retired_at=0.343 s ... last>-60dB=0.343 s'.

**Suggested fix.** In applyPendingSwap, clear the mode set: sharedBank_.setModes(nullptr-safe zero arrays, 0, ...) or add a ModalResonatorBank::clearModes() that zeroes numModes_/numActiveModes_/active_. Give retirement a body-aware silence test: for String, the waveguide output envelope below a threshold, with the safety net counted in samples, not blocks. Tests:
- A String note after a Membrane note on the same DrumVoice retires within decay + 1 s.
- A fresh String note with decay 1.0 is not retired before its -60 dB time at blocks 64 and 512.

**Verifier notes.**
- numActiveModes_ changes only in computeModeCoefficients (:760, :840-847) and flushSilentModes (:461-471), which runs only from the bank's own processBlock (:446, :457); StringBody ignores the bank in reset, configureForNoteOn and processBlock (string_body.h:38-41, 43-59, 82-89).
- The voice also skips the bank for String (drum_voice.h:1576-1577, 1589-1590, 1644); the comment at drum_voice.h:277-285 assumes "no modes are configured", which is false after a swap from a modal body. noteOff (:451) only calls damp().
- Probe st.exe re-run by all three verifiers: fresh voice block 64 retired at 0.343 s against a natural -60 dB point of 0.639 s; block 512 at 0.789 s; after Membrane, not retired in 20 s with bankActiveModes=44.
- Reachability: a natural modal retirement leaves the count at 0 (the truncation case, every String note at small buffers); the stuck case needs a slot reused while its modal note still rings, via resetForKitSwitch (drum_voice.h:467-491), a steal/choke shadow swap (voice_pool.cpp:221) or a body change on a retriggering pad.
- Stuck slots cost polyphony, waveguide CPU, a wrong active-voice meter and a coupling noteOff that never fires (voice_pool.cpp:389-390). Severity high kept.

#### MB-136 — Every per-component allocation assertion is vacuous: AllocationScope::getAllocationCount() is read while the scope is still open, so it always returns 0

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp:443-464](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp#L443)

**Problem.** 28 Membrum test TUs (39 call sites repo-wide) do `TestHelpers::AllocationScope scope; ...; CHECK(scope.getAllocationCount() == 0)` inside the scope. AllocationScope stores the count in `count_` only in its destructor (tests/test_helpers/allocation_detector.h:111-131), so inside the scope it always returns its initial 0. The checks cannot fail.

**Why wrong.** The helper's own comment (allocation_detector.h:145-147) says the count is latched in the destructor and that a read inside an open scope must go through AllocationDetector::instance().getAllocationCount(). SC-011 and FR-072 (no allocation on the audio thread) are reported as covered by tests that cannot detect an allocation.

**Consequence.** A real audio-thread allocation ships green. ExciterBank::applyPendingSwap (exciter_bank.h:198-235) emplaces a new exciter and calls its prepare() inside noteOn(). For Mallet and Impulse that reaches ImpactExciter::prepare -> combDelay_.prepare -> buffer_.resize (impact_exciter.h:66, delay_line.h:316). For String, the body swap reaches WaveguideString::prepare. The 168-combination matrix triggers exactly this swap inside its scope (a fresh voice, setExciterType(Mallet), then noteOn inside the scope) and still passes. Measured: membrum_tests.exe "ExciterBodyMatrix144: all 168 combos audible finite bounded alloc-free" -> All tests passed (842 assertions), exit 0. The voice-pool tests that read the count correctly (stopTracking) avoid the swap on purpose; see the separate SC-007 finding (MB-137).

**Evidence.** allocation_detector.h:117-123: `~AllocationScope() { count_ = AllocationDetector::instance().stopTracking(); }  size_t getAllocationCount() const { return count_; }`. test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp:445-450: `{ TestHelpers::AllocationScope scope; voice.noteOn(kVelocity100); stats = processAndCollect(...); allocCount = scope.getAllocationCount(); }`. The same pattern is at test_allocation_matrix.cpp:130-163 (noteOn, processBlock, noteOff, process) and test_body_bank.cpp:121, test_exciter_bank.cpp:113, test_{bell,membrane,noise,plate,shell,string}_body.cpp, test_{clap,feedback,fm_impulse,friction,impulse,mallet,noise_burst}_exciter.cpp, test_click_layer.cpp:56, test_noise_layer.cpp:69, test_tone_shaper.cpp:294/304/325, test_decay_skew.cpp:193, test_mode_stretch.cpp:187, test_mode_inject.cpp:186, test_material_morph.cpp:192, test_nonlinear_coupling.cpp:405. Measurement: the 168 matrix passes with a Mallet swap inside the scope.

**Suggested fix.** Fix the shared helper rather than 39 call sites: make AllocationScope::getAllocationCount() return AllocationDetector::instance().getAllocationCount() while the scope is open, and the latched count after it closes. Add a positive control in test_allocation_matrix.cpp: TEST_CASE("AllocationScope counts inside an open scope", "[membrum][allocation]") opens a scope, calls TestHelpers::allocateObservably(), and asserts scope.getAllocationCount() >= 1. After the fix, the 168 matrix must go red on the Mallet, Clap and FM swaps and on the String body swap until the exciter and body prepare work moves off the audio thread. dsp/tests (aether_reverb, cavern_verb, atmosphere_engine, resonance_drift_network) and seraphis lifecycle_test use the same pattern; gate those consumers too.

**Verifier notes.**
- allocation_detector.h:111-131: only the destructor (117-119) sets `count_`; getAllocationCount() (121-123) returns `count_`, initialised to 0 (line 130); the comment at 145-147 documents the correct in-scope read.
- Every Membrum site reads inside the open braces (one verifier counted 30 `scope.getAllocationCount()` sites across 25 files); only test_membrum_parameters_v2.cpp:274 reads the detector directly and is correct.
- The binary does count allocations (test_allocation_matrix.cpp:34 includes allocation_operator_overrides.h), so the read is the fault, not a missing override.
- The hidden allocation is real: configureFor144 (test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp:344-353) sets types with no warm-up; noteOn (line 447) -> drum_voice.h:343 trigger -> exciter_bank.h:55-56 applyPendingSwap -> :205-235 emplace + prepare -> mallet_exciter.h:45 -> impact_exciter.h:66 -> delay_line.h:316 `buffer_.resize` on an empty vector. The "Emplace ... (no heap)" comment at exciter_bank.h:200 is wrong.
- Production reaches the same path: pad_config_apply.h:32-33 sets exciter/body type at every note-on; test_allocation_matrix.cpp:104-111 does an untracked warm-up to dodge it.

#### MB-137 — SC-007 zero-allocation tests hide the known exciter/body-swap allocation by forcing every pad to Impulse+Membrane

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/voice_pool/test_per_pad_dispatch.cpp:359-369](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/voice_pool/test_per_pad_dispatch.cpp#L359)

**Problem.** The only voice-pool allocation tests that read the detector correctly (stopTracking) set every pad to the same exciter and body. Variant swaps never happen, so the allocation the comment admits to is never measured. test_polyphony_allocation_matrix.cpp:73-75 and test_coupling_fuzz.cpp:101-103 do the same.

**Why wrong.** Real kits mix exciter and body types across pads. A voice slot moves between pads, so every hit on a pad whose type differs from the slot's previous pad runs ExciterBank/BodyBank::applyPendingSwap on the audio thread, and that calls prepare(), which allocates (delay_line.h:316). The comment blames 'MSVC CRT heap allocations for stack overflow guard pages' from the std::swap. The code shows prepare() resizing std::vector buffers inside noteOn. Uniform types were chosen to make a known red go green.

**Consequence.** Allocation, and the FM wavetable FFT build if FMImpulse is involved, on the audio thread at note-on after every kit load or pad edit. No gate covers it.

**Evidence.** test_per_pad_dispatch.cpp:360-366: "Use uniform exciter/body types across pads (Impulse + Membrane) because ExciterBank/BodyBank variant swaps during voice stealing ... trigger MSVC CRT heap allocations". test_polyphony_allocation_matrix.cpp:74-75: setAllPadsExciterType(pool, Impulse); setAllPadsBodyModel(pool, Membrane). exciter_bank.h:235: `std::visit([sr, vid](auto& e) noexcept { e.prepare(sr, vid); }, active_);` inside applyPendingSwap, called from trigger() (:53-56).

**Suggested fix.** In test_per_pad_dispatch.cpp, add TEST_CASE("SC-007: zero allocations with heterogeneous exciter/body pads", "[membrum][voice_pool][rt-safety]"). Assign pads round-robin over all 7 ExciterTypes and 6 BodyModelTypes, run the same 10 s fuzz between detector.startTracking() and stopTracking(), and REQUIRE allocCount == 0. It is red today. The fix is to pre-prepare every variant alternative at prepare() time, or keep per-type exciter and body instances, so a swap never allocates.

**Verifier notes.**
- Every stopTracking-based pool/processor allocation test forces Impulse+Membrane: test_per_pad_dispatch.cpp:367-369, test_polyphony_allocation_matrix.cpp:74-75, test_coupling_fuzz.cpp:102-103, test_choke_allocation_free.cpp:48-49, test_voice_pool_allocation_free.cpp:44-45; test_allocation_matrix.cpp:104-123 runs the swap in an untracked warm-up.
- The swap is reachable at every note-on: voice_pool.cpp:232 applyPadConfigToSlot -> pad_config_apply.h:32-33 -> exciter_bank.h:53-56 / body_bank.h:58-62 applyPendingSwap when the type changed (drum_voice.h:244, 343).
- FMImpulseExciter::prepare (fm_impulse_exciter.h:32-36) -> FMOperator::prepare, documented "NOT real-time safe (allocates internally via FFT for wavetable)" (fm_operator.h:59/101-109), which builds FFT objects and vectors (wavetable_generator.h:236-288), twice; the "never on the audio thread" comment at fm_impulse_exciter.h:17-19 is contradicted.
- StringBody::prepare (string_body.h:32-35) -> WaveguideString::prepare (waveguide_string.h:105-110) -> two DelayLine::prepare resizes (delay_line.h:316) of about 4096 floats each on a freshly emplaced, empty vector; destroying the old StringBody also frees.
- Factory kits mix these types (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp references FMImpulse / String 59 times), so slot-type changes are routine with 16 slots across 32 pads. High stands.

#### MB-139 — No test covers the preset SAVE paths against the processor: the noiseLayerGain and body-damping loss (extra focus lead 1) ships green

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/preset/test_kit_uimode_roundtrip.cpp:44-128](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/preset/test_kit_uimode_roundtrip.cpp#L44)

**Problem.** Every save-provider test is controller to controller: kitPresetStateProvider loaded into a second Controller. Pad-preset tests check only blob size, version, exciter, body and material (test_pad_preset.cpp:78-150), or start from hand-built blobs (buildPadPresetBlob). test_kit_browser_load.cpp:290-320 compares browser LOAD against host LOAD with a writeKitBlob-built kit, so it never sees a controller-built blob. Its kit A then kit B sequence even leaves the controller holding A's stale B1/B3 (0.4/0.3) after B's sentinel load, and no save follows to expose it.

**Why wrong.** buildPadSnapshotFromParams (controller_state_codec.cpp:116-181) has no kLateSlots row for snapIndex 57 (comment at :91). PadSnapshot::sound therefore keeps the value-initialised 0.0 there, and State::applyPadSnapshot / applyPadPresetSnapshot clamp it to 0.1 on load (state_codec.cpp:243, 326). The PadConfig default is 1.0 and the default-kit snare uses 6.2. Slots 42/43 are written from the controller parameter: registered default 0.5 (controller.cpp:227), or a stale value, because applyPadSnapshotToParams skips sentinel slots (controller_state_codec.cpp:263-268). So the -1 'derive' sentinel is lost. The only path that preserves both fields is the processor's getState (state_codec.cpp:124, 147).

**Consequence.** A user who saves a kit or pad preset and reloads it gets every pad's noise layer at 0.1x (-20 dB on a default pad; about -36 dB on the default-kit snare wire, 6.2 to 0.1). Every untouched pad also gets an explicit damping override (b1 = 0.2 + 0.5 x 49.8 = 25.1 s^-1) in place of the material and decay derived law. The test suite cannot see this.

**Evidence.** controller_state_codec.cpp:91: "// Wire coupling (sound[58] -> offset 65). snapIndex 57 = noiseLayerGain." There is no kLateSlots entry for 57 (:58-93). state_codec.cpp:243: `cfg.noiseLayerGain = std::clamp(static_cast<float>(snap.sound[57]), 0.1f, 16.0f);`. controller.cpp:227: Body Damping b1 defaultValue 0.5. test_kit_uimode_roundtrip.cpp:53-65 saver -> loader, both Controllers. test_pad_preset.cpp:662 'Pad preset load applies noiseLayerGain' uses a hand-built blob.

**Suggested fix.** Add to test_kit_browser_load.cpp TEST_CASE("Kit preset saved from the controller reloads to the processor's own state", "[membrum][presets][state][save]"). Steps: host-load the default kit into processor P and controller C (setState + setComponentState); bytes0 = P.getState; blob = C.kitPresetStateProvider(); browserLoad(blob) and forwardEditsAndProcess; bytes1 = P.getState; CHECK(bytes1 == bytes0), with CAPTURE of pads[1].sound[57] and pads[5].sound[42..43]. Add the pad-preset twin in test_pad_preset.cpp: TEST_CASE("Pad preset saved from the controller reloads to the processor's pad config", "[membrum][presets][pad][save]"), using padPresetStateProvider, LoadPadPreset and a toPadSnapshot comparison of the target pad. Both must be red today. Also CHECK that the render RMS of a snare and a tom hit is unchanged after the round trip, to within 0.1 dB.

**Verifier notes.**
- Save paths confirmed: kitPresetStateProvider (controller_state.cpp:105-118) and padPresetStateProvider (:196-215) build from controller params and are wired into the preset manager (controller.cpp:740, 760); kLateSlots (controller_state_codec.cpp:58-93) has no row 57; `std::array<double,59> sound{}` (state_codec.h:60) leaves it 0.0; defaults are 1.0 (pad_config.h:261) and 6.2 for the snare (default_kit.h:120), so 20*log10(6.2/0.1) = 35.8 dB.
- The -1 sentinel cannot live in a parameter (controller.cpp:227-228 default 0.5; load skip at controller_state_codec.cpp:263-268); applyPadSnapshot (state_codec.cpp:213-222) turns the saved 0.5 into an explicit override.
- Every StateProvider test is controller to controller: test_kit_uimode_roundtrip.cpp:53-65 / :101-109, test_pad_preset.cpp:87/125/282, test_coupling_state.cpp:245, test_editor_asan_lifecycle.cpp:125; test_kit_browser_load.cpp builds kits from getState / writeKitBlob (:168, :175, :195-221); the noiseLayerGain tests (test_pad_preset.cpp:539, 556, 662) use hand-built snapshots.
- Verifiers did not build or run anything; the dB figures are arithmetic on the cited constants (the b1 = 25.1 s^-1 figure was not independently checked).
- Severity split: one verifier recommends medium, since this is the test-gap twin of the bug findings (MB-152, MB-166) that carry the user impact; the other two keep high because the gap hides an audible change to every saved preset.

#### MB-141 — No test checks note timing against Event::sampleOffset or render invariance across host block sizes; the SC-009 pitch-glide test runs only the per-sample renderer no host uses

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/tone_shaper/test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:92-141](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/tone_shaper/test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp#L92)

**Problem.** (1) Processor::processEvents never reads event.sampleOffset (processor.cpp:559-599), and VoicePool::noteOn takes no offset, so every note starts at the block start. Every test passes sampleOffset 0; the only non-zero offset (test_editor_asan_lifecycle.cpp:210) has no assertion. (2) No test renders the same hit at several host block sizes. The production renderer refreshes the pitch envelope, tension and morph once per chunk of up to 2048 samples (drum_voice.h:699-746), and the 256-silent-block retirement net counts calls, not samples (drum_voice.h:660-665). (3) The SC-009 808 glide test renders with voice.process() (line 119), which updates the pitch every sample (drum_voice.h:506-510). VoicePool always calls processBlock (voice_pool.cpp:356, 471).

**Why wrong.** A drum synth must place notes sample-accurately: flams and rolls must not jitter with the buffer size, and output must not depend on how the host partitions blocks. SC-009 (160 -> 50 Hz within 20 ms) is a property of the shipping path, and the test proves it for a path the plugin never runs.

**Consequence.** Flams and rolls are quantised to the host buffer (up to 46 ms at 2048), the pitch sweep is stair-stepped differently per block size, and String/NoiseBody tails are cut after 256 blocks (0.37 s at 64-sample blocks vs 5.9 s at 1024). All of this ships green.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:573-585: the kNoteOnEvent case calls voicePool_.noteOn(pitch, velocity) with no offset. Grep 'sampleOffset' in src: only processor.cpp:164-165, the parameter queue. test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:119: `buf[i] = voice.process();`. drum_voice.h:734-745: one processPitchEnvelope() sample, then the chunk-1 remaining samples consumed, then retuneFundamental once per chunk. drum_voice.h:663: `if (silentBlockCount_ > 256)`.

**Suggested fix.** (a) New tests/unit/processor/test_note_timing.cpp, TEST_CASE("Note-on honours Event::sampleOffset", "[membrum][processor][timing]"): 512-sample block, noteOn at sampleOffset 300; REQUIRE that the first sample with |x| > 1e-4 is at index >= 300 and within 2 samples of it. Twin case: two notes at offsets 0 and 256 produce two onsets. (b) TEST_CASE("Render is invariant to host block size", "[membrum][processor][timing]"): the default kit, a kick with the pitch envelope, a String pad and a NoiseBody pad, rendered at blocks {32, 64, 256, 1024, 4096}; CHECK pairwise RMS difference <= -80 dBFS and equal tail lengths (first sample under -90 dBFS). (c) Change test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp to render through voice.processBlock with 64- and 512-sample blocks, and through VoicePool.

**Verifier notes.**
- Part 1 holds for all three verifiers: processEvents (processor.cpp:559-599) calls voicePool_.noteOn/noteOff (583-584, 580/592) without the offset; every test note uses offset 0; the non-zero offsets (test_editor_asan_lifecycle.cpp:210, test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:890) are note-offs with no timing assertion. No spec or manual text makes block-start quantisation a design choice.
- Production passes the whole host block down (processor.cpp:636, 663-666; voice_pool.cpp:356, 410, 471, 528), so the pitch refresh rate equals the host block, not the 64 samples the comments at drum_voice.h:616-619 and 705-707 claim.
- Dissent on part 2: test_tom_body_depth.cpp:417-447 (block 64 vs 512, per-frame RMS within 1 dB) and test_wire_coupling.cpp:342-374 (late-window RMS within 3 dB) do render at two block sizes, and docs/tom-depth-implementation-plan.md:313/:409 rule out a sample-exact cross-block test because block-rate refresh "will fail by design"; the -80 dBFS invariance ask contradicts that recorded decision. That verifier recommends a lower severity; the call-counting safety net (drum_voice.h:660-665) is better filed as its own code finding (see MB-160).
- Part 3 partly holds: test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:119 uses process(); test_tom_body_depth.cpp:366-382 (block 64) and test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp:38-54/91-141 (block 256, endFreq < 0.5*startFreq only) exercise the block path but not the SC-009 numbers.
- The NoiseBody part of the tail claim is weaker: NoiseBody is modal (drum_voice.h:1560); String runs a waveguide (body_bank.h:121-128, 194-195).

#### MB-151 — Signal-path finding 'pitch envelope refresh is block-rate coarse' (findings.json confirmed[17]) is still present and was dropped from the remediation tracker: measured 1600-cent steps at 1024-sample blocks

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** prior-audit-regression · **Dimension:** prior-audit-regressions · **Corroborated by measurement:** yes · **Corroborated by research:** yes (contradicted by the literature)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:589, 699-746, 615-619, 703-707, 927-965](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L589)

**Problem.** The fast path refreshes the pitch envelope once per chunk of up to kMaxBlockSize = 2048 samples. It takes the chunk's FIRST envelope value and throws away the other chunk-1 values. VoicePool passes the whole host block, so the effective rate is one update per host block. The slow (Feedback) path retunes once per whole block with no chunking. The comments at 615-619, 703-707 and 929-932 still claim a '64-sample block ... ~14 update points across a 20 ms sweep'. Nothing subdivides to 64 samples.

**Why wrong.** Prior finding confirmed[17] (medium) recorded exactly this: three renderers at three refresh rates, and false 64-sample comments. It appears in neither the H/M/L list nor the REMEDIATION STATUS open list of AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md, so it was never fixed. A pitch sweep must not depend on the host buffer size.

**Consequence.** 808-style drops become audible staircases whose shape changes with the DAW buffer setting. A 50 ms 160->50 Hz sweep gets 2-3 pitch values at 1024-sample blocks. The same project renders differently at different buffer sizes and offline versus realtime.

**Evidence.** F:/tmp/membrum-audit/probe-results.txt:369-371 `pitchenv:body=Membrane:knee=0:bs=1024 ... max err vs bs8 (c) / max step (c) = ... / 1599 / 1602` and bs=64 `911 / 933`, with the same numbers for every modal body (363-392). drum_voice.h:701 `const int chunk = remaining < kMaxBlockSize ? remaining : kMaxBlockSize;` :741-742 consumes chunk-1 samples. AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.findings.json confirmed[17] 'Pitch envelope refresh is block-rate coarse and diverges between fast and slow paths'.

**Corroborating measurement.** Probe pitchenv:staircase: "20 ms: bs32 119/40, bs64 233/80, bs256 629/281, bs1024 2012/991; 50 ms: bs64 95/32, bs1024 928/405" (max/rms cents). drum_voice.h:701 `const int chunk = remaining < kMaxBlockSize ? remaining : kMaxBlockSize;` and :741-742 `for (int i = 1; i < chunk; ++i) (void)toneShaper_.processPitchEnvelope();`.

**Corroborating research.** Physics (contradicted): the tension glide is refreshed at block rate, independent of the host buffer size: MAB DAFx-10 Sec. 4.2 computes Tqs at a FIXED decimation (every 32 samples = 0.73 ms at 44.1 kHz) and linearly interpolates between points, so the result is independent of the host buffer. The refresh interval should be a fixed sub-chunk (e.g. 32 samples) inside processBlockFast and processBlockSlow, with the energy read at the start of each sub-chunk. Source (evidence quality strong): Marogna, Avanzini, Bank, "Energy based synthesis of tension modulation in membranes", DAFx-10, https://people.ece.cornell.edu/land/courses/ece5760/LABS/s2016/MarognaAvanziniBank_tension_modulation.pdf: "the membrane energy can be computed at a lower rate, and the continuous energy curve can be obtained by linearly interpolating between the computed points"; Fig. 3c uses a decimation factor of 32 ("Tqs is computed every 32/44.1 = 0.73 ms") and is perceptually similar to the full model.

**Suggested fix.** Subdivide the fast-path chunk into fixed sub-blocks (for example 32 or 64 samples) whenever the pitch envelope, morph or tension is active, with updateModes per sub-block. Apply the same sub-blocking in processBlockSlow. Correct the comments. Add a test that renders a 160->50 Hz / 50 ms sweep at block sizes 64 and 1024 and REQUIREs that mode0 stays within 50 cents of the block-size-8 reference at every 1 ms point.

**Verifier notes.**
- Fast path: chunk = min(remaining, 2048) (drum_voice.h:589, :701), one processPitchEnvelope value, chunk-1 discarded (:741-742), one retuneFundamental (:745); only the Feedback exciter takes the slow path (:620), which retunes once per block (:960-965) and only advances the envelope per sample (:1021-1022).
- Nothing upstream sub-blocks: processor.cpp:636/663 and voice_pool.cpp:356, 410, 471, 528 pass numSamples straight through; the 64-sample comments (:615-619, :703-707, :929-932) describe nothing in the code.
- The prior audit's mitigation (findings.json:496, "coefficient smoothing ramps the frequency") does not hold: smoothCoefficients is one one-pole step per processBlock call with a 2 ms constant (modal_resonator_bank.h:314-317, :647, :906-913), adding lag and block-size dependence rather than interpolating.
- Prior status: findings.json:481-503 (confirmed medium); the .md tracker covers only H-3 and M-1 (pitch envelope / morph reach all bodies, :28-33, :241, :255), nothing on refresh granularity.
