- Measurements: probe-results.txt:367 20 ms sweep at bs=1024, 2012 cents (the whole drop collapses into one jump); :368 629 cents at bs=256; :375-404 1599/1602 cents at bs=1024 for Membrane, Plate, Shell, Bell and NoiseBody.
- Reach: the default kick uses a 20 ms sweep (default_kit.h:61) and the default toms enable the envelope (default_kit.h:477); no test pins the envelope across block sizes. Severity raised from the prior medium to high on the measured magnitude.

#### MB-152 — R-202/R-203 partially fixed: the browser load path was unified but the performEdit replay still re-applies the kit (2119 edits, 162 matrix rebuilds, hybrid kits on interleave, divergent clamping), and the save providers still drop noiseLayerGain and the damping sentinel

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** prior-audit-regression · **Dimension:** prior-audit-regressions

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state.cpp:105-118, 161-172, 196-215, 259-271](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state.cpp#L105)

**Problem.** Load side: kitPresetLoadProvider sends LoadPresetState (processor applyKitSnapshot) and then replays every parameter with beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit. Those edits reach Processor::processParameterChanges and apply the kit a second time, through VoicePool::setPadConfigField. The T1.36 acceptance rule said 'Never a second apply'. Save side: kitPresetStateProvider and padPresetStateProvider build the blob from controller parameters (ControllerState::buildSnapshot / buildPadSnapshotFromParams, controller_state_codec.cpp:116-181). That writes sound[57] (noiseLayerGain, no ParamID) as 0.0, which loads clamped to 0.1 (state_codec.cpp:243). It also writes the B1/B3 parameter value (default 0.5) where the processor holds the -1 sentinel. These are the same two fields R-202 named for the load path.

**Why wrong.** R-202 / R-203 (specs/ruinae-audit/fix-plan.md:109-110, T1.36/T1.37) required one apply and named noiseLayerGain and the sentinel as lost fields. The fix closed only the load direction. The second apply also clamps differently: applyPadSnapshot leaves slots 0-33 unclamped (state_codec.cpp:167-200), while the controller setter clamps to [0,1] (controller_state.cpp:165).

**Consequence.** Measured. Kit-preset save then reload changes every pad's noiseLayerGain to 0.1. On the Acoustic Studio snare (6.2 -> 0.1) energy above 3 kHz drops from -12.8 to -48.4 dB. On the default-kit kick, damping goes from -1 to 0.5 and decay60 from 0.97 s to 0.19 s. One kit load produces 2119 undo/automation edits and 162 recomputeCouplingMatrix calls in one block. Two quick loads produce a hybrid kit (snare max diff 0.477 versus a pure K2 load). A blob with decay 1.7 ends at 1.7 via the message route and 1.0 via the edits.

**Evidence.** F:/tmp/membrum-audit/probe-results.txt:18 `performEdit count ... = 2119 (2112 / 7) / 2119 / 2119 / 162`; :20 interleave hybrid `snare max diff vs pure K2 = 0.4774`; :23 `decay msg/edits ... = 1.700/1.000`; :396 pad38 `noiseLayerGain 6.200->0.100 ... energy>3k dB -12.83->-48.37`; :407 default-kit pad36 `dampB1 -1.000->0.500 ... decay60 0.970 s->0.190 s`. controller_state_codec.cpp:91 `snapIndex 57 = noiseLayerGain` has no kLateSlots row.

**Suggested fix.** Save: have both save providers ask the processor for its blob, or give the controller a mirror of slot 57 and of the sentinel that every load path fills. Load: let the processor be the only applier: mark the replay edits so the processor skips them, or do not performEdit fields the processor already holds. Tests: kit-preset save -> processor setState -> getState must be byte-identical to the processor's own getState; a browser load must cause at most 1 recomputeCouplingMatrix call; two interleaved loads must end on K2.

**Verifier notes.**
- Save side confirmed in code (controller_state.cpp:105-118, :196-215; controller_state_codec.cpp:58-93 has no row 57; state_codec.cpp:243/:326 clamp to 0.1; toPadSnapshot :124-125, :147 keeps the real values) and by measurement, at probe-results.txt lines 408-427 rather than the cited 396/407: kit round trip not byte-identical with slot57 differing on all 32 pads (:408, :414); default kit slot42 x22, slot43 x16 (:420); snare pad38 6.2 -> 0.1, >3 kHz energy -12.83 -> -48.37 dB (:410); kick pad36 decay60 0.97 -> 0.19 s (:421); pad42 0.32 -> 0.02 s (:424); pad-preset path the same (:426-427).
- Factory kits come from tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp and are unaffected; every user-saved kit or pad preset is affected. No test compares a provider save through a processor load to getState (test_pad_preset.cpp:523-556 uses hand-built blobs).
- Load side real but secondary: the replay (controller_state.cpp:150-172, pad path :247-271) is deliberate per the comment at :161-162 and fix-plan.md T1.36 (~915-929) keeps the controller mirror with performEdit, so "regression" overstates this half; its "Never a second apply" (fix-plan.md:926) refers to the processor-side apply.
- For valid factory kits the second apply changes no values (probe :24-25 "fields differing = none"); its costs are undo/automation entries and a CPU spike. The clamp divergence (:26) needs an out-of-range blob; the interleave hybrid (:23) is transient ("fields != K2 after K2 edits = none").
- All verifiers keep high on the strength of the save-side data loss alone; the load-side parts would be medium or low on their own.

#### MB-159 — Pitch envelope, tension glide and Material Morph barely move the modal bank in the processBlock renderers: the bank only steps ~1% per call toward the new target

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-path · **Dimension:** gestalt-voice

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:244, 302, 318-321, 734-770, 960-977](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L244); [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:213, 431-447, 526-529, 647, 906-914](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L213)

**Problem.** Every DrumVoice retune (retuneFundamental -> updateModalFundamentalOnBank -> sharedBank.updateModes, and the morph refresh through pushCachedModes) only writes the coefficient TARGETS. The values the kernel uses (epsilon_, radius_, inputGain_) move toward the targets in smoothCoefficients(), which runs ONCE per processBlock call with the per-SAMPLE 2 ms coefficient: `smoothCoeff_ = exp(-1/(kSmoothingTimeMs*0.001*sr))` and `epsilon_[k] += oneMinusCoeff * (epsilonTarget_[k] - epsilon_[k])`, about 1.04% per call at 48 kHz. DrumVoice calls the bank's processBlock once per chunk, and a chunk is the whole host block (up to 2048 samples). At noteOn, setModes snaps the bank to the NATURAL pitch (MembraneBody::configureForNoteOn -> setModes; the mappers ignore pitchHz). The strike probe's bank.reset() snaps it again, and only then does retuneFundamental(initialPitchHz) set the start pitch as a target. The slow path is the same: prepareBlockSmoothing() runs once per block. Only the single-sample process() smooths per sample.

**Why wrong.** The pitch envelope is documented as 'a 20 ms sweep ... ~14 refresh points', and spec SC-009 asks for a 160->50 Hz glide within +/-10% at 20 ms. In the audible path the modes lag the envelope by a time constant of about 96 host blocks. That makes the pitch drop, the tension glide and the morph depend on the host block size. It also breaks the three-renderer equivalence: process() (per-sample smoothing) glides correctly, processBlock does not.

**Consequence.** 808-style kick and tom pitch drops, which the factory kits use, are close to inaudible and change with the DAW buffer size. Pad 4 of 'Experimental FX Kit' (generator.cpp:1437-1438, 230->160 Hz in 60 ms) never sweeps. Material Morph sweeps (10..2000 ms) and Membrane tension glide are smeared over seconds. The existing tests do not catch it: test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp:123-138 reads getModeFrequency(0), which returns epsilonTarget_ (the target, modal_resonator_bank.h:529), not the running coefficient. test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:119 renders through voice.process(), the per-sample path. The audit probe 10c reads the target the same way.

**Evidence.** modal_resonator_bank.h:431-447 `void processBlock(...) { smoothCoefficients(); for (...) {...} flushSilentModes(); }`; :906-914 smoothCoefficients one step per call; :647 kSmoothingTimeMs = 2.0f. drum_voice.h:741-745 consume chunk-1 envelope samples, then retuneFundamental(pitchHz) once per chunk; voice_pool.cpp:356/471 pass the whole host block. Node model of that arithmetic (scratchpad smooth_lag.js; epsilon starts at the natural f0, one 1.036% step per block, target = pitch env), kick with natural 79 Hz and 160->50 Hz in 50 ms at 48 kHz, audible mode-0 Hz at 5/25/50/100/300 ms:

| Block size | 5 ms | 25 ms | 50 ms | 100 ms | 300 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 142 | 94 | 52 | 50 | 50 |
| 64 | 82 | 87 | 83 | 72 | 55 |
| 256 | 80 | 82 | 81 | 78 | 69 |
| 512 | 80 | 81 | 80 | 79 | 74 |
| 1024 | 80 | 80 | 80 | 79 | 76 |

The H-3 test patch (800->100 Hz in 60 ms, natural 158 Hz) at bs256 gives 165/179/181/174/150 Hz while the test asserts a sweep from the targets.

**Suggested fix.** In DrumVoice, retune on a fixed control grid that does not depend on the host block (for example sub-chunks of 32-64 samples inside processBlockFast and processBlockSlow), and call sharedBank.snapCoefficients() after each updateModes. That API exists for exactly this caller pattern (modal_resonator_bank.h:307-351; Seraphis ContinuousBody uses it). Fixing it in Membrum keeps Innexus bit-identical. Regression test: render a Membrane voice with Start 160 / End 50 Hz / 50 ms through processBlock at block sizes 1, 64, 512 and 1024. Estimate the instantaneous f0 from the AUDIO (zero-crossing or autocorrelation over 2-3 ms windows at 5 / 25 / 60 ms) and require every block size to match the bs=1 reference within 50 cents. Also change test_pitch_env_all_bodies to measure the audio rather than getModeFrequency.

**Verifier notes.**
- Smoothing is one per-sample-coefficient step per call: modal_resonator_bank.h:213 / :647 (1 - exp(-1/96) = 1.04% at 48 kHz), smoothCoefficients :906-914, called once per processBlock (:431-433, :450-453) and per prepareBlockSmoothing (:386-389); only processSample (:421-424) smooths every sample.
- updateModes (:294-305) writes targets only (snapSmoothing=false; snap at :877-881 only for setModes); the bank's own comment (:314-323) describes this block-size dependence and snapCoefficients() (:342-351) exists for it, but no file under plugins/membrum calls it (used only by continuous_body.h and DSP tests).
- Voice path: processBlockFast (drum_voice.h:699-770) retunes once per chunk (:745 -> :1587-1626), tension (:747-754) and morph (:762-770 -> :1638-1665) the same, then one bank step via bodyBank_.processBlock (:799); processBlockSlow retunes once (:960-977) and calls prepareBlockSmoothing once (:1002).
- At note-on, configureForNoteOn -> setModes snaps to the natural modes (membrane_body.h:29-43), the strike probe's bank.reset() (drum_voice.h:1295/1359) snaps again, and only then does :318-321 set the start pitch as a target; nothing in noteOn (:339-418) snaps after it.
- Independent arithmetic: 50 ms at bs=256 is about 9.4 blocks, 1 - 0.9896^9.4 is about 9% convergence; at bs=512, about 5%; consistent with the reviewer's model.
- getModeFrequency (:526-533) returns epsilonTarget_, so test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp:123/:127 read the target; its String case measures audio but String uses a waveguide with its own smoother and is unaffected.

#### MB-160 — Retirement depends only on the shared modal bank's mode count, which the String body never updates: a String voice is either cut after 256 host blocks or, after a kit switch, never retired

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-management · **Dimension:** gestalt-voice

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:467-491, 639-669](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L467); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h:45-50, 177-181](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h#L45); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/string_body.h:82-89](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/string_body.h#L82); [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:222-236](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L222)

**Problem.** The retirement gate is `bankSilent = sharedBank.getNumActiveModes() == 0`, with a safety net that counts processBlock CALLS (`if (silentBlockCount_ > 256) active_ = false`). The String body never touches the shared bank (StringBody::processBlock calls only string_.process). Two cases follow. (a) The slot's bank already reports 0 modes (fresh slot, or the previous voice retired): bankSilent is true from the first block, so a ringing String voice is force-retired after 257 host blocks. (b) The slot's bank still reports N > 0: ModalResonatorBank::reset() zeroes the states but leaves numActiveModes_ and active_[]. Both BodyBank::applyPendingSwap() and resetForKitSwitch() reach only that reset(), so a String voice started on that slot sees bankSilent == false for ever and never retires. Path to (b): a kit switch while modal voices ring (resetForKitSwitch -> bodyBank_.reset()), then a String pad on that slot. The comment at 639-643 justifies ignoring the noise and click layers, but the same 256-block net also cuts NoiseBody's internal noise bed, the parallel noise layer (decay up to 2000 ms) and the ModeInject series (T60 up to 5 s) once the modes die.

**Why wrong.** A voice's life must follow what it actually outputs. For the waveguide body the modal-bank count says nothing about that. The cut-off time must not depend on the host block size; the comment `≈1.4 s at 48 kHz / 256 blocks` silently assumes 256-sample blocks.

**Consequence.** String pads (used in several factory kits, for example generator.cpp:1560, 2877, 3541, 5139, 6159) with decays up to about 10 s are cut at 0.34 s at 64-sample host blocks, 2.7 s at 512 and 10.9 s at 2048: the same project sounds different per buffer size, with an audible chop. After a kit load during playback, String voices on recycled slots never end. That is a CPU leak, a held slot and stale isAnyVoiceActive, and getPartialInfo() then feeds the coupling engine the previous body's frequencies.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:644-647 `const bool bankSilent = sharedBank.getNumActiveModes() == 0; ... if (bankSilent && envFinished)`; :660-664 `if (bankSilent) { ++silentBlockCount_; if (silentBlockCount_ > 256)  // ≈1.4 s at 48 kHz / 256 blocks`; string_body.h:82-89 processBlock ignores sharedBank; modal_resonator_bank.h:222-236 reset() memsets sinState_/cosState_ and snaps arrays, with no numActiveModes_ or active_ write; body_bank.h:181 `sharedBank_.reset();` in applyPendingSwap; drum_voice.h:470 `bodyBank_.reset();` in resetForKitSwitch, which sets active_ = false but leaves the bank count.

**Suggested fix.** Make retirement body-aware. For String, use a waveguide energy or peak follower (or the voice's own post-chain peak over a sample-time window). For every body, count silence in SAMPLES, not calls, and include the noise-layer, ModeInject and NoiseBody noise envelopes in the 'still sounding' test. Clear the bank's activity in BodyBank::applyPendingSwap and resetForKitSwitch: add a Membrum-side reset of active_ / numActiveModes_, or a ModalResonatorBank::clearModes() that leaves Innexus untouched. Tests: (1) a String pad with decay 1.0 and no note-off, rendered at bs 64 and 1024, must retire at the same time within 10 ms, and only after its output falls below -90 dBFS. (2) Hit a Membrane pad, resetAllVoicesForKitSwitch while it rings, apply a String pad to the same slot and hit it: the voice must retire within 15 s.

**Verifier notes.**
- Gate and net confirmed (drum_voice.h:644-651, :660-665, a hard cut with no ramp); the count is per host block because the processor calls the pool once with data.numSamples (processor.cpp:636/663) and the pool calls each voice once (voice_pool.cpp:356/471).
- String never touches the count: string_body.h:38-89 ignores sharedBank; drum_voice.h:1576-1593, 1644-1648 route String to the waveguide setters; numActiveModes_ is written only in computeModeCoefficients (modal_resonator_bank.h:760/841) and flushSilentModes (:461-474, run only inside bank processBlock :446/457); damp() (:507-516) and reset() (:222-236) leave it alone.
- Case (a): cut after 257 blocks = 0.34 s at 64 samples / 48 kHz, 0.69 s at 128, 1.37 s at 256, 2.74 s at 512; StringMapper decay goes to (0.5..4) x (0.3..3) s (string_mapper.h:56-58), WaveguideString T60 clamped to 0.01..10 s (waveguide_string.h:142-144). A 2 s string at 64-sample buffers is still near -10 dB when zeroed (audible chop); at 512 the cut falls after the -60 dBFS auto-noteOff (voice_pool.cpp:380-384) and is benign.
- Case (b): resetForKitSwitch (drum_voice.h:467-491) and the steal swap (voice_pool.cpp:922) leave the count; once the auto-noteOff release finishes, bankSilent stays false for ever, so the voice never reaches voiceFinished (voice_pool.cpp:386-396). Its output is silent (env = 0): a CPU and polyphony leak, not an audible tone.
- No intent, guard, test or prior ruling covers it; the "no modes are configured" note at drum_voice.h:277-284 only holds on a fresh bank. Verifiers did not render audio for this finding; figures come from code constants (MB-106's probe measures the same mechanism).

#### MB-163 — Automatable selected-pad proxies: recorded automation rewrites whichever pad is selected at playback, and the host's per-pad and proxy values go stale

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** param-plumbing · **Dimension:** gestalt-controller

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:84-155, 281-670, 861-891, 961-985](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L84)

**Problem.** Every editor knob binds to a global proxy ID (editor.uidesc:29-31 Material=100, Size=101, Decay=102 ...), and every proxy is registered with kCanAutomate. A knob edit records automation on the proxy. The processor applies proxy values to processor-side selectedPadIndex_ at playback time. The controller forwards to the per-pad parameter only through the base setter (:869-871), with no performEdit, so the host never learns the per-pad value. On a pad switch syncGlobalProxyFromPad also updates the proxies through the base setter (:969), so the host's proxy values stay at the previous pad's numbers. Spec 139 FR-091 says these updates go through performEdit/endEdit.

**Why wrong.** An automation lane must address a fixed target. With selected-pad proxies the lane is a function of a second piece of editor state (kSelectedPadId, itself automatable). The host's cached values must also match what the plugin plays; VST3 updates the host only through performEdit or restartComponent(kParamValuesChanged).

**Consequence.** A user writes Decay automation while pad 1 is selected, then clicks pad 5 to edit it and presses play. The lane now rewrites pad 5's decay, and that change persists into the processor state. Host undo of a proxy edit applies the old value to the currently selected pad, which may be a different pad. Host-side lanes and generic editors for 'Pad NN ...' parameters show values that the proxy edits silently changed.

**Evidence.** controller.cpp:866-871 'const auto padId = ... padParamId(selectedPadIndex_, mapping.padOffset)); suppressProxyForward_ = true; EditControllerEx1::setParamNormalized(padId, value);'; :969 'EditControllerEx1::setParamNormalized(mapping.globalId, padValue);'; :283 'new RangeParameter(STR16("Material"), kMaterialId, ... ParameterInfo::kCanAutomate)'; specs/139-membrum-phase4-pads/spec.md:321 'These updates are issued one-at-a-time via performEdit/endEdit'.

**Suggested fix.** Either make the proxies non-automatable (drop kCanAutomate; have the editor controls performEdit the per-pad ID of the selected pad, for example by remapping tags in verifyView or a sub-controller), or at least performEdit the per-pad ID alongside the proxy in setParamNormalized and call restartComponent(kParamValuesChanged) after a pad switch. Test: record proxy automation for pad 0, change kSelectedPadId to 5, replay the lane through processParameterChanges, then assert pad 5's PadConfig is unchanged.

**Verifier notes.**
- Proxies registered kCanAutomate (controller.cpp:281-314 through :670; Output Bus :578-580) and bound by the editor knobs (editor.uidesc:29-31; SelectedPad=260 at :26).
- The processor applies each proxy to its current selectedPadIndex_ (processor.cpp:268-521, e.g. :268, :274), which follows kSelectedPadId (:395-400) set by PadGridView's performEdit (controller.cpp:1054-1063, even with no lane); the result is saved by getState (processor.cpp:883), so the wrong-pad edit persists.
- Neither the proxy forward (controller.cpp:866-871, forwardGlobalToPad :993-997) nor the pad-switch resync (:961-971) calls performEdit, and no restartComponent(kParamValuesChanged) exists in plugins/membrum/src; FR-091 (spec.md:321) is marked MET in its compliance row (:462) despite this.
- No prior audit, MANUAL.md or spec-139 clarification accepts the automation consequence; MANUAL.md:104 says "All parameters remain reachable via host automation".
- The "stale host values" half is weaker: generic editors read getParamNormalized, which is current; the real hazard is touch/latch baselines and per-pad lanes in read mode overriding proxy edits.
- Severity split: one verifier recommends medium (selected-pad proxies are an intended design and the failure needs a specific record / reselect / play sequence, no audio corruption); the other two keep high because editing different pads is the normal workflow in a 32-pad drum synth.

#### MB-166 — Preset SAVE turns the body-damping -1 sentinel into an explicit 0.5 override, shortening untouched pads 5-16x

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp:70-71, 159-163, 263-268, 309-316](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp#L70)

**Problem.** The controller registers per-pad Body Damping b1/b3 with default 0.5 (controller.cpp:227-228). buildPadSnapshotFromParams writes every kLateSlots value, so slots 42 and 43 are saved as that parameter value, never as -1. On load, applyPadSnapshotToParams and applyPadPresetSnapshotToParams skip the write when the blob holds the sentinel (lines 267, 315). The controller therefore keeps a stale value, and the next save bakes that value in as an explicit override.

**Why wrong.** PadConfig bodyDampingB1/B3 = -1 means "derive the damping from Decay and Material" (pad_config.h; membrane_mapper.h:71-78 applies an override only when >= 0). A normalised VST parameter cannot represent -1, so the controller is not a valid source for these slots. Host getState (toPadSnapshot) keeps -1.

**Consequence.** Saving and reloading the default kit changes the decay of every pad that relied on the derived damping: kick 0.97 s -> 0.19 s, tom 1.54 s -> 0.23 s, closed hat 0.32 s -> 0.02 s. A pad preset saved from an untouched tom loses most of its ring.

**Evidence.** Probe focus1:save-path:kit:default-kit:pad36+pad41+pad42: "kick B1/B3 -1->0.5, 0.97->0.19 s, RMS -33.92->-39.55; tom B1 -1->0.5, 1.54->0.23 s, RMS -31.20->-35.63; hat 0.32->0.02 s". focus1:save-path:pad: "pad41: slot42 -1->0.5 + slot57 1->0.1, decay 1.54->0.23 s". controller.cpp:227 `.name = "Body Damping b1", ... .defaultValue = 0.5`; controller_state_codec.cpp:267 `if (isSentinelSlot && snap.sound[slot.snapIndex] < 0.0) continue;`.

**Suggested fix.** Keep a per-pad 'damping override active' flag on the controller (or a processor-side mirror) and write -1 into slots 42/43 when no override is set. Fix together with the noiseLayerGain mirror (same root cause: the controller builds blobs from parameters, and some sound fields have no lossless parameter). Test: default kit save, reload into a processor, getState byte compare; tom decay60 is unchanged.

**Verifier notes.**
- The controller cannot hold the sentinel: controller.cpp:227-228 default 0.5; the comment at :221-226 says the override should apply only once the host or user writes a value, and cites "Phase 1 bit-identity for untouched pads", which this save path breaks.
- Loads leave 0.5 in place: setComponentState (controller_state.cpp:83-88) and kitPresetLoadProvider (:163-172) skip sentinel slots (controller_state_codec.cpp:263-268); padPresetLoadProvider the same (:313-316). The comment at :252-262 covers only the load direction.
- Saves copy kLateSlots verbatim (controller_state_codec.cpp:159-163, rows :70-71) via kitPresetStateProvider (controller_state.cpp:111) and padPresetStateProvider (:201-202); host getState keeps -1 (state_codec.cpp:124-125).
- On reload state_codec.cpp:213-222 (pad path :333-336) stores the clamped 0.5 as an override; membrane_mapper.h:71-74 gives b1 = 0.2 + 0.5*49.8 = 25.1 s^-1, fundamental T60 about 6.91/25.1 = 0.28 s, consistent with the probe's 0.19-0.23 s.
- Affected pads match default_kit.h: Kick (60-85), Hat (186-208) and Perc (274-294) set neither B1 nor B3; Tom leaves B1 at -1 on purpose (171-174); Snare, Cymbal and Clap set explicit values (130-131, 249-250, 323-324) and are unaffected by this half.
- No test pins the save path (test_kit_browser_load.cpp:192-211 and test_pad_preset.cpp:544-556 feed hand-built sentinel blobs to the load path only). Verifiers did not re-run the probe. High stands.

#### MB-167 — Tom Resonance (global 272) is a dead parameter for the same reason: it only rebuilds the unused coupling matrix

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dead-parameter · **Dimension:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:418-423, 131-143](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L418)

**Problem.** kTomResonanceId stores tomResonance_ and calls recomputeCouplingMatrix(). The matrix (Tom->Tom gain tomRes*0.05) is never consumed by the audio path (processor.cpp:693-708 uses only couplingEngine_ with its global amount).

**Why wrong.** Spec 140 SC-008 requires mode-coincident toms to couple >= 12 dB more than mode-gap toms. Tom Resonance is the control for that coupling and must change the sound.

**Consequence.** Tom Resonance does nothing: renders are bit-identical in its own context. This is the parameter users reach for to make toms sing together.

**Evidence.** Quality probe param:global=272:tomResonance: "bit-identical on 36, 38, 42; live=no", verdict bad. processor.cpp:418-423 `case kTomResonanceId: { ... tomResonance_.store(clamped, ...); recomputeCouplingMatrix(); break; }`.

**Suggested fix.** Same fix as Snare Buzz: route effectiveGain_ into the resonator registration or the per-source send gain. Test: two toms with coincident modes, tomResonance 0 vs 1, partner-band energy difference >= 6 dB.

**Verifier notes.**
- processor.cpp:418-424 stores and calls recomputeCouplingMatrix(), which (131-143) only writes effectiveGain_ via recomputeFromTier1 (coupling_matrix.h:74).
- No production reader: couplingMatrix_ appears only at processor.h:145, processor.cpp:138 (plus the rebuilds at 187-227, 415, 422, 988, 1012) and the test accessor couplingMatrixForTest (processor.h:81); getEffectiveGain / effectiveGainArray are called only from test_coupling_matrix.cpp and test_coupling_integration.cpp, which check matrix numbers, not audio.
- The audio chain (processor.cpp:693-708: mono sum -> couplingDelay_ -> couplingEngine_.process -> applyEnergyLimiter) is controlled only by setAmount(globalCoupling) (:408, :978; sympathetic_resonance.h:152); voice registration (voice_pool.cpp:243-248) uses couplingAmount only as a > 0 gate. Otherwise the value only reaches state save/restore (processor.cpp:889, 976; state_codec.cpp:397, 483).
- Design intent is the opposite: spec 140 FR-014 (per-pair gain = globalCoupling * effectiveGain * amt * amt), FR-030, tasks.md:122 ("Set Tom Resonance to 0 -- no coupling occurs"); MANUAL.md:432 documents it as audible; CHANGELOG.md:465-467 claims the Tier 1 knobs work; the FR-014 compliance row cites only setAmount(globalCoupling).
- The SC-008 render test (test_coupling_integration.cpp:569-575) switches Global Coupling and Tom Resonance together, so it cannot show Tom Resonance's own effect.
- The knob is visible (editor.uidesc:24, 405-407) and factory kits set it 0.30-0.78 (preset-retune/kits/*.md). Not a safety or RT bug, but a visible, documented, saved control with no effect; severity kept.

#### MB-173 — Brightness macro round trip is lossy: 0.5 -> 1 -> 0.5 leaves the filter cutoff at 0.8 instead of 1.0

**Severity:** high (filed as medium, raised in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/macro_mapper.cpp:146-158](plugins/membrum/src/processor/macro_mapper.cpp#L146-L158)

**Problem.** applyBrightness adds (newDelta - oldDelta) and then clamp01s the result. Going up, the delta is clamped away at 1.0, but going down the full delta is subtracted, so the field ends below its start. All five appliers share this pattern (lines 127-219).

**Why wrong.** Spec 141 SC-006: macros at 0.5 are neutral and leave underlying parameters where the preset placed them. A macro sweep that returns to its start must restore the underlying values.

**Consequence.** Each macro gesture that hits a parameter's limit permanently shifts the pad: the cutoff drops from fully open to 0.8 (about 5 kHz) after one sweep, and repeated sweeps drift further.

**Evidence.** Probe macro:Brightness round trip: "1.0000 / 1.0000 / 0.8000" (tsFilterCutoff before / at 1 / after). macro_mapper.cpp:151-153 `cfg.tsFilterCutoff = clamp01(cfg.tsFilterCutoff + (linDelta(m, ...) - linDelta(mOld, ...)));`

**Suggested fix.** Store the per-pad base value (pre-macro) and compute field = clamp01(base + delta(m)) instead of accumulating increments. Alternatively, track the applied (post-clamp) delta in the cache and subtract that. Test: for every macro, 0.5 -> 1 -> 0 -> 0.5 restores every target field exactly.

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed from source: macro_mapper.cpp:151-153 adds the unclamped difference and then clamp01s; the cache stores the raw macro value (lines 91-95), not the delta actually applied, and nothing restores a base value. Every macro change runs setPadConfigField then macroMapper_.apply on the live PadConfig (processor.cpp:217-223); the only resets (invalidateCache + syncCacheFromCfg on kit / pad load, processor.cpp:994-1017) take the current fields as the baseline. With tsFilterCutoff default 1.0 (pad_config.h:197) and kBrightnessCutoffSpan 0.40 (macro_mapper.h:106) the result is 0.8, i.e. 20*1000^0.8 ≈ 5.0 kHz (pad_config_apply.h:84). No round-trip test exists (test_macro_mapper.cpp:106, 193). Upgrade reason: modeInjectAmount defaults to 0.0 (pad_config.h:214) with kBrightnessModeInjectSpan 0.30, so Brightness 0.5 -> 0 -> 0.5 leaves modeInject at +0.15, and modeInject > 0 rings undamped (plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md): one ordinary gesture can turn a default pad into an infinite-ring voice.
- Confirmed; the behaviour contradicts specs/141-membrum-phase6-ui/spec.md FR-021 (a macro at 0.5 "leaves underlying parameters at their un-macro-driven base values") and line 349 (offsets "relative to registered defaults (not live values)"); the SC-006 citation is a little loose. Also recommends the upgrade: Complexity hits modeInject the same way (kComplexityModeInjectSpan 0.30). The drift sits in the processor PadConfig that getState saves, while the controller's own cutoff / modeInject parameters do not move, so editor and engine disagree.
- Confirmed: linDelta(m,s) = (m-0.5)*s (lines 30-33); repeated sweeps move the value 0.2 further each time down to 0; the darkened value persists in VoicePool::padConfigs_, which getState serialises (state_codec.cpp:77). No test covers a sweep that hits the clamp (test_macro_preset_load_regression.cpp only checks setState byte round trips). This verifier judged medium adequate, since only a gesture that reaches a field's limit triggers it.

#### MB-208 — Physics (contradicted): Linear interpolation inside the loop gives exact fractional delay and keeps the loop gain flat (the code comment's claim)

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:string-body

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/waveguide_string.h:6, 186-191](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/waveguide_string.h#L186-L191)

**Problem.** The loop is read with bridgeSideDelay_.readLinear(bridgeDelayFloat_) (:191). The comment at :187-190 says linear interpolation 'provides exact fractional delay at all frequencies (unlike allpass which has frequency-dependent delay)'. The file header (:6) advertises a 'Thiran fractional delay' that the code does not use. The repo's own DelayLine documentation (delay_line.h:42-43) says readLinear is 'for modulated delays' and readAllpass is 'for feedback loops'. Measured at 48 kHz with Material 1 (S = 0, which string_mapper.h:50-52 describes as 'flat loop gain => all harmonics survive equally') and T60 4 s, for f0 = 790..826 Hz (Size near 0). With fractional delay 0.000 (f0 800), the 10th harmonic's T60 is 4.475 s. With fractional delays 0.11-0.90, it is 0.108-0.161 s. The fundamental's T60 is 2.54-3.49 s against the 4 s that was set.

**Why wrong.** Linear interpolation is the one-zero FIR (1-d) + d z^-1. Its gain is cos(w/2) at d = 0.5, with a zero at Nyquist, and its phase delay depends on frequency except at d = 0 and d = 0.5. Inside a loop this adds damping that depends on d at every round trip. The textbook remedy is a first-order allpass (Thiran) tuning filter, H_eta(z) = (eta + z^-1)/(1 + eta z^-1) with eta = (1-d)/(1+d), keeping d in [eps, 1+eps). It has unity gain and costs the same as linear interpolation. Lagrange order 3 or higher also works if a small HF loss is accepted.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- J.O. Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Delay-Line Interpolation' [textbook] https://www.dsprelated.com/freebooks/pasp/Delay_Line_Interpolation.html: Linear interpolation is attenuated near half the sampling rate and is 'nowhere flat within the passband'. Amplitude errors 'can be highly audible (particularly when the loop gain is close to 1)' in feedback loops such as string models. First-order allpass interpolation 'costs the same as linear interpolation' and 'has no gain distortion'.
- J.O. Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Fractional Delay Filtering by Linear Interpolation' [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Fractional_Delay_Filtering_Linear.html: Linear interpolation is a one-zero FIR filter and is accurate only at low frequencies. Amplitude-response errors are highly audible in feedback loops, and allpass interpolation is suggested to remove them.
- J.O. Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Extended Karplus-Strong Algorithm' [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Extended_Karplus_Strong_Algorithm.html: EKS tunes with a first-order string-tuning allpass H_eta(z) = -(eta - z^-1)/(1 - eta z^-1), with eta in [-1/11, 2/3] for delays of 0.2..1.2 samples, offset to [eps, 1+eps).

**Consequence.** Very audible, and it makes Size an erratic brightness control. A 0.6 % move of Size (790 to 800 Hz) changes the 8 kHz partial's ring from 0.11 s to 4.5 s, a factor of 40. The fundamental decays up to 37 % faster than the Decay knob says. Material 1 ('bright, all harmonics survive') is bright only when the loop length happens to be an integer number of samples. Which pads land on an integer depends on the sample rate (48000/800 = 60 exactly), so a kit sounds brighter or duller at 44.1 kHz than at 48 kHz. The String body's brightness is largely random across pads, which hides the Material control.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: not ruled in 2026-06. That research verdict (findings.json, the loss-filter entry) checked only the loss filter and the pick comb and never looked at the read interpolator. The readLinear call predates that audit and is unchanged.

**Suggested fix.** Replace readLinear(D) with an integer read of floor(D - eps) plus a first-order Thiran allpass whose fractional part is in [eps, 1+eps) (DelayLine::readAllpass already exists). Re-derive the delay budget with the allpass phase delay at f0, or simply use retune()'s exact budget D = period - 1 - dLoss - dDisp - dDC - dAP. For retune() glides, crossfade two allpass taps or use Lagrange 3, since a jump in the allpass state causes a transient. WaveguideString is shared with Innexus (innexus_voice.h), so both suites must be gated. Pinning test: with brightness 0 at 48 kHz, f0 in {790, 795, 800, 805, 810, 815, 820, 826}, the T60 of harmonic 10 must stay within +/-15 % of the T60 that was set, and the fundamental's T60 within +/-10 %. Also correct the comments at :6 and :187-190.

**Verifier notes**
- Holds from source and a hand check (no render run). Membrum reaches the path: string_body.h:30 owns the WaveguideString, configureForNoteOn (:47-58) sets it up, and all three renderers call WaveguideString::process (string_body.h:66, :75, :87-88). The header's Thiran / "allpass interpolation in feedback loop" claims (:6, :16) are not implemented (lines 843, 873 say readLinear handles the fraction); readAllpass exists (delay_line.h:167, :417). Nothing compensates the interpolator loss: computeRho (:596-601) and noteOn's gTotal (:394-399) model only the loss filter, and D (:337) leaves an f0-dependent fraction. Mapper: f0 = 800*0.1^size (string_mapper.h:40), brightness = 1 - material (:53). Hand check at 48 kHz, harmonic 10: |H| = 0.950 at d = 0.11 (T60 ≈ 0.17 s), 0.866 at d = 0.5 (≈ 0.06 s); fundamental at d = 0.5 ≈ 2.45 s. Severity kept high.
- Could not refute. The interpolator is inside the loop (:191 -> soft clip -> DC blocker -> dispersion -> loss filter :213 -> back into the delay :221); computeThiranPhaseDelay (:665) is never used for the loop read; readLinear (delay_line.h:372-384, :436-439) is `y0 + frac*(y1-y0)`, and a Thiran readAllpass already exists (:417-486). Analytic |H(w)| = sqrt(1 - 2d(1-d)(1-cos w)) reproduces the reported harmonic-10 range in order and direction, and the fundamental at d = 0.5 gives ≈ 3.0 s, inside the reported 2.54-3.49 s. The cited PASP pages say what the finding says.
- Confirmed but recommends a downgrade. The linear read is a documented deliberate choice: specs/_archive_/129-waveguide-string-resonance/spec.md:127 (FR-004, amended) mandates Lagrange-1 because Thiran gave 5-10 cent pitch errors, accepting the HF rolloff "as the loss filter already attenuates high frequencies". That premise fails in Membrum: Material 1 gives S = 0 (string_mapper.h:53, waveguide_string.h:184), and the interpolator's d spans [0,1) while Material only moves S over [0,0.5]. The numbers check analytically, the sample-rate dependence is real (:322, :337), and String is used in the factory kits (12 BodyModelType::String references in tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp). Downgrade reasons: the choice is documented; String covers only 80-800 Hz (string_mapper.h:40), so the fundamental error matters only near Size 0 (at Size 0.5 the interpolator's T60 term is about 200 s); the large effect is limited to upper partials at small Size and high Material on one of six bodies.

#### MB-210 — Physics (contradicted): The pitch envelope retunes the String waveguide (audit H-3 fix)

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:string-body

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h:121-130](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h#L121-L130) (with [drum_voice.h:1587-1593, 313-321](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1587-L1593); [waveguide_string.h:134-140, 175-183](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/waveguide_string.h#L134-L140))

**Problem.** retuneFundamental(pitchHz) for String calls bodyBank_.setStringFrequency, which calls string_.setFrequency(pitchHz) (body_bank.h:126-130). setFrequency only re-targets frequencySmoother_ (:134-140). That smoother feeds only rho = computeRho(exp2(logF), T60) (:175-183), the per-pass gain. The loop length bridgeDelayFloat_ is set only in noteOn (:341) or in retune() (:535), and Membrum never calls retune(). Measured at 48 kHz: noteOn(800) followed by setFrequency(100) still peaks at 799.06 Hz, and the magnitude at 100 Hz is 1.3e-5. retune(100) gives 100.00 Hz. The same call shortens the 800 Hz fundamental's T60 from 1.500 s to 0.241 s (set 2 s), because rho is now computed for 100 passes per second while the loop runs 800.

**Why wrong.** A waveguide's pitch is set by the total loop delay, the period, not by the loss gain. A pitch glide must change the delay length (with the fractional-delay filter) while keeping rho = 0.001^(1/(f_actual*T60)). The PASP EKS tuning allpass and WaveguideString::retune() (:515-544, which uses the exact budget D = period - 1 - dLoss - dDisp - dDC) do exactly this.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- J.O. Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Extended Karplus-Strong Algorithm' [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Extended_Karplus_Strong_Algorithm.html: Pitch is set by the delay-line length N plus the string-tuning allpass fractional delay. The damping filter |H_d| <= 1 sets decay, not pitch.
- J.O. Smith, 'One-Zero String Damping Filter' (CCRMA REALSIMPLE) [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/realsimple/faust_strings/One_Zero_String_Damping_Filter.html: rho = 0.001^(PT/t60) is tied to the actual loop period P. Using a frequency other than the actual one gives the wrong decay, which is what the measured 6x T60 shortening shows.

**Consequence.** On String pads the pitch envelope (808-style drop, tom glide) is still pitch-dead. Instead it silently changes the decay: a downward sweep shortens the ring about 6x, an upward sweep lengthens it. The user hears a choked hit, not a glide. The regression test test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp:143-189 passes vacuously. It compares only the zero-crossing rate early and late within the swept render, which falls in any case as the noise burst's HF decays.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 finding H-3 (pitch envelope inert on Plate/Shell/String/Bell/NoiseBody) is marked DONE in AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:33 and :241 ('String retunes its waveguide'). For String the fix (commit 5a6ab530, #245) routes through setFrequency, which does not move the pitch, so H-3 is still present for the String body. This repeats H-3.

**Suggested fix.** Add StringBody::retune(pitchHz) calling string_.retune(pitchHz), and make BodyBank::setStringFrequency call it instead of setFrequency. Throttle it to once per chunk, which matches the modal retune cadence, and leave the frequency smoother consistent with the real loop so rho stays matched. Pinning test: replace the zero-crossing check. Measure the fundamental by Goertzel peak search in the last 100 ms of a 800->100 Hz, 120 ms sweep and require 100 Hz +/-5 cents. Require the swept render's T60 within +/-15 % of the flat render's T60 at the end pitch.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute; every link checks out. drum_voice.h:1587-1593 routes String to setStringFrequency (the :1585 comment claims it "retunes via its frequency smoother"); body_bank.h:126-130 only calls setFrequency; waveguide_string.h:134-140 only re-targets the smoother, whose output feeds only cachedRho_ (:161, :175-183, :596-601); bridgeDelayFloat_ is assigned only in noteOn (:341) and retune() (:535), and the library's own doc (:548-551) says the smoother "feeds nothing but the loop-loss gain rho". A grep finds no `.retune(` or snapSmoothers in plugins/membrum; setStringFrequency has one caller (drum_voice.h:1590). test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp:143-189 only checks maxDiff > 1e-4 and a zero-crossing drop (:185-188), both satisfiable without any pitch change. The 799.06 Hz measurement was not re-run but agrees with the path. H-3 is still present for String; high fits.
- Confirmed; the call is reached from the noteOn seed (:318-321), the per-sample path (:1598) and the block paths (:745, :964); bridgeDelayFloat_ is otherwise written only in silence() (:259), and StringBody (string_body.h:43-59) only calls setFrequency then noteOn. Decay check: rho computed for 100 Hz while the loop runs about 800 passes/s gives 2 s × 100/800 = 0.25 s, matching the quoted 0.241 s. The PASP EKS page (fetched) defines N as the pitch period and the damping filter only needs |H_d| <= 1.
- Could not refute, and it is not a documented simplification: AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:33 and :241 mark H-3 DONE with "String retunes its waveguide", and body_bank.h:121-125 claims the same; String is a physical waveguide, not Unnatural Zone behaviour. The note-on seed (:320) already applies the wrong rho from the first sample, because it targets initialPitchHz while the loop sits at the mapper f0. Severity high, the same as the original H-3.

#### MB-232 — Physics (contradicted): Cross-pad 'sympathetic resonance' rings resonators tuned to the STRUCK voice's own partials, not the unstruck pads

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:coupling-models · **Also flagged by:** research:extra:snare-wire-and-sympathetic-claims

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h:38-40, 113-168, 179-259, 312-358](dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h#L179-L259); [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:243-248](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L243-L248); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1250-1258](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1250-L1258); [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:688-708](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L688-L708)

**Problem.** At noteOn, VoicePool calls couplingEngine_->noteOn(slot, getPartialInfo()) only for the voice being struck (voice_pool.cpp:243-248). getPartialInfo returns that voice's first 4 bank mode frequencies (drum_voice.h:1250-1258). Pads that have not been struck register no resonators. The processor feeds the mono sum (L+R)/2 through a 0.5-2 ms delay into SympatheticResonance::process, then an energy limiter (threshold 0.1 = -20 dBFS, processor.h:183-196), and adds the result to L and R. The engine's coupling gain maps amount 0..1 to -46..-26 dB (152-160). Membrum never calls setDecay, so userQ_ = 316.2. Q_eff = Q * clamp(500 / f, 0.5, 1); the resulting T60 = 6.908 Q / (pi f) is 11.6 s at 60 Hz, 6.95 s at 100 Hz, 3.5 s at 200 Hz and 0.35 s at 1 kHz. Resonators within 0.3 Hz merge. The header cites the piano sympathetic-string model (Lehtonen et al. 2007) for the gain range and for '4 partials capture 95 %'.

**Why wrong.** Sympathetic response in a kit is the forced response of an UNSTRUCK drum. The sound field from the struck drum drives the receiver's own modes at the receiver's own frequencies, and they decay with the receiver's own damping, so the response is largest where source partials coincide with receiver modes. A snare receiver responds with WIRE BUZZ (broadband collision noise), and only once its snare head passes the critical amplitude (F&R §18.13); practitioner guides state the same (toms tuned near the snare head make the wires buzz). A drum head's (01) mode loses its energy by radiation within about 0.5 s (F&R §18.10), so a receiver ringing 7-12 s is far longer than any drum. A resonator bank tuned to the struck voice's own partials is an artificial high-Q reverb of the source, not sympathetic response. Lehtonen 2007 describes piano strings coupled through the bridge and does not transfer to drums. No peer-reviewed measurement of kit sympathetic levels was found.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., §18.10 and §18.13, 1998 [textbook] https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf: The (01) mode of a side drum 'loses energy so rapidly (by sound radiation) that after a half second it has fallen below some of the antisymmetric modes'. Snares need a critical snare-head amplitude to sound at all.
- Yamaha Hub, 'Discover the sonic possibilities of your drums, part 2' [docs] https://hub.yamaha.com/drums/d-how-to/discover-the-sonic-possibilities-of-your-drums-part-2/: Practitioner guidance: a snare that buzzes when a tom is hit is cured by not tuning the toms close to the snare in pitch. The receiver (the snare head plus wires) responds to source energy near its own modes. Corroboration only.
- Long & McQuade, 'Sympathetic Snare Buzz: Symptoms, Causes and Cures' [blog] https://www.long-mcquade.com/blog/176/Sympathetic-Snare-Buzz-Symptoms-Causes-And-Cures.htm: Tom or kick partials near the snare-head modes make the wires vibrate. Weak corroboration, not the basis for the verdict.

**Consequence.** With Global Coupling up, striking the kick or a tom does not make the snare buzz or the other toms ring. It adds a faint (about -40 dB per SC-002) resonance at the struck drum's own first 4 partials that lasts 7-12 s at kick and tom pitches, longer than the drum itself. Kit interplay, a main reason a real kit sounds alive and not like 32 one-shots, is missing, and every kit gets the same generic tail. The SC-008 test ('mode-coincident toms couple at least 12 dB more', test_coupling_integration.cpp:518-607) strikes only pad 5. Pad 9 registers no resonators, so the energy it measures at 158.9 Hz comes from pad 5's own second partial, and the test passes whatever pad 9 is tuned to.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: none (2026-06 research[5] only noted CouplingMatrix as a separate inter-pad system with kMaxCoefficient 0.05 and gave no verdict on the sympathetic engine).

**Suggested fix.** Make the receivers the unstruck pads. At kit load or pad edit, register for every pad with couplingAmount > 0 its first N modes at the pad's natural frequencies, with damping from that pad's own DampingLaw (not Q 316). Drive receiver j with sum over i of gain[i][j] * (voice i output), using CouplingMatrix::effectiveGainArray() so that Kick->Snare and Tom->Tom routing exists. For Snare receivers, feed the receiver's amplitude into that pad's wire-noise path through the critical-amplitude law. Tests: (1) a kick-only hit with Snare Buzz 1 versus 0 must differ by at least 20 dB in snare wire-band energy, and Snare Buzz 0 must match coupling-off within -120 dB; (2) rewrite SC-008 so the receiver pad is NOT struck, and require at least 12 dB more energy at the receiver's f0 when it coincides with a driver partial than when it falls in a gap; (3) require a sympathetic T60 at most 1.5x the receiving pad's own T60.

**Verifier notes**
- Every cited site re-read; the code does what the finding says. Resonators are registered only in the struck slot's NoteOn branch (voice_pool.cpp:243-248), gated on that pad's couplingAmount > 0; noteOff calls appear only at voice_pool.cpp:167, 207, 272, 389, 1041. kSympatheticPartialCount = 4 (sympathetic_resonance.h:40, citing Lehtonen 2007). No Membrum setDecay call, so userQ_ = 316.2 (lines 128, 542); Q_eff (440-444) and r = exp(-pi f/(Q fs)) (426-436) give the quoted T60s; merge threshold 0.3 Hz (line 49). CouplingMatrix::effectiveGain is computed (processor.cpp:138) but read only by couplingMatrixForTest (processor.h:81). The SC-008 test (test_coupling_integration.cpp:518-732) strikes only note 41 (line 583), although its comment at 537-539 claims pad 9 is also struck. Severity kept: opt-in via Global Coupling and capped at -20 dBFS.
- Could not refute; adds that Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance never reach the audio: their cases (processor.cpp:411-423) only call recomputeCouplingMatrix (131-143), and effectiveGainArray() appears only in its own definition (coupling_matrix.h:85), so both knobs (registered at controller.cpp:517-526) are effectively dead. The SC-008 12 dB ratio follows from where the measurement bands sit relative to pad 5's own modes (158.9 Hz second mode vs a 130 Hz gap). The physics argument does not depend on any disputed source.
- Not a recorded simplification; the spec asks for the opposite. specs/140-membrum-phase5-coupling/spec.md requires snare-wire energy at the snare's modes when the kick is struck (US1 / SC-002, lines 85-95, 268), coupling proportional to the match with the destination pad's modes (FR-005, 193), Snare Buzz setting kick-to-snare gain (FR-013, 201), and a couplingAmount-0 pad excluded as receiver (FR-021, acceptance 147). snareBuzz_ / tomResonance_ are read only in recomputeCouplingMatrix (processor.cpp:131-143) and state I/O (887-889, 975-976). research.md documents only the insertion point and no prior audit rules on it. The SC-008 test is vacuous for receiver tuning.

#### MB-237 — Physics (contradicted): The configured pitch sweep (start -> end over Time) actually reaches the modal body on the paths a host uses

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:pitch-envelope-808

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:313-321, 589, 613-620, 703-746, 960-965](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L703-L746); [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:213, 431-434, 526-533, 647, 906-914](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L906-L914)

**Problem.** At note-on the body is set up with setModes at the Size-derived natural f0, which snaps the coefficients. The start pitch is then 'seeded' with retuneFundamental(initialPitchHz) (drum_voice.h:318-321). That goes to updateModalFundamentalOnBank -> ModalResonatorBank::updateModes, which writes only epsilonTarget_/radiusTarget_ (it never calls snapCoefficients, and there is no snapCoefficients call anywhere in plugins/membrum/src). Per block, processBlockFast reads the envelope ONCE per chunk (the chunk is the whole host block, capped at kMaxBlockSize = 2048) and retunes the target (734-746). processBlockSlow does the same once per block (960-965). The bank then moves its live coefficients toward the target ONCE per processBlock call (smoothCoefficients at 431-434, 906-914), using a coefficient sized for a PER-SAMPLE 2 ms one-pole: kSmoothingTimeMs = 2.0 (647), smoothCoeff_ = exp(-1/(0.002*fs)) (213), so it covers 1.13 % of the gap per block at 44.1 kHz. The sounding pitch therefore glides with a time constant of about 88 HOST BLOCKS whatever Time is set to.

MEASURED with a standalone probe (C:/Users/scab/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/af40cef86e602ebb/69f67fe4-9e20-4f6f-a325-fd4459c6f76b/scratchpad/pe_probe/probe.cpp: real DrumVoice linked against the build's KrateDSP.lib, default-kit kick pad config with noise, click and tension off, velocity 100, 44.1 kHz). It reads the bank's live epsilon_[0] and runs a Goertzel peak over the audio at 150-350 ms.
- Default-kit kick (160 -> 50 Hz, 20 ms): live f0 at t = 0 is 80.0 Hz on every path, so 160 Hz never sounds. Settled audio peak: 50.1 Hz per sample, 50.9 at 32-sample blocks, 55.0 at 64, 62.2 at 128, 69.0 at 256, 73.7 at 512, 76.8 at 1024, 78.4 at 2048.
- 808-kit kick (200 -> 40 Hz, 30 ms): 39.9 / 41.5 / 47.6 / 57.2 / 66.3 / 72.6 / 76.2 / 78.4 Hz.
- 909-kit kick (180 -> 55 Hz, 20 ms): 55.0 / 55.9 / 59.7 / 65.5 / 71.2 / 75.1 / 77.6 / 79.0 Hz.
- Live f0 at 512-sample blocks: 79.7 Hz at 20 ms, 77.5 at 100 ms, 63.9 at 800 ms.
- Even the per-sample process() path starts at 80 Hz and first glides UP toward the target (808 config: 103 Hz at 5 ms).

The H-3 regression test only reads getModeFrequency(0), which returns epsilonTarget_ (modal_resonator_bank.h:526-533), so it cannot see any of this.

**Why wrong.** A swept modal or magic-circle resonator needs its frequency coefficient eps(n) = 2 sin(pi f_n T) to follow the instantaneous frequency f_n per sample (JOS, PASP 'Digital Sinusoid Generators'), or on a short fixed control grid whose coefficients are snapped and not left to a per-block one-pole. The note must start with the coefficients AT the start frequency. The bank already offers this: snapCoefficients(), whose doc comment (modal_resonator_bank.h:314-323) explains that block-rate smoothing makes the trajectory depend on how the host splits its buffers, and that Seraphis' ContinuousBody retunes on a 64-sample grid and snaps for exactly this reason. Expected: post-sweep pitch equal to End within a few percent at every host block size, and the start pitch audible in the first period.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- J.O. Smith III, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Digital Sinusoid Generators' (CCRMA online book) [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Digital_Sinusoid_Generators.html: Magic-circle (modified coupled form) update x1(n) = x1(n-1) + eps*x2(n-1), x2(n) = -eps*x1(n) + x2(n-1), with eps = 2 sin(pi f_n T), where f_n is the instantaneous frequency at sample n. So the frequency coefficient is defined per sample, which is the form a swept resonator should follow.
- Werner, Abel & Smith, 'A Physically-Informed, Circuit-Bendable, Digital Model of the Roland TR-808 Bass Drum Circuit', DAFx-14, 2014 [paper] https://dafx14.fau.de/papers/dafx14_kurt_james_werner_a_physically_informed,_ci.pdf: The 808's defining pitch events happen within about 6 ms (an attack jump of more than an octave, 'less than a single period at the higher frequency'). A renderer whose pitch control lags by hundreds of ms cannot produce them.

**Consequence.** HIGH and audible. In a real host (128-1024-sample buffers) every pitch-swept pad, which includes every factory kick, the pitched toms and the timpani, plays at roughly its Size-derived natural f0 and then drifts slowly toward End over 0.3-2 s. The 'zap' / 'boom' attack is missing. The kick settles 4-7 semitones sharp (73.7 Hz instead of 50 Hz at 512 samples). The sound changes with the host buffer size (78.4 Hz at 2048 vs 50.1 Hz offline), and the 44.1 / 48 / 96 kHz renders differ for the same buffer length in samples. This flattens the main pitch-motion axis that sets kicks and toms apart, so kits sound more alike and more static. The same lag applies to the tension-modulation glide, which goes through the same updateModalFundamentalOnBank call (746-754). The String body retunes its waveguide directly and was not probed.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 signal-path audit, findings.json confirmed[17], 'Pitch envelope refresh is block-rate coarse and diverges between fast and slow paths' (no H/M/L id in the .md tracker; not remediated). The correctness lens rated it medium and the audibility lens low, on the stated premise that the bank's coefficient smoothing 'ramps rather than hard-stepping' and so blunts the staircase. Measurement refutes that premise: the per-block application of a per-sample 2 ms smoother is the dominant failure, stretching every sweep to about 88 host blocks. H-3 (marked DONE) 'seeds the START pitch on every body', but only into the target, so the start pitch is still never heard. The code is unchanged in substance since that audit: the bank smoothing has been 2 ms per block since #215, and the fast and slow paths still retune once per chunk. Upgrade to high.

**Suggested fix.**
1. In DrumVoice::noteOn, after retuneFundamental(initialPitchHz) (drum_voice.h:320), call bodyBank_.getSharedBank().snapCoefficients(); the state was just cleared by setModes, so a snap is click-free.
2. In processBlockFast and processBlockSlow, when pitchEnvActive || tensionActive, split each chunk into a fixed control grid of at most 32 samples (about 0.7 ms at 44.1 kHz). Read the envelope at each sub-block's sample index, call updateModes, then snapCoefficients(), the way Seraphis' ContinuousBody does. Otherwise use a per-sample epsilon ramp.
3. Fix the comments that claim '64-sample block, ~14 update points' (613-620, 703-707).

Tests: (a) render the default-kit kick through DrumVoice::processBlock at block sizes 1, 32, 64, 512 and 2048; require the Goertzel peak over 150-350 ms within +/-3 % of 50 Hz for all, and within 1 % of the per-sample render. (b) Require the dominant frequency over the first 3 ms (or the first zero-crossing period) at 0.85 x Start or higher. (c) Change test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp to measure the rendered audio instead of getModeFrequency(0), which reads the target.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute; every link re-read. The seed goes through updateModalFundamentalOnBank (drum_voice.h:1607-1627) to updateModes, which writes targets only; setModes snaps via computeModeCoefficients(...,true) (modal_resonator_bank.h:258-275); snapCoefficients (342) is called only in continuous_body.h:2860 (Seraphis). The whole host block reaches each voice unsplit (processor.cpp:636/663, voice_pool.cpp:356/471), and membrane_body.h:68 calls bank.processBlock once. The slow path retunes once per block (960-972) with one prepareBlockSmoothing (1002). test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp:123/127/243/245 measures through getModeFrequency, i.e. the target. The cited probe file exists and its numbers fit the mechanism. Repeats 2026-06 confirmed[17] with a stronger, measured mechanism; high justified.
- Could not refute. setModes snaps live coefficients (mrb.h:272-273, 877-881); updateModes (294-305) writes targets only, and mrb.h:325 itself says no existing call path invokes snapCoefficients. The smoother runs once per processBlock (431-433, 450-453) or prepareBlockSmoothing (386-389). Cross-check: at 512 samples, 150-350 ms is 13-30 blocks, closing 14-29 % of the 80 -> 50 Hz gap, about 72-76 Hz against the reported 73.7 Hz; per-sample process() smooths every sample (421-424) and converges near 50.1 Hz. The JOS 'Digital Sinusoid Generators' page (opened) defines eps = 2 sin(pi f_n T) per sample.
- Confirmed; the probe exists (scratchpad pe_probe/probe.cpp and probe.exe) and its numbers fit the arithmetic: a time constant of about 88 host blocks (about 1 s at 512 samples). The deviation is not intended: the comments at drum_voice.h:613-620 and 703-707 claim about 14 refresh points and no stair-stepping. The prior audit's low / medium ratings rested on a wrong premise; this is not Unnatural Zone behaviour and no simplification ruling covers losing the sweep. Every pitch-swept factory kick is affected and changes with buffer size; severity stays high.

#### MB-258 — Physics (contradicted): Cross-pad coupling makes idle drums ring in sympathy ('kick makes snare wires buzz', Snare Buzz / Tom Resonance route energy through a category matrix into other pads' excitation)

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:extra:snare-wire-and-sympathetic-claims

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/MANUAL.md:426-437](plugins/membrum/MANUAL.md#L426-L437) (code: [processor.cpp:131-143, 411-424, 693-706](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L411-L424); [voice_pool.cpp:243-248](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L243-L248); [sympathetic_resonance.h:179-249, 312-348](dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h#L179-L249))

**Problem.** The manual says the struck pad's output 'is mixed into other pads' excitation paths according to a coupling matrix', which models the snare buzzing on a kick and toms ringing in sympathy. The code does something else.
1. Only the STRUCK voice registers resonators, at its own first 4 bank modes (voice_pool.cpp:243-248, getPartialInfo drum_voice.h:1250-1258). An idle pad has no voice and therefore no resonator.
2. The delayed mono mix drives that pool, and the result is added to outL/outR (processor.cpp:698-706), not to any pad's exciter.
3. kSnareBuzzId and kTomResonanceId only call recomputeCouplingMatrix() (processor.cpp:411-424), which fills couplingMatrix_. Nothing on the audio path reads it; the only reader is couplingMatrixForTest() (processor.h:81). git history: getEffectiveGain was only ever read by the UI matrix-activity publisher, which commit 40d9aac6 removed. That commit's message says the Tier 1 category math 'was always doing the useful work'. Per-pad Coupling Amount acts only as a >0 gate (voice_pool.cpp:243-244).
4. Test SC-008 (tests/unit/processor/test_coupling_integration.cpp:518-600) strikes only pad 5. The 'receiver' pad 9 never sounds, so its Size cannot reach the engine. The asserted 12 dB difference is pad 5's own (1.594) mode at about 158.9 Hz against a gap at 130 Hz. SC-002 (:240-285) only compares global coupling on and off.

**Why wrong.** In a kit, every drum is an undamped receiver whether or not it was struck. Airborne pressure and the hardware drive an idle drum's heads, and it responds at its OWN modes, strongest where they coincide with the driver's spectrum. On a snare, motion of the snare-side head launches the wires, so a kick produces buzz (Rossing 1992; Bilbao/Torin). The correct form: every enabled pad with couplingAmount > 0 keeps its first N modes as receiver resonators, present even when the pad is idle. Each receiver is driven by sum over sources of effectiveGain[src][dst] * delayed source output, using the category matrix that recomputeCouplingMatrix already builds. A snare-category receiver's output should also drive that pad's wire/noise layer, so that kick-induced buzz is noise, not a pure tone. The current engine follows the piano-pedal design of spec 132 (resonators at the sounding notes' partials, 'don't model who excites whom', spec 132:235). For drums that mostly reinforces the struck drum's own partials.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of Drums', Physics Today 45(3), 1992 [paper] https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf: In a two-headed drum there is 'appreciable coupling between the two heads ... acoustically through the enclosed air or mechanically through the shell'. The snare head vibrates against the snares. Any drum's response is through its own (mode-paired) modes.
- S. Bilbao, A. Torin, V. Chatziioannou, 'Numerical Modeling of Collisions in Musical Instruments', Acta Acustica 2012 [paper] https://www.ness.music.ed.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/bilbao_acustica_r2.pdf: Snare model: the drum is 'immersed in a box of air' and the snares are launched by contact with the lower membrane, which pressure drives. Buzz is wire collision driven by snare-head motion, not a tuned resonance of the source drum.

**Consequence.** Two knobs on the Coupling panel, Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance, are dead: moving them changes nothing in the output. The headline effect the manual describes, a kick making an idle snare buzz or toms ringing in sympathy, cannot happen. Global Coupling instead adds a quiet tonal ring at the struck pad's own partials, the same for every kit and category, which adds to kits sounding generic. The SC-008 test passes vacuously and hides this. It also makes the about 96 recomputeCouplingMatrix calls per kit load (extra focus item 2) pure wasted work.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: none (not reported by the 2026-06 correctness audit or the 2026-06-07 signal-path audit; the matrix has been unread on the audio path since it was introduced, and 40d9aac6 removed its only reader, the UI).

**Suggested fix.** Either (A) implement receiver coupling: on prepare/kit load, register the first 4 modes of every enabled pad (couplingAmount > 0) as persistent receiver resonators tagged with their pad. Per block, feed each receiver group the delayed main-bus contribution of each source pad scaled by couplingMatrix_.getEffectiveGain(src, dst). VoicePool would need per-pad (or per-category, 5 buses) pre-mix taps to keep the cost bounded. Route snare-category receiver energy into that pad's wire/noise layer. Or (B) remove Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance and rewrite MANUAL.md:426-437. Tests to pin (A): (1) strike only the kick (note 36) and assert that output energy at the idle snare pad's mode frequencies and in 4-8 kHz rises at least 12 dB from Snare Buzz 0 to 1; (2) rewrite SC-008 so that changing the never-struck receiver's Size moves the coupling peak to the receiver's f0; (3) assert Tom Resonance 0 vs 1 changes tom-to-tom coupling energy by at least 12 dB.

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed from source. A grep for getEffectiveGain / couplingMatrix_ / couplingMatrixForTest finds only coupling_matrix.h:79, processor.h:81/145, the recompute call sites and the test files; nothing in process() or VoicePool reads the matrix. SympatheticResonance::process (sympathetic_resonance.h:312-324) scales its single input by the global amount only (setAmount :152-160). The matrix tests (test_coupling_integration.cpp:369-514, 818-878) assert only couplingMatrixForTest() values, never audio. Nuance that does not refute it: two ringing voices cross-excite through the shared mono mix, but at their own partials and never through the matrix. Severity left at high (no safety, crash or real-time hazard).
- Could not refute; the defect stands on the code alone. `git log -S getEffectiveGain` shows fc419e65 added the readers and 40d9aac6 removed both. The physics framing (Rossing 1992; Bilbao / Torin / Chatziioannou) is standard and correctly applied. Recommends lowering from high: a dead-parameter and documentation mismatch, both knobs default to 0, no instability, NaN, crash or RT violation.
- Confirmed from source and from this audit's measurement. Grep sites: coupling_matrix.h:79-87, processor.cpp:187-227, 415, 422, 988, 1012, processor.h:81. Not a documented simplification: spec 140 (spec.md:83-95, US1 P1) requires kick-induced energy at the snare's modes scaling with Snare Buzz, data-model.md:209-227 requires effectiveGain[src][dst], and spec 141:403 defers only the dedicated snare-wire DSP while keeping Snare Buzz as "the UX surface". 40d9aac6's claim that Tier 1 "was always doing the useful work" is false. Prior items L-7, L-9, M-6 concern the per-voice secondary shell, not cross-pad coupling. Measured: specs/membrum-audit/probes/param-audibility.csv:203-208 rates snareBuzz (271) and tomResonance (272) "bad", "bit-identical on all 3 base pads"; rows 200-202 and 110-112 show Global Coupling and per-pad couplingAmount moving the output by at most about 0.01 dB ("inaudibly weak").

#### MB-260 — FMImpulse strike normalisation is measured only at velocity 1.0, but the FM carrier frequency moves with velocity: on Bell bodies a vel-100 hit lands up to 3.7x (+11.3 dB) over the body budget and reaches the limiter (Glass Bell Garden 46, Latin Perc 46, LinnDrum CR-78 40)

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-gain-staging · **Dimension:** followup:strike-norm-miss-bell-pads

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1336-1338](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1336-L1338) (probe trigger(1.0f)); [drum_voice.h:302-304](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L302-L304) (call site); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/fm_impulse_exciter.h:83, 93](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/fm_impulse_exciter.h#L83-L93)

**Problem.** probeStrikePeakExcited drives the bank with the live exciter at a fixed velocity of 1.0 (drum_voice.h:1338 `exciterBank_.trigger(1.0f)`). For FMImpulse, velocity sets more than the amplitude. It also sets the carrier frequency, `baseFreq = 400.0f * std::pow(6.25f, velocity)` (fm_impulse_exciter.h:83), so 2500 Hz at v=1 and 1693 Hz at v=100/127, plus the sideband set (modulator = baseFreq x ratio). The excitation is tonal, and a Bell body has a few sparse high-Q modes. The bank's response to the played hit therefore depends on whether that velocity's carrier and sidebands land on a mode. The gain measured at 2500 Hz is then applied to a hit at a different frequency. In effect this is a fourth cause beside the critic's (a)/(b)/(c): the probe excitation's spectrum differs from the note's.

**Why wrong.** kBodyHeadroom (drum_voice.h:286-306, audit N-1) promises the configured body's strike peak at 0.5 x level for a canonical hard strike, with softer hits below that. A gain measured with one excitation spectrum is valid only for an excitation with the same spectrum. Here the spectrum depends on velocity, so the normalisation holds only at v=1.0. Critic candidates checked: (b), the 30 ms window, is not the cause, because these pads peak at 2-15 ms. (a), the mallet hint, does not apply to FMImpulse. (c) adds at most 0.66 dB: no single post-bank stage changes these pads' peak by more than that (dDriveFold/dFilter/dModeInject/dNlc/dNoise/dClick/dShell/dPitchEnv/dTension/dMorph are all <= 0.66 dB on LinnDrum 40, <= 0.33 dB on GBG 46 and 0.00 dB on Latin 46).

**Consequence.** One ordinary velocity-100 hit on these bells drives the main bus into the -1 dBTP limiter, and on Glass Bell Garden 46 it also crosses the voice hardClip rail. Level does not rise with velocity. It is jagged: GBG 46 is +2.26 dBFS at v=0.78, -3.68 at v=0.875, +1.61 at v=0.9375 and -6.60 at v=1.0. LinnDrum 40 is -10.56 dBFS at v=0.75 and -3.08 at v=0.78, a 7.5 dB jump over one 1/32 velocity step. A soft hit can be 9 dB louder than a full hit. Of 66 enabled FMImpulse factory pads, 14 exceed the linear budget by more than 3 dB at vel 100: GBG 46 1.85x, GBG 44 1.48x, Latin 46 1.37x, LinnDrum 40 1.31x, Chaos Engine 53/44/40, Cajon and Frames 51, World Metal 60/65/63, Acoustic Studio 56, Ghost Bones 40, and Experimental FX 36/37. The impact exciters show the same mechanism, weaker. Contact time scales by `pow(max(1-v,0.01),0.2)` and the cutoff by `exp2(1.5 v)` (impact_exciter.h:129-139, 171), so the v=1 probe pulse is 0.54x as long as a vel-100 pulse. 4 of 101 Mallet pads exceed +3 dB, worst World Metal 67 at 1.22x. Impulse peaks at 0.62x, NoiseBurst at 0.56x and Clap at 0.34x, so those three stay within budget. The 0.5 ms amp-envelope attack (drum_voice.h:159) also hides the v=1 peak of very short strikes: World Metal 67 renders at 0.33x at v=1.

**Evidence.** Probe TU specs/membrum-audit/probes/audit_limiter_probe.cpp.txt (hidden [.][audit-probe], 48 kHz, block 256, DrumVoice + State::applyPadSnapshot + applyPadConfigToVoice, fresh voice per render). Results are in specs/membrum-audit/probes/limiter-pads.csv, limiter-velocity-sweep.csv and limiter-probe-summary.txt. The 'neutral' renders zero drive/fold, bypass the filter (cutoff 1, env 0.5), and set modeInject, NLC, noise mix, click mix, shell, pitch env, tension and morph to 0. Normalised peak = peak/(level x vel); 0.5 means the probe is right. Results per pad, n787 / n1 (neutral normalised peak at vel 100/127 / at vel 1.0), pre-limiter peak (x pan gain):
- GBG 46 FMImpulse/Bell size .22 level .688 pan .74 -> 1.846 / 0.500 (peak at 10.5 ms / 3.2 ms), pre-limiter +2.24 dBFS.
- Latin Perc 46 -> 1.369 / 0.500, -0.72 dBFS.
- LinnDrum 40 -> 1.313 / 0.500, -0.21 dBFS.
- GBG 44 -> 1.483 / 0.500, -1.71 dBFS.

At v=1 all four sit exactly at 0.500, so the probe is exact at the velocity it measures. Velocity sweep, GBG 46 pre-limiter dBFS: v .25 -22.34, .5 -3.78, .625 -6.62, .75 -2.93, .781 +2.26, .875 -3.68, .9375 +1.61, 1.0 -6.60. Code: drum_voice.h:1338 `exciterBank_.trigger(1.0f);`; fm_impulse_exciter.h:83 `const float baseFreq = 400.0f * std::pow(6.25f, velocity); // 400 → 2500`; :93 `carrierAmplitude_ = velocity;`. Pan gain also contributes: GBG 46 panGain 1.298 (+2.3 dB), and pan already has its own reported finding.

**Suggested fix.** Normalise against the excitation the note actually uses. Probe at the note's own velocity, adding velocity to StrikeNormKey with the gain cached per velocity bucket, then rescale the result so the budget stays tied to velocity. Alternatively, make the exciter's spectral parameters independent of velocity at the probe: probe the FM carrier at the note's carrier frequency, and keep the velocity law to amplitude only. A cheaper option is to tie the FM base frequency to the pad's natural fundamental (naturalFundamentalHz_), so ratio and velocity no longer sweep it through the bell's modes. Regression test: render the GBG 46 / Latin 46 / LinnDrum 40 configs (state codec from the factory .vstpreset) at velocities 0.25..1.0 in 1/32 steps with the post-chain neutral. Assert that the peak is monotonic non-decreasing in velocity within 1 dB, and that it stays <= 0.5 x level x 1.12 at every velocity.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute. drum_voice.h:302-304 -> measuredStrikeOutputGain (1394-1411) -> probeStrikePeakExcited (1322-1363), which triggers the exciter and the click layer at 1.0 (:1338, :1340); gain = kBodyHeadroom / peak (:1386). StrikeNormKey (1717-1727) holds neither velocity nor the FM ratio. In FMImpulseExciter::trigger velocity moves the carrier (:83), the modulator (baseFreq * ratio, :86), the modulation index (0.5 + 2.5 v, :90) and the amplitude (:93). In limiter-velocity-sweep.csv every pad sits at 0.500 at v=1.0 while the three FM/Bell pads swing 0.14-1.87 and their dominant frequency jumps between body modes; the non-FM controls (GBG 57, World Metal 55) rise smoothly and stay at or below about 0.67. limiter-probe-summary.txt:7, 120-135: n=66, max 1.85, 14 pads above 0.707.
- Confirmed. No spec makes the normalisation v=1-only by design: the comment at 1336 only names v=1 as the reference, and the intent (286-299, N-1) is a bounded body budget; the velocity-to-carrier sweep exists for timbre (FR-016 / SC-004 centroid), not for +11 dB level jumps. Only exciter-level tests cover it (test_fm_impulse_exciter.cpp:41, 63). Severity kept: the aux buses are pre-limiter and see the overs, and the jagged velocity response is audible. Caveat: some non-monotonicity is inherent in sweeping an FM carrier across sparse modes, so the fix also needs a design decision on how far velocity should move the carrier.
- Mechanism confirmed, impact partly overstated; recommends a downgrade. "Crosses the voice hardClip rail" does not hold: for GBG 46 at v=.787 the voice peak is 1.846 × 0.688 × 0.787 ≈ 0.9995; the +2.24 dBFS includes the 1.298 pan gain (+2.27 dB), so the mono voice sits at about -0.01 dBFS, touching the rail (drum_voice.h:566/885) without exceeding it. The limiter consequence is small and partly due to the separately reported pan gain: without pan GBG 46 is about 0 dBFS.

#### MB-265 — Tone-shaper filter is nearly dead on any voice slot whose last filtered state was open: the SVF g-smoother takes 20-55 ms (not 5 ms) to come down, so a hat at LP 317 Hz plays 46 dB louder on a fresh slot than on a warm one

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-layers-shaper · **Dimension:** followup:toneshaper-filter-glide · **Also flagged by:** followup:velocity-timbre-inversion

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:74-83, 151-156, 319-363, 427-457](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h#L319-L363)

**Problem.** ToneShaper::prepare sets the cutoff to 20 kHz while smoothing is still off (svf.h:204-211 updates g_ immediately), then enables smoothing (tone_shaper.h:79-83). At note-on, applyPadConfigToVoice (voice_pool.cpp:232 -> pad_config_apply.h:78-86) calls setFilterType / setFilterCutoff, which set only gTarget_ and the mix targets. ToneShaper::noteOn then calls filter_.resetIntegrators() (tone_shaper.h:348). That clears the integrator state but leaves g_, k_ and m0..m2 where the slot's previous note left them. On a never-used slot that is g = tan(pi*20000/fs). The smoother is a one-pole on g with a 5 ms time constant (svf.h:147-153, 494-516, 529-535). Because g = tan(pi fc/fs) is nearly linear in fc only at low frequencies, a downward move spans 3-4 decades of g. In log frequency it takes many time constants. Exact float simulation of advanceSmoother (svf-glide-times.txt), from 20 kHz to the target, gives the time until g is within 2x (about 1 octave) of the target:
- 44.1 kHz: 20 Hz 42.4 ms, 300 Hz 28.8 ms, 1 kHz 22.7 ms.
- 48 kHz: 20 Hz 39.8 ms, 300 Hz 26.2 ms, 1 kHz 20.1 ms.
- 96 kHz: 20 Hz 35.3 ms, 300 Hz 21.7 ms, 1 kHz 15.6 ms.
