Within one semitone takes 30-57 ms. The effective cutoff for a 20 Hz target at 44.1 kHz is still 16.7 kHz at 5 ms, 10.5 kHz at 10 ms and 1.76 kHz at 20 ms. A hat, click or snare transient therefore passes almost unfiltered, while the tail (where the filter does work) holds little energy. Upward moves are fast: 3.3-3.5 ms to within 2x, because g grows toward a large target. So the asymmetry penalises exactly the useful direction: closing the filter.

**Why wrong.** A per-note tone parameter must give the same timbre on every hit of the pad. The SVF smoother exists to de-click parameter automation on a continuous signal (svf.h:231-235). At note-on the integrators have just been zeroed (tone_shaper.h:348), so no state continuity is left to protect. SVF::reset() (svf.h:277-287) already snaps g/k/mix to their targets, and the svf.h snapToTarget docstring (300-308) recommends a snap 'on note retrigger'. The noteOn comment at tone_shaper.h:328-331 rejects snapToTarget only because snapToTarget does not clear the integrators. Clearing them AND snapping (that is, reset()) removes the objection. The MB-042 finding ('glides ... over 5 ms') understates the effect: 5 ms is the time constant of a linear smoother on g, not the time to reach the cutoff.

**Consequence.** The temporary probe (specs/membrum-audit/probes/filter-glide.csv) rendered a real Processor at 48 kHz with 16 buses. The same pad and the same parameters were hit on a fresh slot and on a slot warmed by the same pad. The first 500 ms RMS:
- Default-kit hat (42), LP 317 Hz: fresh -49.84 dBFS, warm -95.92 dBFS (bypass -48.99). The fresh hit is 0.85 dB from bypass, the warm hit 46 dB down. Centroid over the first 50 ms: 6229 Hz fresh, 3061 Hz warm.
- Hat, LP 20 Hz: fresh -49.86, warm -98.03.
- Snare (38), LP 317 Hz: rms500 -36.01 vs -36.82, but energy above 2 kHz in the first 50 ms is 29.1 dB vs -6.1 dB, a 35 dB brightness difference (centroid 2476 vs 333 Hz).
- Snare, LP 20 Hz: -36.25 vs -65.35.
- Hat, HP 632 Hz: fresh lets 12.5 dB more energy below 400 Hz through than warm (lo50 -47.59 vs -60.11).
- Filter Env Amount -1 / 0 / +1 on the hat at LP 317 Hz: fresh -49.85 / -49.84 / -49.77 (0.08 dB span); warm -98.26 / -95.92 / -72.89 (25 dB span).

At 44.1 kHz the results are the same (hat LP 317 Hz: fresh -50.73, warm -88.14). So on a fresh or open-history slot, Filter Cutoff, Filter Type, Resonance and the whole filter envelope are effectively dead for hats, clicks, rimshots and snare attacks. On a warm slot they work. The user hears the same pad alternate between filtered and unfiltered.

Factory exposure, decoded from the 20 .vstpreset files (factory-filter-pads.csv): 85 of 459 enabled pads engage the filter (30 LP, 38 HP, 17 BP), 60 of them with a non-zero envelope amount. That includes:
- every snare in Acoustic Studio, Rock, Vintage Wood, Orchestral, 808, 909, LinnDrum and Trap (LP 5-11.5 kHz with an envelope);
- the HP 800 Hz open hats (Acoustic Studio 46, 808 46);
- the Orchestral hats (HP 1449 Hz);
- all 16 Ghost Bones pads.

**Evidence.**
- tone_shaper.h:79-83 'filter_.prepare(sampleRate); ... filter_.setCutoff(filterCutoffHz_); ... filter_.enableSmoothing(true);' (filterCutoffHz_ = 20000.0f at :489).
- tone_shaper.h:348 'filter_.resetIntegrators();' with no snap.
- svf.h:204-211 setCutoff: 'if (smoothingEnabled_) { gTarget_ = computeG(cutoffHz_); }'.
- svf.h:295-298 resetIntegrators clears ic1eq_/ic2eq_ only.
- svf.h:510-516 'g_ += smoothCoeff_ * gDiff;'.
- svf.h:531-532 'smoothCoeff_ = 1 - exp(-1/(smoothingTimeSec_ * sr))' with kDefaultSmoothingTimeSec = 0.005f (:153).
- svf.h:489-491 computeG = tan(pi*hz/fs).
- voice_pool.cpp:232-233 'applyPadConfigToSlot(slot, padIndex); VP_VOICES[slot].noteOn(clampedVel);'.
- Measurement (svf-glide-times.txt): 44.1 kHz, 20000->20 Hz: gStart 6.80, gTarget 0.00142, t(within 2x) 42.4 ms; fc at 5/10/20/30 ms = 16702/10451/1758/256 Hz.
- Probe filter-glide.csv rows '48000,42,LP317Hz,priority_fresh,0,0,0,-39.84,-49.84,6229,16.90,...' vs '48000,42,LP317Hz,priority_warm_samepad,1,0,0,-85.92,-95.92,3061,-33.84,...'; hat LP20Hz fresh -49.86 vs warm -98.03; snare LP317Hz hi50 29.10 vs -6.11.
- Probe TU: specs/membrum-audit/probes/audit_filter_glide_probe.cpp.txt.

**Suggested fix.** In ToneShaper::noteOn, replace filter_.resetIntegrators() with filter_.reset(). reset() zeroes the integrators and snaps g/k/m0..m2 to the targets that applyPadConfigToVoice has just set. The envelope's first update (cutoffUpdateCounter_ forced to kCutoffUpdateInterval) then starts from base * 8^0 = base, so no jump remains. Keep the smoother for in-note envelope modulation. Regression test (processor level, multi-bus):
1. Max polyphony 4, policy Priority (slot 0 reused). Set pad 42 to LP 317 Hz. Hit twice, 1 s apart, with note-off at +100 ms.
2. REQUIRE that the hit-1 and hit-2 rms500 are within 1 dB, and that energy above 2 kHz in the first 50 ms is within 2 dB. Today: 46 dB and 51 dB apart.
3. Add a ToneShaper unit case: prepare(), setFilterCutoff(300), noteOn(), white noise in. REQUIRE output RMS in the first 5 ms at least 20 dB below input RMS.

**Verifier notes**

At note-on pad_config_apply.h:80-86 sets only targets (svf.h:206-207, 223-224, 190-191), and DrumVoice::noteOn (drum_voice.h:224) -> ToneShaper::noteOn clears only the integrators (svf.h:295-298). The only full SVF::reset() (svf.h:277-287) is reached via ToneShaper::reset (tone_shaper.h:120-128) from resetForKitSwitch (drum_voice.h:477). Glide math at 48 kHz, 20 kHz -> 317 Hz: g0 3.73, gt 0.0208, 5 ms × ln(178) ≈ 26 ms, matching the claimed 26.2 ms. A bypassed filter (tone_shaper.h:427-429) never advances the smoother, which explains fresh vs warm; the forced envelope update (351, 449-455) only re-sets the target. CSV rows confirmed; in the oldest_rotation run, hit 4 (slot 0 reused) drops to -84.72.

Not intended: the noteOn comment (tone_shaper.h:321-347) rejects snapToTarget only because it keeps stale integrator energy, and svf.h:289-294 concerns in-note modulation. reset() does both, so the suggested fix is valid.

Under oldest-voice rotation slots 1-3 also play unfiltered (lines 165-167), so the first hit on each of the 16 slots in a session plays unfiltered. Impact caveats, not enough to lower severity: the 46 dB headline uses a probe-set LP 317 Hz on the default hat, whose factory filter is bypassed; factory snares at LP 5-11.5 kHz glide only about 12 ms, giving a brighter first ~10 ms rather than 46 dB; HP factory pads let lows through in the attack.

#### MB-109 — Body-damping default is written four different ways; factory kits store explicit B1/B3 on 429 of 459 pads, so Decay does not change the modal ring

**Severity:** high · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** duplication · **Dimension:** duplication-drift

**Location:** [tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:131-136](tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp#L131-L136)

**Problem.** The 'no damping override' default exists as -1.0f sentinel (pad_config.h:282-283, voice_common_params.h), 0.5 (controller.cpp:227-228 per-pad, :621-625 proxy), 0.40 (generator Pad struct :135-136, with the comment 'The PadConfig sentinel ... cannot survive the controller's normalised parameter system, so write explicit mid-range defaults') and 0.4 (drum_voice.h:1472-1473 shell fallback). dampingLawFromParams (membrane_mapper.h:64-80) REPLACES law.b1/b3 whenever the value is >= 0, and every modal mapper (membrane :177, plate :95, shell :93, bell :90, noise_body :149) routes decayTime only through it. So with both overrides set, decayTime has no effect on the bank. decayTime is built from Decay, Material, Size, decaySkew bias and the Tightness / Body Size macro decay deltas. I parsed all 20 shipped kits: 459 enabled pads, 0 sentinels, 429 non-String pads with both B1 and B3 >= 0.

**Why wrong.** Decay is a primary Simple-view knob ('Decay', editor.uidesc:235). The sentinel design (pad_config.h:280-281: '-1.0f sentinel means derive from decay/material via mapper') exists so that Decay drives the ring. The generator works around the controller's lack of a sentinel encoding by duplicating a different default, which turns the sentinel path off for every factory pad.

**Consequence.** After loading any factory kit, turning Decay (or the decay part of Material, Tightness or Body Size) on a Membrane / Plate / Shell / Bell / NoiseBody pad leaves the body's ring length unchanged. Only modeInject decay, the NoiseBody noise bed and String still react. The same knob works on a fresh instance (DefaultKit keeps sentinels) and stops working after a factory or controller-saved kit load, so behaviour depends on how the kit was loaded.

**Evidence.** generator.cpp:135-136 'double bodyDampingB1 = 0.40; double bodyDampingB3 = 0.40;'. membrane_mapper.h:71-78 'if (params.bodyDampingB1 >= 0.0f) { ... law.b1 = 0.2f + n * 49.8f; }'. drum_voice.h:1472-1473 '(bodyDampingB1_ >= 0.0f) ? bodyDampingB1_ : 0.4f'. Probe (scratchpad damp.js over plugins/membrum/resources/presets/Kit Presets): '{ total: 459, sentinel: 0, overridden: 429 }'; e.g. 'Acoustic/Acoustic Studio Kit.vstpreset v5 enabled=28 bothOverridden(nonString)=28 sentinel=0'.

**Suggested fix.** Give the damping overrides a representable 'auto' encoding in one place: either a separate per-pad 'Damping Override' toggle offset, or map normalised 0 to 'auto' with the override range on (0,1]. Make PadConfig, controller registration, generator and drum_voice.h:1472 use that single constant, and regenerate the factory kits with 'auto' where the pad's decay should be knob-driven. Test: for each factory kit, sweep Decay 0.1 to 0.9 on an enabled Membrane pad and require the -60 dB time to change by at least 2x (it is unchanged today).

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed on the mechanism and the factory-kit claim, with one inaccuracy about DefaultKit (the default kit sets explicit b1/b3 on some pads; see the next note). The bodies pass only r.damping to the bank (membrane_body.h:37-40, plate_body.h:37-40, shell_body.h:33-36, bell_body.h:33-36, noise_body.h:64-67); only string_body.h:50 uses decayTime directly. decay_ is otherwise read only at drum_voice.h:185, 1525 and 331 (modeInject), and the amp envelope is fixed (159-162). The macros write only cfg.decay / decaySkew (macro_mapper.cpp:136-141, 173-175). The generator never writes -1. Decay is a primary 56 px knob in SelectedPadSimple (editor.uidesc:152-153), while Damp b1/b3 appear only in Advanced (244-247). MANUAL.md:206 calls Decay "Global decay-time scaling", and MANUAL.md:237's promise holds false because the controller default 0.5 (controller.cpp:227-228) is itself an override.
- Refutes it as drift: this is the documented precedence rule. MANUAL.md:237 presents Decay / Material as convenience derivations; PRESET-RETUNE-PLAN.md:101 and preset-retune/00-param-dictionary.md:13 say Decay is "overridden by b1"; PRESET-RETUNE-PLAN.md:99 says the generator's 0.40/0.40 is knowingly not neutral and modal pads "must set b1/b3 explicitly"; archetype docs call b1 "the real ring-length control". The default kit sets explicit b1/b3 on purpose (default_kit.h:130-131 snare, 249-250 cymbal, 323-324 clap) and keeps the sentinel on the tom (171-174). Each differing value carries its own justification (generator :131-134, controller.cpp:221-226, controller_state_codec.cpp:252-262), and drum_voice.h:1472-1473 is the shell bank's own fallback, not a fourth copy. Residual narrower point: MANUAL.md:237 says "default position", but the b1/b3 knob default 0.5 is an override, so resetting the knob does not bring Decay back.
- Confirmed: the law has only b1 and b3 (modal_resonator_bank.h:111-119, 133-139), both replaced when the override is >= 0; Material still moves stretch (membrane_mapper.h:138), so it is not fully dead. Only the processor's DefaultKit sentinel path (drum_voice.h:1742) keeps Decay live. Hand-tuned b1/b3 is valid voicing, but a primary knob that does nothing across all 20 shipped kits, with a manual that says otherwise, justifies keeping the severity.

### Medium (71)

#### MB-005 — Each voice steal or choke does std::swap of two 270 KB DrumVoice objects: a 270 KB temporary on the audio-thread stack and about 0.8 MB of copying per swap

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** rt-safety · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Also flagged by:** gestalt-processor

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:922](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L922) (beginFastRelease; callers 171, 221, 583, 1047)

**Problem.** beginFastRelease snapshots the live voice into the shadow slot with std::swap(VP_RVOICES[slot], VP_VOICES[slot]). std::swap move-constructs a full DrumVoice temporary on the calling (audio) thread's stack. sizeof(DrumVoice) = 270,688 bytes (measured; the voice_pool.h comment's 224096 is stale). A swap moves three whole voices. A choke group runs one swap per choked voice in one noteOn (processChokeGroups :1034-1070, up to 16), and a steal runs one more.

**Why wrong.** Audio-thread stacks are not guaranteed to be large. Secondary threads on macOS default to 512 KB, and AU / host render threads are often 512 KB or smaller. A 270 KB frame plus the voice's own call chain (noteOn, mapper, probe) risks a stack overflow. The copy is also unbounded per event (16 x ~10 us, with outliers to 158 us).

**Consequence.** Possible stack-overflow crash in hosts with small render-thread stacks (macOS AU especially), and CPU spikes on choke storms (open / closed hat groups, rolls through the forced-steal path).

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:922 `std::swap(VP_RVOICES[slot], VP_VOICES[slot]);`. Probe probe2.cpp (scratchpad rtprobe): `sizeof(DrumVoice) = 270688 bytes`; `std::swap(DrumVoice) avg 9.8 us worst 158.3 us` over 200 swaps at 48 kHz.

**Suggested fix.** Do not move voices. Keep an index indirection: a per-slot pointer or index into a 32-voice storage array, and swap the two indices in beginFastRelease. That is O(1), with no stack temporary. Test: a static_assert or a test that beginFastRelease does not move a DrumVoice (for example, check that DrumVoice addresses are stable across a steal), plus a CPU-lane case for a 16-voice choke.

**Verifier notes**
- The defect is real: DrumVoice has no custom swap, move constructor or unique_ptr indirection, so generic std::swap move-constructs a full stack temporary and does two move-assignments, copying inline storage. voice_pool.h:23-27 gives a stale 224,096 bytes; test_voice_pool_scaffold.cpp:29 records the per-voice size. All callers run on the audio thread, including processChokeGroups at :1047 and :1068 (loop :1034-1070, up to kMaxVoices = 16). The early return at :892-893 limits it to one swap per slot, so "unbounded" is overstated (bounded at 16 per event). The comment at :895-918 confirms the deliberate whole-object move.
- Could not refute. Inline storage includes `std::array<float, kMaxBlockSize>` scratch arrays (drum_voice.h:1679-1687); the steal at :221 passes force = true, bypassing the idempotence return at :892. voice_pool.h:29-37 and the plan accept the 6.84 MiB heap footprint but say nothing about a stack temporary; no spec (specs/13[6-9]*) mentions it, the 2026-06 audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:284) discussed only the M-8 idempotence click, and no test checks stack use or steal time. The overflow is plausible, not demonstrated; medium stands.
- Mechanism real, consequence overstated; judged a low-severity RT-efficiency and robustness concern. Copy assignment is deleted because of BowExciter (static_assert at 919); the voice arrays are on the heap (voicesPtr_ / releasingVoicesPtr_, :26-27), only the temporary is on the stack. sizeof 270688 is confirmed by rtprobe run_swap.log line 1, but the swap timings (9.8 / 158.3 us) appear in no log and are unverified. The frame fits the 1 MB Windows, 512 KB macOS and 8 MB Linux defaults, MSVC and Apple clang emit stack probes (__chkstk, ___chkstk_darwin), and real choke groups usually choke 1-2 voices. The index-indirection fix is still sensible.

#### MB-006 — AuditionPad and AuditionPadOff share one atomic word, so a pad press and release between two audio blocks overwrite each other

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** threading · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Also flagged by:** ui-wiring

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:1186-1216, 540-556](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L1186-L1216); [processor.h:121-126](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.h#L121-L126)

**Problem.** Both messages store into the single std::atomic<uint32_t> pendingAudition_. consumePendingAudition() takes only the last word per block (exchange(0)). Two cases lose a message:
- If mouse-down and mouse-up (controller.cpp:1079 'AuditionPad', 1097 'AuditionPadOff') both arrive between two process() calls, only the Off is seen: the audition never sounds.
- If the Off for pad A and the On for pad B arrive together, A's note-off is lost.

A tap or a fast click shorter than one host buffer is ordinary at 1024 / 2048-sample buffers (23-46 ms).

**Why wrong.** The UI-to-audio event channel has to keep every event in order. A single-slot mailbox is lossy by construction.

**Consequence.** Quick pad clicks are silent with large host buffers, and a held audition can miss its note-off (Friction / long-decay pads keep ringing until auto-release).

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:1198 `pendingAudition_.store(word, std::memory_order_release);` (On) and :1214 the same store for Off. processor.cpp:542 `const std::uint32_t word = pendingAudition_.exchange(0u, std::memory_order_acq_rel);` processes a single word per block.

**Suggested fix.** Use a small SPSC ring of audition events, for example 16 entries, written in notify() and drained in process(). Test: post AuditionPad then AuditionPadOff before one process() call and assert a voice became Active in that block and received a noteOff.

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed: processor.h:126 declares one atomic; notify overwrites it for "AuditionPad" (processor.cpp:1194-1198) and "AuditionPadOff" (1210-1214) with no queue, compare-exchange or merge; consumePendingAudition (540-556) acts on one word per block. The UI sends both with no minimum hold: PadGridView mouse-down (pad_grid_view.cpp:287-299, auditionHeldPad_ at :305) and mouse-up (:389-393), turned into IMessages at controller.cpp:1070-1085 and 1091-1102. Medium fits: editor audition only, host MIDI unaffected.
- Confirmed, with no guard, ruling or test. process() calls consumePendingAudition once per block (processor.cpp:622), which takes one branch (:549-553 noteOff, :554-555 noteOn). The lost note-off matters: VoicePool::noteOff (voice_pool.cpp:283-299) now gates the amp envelope and damps the bank (FR-114 / Phase 8A.5), so a Friction pad keeps sounding. The only covering test (test_morph_host_simulation.cpp:137-190) sends AuditionPad alone.
- Confirmed. The note-on is lost when both events reach notify() within one block period: 23 ms at 1024, 46 ms at 2048, 93 ms at 4096 samples (44.1 kHz), or at any buffer size when a UI-thread stall delivers queued down / up events back to back. No auto-release path exists and the 256-silent-block safety net acts only on silence, so the stuck-Friction consequence is if anything understated. Severity unchanged.

#### MB-010 — No NaN barrier anywhere: a non-finite pad field makes a voice emit NaN forever and never retire, and it latches the coupling energy limiter

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dsp-numerics · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Also flagged by:** lifecycle-state, portability-quality · **Corroborated by measurement:** yes (see below)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.cpp:167-200](plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.cpp#L167-L200) (also state_codec.cpp:202-245; dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/sigmoid.h:267-269; modal_resonator_bank.h:461-474; voice_pool.cpp:478-486; processor.h:183-196; true_peak_limiter.h:189-215)

**Problem.** applyPadSnapshot copies sound slots 0-33 (material, size, decay, strikePosition, all tone-shaper and morph fields, fmRatio...) with a bare static_cast and no finiteness or range check. readKitBlob does not validate them either. Slots 34+ use std::clamp, which also returns NaN for a NaN input. Downstream nothing stops NaN. hardClip is std::clamp (sigmoid.h:267-269), so NaN passes the 'safety rail'. flushSilentModes tests `energy < kSilenceThreshold`, which is false for NaN, so the mode never flushes and the voice never retires. VoicePool's `peak = std::max(peak, a)` drops NaN, so the voice looks quiet. applyEnergyLimiter: once energyEnvelope_ is NaN, `energyEnvelope_ > kThreshold` is always false, so the -20 dBFS coupling cap is permanently off until applyKitSnapshot resets it (processor.cpp:967). TruePeakLimiter assumes finite input (its own comment at :189-192) and passes NaN through std::clamp. The only finiteness check in the plugin DSP is FeedbackExciter's bodyFeedback guard (feedback_exciter.h:147).

**Why wrong.** Project rule: NaN/Inf must never reach the output. State read from a file is untrusted input and must be range- and finiteness-validated at the codec, as the codec already does for the enums, choke, bus and macros. Under the macOS -ffast-math build, NaN comparisons are additionally undefined.

**Consequence.** One corrupt or hand-edited .vstpreset or host project (a NaN or Inf float64 in slots 0-33) makes that pad output NaN on every hit, permanently: the voice never retires. In hosts that do not sanitise, that is a dead or exploding channel. With coupling enabled, the NaN also poisons the coupling resonators and disables the energy limiter until the next kit load.

**Evidence.** Measured (probe nanSlot(), IEEE build): a quiet-NaN in PadConfig::material, size, decay or strikePosition gives 'non-finite samples 881920 / 881920, active after 20.0 s: YES' for each. tsFilterCutoff NaN gives all-NaN output, voice retired at 6.1 s. Code: `cfg.material = static_cast<float>(snap.sound[0]);` (state_codec.cpp:167) through `cfg.frictionPressure = static_cast<float>(snap.sound[33]);` (:200). `return std::clamp(x, -threshold, threshold);` (sigmoid.h:268). `if (energy < kSilenceThreshold)` (modal_resonator_bank.h:467). `if (energyEnvelope_ > kThreshold)` (processor.h:191).

Corroborated by measurement: Probe state:malformed-stored: "NON-FINITE stored and written back by getState; output finite (peak -11.4..-12.3 dBFS)". focus3:applyPadSnapshot-clamp: "slots kept > 1.0: 0-27, 30-33". focus2:double-apply:out-of-range-slots: "1.700/1.000, -0.300/0.000" (msg/edits). state_codec.cpp:167 `cfg.material = static_cast<float>(snap.sound[0]);`.

**Suggested fix.** In applyPadSnapshot and applyPadPresetSnapshot, replace each non-finite slot with its PadConfig default via Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite (db_utils.h), and clamp slots 0-33 to [0,1] except the documented sentinels, the same as slots 34+. Optionally add a per-voice rail: if !detail::isFinite(the block's last output sample), reset the voice. Tests: build a kit blob with NaN in sound[0] and in sound[35], setState, render, and assert finite output and a retired voice; an applyPadSnapshot unit test with NaN and +/-Inf per slot. Put the test in an IEEE TU (dsp_ieee_tests pattern), since it injects NaN.

**Verifier notes**
- The chain holds. applyPadPresetSnapshot (:284-315) repeats the bare copy; readKitBlob (:456-460) and readPadPresetBlob (:573-577) read sound slots raw; applyKitSnapshot (processor.cpp:939) and applyPadPresetSnapshot (:1008) push them into the pool. Grep finds no isFinite / isNaN / isnan in plugins/membrum/src. The pool's std::max(0, NaN) reads silent and auto-noteOffs (voice_pool.cpp:380-384, :508), but retirement needs bankSilent (drum_voice.h:645-651, 660-665), so the voice stays active forever. The limiter resets only at processor.cpp:967 or :1084. TruePeakLimiter's comment (true_peak_limiter.h:189-192) assumes hardClip bounds every voice, which is false for NaN; the aux buses (voice_pool.cpp:500-504) get raw NaN. Medium: the trigger needs a bad file.
- Could not refute. The b1 sentinel test `b1Raw < 0.0` (:216) is false for NaN, so NaN also passes the following clamp; readKitBlob (:421-507) validates other fields but reads pad.sound raw. The only guard is feedback_exciter.h:146 via float_guard. The SVF's NaN reset (svf.h:360-362) runs only when the filter stage is engaged (tone_shaper.h:430-458), so a bypassed-filter pad passes NaN straight out. Prior correctness-audit Finding 7 fixed only the FeedbackExciter follower. No Membrum test injects NaN into a state blob; test_stability_guard.cpp covers feedback only and uses the forbidden bit-mask clone (:36-40).
- Could not refute. state_codec.cpp:36 reads each value with a bare readDouble, and a double above FLT_MAX in slots 0-33 casts to ±Inf, so a corrupted exponent also yields Inf. Kept at medium rather than lower: the effect is permanent, NaN on a host bus can silence the mix, and the blob has no checksum. The probe was not re-run but agrees with the traced path.

#### MB-012 — noteOff (and fast-release) damping is a per-sample radius factor, so the release time halves every time the sample rate doubles

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dsp-numerics · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Corroborated by research:** yes (see below)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:57-71, 104-107, 442-452](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L442-L452)

**Problem.** noteOff() calls bank.damp(kNoteOffDampScale = 0.997f) and fastReleaseDamp() calls damp(0.88f). damp() multiplies every mode's radius once (modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516). The radius is a per-sample pole, so the added decay rate is -ln(0.997) * sr: 132 /s at 44.1 kHz and 577 /s at 192 kHz. The comment at :59-61 states a 50 ms release, which holds at one sample rate only. VoicePool also calls noteOff on every block whose peak is < 1e-3 (voice_pool.cpp:508-512), so the factor compounds per block, which makes the decay depend on the block size as well.

**Why wrong.** Time constants must be specified in seconds and converted with the current sample rate. The rest of the voice does this (ADSR in ms, energyAlpha_ = exp(-1/(0.02*sr)), the pool's fastReleaseK_).

**Consequence.** The same kit releases twice as fast at 96 kHz and four times as fast at 192 kHz: toms and cymbals ended by note-off sound choked at high sample rates. Offline bounces at a different rate do not match real-time playback.

**Evidence.** Measured (probe releaseVsRate(), Impulse + Membrane, decay 1, material 1, noise and click off, noteOff at 100 ms, block 64): time to -60 dB after noteOff is 38.9 ms at 44.1 kHz, 19.0 ms at 96 kHz and 10.0 ms at 192 kHz (reference peaks 0.318 / 0.319 / 0.320). Code: `static constexpr float kNoteOffDampScale = 0.997f;` (:64), `bodyBank_.getSharedBank().damp(kNoteOffDampScale);` (:451), `radiusTarget_[k] *= scale; radius_[k] *= scale;` (modal_resonator_bank.h:513-514).

Corroborated by research: Physics (contradicted): Note-off 'release through the body's own damping law' is a per-sample radius multiply: sample-rate dependent, and undone by the next per-chunk retune. The comment at 57-63 says scaling the radius 'brings the effective t60 to ~50 ms ... while still letting the body's damping law drive'. To hold, the release has to be expressed as an added decay RATE (s^-1). That makes it independent of fs, and it has to live inside the law computeModeCoefficients applies, so a retune keeps it. In the physical model a struck drum has no note-off at all: decay comes only from the head and shell losses. If a held-gate release is wanted, its rate must not depend on fs or on which modulation path happens to be active. Sources (evidence quality moderate): Chaigne A., Askenfelt A., JASA 95(2), 1994 [paper] https://www.math.kent.edu/~zheng/62262/piano_wave.pdf: Decay is a continuous-time rate (alpha = b1 + b3*omega^2, s^-1). A per-sample factor exp(-alpha/fs) is the sample-rate-invariant discretisation, while a fixed per-sample multiplier such as 0.997 corresponds to a rate proportional to fs.

**Suggested fix.** Store the release as a time and convert it at prepare: dampScale = exp(-ln(1000) / (T60_release * sampleRate)), for example T60 ~ 40 ms for noteOff. Do the same for the fast-release scale. Apply the noteOff damp once per gate, not on every quiet block. Test: Impulse + Membrane, decay 1, noteOff at 100 ms. The time to -60 dB after noteOff must agree within 10 % at 44.1, 96 and 192 kHz.

**Verifier notes**
- Confirmed from source. fastReleaseDamp() is invoked from beginFastRelease (voice_pool.cpp:937); the radii are per-sample poles, radiusTarget_ = exp(-decayRate / sampleRate_) (modal_resonator_bank.h:368, :824), applied every sample in the recursion (:938, 950-959). The added rate is about 132 /s at 44.1 kHz (T60 ≈ 52 ms), 288 /s at 96 kHz and 577 /s at 192 kHz, matching the measured 1/sr scaling. Nothing undoes the damp: setModes runs only at note-on and for the shell bank (drum_voice.h:1482), updateDampingLaw is never called, and smoothCoefficients (906-914) smooths toward the damped target. The block-size claim holds too: noteOff runs on every quiet Active block (voice_pool.cpp:380-384, 508-512).
- Confirmed, nothing guards or documents it. The amp-envelope release is 300 ms in ms units (drum_voice.h:159-162), far longer than the body release, so the damp sets the audible release; the comment at :448-449 says "@ 44.1 kHz". The block-size effect only acts below about -60 dBFS, so it is secondary. Per-sample decay ln(1000) / (-ln 0.997) ≈ 2300 samples, i.e. 52 ms at 44.1 kHz. Medium stands.
- Confirmed (probe not re-run). The comment at :448 ("0.993 yields ~50 ms @ 44.1 kHz") is stale, since the constant is 0.997. Drum MIDI from DAW clips sends note-offs shorter than tom or cymbal decays (a 1/16 at 120 BPM gates at 125 ms), so the post-gate tail at 96 kHz is about half that at 44.1 kHz. The fast-release path (0.88 per sample, ~1.2 ms T60 at 44.1 kHz, ~0.3 ms at 192 kHz) runs inside the time-based 5 ms crossfade, so its audible effect is small.

#### MB-014 — Membrum's NaN/Inf test guards are bit-mask clones or std::isfinite in fast-math TUs, so they are vacuous on the macOS leg

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/CMakeLists.txt:250-267](plugins/membrum/tests/CMakeLists.txt#L250-L267)

**Problem.** About 30 Membrum test helpers classify finiteness with the hand-written `(bits & 0x7F800000u) == 0x7F800000u` clone. Examples: test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp:48 (the SC-007 36-combination no-NaN sweep), test_stability_guard.cpp:40, test_default_kit.cpp:36, membrum_processor_tests.cpp:423/431, test_phase1_regression.cpp:44 and every voice_pool helper. Others use std::isfinite in normal TUs (test_coupling_phase9_verification.cpp:196-197, 285-286, 318-319; test_secondary_shell_paths.cpp:98-99). The CMake comment at :250-252 says bit manipulation means '-fno-fast-math is NOT needed'. Only two TUs get per-file flags, and those are `-fno-fast-math;-ffp-contract=off` without -fno-finite-math-only.

**Why wrong.** Root and dsp/CLAUDE.md: Apple clang folds the bit-mask clone to 'finite' even through memcpy under -ffast-math (seven helpers were vacuous before). Classify only through Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite / isNaN / isInf. An IEEE flag set is all three flags on one line (tools/lint-ieee-flag-sets.js).

**Consequence.** On the macOS CI leg, the SC-007 'no NaN/Inf across all exciter x body combinations' test and the other stability tests cannot fail, so a NaN regression like the unguarded paths above would ship green.

**Evidence.** Grep under plugins/membrum/tests finds 0x7F800000u in test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp:48, test_stability_guard.cpp:40, test_default_kit.cpp:36, test_voice_pool_allocate.cpp:26, test_steal_click_free.cpp:98, test_choke_click_free.cpp:43, perf/*.cpp, approval/test_phase1_regression.cpp:44 and more. std::isfinite appears in test_coupling_phase9_verification.cpp:196 and test_secondary_shell_paths.cpp:98. CMake: `# Therefore, -fno-fast-math is NOT needed for this test file.` (:252) and `COMPILE_OPTIONS "-fno-fast-math;-ffp-contract=off"` (:265).

**Suggested fix.** Replace every local isFinite or isNonFinite helper in plugins/membrum/tests with Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite. Move NaN-injection cases into an IEEE-flagged TU. Fix the comment at :250-252. Use `-fno-fast-math;-fno-finite-math-only;-ffp-contract=off` for the two flagged TUs. Check with tools/lint-finite-bitmask.js and tools/macos-fastmath-repro.sh.

**Verifier notes**
- Could not refute. The Apple build applies `-ffast-math -ffp-contract=fast` directory-wide (extern/vst3sdk/cmake/modules/SMTG_PlatformToolset.cmake:46; root CMakeLists.txt:420, :532). test_exciter_body_matrix.cpp:44-49 isNaNOrInfBits is the forbidden clone, and its comments (:7-9, :22-23, :42-43) wrongly claim fast-math safety; dsp/CLAUDE.md:48, :175 say Apple clang folds it. tools/lint-finite-bitmask-baseline.json:41-69 already lists 29 Membrum test files: baselined debt, not fixed. Only test_coupling_energy.cpp:188 is protected. Weaker sub-claim: clang's -fno-fast-math may already reset finite-math-only, so that part may be a lint-rule gap. Test gap, not a runtime bug; medium fits.
- Confirmed. tools/lint-ieee-flag-sets.js:5 checks only for -ffp-contract=off, so the missing -fno-finite-math-only passes CI, while dsp/CLAUDE.md:181 defines the IEEE set as all three flags. Recommends lowering severity: Linux (no fast-math) and Windows run the same tests with working checks, so only a macOS-only NaN regression would slip through, and the debt is a tracked ratchet item.
- Confirmed. The macOS leg really compiles these TUs with fast-math: ci.yml:726 configures with `-G Xcode`, and :753 / :824 build and run membrum_tests there. tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json:9-10 lists the two std::isfinite TUs. What ships green is a NaN that only the macOS fast-math build produces, the class the repo has been hit by before (dsp/CLAUDE.md:177, HarmonicFold); the perf/*.cpp hits sit in hidden [.perf] cases and matter less. Medium, no change.

#### MB-021 — StrikeNormKey omits FM Ratio and Friction Pressure: after editing either, the cached body gain is stale by 3-7 dB until some other key field changes on that slot

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** exciter · **Dimension:** exciters

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1400-1411](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1400-L1411)

**Problem.** The key holds body, exciter, material, size, decay, strikePos, stretch, skew, airLoading, scatter, b1, b3, the click params and noiseBurstContact. It does not hold fmRatio or frictionPressure, both of which change the probed excitation spectrum (FM centroid 5.9 kHz at ratio norm 0 to 11.2 kHz at norm 1).

**Why wrong.** The key must cover every input that changes the probed excitation (Fix-D comment at 1389-1393: 're-measures only when ... the excitation shape change[s]').

**Consequence.** Turning FM Ratio or Friction Pressure on a pad leaves the next hits on slots that last played this pad at the wrong level (FM: -2.9 to -7.1 dB; Friction pressure 0 to 1: -3.4 dB on Membrane). Slots that played another pad in between re-probe correctly, so the same pad's level jumps between hits.

**Evidence.** keyprobe.cpp (v=1, click 0): 'FM body 0 ratioNorm 0.133->1.00: cached-gain peak 0.220 vs fresh 0.500 (-7.1 dB)', 'FM body 1 ... ->1.00 ... (-5.5 dB)', 'FM body 4 ... (-4.4 dB)', 'Friction body 0 pressure 0->1: cached 0.339 fresh 0.500'. Exciter probe centroid at ratio norm 0.000 / 0.133 / 0.5 / 1.0 = 5864 / 6274 / 9350 / 11206 Hz.

**Suggested fix.** Add fmRatio and frictionPressure (and feedbackAmount, if the Feedback path is ever normalised) to StrikeNormKey through ExciterBank getters. Test: play an FM pad, change the ratio, play again, and compare with a fresh voice (within 0.5 dB).

**Verifier notes**
- Code path confirms it (keyprobe not re-run). StrikeNormKey (drum_voice.h:1717-1727) has no fmRatio or frictionPressure field, and strikeNormKey_ is written only at 1409 (declared 1728). The probe uses the live exciter: FMImpulseExciter::trigger sets the modulator to baseFreq * (1 + 3 * modulatorRatioNorm_) (fm_impulse_exciter.h:80-86), and FrictionExciter adds pressureAmount_ * 0.5 to bow pressure (friction_exciter.h:67-80). Each note-on pushes the new values (pad_config_apply.h:58, :60 -> exciter_bank.h:146-169) without touching the key, and only Feedback and String bypass the cached gain (drum_voice.h:269-305).
- Confirmed. The values reach the live exciter via DrumVoice::setFMRatio / setFrictionPressure (drum_voice.h:1227-1229) -> FMImpulseExciter::setModulatorRatio (fm_impulse_exciter.h:110) / FrictionExciter::setPressure. Feedback is correctly excluded (clip branch, drum_voice.h:272-276). No spec or prior ruling makes the omission intentional; the Fix-D comment states the opposite intent. Medium.
- Confirmed. In the probe, velocity 1.0 maps to bow pressure 0.5 + pressureAmount * 0.5 (friction_exciter.h:79-81), so pressure 0 -> 1 doubles the probe's bow force. The stale gain can be too quiet or too loud, and it depends on which slot plays the note, which the cache is meant to prevent. Only FMImpulse / Friction pads with a modal body are affected, after an edit or automation of one of these two parameters. Medium is right.

#### MB-024 — Noise-based exciters and the click layer change level and balance with the sample rate (Violet NoiseBurst -10 dB at 96 kHz; Feedback seed impulse is a fixed 2 samples)

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** exciter · **Dimension:** exciters

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/noise_burst_exciter.h:51, 105-110, 139-140](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/noise_burst_exciter.h#L51)

**Problem.** NoiseBurst bandpasses per-sample-variance Violet noise at a fixed Hz centre, so the in-band power scales as (f/sr)^2 x BW/sr. Clap and ClickLayer use white noise through a fixed-Hz bandpass (power proportional to 1/sr). FeedbackExciter injects a 2-sample impulse (feedback_exciter.h:124, 163-167) whose energy halves with every doubling of the rate. Impulse, Mallet and FM are rate-independent (measured).

**Why wrong.** Level and timbre must not depend on the host sample rate. The body peak is renormalised at v=1, but the click goes straight to the output un-normalised, and the exciter-to-click balance inside the probe and the note shifts.

**Consequence.** The same kit sounds different at 44.1 kHz and 96/192 kHz. NoiseBurst pads with a click lose noise against click: voice RMS 0.0146 -> 0.0210 (+3.2 dB) at 192 kHz with the same peak, and the NoiseBurst-only RMS falls 0.0126 -> 0.0088 (-3.1 dB). The click transient itself is about 4 dB quieter at 96 kHz.

**Evidence.** probe.cpp at v=1, peak and E=sum(x^2)/sr: NoiseBurst 44.1k pk 0.6282 E 9.544e-05 | 96k pk 0.1899 E 9.718e-06 | 192k pk 0.1148 E 1.884e-06; Clap E 1.035e-04 / 4.158e-05 / 2.396e-05; Feedback pk 0.8467 / 0.6416 / 0.3775; Impulse E 1.357e-03 / 1.341e-03 / 1.341e-03; FM E 2.670e-03 at all three rates. vprobe.cpp NoiseBurst Membrane: click 0 RMS 0.0126 / 0.0115 / 0.0088; click 0.5 RMS 0.0146 / 0.0180 / 0.0210.

**Suggested fix.** Scale the noise sources by sqrt(sr/44100) (white) or the matching violet factor, and set the Feedback seed impulse length in time (for example 0.05 ms) rather than in samples. Test: exciter energy (sum x^2 / sr) and click peak within 0.5 dB across 44.1 / 96 / 192 kHz.

**Verifier notes.**
- Violet is a per-sample differentiator `(white - prevWhite) * 0.5` (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/noise_oscillator.h:341-345) fed into a fixed-Hz SVF bandpass (noise_burst_exciter.h:58-60, 105-107), so in-band energy falls roughly as sr^-3; measured 9.8x from 44.1k to 96k against a predicted 10.3x.
- ClickLayer (click_layer.h:46-51, 118-119) is white noise through a fixed-Hz bandpass with no rate compensation (about -3.4 dB at 96k) and reaches the output directly (drum_voice.h:531-550, 787-892); only the body is strike-normalised (drum_voice.h:283, 1366-1386, 1408).
- FeedbackExciter seeds a fixed 2-sample impulse (feedback_exciter.h:124, 163-167), matching the measured peak falling 0.8467 -> 0.6416 -> 0.3775; Feedback also skips the excited-probe renormalisation.
- The only sample-rate test, test_noise_burst_exciter.cpp:111-124, checks finiteness and peak bound, never level; no spec or prior audit rules rate dependence intended.
- probeStrikePeakExcited (drum_voice.h:1322-1387) re-levels the primary body at each rate, so NoiseBurst-only voice level moves just -0.8 dB at 96 kHz; the uncompensated parts are the click's direct path (-3.4 / -6.4 dB at 96 / 192 kHz) and the click/NoiseBurst balance (+1.8 / +3.2 dB RMS). One verifier recommended a downgrade on that basis; the others kept medium.

#### MB-031 — The 'physical' Mode Stretch (1.0) stretches Plate, Shell, Bell and NoiseBody partials (bell nominal/hum +23 cents, plate top mode x1.89) because the bank's stretch ceiling was widened 10x with no re-baselining

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** body-model · **Dimension:** bodies-modal (also flagged by: parameter-audibility) · **Corroborated by measurement** · **Corroborated by research**

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_mapper.h:58-62](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_mapper.h#L58)

**Problem.** Plate (:58-62), Shell (shell_mapper.h:61), Bell (bell_mapper.h:56) and NoiseBody (noise_body_mapper.h:119) set stretch = (modeStretch-0.5)/1.5. At the default modeStretch 1.0 (pad_config.h:212, normalized 0.333 = 'physical') that gives 0.333. The bank then applies B = stretch^2 * 0.01 = 1.11e-3 and f *= sqrt(1 + B*(k+1)^2) using the ARRAY INDEX (modal_resonator_bank.h:783, 806-807). The 0.01 ceiling was widened from 0.001 in audit 3-B (comment :776-782) without changing these baselines. Only Membrane subtracts the unity baseline (membrane_mapper.h:136-138), but it still adds material*0.3 of stretch: B = 2.25e-4 at the default material 0.5.

**Why wrong.** modeStretch 1.0 is documented as physical: 'default = no stretch' (pad_config_apply.h:123). The mode tables (Hibberts bell partials, Chladni plate law, free-free bar ratios) should sound at their stated ratios by default. A stiff-string sqrt(1+Bn^2) law keyed on a sorted 2-D table index is not physical for plates, bells or membranes.

**Consequence.** Default timbre is detuned from the stated mode tables:
- Bell: nominal/hum = 4.053 instead of 4 (+23 cents); prime/hum 2.0033; tierce/prime 1.2033. The octave structure that defines a bell is out of tune.
- Plate: top mode (k=47) x1.887, k=15 x1.133, k=7 x1.035.
- NoiseBody: top mode x2.356.
- Membrane at default material: top mode x1.232 (x1.753 at material 1).

The Stretch knob has no neutral point on these bodies.

**Evidence.** modal_resonator_bank.h:783 `const float B = stretch * stretch * 0.01f;` :806-807 `const float n_k = static_cast<float>(k + 1); float f_w = f_k * std::sqrt(1.0f + B * n_k * n_k);`. plate_mapper.h:60-62 `const float stretchNorm = std::clamp((params.modeStretch - 0.5f) * (1.0f / 1.5f), 0.0f, 1.0f); r.stretch = stretchNorm;`. pad_config.h:212 `float modeStretch = 0.333333f; // norm of [0.5, 2.0], default 1.0`. Computed: B = 1.111e-3, bell nominal/hum 4.0529 (+23 cents), plate k=47 x1.887, noisebody k=63 x2.356, membrane mat 0.5 k=47 x1.232.

**Corroborated by measurement.** Probe modes, bank vs table at neutral modeStretch: "Plate/Shell/Bell +0.9,+3.8,+8.6,+15.2,+23.7,+33.9,+45.9,+59.4 c" (plate_mapper.h:60-62).

**Corroborated by research (physics: contradicted).** A neutral setting should leave the body's ratios unchanged. A plate is already dispersive (f proportional to lambda^2, Kirchhoff bending); the string inharmonicity factor sqrt(1 + B n^2) applied by table index has no plate meaning. From the coded formula, at modeStretch 1.0 the plate table goes k=9 5.79 -> 6.10, k=23 14.31 -> 18.32, k=47 29.40 -> 55.44 (1.9x); at the default kit's crash/clap setting 1.4 (B = 3.6e-3), k=47 reaches 89.46 (3.0x). Sources (moderate): N.H. Fletcher & T.D. Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments*, 2nd ed., 1998, ch. 2-3 (https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-21603-4); A.W. Leissa, *Vibration of Plates*, NASA SP-160, 1969.

**Suggested fix.** Subtract the unity baseline in every mapper, as Membrane does: stretch = max(0, norm - 1/3) * 1.5. Decide whether Membrane's material*0.3 term should survive the 10x ceiling. Consider keying stretch on the mode's ratio rather than its index.

Test: for each modal body at modeStretch = 1.0 and scatter 0, getModeFrequency(k)/getModeFrequency(0) must equal the table ratio within 0.1 % for every surviving mode (bell nominal/hum = 4.000).

**Verifier notes.**
- plate_mapper.h:60-62, bell_mapper.h:55-57, shell_mapper.h:60-62 and noise_body_mapper.h:118-120 all use clamp((modeStretch-0.5)/1.5); default 1.0 (pad_config.h:212, pad_config_apply.h:125-126) gives stretch 0.333; only membrane_mapper.h:136-138 subtracts kUnityStretchNorm.
- The stretch reaches the bank through drum_voice.h:1619-1625 and 1658-1664; modal_resonator_bank.h:781-782 claims "Membrum default-off get B==0", which is false for the four non-Membrane bodies.
- Documented intent contradicts behaviour: voice_common_params.h:23 "default 1.0 (no stretch)", specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:235 (FR-050) "Default value 1.0 (physical)", unnatural_zone_contract.md:9.
- Tests hide it: test_plate_body.cpp:135-137 sets modeStretch 0.5 "to neutralise the modeStretch warp"; test_bell_body.cpp:44-81 / 71-77 allow ±3 % (x1.8) around the table, and the shift is 1.3 %.
- Numbers recomputed (bell nominal/hum 4.053, plate k=47 x1.887, NoiseBody k=63 x2.356 with kNoiseBodyModeCount 64 at noise_body_mapper.h:73); one verifier got membrane k=47 x1.223 vs the claimed x1.232.
- Membrane's material*0.3 term is deliberate Phase 1 behaviour for FR-031 bit-identity (membrane_mapper.h:131-135), so that part is a design question, not a confirmed bug.
- Medium kept: no instability, but the fix changes factory-kit sound (default_kit.h:231, :348 set modeStretch 0.6 on purpose), so kits need re-auditioning.

#### MB-032 — Strike-normalisation cache survives a sample-rate change, so cache-hit hits are about 6.8 dB too loud (44.1 to 96 kHz) or too quiet (the reverse)

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** gain-staging · **Dimension:** bodies-modal (also flagged by: gestalt-voice)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:119-164, 1394-1412, 1717-1729](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1394)

**Problem.** measuredStrikeOutputGain caches strikeNormGain_ under StrikeNormKey (body, exciter, material, size, ...). The key has no sample rate, and DrumVoice::prepare() (lines 119-164), which VoicePool::prepare calls for setupProcessing and setActive, never clears it. Bank state amplitude for a fixed-duration strike is proportional to sample rate, because the coupled-form input gain is per sample (modal_resonator_bank.h:835-838). So is the probe peak the gain is derived from.

**Why wrong.** Body output must be normalised to kBodyHeadroom (0.5) at the CURRENT rate. A cached gain from another rate is off by the rate ratio.

**Consequence.** After the host changes sample rate without re-instantiating the plugin, every hit whose slot last played the same pad configuration reuses the old gain. Measured at 44.1 -> 96 kHz, the probe peak is x2.18, so the old gain is 6.8 dB too high (and 6.8 dB too low the other way). A single-pad pattern keeps the wrong level for good, and a pad's level then varies with which slot plays it.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:1400-1411 key without sampleRate; `if (!(key == strikeNormKey_)) { strikeNormGain_ = ...; }`. prepare() (119-164) has no strikeNormKey_ write (grep: strikeNormKey_ is used only at 1407, 1409, 1728). Node model of the coupled form (energy_sr.js) with a 2 ms raised-cosine probe and a 9.5 ms mallet pulse, peak state relative to 44.1 kHz: x0.50 at 22.05 kHz, x1.09 at 48 kHz, x2.18 at 96 kHz, x4.35 at 192 kHz.

**Suggested fix.** Reset strikeNormKey_ to its sentinel (body = kCount) in DrumVoice::prepare(), or add sampleRate to the key.

Test: prepare at 44.1 kHz, noteOn and render; prepare at 96 kHz, noteOn the same pad. bank.getOutputGain() must equal a fresh voice prepared at 96 kHz within 1 %.

**Verifier notes.**
- The key struct (drum_voice.h:1717-1727) holds body, exciter, material, size, decay, strikePos, modeStretch, decaySkew, airLoading, modeScatter, b1, b3, click params and noiseBurstContact, but no sample rate; the probe runs only on a key mismatch (1407-1410), and noteOn uses it at drum_voice.h:302-304.
- DrumVoice::prepare (119-164) never writes strikeNormKey_ / strikeNormGain_; voices are allocated once in the VoicePool constructor (voice_pool.cpp:34-35) and re-prepared in place (voice_pool.cpp:106-114) from Processor::setupProcessing (processor.cpp:1075) and setActive (processor.cpp:1097).
- The bank injects `gain_k = amp` per sample with no 1/sr factor (modal_resonator_bank.h:835-839, 934-938) while R_k and eps_k are rate-correct (823-835), so a fixed-duration strike's ring amplitude and the 30 ms probe peak (drum_voice.h:1329) scale roughly with sr; x2.18 = 96/44.1 (6.76 dB).
- After 44.1 -> 96 kHz the body strike peak becomes about 1.09 instead of 0.5; full-velocity hits are partly absorbed by the hardClip rail and the -1 dBTP limiter, lower velocities come out the full ~6.8 dB louder; the reverse direction is ~6.8 dB quieter with nothing to mask it.
- The N-1 entries in AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md describe the cache only as a re-probe saving; nothing invalidates it on prepare. Nyquist culling (modal_resonator_bank.h:813) also changes the active mode set between rates.
- Medium kept: the trigger is less common than normal playing, but it persists for the session and the fix is trivial.

#### MB-033 — Membrane tension-glide depth scales with sample rate squared: 0.34 semitones at 22.05 kHz, 1.3 at 44.1 kHz, the 3-semitone clamp at 96 kHz and above

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** body-model · **Dimension:** bodies-modal · **Corroborated by research**

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:86-100, 420-421, 725-728, 910-914](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L86)

**Problem.** tensionPitchMod = 1 + tensionModAmt*3.3e-5 * energyEnv_, with energyEnv_ following ModalResonatorBank::getModalEnergy() = sum(sin^2+cos^2) (modal_resonator_bank.h:493-499). That energy is taken BEFORE the output gain, on purpose ('invariant to outputGain_'). But the state amplitude for a given physical strike is proportional to sample rate (per-sample input gain), so the energy is proportional to sr^2. kTensionEnergyScale was calibrated at 44.1 kHz ('modal energy for a hard tom hit peaks ~2.4e3', line 92).

**Why wrong.** A physical pitch glide must not depend on the host sample rate. The output level is made rate-independent by the measured-strike gain, but the energy driving the glide is not.

**Consequence.** A hard tom hit at full tension glides about:
- 0.34 semitones at 22.05 kHz;
- 1.32 semitones at 44.1 kHz;
- 3.0 semitones at 96 and 192 kHz (pinned at kTensionPitchModMax 1.19, so velocity no longer changes the glide).

The default-kit toms use tensionModAmt 0.25 (default_kit.h:183), so their glide also varies about 19x in depth between 22.05 and 192 kHz.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:94 `kTensionEnergyScale = 3.3e-5f`; :725-727 `std::min(1.0f + tensionAmtEffective_ * energyEnv_, kTensionPitchModMax)`; :912 `const float e = bodyBank_.getSharedBank().getModalEnergy();`. Node coupled-form model: peak energy x0.25 at 22.05 kHz, x4.74 at 96 kHz, x18.95 at 192 kHz vs 44.1 kHz. Scaling the 2.4e3 calibration gives 0.34 / 1.32 / 3.01 / 3.01 semitones at 22.05 / 44.1 / 96 / 192 kHz.

**Corroborated by research (physics: contradicted).** In Marogna, Avanzini & Bank Eq. 20, Tqs/T0 = Eh E / (2R^2 (1-nu^2) T0^2) uses a physical energy in joules that does not depend on the simulation sample rate; the energy estimate must be normalised (divide getModalEnergy by (sr/44100)^2, use rate-independent displacement amplitudes, or normalise to the noteOn strike peak). Source (strong): Marogna, Avanzini, Bank, "Energy based synthesis of tension modulation in membranes", DAFx-10 (https://people.ece.cornell.edu/land/courses/ece5760/LABS/s2016/MarognaAvanziniBank_tension_modulation.pdf), Eq. 19-20.

**Suggested fix.** Normalise the energy by (sampleRate/44100)^2, or derive it from the output-gain-scaled signal energy, e.g. energy * outputGain^2 / kBodyHeadroom^2.

Test: the tom tension case from test_per_mode_damping.cpp:481, at 44.1 / 96 / 192 kHz. The sounding glide (in semitones) must agree within 20 %.

**Verifier notes.**
- Chain confirmed: tensionAmtEffective_ = tensionModAmt * 3.3e-5 (drum_voice.h:420-421, :94) with no rate term; energyEnv_ fed per chunk from getModalEnergy (drum_voice.h:912-914, slow path 1075-1077); pitchMod = min(1 + amt*energyEnv_, 1.19) (:725-727, :946-950); energyAlpha_ is rate-corrected (drum_voice.h:132-133) but the followed value is not.
- The energy scales as sr^2 because `gain_k = amp` is injected per sample (modal_resonator_bank.h:835, 938/959) and exciter pulses are fixed-amplitude with duration T*sampleRate (impact_exciter.h:129, 146; the energy cap at :79-80, :297 scales both sides alike).
- A verifier's standalone probe of the test_per_mode_damping.cpp:481 setup measured peak modal energy 1044 / 4131 / 4991 / 18060 / 75010 at 22.05 / 44.1 / 48 / 96 / 192 kHz (sr^2), glide at tension 1.0 0.446 / 1.677 / 2.003 / 3.012 / 3.012 semitones, at tension 0.25 0.113 / 0.435 / 0.523 / 1.810 / 3.012 (about 27x), with base f0 158.13 Hz at every rate.
- At velocity 0.3, tension 1.0 the glide is 0.032 / 0.140 / 0.173 / 0.823 / 2.272 semitones: the clamp flattens the velocity response at high rates.
- No test covers more than one rate (test_per_mode_damping.cpp:491 prepares at 44100 only; test_body_resonant_peak.cpp:185 likewise). Prior N-1 (AUDIT-signal-path findings.json:1141) described the older output-energy design; the N-1 fix introduced this dependence. Wire coupling is unaffected (self-normalising ratio, drum_voice.h:1512).

#### MB-034 — Note-off damping is a fixed per-sample radius scale, so the release time scales with 1/sampleRate and compounds on every auto-release block

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** body-model · **Dimension:** bodies-modal

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:64, 442-452](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L64)

**Problem.** noteOff() calls sharedBank.damp(kNoteOffDampScale = 0.997), which multiplies every mode's per-sample radius (modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516). The added decay rate is -ln(0.997)*sr, so the release is proportional to 1/sr. VoicePool also calls voice.noteOff() on EVERY block whose peak is below 1e-3 while the meta is Active (voice_pool.cpp:508-512), so the scale compounds: 0.997^n after n quiet blocks. The comment at :448 still says 0.993.

**Why wrong.** A release time must be given in seconds. The radius scale should be exp(-k/sr) with k chosen for a target T60, and damping should be applied once per note-off.

**Consequence.** Extra note-off T60 is 52 ms at 44.1 kHz, 48 ms at 48 kHz, 24 ms at 96 kHz and 12 ms at 192 kHz. Note-off truncation of drum tails is about 4x harsher at 192 kHz, and repeated auto-release calls make it harsher still and dependent on host block size.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:64 `static constexpr float kNoteOffDampScale = 0.997f;`; :448-451 comment '0.993 yields ~50 ms' + `bodyBank_.getSharedBank().damp(kNoteOffDampScale);`. modal_resonator_bank.h:513-514 `radiusTarget_[k] *= scale; radius_[k] *= scale;`. voice_pool.cpp:508-512 `if (peak < kSilenceThreshold && meta_[slot].state == VoiceSlotState::Active) { VP_VOICES[slot].noteOff(); }`. T60 = 6.908/(0.0030045*sr): 52.1 / 47.9 / 24.0 / 12.0 ms.

**Suggested fix.** Compute the scale in prepare: noteOffScale_ = exp(-ln(1000)/(0.05*sr)) for a 50 ms T60. Let damp apply only once per note: guard it with a flag cleared at noteOn, or make the pool's auto-release call a separate gate-only method. Fix the 0.993 comment.

Test: hold a Membrane note, send noteOff, and measure the T60 of the release at 44.1 and 192 kHz: they must agree within 10 %. Feed the pool a quiet tail with 32-sample blocks and assert damp is applied once.

**Verifier notes.**
- Radii are per-sample (R_k = exp(-decayRate_k / sampleRate_), modal_resonator_bank.h:368, :824), so damp(0.997) adds 0.0030045*sr per second; T60 arithmetic (52.1 ms at 44.1 kHz, 12.0 ms at 192 kHz) confirmed; the :59-63 header calibrates for 44.1 kHz only.
- Note-offs reach the voice from processor.cpp:551, :580, :592 via VoicePool::noteOff (voice_pool.cpp:283-300), which has no "already released" guard and never changes meta_ state.
- Compounding is real: voice_pool.cpp:380-384 and :508-512 call noteOff on every quiet block while meta stays Active; with 32-sample blocks 100 blocks (73 ms) take the radius to about 0.74.
- Not a repeat of a prior finding: AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.findings.json flagged only pad Level vs auto-release, and its verifier called the damp "a one-time radius multiply", which the repeated pool call disproves.
- Caveat: with a pitch envelope, tension or Material Morph active, per-chunk updateModes (drum_voice.h:745/753/769 -> 1619/1658; modal_resonator_bank.h:824/838) rewrites radiusTarget_ and largely undoes the damp, a separate inconsistency.
- One verifier judged the compounding half inaudible (it starts only once the voice is below -60 dBFS, so its effect is mainly earlier retirement), while the rate half affects every note-off at 96/192 kHz (the 300 ms amp release, drum_voice.h:162, is rate-independent, so the body damp decides the tail); medium kept.

#### MB-035 — String body skips strike normalisation and injects a fixed velocity-1.0 noise burst into its loop, so it peaks near the 1.0 soft-clip ceiling against the 0.5 budget of every other body

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** gain-staging · **Dimension:** bodies-modal · **Corroborated by research**

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/string_body.h:41-58](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/string_body.h#L41)

**Problem.** configureForNoteOn calls string_.noteOn(r.frequencyHz, 1.0f). WaveguideString::noteOn fills a period of the loop with RMS-normalised LP noise at velocity*excitationGain (waveguide_string.h:409, 450-463), independent of the hit velocity. The loop output passes softClip(feedback + excitation) with threshold 1.0 (:194-197, 46). DrumVoice explicitly skips the measured-strike normalisation for String (drum_voice.h:277-285: 'the bank's output gain never reaches the audio path').

**Why wrong.** kBodyHeadroom (0.5, -6 dBFS strike peak, drum_voice.h:84) is the per-body budget that keeps bodies level-matched and below the limiter. The String body bypasses it entirely. The hit velocity should shape the string's excitation, not just the amp envelope.

**Consequence.** String pads sit near the soft-clip ceiling. A simplified loop model gives peak 0.99 at velocity 0.24, 0.5 and 1.0, about +6 dB over modal bodies at the same settings. Velocity reaches the String timbre only through the small exciter term; its level comes only from the amp envelope's velocity scaling. Level balance in kits that mix String and modal pads depends on that, and the main-bus limiter works harder.

**Evidence.** string_body.h:57 `string_.noteOn(r.frequencyHz, 1.0f);`. waveguide_string.h:409 `float velScale = velocity * excitationGain_;`, :462 `bridgeSideDelay_.write(excBuf[i] * normScale * velScale);`, :46 `kSoftClipThreshold = 1.0f`, :197 `float output = softClip(junction);`. drum_voice.h:277-285 String branch sets an unused bank gain. Simplified node loop model (string_level.js; DC blocker and dispersion omitted): peak 0.991 / 0.994 / 0.991 at v = 0.24 / 0.5 / 1.0.

**Corroborated by research (physics: contradicted).** An ideal struck string starts from zero displacement with a nonzero initial velocity distribution at the strike point; in a waveguide the strike is a velocity/force injection into both rails at x = beta*L, leaving nulls at harmonics with a node at beta. A random-displacement fill is the plucked-string (Karplus-Strong) model; its amplitude should follow the strike velocity, or be zero when an external exciter provides the strike. Sources (strong): J.O. Smith, *Physical Audio Signal Processing*, "The Ideal Struck String" (https://www.dsprelated.com/freebooks/pasp/Ideal_Struck_String.html) and "Extended Karplus-Strong Algorithm" (https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Extended_Karplus_Strong_Algorithm.html).

**Suggested fix.** Pass the note velocity, or a canonical 1.0 used only for a normalisation probe, into string_.noteOn. Then normalise the String output to kBodyHeadroom: probe the waveguide's 30 ms peak on a cache miss, as for modal bodies, and apply a gain in StringBody::processBlock/processSample.

Test: the peak at velocity 1.0 of the String body vs the Membrane body at the same Size/Material must be within 3 dB, and the String peak at velocity 0.24 must be at least 6 dB below velocity 1.0 before the amp envelope.

**Verifier notes.**
- string_body.h:58 always calls `string_.noteOn(r.frequencyHz, 1.0f)`; the header (:13-15) calls the fixed velocity deliberate ("Phase 2 uses a fixed velocity=1.0") and claims the exciter drives the audible output, which the code contradicts (stale rationale, not a guard).
- waveguide_string.h:400 `excitationGain_ = freqScale / gTotal` (about 0.7 or more), :409, :454-462 RMS-normalise the burst to 1 and write it scaled into the loop; process() (:191-197) soft-clips at 1.0 (:588-592), so output peaks sit just under 1.0.
- StringBody::processBlock/processSample (string_body.h:62-89) return the waveguide output unscaled; drum_voice.h:277-285 only sets the unused bank gain, while modal bodies get measuredStrikeOutputGain (drum_voice.h:302-304, 1366-1386).
- This repeats the String exclusion left open by prior N-1: AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:144-147 measured "String (waveguide, different norm) ≈ 0.99", and :120 / :415 left String on the impulse bound ("harmless" refers to the unused bank gain). No headroom test covers String; test_string_body.cpp's only level case is Level=0 (:370-409).
- Factory kits use String pads (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1560, 2877, 3541, 5014, 5139, 5290, 5977, 6159, 6432, 6584).
- Velocity still sets the level through the ADSR (drum_voice.h:163, 436; adsr_envelope.h:512), so dynamics are not flattened; what is lost is velocity-to-timbre and the per-body level contract (+5.9 dB). One verifier recommended a downgrade because the constant offset is absorbed by per-pad Level and a single centre-panned String voice (x0.707) stays below -1 dBTP, so "limiter works harder" is not shown; final severity stays medium.

#### MB-036 — Strike-norm probe runs a 30 ms render on the audio thread on almost every note-on, because the per-slot cache thrashes when slots rotate across pads

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** rt-safety · **Dimension:** bodies-modal (also flagged by: voice-signal-path)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1322-1363, 1394-1412](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1322)

**Problem.** On a key miss, probeStrikePeakExcited renders 0.030*sr samples through bank.processSample(), which does per-sample coefficient smoothing (3*numModes) plus the scalar core (modal_resonator_bank.h:421-425, 919-966) over up to 64 modes (NoiseBody), with the exciter and click per sample. The key is stored per DrumVoice. VoicePool allocates slots in Oldest order, so successive notes of different pads land on slots that last played another pad. In typical patterns nearly every note-on misses the cache.

**Why wrong.** The audio-thread cost at note-on must be bounded and small. A 30 ms render per note, multiplied by coincident note-ons in one block, is an unbounded-by-design spike that the hidden [.perf] CPU budgets never exercise.

**Consequence.** Each miss costs about 1440 samples x 64 modes x ~10 flops at 48 kHz, roughly 1 M flops (5760 samples at 192 kHz). Several coincident note-ons of different pads (kick + snare + hat + crash) in one small block multiply that. This is a CPU spike and xrun risk at low latency. It is an estimate from the code; no probe was run by the finder.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:1329 `const int probeLen = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(0.030f * sr));` loop :1344-1353 `lastBody = bank.processSample(exc);`. :1407 `if (!(key == strikeNormKey_))` with strikeNormKey_ a DrumVoice member (:1728). modal_resonator_bank.h:421-425 processSample calls smoothCoefficients() every sample.

**Suggested fix.** Cache the gain per PAD in VoicePool (keyed as today), not per voice slot, and compute it off the audio thread when the pad config changes or the kit loads. Or at least keep a small multi-entry cache in the pool shared by all voices.

Test: a [.perf] case firing 16 distinct pads in one 64-sample block must meet the per-block budget; a unit test counts probe invocations for a 4-pad pattern over 64 hits (expect at most 4).

**Verifier notes.**
- The probe runs on the audio thread: VoicePool::noteOn (voice_pool.cpp:196-233) -> DrumVoice::noteOn -> measuredStrikeOutputGain (drum_voice.h:302-304) for every non-Feedback, non-String body; processSample(float) runs smoothCoefficients() and the scalar processSampleCore per sample (modal_resonator_bank.h:374-377, 906-913, 919-966), a path the bank's own comment (:379-385) says "blew the per-voice CPU budget". kMaxModes is 96 (:73).
- The cache is per slot (drum_voice.h:1728-1729), contradicting the intent at drum_voice.h:300-301 ("repeated hits on an unchanged pad pay the probe render only once"); findIdleVoiceOldest (voice_allocator.h:567-581) is an LRU rotation, and beginFastRelease's std::swap of main and shadow voices (voice_pool.cpp:922) moves the key with the object, so a retrigger can miss too.
- Overstated: a same-note retrigger while the pad's voice is still Active or Releasing reuses that slot (voice_allocator.h:238-243, 830-839, 843-869), so rolls within the tail hit the cache; "nearly every note-on misses" is too strong, but misses are frequent (short pads that retire between hits, irregular patterns, first hit after a tail ends).
- A verifier timed DrumVoice::noteOn (g++ -O2, WSL, FTZ/DAZ): hit 1.6-3.9 us; miss at 48 kHz 78 us (Bell), 165-191 us (Membrane / Plate), 246 us (NoiseBody), against a 1333 us 64-sample block; 148-450 us at 96 kHz (block 667 us); 292-876 us at 192 kHz (block 333 us). Four coincident misses at 48 kHz take 0.7-1.0 ms (50-75 % of a 64-sample block); a miss costs 45-75x a hit.
- Nothing warms the cache off the audio thread (no warm/precompute/prime in src), and tests/perf/test_polyphony_stress_16.cpp:136-144 calls noteOn outside the timed region with the Feedback exciter, which skips the probe.

#### MB-039 — A String voice whose shared bank still counts modes (kit switch or body swap while ringing) never retires and feeds stale partials to coupling

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-management · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h:45-50, 177-213](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/body_bank.h#L45)

**Problem.** BodyBank::reset() (resetForKitSwitch, drum_voice.h:470) and applyPendingSwap() (181) call ModalResonatorBank::reset(), which zeroes the oscillator states but leaves active_[] and numActiveModes_ untouched (modal_resonator_bank.h:222-236). A modal body later recounts them in setModes. The String body never calls setModes or processBlock on the shared bank (string_body.h:43-89), so the stale count is never recomputed or flushed. bankSilent (drum_voice.h:645) then stays false forever, and getPartialInfo (drum_voice.h:1250-1258) reports the previous body's mode frequencies to the sympathetic-coupling engine.

**Why wrong.** A body swap or kit wipe must leave the bank in a state consistent with the new body. A String voice with a non-zero modal count disables both the retirement and the safety net, and couples at frequencies the pad does not play.

**Consequence.** Suppose a kit is loaded while a Membrane/Plate/... voice rings, and a String pad's next hit lands on that slot. That String voice is immortal (slot held, CPU used, silence flags never set), and if the pad's couplingAmount > 0 its coupling resonators are tuned to the old body's modes.

**Evidence.** modal_resonator_bank.h:222-236 reset() has no `numActiveModes_ = 0` and no active_ clear; body_bank.h:181 `sharedBank_.reset();`. Probe vo_probe.cpp B2 (Membrane hit, 512 samples, then setBodyModel(String) + noteOn on the same voice, 512-sample blocks): 'retiredAt=never in 20 s, bankActiveModes=44'.

**Suggested fix.** Give ModalResonatorBank (or BodyBank) a full clear that also zeroes active_[] and numActiveModes_ and the coefficient targets, and use it in applyPendingSwap and BodyBank::reset(). Alternatively, have StringBody::configureForNoteOn call setModes with 0 partials. getPartialInfo should take its partials from the String frequency for String bodies.

Test: voice with Membrane noteOn, render 512, setBodyModel(String), noteOn, render 20 s, REQUIRE(!isActive()) and getNumActiveModes()==0; add the same after resetForKitSwitch().

**Verifier notes.**
- ModalResonatorBank::reset() (modal_resonator_bank.h:222-236) never touches active_[], numActiveModes_ or numModes_; only setModes recounts (:759-760, :840-841) and only flushSilentModes inside processBlock decrements (:446, :457, :461-474).
- BodyBank::reset() (body_bank.h:45-50) and applyPendingSwap() (:181) only call sharedBank_.reset(); resetForKitSwitch (drum_voice.h:467-491) runs it on every main and shadow slot via VoicePool::resetAllVoicesForKitSwitch (voice_pool.cpp:268-281).
- StringBody (string_body.h:38-89) ignores the shared bank in every method, and DrumVoice's String paths skip it too (drum_voice.h:1576-1577, 1589-1590, 1644-1647); the noteOn String branch comment (drum_voice.h:277-285) "no modes are configured" assumes a clean bank, which is false here.
- Retirement (drum_voice.h:645-651) and the 256-block safety net (:660-669) both need getNumActiveModes()==0; the pool frees a slot only on !isActive() (voice_pool.cpp:354, 386-396, 469, 518), so peak-based auto noteOff cannot free it.
- Reachable in the plugin: kit load while a modal voice rings, or a steal/choke swap (voice_pool.cpp:922) bringing back a shadow with a stale count; factory kits contain many String pads (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1560, 2877, 3541, 5014, ...).
- getPartialInfo (drum_voice.h:1250-1258) reads stale numModes_/epsilonTarget_ (modal_resonator_bank.h:526-529), passed to couplingEngine_->noteOn when couplingAmount > 0 (voice_pool.cpp:243-248).
- Verifiers could not find the quoted vo_probe.cpp under f:/tmp and did not run one; the chain is established from source. No test pins it (test_body_bank.cpp has no getNumActiveModes or isActive check).

#### MB-041 — The single-sample renderer process() diverges from the production block renderers, yet the SC-009 pitch-envelope test and the Phase-1 golden run only process()

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** parallel-path · **Dimension:** voice-signal-path (also flagged by: parallel-paths)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:497-567](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L497)

**Problem.** process() lacks the secondary shell bank, tension modulation and the wire-coupling follower (wireGainMod_ stays 1, 541-549). It never runs retirement or flushSilentModes, so active_ is never cleared on this path. It refreshes the pitch envelope and morph per sample (506-519) and uses the per-sample-smoothing bank.processSample, while processBlockFast and processBlockSlow refresh once per chunk or block through block-rate smoothing. Production (VoicePool, voice_pool.cpp:471, 528) uses only processBlock.

**Why wrong.** The three renderers are meant to stay behaviour-equivalent. A spec acceptance test should exercise the renderer that ships.

**Consequence.** SC-009 (test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:119 `buf[i] = voice.process();`) passes while the shipped block path does not reach 50 Hz at 20 ms (see the pitch-envelope finding). The Phase-1 golden (test_phase1_regression.cpp:71) likewise pins a path no host runs. Regressions in the block path's pitch, shell, tension, wire and retirement stages pass these tests.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:542-546 comment: 'This per-sample process() path ... does not run the block-rate energy follower -- same convention as tension mod and the secondary shell bank, which are also block-path-only'. No secondaryBank_ use or active_ write in 497-567. tests/unit/tone_shaper/test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:119 and tests/approval/test_phase1_regression.cpp:71 both call voice.process(). The probe (vo_probe2.cpp) shows process() tracking the 400 -> 80 Hz sweep (221 -> 80 Hz) while processBlock at 256 samples stays at 87-92 Hz.

**Suggested fix.** Port the spec acceptance tests (SC-009, the phase-1 golden, the pitch-env/morph tests in tests/unit/tone_shaper and unnatural) to DrumVoice::processBlock at several block sizes. Either delete process() or implement it as processBlock(&out, 1) so a single implementation exists.

Test: a renderer-equivalence case rendering the same note through process() and processBlock at block sizes 1/64/2048 and comparing fingerprints.

**Verifier notes.**
- Production uses only processBlock: processor.cpp:636, :663 -> VoicePool::processBlock -> DrumVoice::processBlock (voice_pool.cpp:356, 410, 471, 528); no src .cpp calls DrumVoice::process().
- process() never touches secondaryBank_ (block path :818, :1011/:1041), has no tension modulation (:722-754), leaves wireGainMod_ at 1 (:488, :547-549) and never clears active_ (retirement only at :644-669).
- The block path refreshes pitch and morph once per chunk = whole host block (no sub-blocking, voice_pool.cpp:454, :471; drum_voice.h:701, 734-746, 762-770); the :613-619 comment assumes 64-sample blocks and the :584-587 comment saying pitch-env/morph take the slow path is stale (processBlock:620 routes only Feedback there).
- One verifier showed the block path barely moves: updateModes does not snap (modal_resonator_bank.h:303) and smoothing (smoothCoeff = exp(-1/(2 ms * fs)), :213, :647) advances one step per block, so at 256-sample blocks only about 3.8 % of the retune lands by 20 ms (14.5 % at 64, under one step at 2048), consistent with the quoted 87-92 Hz.
- Both cited tests render only through process() (test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:118-119, test_phase1_regression.cpp:70-71); the only processBlock pitch test (test_pitch_env_all_bodies.cpp:48, 123-138) is qualitative and reads getModeFrequency(0) = epsilonTarget_ (modal_resonator_bank.h:526-533), not the sounding smoothed epsilon_. No renderer-equivalence test exists (test_tom_body_depth.cpp:404 notes one was removed).
- One verifier recommended a downgrade because process() never ships (the audible harm belongs to the separate pitch-envelope finding); final severity stays medium.

#### MB-044 — Tone-shaper bypass ignores the filter type: HP/BP jumps by 20 dB between cutoff 0.999 and 1.0

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** layers-shaper · **Dimension:** layers-shaper (also flagged by: parameter-audibility)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:427-428, 467-474](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h#L427)

**Problem.** filterBypass = cutoff >= 20000 && envAmount == 0 for every filter type. A Highpass or Bandpass at 20 kHz, which should remove almost everything, is replaced by a full-band passthrough. The cutoff comes from 20*pow(1000, norm) (pad_config_apply.h:83-84), so whether norm 1.0 lands exactly on 20000.0 depends on pow's last bit. Under macOS -ffast-math pow may give 19999.99, which disables the bypass on that platform only.

**Why wrong.** The cutoff knob must be continuous for every filter type. The bypass identity (FR-045) is meant for the neutral LP setting only. The root CLAUDE.md rule requires an exact endpoint to be produced by a branch or clamp, not by arithmetic that only happens to land on it.

**Consequence.** HP/BP pads swept to the top of the cutoff knob suddenly play unfiltered at +20 dB (automation spike). The norm-1.0 HP/BP behaviour may differ between Windows and macOS.

**Evidence.** Probe test 8 (HP): norm 0.990 (18665 Hz) rms 0.015281 (-36.3 dBFS); norm 0.999 (19862 Hz) rms 0.015281 (-36.3 dBFS); norm 1.000 (20000 Hz) rms 0.149272 (-16.5 dBFS). Code: :427 `const bool filterBypass = (filterCutoffHz_ >= 20000.0f) && (filterEnvAmount_ == 0.0f);`.

**Suggested fix.** Bypass only when filterType_ == Lowpass. Decide the endpoint with a branch on the normalised value (norm >= 1 -> bypass) instead of comparing the pow result.

Test: HP and BP at norm 0.999 vs 1.0 differ by no more than 1 dB in output RMS; LP at norm 1.0 stays bit-identical to bypass.

**Verifier notes.**
- tone_shaper.h:427-428 never reads filterType_ (stored at :136, member at :488, selects LP/HP/BP at :137-148); isBypassed() (:467-474) has the same gap; setFilterCutoff (:151-156) does not clamp.
- All three renderers call toneShaper_.processSample (drum_voice.h:559, 883, 896, 1059), so all take the same bypass branch.
- HP/BP are user-selectable (editor.uidesc:269-270); recipes.json:16912 notes "engaging the filter (cutoff<20k) is required for the HP type to act", showing the authors knew.
- Impact is wider than stated: the default pad has tsFilterCutoff 1.0 (pad_config.h:197) and tsFilterEnvAmount 0.5, which decodes to exactly 0.0 (pad_config.h:199, pad_config_apply.h:86), so choosing HP or BP on a default pad does nothing audible until the cutoff moves, then the level drops about 20 dB.
- FR-045 (specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:229) requires a no-effect bypass state per stage; for HP that would be the lowest cutoff, so it does not justify this.
- The macOS fast-math part is speculative and unmeasured (`pow(1000.f, 1.f)` is usually exact); it only moves where the jump happens, not whether it exists.

#### MB-045 — modeInject output is unscaled against the body budget: amount 1 pins the voice on its hardClip rail

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** layers-shaper · **Dimension:** layers-shaper

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/mode_inject.h:54-61, 124-126, 137-145](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/mode_inject.h#L54)

**Problem.** The 8 partials have amplitude 1/k (sum about 2.72), skipNormalization=true, and process() returns amount*env*bank. The result is added after the body has been normalised to kBodyHeadroom 0.5 (drum_voice.h:557, 893, 1056), with no headroom scaling. At amount 0.5 the voice peaks at 0.80, and at 1.0 it sits on the hardClip safety rail for hundreds of samples.

**Why wrong.** drum_voice.h:561-566 states that the hardClip rail 'engages only on a pathological/runaway voice, never on a musical hit at the Step-3/4 budget'. A full-scale value of a user knob is a musical setting.

**Consequence.** Hard-clipping distortion, and the pad jumps about 8 dB in level, when modeInject is turned up. The knob's top half mostly changes loudness and adds clipping rather than adding harmonics.

**Evidence.** Probe tests 5/10 (Membrane, material 0.5, decay 0.8, level 0.8, block 256, 1 s): inject 0.00 peak 0.403 (-7.9 dBFS); 0.30 peak 0.513; 0.50 peak 0.802; 1.00 peak 1.000 with 804 samples at the hardClip rail.
