**Consequence.** Coupling-resonator leaks (orphaned sympathetic ringing, refcounts), aux-bus silence flags, aux zeroing and any future drift in the multi-bus path are untested. A bug that only appears with aux buses (the PluginBuddy "continuous sine" report at :1497-1502) is caught only by ad hoc cases.

**Evidence.** Grep `numOutputs` in plugins/membrum/tests: = 1 in membrum_processor_tests.cpp:93, test_coupling_energy.cpp:90, test_coupling_integration.cpp:101, test_coupling_state.cpp:77, test_kit_preset_load_render.cpp:109, test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:228/1179, test_kit_browser_load.cpp:141, test_pad_preset.cpp:475, test_macro_automation_extreme.cpp:105, test_output_level_measure.cpp:93, and more. voice_pool.cpp:386-396 (mono, with coupling noteOff) vs 514-519 (multi-bus, without).

**Suggested fix.** Make the shared processor fixtures default to the real topology, numOutputs = kMaxOutputBuses with aux buffers allocated. Add to test_coupling_integration.cpp `TEST_CASE("Mono and multi-bus render paths are equivalent on the main bus", "[membrum][processor][multi-bus]")`: render the same note sequence with numOutputs=1 and numOutputs=16 (all aux inactive), CHECK the main-bus difference <= -120 dBFS, then after every voice has retired CHECK the coupling engine's active resonator count is 0 in both. It is red today because of the missing noteOff at voice_pool.cpp:514-519. (Verifiers: this last assertion would NOT go red; see notes.)

**Verifier notes:**
- Test gap and drift both confirmed: processor.cpp:633-637 (mono when numOutputBuses <= 1) vs 638-666 (multi-bus); only test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:1545 and test_coupling_phase9_verification.cpp:121 use several buses; voice_pool.cpp:386-396 calls couplingEngine_->noteOff(slot), voice_pool.cpp:514-519 does not.
- Consequence overstated: SympatheticResonance::noteOff (sympathetic_resonance.h:264-298) only edits ownerVoiceIds_ / refCounts_ / voiceIds_; resonators are reclaimed by envelope alone in process() (337-351), and noteOn calls noteOff(voiceId) first (179-181), so there is no leak or orphaned ringing, only stale refcounts that skew the merge average (199-204) and can fill the 8-entry owner list.
- The proposed "active resonator count is 0" assertion would not be red because of voice_pool.cpp:514-519, since envelope reclaim zeroes the count on both paths.
- Steal (voice_pool.cpp:207) and choke (voice_pool.cpp:1041) still call noteOff on both paths; 29 of 31 `numOutputs =` assignments in the tests are 1.
- Aux routing is partly covered: tests/unit/voice_pool/test_multi_bus_output.cpp calls the multi-bus overload directly in 7 cases; processor-level aux silence flags and aux zeroing (processor.cpp:644-680) remain unpinned.
- Net: real test gap and real maintenance-hazard drift, nil audible impact today; medium or low, not high. Still add the noteOff at voice_pool.cpp:514 and default the fixtures to the multi-bus topology.

#### MB-142 — The phase-1 golden is a self-regenerated change detector over the unused per-sample renderer, and it silently skips when the file is missing

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/approval/test_phase1_regression.cpp:40-45, 51-73, 79-95, 160-168](plugins/membrum/tests/approval/test_phase1_regression.cpp#L40-L45)

**Problem.** (1) The golden renders through DrumVoice::process() (line 71), the single-sample renderer. It has no secondary shell, tension or wire follower, and VoicePool never calls it. (2) The golden is produced by the hidden [.generate_golden] case from the same code. It has been regenerated five times (git log: f4343de1, 08975a47, 41877a8e, 0a869cea, a1480c6b), each time output changed, so it carries no independent truth. (3) If the file is not found it calls WARN and SUCCEED and returns (160-168). The locator tries relative paths and a hard-coded F:/projects/iterum path, so a runner whose working directory is not the repo root skips the test silently. (4) isFiniteSample is the forbidden 0x7F800000 bit-mask clone (40-45), which Apple clang folds to "finite" under -ffast-math.

**Why wrong.** A regression golden should pin the shipping path (VoicePool/processor processBlock) and fail loudly when missing. A bit-mask finiteness check is vacuous on the macOS leg (root CLAUDE.md fast-math rules; it is in the lint-finite-bitmask baseline).

**Consequence.** Regressions in processBlockFast/Slow, the pool, the limiter or the per-pad pipeline are not caught. A renamed or moved golden turns the test green. The macOS NaN check on golden generation is a no-op.

**Evidence.** test_phase1_regression.cpp:71 `out[i] = voice.process();`; :162-167 `if (!readGolden(path, golden)) { WARN(...); SUCCEED("Skipping regression comparison until golden is generated."); return; }`; :86 `"F:/projects/iterum/plugins/membrum/tests/golden/phase1_default.bin"`; :44 `return (bits & 0x7F800000u) != 0x7F800000u;`. tools/lint-finite-bitmask-baseline.json:41 lists this file.

**Suggested fix.** Render the golden through VoicePool::processBlock (64-sample blocks) and compare with tests/test_helpers/render_fingerprint.h (aggregate metrics plus checkpoints) instead of a raw-sample RMS. Replace the WARN/SUCCEED skip with `REQUIRE(readGolden(...))`, locating the file via MEMBRUM_RESOURCES_DIR/../tests/golden. Use Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite. Record why each re-baseline happened in a sidecar note so a re-baseline is a reviewed decision.

**Verifier notes:**
- All four sub-claims confirmed: test_phase1_regression.cpp:70-71 calls `voice.process()`, while VoicePool calls only `DrumVoice::processBlock` (voice_pool.cpp:356, 410, 471, 528), which dispatches to processBlockSlow / processBlockFast (drum_voice.h:591-629); drum_voice.h:542-546 says the energy follower, tension mod and secondary shell are "block-path-only".
- The golden was re-baselined even more often than claimed: `git log` on phase1_default.bin shows 8 commits (25b41aa0, 89cf0c64, c7ee78ef, f4343de1, 08975a47, 41877a8e, 0a869cea, a1480c6b); the header at :9-15 admits deliberate re-baselines.
- The silent skip is latent but real: tests/CMakeLists.txt:277 calls catch_discover_tests without WORKING_DIRECTORY, so ctest from the binary dir resolves only the hard-coded F: path; run-gate.js:155 spawns with the repo-root cwd, so the usual local gate does find the file.
- The bit-mask clone (:40-45, baseline :41) is used only in the hidden generation case (:140), so its impact is limited to golden generation.
- No other render golden or fingerprint exists in plugins/membrum/tests (tests/golden/ holds only phase1_default.bin and the state blob phase2_state_v2.bin); other tests (e.g. test_secondary_shell_paths.cpp) cover parts of the block path. Medium fits a test gap with no user-facing effect.

#### MB-148 — No test chokes a slot whose shadow is still fading from a steal (non-forced beginFastRelease early return), and the "third steal inside 5 ms" case is uncovered

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Also flagged by:** prior-audit-regressions · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:892-893, 1037-1058](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L892-L893)

**Problem.** processChokeGroups calls beginFastRelease(slot) without force. If that slot's shadow is still FastReleasing (a steal within the last ~5 ms), beginFastRelease returns at :892 without swapping, but the caller still marks meta_ Free and idles the allocator slot (1055-1057). The ringing main voice keeps playing unramped and unchoked. The voice-pool tests cover double-steal idempotence (test_fast_release_double_steal.cpp:64) and the M-8 forced re-steal (test_fast_release_resteal_collision.cpp:144), but not choke, Quietest pre-steal or polyphony shrink into a busy shadow, nor a third same-slot steal inside 5 ms.

**Why wrong.** A choke group (open/closed hat) must silence every voice of the group within 5 +/- 1 ms (spec 138 SC-022). A non-forced fast release into a busy shadow silently breaks that.

**Consequence.** An open hat keeps ringing after the closed hat when the two hits arrive within 5 ms of a steal on the same slot. Fast hat patterns at full polyphony can do this.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:892-893: `if (releasingMeta_[slot].state == VoiceSlotState::FastReleasing && !force) return;`. voice_pool.cpp:1047-1057: `beginFastRelease(slot); ... meta_[slot].state = VoiceSlotState::Free; (void)allocator_.noteOff(victimNote); allocator_.voiceFinished(...)`. Voice-pool TEST_CASE list: test_fast_release_double_steal.cpp:64, test_fast_release_resteal_collision.cpp:144, test_choke_click_free.cpp:353, test_choke_group.cpp:60-304, none with a busy shadow plus choke.

**Suggested fix.** Add to test_choke_click_free.cpp `TEST_CASE("Choke into a slot whose shadow is still fading mutes the main voice within 6 ms", "[membrum][voice_pool][choke][m8]")`. maxPolyphony 4, fill the slots, steal slot k (shadow busy), within 2 ms trigger a choke-group mate of slot k's new voice, then CHECK the slot-k contribution is below -60 dBFS 6 ms later. Same pattern for Quietest pre-steal and setMaxPolyphony shrink, plus `TEST_CASE("Three same-slot steals within 5 ms are click-free", ...)` asserting click peak <= -30 dBFS.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code path confirmed: voice_pool.cpp:892-893 returns early when the shadow is FastReleasing and `force` is false, skipping the swap (:922) and snapshot (:946-951); processChokeGroups (:1047), the Quietest pre-steal (:171-177) and the polyphony-shrink path (:583-584) are all non-forced; only the allocator Steal path passes force=true (:221), and its M-8 comment (:214-220) assumes the choke already retired its victims.
- processBlock renders any voice with VP_VOICES[slot].isActive() whatever its meta state (:354, :469); the auto-noteOff (:380-381, :508-509) and natural-finish path (:386) run only while meta is Active, so the un-swapped voice is neither faded nor tracked.
- Two outcomes, both breaking FR-134 / SC-022: if the allocator places the next note on another idle slot (findIdleVoiceOldest voice_allocator.h:567, findIdleVoiceAny :608) the choked voice rings on; if it picks the same slot, applyPadConfigToSlot + noteOn (:232-233) overwrite it with no fade, a click.
- Stronger trigger: a freshly stolen voice has currentLevel 0 (:256) until the next block, so the second of two coincident note-ons at full polyphony picks it as Quietest and overwrites it in the same block.
- Window length is disputed: one verifier reads applyFastRelease (:988-995, gain < 1e-6) as ~69 ms and argued for an upgrade; another reads fastReleaseK_ = exp(-ln(1e6)/(0.005*sr)) (voice_pool.cpp:85-86, voice_pool.h:82-83) as exactly 5 ms (220 samples at 44.1 kHz). A previous choke on the slot also occupies the shadow.
- No test covers it: test_choke_allocation_free.cpp:40 checks only allocation and finiteness; test_fast_release_double_steal.cpp asserts the very early return that causes this.

#### MB-161 — With Material Morph on, the per-chunk morph refresh overwrites the pitch-envelope and tension scaling (the last updateModes in the chunk wins)

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-path · **Dimension:** gestalt-voice · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:506-519, 734-770, 960-977, 1607-1665](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L734-L770)

**Problem.** In every renderer the order per chunk is: (1) retuneFundamental(pitchHz) or the tension branch, which scales cachedMapperResult_ by pitchHz / naturalFundamentalHz_ and calls updateModes; then (2) if morph is enabled, refreshBodyForMaterialOnBank, which REPLACES cachedMapperResult_ with mapModalBody(..., pitchHz 0) and calls pushCachedModes -> updateModes with the unscaled, natural-pitch frequencies. The bank targets after each chunk are therefore always at the natural pitch. morphActive is just isEnabled(), so this repeats every chunk for the whole note, even after the morph has finished.

**Why wrong.** The pitch envelope, tension and morph are independent per-pad features, and the comment at 1601-1606 says the scaling works for whatever mapper result is cached. The morph should change timbre and damping while the pitch modulation keeps scaling the frequencies.

**Consequence.** Any pad with Morph Enabled has a dead pitch envelope (apart from the noteOn seed, which is overwritten by the first chunk) and a dead tension glide. Example: factory pad 4 of "Experimental FX Kit" sets tsPitchEnvTime 0.12 (230->160 Hz) together with morphEnabled 1.0 (generator.cpp:1437-1443). Many other factory pads enable morph (generator.cpp:1455, 1569, 1613, ...). This compounds the smoothing-lag finding: fixing that alone does not restore the sweep on morph pads.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:734-746 `retuneFundamental(pitchHz);` followed by :762-769 `if (morphActive) { ... refreshBodyForMaterialOnBank(bodyBank_.getSharedBank(), m); }`; :1650-1651 `cachedMapperResult_ = mapModalBody(t, p, /*pitchHz*/ 0.0f); pushCachedModes(sharedBank);` (unscaled); the same order in processBlockSlow :960-977 and process() :506-519; :609 `morphActive = unnaturalZone_.materialMorph.isEnabled()`.

**Suggested fix.** Keep one "push modes" function per chunk. Re-map for the morph material if morph is active, then apply the current pitch ratio (pitch-env Hz x tension mod / natural f0) to that result, then call updateModes once. Store the last ratio so live parameter edits (updateModalParameters) re-apply it as well. Test: Membrane pad with morph 0.2->0.8 over 300 ms and pitch env 160->50 Hz over 50 ms. At 100 ms the bank's mode-0 frequency (target, and once the lag is fixed the audio f0) must be about 50 Hz x (mode0 / natural), not the natural f0.

**Verifier notes:**
- Traced through all three renderers: updateModalFundamentalOnBank (:1607-1626) scales and calls updateModes, then refreshBodyForMaterialOnBank (:1638-1652) resets cachedMapperResult_ to mapModalBody(t, p, 0.0f) and pushCachedModes (:1656-1665) calls updateModes with unscaled frequencies; same order at :960-977 and :506-519.
- The mappers ignore pitch (unnamed `float /*pitchHz*/` in membrane_mapper.h:89, plate_mapper.h:34, shell_mapper.h:39, bell_mapper.h:30, noise_body_mapper.h:90), and ModalResonatorBank::updateModes (modal_resonator_bank.h:294-305) rewrites the coefficient targets, so the second call wins.
- morphActive is isEnabled() (material_morph.h:65), not isActive() (:110-113); after the morph ends process() keeps returning endMaterial_ (:84-89), so the override never stops. The noteOn seed (:318-320) is overwritten by the first chunk.
- Scope: the five modal bodies only; String returns early through refreshStringMaterial (:1644-1648). The tension glide is lost only on Membrane pads.
- Quantified for Experimental FX Kit pad 4 (generator.cpp:1430-1443): Plate size 0.55 has natural f0 ≈ 225 Hz (natural_fundamental.h:34-39), so the designed 230->160 Hz sweep is gone and the pad settles ~5.9 semitones sharp; pad 2 (generator.cpp:1718, 1730-1732, 210->150 Hz) is also affected.
- Nothing makes the features exclusive (MANUAL.md:355; comment at 1601-1606 implies they compose), and no test combines morph with the pitch envelope.

#### MB-168 — Per-pad Coupling Amount (offset 36) only gates on > 0; its magnitude has no audible effect

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dead-parameter · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:243-248](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L243-L248)

**Problem.** The only audio-path use of couplingAmount is the on/off test `padConfigs_[padIndex].couplingAmount > 0.0f` before couplingEngine_->noteOn(slot, partials). The value itself feeds only recomputeCouplingMatrix (processor.cpp:131-143, 208-216), whose output is unused.

**Why wrong.** Spec 140 FR-014/FR-023 describe couplingAmount as a per-pad scalar that weights the pad as source and receiver. A continuous 0..1 knob that acts as a boolean is a weak parameter.

**Consequence.** Turning a pad's Coupling Amount from 0.01 to 1.0 changes nothing. Level, centroid, decay and band distance all change by less than 0.1 dB / 1 %.

**Evidence.** Quality probe param:offset=36:couplingAmount: "36: 0.0/0/0/0.0 ; 38: 0.0/0/0/0.0 ; 42: 0.0/0/0/0.0 (not bit-identical); live=no". voice_pool.cpp:243-244 `if (couplingEngine_ != nullptr && padConfigs_[static_cast<std::size_t>(padIndex)].couplingAmount > 0.0f)`.

**Suggested fix.** Scale the voice's partial registration gain (or the per-voice send into the coupling engine) by couplingAmount, the same wiring that would revive Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance. Test: partner energy grows monotonically with couplingAmount.

**Verifier notes:**
- The only audio-path read is the gate at voice_pool.cpp:243-248; the partials (SympatheticPartialInfo, drum_voice.h:1250) carry no amount and SympatheticResonance::noteOn (sympathetic_resonance.h:179) takes no gain.
- recomputeCouplingMatrix (processor.cpp:131-143) fills CouplingMatrix::effectiveGain_ (coupling_matrix.h:42-99); a grep for couplingMatrix_ / effectiveGain / getEffectiveGain finds no reader except the test accessor couplingMatrixForTest() (processor.h:81).
- The coupling stage (processor.cpp:693-707) is mono sum -> couplingDelay_ -> couplingEngine_.process -> limiter, with strength set only by the global setAmount (processor.cpp:404-408, 978).
- Other reads are state I/O, clamping or MacroMapper writes (state_codec.cpp:153/249/401/491, controller_state_codec.cpp:171/244, macro_mapper.cpp:206, voice_pool.cpp:661); the Complexity macro's couplingAmount leg (processor.cpp:224-228) is therefore near-dead too.
- The knob is user-visible (editor.uidesc:93 binds tag 1036, :241 places the ArcKnob), and MANUAL.md:376 and the processor.cpp:210-213 comment describe a continuous weight.
- Evidence caveat: the probe likely ran with globalCoupling at its default 0 (plugin_ids.h:114), which bypasses the engine, so the measurement alone is weak; the source trace proves the claim regardless.

#### MB-171 — Kick pitch and decay depend on sample rate: tension modulation uses raw modal state energy, which grows with the number of excitation samples

**Severity:** medium (one verifier recommends low) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured · **Corroborated by research:** Physics (oversimplified): snare wire buzz = noise layer scaled by the head's self-normalised modal-energy envelope (Fletcher & Rossing §18.13; Torin, Hamilton & Bilbao, DAFx-14; Torin & Newton, ISMA 2014) · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:420-421, 722-728, 910-914](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L420-L421)

**Problem.** tensionPitchMod = 1 + tensionAmtEffective_ * energyEnv_, where energyEnv_ follows sharedBank.getModalEnergy() (modal_resonator_bank.h:493-499, the sum of sin^2+cos^2 of the raw states). The bank's input gain is the bare mode amplitude, with no 1/sr or (1-R) normalisation, so a fixed-duration exciter pulse injects about sr-proportional amplitude and sr^2 energy. tensionAmtEffective_ = tensionModAmt * kTensionEnergyScale, a constant with no sample-rate term.

**Why wrong.** Pitch, decay and level must not depend on the host sample rate. The bare DrumVoice with tension off is sample-rate invariant (0.1 c).

**Consequence.** The default kick sits 24 cents higher and decays 18 % faster at 192 kHz than at 44.1 kHz, so mixes rendered at different rates differ. The effect grows with tensionModAmt (Tabla bayan 0.78-0.85).

**Evidence.** Probe srate:kick36: "73.43/73.51/74.23/74.56 Hz (+24.4 c), 1.09/1.09/0.96/0.89 s (-18 %)", note "DrumVoice alone is SR-invariant ... Pitch env OFF + tension 0 gives 0.1 c ... from the block-rate pitch env / tension path". drum_voice.h:726 `std::min(1.0f + tensionAmtEffective_ * energyEnv_, kTensionPitchModMax)`; :912 `const float e = bodyBank_.getSharedBank().getModalEnergy();`.

**Suggested fix.** Normalise the energy reading by sample rate (for example divide getModalEnergy() by (sr/48000)^2), or calibrate kTensionEnergyScale per sample rate in prepare(). Test: default kick at 44.1/48/96/192 kHz, fundamental spread <= 5 cents and decay60 spread <= 10 %.

**Verifier notes:**
- Mechanism confirmed: kTensionEnergyScale is the constant 3.3e-5f (drum_voice.h:94), calibrated at :92-93 against a "hard tom hit peaks ~2.4e3" energy at one rate; the follower coefficient is rate-aware (:132, :913) but the energy it follows is not.
- The bank injects with `gain_k = amp` (modal_resonator_bank.h:829-835, normalisation removed on purpose) and the kernel `s_new = R*(s+eps*c) + gain*ex` (:938/:959) sums per-sample inputs; the default kick's ImpactExciter pulse has fixed duration (impact_exciter.h:132-146, :241) and the ClickLayer burst is burstMs * sr (click_layer.h:97), so modal energy scales ~sr^2 (~19x from 44.1 to 192 kHz).
- measuredStrikeOutputGain (drum_voice.h:302) renormalises only the output gain, and getModalEnergy is invariant to outputGain_ (modal_resonator_bank.h:486); wire coupling divides by its running peak (:1512) and is unaffected. Default kick tensionModAmt is 0.8 (default_kit.h:84).
- Pitch part confirmed by probe-results.txt:428-429: tension's own contribution grows from ~+18 c at 44.1 kHz to ~+55 c at 192 kHz (tension 0 reads 72.67 / 72.62 / 72.38 / 72.24 Hz).
- Decay part is misattributed: with tension 0 (:431) decay still falls 19 %, and with block duration scaled to the rate (:430) it stays within 10 %, so the decay shift comes from the fixed 512-sample host block, not tension.
- Practical impact: 1.9 c between 44.1 and 48 kHz, ~+17 c at 96 kHz, ~+24 c at 192 kHz (capped at +300 c by kTensionPitchModMax); one verifier downgrades to low on that basis.

#### MB-175 — String body is not level-normalised: it peaks at -0.02 dBFS while every modal body peaks near -6 dBFS

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:277-285](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L277-L285)

**Problem.** For BodyModelType::String the voice sets bank.setOutputGain(kBodyHeadroom / bank.getInputGainSum()) on the shared modal bank, which the comment admits never reaches the audio path. The WaveguideString output (string_body.h, string_.noteOn(f, 1.0f)) is mixed unscaled.

**Why wrong.** Audit N-1 sets kBodyHeadroom = 0.5 (-6 dBFS strike peak) as the body budget for all bodies, so the pad balance and the limiter margin assume it.

**Consequence.** String pads are about 6 dB hotter than the other bodies at the same Level, ride the hardClip and the bus limiter (Ghost Bones 47/51, Chaos 51), and break the kit balance.

**Evidence.** Probe level:body headroom: "Membrane -5.96, Plate -5.94, Shell -6.67, Bell -5.98, NoiseBody -6.16, String -0.02". drum_voice.h:279-283 comment "the bank's output gain never reaches the audio path" then `bank.setOutputGain(kBodyHeadroom / bank.getInputGainSum());`.

**Suggested fix.** Measure the waveguide's strike peak (a short probe render of string_ after noteOn, cached by frequency, decay and brightness) and apply kBodyHeadroom / peak to the String output. Test: probe level:body headroom gives String within 1 dB of -6.02 dBFS.

**Verifier notes:**
- Source confirmed: only the modal branch calls measuredStrikeOutputGain (drum_voice.h:302-304, 1366-1386); string_body.h:58 calls string_.noteOn(r.frequencyHz, 1.0f) and processSample / processBlock (62-89) return string_.process(excitation) unscaled; bodyScratch goes straight into body + noise + click -> ToneShaper -> hardClip (drum_voice.h:799, 880-885; slow path 1030-1061).
- WaveguideString's own excitation normalisation (waveguide_string.h:370-462) is unrelated to kBodyHeadroom.
- Measurement in specs/membrum-audit/probes/probe-results.txt:34-39: String -0.02 dBFS (flagged "suspicious") vs modal bodies -5.94..-6.67; exciter x body matrix at default Level 0.8 puts String at -1.77..-2.06 dBFS (lines 102, 132, 162, 192, 222, 252, 282) vs Shell -4.1..-8.5.
- Repeats the String part of prior N-1, left unfixed: AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:147 measured String ≈ 0.99, and :120 / :415 call it "harmless" only with respect to the unused bank gain; test_body_headroom_budget.cpp:85 checks only Membrane and Bell.
- Factory kits (verifier's pass over kit-pads.csv, enabled pads): mean String pad peak -10.25 dBFS (n=30) vs -15.7..-18.8 for other bodies; 5 of 30 String pads (~17 %) hit the bus-limiter flag vs 16 of 429 (~3.7 %) others; Chaos Engine 51, Ghost Bones 47 and 51, Drone and Sustain 36, Experimental FX 39 sit at -7.00 dBFS with 0.00 dB margin (quality-results.txt:33, 48, 49).
- Velocity response stays linear at default Level (vel 1.0 vs 0.25 ≈ 12 dB); a hot exciter at Level 1.0 (Clap ≈ +0.2 dBFS) would engage the rail.

#### MB-183 — PadCategory classifies only 2 of 517 factory pads as Snare because the Snare rule requires the NoiseBurst exciter

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-kit-quality · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_category.h:30-46](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_category.h#L30-L46)

**Problem.** classifyPad: Membrane+Mallet -> Tom, Membrane+pitchEnv -> Kick, Membrane+NoiseBurst -> Snare, else Tom. The redesigned snares use Impulse plus the noise layer (default_kit.h:98) and many hand drums carry short pitch envelopes, so snares fall through to Tom or Kick, and congas and bongos become "Kick".

**Why wrong.** Coupling categories (Kick->Snare buzz, Tom->Tom resonance; spec 140) must reflect the pads' real roles. The rules were written for the old NoiseBurst snare recipe.

**Consequence.** Even once Snare Buzz is wired it would have almost no targets: notes 38/40 classify as 9 Kick, 16 Perc, 4 Tom, 1 Snare across the factory kits. Hand Drums congas are classified Kick (kit-pads.csv), so they would be treated as buzz sources.

**Evidence.** Quality category:PadCategory distribution: "76 / 2 / 83 / 75 / 223 ; notes 38/40: Kick 9, Perc 16, Tom 4, Snare 1". kit-pads.csv: "Percussive,Hand Drums,36,0,1,Impulse,Membrane,Kick". pad_category.h:42-43 `if (cfg.exciterType == ExciterType::NoiseBurst) return PadCategory::Snare;`

**Suggested fix.** Classify a Snare by Membrane + noiseLayerMix*noiseLayerGain above a threshold (wire present) regardless of exciter. Classify a Kick by a low f0 (size) plus a pitch env with a large start/end ratio, not just any pitch env time > 0. Test: every factory note-38 snare classifies Snare, and congas/bongos classify Tom.

**Verifier notes:**
- Rules confirmed at pad_category.h:30-45, and rule (b) `tsPitchEnvTime > 0 -> Kick` runs before rule (c), so even a NoiseBurst snare with a pitch envelope classifies Kick (808, 909, LinnDrum, Trap, Jazz Brushes note-38 snares).
- The default snare (default_kit.h:87-120) is Impulse + Membrane with noiseLayerMix 0.65 / noiseLayerGain 6.2 and tsPitchEnvTime defaults to 0 (pad_config.h:204), so the default kit's own snares at notes 38 and 40 (default_kit.h:410, 412) classify Tom and receive Tom Resonance (coupling_matrix.h:61-63).
- Consumers: processor.cpp:116/186/197/205/987/1011 feed CouplingMatrix::recomputeFromTier1 (processor.cpp:138), which couples only Kick->Snare and Tom->Tom (coupling_matrix.h:56-63); pad_grid_view.cpp:116-122 labels the grid from the same function, so the editor shows these snares as "K" or "T".
- Snare Buzz is already wired and visible (controller.cpp:517, processor.cpp:411-414, editor.uidesc:23 and 402-404, MANUAL.md:431), so the knob is dead in 19 of 20 factory kits and the default kit.
- Recount of specs/membrum-audit/probes/kit-pads.csv: 459 enabled pads (not 517): Kick 76, Snare 2, Tom 83, HatCymbal 75, Perc 223; notes 38/40 give Kick 13, Perc 22, Tom 4, Snare 1; the two Snares are Jazz Brushes 39 and Orchestral 38; Hand Drums / Latin Perc membranes at 36, 38, 39, 42, 44 classify Kick (kit-pads.csv:354-357).
- Tests use a hand-built NoiseBurst snare (test_pad_category.cpp:69-76, test_coupling_integration.cpp:333-338), never the real default-kit snare. Medium fits: Snare Buzz defaults to 0 (plugin_ids.h:115) and gain is capped at kMaxCoefficient 0.05 (coupling_matrix.h:23).

#### MB-186 — Experimental FX kit: metal hats 42/44 are bit-identical and 46 is within 1 dB (only Decay differs, and Decay is dead under b1/b3 overrides)

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-kit-quality · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1451-1467](tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp#L1451-L1467)

**Problem.** pads[8] = pads[6] with decay 0.08 -> 0.04; pads[10] = pads[6] with decay 0.60 and noiseLayerDecay 0.55. Pad 6 sets bodyDampingB3 = 0.0 and inherits the generator's default bodyDampingB1 = 0.40 (line 135), so both overrides are set and Decay has no effect (ENGINE cause, see the Decay finding). Only noiseLayerDecay separates 46.

**Why wrong.** Closed, pedal and open hat should differ clearly in length.

**Consequence.** Notes 42 and 44 render identically (bandDist 0.00), and the open hat 46 is within 1.02 dB of both. The kit has no usable open/closed hat contrast.

**Evidence.** Quality sameness: "ExpFX 42 vs 44: 0.00/1.000/1.000; ExpFX 42/44 vs 46: 1.02/1.046/1.000". Generator 1463-1467 `pads[8] = pads[6]; pads[8].decay = 0.04; pads[10] = pads[6]; pads[10].decay = 0.60; pads[10].noiseLayerDecay = 0.55;` 1457 `pads[6].bodyDampingB3 = 0.0;`

**Suggested fix.** ENGINE: revive Decay under overrides. DATA: give the three hats distinct bodyDampingB1 values (for example 0.75 / 0.85 / 0.2) and noiseLayerDecay values. Test: sameness probe 0 near-dups, and 46 decay60 >= 3x that of 42.

**Verifier notes:**
- Data confirmed: experimentalKit() (generator.cpp:1380-1381) starts from defaultPads() (:216-217); pad 6 is Bell/NoiseBurst, sets only bodyDampingB3 = 0.0 (:1457) and keeps the struct defaults bodyDampingB1 = 0.40 (:135) and noiseLayerDecay 0.3 (:118); nothing after :1469 touches pads 6, 8 or 10. The shipped file is plugins/membrum/resources/presets/Kit Presets/Unnatural/Experimental FX Kit.vstpreset.
- Decay only feeds r.decayTime (bell_mapper.h:61-68), which dampingLawFromParams (membrane_mapper.h:64-80) discards when both B1 >= 0 and B3 >= 0 (DampingLaw has only b1 / b3, modal_resonator_bank.h:111-139); here b1 ≈ 20.1 s^-1, T60 ≈ 0.34 s.
- Decay's other uses do nothing here: modeInject.setDecaySeconds (drum_voice.h:331) with modeInjectAmount 0, the fixed amp envelope (drum_voice.h:159-162), the strike-norm cache key (drum_voice.h:1401, same measured bank so same gain), and the secondary shell uses bodyDampingB1_ (drum_voice.h:1472).
- Result matches the measurement: 42 and 44 render bit-identically; 46 differs only by noise-layer decay (noise_layer.h:90), the ~1 dB gap.
- Context: MANUAL.md:237 documents Decay as a convenience derivation only when the Phase 8A knobs are at default, so the ENGINE half of the fix is arguable; the factory-kit data defect stands, and other kits avoid it by giving the hats distinct bodyDampingB1 values.

#### MB-204 — Physics (contradicted): Strike-position weighting cos(m*theta)*cos(n*pi*rho) is the free-plate mode shape at the strike point

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:plate-modes · **Also flagged by:** research:strike-position, research:extra:plate-chladni-exponent · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h:103-129](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h#L103-L129) (consumers [plate_mapper.h:45-53](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_mapper.h#L45-L53) with a 0.05 floor, [noise_body_mapper.h:108-113](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h#L108-L113) with a 0.03 floor)

**Problem.** rho = 0.40 + 0.50*strikePos; theta = strikePos*pi/2; amplitude = |cos(m*theta) * cos(n*pi*rho)|, floored at 0.05 for Plate and 0.03 for NoiseBody. The comment says the shape is R_mn(r) cos(m theta) (Leissa; Rossing Ch. 3), so a strike sweeping both radius and azimuth excites every mode.

**Why wrong.** A free circular plate is axisymmetric. A point strike at (r0, theta0) excites the member of each degenerate pair (cos m theta, sin m theta) that is aligned with theta0, so the modal weight is |R_mn(r0)| / ||R_mn|| and does not depend on azimuth. The cos(m theta) factor is therefore non-physical. R_mn = J_m(lambda r) + C I_m(lambda r), which goes like r^m near the centre; Rossing (2001) observes the centre of the n=0 cymbal modes barely moves and that this still region grows with m. cos(n pi rho) is not R_mn either: the coded n=0 radial factor is 1 at every radius, and the coded nodal circles fall at the wrong radii (the (0,1) node is at rho = 0.5 in the code and 0.68 physically). Measured with the Leissa-validated solver (unit modal mass, relative weights): at strikePos 0.3 (the default and the default kit's value; rho 0.55), physical (2,1) 0.98 and (3,1) 1.00 against coded 0.09 and 0.05; physical (6,0) 0.12 and (7,0) 0.09 against coded 0.95 and 0.99. At strikePos 0.5 (theta 45 degrees) the coded fundamental (2,0) and (6,0) are nulled to the floor, while (2,0) is physically 0.58. At strikePos 0 (rho 0.4), every (m,0) mode is coded 1.0 but is physically 0.01-0.21. At strikePos 1 (theta 90 degrees), every odd-m mode is floored even though (3,0), (5,0) and (7,0) are physically about 0.96-1.0 near the edge.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- A.W. Leissa, *Vibration of Plates*, NASA SP-160, 1969, sec. 2.1.3 [textbook]: free-plate mode shape W = [J_n(kr) + C_n I_n(kr)] cos(n theta), with C_n set by the free-edge moment condition; the radial function is a Bessel/modified-Bessel combination, not a cosine.
- T.D. Rossing, "Acoustics of percussion instruments: Recent progress", Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 22(3), 2001, sec. 6.1 [paper] https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ast/22/3/22_3_177/_pdf: "In the n = 0 modes, the center of the cymbal vibrates very little, and this nodal region expands as m increases."
- S. Bilbao, Modal synthesis (CCRMA online notes) [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~bilbao/booktop/node14.html: a point excitation drives each mode in proportion to the mode shape (the projection) at the excitation location.

**Consequence.** Strike Position on Plate and NoiseBody pads runs a pseudo-random comb rather than a centre-to-edge timbre sweep. At the default 0.3 the code boosts the high (m,0) partials that a mid-radius strike barely excites, and nearly removes the (2,1)/(3,1) ring modes that should dominate. At 0.5 the fundamental drops to the floor. The physically expected cue (centre strike dull, edge strike bright and dense in (m,0) modes) is missing or inverted, so this axis does little to separate one metallic pad from another.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research[7] ruled "nuanced" on the old rectangular sin(m pi x) sin(n pi y) weighting: the formula was right, but the strike range was too narrow and the floor was 0.05. The code has changed since: the tracker (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:74) records the switch to cos(m theta) cos(n pi rho). The new formula is not the free-plate shape it claims to be, and the 0.05 floor is still there, so a strike-position defect still applies with a different cause.

**Suggested fix.** Drop the azimuth term. Have the generator emit, for each (m,n), the normalized radial shape R_mn(rho)/||R_mn|| sampled on, say, 33 radii from the Leissa solution, and interpolate it linearly at rho = 0.05 + 0.9*strikePos (centre to near edge). Remove or lower the 0.05/0.03 floors, since the physical shape has no permanent null across a radius sweep except the true nodal circles. Tests: (a) for every (m,0) mode, the weight at strikePos 1 exceeds the weight at strikePos 0.2; (b) the (0,1) weight has its minimum at rho 0.68 +/- 0.03; (c) (2,0) never falls to the floor for strikePos in [0.2, 1]; (d) rewrite the "every mode responds" test at test_plate_body.cpp:97-122 to compare against the generated R_mn table.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed: plate_modes.h:117-129 computePlateAmplitude (rho l.124, theta l.125, return l.128); plate_mapper.h:46-53 floors |amp| at 0.05 over all 48 modes, noise_body_mapper.h:108-113 at 0.03; both use kPlateIndices (l.70-83). strikePos is passed through normalized (voice_common_params.h:19, drum_voice.h:186/1401, pad_config_apply.h:37).
- Coded values recomputed by hand and match: at 0.3, (2,1) 0.09, (3,1) 0.024 floored to 0.05, (6,0) 0.95, (7,0) 0.99; at 0.5, (2,0) and (6,0) are 0 (floored, about -26 dB); at 1, every odd m is 0; at 0, every (m,0) is 1.
- One verifier solved the axisymmetric free-edge eigenproblem in Node (nu = 0.3): lambda^2 = 9.003, the textbook (0,1) value, with the nodal circle at r = 0.680, against the coded 0.5.
- Degenerate-pair azimuth independence is standard modal theory; Bilbao node14 (fetched) confirms excitation weight = mode shape at the strike point. The Rossing 2001 PDF is a scanned image and could not be read.
- Context: the azimuth sweep is intentional ("so every mode responds", comment :107-116; AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:74), and test_plate_body.cpp:97-121 pins only that every mode moves; the comment still presents it as the Leissa shape, so it is a mistaken physical claim, not a ruled simplification. Correctness-audit Finding 8 and the 2026-06 verdict covered the older formula.
- Severity medium kept: one knob on 2 of 6 bodies, NoiseBody's dense wash partly masks the comb; output stays stable.

#### MB-206 — Physics (contradicted): Bell Strike Position = strike azimuth, weighted by |cos(m*theta)|

**Severity:** medium (one verifier recommends lower) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:shell-bell-modes · **Also flagged by:** research:strike-position, research:extra:bell-partials-hibberts (x2) · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/bell_modes.h:22-40, 78-102](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/bell_modes.h#L22-L40)

**Problem.** theta = strikePos * pi/2; amplitude = |cos(m*theta)| / (1 + 0.12 n), floored at 0.05 in BellMapper (bell_mapper.h:43-48). The header calls this the physically correct mode-shape form: "what actually varies the timbre is WHERE around the rim (azimuth theta) the bell is struck".

**Why wrong.** For an axisymmetric bell, every partial with m > 0 is a degenerate pair, cos(m*theta) and sin(m*theta), at one frequency. A point strike at any azimuth excites the combination cos(m(theta - theta0)), whose amplitude does NOT depend on theta0: the mode pattern orients itself to the strike point. Azimuth matters only when asymmetry splits the pair; then each member is weighted cos^2 / sin^2 by azimuth and the pair beats (warble). Cha, Buschert & King measured this directly: with the pair brought back to one frequency, "the amplitude is nearly constant as the bell rotates". The physically meaningful strike variable is the HEIGHT on the profile relative to each partial's nodal circles. Hibberts gives nodal-circle heights as a fraction from lip to shoulder: prime 0.30, tierce 0.54, quint 0.19, nominal 0.54. The code sets that factor to about 1.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- S. Cha, J. Buschert, D. King, "Pseudo-Degeneracy in Handbell Modes", arXiv:1004.0491 (2010) [paper] https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0491: "These two modes would be identical in frequency and truly degenerate if the bell were perfectly symmetrical about its axis." In the pseudo-degenerate case "the amplitude is nearly constant as the bell rotates". (arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed.)
- Perrin, Charnley & DePont, "Normal modes of the modern English church bell", J. Sound Vib. 90(1) (1983) [paper] https://www.hibberts.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/perrin_charnley_depont_1982.pdf: m > 0 modes occur in degenerate pairs (singlets only for m = 0). From the search summary; the PDF is a scanned image.
- Hibberts, "Identifying bell partials" [docs] https://www.hibberts.co.uk/identifying-bell-partials/: nodal-circle heights from lip to shoulder: prime 0.30, tierce 0.54, quint 0.19, nominal 0.54.
- Hibberts, "Doublets or warble in bells" [docs] https://www.hibberts.co.uk/doublets-or-warble-in-bells/: doublets arise only when a bell is "not symmetrical about its vertical axis".

**Consequence.** With one mode per partial, the knob can delete partials that a real bell never loses by being struck at another point on the rim. At strikePos = 1/3 (theta = 30°), both m=3 partials, the tierce and the quint, fall to the 0.05 floor while the hum keeps 0.5 and the nominal 0.45: the tierce, the bell's defining minor third, drops about 19 dB relative to the nominal. At strikePos = 1.0 (theta = 90°), every odd-m partial is floored. This is audible: some settings strip the bell character. It also contradicts the code's own "physics change" comment.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 ruled the earlier radial |cos((k+1)*pi*r)| OVERSIMPLIFIED and recommended a "meridional cos(m*theta) x through-thickness phi_n" form. d9cd848b implemented only the cos(m*theta) half, taking strikePos as the azimuth and setting Z_n ≈ 1. The new form is itself contradicted for a symmetric single-mode model, so the prior recommendation was not correctly realised.

**Suggested fix.** Option A (axisymmetric bell): make each partial's amplitude independent of azimuth and map Strike Position to strike HEIGHT h in [lip, shoulder]. Weight each partial by a profile factor with zeros at its nodal circles, e.g. |cos(pi*(h - h_node)/...)|-style using Hibberts' heights (prime 0.30, tierce 0.54, quint 0.19, nominal 0.54). Option B (real, slightly asymmetric bell): model each m > 0 partial as a split doublet at f(1 ± delta/2), delta ≈ 1e-3..5e-3, with weights cos^2(m*theta0) and sin^2(m*theta0). Azimuth then controls warble, not presence. Test for A: the summed energy of each partial is constant within 0.5 dB across a sweep of the azimuth; the tierce never falls more than 12 dB below the nominal over the whole knob range. Test for B: the doublet amplitudes satisfy a^2 + b^2 = const across theta0.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed: bell_modes.h:96-101 (theta and amplitude), header :22-33 ("azimuth around the rim", Z_n ≈ 1), table :72-76 (hum {2,0}, prime {2,1}, tierce {3,1}, quint {3,1}, nominal {4,1}), floor at bell_mapper.h:43-48; bell_body.h:32-38 passes amplitudes straight to setModes and drum_voice.h:1556 dispatches Bell to BellMapper::map; the decay-skew tilt (bell_mapper.h:76-86) is not a strike shape.
- Arithmetic checks: at strikePos 1/3 tierce/quint = 0 -> floor, hum 0.5, nominal 0.446, tierce vs nominal -19.0 dB; at 1 every odd-m partial is floored.
- Literature: Hibberts "Doublets or warble" (opened) confirms azimuth only redistributes energy between members of a split pair; the arXiv:1004.0491 abstract confirms near-degenerate pairs (the quoted body line was not verified); degenerate pairs are standard (Fletcher & Rossing ch. 21; Perrin et al. 1983). Hibberts' nodal heights were not verified.
- Not a documented simplification: the header calls it a "PHYSICS CHANGE" and AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:76 / :327 mark it DONE; the prior ruling (findings.json ~1388-1392) asked for cos(m*theta) times phi_n, and only the azimuth half was built.
- Severity dispute: presets use the behaviour deliberately (generator.cpp:2807-2820 voices Crotales at strikePos 0.50 to clamp hum and prime; Bell pads at 0.18 / 0.30, e.g. :801, :969, :1856, :2792, keep m=3 well above the floor), so no shipped preset loses its tierce; partial deletion is reachable only by turning the knob. No test covers computeBellAmplitude (only test_decay_skew_all_bodies.cpp:111-116).

#### MB-209 — Physics (oversimplified): High-frequency decay (brightness) mapping: a fixed S per Material, applied once per period

**Severity:** medium (one verifier recommends low) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:string-body · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/string_mapper.h:43-58](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/string_mapper.h#L43-L58) (and [waveguide_string.h:184, 212-214](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/waveguide_string.h#L184))

**Problem.** S = 0.5*(1 - material), independent of f0 and fs. The fundamental's T60 is lerp(0.5, 4, material) * exp(lerp(ln 0.3, ln 3, decay)) = 0.15..12 s, which setDecay clamps to 10 s (waveguide_string.h:144). Because the one-zero filter acts once per period, a partial at frequency f loses -20log10|(1-S)+S e^{-j2pi f/fs}| dB per period, f0 periods per second. Measured: f0 200 Hz, T60 4 s, partial nearest 4 kHz. Material 0 (S = 0.5) gives T60 0.445 / 0.491 / 1.443 s at 44.1 / 48 / 96 kHz. Material 0.5 gives 0.450 / 0.688 / 1.818 s. Material 1 gives 0.697 (44.1 kHz, fractional delay not 0) / 4.109 / 4.054 s. Analytically, at S = 0.5 the per-period gain at 4 kHz is cos(pi*4000/fs) = 0.9597 / 0.9659 / 0.9914.

**Why wrong.** The form is canonical EKS (Faust's pluck uses the same fixed S), and the direction is right: higher Material gives less HF loss and a longer tail, as metal versus gut or nylon would. For a sound that does not depend on the sample rate or Size, the literature designs the loop filter from target decay times in seconds per partial. The energy of partial k obeys E_{m+1}(w_k) = |H(w_k)|^2 E_m(w_k) per period, so the required per-period gain is |H(w_k)| = 10^(-3/(f0*T60(f_k))). With a target damping law sigma(f) = b1 + b3 f^2 (Chaigne-Askenfelt), S must be solved per note from f0 and fs: S(1-S) = (1 - (g_ref/rho)^2) / (4 sin^2(pi f_ref/fs)), clamped to S in [0, 0.5]. The alternative is the Valimaki / Bank-Valimaki one-pole loss filter g(1+a)/(1+a z^-1), designed from T60 at DC and at a high frequency.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- J.O. Smith, *Physical Audio Signal Processing*, "Loop Filter Identification" [textbook] https://www.dsprelated.com/freebooks/pasp/Loop_Filter_Identification.html: the desired loop-filter gain at each harmonic comes from the measured decay rate of the nearest partial; E_{m+1}(w_k) = |H_l(w_k)|^2 E_m(w_k) once per period.
- J.O. Smith, "One-Zero String Damping Filter" (CCRMA REALSIMPLE) [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/realsimple/faust_strings/One_Zero_String_Damping_Filter.html: the filter is applied once per period P; rho is tied to PT and t60; a fixed S gives an HF decay in seconds that scales with f0 and fs.
- Chaigne & Askenfelt, "Numerical simulations of piano strings I", JASA 95(2), 1994 [paper]: per-mode decay rate sigma = b1 + b3*omega^2 in physical frequency, independent of any sampling grid.

**Consequence.** The String body's brightness (how long the upper partials ring) changes by about 3x between a 48 kHz and a 96 kHz session, so a factory kit sounds duller at 44.1 kHz and brighter at 96 kHz. It also scales with Size: the same Material gives 10x the HF decay rate in seconds at Size 0 (800 Hz) as at Size 1 (80 Hz). Material therefore does not set a consistent timbre across pads, which makes String pads harder to voice distinctly.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: Not ruled in 2026-06. The earlier research verdict confirmed that S darkens the tail monotonically but did not examine the dependence on sample rate or f0. Code unchanged since then (string_mapper.h last touched by #245, 2026-06-07).

**Suggested fix.** In StringMapper (or a new WaveguideString::setHfDecay(T60hf, fRef)), compute S per note from f0, fs and a Material-driven HF T60 at a fixed reference frequency (for example 4 kHz) using the closed form above. Keep rho for the fundamental. Pinning test: render at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz (after the claim-2 interpolator fix); the T60 of the partial nearest 4 kHz must agree within +/-15 % across rates, and for Material 0 must equal the mapper's target HF T60 within +/-15 %.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed: string_mapper.h:53 brightness = 1 - material, :56-58 decayTime; string_body.h:47-58 and body_bank.h:140-142 forward unchanged; waveguide_string.h:144 clamps T60 to [0.01, 10] s, :184 / :319 S = brightness*0.5, :212-214 one-zero loss once per loop; computeRho (:178, :318, :596-601) tunes only the fundamental. Nothing compensates S for fs or f0.
- Analytic check: at S = 0.5 the per-period gain is cos(pi f/fs) (0.9659 at 48 kHz, 0.9914 at 96 kHz); the HF loss per second goes as f0*(f/fs)^2, so doubling fs cuts it ~4x, consistent with the ~3x measured T60 change.
- Literature opened and quoted correctly (CCRMA REALSIMPLE one-zero page, PASP loop-filter identification); Membrum's form matches the Faust code (rho from freq*t60, fixed S = B/2).
- Contradicts the WaveguideString spec: specs/_archive_/129-waveguide-string-resonance/spec.md:116 requires all loss-filter coefficients to be recalculated for the active sample rate; FR-005 (:128) defines rho in seconds. The 2026-06 audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:318, findings.json:1490-1511) checked only form and monotonicity. Factory kits use String (generator.cpp:1560, 2877, 3541, 5014, 5139, 5290, 5977, 6159, 6432, 6584).
- Downgrade argument (one verifier): 44.1 vs 48 kHz differs only ~10 % (0.445 vs 0.491 s); the ~3x change appears only at 88.2/96 kHz; f0 / Size scaling is the defining character of canonical EKS; the Material=1 44.1 kHz anomaly comes from the fractional-delay interpolator, a separate claim.

#### MB-213 — Physics (contradicted): NoiseBody's 64-mode cloud is dense enough to fuse into a cymbal wash

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED (one verifier partly refutes the physics framing) · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:noise-body · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h:58-63, 73, 95-106](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h#L58-L63); [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:783-819](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L783-L819)

**Problem.** kNoiseBodyModeCount = 64. The comment says 32 modes over 0.7-20 kHz leave about 600 Hz spacing, which resolves as "a pitched chime (defect D6)", and that "64 halves the spacing so the upper cluster reads as colored noise". The fundamental is f0 = 1500 * 0.1^size, i.e. 150 to 1500 Hz for the (2,0) mode. The bank culls every mode with f >= 0.49*sr after stretch and scatter. I recomputed the bank's arithmetic in Node from the actual table and the formulas. Default-kit Hat (size 0.15, stretch norm 1/3, scatter 0.10) at 44.1 kHz: f0 = 1061.9 Hz, 26 of 64 modes survive (highest 21463 Hz), median spacing 818 Hz. Default-kit Cymbal (size 0.3, stretch norm 0.6, scatter 0.35) at 44.1 kHz: f0 = 751.8 Hz, 26 of 64 survive, median spacing 687 Hz. At 96 kHz the counts are 42 and 39. Audit probe srate:crash49 (f:/tmp/membrum-audit/probe-results.txt:414-419) measured the default crash across rates. RMS(1 s) = -29.69 / -29.68 / -32.41 / -34.23 dB and 40 ms centroid = 8280 / 8664 / 13256 / 20225 Hz at 44.1 / 48 / 96 / 192 kHz.

**Why wrong.** A real cymbal is a dense cloud that starts in the tens of Hz. Table 20.1 gives c1 = 7.7 to 20.6 Hz with p of about 1.5 to 1.86, which places the (2,0) mode at about 25 to 60 Hz. F&R Fig. 20.2 shows the first 15 resonances of a 38-cm cymbal in the low hundreds of Hz (164 Hz and 244 Hz among them). About 300 modes were measured in a 16-inch cymbal (Wilbur & Rossing). The modes "mix" above the first six, and coupling is strong, so "a large number of partials quickly appear in the spectrum" (F&R 20.3). NoiseBody instead puts (2,0) at 750 to 1060 Hz for its cymbal and hat and spends most of its 64-entry table above Nyquist. The realised cloud is 26 modes with about 690 to 820 Hz median spacing at 44.1 kHz, which is the "about 600 Hz, resolvable, pitched chime" density the code's own comment calls defect D6. Because the culled count depends on the sample rate, the crash timbre and level also depend on the sample rate.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments*, 2nd ed., 1998, Sec. 20.2-20.3, Table 20.1, Fig. 20.2 [textbook] https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf: 38-cm cymbal resonances include 164 and 244 Hz; above the first six, modes mix; n=0 fit constants c1 = 7.7-20.6 Hz; "The coupling between vibrational modes in a cymbal is strong, so that a large number of partials quickly appear in the spectrum, however it is excited."
- Wilbur, C. & Rossing, T.D., "Vibrational modes of cymbals and Chladni's law", ASA 1996 abstract 5pMU8 [paper] https://www.auditory.org/asamtgs/asa96haw/5pMU/5pMU8.html: some 300 modes observed in a 16-in.-diameter cymbal.
- Werner, K.J., Abel, J.S., Smith, J.O., "The TR-808 Cymbal: a Physically-Informed, Circuit-Bendable, Digital Model", Proc. ICMC|SMC 2014, pp. 1453-1460 [paper] https://speech.di.uoa.gr/ICMC-SMC-2014/images/VOL_2/1453.pdf: six rectangular oscillators whose odd harmonics form "tightly-packed, inharmonically-related partials by design"; density, not a sparse ladder, is the load-bearing feature.

**Consequence.** The default-kit hat and crash (and the clap, also on NoiseBody) get a sparse 26-partial ladder at 44.1 kHz rather than the intended fused wash. The pitch salience the 64-mode change was meant to remove remains, and default_kit.h:301-306 and 343-349 have to fight it with heavy Scatter and Stretch. The crash also renders 4.5 dB quieter in RMS(1 s), with its 40 ms centroid moving from 8.3 to 20.2 kHz, between 44.1 and 192 kHz. A project rendered at 96 kHz sounds different from the same project at 44.1 kHz. All NoiseBody instruments share the same sparse skeleton, which contributes to hats and cymbals sounding alike across kits.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: none (no 2026-06 literature entry on NoiseBody density; the 64-mode count came later, in CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN Phase 5. Its intent is defeated by the stretch default below, together with the B_max widening the 2026-06 audit introduced.)

**Suggested fix.** Band-limit the cloud before choosing it, instead of culling after. Either (a) lower the NoiseBody f0 law toward real cymbal (2,0) values and run more of the table, or (b) select the 64 consecutive kPlateRatios entries whose stretched and scattered frequencies fall in [f_lo, 0.45*sr], generating the table further than 96 entries if needed, so every rate keeps 64 modes in the audible band. Also apply the Stretch-default fix (next claim), which alone keeps about 40 modes. Tests: (1) NoiseBody at 44.1 and 96 kHz with the default-kit Hat and Cymbal configs installs >= 56 active modes (getNumActiveModes) and the median gap in 2 to 10 kHz is < 300 Hz; (2) the srate:crash49 probe stays within 1 dB RMS(1 s) and 10 % centroid(40 ms) across 44.1 to 192 kHz.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed: noise_body_mapper.h:73 (64 modes), :58-63 (D6 comment), :95 (f0 law), :97-106 (table fill; cap lowered only for the Feedback exciter, drum_voice.h:197-199), :118-120 (stretchNorm; the default modeStretch 0.333 denormalises to 1.0x via pad_config_apply.h:125-126 and pad_config.h:212, giving 1/3), :110-111 (0.03 floor); bank B = stretch^2*0.01 (:783), scatter (:784, :810, kScatterD :655-656), cull at kNyquistGuard 0.49 (:645, :813) after stretch and scatter.
- Node recomputation with the real kPlateRatios (plate_modes.h:88-101) and default-kit configs (Hat default_kit.h:186-207, Cymbal :210-271, Clap :296-348) matches: Hat 26 modes / 817 Hz, Cymbal 26 / 687 Hz, Clap 23 / 771 Hz at 44.1 kHz; 42 / 39 at 96 kHz; 62 / 57 at 192 kHz, with the audible part staying 24 modes. Zero stretch keeps 33 modes at 618 Hz (Hat) and 46 at 350 Hz (Cymbal).
- The srate:crash49 probe is at probe-results.txt lines 436-441, not 414-419; values as quoted (max RMS deviation 4.55 dB, centroid deviation 133 %). Plausible mechanism: strike-peak normalisation to kBodyHeadroom (drum_voice.h:1366-1386) counts the extra ultrasonic modes and pushes the audible ones down.
- Literature opened and quoted accurately (F&R PDF Sec. 20.2-20.3 verbatim; Wilbur & Rossing abstract).
- Partial refutation (one verifier): CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN.md:60-62 chooses a "perceptual-model style", the f0 law is FR-032 (noise_body_mapper.h:12), and the wash comes by design from the noise layers (default_kit.h:257-262), so the 750-1060 Hz (2,0) is a documented simplification; what survives is the internal defect that the stretch defeats Phase 5's density goal (CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN.md:288-321, D6 at :51) and the sample-rate dependence.

#### MB-222 — Physics (contradicted): A 20 ms one-pole follower on modal energy reproduces the "upward jump at the strike that relaxes back" (Avanzini et al.)

**Severity:** medium (filed high, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:tension-modulation · **Also flagged by:** research:extra:tension-mod-2-semitones · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:130-133, 422, 703-717, 902-920, 1069-1083](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L130-L133)

**Problem.** energyAlpha_ = exp(-1/(0.02*sr)), so tau = 20 ms (130-133). energyEnv_ is set to 0 at noteOn (422). At the END of each chunk: energyEnv_ = a*energyEnv_ + (1-a)*getModalEnergy(), with a = energyAlpha_^chunk (912-914, slow path 1075-1077). The value is used at the START of the next chunk. The comment at 709-717 says this "reproduces exactly that up-then-relax curve". Measured with a standalone probe (scratchpad tension_probe.cpp and tension_kit_probe.cpp, linked against build/windows-x64-release KrateDSP, 44.1 kHz, 64-sample blocks). Every default-kit Membrane pad with tension starts at nominal pitch (+0.00..+0.08 st at 1.5 ms), RISES, and peaks 30-49 ms after the strike. Pad 0 kick at vel 1: +0.08 st at 1.5 ms, +1.26 at 10 ms, +2.24 at 30 ms, peak +2.31 at 42 ms, +1.58 at 100 ms. Pad 5 floor tom: peak +0.80 st at 41 ms. Generic tom (material .4, size .5, Mallet, knob 1): +0.49 st at 5 ms, peak +1.68 at 46-49 ms. The unit test's own comment says "pitchMod tends to peak between t=20 ms and t=80 ms" (test_per_mode_damping.cpp:485-488).

**Why wrong.** The energy of a struck membrane is already a smooth, slowly decaying signal. It peaks at the end of stick contact (about 1 ms) and the kinetic and potential terms oscillate in antiphase (MAB DAFx-10 Sec. 4.1, Fig. 2a). The paper uses it directly as Tqs with no low-pass. It calls the "slow initial rise" of a low-pass-estimated Tqs "the time-domain side effect of lowpass filtering", so a reference artefact. Measured toms start at the tension-modulated (highest) frequency and glide DOWN: "the initial samples correspond to a peak ... at the tension modulated frequency ... activity gradually shifts to lower frequencies" (Kirby & Sandler DAFx-20 Sec. 3.3). Correct form: pitchMod(t) = f(E(t)) with E taken from the bank without a 20 ms lag. A follower, if any, should be at most about the contact time (<= 1-2 ms), or the energy should be decimated and linearly interpolated (MAB use a factor of 32, i.e. 0.73 ms).

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Marogna, Avanzini, Bank, "Energy based synthesis of tension modulation in membranes", DAFx-10 [paper] https://people.ece.cornell.edu/land/courses/ece5760/LABS/s2016/MarognaAvanziniBank_tension_modulation.pdf: "The slow initial rise of the quasistatic tension Tqs is the time-domain side effect of lowpass filtering." Sec. 4.1: the total energy is "a slowly decaying signal"; the energy-based Tqs "shows the correct behavior". Sec. 4.2: Tqs every 32 samples (0.73 ms) with linear interpolation.
- Kirby & Sandler, "Advanced Fourier decomposition for realistic drum synthesis", Proc. DAFx-20, pp. 155-162 [paper] https://dafx2020.mdw.ac.at/proceedings/papers/DAFx2020_paper_66.pdf: 416 tom samples; initial samples sit at the tension-modulated frequency and activity shifts down to the unmodulated frequency.
- Kirby & Sandler, "The evolution of drum modes with strike intensity: Analysis and synthesis using the discrete cosine transform", JASA 150(1):202-214, 2021 [paper] https://doi.org/10.1121/10.0005509: a tom struck at 67 intensities shows a velocity-dependent evolution of the pitch glide.

**Consequence.** This is audible and wrong in shape. Every tension-enabled Membrane pad gets an upward swoop over the first 30-50 ms, which is where most of the energy and the perceived pitch are. The descending tension glide of a real tom appears only in the tail. The project's own preset generator shows this: "tom tensionMod 0 (fights the descending boom-glide)" (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1129-1130 and 1298). The default kit works around it with a fixed pitch envelope (default_kit.h:451ff), which does not respond to velocity. So kits lose the velocity-dependent glide that separates a hard tom hit from a soft one, and toms sound alike.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research[6] noted that "the 20 ms follower lags the transient" and that the value is used one block late. It treated this only as lowering the peak, not as a wrong shape. The follower was reworked to modal energy (N-1) but the 20 ms tau and the zero start are unchanged, so the lag remains.

**Suggested fix.** Drive tensionPitchMod from the bank's current getModalEnergy() without the 20 ms lag. Read it per sub-chunk of <= 32 samples and interpolate, or keep a follower with tau <= 1 ms. Remove the energyEnv_ = 0 onset gap by seeding the value right after the first excitation samples. Fix the comment at 709-717. Test: render a Membrane tom (knob 1, v 1) and record mode-0 frequency every 32 samples. Require the maximum within the first 5 ms, then monotonic non-increase after 5 ms (tolerance 0.02 st). Require f(2 ms) > f(30 ms) > f(100 ms) > f(300 ms).

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed in both renderers: drum_voice.h:130-133 (tau 20 ms), :422 (zero at noteOn), :725-728 / :945-951 (read at chunk start, capped at 1.19), :910-914 / :1075-1077 (update at chunk end); getModalEnergy (modal_resonator_bank.h:493-499) is already smooth per its own comment (483-486).
- A zero-start 20 ms one-pole fed by a decaying energy peaks at t = tau*Te/(Te - tau)*ln(Te/tau), ~30-50 ms for tom energy decay constants, matching the probe and test_per_mode_damping.cpp:485-488; that test checks only the peak f0 (503-507), never the shape.
- The comment at :709-717 is stale (it describes a follower "fed by |out|^2", while since N-1 it is fed by modal energy, :902-914) and wrong: a 20 ms low-pass from zero cannot jump at the strike.
- MAB DAFx-10 (downloaded and read): pitch "decreases as the sound decays", Tqs "decays slowly", and the low-pass initial rise is named an artefact; same system as Membrum's.
- The project works around it: default_kit.h:178-183 lowers the tom's tensionModAmt to 0.25 because the follower "drifts the pitch UP"; generator.cpp:1129-1130 and 1298 set tom tensionMod 0. The default kick (tensionModAmt 0.8, default_kit.h:84) gets a 0 to ~+2.3 st upward swoop over ~40 ms.
- Not covered by AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:319 or correctness-audit.md. Downgraded from high because tension is an optional character knob and the factory kits largely avoid it; the impact is mainly on user-dialled Tension and the kick.

#### MB-225 — Physics (contradicted): Impact (Impulse / Mallet) pulse: velocity shortens contact time by (1-v)^0.2 and sets force amplitude as v^0.6 ("Hertzian scaling")

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:exciter-physics · **Source:** research

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/impact_exciter.h:129-139](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/impact_exciter.h#L129-L139) (amplitude, T), [77-80](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/impact_exciter.h#L77-L80) + [296-301](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/impact_exciter.h#L296-L301) (energy cap); consumers [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/impulse_exciter.h:37-39](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/impulse_exciter.h#L37-L39), [mallet_exciter.h:81-90](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/mallet_exciter.h#L81-L90); voice [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:163, 302-304, 436, 1336-1338](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L163)

**Problem.** amplitude_ = pow(v, 0.6) (line 129). T = 0.5 ms + 14.5 ms * mass^0.4 (lines 132-134), then T *= pow(max(1-v, 0.01), 0.2) (lines 138-139), ±5 % jitter. Pulse = amplitude * sin(pi*t^(1-skew))^gamma, gamma = 1+3*hEff, hEff = hardness + 0.1v. Impulse: hardness lerp(0.3,0.8,v), brightness lerp(0.15,0.4,v), mass 0.3; Mallet: hardness lerp(0.1,0.6,v), brightness lerp(-0.5,-0.2,v), mass 0.3*min(size/0.5,1)^3. The voice then multiplies by velocity AGAIN through the velocity-scaled amp envelope (drum_voice.h:163 setVelocityScaling(true), :436 setVelocity) and normalises the body's output gain to a strike probed at v = 1.0 (drum_voice.h:1336-1338). MEASURED (scratchpad probe exciter_probe.cpp, 44.1 kHz, size 1): contact T = 8.91 / 7.91 / 6.89 / 5.74 / 3.61 ms at v = 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9 / 1.0. Net impulse (sum of the exciter output = the drive of low modes) for Impulse: 48.7 / 103.4 / 116.8 / 104.0 / 92.2 / 67.9 at v = 0.1/0.5/0.75/0.9/0.95/1.0, i.e. it PEAKS at v ~ 0.75 and v = 1.0 drives a 60 Hz mode 4.2 dB less than v = 0.75 (resonator peak 12238 -> 7560); identical shape at 96 kHz and for Mallet. VOICE LEVEL (voice_vel_probe.cpp, real DrumVoice + DefaultKit pads): default Kick (pad 0, Impulse) 300 ms RMS 0.0810 at v = 0.9 vs 0.0728 at v = 1.0 (-0.9 dB), 55 Hz band -1.8 dB; Low Floor Tom (pad 5, Mallet) RMS 0.1135 at v = 0.9 vs 0.0950 at v = 1.0 (-1.5 dB), peak 0.4995 at v = 0.95 > 0.4775 at v = 1.0. The FR-034 energy cap never engages: max energy / threshold = 0.177 over every velocity, both sample rates (threshold is 4x the default-parameter strike energy and the 5 ms leaky integrator cannot reach it).

**Why wrong.** For a power-law (Hertz / Hunt-Crossley) contact f = k x^alpha between a mallet of mass m and a struck object, contact time t0 is proportional to (m/k)^(1/(alpha+1)) and DECREASES weakly with impact speed: t0 proportional to v^-((alpha-1)/(alpha+1)) = v^-0.2 for Hertz alpha = 1.5 (v^-0.43 for felt alpha ~ 2.5). The impulse delivered (integral of F dt = m v (1+e)) is linear in v, so the low-mode drive must rise monotonically with velocity, and peak force rises as v^(2 alpha/(alpha+1)) = v^1.2 (Hertz). The coded law has the 1/5 exponent of Hertz but applies it to (1-v): contact time is almost flat over the lower 70 % of velocity (factor 0.98 -> 0.79) and collapses near v = 1 (0.40), the opposite curvature to v^-0.2 (whose steepest change is at LOW velocity), and because amplitude only rises as v^0.6 the pulse area falls at the top of the range. Avanzini & Rocchesso also show that the brighter attack of a hard hit comes from the SHORTER contact, consistent in sign with the code but not at the expense of delivered momentum.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- F. Avanzini, D. Rocchesso, "Physical modeling of impacts: theory and experiments on contact time and spectral centroid", SMC 2004 [paper] https://avanzini.di.unimi.it/downloads/publications/avanzini_smc04_finalsub.pdf: f = k x^alpha (alpha 1.5 for spheres, 1.5-3.5 for piano felt); t0 proportional to (m/k)^(1/(alpha+1)) and dependent on impact velocity; short t0 gives a bright attack.
- S. Bilbao, A. Torin, V. Chatziioannou, "Numerical modeling of collisions in musical instruments", Acta Acustica united with Acustica 101(1), 2015 (arXiv:1405.2589) [paper] https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1405.2589: mallet-membrane example K = 1.6e8, alpha = 2.54, M = 0.028 kg; "a general decrease in contact time with increasing strike velocity".
- "Hertz beyond belief" (arXiv:1306.4952) [paper] https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.4952: collision time has a very weak dependence on impact velocity (the v^-1/5 law), even with ~40 % viscous loss.
- K. L. Johnson, *Contact Mechanics*, Cambridge University Press 1985, ch. 11 [textbook]: Hertz impact duration proportional to (m^2/(R E*^2 v))^(1/5), peak force proportional to m^(3/5) v^(6/5); impulse = m v (1+e).

**Consequence.** The hardest MIDI velocities (about 116-127) hit the body LESS hard than about 95-115: on the default kick and floor tom the body is 1-2 dB quieter and thinner at v = 127 than at v = 115 (measured), while the attack only brightens. A drummer or a programmed part at full velocity gets a weaker, clickier hit instead of the heaviest one, and rolls that crescendo into 127 dip at the top. It also compresses the top of every Impulse/Mallet pad's dynamic range (the two most used exciters: Impulse is the default kick and ~84 generator mentions, Mallet ~42), which makes hard and medium hits sound alike. Separately, the velocity is applied twice (exciter amplitude v^0.6 x amp envelope v), giving a ~v^1.6 level law (-19 dB at v = 0.25 vs a physical -12 dB) below the inversion; that may be a deliberate dynamics choice but is not documented as such.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research entry 8 ruled the impact exciter "nuanced / oversimplified: qualitative mappings physically CORRECT in sign" and named the energy cap (lines 298-303) as compressing velocity. Code unchanged since (only the 2026-11-05 tidy sweep touched impact_exciter.h; Mallet gained the D4 size hint 2026-07-18). This audit REVISES it: the sign is right for contact time but the delivered impulse is non-monotonic (measured), and the energy cap never engages (measured max 0.177 of threshold), so it cannot be what compresses velocity.

**Suggested fix.** In ImpactExciter::trigger replace the (1-v)^0.2 factor with a Hertz law on a mapped strike speed: vPhys = 0.1 + 0.9 v, T = Tmass(mass) * pow(vPhys, -0.2) normalised so T(v=1) keeps today's 3.6 ms target or the spec's value; then set amplitude_ so the pulse AREA is proportional to v (momentum conservation): amplitude_ = v * Aref / (T_samples * meanShape(gamma, skew)), with meanShape computed by a bounded sum over the pulse at trigger (<= 15 ms, RT-safe) or the closed form Gamma((gamma+1)/2)/(sqrt(pi) Gamma(gamma/2+1)) for skew 0. Peak force then rises ~v^1.2 by itself. Delete or recalibrate the FR-034 energy cap (measured inert). Decide and document whether the amp envelope should still scale by velocity. Tests: (a) ImpactExciter net impulse / v constant within +-5 % for v in {0.1..1.0}; (b) T(0.25)/T(1.0) = 4^0.2 = 1.32 +- 0.05; (c) voice level: DefaultKit pads 0 and 5 300 ms RMS and fundamental-band RMS strictly increasing over v in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95, 1.0} (today SC-005 only compares 127 vs 30, membrum_processor_tests.cpp:488, so the inversion passes). The Phase-1 regression golden (approval/test_phase1_regression.cpp) changes and must be regenerated deliberately.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed: impact_exciter.h:129 (v^0.6), :132-134 (T), :138-139 ((1-v)^0.2), :120-123 (hEff, gamma), :143 (jitter), :241 (pulse), :194-217 (10-20 % bounce at half duration), :182-190 (comb off at strike position 0), :285 (lowpass SVF, unity DC); consumers impulse_exciter.h:37-39 and mallet_exciter.h:81-90 as stated; velocity applied twice (drum_voice.h:163, :436); gain probe at fixed v = 1.0 (drum_voice.h:1336-1338).
- Pulse area recomputed with the closed-form mean of sin^gamma: Impulse v = 0.75 / 0.9 / 1.0 gives 2.47 / 2.22 / 1.46 (≈ -4.6 dB at v = 1 vs 0.75), and with bounce v = 1.0 is 0.58 of v = 0.75 (-4.7 dB), matching the probe's 67.9 / 116.8; the amp-envelope velocity scaling only partly offsets it (0.9 * 2.22 = 2.0 vs 1.46), and the output-gain normalisation (drum_voice.h:283, 1366-1386) is velocity-independent.
- Energy cap inert by arithmetic: threshold ≈ 363 vs strike energy ≈ 50 (≈ 0.14), consistent with the measured 0.177.
- Literature checked: Bilbao/Torin/Chatziioannou (arXiv 1405.2589, Sec. 7.2, Fig. 12) and arXiv 1306.4952 confirm the weak v^-1/5 contact-time law; momentum change m*v*(1+e) rises monotonically with v.
- Contradicts its own design intent: specs/Innexus-physical-modelling-roadmap.md:644-646 writes `effectiveT *= pow(1.0 - velocity, 0.2)` with the comment "physically: T ~ v^(-1/5)". Neither AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md §3 (lines 308-333) nor correctness-audit.md rules it acceptable.
- No membrum test checks that level rises monotonically with velocity. Medium fits an audible velocity inversion at the top of the range on the two most-used exciters.

#### MB-229 — Physics (oversimplified): The parallel noise layer follows SMS deterministic+stochastic / PhISEM stochastic modelling of percussion

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:click-noise-layers (source: research, verify round: research)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h:3-13](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h#L3-L13), also 77-95, 153-170, 178-191; [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:137-147](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L137-L147), also 159-163, 436, 547-550, 855-864, 1499-1515

**Problem.** NoiseLayer = NoiseOscillator (colour Brown/Pink/White/Violet) -> SVF (forced to Lowpass in DrumVoice, drum_voice.h:147) -> ADSR (attack 0.5 ms, exponential decay 20-2000 ms, sustain 0) -> mix, times standaloneGain * noiseLayerGain * wireGainMod. `trigger(float /*velocity*/)` IGNORES velocity (noise_layer.h:158). The filter cutoff and colour are fixed per pad. The layer's only velocity dependence is the voice amp envelope (setVelocityScaling(true), peak = velocity; drum_voice.h:163, 436; adsr_envelope.h:512), so noise ~ v. The body goes through an exciter whose amplitude is v^0.6 plus velocity-dependent hardness and brightness (impact_exciter.h:129; impulse_exciter.h:37-39), with a body gain fixed by a v=1 probe, and is also scaled by the amp env. Wire coupling (snare wireCoupling 0.45) tracks the head envelope, but computeWireGainMod is deliberately "self-normalising ... velocity- and gain-staging-independent" (drum_voice.h:1499-1515), and it is block-path only. MEASURED (voice_probe, default kit, DrumVoice::process, 48 kHz): the snare noise-layer RMS(0-50 ms) relative to the body is -5.8 dB at v=1.0, +1.3 dB at v=0.5 and +6.1 dB at v=0.3. Peaks at v=0.3: noise -20.7 dBFS vs body -29.5 dBFS. From v=1 to v=0.3 the body peak falls 21.5 dB, the noise 10.4 dB. Kick: -14.6 -> -12.1 dB; floor tom: -16.4 -> -13.4 dB; closed hat: -24.9 -> -19.2 dB.

**Why wrong.** In SMS the stochastic part is the analysed residual, rendered as noise through a time-varying filter. PhISEM (Cook), as implemented in STK Shakers, drives the noise from the system energy: `sndLevel_ += shakeEnergy_` on each collision event, the energy decays exponentially, and the ratchet branch uses `input = sndLevel_ * noise() * shakeEnergy_`. So noise amplitude follows the excitation energy. For the snare (the main consumer, noiseLayerGain 6.2), the buzz is produced by the snare head vibrating against the wires: "When the upper, or batter, head is struck, the snare head vibrates against the snares" (Rossing 1992). It is a nonlinear membrane-wire collision process (Torin & Newton), so it should scale at least in proportion to the head amplitude and should not grow relative to the head on soft strokes. A noise source with its own fixed envelope and a velocity law that differs from the body's is a defensible "noise partner" in the SNT sense. But it is not PhISEM, and its level does not follow the body's energy.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- J.O. Smith III, "Spectral Modeling Synthesis", *Spectral Audio Signal Processing* (CCRMA online book) [textbook], https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/sasp/Spectral_Modeling_Synthesis.html: Sines+Noise uses "filtered noise as a replacement for many sinusoids when modeling noise" (pseudo-random numbers passed through a filter); S+N+T handles transients separately.
- P.R. Cook / G. Scavone, STK Shakers class (PhISEM implementation) [docs], https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thestk/stk/master/include/Shakers.h: PhISEM = "algorithmic approach for simulating collisions of multiple independent sound producing objects". Collision test `randomFloat(1024) < nObjects_`; `sndLevel_ += shakeEnergy_`; `input = sndLevel_ * noise() * shakeEnergy_`; `shakeEnergy_ *= systemDecay_`, `sndLevel_ *= soundDecay_`. The noise level is driven by the excitation energy.
- T.D. Rossing, "Acoustics of drums", *Physics Today* 45(3):40, 1992 [paper], https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf: "When the upper, or batter, head is struck, the snare head vibrates against the snares. Alternatively, the snares can be moved away from the head to give a totally different sound."
- A. Torin & M. Newton, "Collisions in drum membranes: a preliminary study on a simplified system" (NESS project, Univ. of Edinburgh, 2014) [paper], https://www.ness.music.ed.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2014/05/Snare_final.pdf: snare buzz comes from "secondary collisions between the lower membrane and a number of metal wires", modelled with a power-law contact force; experiment and model both show "the nonlinear nature of the snare-membrane interaction".

**Consequence.** The noise-to-body balance changes with velocity, most of all on the snare. A ghost note (v=0.3) is 6 dB more wire than head and its noise peak sits 8.8 dB above the body peak. At full velocity the head dominates by 5.8 dB. Soft playing therefore sounds like a different, brush-like instrument rather than a quieter snare, and the dynamic range of the snare's tonal component is compressed into noise. The layer also has no velocity-to-brightness mapping, so dynamics produce no timbre change in the noise. The lowpass rationale "no spectral peak ... what real percussion noise sounds like" (drum_voice.h:137-147) is false above Q~0.707, and resonance maps to Q 0.3-5.0 (noise_layer.h:288-291). This repeats open item L-6.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: no 2026-06 literature verdict on the noise layer. Code findings H-2 (layers burying the body; fixed b4c63577, x3 -> 0.243) and M-7 (bandpass vs lowpass calibration; fixed) addressed level only. L-6 (Q up to 5 on the "no peak" Lowpass) is still open and unchanged (noise_layer.h:288-291). Added since: noiseLayerGain, wire coupling (self-normalised, block path only) and the cutoff-compensated standaloneGain. None of them makes the noise follow velocity or body energy.

**Suggested fix.** Give `NoiseLayer::trigger` a real velocity law that matches the body's: scale the layer by velocity^0.6 (ImpactExciter's amplitude law) before the amp envelope, or by the body's measured strike peak ratio. Alternatively, make wire coupling scale with ABSOLUTE modal energy, not the running-peak-normalised ratio, so the buzz follows the head as in PhISEM / snare collisions. Optionally add velocity -> cutoff (e.g. cutoff * 2^(0.5*(v-1))). Test: render the default-kit snare at v=1, 0.5, 0.3 and assert that the noise-layer-to-body RMS ratio (0-50 ms) stays within ±2 dB across velocities (today: -5.8, +1.3, +6.1 dB).

**Verifier notes.**
- Code confirmed: noise_layer.h:158 drops velocity; configure() (noise_layer.h:77-95, denormDecayMs 293-301) is fixed per pad; Lowpass forced at drum_voice.h:147; output = processSample() * standaloneGain() * noiseLayerGain_ * wireGainMod_ (drum_voice.h:548-549, 855-861, 1050-1051); amp env setVelocityScaling(true)/setVelocity (drum_voice.h:163, 436; adsr_envelope.h:512), so noise ~ v while the body ~ v^1.6 (impact_exciter.h:120, 129, 171; StrikeNormKey holds no velocity, drum_voice.h:1394-1411); bloom gating (drum_voice.h:357-371) never applies to the Membrane snare; default snare noiseLayerGain 6.2 / wireCoupling 0.45 (default_kit.h:120, 124); membrum_processor_tests.cpp:649-660 zeroes noise/click for SC-005 so no test pins the balance.
