Caveats: the header (noise_layer.h:6-8) cites SMS / SNT / Chromaphone, not PhISEM, so the title overstates; the Q point repeats open L-6.
- Code facts hold (noise_layer.h:158, 178-191, 196-215; drum_voice.h:372 trigger is a level no-op; 547-549, 855-864, 884-885; computeWireGainMod 1506-1515 updated only on the block path 910-919); the quoted 10.4 dB noise drop matches 20·log10(0.3) = -10.46 dB. Literature not refuted: fetched STK Shakers.h confirms the energy-driven PhISEM update lines; Rossing confirms head-driven buzz. L-6 still open (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:298).
- Not refuted: mechanism confirmed (noise_layer.h:158-170, 178-191, 208-214; drum_voice.h:163, 436; impact_exciter.h:120, 129, 171); the sibling ClickLayer keeps velocity_ (click_layer.h:87-95, 133), so dropping it in NoiseLayer reads as an oversight; no spec or ruling accepts a velocity-independent noise layer, and it is not Unnatural Zone; an ~11-12 dB balance swing on the snare is clearly audible, medium fits.

#### MB-233 — Physics (contradicted): CouplingMatrix category routing (Snare Buzz: Kick->Snare, Tom Resonance: Tom->Tom) decides which pads excite which

**Severity:** medium (finder: high) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:coupling-models (source: research, verify round: research)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/coupling_matrix.h:4-11](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/coupling_matrix.h#L4-L11), also 42-77; [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:131-143](/plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L131-L143), also 411-424

**Problem.** `recomputeFromTier1` fills `effectiveGain_[src][dst] = snareBuzz * 0.05` for Kick->Snare pairs and `tomResonance * 0.05` for Tom->Tom pairs, scaled by `couplingAmount[src] * couplingAmount[dst]`. The header calls these "per-pair sympathetic-resonance coefficients". The processor recomputes the matrix on every Snare Buzz or Tom Resonance change, per-pad coupling edit and kit load. No code outside tests reads `effectiveGain_`: a grep of plugins/membrum/src finds `getEffectiveGain` / `effectiveGainArray` only in coupling_matrix.h and `couplingMatrixForTest` (processor.h:81). Git history shows the only consumer that ever existed was the UI matrix-activity publisher, removed in 40d9aac6 ("membrum 0.9.0: master gain + Matrix removal"). That commit message says "the category-driven coupling math was always doing the useful work", but the matrix never reached the audio path, and SympatheticResonance has no per-pair gain input.

**Why wrong.** A per-pair coefficient matrix is the right structure for frequency- and category-selective sympathetic coupling: the receiver must be driven in proportion to gain[src][dst] (forced-response physics, Fletcher & Rossing). As coded, Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance change no sample of audio. The physical model claimed in the header is not implemented.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments*, 2nd ed., §18.13, 1998 [textbook], https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf: the snare response requires the snare head to be driven above a critical amplitude. Snare buzz is a property of the receiving drum, so any "Snare Buzz" control has to drive the receiver.

**Consequence.** Two user-facing knobs (Snare Buzz 271, Tom Resonance 272) are dead parameters. Factory kits set them (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:1674-1676: snareBuzz 0.18, tomResonance 0.22) and they change nothing. The tests do not catch this: SC-002 "kick triggers audible snare buzz" (test_coupling_integration.cpp:240-285) holds Snare Buzz at 0.5 in both runs and varies only Global Coupling, and the Tom Resonance tests check only matrix values (347-405).

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: not ruled in 2026-06; coupling_matrix.h kMaxCoefficient 0.05 was only mentioned in research[5].

**Suggested fix.** Either wire `effectiveGainArray()` into the receiver drive as described in the sympathetic-resonance claim, or remove both parameters (keeping the state-format slot). Pinning test: render a kick-only hit with Global Coupling 1 and Snare Buzz 0 versus 1. The outputs must differ by at least 20 dB of snare-band energy. Today they are bit-identical, so the test fails first.

**Verifier notes.**
- Confirmed: coupling_matrix.h:42-77 writes the matrix; only readers are getEffectiveGain (:79) / effectiveGainArray (:85); couplingMatrix_ appears only at processor.h:81, processor.h:145 and processor.cpp:138; the audio path (processor.cpp:693-708) is mono sum -> couplingDelay_ -> couplingEngine_.process -> applyEnergyLimiter with no per-pair input; couplingEngine_.setAmount is driven only by kGlobalCouplingId (processor.cpp:408, 978); snareBuzz_/tomResonance_ only stored (414, 421, 975-976), fed to the recompute (139-140) and saved (886-889). Commit 40d9aac6 exists. Recommends downgrade: two dead knobs and a misleading header, nothing unstable, so medium rather than high.
- Not refuted: same source trace (coupling_matrix.h:42-77, 79-88; processor.cpp:138-142, 411-421, 693-707, 886-889, 975-976); voice_pool.cpp:243-248 gates partial registration only on `couplingAmount > 0`, no per-pair gain or category routing. The knobs are on ArcKnobs (editor.uidesc:23-24, 402-407) and MANUAL.md:124, 431-432 describes routing that does not exist. The defect stands without the literature; "physics-contradicted" is a misnomer (an unused coefficient table, not a contradicted model).
- Confirmed from source; SympatheticResonance's public API (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h:113-370) has no per-pair or per-receiver gain. Not a documented simplification: MANUAL.md:431-432, docs/index.html:89, membrum_signal_flow.dot:288 and CHANGELOG.md:465-467 all claim category routing; no prior-audit ruling covers it. Recommends lowering from high (inert knobs, no wrong or unstable output); notes kMaxCoefficient 0.05 (~-26 dB per pair) and the -20 dBFS limiter make the suggested 20 dB pinning test probably unrealistic.

#### MB-234 — Physics (contradicted): NonlinearCoupling imitates the von Karman energy cascade: amplitude-dependent brightening and delayed HF bloom

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:nonlinear-coupling; also flagged by research:nonlinear-coupling (source: research, verify round: research)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/nonlinear_coupling.h:6-15](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/nonlinear_coupling.h#L6-L15), also 78-92, 99-127 (applied to body + noise + click + modeInject at [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:550-558](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L550-L558), 893-895, 1056-1058)

**Problem.** The stage is a memoryless, odd-symmetric soft clipper y = x + a*(recipSqrt(x*d) - x) with d = 1 + 6*vel*a*env. env is an RMS follower whose attack runs 120 - 90*vel ms and whose release is 200 ms, with coefficients exp(-2*pi/(t*fs)) (envelope_follower.h:318-371). Measured by re-implementing it (scratchpad nlc_probe.js) on a 48-mode default-stretched Plate tone, 253 Hz, -6 dBFS strike peak: 93-96 % of the added signal is an in-phase LINEAR gain, i.e. an expander, not new spectrum. At amount 0.35 / vel 1 (the default-kit crash value, default_kit.h:234) the level rises +0.8 dB in 0-50 ms, the spectral centroid moves 2294 -> 2302 Hz (+0.35 %) and the distortion products sit 32 dB below the body. At amount 1 / vel 1 the level rises +5.2 dB in 0-50 ms and +4.3 dB in 50-300 ms, the centroid moves +1.7 % and distortion sits at -14 dB. On a low 5-mode membrane tone at amount 1 the level rises +6.0 dB with no centroid change. The env peaks 15-37 ms after the strike. Nothing in the stage limits energy.

**Why wrong.** Geometric (von Karman) nonlinearity in plates and shells EXCHANGES energy between the structure's own modes. The transfer follows internal-resonance frequency rules (omega = a_i omega_i + a_j omega_j; quadratic coupling from curvature in shells and cymbals, cubic in flat plates). It produces the delayed, sustained appearance of HF modal components, which then decay with their own modal damping, and it creates no energy. The cheap controllable synthesis form in the literature is an energy-conserving coupled resonant filter bank: power above a threshold moves from mode j to neighbouring modes through a matrix M whose column sums are <= 0, so no energy is created (Poirot, Bilbao & Kronland-Martinet, DAFx 2023 / EURASIP 2024). A static waveshaper instead adds energy (here, mostly a gain boost), places its products at odd intermodulation and harmonic frequencies of the input rather than at the plate's modes, and those products fall as the cube of the amplitude instead of ringing on.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Chaigne, Touzé & Thomas, "Nonlinear vibrations and chaos in gongs and cymbals", *Acoust. Sci. & Tech.* 26(5) 2005 [paper], https://perso.ensta.fr/~touze/PDF/ChaosGong.pdf: typical features "amplitude-dependent level of harmonics..., pitch glide, bifurcations, energy exchange between modes through nonlinear coupling and chaos"; "The energy transfer between modes is a consequence of quadratic nonlinearity due to curvature of the shell and is fully governed by frequency rules" (combination resonances p*Omega = a_i omega_i + a_j omega_j).
- Poirot, Bilbao & Kronland-Martinet, "A coupled resonant filter bank for the sound synthesis of nonlinear sources", DAFx 2023 [paper], https://www.dafx.de/paper-archive/2023/DAFx23_paper_42.pdf: nonlinear plates need "energy transfer between different modes", which "may cause the delayed and sustained appearance of tonal components that cannot be generated by linear filtering". Eq. (15)/(19): sum_i T_i <= 0, which "impedes the creation of energy during transfer". Sec. 5.1: transfers to near-frequency filters give "a gradual cascade of energy towards the high-frequency range", followed by "a usual exponential decay after the delayed appearance of the high frequency component".
- Ducceschi & Touzé, "Modal approach for nonlinear vibrations of damped impacted plates: Application to sound synthesis of gongs and cymbals", *J. Sound Vib.* 344 (2015) [paper], https://perso.ensta-paris.fr/~touze/modalsynthesis.html: energy-conserving modal scheme of nonlinearly (cubically) coupled modal ODEs for von Karman plates, with per-mode damping (abstract, via search).

**Consequence.** The control mainly makes louder hits louder. At amount 1, a hard hit gains about 5-6 dB over the first 300 ms, with almost no change in brightness, a level expansion the user does not expect from a "character" knob. The expansion pushes those voices into the -1 dBTP limiter and widens the velocity spread in a way that differs between pads that do and do not use the knob. At the default-kit crash value of 0.35 the advertised "bloom" brightening is about +0.35 % centroid, which is inaudible, so the cymbal's bloom comes almost entirely from the separate noise-filter sweep (drum_voice.h:347-371). The products are distortion of body + noise + click, not new plate modes, so they do not ring on as shimmer. MANUAL.md:349 calls it "energy-limited cross-mode coupling" producing "FM-like sidebands"; no limiter exists, and the effect is not frequency modulation.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: no 2026-06 research verdict covered this. Code findings M-3 and M-4 (whole-signal recipSqrt compressor; transient-only dEnv AM) were fixed by the env-LEVEL redesign, and the REMEDIATION tracker (AUDIT md :92) calls the new mechanism "grounded in literature". This audit finds that claim not delivered by today's code: the redesign trades the old -18 % compressor for an expander of up to +6 dB.

**Suggested fix.** Remove the linear part so the stage changes timbre, not level. Use excess = recipSqrt(x*d)/d - x, which has unity small-signal gain, or a Chebyshev T3 term, and high-pass the excess before adding a*excess. Alternatively, implement the energy-conserving Poirot transfer in the shared bank: per block, move power above threshold theta from mode j to its spectral neighbours with a_ij = 1 - |f_j - f_i|/f+ and column sums <= 0. Fix MANUAL.md:349. Test ([UnnaturalZone][NonlinearCoupling]): render a Plate hit at vel 1 with amount 0 and amount 1. Assert total energy in 0-300 ms within ±0.5 dB (no creation) and the energy fraction above 4 kHz up by >= 3 dB in the 30-200 ms window, with the HF fraction peaking later than 10 ms. Today's code fails the first assertion (+5 dB).

**Verifier notes.**
- Code described correctly: nonlinear_coupling.h:117-126 (drive = 1 + 6*velocity_*amount_*env; y = x + amount_*(recipSqrt(x*drive) - x)), recipSqrt = x/sqrt(x^2+1) (dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/sigmoid.h:188-194), follower set at :59, :89-90, envelope_follower.h:362. Small-signal algebra gives y ≈ x*(1 + a*(d-1)), an in-phase gain (+4 to +9 dB at a = vel = 1, env ~0.3), matching +5 to +6 dB; no energy limiter. Call sites real (drum_voice.h:557-558, 893-895, 1056-1058). MANUAL.md:349 wrong. Mitigation: the header (:6-15) openly says it is not a von Karman/Poirot model, but the expander contradicts its own "louder = brighter" comments (:30-32, :113-116). Medium.
- Not refuted: Poirot/Bilbao/Kronland-Martinet DAFx 2023 (paper 42) and the 2024 EURASIP follow-up (DOI 10.1186/s13636-024-00358-2) confirmed by search, on Föppl-von Kármán plates; the code cites the same literature (nonlinear_coupling.h:9-11, 80-82). Exact PDF quotes not verified (binary only). Mitigation in :6-15 does not refute because :78-84 still claims the delayed-HF cascade, MANUAL.md:349 describes a non-existent limiter, and the expander contradicts the stated brightening goal (:7-8).
- Physics framing refuted (the simplification is deliberate and documented, nonlinear_coupling.h:6-15, AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:92), but the level-expander defect is confirmed: nonlinear_coupling.h:118-126, sigmoid.h:193; the M-2 fix (AUDIT md:91) treats an uncompensated recipSqrt slope as a bug, yet this stage never got the makeup. Own probe (scratchpad nlc_check.js): +1.3 / +3.3 / +6.6 dB at amount 0.35 / 0.6 / 1.0. test_nonlinear_coupling.cpp (151-161, 356-378) counts linear gain as "added harmonic energy" and pins no level. Medium stands; fix = small-signal makeup (divide by d) + level test + MANUAL correction, not a physics rewrite.

#### MB-236 — Physics (contradicted): Decay Skew inverts the Chaigne-Lambourg decay-vs-frequency law (fundamental dies, shimmer sustains)

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:nonlinear-coupling (source: research, verify round: research)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:140-173](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L140-L173) (same pattern [plate_mapper.h:68-91](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_mapper.h#L68-L91), [shell_mapper.h:69-89](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_mapper.h#L69-L89), [bell_mapper.h:64-86](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/bell_mapper.h#L64-L86), [noise_body_mapper.h:125-145](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h#L125-L145)); b3 clamp at [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:767](/dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L767) and dampingLawFromLegacy :133-139

**Problem.** skew in [-1, +1] does two things. (1) It scales the GLOBAL decay time by (1 - 0.3*skew), the same for every mode. (2) It scales the initial AMPLITUDE of mode k by ratio_k^(-skew), clamped to [1/8, 8]. The per-mode damping law stays sigma_k = b1 + b3*f_k^2 with b3 = max(b3, 0), so higher modes always decay at least as fast as lower ones, at every skew. The test that claims US6-2 (tests/unit/unnatural/test_decay_skew.cpp:6-13, 90-127) checks an amplitude (Goertzel energy) ratio, not T60. The sign is also inverted in the manual: positive skew attenuates the high modes and shortens decay, a darker and shorter sound, while MANUAL.md:347 says "positive = bright sustain, negative = dark sustain".

**Why wrong.** Spec 135:179 and unnatural_zone_contract.md:49/:52/:165 require that skew = -1 makes T60(fundamental) < T60(highest mode), i.e. an inverted per-mode decay. In the physical law (Chaigne & Lambourg 2001), decay factors from thermoelastic, viscoelastic and radiation losses rise with frequency, hence b3 > 0. An inversion therefore needs a PER-MODE decay change, which spec 137 research.md §9 specifies as decay_k = base_k * (f_k/f_1)^(-skew). An amplitude tilt plus a global decay change is not that.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- Chaigne & Lambourg, "Time-domain simulation of damped impacted plates. I. Theory and experiments", *JASA* 109 (2001) [paper], https://hal-ensta.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00830699: the model's thermoelastic, viscoelastic and radiation damping terms reproduce the measured frequency dependence of decay factors in plates of four materials (abstract, via search). This is the natural law Decay Skew is specified to invert.
- specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/research.md §9 and contracts/unnatural_zone_contract.md:39-52, 165 [docs]: Decay Skew = -1 means "fundamental decays fast, high modes sustain", and the acceptance test measures T60 of mode 0 vs the highest mode. The scalar-bias approach was a stopgap with a per-block per-mode fallback "if the US6-2 inversion test cannot be satisfied".

**Consequence.** Decay Skew acts as a spectral tilt plus a ±30 % length control. The "fundamental dies while shimmer sustains" effect the spec describes never happens, because the top modes still die first. The manual describes the sign backwards, and the Tightness macro's description, "faster high-mode falloff" (MANUAL.md:175), describes something the parameter does not do.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: the 2026-06 code finding M-5 ("decaySkew degrades to ±30% global decay nudge for Plate/Shell/Bell/NoiseBody") was marked DONE after adding the per-mode AMPLITUDE tilt. No research[] verdict covered it. The per-mode DECAY inversion the spec requires was never implemented, so the gap persists.

**Suggested fix.** Implement research.md §9: compute a per-mode decay multiplier m_k = (f_k/f_1)^(-skew) in the mapper and pass per-mode decay rates to the bank. This needs a per-mode-sigma setModes overload, or b1_k = b1*m_k with sigma_k >= 0.2 s^-1 for stability. Keep the amplitude tilt optional. Correct MANUAL.md:347 and :175. Restore the US6-2 test: at skew = -1, the measured T60 of mode 0 is less than that of the top mode on every modal body; at skew = +1 their ratio rises above the skew = 0 value. Update the stale "ratio[8]=12.5" plate comment in test_decay_skew_all_bodies.cpp:59.

**Verifier notes.**
- Confirmed: membrane_mapper.h:146-152 (global skewBias), :160-173 (amplitude tilt, kDecaySkewMaxModeTilt = 8 at :51), :177 -> dampingLawFromParams (:64-80) -> dampingLawFromLegacy (modal_resonator_bank.h:133-138); bank clamps b3 >= 0 (:767), decayRate_k = b1 + b3*f_w^2 (:823, :367). Source admits it (membrane_mapper.h:142-145; test_decay_skew.cpp:6-13 "weaker assertion than strict t60 inversion"); the test only checks a Goertzel ratio (:127-130). Same pattern in plate:69, shell:69, bell:64, noise_body:125; drum_voice.h only routes the value (:189, :1402, :1529). Spec requires a real T60 inversion (unnatural_zone_contract.md:49, :165; specs/135:179). MANUAL.md:347 and :175 are wrong. The b3 >= 0 natural law itself is correct; the defect is the unmet Unnatural control.
- Holds against code and source: pad_config_apply.h:128 only denormalises; spec 137 spec.md:132 (US6-2), research.md:284-289 and :298 / plan.md:447 name per-block updateModes as the fallback, but the test was weakened instead; spec.md:567 marks FR-051 MET "with per-mode damping override", which does not exist. macro_mapper.cpp:141-143 only raises decaySkew. The JASA source is peer-reviewed (HAL hal-00830699 abstract found by search).
- Mechanism confirmed; worked example with the test's patch (test_decay_skew.cpp:56-58): b3 ~2e-5 gives mode 7 (~1.29 kHz) sigma ~33 s^-1 vs b1 ~1 s^-1, so even with the 8x boost mode 7 dies first. Only partly documented (research.md:294-298 escalation path not taken; false MET row spec.md:567); prior M-5 fix only extended the amplitude tilt (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:62, 271). MANUAL.md:347 sign is backwards. Recommends downgrade to low: Unnatural Zone is non-physical by design, default 0, the knob still works as tilt + length.

#### MB-244 — Physics (oversimplified): Modes with n >= 2 and (m >= 6, 1) left unshifted because 'Rossing's published data doesn't quantify them'

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:extra:timpani-air-loading-series (source: research, verify round: research)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:88-91](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h#L88-L91), also 98-105

**Problem.** Every index except 2 / 4 / 6 / 9 has scale 1.0. At airLoading = 1 the ratios relative to (1,1) are: (1,2) 1.831, (2,2) 2.197, (0,3) 2.258, (3,2) 2.547, (6,1) 2.593. The shifted (4,1) is 2.44 and (5,1) is 2.90, so (6,1) at 2.593 now lies BELOW (5,1). The (m,1) family is no longer monotonic in m.

**Why wrong.** The stated reason does not hold: the data exists. Measured with kettle (Table 18.2): (1,2) 2.00, (2,2) 2.86, (0,3) 2.71. Calculated with kettle (Table 18.1): (1,2) 2.34, (2,2) 2.74, (3,2) 3.28, (6,1) 3.38, (1,3) 3.38, (4,2) 3.80. Relative to the code these are: (1,2) -153 cents, (2,2) -457 cents, (3,2) -438 cents, (6,1) -459 cents. Rayleigh's octave overtone (2.00) comes from (1,2) (F&R p.498). On a real drum (1,2) and (3,1) nearly coincide at 340 / 344 Hz, while the code leaves (1,2) at 1.83. Holding these modes at unity is a deliberate, documented simplification (comment at lines 88-91), but it rests on a wrong premise.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing 1998, Tables 18.1 and 18.2, and §18.1 p.498 [textbook], https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf: Table 18.1 (with kettle, calculated, f/f11): 12 2.34, 22 2.74, 32 3.28, 61 3.38, 13 3.38, 42 3.80. Table 18.2 (measured): 12 2.00, 22 2.86, 03 2.71. p.498: Rayleigh's overtones at 1.50, 1.88 and 2.00 come from (21), (31) and (12).

**Consequence.** At high airLoading, a strong (1,2) partial sits about 150 cents below the octave partial (3,1) = 2.00 and beats against it. (6,1) lands between (4,1) and (5,1), and (2,2) / (0,3) sit a third to a fourth low. This blurs the "definite pitch" that air loading is meant to produce. The setting gets less tuned and more gong-like than a timpani. The (6,1) inversion is clearest at near-rim strikes, where J6 is large.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research[10] accepted holding n>=2 at unity as "faithful to the limit of Rossing's published data". That premise is wrong: F&R Tables 18.1/18.2 give these modes. The (6,1) ordering inversion was not noticed. The code is unchanged, so the earlier ruling should be revised.

**Suggested fix.** Extend kAirLoadingTargetScale to every mode in F&R Tables 18.1/18.2. Use the measured value where Table 18.2 has one, otherwise the Table 18.1 calculated value. For modes beyond the tables, use the shift of the highest tabulated mode with the same m (or the same n), so each family stays monotonic. Tests on MembraneMapper::map: for every airLoading in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}, CHECK f(m+1,1) > f(m,1) for m = 1..13 and f(m,n+1) > f(m,n). At airLoading = 1, CHECK f(1,2)/f(1,1) == Approx(2.00).epsilon(0.03) and f(6,1)/f(1,1) == Approx(3.38).epsilon(0.03).

**Verifier notes.**
- Not refuted on the code lens: kAirLoadingTargetScale (membrane_modes.h:98-105) differs from 1.0 only at indices 2/4/6/9 (1.1192 / 1.2012 / 1.2321 / 1.2668); applied at membrane_mapper.h:100-108; recomputed ratios match ((6,1) 2.593 < (5,1) 2.900; (1,1) = 1.5933 at membrane_modes.h:31-36). The bank's stretch warp (modal_resonator_bank.h:783, 806-807) cannot undo it (f(6,1)/f(5,1) = 0.988 even at stretch 1). Only test (test_per_mode_damping.cpp:611-643) checks five (m,1) ratios, no monotonicity. Literature values not checked. Side note: the comment at membrane_modes.h:64-66 says air loading raises the (0,n) modes, yet they are at 1.0.
- Confirmed from code and from the textbook (PDF downloaded, pdftotext): Table 18.1 with kettle 12 2.34, 41 2.46, 22 2.74, 51 2.93, 32 3.28, 61 3.38, 13 3.38, 42 3.80; Table 18.2 (Christian et al. 1984) 31 340 Hz (1.97), 12 344 Hz (2.00), 22 2.86, 03 2.71, 51 2.91; §18.1 Rayleigh's octave from (12). Every quoted number and cents value matches; the comment's premise is false. Caveats: calculated vs measured (1,2) differ (both far above 1.83); tables describe one drum.
- Confirmed but recommends low: inversion persists at the default airLoading 0.6 (pad_config.h:291; 2.656 vs 2.593) and at material 1; contradicts the header intent (membrane_modes.h:64-69); prior ruling (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:312) missed it. But at default strikePos 0.3 (default_kit.h:52, 107, 149, 192, 280, 320) J6 is ~37 dB below (1,1), so the inversion only matters at rim strikes; could not retrieve Tables 18.1/18.2 by web search, and Benade/HyperPhysics measured ratios (1.00, 1.504, 1.742, 2.00, 2.245, 2.494) sit near the code's values, weakening the n>=2 mistuning claim.

#### MB-252 — Physics (oversimplified): The R = b1 + b3*f^2 per-mode damping law is used as the drum-head (Membrane) loss law

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:extra:chaigne-damping-law (source: research, verify round: research)

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:106-139](/dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L106-L139), also 362-368 (also [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:53-80](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L53-L80), 148-152, 177)

**Problem.** decayRate_k = b1 + b3*f_k^2 (s^-1), with f in Hz and R_k = exp(-decayRate_k/fs) (modal_resonator_bank.h:107, 367-368). On the Membrane legacy path b1 = 1/decayTime, where decayTime = lerp(0.15,0.8,material)*(1+0.1*size)*exp(lerp(ln0.3,ln3,decay)), clamped to [0.01,5] s, and b3 = (1-material)*4e-5. With overrides: b1 = 0.2+n*49.8, b3 = n*1e-3. Decay is therefore strictly monotonic in frequency: the (0,1) fundamental is always the longest-ringing mode. Computed for the default kit: kick (0,1) 79 Hz T60 1.48 s, then 1.40/1.27/1.13 s up the series. Tom size 0.5: 158 Hz 1.11 s, 252 Hz 0.58 s, 362 Hz 0.31 s. There is no per-mode radiation term; airLoading only moves frequencies (membrane_mapper.h:100-109).

**Why wrong.** A frequency-squared loss is a legitimate membrane loss mechanism. The Bilbao/Webb timpani model carries a viscothermal Kelvin-Voigt term c_M^2*eta*Laplacian(dw/dt), which gives sigma proportional to k^2 proportional to f^2 for a membrane. In modal synthesis the same form is Rayleigh (proportional) damping, c_i = alpha1 + alpha2*omega_i^2. On measured drums, however, radiation dominates the loss, and it depends on mode class, not monotonically on frequency. Fletcher & Rossing Table 18.4 (after Christian et al. 1984), 26-in timpani with kettle at T=3710 N/m: (01) 128 Hz 0.4 s, (11) 145 Hz 2.3 s, (21) 218 Hz 3.7 s, (31) 287 Hz 4.6 s, (02) 235 Hz 0.3 s, (03) 383 Hz 0.5 s. So the (n,1) family outlasts (0,1) by 5-10x, and the decay time RISES with frequency across it. Section 18.7 says radiation accounts for a major part of membrane damping (monopole (0,n) modes damp fastest, dipole and quadrupole slower). Table 18.8 (Bork 1983, 32-cm tom-tom): (01) T60 0.8-1.05 s against 1.1-2.7 s in the 500 Hz third-octave band. The correct form is sigma_k = b1 + b3*f_k^2 + r_k, where r_k is a radiation term set by the mode's multipole order (m = 0 large, m = 1 smaller, m >= 2 smaller still).

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- N. H. Fletcher & T. D. Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments*, 2nd ed., Springer 1998, Table 18.4, Sec. 18.7, Table 18.8 [textbook], https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf: Table 18.4 (timpani, after Christian et al. 1984): the (11), (21), (31), (41) modes decay much more slowly than (01), (02), (03), e.g. with kettle at T=3710 N/m: (01) 0.4 s, (11) 2.3 s, (21) 3.7 s, (31) 4.6 s. Sec. 18.7: radiation accounts for a major part of the damping; the monopole (01) mode radiates and damps out rapidly. Table 18.8 (Bork 1983): 32-cm tom-tom (01) T60 0.8-1.05 s, 500 Hz band T60 1.1-2.7 s.
- C. J. Webb, *Parallel computation techniques for virtual acoustics and physical modelling synthesis*, PhD thesis, Univ. of Edinburgh 2014, ch. 7 (Bilbao/Webb timpani model), Eq. 7.2 [thesis], https://www.ness.music.ed.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/CJWebb_thesis-1.pdf: the membrane PDE includes a term c_M^2*eta*Laplacian_2D(dw/dt), where eta "determines viscothermal damping effects"; for a membrane this gives a mode decay proportional to k^2, i.e. f^2.
- A. Sterling, N. Rewkowski, R. L. Klatzky, M. C. Lin, "Audio-Material Reconstruction for Virtualized Reality Using a Probabilistic Damping Model", *IEEE TVCG* 2019 [paper], https://gamma.cs.unc.edu/ProbDampModel/data/pdm.pdf: Eq. 1, Rayleigh damping c_i = alpha1 + alpha2*lambda_i (lambda = omega^2) is "the most common damping model for sound synthesis", i.e. the b1 + b3*f^2 form.
- T. D. Rossing, "Acoustics of Drums", *Physics Today* 45(3), 40-47, 1992 [paper], https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf: air loading sets the harmonic relation of kettledrum modes, and the other effects "may have considerable effect on the rate of decay of the sound".

**Consequence.** Every Membrane pad gets the same envelope: the (0,1) thump rings longest and every overtone fades monotonically faster. A timpani or tuned-tom preset cannot sustain its pitched (1,1)/(2,1)/(3,1) family over a fast-dying (0,1). airLoading moves the (n,1) modes toward 1:1.5:2 but they still decay faster than the fundamental, so the harmonic pitch the feature is meant to create fades first. This pushes all membranes toward one "boom plus fading overtones" character and contributes to kits sounding alike.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: research[3] of AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07 ruled the b1 + b3*f^2 form "confirmed" as the Chaigne & Askenfelt law, noting that the linear Chaigne-Lambourg term is missing and that the b3 ceiling is not fitted. The DampingLaw and Membrane mapper code is unchanged since then, so that ruling still describes the form. That audit did not compare against measured drum decay (F&R Table 18.4/18.8). This audit finds the law too simple for drum heads because the radiation-dominated, mode-class-dependent decay is missing.

**Suggested fix.** Add a per-mode radiation-loss term keyed by Bessel order m: sigma_k = b1 + b3*f_k^2 + airLoading*R*g(m_k)*f_k^p. g(0) is large (monopole), g(1) is medium and g(>=2) is small, calibrated so that at airLoading = 1 the T60 ratios reproduce F&R Table 18.4 within a factor of about 1.5 ((11)/(01) about 5, (21)/(11) about 1.6). At airLoading = 0 it stays bit-identical to today's law. The bank already accepts per-mode frequencies, so the term can be passed as a per-mode damping offset. Test (membrum_tests, [membrane_body]): Membrane, size 0.5, decay 0.5, airLoading 1. Read the bank's per-mode radius (or fit per-mode envelopes) and assert T60(1,1) > 2*T60(0,1), T60(2,1) >= T60(1,1) and T60(0,2) < T60(1,1). A second case asserts that airLoading = 0 radii equal today's law.

**Verifier notes.**
- Claim matches the code: modal_resonator_bank.h:106-119 documents and :823-824 / :367-368 implement R_k = exp(-(b1 + b3*f_k^2)/fs); only b1 >= 0.2 and b3 >= 0 clamps (766-767); dampingLawFromLegacy (133-139); membrane_mapper.h:121 brightness = material, :148-152 decayTime, :177, override path :71-78. airLoading (100-109) and Decay Skew (160-173) do not change per-mode decay; drum_voice.h live refreshes (1619-1623, 1658-1662) pass one b1/b3 pair; no "radiation"/"perModeDecay"/"perModeDamping" in plugins/membrum/src. Prior research[3] confirmed only the form. Medium fits as a design limitation.
- Not refuted: code (modal_resonator_bank.h:823-824, 367-368; membrane_body.h:36-42; membrane_mapper.h:64-80, 100-109, 140-173) confirms no Bessel-order term; default-kit T60 figures not re-derived. Literature verified from the downloaded F&R PDF: Table 18.4 numbers match exactly, and WITHOUT kettle (T = 2820 N/m) (01) 1.5 s, (11) 3.4 s, (21) 3.4 s, (31) 4.6 s, so the mode-class ordering also holds for an unbaffled head; the book's notes on monopole vs dipole decay; §18.7 radiation; Table 18.8 matches.
- Code matches (modal_resonator_bank.h:367-368, :823-824; membrane_mapper.h:64-80, 115-117, 133-139, 146-152, 160-173, 177). Not documented as accepted: prior section 3-A (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:313; findings.json:1043-1074, 1071) and the project's own archetype note (preset-retune/archetypes/acoustic-maple-kick-acoustic-bass-drum.md:9) say (1,1) should outlast (0,1). Recommends downgrade to low: the monotonic profile is a documented design axis (spec 135-membrum-drum-synth.md:179; MANUAL.md:237), the tom retune relies on the b3 gradient (docs/tom-depth-implementation-plan.md:14, 222-232; CHANGELOG.md:138-149, 147), and the "kits sound alike" causal claim is unmeasured.

#### MB-264 — The FR-114 'note-off is a no-op' test passes while the voice is gated off and damped; no test checks that a short MIDI note still plays the full hit

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** followup:noteoff-truncation-fr114 (source: followup, verify round: followup)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/voice_pool/test_voice_pool_allocate.cpp:61-79](/plugins/membrum/tests/unit/voice_pool/test_voice_pool_allocate.cpp#L61-L79)

**Problem.** The case "VoicePool: note-off is a no-op for percussion voices" asserts only `getActiveVoiceCount() == 1` one block after `pool.noteOff(36)`. The pool's count reads meta_ state, which noteOff does not change. Meanwhile DrumVoice::noteOff has already gated the envelope and damped the bank. The next case (:91-107) was rewritten in 89cf0c64 to need an explicit noteOff for the voice to retire. The test file therefore pins both the spec rule and its violation. The factory infinite-ring sweeps also send paired NoteOn/NoteOff (preset-retune/kits/06-orchestralKit-fix-plan.md:182 D3), so their decay assertions lean on the note-off damp too.

**Why wrong.** A test named for FR-114 has to compare audio, not bookkeeping: the requirement says the voice's envelope must not be forced into release. As written it cannot fail on the regression it names. Every timing test also uses note lengths of 100 ms or more, so neither the tail cut nor the same-block silence (MB findings above) is covered.

**Consequence.** The spec divergence shipped green through every gate since 2026-04-17, and the same-block dropped-hit bug has no guard.

**Evidence.** test_voice_pool_allocate.cpp:75-78: `// FR-114: note-off must NOT decrement the voice count immediately. pool.noteOff(36); pool.processBlock(...); REQUIRE(pool.getActiveVoiceCount() == 1);`. :93-98: "Phase 8A.5: voices now retire either via auto-release ... or via explicit noteOff". `git show 89cf0c64`: "test_voice_pool_allocate "voice naturally becomes inactive": reworked to retire the voice via an explicit noteOff". voice_pool.cpp:296: `VP_VOICES[slot].noteOff();`.

**Suggested fix.** Replace the case with a render comparison: a note-on with a note-off after 1 block, a note-on with a note-off at 125 ms, and a note-on alone, compared over 2 s at -120 dB (or, if a per-pad release option is introduced, both option states). Add the processor-level same-block note-on/note-off case at blocks 256 and 1024. Make the factory sweeps run note-on-only as well (D3 in the orchestral fix plan).

**Verifier notes.**
- Confirmed: the case (test_voice_pool_allocate.cpp:61-79) checks only the count; VoicePool::noteOff (voice_pool.cpp:283-300, :296) calls the voice's noteOff; DrumVoice::noteOff (drum_voice.h:442-452) releases the exciter, tone shaper, gates the amp env and damps the bank (~50 ms); retirement happens later (voice_pool.cpp:386-396). FR-114 still forbids this (specs/138-membrum-phase3-polyphony/spec.md:161; voicepool_api.md:66), no amendment. Next case (:81-107) needs the noteOff. membrum_processor_tests.cpp:230-261 (FR-013) only checks output > 0. Nuance: FR-013 (Phase 1) expected a release, so the specs conflict; either way the FR-114 case asserts nothing about audio.
- Holds: the damp is a recorded design decision (voice_pool.cpp:285-290; CHANGELOG.md:636), but the spec was never amended and the test verifies no audio. Only processor note-off tests are membrum_processor_tests.cpp:213-224 and :230-261. processEvents ignores sampleOffset (processor.cpp:577-593). Audit probe (specs/membrum-audit/probes/audit_noteoff_probe.cpp.txt; f:/tmp/membrum-audit/noteoff-probe.csv): 5 ms note-off at block 256/1024 gives -60 dB decay 0.00 s and tail -300 dB on every pad; 125 ms note-off cuts tom tails 16-46 dB (LowFloorTom 1.56 s -> 0.16 s); Kick at 125 ms -18.5 dB at 256 vs -44.4 dB at 1024.
- Confirmed: ModalResonatorBank::damp (modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516) scales radii by 0.997, ~51 ms T60 (drum_voice.h:58-64), amp release 300 ms (:162); voice_pool.h:115-117 still says "bookkeeping only (FR-114)"; processEvents (processor.cpp:559-599) applies on/off at block start; only short-note test test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:855-919 (runRapidNoteOnOffPairs) asserts only decay to silence. git show 89cf0c64 ("Phase 8A.5 -- decouple amp envelope from voice lifetime", 2026-04-17). Medium.

#### MB-266 — The quality lane's 'ok' verdicts for Filter Type / Cutoff / Resonance / Env (offsets 7-10, 17-20) measured the coefficient glide, not the parameter; the US5-2 unit test's 'filter still closed at t=1 ms' premise is false

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** followup:toneshaper-filter-glide (source: followup, verify round: followup)

**Location:** [specs/membrum-audit/probes/audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt:1070-1085](/specs/membrum-audit/probes/audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt#L1070-L1085), also 1117-1120 (results param-audibility.csv rows 23-34, 53-64); [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/tone_shaper/test_tone_shaper.cpp:234-272](/plugins/membrum/tests/unit/tone_shaper/test_tone_shaper.cpp#L234-L272)

**Problem.** renderParam builds a new Rig (a fresh Processor) for every parameter step and hits the pad once (audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt:1070-1085, 1117-1120). Every measured hit therefore lands on a never-used slot, where the SVF starts at g(20 kHz) and the filter has not closed before the transient has passed. The verdict rule marks a parameter "suspicious" only when all three base pads are weak (:1173-1174). The kick's centroid shift (from the slow glide on its long tail) carries every filter row to "ok".
The Membrum unit test "Filter envelope sweep modulates LP cutoff (US5-2)" has the same problem. It calls ts.prepare() and then setFilterCutoff(200) with smoothing already on, so g starts at 20 kHz. Its comment says "t ≈ 1 ms (filter still closed, lowpass blocks 3 kHz)". With the glide the filter is near 19 kHz at 1 ms (svf-glide-times.txt). The test can pass while the filter never reaches 200 Hz in the measured windows.

**Why wrong.** An audibility probe for a per-note parameter must measure the steady-state behaviour a player hears on a warmed instrument, or both fresh and warm slots. A unit test whose comment states the opposite of the code's behaviour pins nothing. Both let the dead-filter defect ship green.

**Consequence.** In param-audibility.csv, LP from 20 Hz to 20 kHz changes the hat by 0.89 dB with the centroid at 8.27 kHz (row 28), and the snare by 0.66 dB (row 27). Filter Env Amount -1..+1 changes 0.07-0.15 dB (rows 32-34). Env Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release on the hat change at most 0.07 dB (rows 55, 58, 61, 64). All are labelled "ok". On a warm slot the same hat at LP 317 Hz with env -1 / 0 / +1 spans 25 dB (filter-glide.csv). The audit's dead-parameter table therefore misses about 8 parameters that are dead in exactly the context it measured, and live in the context it did not.

**Evidence.**
- audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt:1072 `Rig rig(c.aux);` inside renderParam, one note-on per render (:1080).
- param-audibility.csv:28 `offset=8:tsFilterCutoff,"LP, env amount 0",42,5,"-49.9 -49.9 -49.8 -49.4 -49.0","8265 8264 8256 8033 8370",...,0.89,...,ok`.
- :34 `offset=10:tsFilterEnvAmount,...,42,5,"-49.9 -49.8 -49.8 -49.8 -49.8",...,0.08,...,ok`.
- :55 `offset=17:tsFilterEnvAttack,...,42,...,0.04,...,ok`.
- test_tone_shaper.cpp:235-239 `ts.prepare(kSampleRate); ... ts.setFilterCutoff(200.0f);` and :253 `//   t ≈ 1 ms    (filter still closed, lowpass blocks 3 kHz)`.
- svf-glide-times.txt: fc at 1 ms = 19556 Hz (44.1 kHz) / 19168 Hz (48 kHz) for a 20 Hz target.
- filter-glide.csv: hat LP317_env-1/env0/env+1 warm -98.26/-95.92/-72.89 vs fresh -49.85/-49.84/-49.77.

**Suggested fix.** For tone-shaper offsets, render each step twice on the same rig with Priority policy (or poly 4 and five hits) and score the second, warm hit. After the noteOn snap fix, also REQUIRE fresh and warm to agree within 1 dB.
Rewrite test_tone_shaper.cpp US5-2:
1. Insert noise only after noteOn.
2. Assert absolute attenuation: the 3 kHz Goertzel magnitude in the 0-3 ms window at least 20 dB below the input's.

That assertion fails today and passes after the fix.

**Verifier notes.**
- Not refuted: ToneShaper::prepare (plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:79-83, default 20000 at :489) + SVF::prepare (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/svf.h:161-176) start g at g(20 kHz), 5 ms smoothing (svf.h:153); setFilterCutoff (tone_shaper.h:151-156) only moves the target (svf.h:204-208); noteOn (tone_shaper.h:319-363) calls resetIntegrators, which leaves g_ (svf.h:289-298); only reset() via resetForKitSwitch (drum_voice.h:477) snaps. Probe (:1070-1085, :1080, :1119, :1173-1174) and CSV rows (26, 28, 32-34, 55, 58, 61, 64) match. filter-glide.csv rows 182/192/202 vs 183/193/203 confirm the fresh/warm gap. test_tone_shaper.cpp:253 comment false; :271 compares two mostly-open windows.
- Not refuted; no spec or prior ruling makes fresh-slot-only measurement intentional. svf.h:511, 529-535 smoother; svf-glide-times.js.txt reproduces the law (svf-glide-times.txt:1, 8). test_tone_shaper.cpp:271-272 assertions are relative only. Minor overstatement: Filter Type changes the kick 19.89 dB (row 23) and Cutoff the kick 5.33 dB / 127 % centroid (row 26), so those "ok" verdicts are partly legitimate.
- Defect real; consequence holds for Cutoff and Env rows, overstated for Filter Type (offset 7). Mechanism confirmed (tone_shaper.h:79-83, :348; svf.h:161-176, 204-211, 295-298, 494-526, 153); gStart = tan(pi·20000/44100) = 6.80 gives ~19.5 kHz at 1 ms, 1758 Hz at 20 ms. Rows 32-34 are worse than stated (kick and snare fail every metric; the hat is rescued only by a 0.04 -> 0.05 s decay artefact). Warm vs fresh ~25 dB (filter-glide.csv lines 182-203). Unit test: kSampleRate 44100 (test_tone_shaper.cpp:27), no snap at :235-246.

#### MB-267 — SC-004 / SC-005 stay green because the exciter test measures the bare exciter's full-band centroid and the processor test was relaxed to 'either direction'; the spec 136 compliance row still claims > 2x

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** followup:velocity-timbre-inversion (source: followup, verify round: followup)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/exciters/test_velocity_mapping.cpp:29-56](/plugins/membrum/tests/unit/exciters/test_velocity_mapping.cpp#L29-L56), also 60-86 (also [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/membrum_processor_tests.cpp:533-569](/plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/membrum_processor_tests.cpp#L533-L569); specs/136-membrum-*/spec.md:196, 297; [specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:327](/specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md#L327), 541, 599)

**Problem.** test_velocity_mapping.cpp renders a bare ExciterBank (default params, voiceId 0, no body, no click, no noise layer, no amp envelope, no tone shaper) for 441 samples at velocity 0.23 vs 1.0. It takes the full-band DFT centroid, which is dominated by the content above 6 kHz that the velocity-opened ImpactExciter SVF adds. Clap is not in the list (l.66-73). membrum_processor_tests.cpp:533-569 ("SC-005") was rewritten to `REQUIRE(ratio < 0.9 || ratio > 1.1)`. Its own comment (l.542-544) says soft hits "typically ... average BRIGHTER", so an inversion passes. The spec 136 compliance row (l.297) still reads "> 2x centroid (threshold > 2.0f) MET", and spec 137 l.599 cites the bare-exciter test as proof of SC-004.

**Why wrong.** SC-004 / FR-016 (spec 137:192, 327) and SC-005 (spec 136:196) are claims about what the instrument does with velocity, and only a voice- or processor-level render can verify them. A test that accepts either direction cannot detect an inversion. A compliance row that cites a threshold the test no longer enforces is a false MET (CLAUDE.md Completion Honesty).

**Consequence.** The factory kits ship with velocity-inverted timbre on snares, hand drums and a kick (0.53-0.97) and flat timbre on many others, while every velocity test is green. Examples: Drone and Sustain 36 Friction/String is 0.999 even body-only, i.e. velocity is a pure 10.9 dB gain; Orchestral 38 is 1.002. The bare-exciter test shows Impulse at 5.1x (1098 -> 5647 Hz full band), yet below 2.5 kHz the same exciter moves only 187 -> 236 Hz and tilts 18 dB darker.

**Evidence.** test_velocity_mapping.cpp:40-55 `bank.trigger(0.23f); ... bank2.trigger(1.0f); ... spectralCentroidDFT(buf, numSamples, sr)` with kSamples = 441 (l.64) and 6 types (l.66-73, no Clap); l.84 `CHECK(r.ratio >= 2.0f)`. membrum_processor_tests.cpp:569 `REQUIRE((ratio < 0.9f || ratio > 1.1f));` with the comment at l.542-544 "the centroid difference can be either direction (typically soft hits average BRIGHTER ...)". specs/136 spec.md:297 "| SC-005 | ✅ MET | ... > 2x centroid (threshold > 2.0f)". Measured (probe C) Impulse full band 1098.1 -> 5647.4 Hz versus below 2.5 kHz 186.7 -> 235.8 Hz. Processor-level (probe1b V0, warm): Hand Drums 42 0.528, Acoustic Studio 36 0.691, Acoustic Studio 38 0.792, Vintage Wood 38 0.860, Rock Big Room 38 0.888, Hand Drums 38 0.959, Ghost Bones 38 0.967, Drone and Sustain 36 0.999 (body-only 0.999, TS neutral 0.980), Orchestral 38 1.002, 909 38 1.038.

**Suggested fix.** Replace the exciter-level centroid with a Processor-level velocity test per exciter x body family (Impulse/Membrane small and large, Mallet/Membrane with pitch envelope, NoiseBurst/Membrane snare with noiseLayerGain 6.2, Impulse/Bell, Friction/String, Clap). Render vel 30 and 127 through the Processor (multi-bus, master -6 dB, peak under the limiter) and REQUIRE centroid(127)/centroid(30) >= the spec value over a 200 ms window. Add Clap to the exciter list. Restore a directional assertion in membrum_processor_tests.cpp:569, or mark SC-005 NOT MET in spec 136 l.297 and spec 137 l.599 until the code meets it.

**Verifier notes.**
- Confirmed, one sub-point weaker: bare ExciterBank render (test_velocity_mapping.cpp:29-56), 6 types without Clap (l.66-73; Clap = 6, kCount = 7 at exciter_type.h:19-20), CHECK at l.84; processor test relaxed (membrum_processor_tests.cpp:569, comment l.540-552); spec 136 SC-005 (spec.md:196) row l.297 is a false MET. Mitigation: spec 137 FR-092 (l.295) asks for the EXCITATION centroid, so citing the exciter test for spec 137 SC-004 is defensible; Clap has a processor-level case (tests/unit/dsp/test_clap_acceptance.cpp:414-436). Kit numbers (probe1b) not re-run. Medium.
- Confirmed, partly intended by the spec: the relaxation cites "Phase 11 (spec 145) re-baseline", but no spec ruling carries it (grep of specs/ finds nothing; spec 145 has no SC-005), so the stale MET row is a Completion Honesty defect. Partly refuted: test_velocity_mapping.cpp and spec 137 rows l.541/l.599 do what FR-092 (spec.md:295) and SC-004 (l.327) define; FR-016/FR-092 say "6 exciter types", predating Clap; the relaxation is deliberate and commented. Recommends downgrade.
- Confirmed core claim (probes not re-run): test_velocity_mapping.cpp:29-56, 35, 53-54, 64, 66-73, 84; dsp/exciter_type.h:19; membrum_processor_tests.cpp:533-569, 542-544; specs/136-membrum-phase1-scaffold/spec.md:196, 297 false MET. Spec 137 SC-004 (l.327) per-exciter wording makes l.599 a literal reading, but FR-016 (l.192) speaks of the instrument's spectral content and Clap is uncovered. No severity change.

#### MB-269 — Any fix that makes modal retunes converge (snap or per-sample smoothing) turns note-off damp() into a no-op: measured -60 dB at 3.45 s instead of 0.052 s

**Severity:** medium (finder: high) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** shared-dsp-contract · **Dimension:** followup:modal-retune-while-ringing (source: followup, verify round: followup)

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516](/dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L507-L516), also 294-305, 342-351, 821-841, 906-914

**Problem.** damp(scale) multiplies radius_ and radiusTarget_ once (507-516) and stores the scale nowhere. updateModes() calls computeModeCoefficients, which rebuilds radiusTarget_ from the damping law alone (823-838: R_k = exp(-(b1+b3 f^2)/fs)). The damped radius is therefore overwritten on every retune. Today the overwrite only partly cancels the release, because smoothCoefficients() moves radius_ 1 % of the gap per processBlock call (906-914). The two fixes that make the pitch envelope, tension and morph retunes actually reach their targets (the already-reported "retunes converge at 2 ms x block size" finding) are a per-chunk updateModes + snapCoefficients (the Seraphis precedent at continuous_body.h:2820-2860) or per-sample smoothing. Either one makes radius_ equal the undamped target within one chunk. DrumVoice calls damp(kNoteOffDampScale) at noteOff (drum_voice.h:451) and damp(kFastReleaseDampScale) in fastReleaseDamp (drum_voice.h:106). It calls updateModes on every chunk while the pitch envelope is active (drum_voice.h:734-746), which is forever once Time > 0, and also while tension (747-754) or morph (762-770) is active.

**Why wrong.** damp() is documented as the STK Modal::damp() note-off idiom, so that "the voice finishes through its own damping law" (modal_resonator_bank.h:501-506). That contract only holds if the damping survives later coefficient rebuilds. A state-preserving retune (updateModes, documented as "Update mode coefficients without clearing filter states", 293) has no reason to cancel a release that is in progress.

**Consequence.** Measured with a 48-mode membrane at 150 Hz, b1 = 2 s^-1, 44.1 kHz, damp(0.997) at 50 ms. Time to -60 dB modal energy: no retune 0.052 s; current updateModes per 64-sample block 0.067 s; updateModes + snapCoefficients per 64 samples 3.454 s; per-sample update + smoothing 3.141 s. At 96 kHz: 0.024 / 0.027 / 3.449 / 2.484 s. If the retune fix lands as-is, note-off stops shortening any voice that has a pitch envelope (the 808 kicks, the default kit's kicks and toms), Membrane tension or Material Morph. Short MIDI notes then ring for their full multi-second tail. fastReleaseDamp loses its body damping too, so steal and choke rely entirely on the pool's gain ramp.

**Evidence.** modal_resonator_bank.h:513-514 `radiusTarget_[k] *= scale; radius_[k] *= scale;` (not persisted); :823-824 `float decayRate_k = b1 + b3 * f_w * f_w; float R_k = std::exp(-decayRate_k / sampleRate_);` then :838 `radiusTarget_[k] = R_k;`; :348-350 snapCoefficients copies the targets into the running arrays. drum_voice.h:451 `bodyBank_.getSharedBank().damp(kNoteOffDampScale);`, :106 fastReleaseDamp, :745 retuneFundamental per chunk -> :1619 sharedBank.updateModes. Probe: specs/membrum-audit/probes/audit_retune_probe.cpp.txt (scratch exe linked against build/windows-x64-release/lib/Release/KrateDSP.lib + hwy.lib, /fp:fast, no repo edits). Results: specs/membrum-audit/probes/retune-probe-results.txt, lines "E3 fs= 44100 damp(0.997) then ..." (0.052 / 0.067 / 3.454 / 3.141 s) and "E3 fs= 96000 ..." (0.024 / 0.027 / 3.449 / 2.484 s). The same probe (E4) shows updateModes re-counts flushed modes (active 0 -> 48 right after updateModes -> 0 after the next processBlock). The fast path is therefore NOT a retirement defect, because flushSilentModes runs at the end of every processBlock (446). Note: during this run git status showed plugins/membrum/tests/CMakeLists.txt modified and plugins/membrum/tests/audit/ untracked; that is another agent's probe, not this one.

**Suggested fix.** Fix this before, or together with, the retune-convergence fix. Give the bank a persistent release multiplier: damp(scale) sets releaseScale_ *= scale, computeModeCoefficients and updateDampingLaw multiply every R_k by releaseScale_, and setModes (note-on) and reset() set it back to 1. damp() is called only by Membrum (grep: Innexus uses processSample(x, decayScale); Seraphis ContinuousBody never calls damp), so Innexus and Seraphis stay bit-identical. Test in membrum_tests (unit/dsp): ring a membrane voice with the pitch envelope on, noteOff, render with 64- and 512-sample host blocks, and require T60 after noteOff within 10 % of the same voice without a pitch envelope, and the same at both block sizes. Add a dsp_processors_tests case: damp(0.997) followed by updateModes + snapCoefficients keeps the damped decay.

**Verifier notes.**
- Mechanism holds (modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516, 294-305, 823-824, 838, 906-914, coefficient :213/:647, ~1.1 % per call; snapCoefficients 342-351; updateDampingLaw 356-370; drum_voice.h:451, :106, 734-746, :1619, 747-754, 762-770, :1658). Consequence overstated, lowered: conditional (today 0.052 -> 0.067 s only); every renderer multiplies by the amp env (drum_voice.h:884-885, 897-898, 1060-1061) gated off at noteOff (:446) with a 300 ms release (:162), so the audible tail is capped at ~300 ms; the cost is a voice that holds its slot and CPU until the bank flushes (bankSilent safety net :645-669); the pool's 5 ms ramp still silences steal/choke. Valid medium fix-ordering hazard.
- Confirmed, nothing guards it; probe numbers in specs/membrum-audit/probes/retune-probe-results.txt:49-52, 60-63. The hazard already shows in one renderer: DrumVoice::process() (497-510) calls updateModes every sample and the bank smooths per sample (modal_resonator_bank.h:421-424), the measured 3.141 s case, a renderer divergence. Downgrade because production audio goes through processBlock only (voice_pool.cpp:356, 410, 471, 528).
- Confirmed (isPitchEnvActive = pitchEnvTimeMs_ > 0, tone_shaper.h:310-313; slow path retunes per block 966-977; E2 at retune-probe-results.txt:22-30 shows the convergence defect is real, 200->40 Hz reaches only 140-198 Hz). Overstated: audible tail grows from ~50-67 ms to the 300 ms amp release (:446, :162); retirement (:645-651, 660-665) would hold a silent voice up to ~3.4 s (CPU, polyphony), not audible ringing; steal/choke bounded by the 5 ms ramp. High -> medium.

#### MB-062 — Default kit: Closed, Pedal and Open Hi-Hat render identically, and so do the Crash and Ride pads

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** kit-quality · **Dimension:** gain-staging-master (source: static, verify round: static)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h:414-431](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h#L414-L431)

**Problem.** DefaultKit::apply assigns DrumTemplate::Hat with no size override to MIDI 42, 44 and 46, and DrumTemplate::Cymbal with no override to MIDI 49, 51, 52, 53, 55, 57 and 59. The table gives these pads no other per-pad differentiation, so a fresh instance plays the same sound on all of them.

**Why wrong.** An open hi-hat must ring longer than a closed one; a ride must differ from a crash (stick ping vs wash). The GM map in the table comment names them as different instruments.

**Consequence.** Measured: MIDI 42 and 46 both give peak 0.1534 and RMS 0.0035 over 2 s; MIDI 49 and 51 both give peak 0.2766 and RMS 0.0232. They are bit-for-bit the same level and decay. The out-of-the-box kit has one hat sound and one cymbal sound spread over 10 pads.

**Evidence.** default_kit.h:414 `{.tmpl = DrumTemplate::Hat, .sizeOverride = -1.0f }, //  6: MIDI 42 Closed Hi-Hat`, :416 MIDI 44 the same, :418 MIDI 46 the same; :421/:423 Cymbal -1 for 49/51. Measured (hidden [.measure][level], 48 kHz): "[level] Closed Hat MIDI=42 peak= 0.1534 ... RMS=0.0035", "[level] Open Hat MIDI=46 peak= 0.1534 ... RMS=0.0035", "[level] Crash MIDI=49 peak= 0.2766 ... RMS=0.0232", "[level] Ride MIDI=51 peak= 0.2766 ... RMS=0.0232".

**Suggested fix.** Give the Hat and Cymbal rows per-pad overrides (decay, size, noise decay; for the ride a smaller body, a stick-like exciter and a longer decay; for the open hat a long noise-layer decay) like the toms get. Test: for the default kit, assert that the RMS over 2 s of pad 46 is >= 6 dB above pad 42, and that the spectral centroid or T60 of 49 vs 51 differs by >= 20 %.

Fresh instance = DefaultKit (processor.cpp:111). The quoted test (tests/unit/processor/test_output_level_measure.cpp:158-179, labels :171-174) matches. Open hat shares the closed hat's noiseLayerDecay 0.15 / decay 0.1 (:191, :200). Affects only the default kit, not the 20 .vstpreset kits; medium.

The rule also makes all Perc pads identical; the user-facing sound sets are the 20 factory kits (e.g. preset-retune/kits/06-electronicKit.md). A reasonable feature request, not a defect against the documented design.
- Confirmed from source (probe not re-run): default_kit.h:414-431, loop :442-444, size branch :354-355 skipped, tom pass :458-481, hats all choke group 1 (:487-489), so an open/closed pair is impossible in the default kit; templates fixed (Hat :186-208, Cymbal from :210); processor.cpp:111. The repo's own papers name the weakness (PRESET-RETUNE-PLAN.md:19; preset-retune/01-current-state.md:50). Hits every new instance, 10 of 32 pads; not the factory kits; medium stays.

#### MB-088 — MB-S03: Released builds wrote blob versions 1 and 2 (and per-pad IDs with stride 64); today's reader accepts only 5, so their projects and kits load silently as the default kit and automation lands on other pads

**Severity:** medium (finder: high) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** lifecycle-state · **Dimension:** lifecycle-state (source: static, verify round: static) · **Corroborated by measurement:** probe state:released-versions: "v0.9.0-0.9.1=1, v0.10.1-0.10.2=2, v0.12.x=5; versions 1,2,4,6 rejected (rc 1), previous kit intact". state_codec.cpp:431 `if (version != kBlobVersion)`; plugin_ids.h:27 "not shipped, so no legacy versions are accepted on read".

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.cpp:428-432](/plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.cpp#L428-L432), also 556-560 (also [state_codec.h:12-13](/plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.h#L12-L13), [processor.cpp:905-916](/plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L905-L916), [controller_state.cpp:64-71](/plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state.cpp#L64-L71))

**Problem.** Origin's tags (`git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/membrum/*`): v0.9.0, v0.9.1, v0.10.1, v0.10.2, v0.12.0-v0.12.5. `git show` per tag:
- v0.9.0 and v0.9.1: kCurrentStateVersion = 1, kBlobVersion = kPadBlobVersion = 1, 52-slot kit sound / 51-slot pad sound, kPadParamStride = 64.
- v0.10.1 and v0.10.2: version 2, 56 slots, stride 64.
- v0.12.0 to v0.12.5: version 5, 59 slots, stride 128.

(v0.11.0, the blob v4 build, is not tagged on origin.)
readKitBlob and readPadPresetBlob return kResultFalse for any version != 5, with no migration.
On a rejected host load:
- Processor::setState returns kResultFalse and the processor keeps whatever it had (DefaultKit from initialize).
- Controller::setComponentState returns kResultFalse and changes no parameter.

Both therefore show the default kit. That much is consistent, but nothing tells the user.
The per-pad parameter stride also changed from 64 to 128, so a host automation lane saved for pad N, offset k (ID 1000+64N+k) now addresses pad floor(N/2), offset 64*(N mod 2)+k. Example: pad 2 Material (1130) is now pad 1 Material. Pad 1 Material (1066) is now pad 0 offset 66, which is inactive and swallowed by setPadConfigField's default branch. kChokeGroupId (252) also changed from RangeParameter (v0.9.0 / v0.10.2 controller.cpp:406 / :442) to StringListParameter (controller.cpp:484-496) at the same ID.

**Why wrong.** Comments and the CHANGELOG justify the strict check with "The plugin has not shipped" (state_codec.h:12-13) and "Pre-release, strict version check with no migration" (CHANGELOG.md:188-191, 230-233). Release tags on origin contradict this. A state reader must either migrate earlier released formats or report the failure. Release state comes from origin's tags.

**Consequence.** A DAW project or user kit saved with v0.9.x or v0.10.x opens with the GM default kit and no error message. If the user saves the project, the original kit is overwritten (data loss). Automation lanes from those versions drive the wrong pad, or nothing. User .vstpreset kits from those versions show "load failed" in the browser. This needs a product decision (migrate v1 and v2, or document the break and surface an error). It is reported because the code's justification is false.

**Evidence.** `git show membrum/v0.9.0:.../plugin_ids.h:28` "kCurrentStateVersion = 1"; .../state_codec.h:104-105 "kBlobVersion = 1; kPadBlobVersion = 1"; membrum/v0.10.2 state_codec.h:105 "kBlobVersion = 2;  // Phase 10: 56-slot sound array"; v0.10.2 pad_config.h:23 "kPadParamStride = 64"; v0.12.0 pad_config.h:25 "kPadParamStride = 128"; current state_codec.cpp:431 `if (version != kBlobVersion) return kResultFalse;`; processor.cpp:911-912; controller_state.cpp:70-71.

**Suggested fix.** Decide explicitly: either add readers for v1 (52/51 slots) and v2 (56 slots) that map old slots onto PadSnapshot (defaults for the slots added later: noiseLayerGain 1.0, wireCoupling 0, pan 0.5, damping -1, knee fields per PadConfig), or keep the rejection and correct the comments and CHANGELOG to say released v0.9/v0.10 data is not loadable. In both cases, report the failure: return kResultFalse and send a "StateLoadFailed" message so the controller's PresetStatus label shows it. Regression test: a v2 blob captured from the v0.10.2 codec (tests/golden/phase2_state_v2.bin is version 2, 268 bytes, but it is a phase-2-era layout, so capture a real v0.10.2 getState) must either load with the migrated values or raise the explicit failure signal. Also add a test that pins the per-pad ID map against a recorded v0.12 table, so the next stride change is caught.

**Verifier notes.**
- Every factual part checked out (origin tags; v0.9.0 plugin_ids.h:28, state_codec.h:104-105, pad_config.h:23; v0.10.2 plugin_ids.h:29, state_codec.h:105-106; v0.12.0 stride 128; state_codec.cpp:431, :559; processor.cpp:906-916; controller_state.cpp:64-71; state_codec.h:12-13 false; choke RangeParameter at v0.10.2 controller.cpp:442 vs StringList controller.cpp:484-486). Downgrade: CHANGELOG.md:188-191, 230-233 announce the no-migration rejection, so it is a documented choice for 0.x; what remains is a false comment, no UI failure signal, and remapped per-pad automation. Medium.
- Facts correct, refuted on context: the rejection is announced in each format-changing release entry (CHANGELOG.md:188-191 [0.12.0], 230-233 [0.11.0], 328-329 [0.10.0] "Legacy v1 blobs are rejected per the existing pre-release policy"); all releases are 0.x; a rejected setState leaves processor and controller consistent. Remaining is low, documentation only: stale state_codec.h:12-14 ("v3", "57 slots", "has not shipped") and no CHANGELOG mention of the stride change.
- Facts check out (release workflow .github/workflows/release.yml:1-30 published the tags; v0.10.2 processor.cpp:980 getState writes via writeKitBlob; offset 66 inactive, kPadActiveParamCountV12 = 66). Downgrade: the break is intended and documented (CHANGELOG.md:188-191, 230-233), 0.x is "pre-release", and it has been live since v0.12.0 (2026-07-22). What is left is a missing runtime failure signal plus a false comment in a pre-1.0 product: medium, not high.

#### MB-107 — noteOff damp() is undone by the per-chunk updateModes() of the pitch envelope, morph or tension, so the release length depends on the host block size

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** shared-dsp-contract · **Dimension:** shared-dsp-contracts (source: static, verify round: static)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:442-452](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L442-L452), also 734-754, 1619-1625 (callee [modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516](/dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L507-L516), 759-841, 906-914)

**Problem.** DrumVoice::noteOff() and fastReleaseDamp() shorten the release through ModalResonatorBank::damp(), which multiplies radius_ AND radiusTarget_ in place. While a pitch envelope is enabled, ToneShaper::isPitchEnvActive() returns true forever once time > 0 (tone_shaper.h:310-313). Each chunk then calls updateModes(), which recomputes radiusTarget_ from the undamped damping law (computeModeCoefficients:823-838) and also resets numActiveModes_/active_ (:760, :840-841). Smoothing then pulls radius_ back to the undamped value at 1/96 per processBlock call. The total extra damping a note-off can apply is about 0.003 x B / (1/96), i.e. about 0.29 x hostBlock nepers. Below about 24-sample blocks that never reaches -60 dB.

**Why wrong.** damp() is documented as the note-off idiom ("so the voice finishes through its own damping law", modal_resonator_bank.h:501-506), and it assumes the mode set is not re-derived afterwards. updateModes() re-derives every radius target from the stored law, so the two bank APIs cannot be combined unless the caller re-applies the damp scale or folds it into the law.

**Consequence.** For pads with a pitch envelope (most kicks and toms), Material Morph or tension, the note-off release and the voice lifetime depend on the host block size. Measured (Impulse/Membrane, pitch env 160->80 Hz over 30 ms, noteOff at 0.2 s, 48 kHz):
- Retirement: 6.591 s at block 8, 5.632 s at 16, 3.713 s at 32, 0.512 s at 64. Without the pitch envelope: 0.361 / 0.404 / 0.478 / 0.479 s.
- Last sample above -60 dB: 0.320 s at block 8 vs 0.230 s without the envelope.

Small-buffer hosts therefore keep these voices alive several seconds longer (slots, CPU, coupling resonators).

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:451 `bodyBank_.getSharedBank().damp(kNoteOffDampScale)` (0.997, :64); :734-745 pitchEnvActive -> retuneFundamental each chunk; :1619 sharedBank.updateModes(...). modal_resonator_bank.h:513-514 `radiusTarget_[k] *= scale; radius_[k] *= scale;` :838 `radiusTarget_[k] = R_k` (undamped); :760 `numActiveModes_ = 0` then :841 `++` per mode; tone_shaper.h:310-313 isPitchEnvActive returns `pitchEnvTimeMs_ > 0`. Probe C:/Users/scab/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/af40cef86e602ebb/69f67fe4-9e20-4f6f-a325-fd4459c6f76b/scratchpad/contract_probe_mb/cp.cpp: "Impulse/Membrane pitchEnv block=8 retired_at=6.591 s ... last>-60dB=0.320 s" vs "noPitchEnv block=8 retired_at=0.361 s ... 0.230 s".

**Suggested fix.** Fold the release into the damping law: on noteOff, store a release multiplier and apply it to cachedMapperResult_.damping (or to the radius targets after every updateModes), so the per-chunk retune preserves it. Also stop retuning once the pitch envelope has finished (ToneShaper should report active only while the segment envelope runs). Test: a pitch-envelope voice with noteOff at 200 ms must reach -60 dB within the same time (±10 %) at blocks 8, 64 and 1024, and retire within 1 s.

**Verifier notes.**
- Not refuted; source and a re-run of cp.exe confirm: drum_voice.h:451, :64; modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516; isPitchEnvActive is a config flag (tone_shaper.h:310-313, processPitchEnvelope keeps returning endHz 380-390); processBlockFast (drum_voice.h:607, 734-746) -> updateModalFundamentalOnBank (:1607-1626) -> updateModes (:294-305) -> computeModeCoefficients (:823-838; :760, :840-841); smoothCoefficients once per processBlock (:431-433, :906-913); tension (:747-753) and morph (:762-769, pushCachedModes :1656-1665) likewise; retirement needs a silent bank (:644-651, safety net :660-665). Re-run matches: 6.591 / 5.632 / 3.713 / 0.512 s vs 0.361 / 0.404 / 0.478 / 0.479 s; 256 / 1024 identical (0.485 / 0.512 s). Medium stays; audible release changes modestly.
- Confirmed by source and probe re-run: damp stored nowhere (drum_voice.h:442-452, 104-107 with 0.88; modal_resonator_bank.h:507-516); retune every chunk for the voice's life (tone_shaper.h:310-313; drum_voice.h:607, 734-746, 1607-1625, 747-754, 762-769, 1656-1665); flushed modes re-activated (:461-474 vs :760, :840-841); smoothing ~1/96 per call (:433, :453, :647, :213). Block-size dependence is real in the plugin: kMaxBlockSize 2048 (drum_voice.h:589), processor.cpp:636/:663 and voice_pool.cpp:356/:471 pass the host block with no sub-splitting.
- Bank-level interaction real, but the claimed consequence does not happen in the plugin: the probe drives DrumVoice alone and skips VoicePool, which calls noteOff() again on every block whose voice peak is below 1e-3 while Active (voice_pool.cpp:377-384, 505-512), re-applying damp(0.997) (drum_voice.h:451) and outpacing the re-smoothing. Retirement needs silent bank + finished 300 ms amp release (drum_voice.h:644-651, :162); shadow voices are freed by the 5 ms ramp (voice_pool.cpp:980-1001). Re-built probe with the pool rule (cp_pool.cpp): pitchEnv vs noPitchEnv retire at 0.323/0.317 s (block 16), 0.409/0.407 (32), 0.479/0.479 (64), 0.485/0.485 (256), 0.512/0.512 (1024); last > -60 dB 0.231 vs 0.226 s (16), 0.230 vs 0.227 s (32).

#### MB-153 — Finding 17 and M-9 decisions rested on a false 'pre-release' premise: v0.10.2 shipped kChokeGroupId as a RangeParameter and a 64-wide pad stride

**Severity:** medium (finder: high) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** prior-audit-regression · **Dimension:** prior-audit-regressions (source: static, verify round: static)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:496](/plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L496) (choke StringList); [pad_config.h:25](/plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h#L25) (stride 128)

#### MB-169 — Global Coupling at full amount adds no measurable level: the -46..-26 dB send plus the -20 dBFS energy limiter make it nearly inaudible

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** measured-dead-parameter · **Dimension:** measured (source: measured, verify round: measured)

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h:147-157](/dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h#L147-L157)

**Problem.** setAmount maps [0,1] to -46..-26 dB of coupling gain. The return is then capped by Processor::applyEnergyLimiter at -20 dBFS (processor.h:183-187). A single kick drives the coupling about 61 dB below the dry signal.

**Why wrong.** A user-facing "Global Coupling" knob at maximum should produce an audible sympathetic halo. Spec 140 SC-008 requires couplings measurable at >= 12 dB differences between tom pairs.

**Consequence.** Sweeping Global Coupling 0..1 changes level by 0.0 dB on the kick, snare and hat and only lengthens a near-silent hat tail. Coupling Delay (273) is inaudible for the same reason.

**Evidence.** Quality probe param:global=270:globalCoupling: "36: 0.0/0/0/0.0 ; 38: 0.0/0/0/0.0 ; 42: 0.0/0/59/0.0". Probe coupling: "-61 dB rel dry (single kick)". sympathetic_resonance.h:156-157 `// Map [0,1] -> [-46, -26] dB -> linear  couplingGain_ = std::pow(10.0f, (-46.0f + 20.0f * amount) / 20.0f);` processor.h:185 `constexpr float kThreshold = 0.1f; // -20 dBFS`.

**Suggested fix.** Re-calibrate the amount range (for example -30..-6 dB) against a measured target, such as a coupled tom pair reaching -30 dB relative to the struck tom. Consider raising the limiter threshold or making it relative. Test: global coupling 1.0 with two tuned toms gives partner-band energy >= -30 dB relative to the dry hit.

**Verifier notes.**
- Observation holds, mechanism wrong: sympathetic_resonance.h:156-157 (-46..-26 dB, applied at :322), resonators normalised and weighted 1/sqrt(n) (:243-244), so the return never exceeds ~-26 dB (+0.43 dB max). Missed root cause: resonators sit only on the struck voice's own partials (voice_pool.cpp:243-247), masked by the dry sound, and the CouplingMatrix is never applied (processor.cpp:138; coupling_matrix.h:79-87 have no caller). The limiter (processor.h:183-196) never engages at -61 dB; SC-008 is a ratio test (spec.md:380; test_coupling_integration.cpp:731-735) and passes; SC-002 (spec.md:268) requires >= 40 dB below the kick (test :279-283). Range calibrated to Lehtonen 2007 (sympathetic_resonance.h:147-149). Recommends low, re-target the fix at CouplingMatrix routing.
- Weak level is a documented choice: SC-002 (specs/140-membrum-phase5-coupling/spec.md:268) sets -40 dB as a ceiling (test_coupling_integration.cpp:277-283); spec lines 85, 102 say "subtle"; the suggested -30 dB target would break that ceiling. SC-008 (spec line 274) is a ratio, checked at test :731-735. Limiter misattributed (processor.h:183-196); the level comes from setAmount (:156-157) and, for a kick, the 100 Hz anti-mud HPF (:120, :355). A 0.0 dB reading is expected. Separate lead: CouplingMatrix::effectiveGain never read on the audio path (processor.cpp:138, 693-707).
- Consequence real and measured, two mechanism parts wrong: mapping confirmed (sympathetic_resonance.h:152-158, :243-244, HPF :55/:120/:355); audit probe specs/membrum-audit/probes/probe-results.txt:18 (audit_probes.cpp.txt:1450-1465) gives "0.00 / -60.98"; param-audibility.csv:200-202 flat level for 36/38/42, only a hat-tail decay change (59.3); Coupling Delay (processor.cpp:695-703) inherits it; test_coupling_integration.cpp:276-282 asserts only > 1e-8 and treats SC-002 as an upper bound. Corrections: the -20 dBFS limiter (processor.h:183-195) is not a cause (the return sits ~-67 dBFS); SC-008 (spec.md:380) is the wrong citation, SC-002 is the relevant one. coupling_matrix.h:79-87 unread on the audio path.

#### MB-178 — Soft hits are brighter than hard hits on 10 of 60 notes: the noise layer ignores velocity while the body scales by about v^1.6

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** measured-kit-quality · **Dimension:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h:158-170](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h#L158)

**Problem.** `NoiseLayer::trigger(float /*velocity*/)` discards velocity, so the noise layer is scaled only by the amp envelope peak (= velocity, drum_voice.h:163 `setVelocityScaling(true)`). The body is scaled by the exciter's velocity law (Impact v^0.6 or similar) times that same envelope, so the bright noise component gains about 0.6 x 20log10(v) dB relative to the body as velocity falls.

**Why wrong.** Physical drums get brighter when hit harder (spec 137 SC-004: velocity 30 vs 127 shifts the spectral centroid by >= 2x in the brightening direction).

**Consequence.** Several kick and snare pads get darker as they are hit harder (centroid ratio hi/lo): Drone 36 0.249, Hand Drums 42 and Latin 36 0.533, Acoustic Studio 36 0.673 and 38 0.796, Vintage Wood 38 0.845, 909 38 0.889, Rock 38 0.904. This inverts expressive playing.

**Evidence.** Quality velocity:inverted brightness: "Drone 36 0.249; Hand Drums 42 & Latin 36 0.533; Acoustic Studio 36 0.673, 38 0.796; Vintage Wood 38 0.845; 909 38 0.889; Rock 38 0.904 ..." (10 of 60). noise_layer.h:158 `void trigger(float /*velocity*/) noexcept`.

**Suggested fix.** Give the noise layer a velocity law at least as steep as the body's (for example noise amplitude x v^0.6, matching the exciter, plus a velocity-driven cutoff lift). Test: notes 36/38/42 of every kit have centroid ratio(vel127/vel40) >= 1.0.

**Verifier notes.**
- The code facts and the probe numbers are real (noise_layer.h:158; noise gain `standaloneGain * noiseLayerGain_ * wireGainMod_` at drum_voice.h:860-861, amp envelope peak = v at drum_voice.h:163, 436 and adsr_envelope.h:512; body ~v^1.6 via impact_exciter.h:129; quality-results.txt:297-348), but no isolation run (noise mix 0 vs on) shows the noise layer is the cause.
- Hand Drums 42 / Latin 36 (0.533): the pad's noise is pink, mix 0.10, cutoff ~849 Hz (membrum_preset_generator.cpp:4079-4095), about -38 dBFS and darker than the bongo modes; its 30.1 dB level difference vs ~16 dB for v^1.6 points to a non-linear stage (nonlinearCoupling velocity at drum_voice.h:333, or tensionModAmt 0.22). Drone 36 (0.249) is Friction/String with drive and fold into an LP (generator.cpp:5976-5989) and velocity-set friction cutoff (friction_exciter.h:86).
- A second lens confirmed the mechanism from source: the noise scales only linearly with v (drum_voice.h:547-549, 860-863, 560/566, 884-885), while the click layer does scale with velocity (click_layer.h:133), so the noise layer is the odd one out; default noiseLayerMix is 0.35 (pad_config.h:251); the SC-004 test (test_velocity_mapping.cpp:29-85) measures the ExciterBank alone and cannot catch a voice-level inversion. Medium is appropriate.
- A third lens: six of the ten pads have a noise layer too quiet to matter (Acoustic Studio 36 mix 0.10 brown, :528-531; Hand Drums 42 / Latin 36, :4093; Hand Drums 38 / Latin 38, :4022; Drone 36, :5996), roughly 30 dB under the body. The noise layer plausibly drives only the four snares (Acoustic Studio 38, Vintage Wood 38, 909 38, Rock 38; mix 0.65-0.78, gain 6.2 at :582-587, :2056-2059, :2338-2341, :2979), whose inversions are mild (10-20 %). SC-004 (specs/137 spec.md:327) is an exciter-in-isolation requirement, so the noise layer does not violate it.

#### MB-214 — Physics (contradicted): Mode Stretch at its documented 'physical' default (1.0) leaves the Chladni ratios unstretched

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:noise-body

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h:118-120](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h#L118) (same pattern [plate_mapper.h:60-62](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_mapper.h#L60), [shell_mapper.h:61](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_mapper.h#L61), [bell_mapper.h:56](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/bell_mapper.h#L56)); [modal_resonator_bank.h:783, 806-807](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L783); [pad_config_apply.h:123-126](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config_apply.h#L123); [pad_config.h:212](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h#L212)

**Problem.** PadConfig.modeStretch defaults to 0.333333 ('norm of [0.5, 2.0], default 1.0'). pad_config_apply.h:125-126 maps it to 0.5 + 0.333333*1.5 = 1.0, and the comment calls that '1.0 = physical'. NoiseBodyMapper then computes stretchNorm = (1.0 - 0.5)/1.5 = 0.3333. The bank sets B = stretch^2 * 0.01 = 1.11e-3 and multiplies every mode by sqrt(1 + B (k+1)^2). That factor is 1.005 at k=2, 1.131 at k=15 (+213 cents), 1.456 at k=31 (+650 cents) and 2.356 at k=63 (+1484 cents). MembraneMapper subtracts kUnityStretchNorm (membrane_mapper.h:136-138) so 1.0 is neutral there; the NoiseBody, Plate, Shell and Bell mappers do not. Audit probe modes:body=Plate:size=0.0 (probe-results.txt:314) measures the same drift on Plate at defaults: bank vs table +8.1 c at k2 and +56.6 c at k7.
