**Why wrong.** The NoiseBody partials should equal f0 * kPlateRatios[k], i.e. the (m+2n)^P law, when Stretch is at its physical default. The stiff-string law f_n = n f0 sqrt(1 + B n^2) describes bending stiffness in a STRING whose index n is the harmonic number. A plate's dispersion is already contained in its eigenvalue law (Chladni exponent p < 2 for cymbals, F&R 3.6 / 20.2), so applying a string-index stretch on top of the plate ordering has no physical basis. That is acceptable as a deliberate Unnatural-Zone effect, but not at the neutral setting.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments*, 2nd ed., 1998, Sec. 3.6 (circular plates) and 20.2 [textbook] <https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf>: plate modal frequencies are f_mn = c(m+2n)^p (p = 2 for flat plates, p < 2 for cymbals). The stiffness dispersion of a plate is expressed by this law, not by a string's sqrt(1+B n^2) on a sorted mode index.
- 2026-06 signal-path audit research entry on Stretch (Russell PSU; F&R; Young 1952), plugins/membrum/AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md section 3-B [docs]: prescribed widening B_max 0.001 -> 0.01 for STRING-like inharmonicity; it did not consider that the plate/noise mappers feed a non-zero stretch at the default.

**Consequence.** At the default, the upper half of the 'Chladni' cloud sits 0.5 to 1.2 octaves sharp of the table. That stretch pushes 38 of the 64 NoiseBody modes past Nyquist at 44.1 kHz for the default hat, so the table the code documents is not the spectrum users hear. Every Plate, Shell, Bell and NoiseBody pad in every factory kit that left Stretch at default carries this stretch.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: new, and partly caused by a prior fix. The 2026-06 audit (section 3-B, 'Stretch: index wrong, range tiny') moved the index to k+1 and widened B_max 0.001 -> 0.01 (fix/membrum-physics-stretch-modeinject-decayskew). The widening raised the never-neutral default B from 1.1e-4 (k=63 factor 1.21) to 1.1e-3 (factor 2.36), so the default deviation grew tenfold in B.

**Suggested fix.** In noise_body_mapper.h (and plate/shell/bell mappers), make 1.0 neutral. Either map stretch = clamp((modeStretch - 1.0) / 1.0, 0, 1) for the stretch side (values below 1.0 compress, or are ignored), or subtract kUnityStretchNorm as membrane_mapper.h:136-138 does. Regenerate goldens and re-check factory kits, since every default-stretch pad changes. Test: NoiseBody with PadConfig defaults at 96 kHz; getModeFrequency(k) / (f0 * kPlateRatios[k]) within 1 cent for k = 0..31. Extend test_noise_body.cpp 'plate ratios within +/-3%', which checks only k = 2 and 4 and therefore misses a 650-cent error at k = 31.

**Verifier notes.**
- Code confirmed: pad_config.h:212, pad_config_apply.h:123-126 ("1.0 = physical / Phase 1 bit-identity"), voice_common_params.h:23 ("default 1.0 (no stretch)"); noise_body_mapper.h:118-120, plate_mapper.h:60-62, shell_mapper.h:60-62 and bell_mapper.h:55-57 give stretchNorm 0.3333 at 1.0 without subtracting kUnityStretchNorm; modal_resonator_bank.h:783 and :806-807 apply the stretch, contradicting the bank's own "Membrum default-off get B==0" comment (:781-782). Hand-computed factors match. The 38-of-64-past-Nyquist count was not re-checked; some factory pads set modeStretch explicitly (default_kit.h:231, 348). Medium fits.
- Second lens could not refute: test_plate_body.cpp:135-137 sets modeStretch 0.5f to "neutralise the modeStretch warp", and preset-retune docs treat 0.333 as neutral (preset-retune/01-current-state.md:56, clave.md:50), so pads meant to be neutral get the warp. The physics argument holds (Chladni law, plate_modes.h:6-35).
- Third lens refutes the severity: AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md (~line 60, "Done — Phase-2 small physics batch") records the non-neutral default as an "Accepted consequence (user-approved)" of widening B_max, with the default golden re-blessed; membrane_mapper.h:138 also keeps a baseline material*0.3 stretch; plate_modes.h:29-33 calls the ratio table a perceptual fit; metallic kits were re-voiced against the current behaviour (prior audit hard gate, line 371). What remains is stale comment wording (pad_config_apply.h:123, voice_common_params.h:23): a nit at most.

#### MB-223 — Physics (oversimplified): Glide depth follows strike strength (energy ~ velocity^2) and the physical membrane parameters

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:tension-modulation

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:408-421, 86-94](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L408)

**Problem.** The comment at 408-419 says the modal energy 'already carries the velocity dependence (a harder strike injects more modal energy ~ velocity^2)'. The depth is knob * 3.3e-5 with no dependence on size, tension or the strike-level normalisation. Measured (knob 1, v 1, 44.1 kHz), same normalised strike peak (kBodyHeadroom). By size: 0.1 (f0 397 Hz) +0.05 st; 0.5 (158 Hz) +1.68; 0.8 (79 Hz) clamped +3.01; 1.0 (50 Hz) clamped for 20-100 ms. By exciter: Mallet +1.68, Impulse +1.64, FMImpulse +0.25, Clap +0.02, NoiseBurst 0.00. By velocity on default-kit pads: pad 11 tom v1 +0.36 / v0.5 +0.08 (about v^2), but pad 0 kick v1 +2.31 / v0.5 +2.05, and pad 5 floor tom v1 +0.80 / v0.5 +0.76, so almost no velocity dependence.

**Why wrong.** From MAB Eq. 20, the relative tension rise is Tqs/T0 = Eh E / (2R^2 (1-nu^2) T0^2). It grows with vibration energy, which for a given drum is the strike strength squared, and with lower tension and smaller radius for the same energy. Glides should scale with strike strength (Kirby & Sandler: higher strike velocities give a wider chirp). The driving energy should be the energy of the vibration as heard, i.e. measured after the strike-level normalisation, not the raw pre-normalisation state, which depends on the exciter. The plugin should also map size/tension explicitly: larger and looser heads glide more for the same loudness.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Marogna, Avanzini, Bank, 'Energy based synthesis of tension modulation in membranes', DAFx-10 [paper] <https://people.ece.cornell.edu/land/courses/ece5760/LABS/s2016/MarognaAvanziniBank_tension_modulation.pdf>: Eq. 20: Tqs = Eh / (2R^2 (1-nu^2) T0) * E(t). The scale depends on Young's modulus, thickness, radius and rest tension. Simulations use impact velocities of 5 m/s and 20 m/s (20 m/s close to the highest dynamic levels, citing Dahl 2004).
- Kirby & Sandler, 'Advanced Fourier decomposition for realistic drum synthesis', DAFx-20 [paper] <https://dafx2020.mdw.ac.at/proceedings/papers/DAFx2020_paper_66.pdf>: Fig. 6 caption: 'Higher strike velocities have more peaks and troughs, and a larger chirp width', i.e. a larger glide on the measured toms.

**Consequence.** Equally loud hits get 0 to 3 st of glide depending on the exciter type and the size knob, not on how hard the pad is played. Brush-like (NoiseBurst) and clap strikes never glide. On the kick and the floor toms the glide barely changes with velocity, so ghost notes and accents glide the same, which flattens dynamics: 'velocity -> timbre mapping' loses its most characteristic membrane cue. Small pads (size < 0.3) get no audible glide at any knob setting, and large pads hit the ceiling.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research[6] said 'energy ~ velocity^2 ... depth ~ velocity^2 is physically sound' for the OLD output-energy driver. The N-1 rework changed the driver to the pre-normalisation modal energy, which introduced the exciter, size and velocity-collapse dependence measured here. The old verdict no longer applies.

**Suggested fix.** Use as driver E_norm = getModalEnergy() * outputGain^2 (the energy at the normalised strike level) divided by a per-note reference energy for a full-velocity strike. pitchMod is then f(knob * v_eff^2-like energy ratio) and is identical across exciters at the same loudness. Add an explicit size/tension term following MAB Eq. 20 (depth proportional to 1/T0^2 ~ 1/f0^4 at fixed R, or a documented perceptual curve). Tests: (a) for each of the 7 exciters at the same normalised peak, the glide at knob 1, v 1 lies within +/-30 % of the Mallet value. (b) For pads 0, 5 and 11, glide(v=0.5)/glide(v=1) is in [0.15, 0.40].

**Verifier notes.**
- Could not refute: depth is `clamp(tensionModAmt_,0,1) * kTensionEnergyScale` (3.3e-5) with no size, tension or strike-level term (drum_voice.h:420-421, 94); glide = `min(1 + amt*energyEnv_, 1.19)`, Membrane only (:724-728, 948-949); energyEnv_ follows `getModalEnergy()` (:912-914, 1075-1077), which is invariant to outputGain_ (modal_resonator_bank.h:486-499), while the heard level is set by `measuredStrikeOutputGain` (:84, 302-304). The comment at 408-419 claiming ~velocity^2 is not enforced. Per-size/exciter numbers not re-run but consistent with the code. Medium fits.
- Second lens (read both PDFs): the papers support only "glide grows with strike energy", which the plugin already does; test_per_mode_damping.cpp:481-528 checks glide rises with velocity. MAB Eq. 19-20 drive the glide from physical membrane energy, not heard loudness, so less glide for a brush/noise strike is consistent with the physics. Eq. 20 also contradicts the size claim: at equal energy a LARGER radius gives LESS relative tension rise (1/R^2), and Membrum's Size is size (f0 = 500*0.1^size, default_kit.h:452), so the proposed 1/f0^4 law misapplies the source. Kirby & Sandler's caption is quoted correctly.
- Third lens could not refute: the strike-normalisation probe uses the configured exciter at velocity 1 with a cache keyed on exciter type and size (drum_voice.h:1322-1362, 1394-1411), so equal heard loudness gives exciter- and size-dependent glide; no document says that is intended (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:122). The kick's velocity collapse has a mechanism: Impulse at size 0.8 (default_kit.h:47-50, 84), amplitude v^0.6 (impact_exciter.h:129) and lower hardness at low velocity (impulse_exciter.h:37). Re-running the diagnostic "N-1 tension: glide in semitones vs velocity" (tests/unit/diagnose/test_body_resonant_peak.cpp:185; Mallet, size 0.5, knob 1) gave v0.3 0.164 st, v0.5 0.430, v0.7 0.982, v1.0 1.895 (about v^2 for the Mallet tom).

#### MB-230 — Physics (unsupported): The noise and click layers are calibrated as ~-18 dBFS accents ~12 dB under the -6 dBFS body, a realistic body-to-noise balance

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-unsupported · **Dimension:** research:click-noise-layers

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h:220-228, 264-276, 303-310, 312-321](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h#L220); [click_layer.h:150-157, 166-173](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/click_layer.h#L150); [tests/unit/dsp/gain_staging_balance_test.cpp:46, 73, 115](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/dsp/gain_staging_balance_test.cpp#L46)

**Problem.** NoiseLayer::kStandaloneOutputGain = 0.243 ('~-18 dBFS @ fcRef', noise_layer.h:321). standaloneGain = 0.243*clamp(sqrt(fcRef/fc), 0.25, 4) with fcRef = 849 Hz (264-276), which is the WHITE-noise bandwidth law, applied whatever the colour. ClickLayer::kStandaloneOutputGain = 0.445 ('~-18 dBFS', click_layer.h:157), with no compensation for the bandpass centre (200-12000 Hz, constant Q 0.8). The calibration test checks only pink noise (color 0.5) and click brightness 0.5 (gain_staging_balance_test.cpp:46, 73, 115). MEASURED (layer_probe, mix 1, 16 seeds): at the calibration cutoff 0.5, noise peaks are brown -22.0, pink -17.9, white -20.9, violet -45.3 dBFS (27 dB spread). At cutoff 0.88: brown -31.7, pink -24.6, white -20.5, violet -27.4. Default-kit layer peaks at v=1: noise snare -8.0, clap -17.6, cymbal -17.7, tom -23.1, kick -24.3, perc -28.4, hat -30.5 dBFS; click tom -14.8, hat -17.3, perc -18.5, snare -20.1, kick -29.4, cymbal -30.8, clap -31.2 dBFS. In the voice (voice_probe, v=1) the noise-to-body RMS (0-50 ms) is kick -14.6, snare -5.8, floor tom -16.4, closed hat -24.9 dB.

**Why wrong.** No source gives a normative body-to-noise ratio for drums, and the code cites none for the '-18 dBFS / 6-12 dB under the body' rule. It is a gain-staging design choice from audit H-2. The physics points the other way for the snare: the snare sound is defined by the wires ('a totally different sound' without them, Rossing 1992), and the default kit already overrides the rule with noiseLayerGain 6.2 (noise 2 dB under the body peak). Measured stick contact pulses carry almost all their energy below 1 kHz (Wagner App. A; sin^2 reference). A click peaking at or above the noise layer at 5-10 kHz centroid (tom -14.8 dBFS) has no physical counterpart. Independently of physics, the calibration holds only at its test point. Constant-bandwidth compensation sqrt(fcRef/fc) is right for white noise only: violet energy below fc grows as fc^3 and brown energy is nearly cutoff-independent. A constant-Q bandpass passes white-noise power proportional to fc, so the click peak rises as sqrt(fc), which the code does not compensate.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- T.D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40, 1992 [paper] <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>: the snare head vibrates against the snares, and removing them gives 'a totally different sound'. The wire component is constitutive of the snare's sound, not a -12 dB accent.
- A. Wagner, 'Analysis of drumbeats', MSc thesis, KTH 2006 [thesis] <https://www.speech.kth.se/publications/masterprojects/2006/AndreasWagner.pdf>: contact force = sin^2 pulse (sinc-like spectrum from DC) plus stick modes at 0.4-2.8 kHz. The attack amplitude rise is proportional to the measured force increase.

**Consequence.** The Color knob doubles as an up-to-27 dB level knob: violet at mid cutoff almost vanishes, and brown at high cutoff loses ~14 dB. A colour sweep is mostly heard as a level change, which makes Color a weak parameter for timbre. The documented -18 dBFS budget is met by only some pads: the hat's parallel layer sits 25 dB under its body, the snare's 6 dB. On the tom the bright click (-14.8 dBFS, 7.8 kHz centroid) is louder than its noise layer and is the hottest non-body element. These numbers come from per-preset hand-tuning, not from the stated calibration, so future preset edits that change colour or brightness silently move layer levels by tens of dB.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: H-2 (2026-06) ruled the layers ~17 dB too loud vs the body. It was fixed in b4c63577 by recalibrating to ~-18 dBFS at ONE point (pink, cutoff 0.5 / click brightness 0.5). Fix C later added the white-noise sqrt(fc) cutoff correction. The colour and click-brightness dependence was never calibrated, and the default kit compensates by hand (noiseLayerGain 6.2 / 3.5 / 2.2). So H-2's intent is only partly met, and this deviation is new.

**Suggested fix.** Compute standaloneGain from the analytic band energy of the selected colour through the selected filter: integrate S_colour(f)*|H_LP(f; fc, Q)|^2 and set gain = target / sqrt(energy) at configure() time, which is control rate. A small precomputed table over (colour, cutoff, Q) is enough. Give the click gain *= sqrt(fcRef/fcBrightness) with the same target. Document that the -18 dBFS target is a design choice, not a physical ratio. Extend gain_staging_balance_test with a colour {0, 0.4, 0.7, 0.95} x cutoff {0.1, 0.5, 0.88} grid and a click brightness {0.1, 0.5, 0.9} grid, each asserting -18 ±3 dBFS.

**Verifier notes.**
- Code lens: nothing misread. noise_layer.h:321 (0.243f), :264-276 (colour-independent sqrt law, fcRef ~849 Hz; doc comment at 220-228 calls it a white-noise rule), :303-310 (colour mapping never read by computeStandaloneGain, called at :87, :109); click_layer.h:157 constant 0.445f with no brightness compensation (:166-173); gains applied at drum_voice.h:532/789/1027/1347 and 548-549/861/1050-1051; the test covers only colour 0.5 and brightness 0.5 (gain_staging_balance_test.cpp:46, 73, 115); default_kit.h:120, 262, 336 override by hand. Probe not re-run, but the colour/brightness dependence follows from source. Medium fits.
- Second lens confirms the engineering defect, not the physics framing. Analytic check: violet = 0.5*(w[n]-w[n-1]) (noise_oscillator.h:341-350) sits ~25 dB under white below 849 Hz at 48 kHz, matching the measured 24 dB gap; brown is a leaky integrator (:317-323), so the sqrt law over-attenuates it at high cutoffs. The code never claims a physical ratio (noise_layer.h:312-319, click_layer.h:151-156), so the Rossing and Wagner citations carry no weight (not opened).
- Third lens refutes it as a physics deviation: the -18 dBFS target is a documented gain-staging target (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:377-403, row 401; line 21 records H-2 fix b4c63577; gain_staging_balance_test.cpp:1-13). The snare case is handled by design via per-pad noiseLayerGain (pad_config.h:261; default_kit.h:96-97, 112-120; wire coupling cited to Bilbao 2012 at :121-124). ClickLayer is a bandpassed-noise transient, not a contact-force model, so Wagner is not a standard it deviates from. What remains is the engineering point (white-noise law, single-point calibration); the 27 dB spread was not reproduced.

#### MB-231 — Physics (oversimplified): Head-to-shell coupling is feedforward only (body drives shell, shell is summed into the output, nothing returns to the head)

**Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:coupling-models

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:380-406, 802-846, 979-1044, 1486-1497](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L380)

**Problem.** At noteOn, if secondaryEnabled_ >= 0.5 and couplingStrength_ > 0, the code calls configureSecondaryBank(), sets the shell output gain to measuredStrikeOutputGain (audit N-1, 397-404) and sets effectiveCoupling_ = clamp(couplingStrength_, 0, 1) (1494-1497; the old 0.25 ceiling is gone). Fast path, 816-843: secExc[i] = bodyScratch[i] * effectiveCoupling_, then secondaryBank_.processBlock, then bodyScratch[i] += secOut[i]. Slow path, 1039-1044: lastShell = secondaryBank_.processSampleNoSmooth(bodyOut * effectiveCoupling_) and bodyWithShell += lastShell. No term returns shell energy to the head (comment 825-841, 1454-1462). The head's modes, frequencies and decay are identical with and without the shell. The comment at 805-808 says the coupling reads the previous block's output; the code uses the current chunk's bodyScratch, so that comment is stale.

**Why wrong.** In a two-headed drum the heads couple 'acoustically through the enclosed air or mechanically through the shell', and this 'leads to the formation of mode pairs' (Rossing 1992). Fletcher & Rossing model the (01) pair as a two-mass oscillator with f1 = f0 and f2 = sqrt(f0^2 + 2 fc^2). Measured values: in a 36 cm side drum the (01) mode splits into 182 and 330 Hz and the (11) into 278 and 341 Hz (F&R Table 18.6). In a bass drum with equal head tensions the (01) pair is 44 and 104 Hz and the (11) pair 76 and 82 Hz, with fc = 67 Hz (F&R §18.9). The dominant partner of the batter head is the resonant head through the air spring, not the shell. A reciprocal coupling that is passive (energy-conserving) is stable at any strength (Torin, Hamilton & Bilbao 2014 prove stability from the energy balance of the coupled membranes, air and snares). Removing the return path is not required for stability.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments*, 2nd ed., §18.9 (bass drum), §18.10 Table 18.6 (side drum), 1998 [textbook] <https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf>: coupling between the two heads gives a doublet in the lowest modes. Bass drum (01) pair at 44 and 104 Hz, (11) pair at 76 and 82 Hz. Two-mass oscillator f1 = f0, f2 = sqrt(f0^2 + 2 fc^2), fc = 67 Hz. Side drum: the 'Drum' column gives (01) at 182 and 330 Hz, (11) at 278 and 341 Hz, against 227 Hz for the batter head alone.
- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, March 1992 [paper] <https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf>: in a two-headed drum there is appreciable coupling between the heads, acoustically through the enclosed air or mechanically through the shell, which leads to the formation of mode pairs. In a snare drum: (0,1) at 183 Hz with the heads in phase; (1,1) pair at 275 Hz (antiphase, air sloshes) and 344 Hz.
- Torin, Hamilton & Bilbao, 'An energy conserving finite difference scheme for the simulation of collisions in snare drums', DAFx-14, 2014 [paper] <https://www.pure.ed.ac.uk/ws/files/17485699/dafx14_submission_56_3.pdf>: batter and carry membranes are coupled through the enclosed air. Energy is conserved by construction, otherwise it is monotonically dissipated, and stability follows from the energy terms being positive. Passive bidirectional coupling is stable.

**Consequence.** The model cannot produce the mode-pair doublets or the slow beating between head and partner, and it cannot shorten the head's decay by draining energy into the partner. Changing secondarySize, secondaryMaterial or couplingStrength only adds a short independent ringing layer on top of an unchanged head. Every coupled pad therefore keeps the same head character plus a generic thud, which pushes kits toward sounding alike. The shell stage is enabled on many factory pads (tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:521-522, 594-595, 680-681 and others).

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research[5]: oversimplified (strong), because real head-shell-air coupling is bidirectional with mode splitting and beating, and stability requires passivity rather than deleting the return path. Code changes since then: the 0.25 coupling cap was removed (1494-1497), the slow path now runs the shell (audit M-6, 1004-1044), and the shell is level-normalised (N-1, 397-404). The feedforward topology is unchanged, so the verdict still applies.

**Suggested fix.** Model the partner (the resonant head, optionally the shell) as a passive two-mass system per low mode pair and diagonalise it at noteOn. The normal modes f1 = f0 and f2 = sqrt(f0^2 + 2 fc^2) (F&R) go into the existing ModalResonatorBank, with each mode's amplitude taken from the strike projection, so the result is unconditionally stable and costs nothing extra per sample. Map fc to couplingStrength. Test: strike a Membrane pad at f0 = 200 Hz with coupling enabled. The (01) band FFT must show two peaks, at f0 and sqrt(f0^2 + 2 fc^2), each within 1 %. With fc small (fc << f0), the band envelope must show beating at |f2 - f1|. Fix the stale comment at 805-808.

**Verifier notes.**
- Topology confirmed (drum_voice.h:391-406, 816-843, 1039-1044, 1494-1497); configureSecondaryBank (1418-1484) builds a separate 24-mode shell bank and never changes the head's modes. No other stage makes doublets: Air Loading only scales each Bessel frequency (membrane_mapper.h:101-107, membrane_modes.h:75-98). The stale comment at 805-808 is real (line 817 reads the current chunk's bodyScratch, written at 799). The passivity justification at 836-838 does not support one-way coupling. Medium fits.
- Second lens: the cited doublets come from HEAD-to-HEAD coupling through the enclosed air, which the finding itself concedes; H. Zhao, "Acoustics of snare drums" (NIU 1990, huskiecommons.lib.niu.edu/allgraduate-thesesdissertations/974/) says head interaction is "mainly caused by acoustical coupling through the air enclosure rather than by mechanical coupling through the drum shell". Head-to-shell coupling is the weak path, where dropping the back-reaction is a standard first-order approximation; mapping f2 = sqrt(f0^2 + 2fc^2) onto a shell knob would model a resonant head Membrum does not have, so the finding is a request for a missing component. Torin et al. show two-way passive coupling CAN be stable, not that one-way weak coupling is wrong.
- Third lens: the deviation is real and not an accepted simplification. Secondary f0 is head f0 * (1 - 0.75*secondarySize) (drum_voice.h:1421-1426), so an upper doublet partner cannot come from this stage. The loop-gain rationale (825-841, 1454-1462) applies to active injection, not passive reciprocal coupling. AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:332 (section 3-C) rules it "OVERSIMPLIFIED, strong" and the tracker (lines 41-52, 204-205) closes only L-7, L-8, M-6 and L-9, so this repeats an open prior ruling. User docs still describe bidirectional coupling with a 0.25 clamp (MANUAL.md:252, docs/index.html:78).

### Low (134)

#### MB-007 — After the DrumVoice swap, FMOperator's wavetable pointer refers to the other voice slot's storage (latent use of a dead object)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** rt-safety · **Dimension:** rt-safety · **Also flagged by:** exciters, shared-dsp-contracts

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/fm_operator.h:89-92, 113, 350-351](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/fm_operator.h#L89)

**Problem.** FMOperator is copy- and move-defaulted, but osc_ stores a raw pointer to its own sineTable_ (osc_.setWavetable(&sineTable_); WavetableOscillator::table_, wavetable_oscillator.h:96-97, 289). When VoicePool swaps a DrumVoice holding an FMImpulseExciter into the shadow slot (voice_pool.cpp:922), the moved operators keep pointing at the ORIGINAL slot's sineTable_. That storage is then re-emplaced with another exciter alternative for the next note. The shadow, and later that same voice re-hit without a type swap (no prepare), read the wavetable through a pointer into another object's variant storage.

**Why wrong.** Reading through a pointer into storage whose object lifetime has ended is undefined behaviour. A type with a self-referential pointer must define move operations that re-point it, or must not be movable.

**Consequence.** Inaudible today: the stale table bytes survive because the smaller alternatives do not overwrite that region, and the sine table is identical across voices. It becomes garbage reads or an out-of-bounds read (numLevels_ / getLevel) as soon as a layout changes or a larger alternative overwrites the region. The same pattern affects any other self-pointer in a moved voice.

**Evidence.** fm_operator.h:91-92 `FMOperator(FMOperator&&) noexcept = default; FMOperator& operator=(FMOperator&&) noexcept = default;` and :113 `osc_.setWavetable(&sineTable_);`. PROBE probe2.cpp (scratchpad rtprobe) swapped an FMImpulse voice into the shadow and re-hit it after the main slot took Impulse / NoiseBurst / Friction / Clap. Max |diff| against an unswapped twin was 0 in all cases, so this is latent, not audible today.

**Suggested fix.** Give FMOperator user-defined copy / move operations that call osc_.setWavetable(&sineTable_) after the member copy. Alternatively remove the voice move altogether (see the swap finding). Test: move-construct a prepared FMOperator, destroy or overwrite the source, and assert the moved operator's output equals a fresh one.

**Verifier notes.**
- Confirmed from source: FMOperator holds a ~90 KB WavetableData inline (fm_operator.h:350; core/wavetable_data.h:102-104) and the oscillator keeps a raw `const WavetableData* table_` read every sample (wavetable_oscillator.h:96-97, 154, 250, 253, 289); FMImpulseExciter (fm_impulse_exciter.h:149-150) lives in ExciterBank's variant (exciter_bank.h:182-189, 254), moved by `std::swap` at voice_pool.cpp:922. Nothing re-points after the swap (beginFastRelease :937, trigger :70-71; prepare only on type change, exciter_bank.h:55-56, 235). UB, inaudible today; out-of-bounds risk real but hypothetical.
- Second lens: one part of the claim is wrong. FMImpulse is only ever emplaced and prepared in the main slot, so a later re-hit back in the main slot points at its own sineTable_ again; only the shadow's 5 ms fade window reads dead storage. No guard, comment (voice_pool.cpp:895-918) or test covers self-pointers. Keep low: the fade damps within ~1 ms (voice_pool.cpp:937) behind the hardClip rail.
- Third lens could not refute: real UB, Low is right. The "re-hit without prepare" case repairs itself via the next swap; out-of-bounds via numLevels_ would need an alternative larger than ~90 KB, and the operators run near 1500 Hz (fm_impulse_exciter.h:7-8), selecting mip levels above the overwritten level-0 region.

#### MB-011 — Membrane strike-position amplitudes are wrong above strikePos ~0.93: the 20-term Bessel series is truncated, not merely imprecise in float

**Severity:** low (filed as medium) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-body-model · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Corroborated by research:** yes (see below)

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:120-160](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h#L120) (used at [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:112-118](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L112))

**Problem.** evaluateBesselJ sums 21 terms of the J_m power series. The mapper evaluates it at x = j_mn * 0.9 * strikePos, up to 0.9 * 19.616 = 17.65. At |x| ~ 17 the series terms grow to about 1e6 before converging, and term 20 is still large, so the result is dominated by truncation. A double-precision 21-term sum is equally wrong. The header claims accuracy 'under 1%' for arguments up to ~17.6.

**Why wrong.** Mode amplitudes must be |J_m(j_mn r/a)| (FR-035). With a truncated series, high modes get large spurious amplitudes, and one of them can become the loudest partial of the drum.

**Consequence.** Turning Strike Position toward the rim on a Membrane pad (strikePos > ~0.93) suddenly boosts the 8.16 x f0 partial (mode 46) to the strongest mode: +7 dB above the true loudest mode, 3x its true amplitude. That is a timbre jump at the top of the knob instead of the physical rim sound.

**Evidence.** Measured with a node probe (scratchpad bessel_probe.js) that reproduces the float code with Math.fround, against a converged 120-term double reference. strikePos 0.9: worst error 0.0030. 0.95: worst error 0.0447 (mode 46). 1.0: mode 46 (m=1, x=17.654) plugin 0.533, 21-term double 0.529, truth 0.176; mode 44 (m=3, x=17.47) plugin 0.251, truth 0.181. The loudest true amplitude at 1.0 is 0.236, so the plugin's loudest mode (0.533) is spurious. Code: `constexpr int kMaxTerms = 20; for (int k = 1; k <= kMaxTerms; ++k) { term *= -halfXSq / (k * (m + k)); result += term; }` (:152-157).

Corroborated by research — Physics (contradicted): evaluateBesselJ (20-term power series in float) stays under 1 % error for strike arguments up to j_mn*0.9 ~ 17.6. For x up to 17.7 the power series needs about 35-40 terms in double (it peaks near k ~ x/2 at ~6e5 and then decays); alternatively Miller backward recurrence, Hankel asymptotics for x > ~12, or a table over strikePos for the 48 fixed j_mn (exact values at strikePos 1.0, e.g. (1,6) 0.176, (0,6) 0.192). Sources (evidence quality strong): measurement membrane_probe.js (float emulation vs a 200-term double series): worst |J| error 0.357 at strikePos 1.0 (mode 46, m=1, x=17.654: 0.533 vs 0.176), 4 modes above 0.01 and 1 above 0.1, error first exceeds 0.01 at strikePos 0.91, and a 20-term double series also gives 0.529, so the error is truncation; M. Abramowitz, I. Stegun, *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*, 1964, eq. 9.1.10 and section 9.12 [textbook]: the ascending series converges for all x but needs terms well past k ~ x/2; backward recurrence is the standard stable method for large x.

**Suggested fix.** Evaluate J_m in double with enough terms to converge (about 40 at x <= 18), or switch to a stable method: Miller backward recurrence, or a precomputed table over (mode, strikePos). Test: for every mode k and strikePos in {0.3, 0.75, 0.95, 1.0}, compare evaluateBesselJ against a high-precision reference within 1e-3 absolute.

**Verifier notes.**
- Real, but starts higher on the knob than claimed. Only caller is membrane_mapper.h:112-118; strikePos is unclamped (drum_voice.h:1119-1124, voice_common_params.h:19). Own probe (bj.js, bj2.js) reproduced 0.533 / 0.529 / 0.176 at 1.0 (+7.09 dB); scanning 0.94-1.0, the loudest mode stays correct up to 0.985 and mode 46 first becomes the spurious loudest only at 0.990 (+1.39 dB), 0.995 (+4.98 dB), 1.0 (+7.09 dB). Recommends a downgrade.
- Second lens confirmed (150-term reference): 0.8 → 0.0007, 0.9 → 0.0019, 0.95 → 0.0447 (loudest still correct), 1.0 → 0.357. No test samples strikePos above 0.85 on the Membrane body (test_membrane_body.cpp:263); the prior audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:326) covered only the Shell mode shape; normalisation to kBodyHeadroom does not fix the inter-mode balance. Held medium.
- Third lens (quadrature reference, bes.js): the spurious-loudest consequence appears only at strikePos >= ~0.99; mode 46 is high and damped quickly by the b3 term (modal_resonator_bank.h:134-138); no factory or default content reaches the range (default_kit.h 0.30-0.32; generator max 0.70 at :1154). No test references evaluateBesselJ. Downgrade to low.

#### MB-013 — Default filter cutoff relies on pow(1000, 1.0) landing exactly on 20000 Hz to bypass the tone-shaper SVF; the macOS fast-math rewrite gives 19999.998

**Severity:** low (filed as medium) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** portability · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config_apply.h:83-84](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config_apply.h#L83) (gate at [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:427-429 and 467-474](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h#L427))

**Problem.** The cutoff is denormalised as 20 * pow(1000, n), and the filter is skipped only when `filterCutoffHz_ >= 20000.0f && filterEnvAmount_ == 0.0f`. Every PadConfig defaults to tsFilterCutoff = 1.0 (pad_config.h:197). Under -ffast-math, clang may rewrite pow(const, x) as exp2(x * log2(const)): exp2f(9.965784f) = 999.99988, times 20 = 19999.998 < 20000. The bypass is then lost for every default pad.

**Why wrong.** Root CLAUDE.md fast-math rule: a value that must be exact at an endpoint (normalized 0 / 1) must be produced by a branch or a clamp, never by arithmetic that only happens to land on the edge in IEEE.

**Consequence.** On macOS (Xcode builds with -ffast-math), every voice runs the SVF lowpass at its 0.495*sr clamp plus the filter envelope, per sample. That costs CPU and attenuates the top octave (about -2 dB at 20 kHz at 44.1 kHz). The Phase-1 default-patch golden and other cross-platform renders diverge from Windows and Linux.

**Evidence.** node with Math.fround: log2f(1000) = 9.965784072875977, exp2f(...) = 999.9998779296875, x20 = 19999.998046875, `>= 20000` false. Code: `v.toneShaper().setFilterCutoff(20.0f * std::pow(1000.0f, std::clamp(cfg.tsFilterCutoff, 0.0f, 1.0f)));` (pad_config_apply.h:83-84); `const bool filterBypass = (filterCutoffHz_ >= 20000.0f) && (filterEnvAmount_ == 0.0f);` (tone_shaper.h:427-428). Not reproduced on a Mac; derived from the documented clang pow -> exp2 transform.

**Suggested fix.** Branch at the endpoint: `const float n = clamp(cfg.tsFilterCutoff, 0, 1); hz = (n >= 1.0f) ? 20000.0f : 20.0f * std::pow(1000.0f, n);`. Or compare the normalized value against 1.0 in the bypass test. Run tools/macos-fastmath-repro.sh or tools/clangcl-fastmath-build.ps1 on a test that asserts ToneShaper::isBypassed() for a default PadConfig.

**Verifier notes.**
- Mechanism confirmed from source (pad_config.h:197, 199; pad_config_apply.h:83-84, 86 gives env amount exactly 0; tone_shaper.h:151-156, 427-429, 467-474); LLVM's `replacePowWithExp` folds pow under afn, and plugins/membrum/CMakeLists.txt:85-109 confirms global fast-math (only membrum_float_guard opts out). No test covers the path (test_tone_shaper_bypass.cpp:65 uses a literal 20000). Audible claim overstated: the SVF cap is 0.495*fs (svf.h:129/691) and the attenuation at 20 kHz is negligible. Downgrade to low.
- Second lens confirmed with a clang probe (scratchpad powprobe/probe.cpp, `-O2 -ffast-math -ffp-contract=fast`): IR shows `@llvm.exp2.f32`; fast-math prints `19999.998 bypass=0`, IEEE prints `20000 bypass=1`; any exp2f within 1 ulp lands below 1000. Only cutoff site in src; macro_mapper.cpp:151 only clamp01s. The Phase-1 golden (test_phase1_regression.cpp:154-183) uses a -90 dBFS RMS tolerance and WARN+SUCCEEDs on a missing file.
- Third lens reproduced it with WSL clang++-18 (powt.cpp). Consequence overstated: the SVF does not run at its clamp but at 19999.998 Hz; a prewarped Butterworth at 20 kHz cuts ~3 dB at 20 kHz, 0.26 dB at 18 kHz, 0.02 dB at 15 kHz; the Phase-1 golden renders a bare DrumVoice that never calls applyPadConfigToVoice (test_phase1_regression.cpp:51-73; member default 20000.0f at tone_shaper.h:489). Remaining defect: a CLAUDE.md fast-math endpoint breach costing macOS CPU and small cross-platform divergence. Recommends a downgrade.

#### MB-015 — Coupling energy limiter uses hard-coded per-sample coefficients, so its release time depends on the sample rate

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** dsp-numerics · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics · **Also flagged by:** gain-staging-master, coupling

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.h:183-196](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.h#L183)

**Problem.** applyEnergyLimiter uses kAttackCoeff = 0.001 and kReleaseCoeff = 0.9999 per sample, regardless of sampleRate_. The release tau is 10000 samples: 227 ms at 44.1 kHz and 52 ms at 192 kHz. The NaN latch of the same function is covered in the NaN-barrier finding.

**Why wrong.** Envelope time constants must be derived from seconds and the current sample rate. Every other follower in the plugin does this, for example energyAlpha_ = exp(-1/(0.02*sr)).

**Consequence.** The coupling (sympathetic resonance) return pumps differently at different host rates: at 96 and 192 kHz the limiter releases 2-4x faster, so the coupling bloom is louder and less controlled than at 44.1 kHz.

**Evidence.** `constexpr float kAttackCoeff = 0.001f; constexpr float kReleaseCoeff = 0.9999f; ... energyEnvelope_ += (1.0f - coeff) * (absVal - energyEnvelope_);` (processor.h:186-190). tau = 1 / (1 - 0.9999) = 10000 samples.

**Suggested fix.** Compute the attack and release coefficients in setupProcessing from times in ms (attack ~0.02 ms, release ~230 ms). Test: drive applyEnergyLimiter with a step at 44.1 and 192 kHz and assert the release time in ms matches within 5 %.

**Verifier notes.**
- Holds: the only caller runs it once per sample in the coupling loop (processor.cpp:698-707), so release tau is fixed at 10000 samples (227 / 104 / 52 ms at 44.1 / 96 / 192 kHz), while the same loop converts the delay from ms (processor.cpp:696) and drum_voice.h:130-133 derives its follower from seconds. Attack is effectively instant at any rate; only release depends on the rate. Low is appropriate.
- Second lens: resets at processor.cpp:967 and 1084 only zero energyEnvelope_. specs/140 FR-040 / SC-007 (spec.md:227, :273) require only a -20 dBFS cap; research.md:68-72 (R5) describes the design in time units ("RMS over a short window (~2ms)"); plan.md:170 gives no time rationale. No prior-audit ruling. Low stays.
- Third lens: test_coupling_fuzz.cpp:59-63 mirrors the limiter and asserts nothing about time constants. Correction to the consequence: the -20 dBFS peak cap holds equally at every rate; release changes only inter-peak ripple (about 0.2 dB vs 0.8 dB gain wobble on 100 Hz at 44.1 vs 192 kHz) and how long gain reduction persists after a burst (227 vs 52 ms). 44.1 vs 48 kHz differs by only 8 %.

#### MB-016 — VoicePool clamps the sample rate to [22050, 192000] while the rest of the processor runs at the host rate

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** dsp-numerics · **Dimension:** dsp-numerics

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:52-58](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L52)

**Problem.** VoicePool::prepare does `sampleRate = std::clamp(sampleRate, 22050.0, 192000.0)` and prepares all 32 DrumVoices at the clamped rate. The processor's limiter, coupling delay and coupling engine use the real sampleRate_. Nothing rejects or flags the unsupported rate.

**Why wrong.** A voice prepared at one rate and rendered at another gives every pitch and time constant off by the ratio. Either reject the unsupported rate or run every component at the same rate.

**Consequence.** At 352.8 or 384 kHz every pad plays an octave (or more) low, with decays and envelopes about 2x long. At 8, 11 or 16 kHz everything is too high. Coupling resonators are then tuned to wrong partial frequencies relative to the main-bus rate.

**Evidence.** `sampleRate  = std::clamp(sampleRate, 22050.0, 192000.0); sampleRate_ = sampleRate;` (voice_pool.cpp:57-58), while processor.cpp setupProcessing prepares couplingDelay_ and busLimiter_ with the unclamped sampleRate_ (processor.cpp:1082-1087).

**Suggested fix.** Remove the clamp and support the host rate, or refuse it consistently (setupProcessing returns kResultFalse outside the range) so no component is misprepared. Test: prepare at 384 kHz, render the default kick, and check f0 against 44.1 kHz.

**Verifier notes.**
- Traced: voice_pool.cpp:109-110 prepares both voice arrays at the clamped rate; DrumVoice::prepare (drum_voice.h:119-150) passes it to every rate-dependent part; setupProcessing (processor.cpp:1067-1091) stores the unclamped rate and uses it for couplingEngine_ (:1081), couplingDelay_ (:1082), busLimiter_ (:1087), the delay time (:696) and CPU budget (:806-812), with no kResultFalse branch; setActive (:1097) does the same. Low because such rates are rare.
- Second lens: the fast-release coefficient also uses the clamped rate (:86). specs/138-membrum-phase3-polyphony/contracts/voicepool_api.md:19 states `sampleRate ∈ [22050, 192000]` as a caller PRE-CONDITION ("implementation clamps if outside") that the processor never enforces; tests (membrum_processor_tests.cpp:1040/1084) cover only 22050..192000; CHANGELOG.md:697 mentions only the tested range.
- Third lens: at 352.8 / 384 kHz pitches drop 1.84x / 2x (about -10.6 / -12 semitones); at 16 kHz pitch rises 1.38x (+5.6 semitones). The clamp also defeats the voice's own Nyquist guard. Low stands (e.g. Reaper or Pyramix DXD rates), but when it triggers it is a gross whole-instrument detune.

#### MB-022 — ImpactExciter stops running its SVF the instant the pulse ends, cutting the filter's response mid-swing: soft Mallet hits on small bodies inject a step of up to 50% of their peak

**Severity:** low (filed as medium) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** exciter · **Dimension:** exciters

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/impact_exciter.h:229-230, 255-258, 284-285](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/impact_exciter.h#L229)

**Problem.** process() returns 0.0 as soon as !pulseActive_ && !bounceActive_ (line 229-230), so the SVF lowpass (line 285) is no longer evaluated. When the low-cutoff filter lags a short pulse (Mallet with a small size hint: T of about 1.5-3.5 ms with cutoff of about 600-900 Hz), its output is still large at the last pulse sample, and the next sample is a hard 0.

**Why wrong.** A filter's state must decay naturally: the excitation should end with the filter's own ring-down, not a truncation. The step is a broadband discontinuity, which a modal bank turns into a click on every mode. That is the opposite of the soft, rounded hit the Mallet exists for (mallet_exciter.h:6-8, US1-2).

**Consequence.** Soft Mallet hits on crotale, glockenspiel and small-bell pads get an HF click. The Mallet spectral centroid even rises at the lowest velocity (382 Hz at v0.1 vs 278 Hz at v0.2), which breaks the velocity-to-brightness order. ImpactExciter is shared with Innexus (any fix changes its output).

**Evidence.** probe.cpp (44.1 kHz): 'Mallet hint 0.1 v 0.1: peak 0.2531 lastNz@79 (1.79 ms) lastVal +0.12666 ratio 0.500'; 'hint 0.1 v 0.3 ... ratio 0.153'; 'hint 0.2 v 0.1 ... ratio 0.178'; 'Mallet hint 1.0 v 0.1 ... ratio 0.042'. Mallet centroid by velocity: 382 / 278 / 289 / 453 Hz at v 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5.

**Suggested fix.** Keep running the SVF (and comb) with zero input until its output falls below about 1e-6, and only then return 0 / report inactive. Alternatively gate on |svf state|. Test: for Mallet hint 0.1, v 0.1, the |last non-zero sample| / peak must be < 0.01 (today 0.50).

**Verifier notes.**
- Code confirmed (impact_exciter.h:229-230, 256-258, 285, isActive at :320); path mallet_exciter.h:81-90, 98-101 → exciter_bank.h:65-113 → drum_voice.h:1028-1030 (also :533, :1350) with no smoothing. Own probe (clang++ -O2, real header): hint 0.1 / v 0.1 ratio 0.515; 0.1 / 0.3 0.153; 0.2 / 0.1 0.175; hint >= 0.5 at v 0.1 0.051; v 1.0 <= 0.003. Centroid inversion and audibility after the modal bank and ClickLayer (drum_voice.h:1026-1029, 1052) not verified. Held medium.
- Second lens: comb off for Mallet; the mallet comment at :84-87 even assumes "an SVF/noise tail past the Hertzian T" that the early return prevents; no spec or prior audit calls the truncation intended. Own probe (probe_impact.cpp) reproduced 0.515 / 0.153 / 0.175 / 0.051, and the final step is the largest sample-to-sample jump. Recommends a downgrade: only v <= ~0.3 on size hint <= ~0.2, and the ClickLayer may mask it (drum_voice.h:787-794).
- Third lens: reset() (:90-105) is not called by ExciterBank::trigger (exciter_bank.h:53-58), so the frozen SVF state also leaks into the next hit after the attack ramp (:278-282). The quoted numbers re-derive from the code (T ~1.76 ms, cutoff ~665 Hz). Impact overstated: the exciter only feeds the modal bank (drum_voice.h:774-799; modal_resonator_bank.h:407-411, 930-936, 984-999), so there is no output discontinuity, only extra high-mode excitation; drum-sized pads are unaffected; the crotale pad (membrum_preset_generator.cpp:2816-2825) layers a deliberate HF click; the centroid figures are the exciter's, not the voice output's. Downgrade.

#### MB-025 — Noise seeding is inconsistent across exciters: Clap and the click layer replay identical noise on every hit of a slot (machine-gun rolls), Friction jitter is identical on all voices, and the strike probe changes the next hit's noise only on a cache miss

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** exciter · **Dimension:** exciters

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/clap_exciter.h:84-88](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/clap_exciter.h#L84)

**Problem.** ClapExciter::trigger and ClickLayer::trigger (click_layer.h:87-90) reset and reseed their noise every hit (seed from voiceId). NoiseBurst, Impact (Impulse, Mallet) and Feedback continue their PRNG across hits. BowExciter ignores voiceId (noiseState_ = 12345 in reset, bow_exciter.h:137). The strike probe (drum_voice.h:1338-1357) consumes Impact RNG draws and resets NoiseBurst's noise on a miss only, although its comment (1318-1320) says 'trigger() fully re-seeds/resets their state, so the probe leaves no residue'.

**Why wrong.** Either every hit should be reproducible (the FR-124 bit-identity goal cited in click_layer.h:79-86) or every hit should vary. Today it is a mix. A same-pad roll goes through allocator retrigger on the SAME slot, so the reseeding exciters produce sample-identical hits. The probe comment is false for Impact and NoiseBurst.

**Consequence.** Clap rolls and every pad's click transient repeat bit-identically (a machine-gun effect). Renders of Impulse, Mallet and NoiseBurst pads depend on cache and slot history, which makes goldens fragile. All simultaneous Friction voices share the same jitter.

**Evidence.** probe.cpp (same ExciterBank hit twice at v=0.8 / two slots): Clap hit1 vs hit2 maxdiff 0.000000, slot3 vs slot4 0.453899; Friction hit1 vs hit2 0.007796, slot3 vs slot4 0.000000; NoiseBurst 0.439764 / 0.496737; Impulse 0.241171 / 0.177113; FMImpulse 0 / 0.

**Suggested fix.** Choose one policy: seed every noise source per hit from (voiceId, hit counter) so hits vary but renders stay reproducible, and give BowExciter a per-voice seed. Fix the probe comment, or reseed after the probe. Test: two consecutive hits of one Clap pad must differ, and a render must be identical between two fresh pools.

**Verifier notes.**
- Traced: `noise_.reset()` reseeds to a per-slot seed (noise_oscillator.h:240; seeds 0xC1A9^voiceId at clap_exciter.h:60, voiceId*2+17 at click_layer.h:45); a same-pad roll retriggers the same slot (voice_allocator.h:238-242, 843-869) and main/shadow share voiceId (voice_pool.cpp:88-110). NoiseBurst does not reseed in trigger (noise_burst_exciter.h:87-107, only reset at :67); the probe resets after measuring (drum_voice.h:1356) only on a cache miss (:1389). BowExciter seed 12345 (bow_exciter.h:137, 352). The Clap/click reseed is deliberate (click_layer.h:79-86, voice_pool.cpp:88-97) but the policy is inconsistent. Low fits.
- Second lens: the "FR-124" the comments cite is the 5 ms fast-release rule in specs/138, not a bit-identity requirement, so no spec requires the reseed. ImpactExciter seeds rng_ only in prepare (impact_exciter.h:57) and draws in trigger (:142-143, 198, 204); FrictionExciter::prepare ignores voiceId (friction_exciter.h:33). The probe comment is false for Impact and only accidentally true for NoiseBurst.
- Third lens adds a missed source: NoiseLayer::trigger (noise_layer.h:160) also calls noise_.reset(), so the parallel noise layer (snare wires, hat hash) also replays per slot. Retrigger emits Steal + NoteOn on the same slot (voice_pool.cpp:203-233). Identical replay is ordinary for sample-based drum machines and is not a crash, level or click defect; making hits vary would not break the spec (specs/138-membrum-phase3-polyphony/spec.md:172).

#### MB-037 — Membrane strike amplitudes are wrong near Strike Position 1.0: the 20-term float Bessel series diverges (mode 46 gives 0.533 vs the true 0.176)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** dsp-numerics · **Dimension:** bodies-modal

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:130-160](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h#L130)

**Problem.** evaluateBesselJ sums 20 terms of the J_m power series in float. MembraneMapper evaluates it at x = j_mn * 0.9 * strikePos, up to 17.65. At x of about 17-18 the series' terms reach about 1e6 and the 20-term truncation remainder is not small, so the result has a large absolute error. The header claims 'accuracy under 1%'.

**Why wrong.** The mode amplitude must be |J_m(j_mn r/a)| (FR-035). The error makes the high-order mode weights at edge strikes (rimshot-like settings) wrong, by up to 3x and +9.6 dB on mode 46.

**Consequence.** At strikePos 1.0, 5 of 48 modes are off by more than 1 % of the largest amplitude: k46 (m1) 0.533 vs 0.176, k44 (m3) 0.251 vs 0.181, k39 (m0) 0.143 vs 0.192, k43 0.181 vs 0.191, k38 0.208 vs 0.195. strikePos 0.3-0.85 is accurate. The Bessel zero table checks out (worst |J_m(j_mn)| = 1.3e-5).

**Evidence.** membrane_modes.h:152-157 `constexpr int kMaxTerms = 20; for (int k = 1; k <= kMaxTerms; ++k) { term *= -halfXSq / (...); result += term; }` (float). membrane_mapper.h:112-117 `r_over_a = params.strikePos * 0.9f; ... std::abs(evaluateBesselJ(m, jmn * r_over_a))`. Node Math.fround emulation vs a 120-term double reference (scratchpad bessel.js): strikePos 1.0, 5 modes off; k46 float 0.533 vs ref 0.176.

**Suggested fix.** Evaluate in double with enough terms (about 40), or use a precomputed 48 x 64 amplitude table over strike position (std::cyl_bessel_j at build time / constexpr). Test: compare evaluateBesselJ against a double-precision reference for all 48 modes at strikePos 0, 0.5, 0.9 and 1.0, with a tolerance of 1 % of the maximum amplitude.

**Verifier notes.**
- Could not refute: float series with kMaxTerms = 20 (membrane_modes.h:130-160), unclamped strikePos (voice_common_params.h:19; drum_voice.h:1121), mode orders per kMembraneBesselOrder (:40-47). Hand check at m=1, x=17.65: largest term ~8e5, last included ~5.3, first dropped ~0.9, so truncation error is O(0.1-1). Own probe (bessel_check.js): 0.5-0.9 clean; 1.0 has k38, k39, k44, k46 off by > 0.01 (k43 just at threshold). Header comment (:123-127) false at the top of the range. Low: timbral only, normalised level.
- Second lens: only caller (grep), no test covers evaluateBesselJ, no design decision documents it; same four modes off at 1.0 (k46 ~3x, +9.6 dB). Notes another session overwrote the scratchpad script mid-run, but both versions do the same comparison.
- Third lens: not a repeat of a prior finding (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:312 checked only Bessel ratios). Relative RMS error across the 48 amplitudes: 25 % at 1.0, 3.7 % at 0.96, 0.9 % at 0.94, <= 0.2 % at 0.5-0.9; wrong k46 is 2.3x the true max (0.236). Affects only Membrane pads above ~0.93 (modes k38-k46, 7.5-8.2x f0), damped by the f^2 term, normalised by drum_voice.h:1366-1386; no default-kit pad affected (default_kit.h 0.3-0.32). Fix is cheap and runs at mapper time.

#### MB-047 — Pitch-envelope LUT rebuild (up to ~4,000 powf) runs on the audio thread at every note-on, even with the envelope off

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** rt-safety · **Dimension:** layers-shaper · **Also flagged by:** gestalt-voice

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:228-283, 537-562](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h#L228)

**Problem.** Every pitch-envelope setter calls rebuildPitchEnv_(). applyPadConfigToVoice calls 8 of them (pad_config_apply.h:101-120) from VoicePool::applyPadConfigToSlot inside noteOn on the audio thread (voice_pool.cpp:232, 769-784). Each rebuild fills one or two 256-entry tables with std::pow (curve_table.h:65-78). This happens even when tsPitchEnvTime is 0. The comment at 537-540 says it is 'never invoked from process()', but it is reached from process() through processEvents and VoicePool::noteOn.

**Why wrong.** Note-on work on the audio thread should be bounded and cheap. A 16-note chord costs about 64k powf in one block for a value that only changes when the user edits the pad.

**Consequence.** A CPU spike per note-on that grows with chord size and roll density. It is not an allocation, but it is wasted budget, and the stale comment misleads maintainers.

**Evidence.** tone_shaper.h:231 'if (prepared_) rebuildPitchEnv_();' in each setter; :537-540 'never invoked from process()'; pad_config_apply.h:101-120 makes 8 pitch setter calls; curve_table.h:76 'float shaped = std::pow(phase, exponent);' in a 256-iteration loop.

**Suggested fix.** Cache the pitch-envelope inputs and rebuild only on change (a dirty flag consumed once at noteOn), or build the tables per pad on the processor's parameter path instead of per voice. Fix the comment. A perf case that counts rebuilds per noteOn for an unchanged pad would catch it (expect 0).

**Verifier notes.**
- Call path confirmed (voice_pool.cpp:232, 784; pad_config_apply.h:101-120; setters at tone_shaper.h:231, 237, 243, 252, 264, 270, 276, 282 with no change check; rebuildPitchEnv_ at :541-562 rebuilds even at time 0 per :545-547; pitch_segment_envelope.h:60-98; curve_table.h:65-78): ~2,056 powf per note-on with the knee off, ~4,112 with it on, all but the last rebuild redundant. Correction: the comment at :537-540 admits "per-pad apply paths" and "process()" likely means ToneShaper::process, so it is optimistic, not false. Low.
- Second lens microbenchmark (pow_bench.cpp, clang++ -O2): 3.43 µs per table, ~27 µs per note-on knee off, ~55 µs knee on, ~0.88 ms for a 16-note coincident hit (vs a 1.33 ms 64-sample block at 48 kHz). Not a strict RT-rule violation (bounded, no allocation). pitch_segment_envelope.h:16-17 ("at user-edit time") is contradicted; the perf stress test (tests/perf/test_polyphony_stress_16.cpp:136-139) only folds note-on cost into an aggregate budget.
- Third lens (pitchenv_probe.cpp): knee off 25.4 µs per note-on (22.9 µs fast-math), knee on 52.1 µs (43.9 µs fast-math); a 16-note hit costs ~0.4-0.8 ms, 30-60 % of a 64-sample block at 48 kHz. Treats the :537-540 comment as wrong. Output unchanged; low is right.

#### MB-048 — NoiseLayer at mix 0 still runs the noise oscillator, SVF and ADSR every sample

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** layers-shaper · **Dimension:** layers-shaper

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h:181-186, 198-206](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h#L181)

**Problem.** When mix_ <= 0 the layer still calls noise_.process(), filter_.process(0) and envelope_.process() per sample (and stepBloom), then writes 0. DrumVoice calls processBlock unconditionally and then multiplies by the gain (drum_voice.h:855-864).

**Why wrong.** The layer is meant to be free when off. The output is already exactly zero, so nothing needs to advance: trigger() resets the noise, filter and envelope at every noteOn (:158-170).

**Consequence.** Wasted CPU on every voice of every pad that turns the noise layer off, up to 32 voices.

**Evidence.** noise_layer.h:198-206 'if (mix_ <= 0.0f) { for (...) { if (bloomActive_) stepBloom(); (void)noise_.process(); (void)filter_.process(0.0f); (void)envelope_.process(); out[i] = 0.0f; } return; }'.

**Suggested fix.** When mix_ <= 0, memset the output and return. In DrumVoice, skip the noise processBlock and gain loop when mix is 0 and the noise scratch was zeroed once. Bit-identity holds because trigger() resets all state.

**Verifier notes.**
- Confirmed: mix_ changes only in configure()/configureRaw() (:79, :106), called for the parallel layer only at note-on (drum_voice.h:346) before trigger() (:372); trigger resets everything and configure clears bloomActive_ (:88); isActive() (:218) is gated on mix_ > 0. An early return is output-identical. Minor: only pads with noiseLayerMix == 0 (default 0.35 at pad_config.h:251; default kit 0.50-0.95). Low as filed.
- Second lens: NoiseOscillator::reset reseeds (noise_oscillator.h:238-244), so skipping cannot change later notes; NoiseBody's own NoiseLayer (noise_body.h:73-121, mix 0.35-0.55) is unaffected. Reachable from factory content (membrum_preset_generator.cpp:548, 1113, 1147, 1158, 1371, 1987, 2228 set mix 0.0). No CPU measured.
- Third lens: setNoiseLayerMix (:1149) takes effect only at the next noteOn. Estimated cost ~0.4 % of one core worst case (16 voices at 48 kHz); "up to 32 voices" overstates it, since shadow slots live only 5 ms. A larger waste of the same kind is missed: with mix > 0 the layer keeps running after its own envelope ends, for the whole modal tail (retirement deliberately not gated on it, drum_voice.h:639), so skipping on !isActive() (:218) is the better fix. Nit-level performance item.

#### MB-055 — Audition uses one atomic word: a pad-down and pad-up between two blocks (or two pads) overwrite each other, and a stale request fires on resume

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** midi-timing · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:540-556, 1186-1215](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L540)

**Problem.** notify() stores AuditionPad and AuditionPadOff into the single `std::atomic<uint32_t> pendingAudition_` with store(). process() consumes it once per block with exchange(0). Any two messages before the next process() call collapse to the last one. A click shorter than one audio block, or a block delayed by the host, loses the note-on (only the note-off is applied). Two quick clicks on different pads lose the first. If the host is not calling process() (inactive or suspended), the last request survives and fires whenever processing resumes.

**Why wrong.** UI audition events are a queue, not a state. Note-on/off pairs must not be lost or merged, and a stale UI event must not trigger sound seconds later.

**Consequence.** Occasional dead pad clicks with large buffers (a 2048-sample block is 46 ms, longer than a quick tap). Fast multi-pad clicking drops hits. A pad can sound unexpectedly when transport or processing resumes.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:1194-1198 `const std::uint32_t word = 0x4000u | ...; pendingAudition_.store(word, std::memory_order_release);`; :1210-1214 AuditionPadOff `pendingAudition_.store(word, ...)` (velocity 0); :542 `const std::uint32_t word = pendingAudition_.exchange(0u, std::memory_order_acq_rel);`; processor.h:126 `std::atomic<std::uint32_t> pendingAudition_{0};`.

**Suggested fix.** Replace the word with a small lock-free SPSC ring (for example 16 entries of {midi, vel}) drained fully each block. Drop entries older than N blocks, or clear the ring in setActive/setProcessing. Test: post AuditionPad then AuditionPadOff before one process() call and assert a voice was started (then released). Post two AuditionPad for different pads and assert two voices.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: mouse-down and mouse-up become separate IMessages (pad_grid_view.cpp:287-299, :389-393; controller.cpp:1070-1085, :1091-1102), both are plain-stored into one word (processor.cpp:1194-1198, :1210-1215; processor.h:126) and consumed once per block by exchange(0) (processor.cpp:622, :540-556), so a down+up inside one block leaves only the noteOff and the click is silent; nothing clears the word on setActive/setProcessing, and the only test (test_morph_host_simulation.cpp:137-190) sends a single AuditionPad. The stale-trigger part bites only if the mouse is still held. Low fits.
- Confirmed: processor.h:121-126 says the word is "Cleared by process() after consumption"; consumption happens after the `numSamples == 0` early return (processor.cpp:613-614). CHANGELOG.md:308-313 documents "Hold-pad audition" (noteOn on down, noteOff on up) as intended, so losing or merging those events contradicts the documented design. Low.
- Confirmed, one sub-claim overstated: a block is 10.7 ms at 512 / 48 kHz and 46 ms at 2048 / 44.1 kHz against a 60-150 ms physical click, so the miss needs large buffers or fast taps (touchpad tap-to-click plausibly repeatable, not measured). A lost note-off (pad A up + pad B down in one block) can leave a Friction pad ringing until stolen. "Stale request fires on resume" is mostly impossible: the leftover word is almost always the velocity-0 off; a stale note-on needs the editor torn down mid-hold. UI audition only; host MIDI (processEvents, :559 on) is unaffected. Low.

#### MB-056 — Pan and output bus are re-read live for ringing and fading voices: automation or re-routing jumps a tail between buses in one block step

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** voice-management · **Dimension:** voice-management-midi

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:361, 476, 489-505, 534, 543-559](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L361)

**Problem.** panGainsForNote and the aux-bus lookup read `padConfigs_[pad].pan` / `.outputBus` at render time for every main and shadow voice, using the stale originatingNote. Changing a pad's Output Bus while it rings moves the whole remaining tail from aux N to aux M (or off the aux) at a block boundary with no fade. Pan automation steps gains once per block (zipper). Both apply to fading shadow voices too.

**Why wrong.** Routing and pan are per-note properties of a sounding percussive voice. Changing them mid-tail without a crossfade produces discontinuities on the aux buses (a hard start or stop of a ringing signal).

**Consequence.** Clicks on aux buses when the user re-routes a pad during playback or automates Output Bus. Audible zipper on pan automation with large blocks.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:756-757 `std::clamp(padConfigs_[static_cast<std::size_t>(pad)].pan, 0.0f, 1.0f)` called per block from :361/:476/:534; :493-494 `const int bus = static_cast<int>(padConfigs_[...].outputBus);` and :547-548 for shadows; setPadConfigField writes these live at :649 and :651-655.

**Suggested fix.** Latch pan gains and the bus into VoiceMeta at noteOn (copy to releasingMeta_ in beginFastRelease), or smooth pan per sample and crossfade a bus change over about 5 ms. Test: ring a pad on aux 2, switch it to aux 3 mid-ring, and assert no aux-2 discontinuity greater than -30 dBFS.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: panGainsForNote is called once per block for main and shadow voices (voice_pool.cpp:361, :420, :476, :534), reads pan live (:756-757) and applies one constant gain pair per block (:479-485, :536-540); the aux route reads outputBus live (:489-505, :543-559); setPadConfigField writes both directly (:649, :651-655). The M-9 comments (:417, :531) only say the shadow keeps its pad's pan. Low is correct. Wording: originatingNote is not stale; the live data is the per-pad config read through it.
- Confirmed: both fields are reached from processParameterChanges (processor.cpp:392 for kOutputBusId, :515-516 for kPadPanId) and both are registered kCanAutomate (controller.cpp:580, :664, :715). No spec, manual or prior audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md M-9 records only that pan was added) makes the live re-read intended. Results: a mid-tail bus change is a step on the aux bus, a pan jump steps a channel gain at once (L 1.414 to 0), pan automation stair-steps per block. Low.
- Holds, impact narrower: no pan smoothing or bus latch exists anywhere under plugins/membrum (grep); only originatingNote is carried over (:253, :947); the main bus is unaffected by a bus change (:483-484). A -20 dBFS tail gives an aux step of about -17 to -20 dBFS (audible click); a hard pan jump clicks on main too; a smooth 1 s sweep at 512 / 48 kHz is about 94 steps of about 0.2 dB, faint and audible only on long tonal tails (Bell, String, modeInject). Per-pad pan and bus behave like mixer-channel settings (mitigating). Low.

#### MB-060 — Aux routing duplicates the pad on main and sends it pre-master and unlimited, while the manual implies a separate route

**Severity:** low (finder: medium; downgraded by verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** gain-staging · **Dimension:** gain-staging-master

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:478-506, 542-560](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L478)

**Problem.** A voice is always summed into main (lines 483-484) and is additionally written to its aux bus (500-504). Main then gets coupling, the -1 dBTP limiter and master gain (-6 dB default); the aux copy gets none of them. The same pad therefore appears twice in the DAW. With master at the default -6 dB, the aux copy is 6 dB louder than the pad's contribution to main, and it is unbounded (hardClip 1.0 x hard-pan sqrt2 = +3 dBFS per voice, summed across voices).

**Why wrong.** Spec 139 (scenario at spec.md:149) does say a pad appears on both main and aux, so the routing itself is intended. But MANUAL.md:374 ('1-15 = aux stereo buses for separate DAW processing') and :527 ('Route the ride or crash to bus 1 ... without affecting the rest of the kit') describe a separate route, and the diagram at MANUAL.md:67-72 splits the bus selector into either Main or Aux. Nothing tells the user that the pad stays on main, that the aux is pre-limiter and pre-master, or how to avoid the doubling.

**Consequence.** A user who follows the manual and routes the ride to Aux 1 with a reverb hears the dry ride on main, plus the aux copy 6 dB hotter than that main contribution and unlimited. Summed coherently in the DAW, the ride rises by up to about 7.5 dB (0.5 + 1.0 linear vs 0.5). Coincident aux-routed hits can exceed 0 dBFS on the aux.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:483-484 `outL[i] += scratch[i] * gainL; outR[i] += scratch[i] * gainR;` then :500-504 `auxL[bus][i] += scratch[i] * gainL; ...`. processor.cpp:663-737: coupling, limiter and master operate on outL/outR (main) only. specs/139-membrum-phase4-pads/spec.md:149 'Pads always appear on the main mix regardless of auxiliary assignment.' MANUAL.md:527 'Route the ride or crash to bus 1 if you want to apply a separate reverb/EQ chain in your DAW without affecting the rest of the kit. Aux buses are pre-master'.

**Suggested fix.** Either add a per-pad 'exclude from main' option (route-only), or document in MANUAL.md:67-87 and :374/:527 that aux buses are post-pan, pre-coupling, pre-limiter and pre-master SENDS, the pad stays on main, and mute the main channel or lower that pad's level to avoid doubling. Test: pad on bus 1 at default master; assert peak(aux1) / peak(main contribution) == 10^(6/20) and document the number.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed (voice_pool.cpp:479-485, :488-506, :536-560; panGainsForNote :744-764 gives gainL^2 + gainR^2 == 2, so +3 dBFS at hard pan and the 6 dB-hotter aux copy hold), but the send model is required by specs/139-membrum-phase4-pads/spec.md FR-041 (:272), FR-042 (:273, "a 'send' model, not an 'exclusive routing' model") and scenario :149. "Nothing tells the user the aux is pre-master" is false: MANUAL.md:87, :449, :527 say so. What remains: the manual never says the pad stays on main, the diagram (:67-72) and :374 read as exclusive routing, and it never says pre-limiter. Low documentation gap.
- Same conclusion: a grep of MANUAL.md for "send" finds nothing, and the manual never mentions the -1 dBTP main-bus limiter (its only "limiter" hits are the coupling energy limiter at :79, :225, :437). The +3 dBFS figure holds only at a hard pan (voice_pool.cpp:759-762). Downgrade to low: a manual and diagram fix only; the code must not change.
- Code confirmed, including processor.cpp:653-659 (aux zeroed), coupling (:690-704), busLimiter_ (:711-717, -1 dBTP ceiling at :1088) and master gain (:726) touching main only. Impact numbers are off: a dry aux at unity sums to 0.5 + 1.0 vs 0.5 = +9.5 dB, not about 7.5 dB; with a 100%-wet reverb insert there is no doubling; one voice on the aux peaks at about -6 dBFS centred or -3 dBFS hard-panned (kBodyHeadroom 0.5 x 1.414), so over 0 dBFS needs several coincident voices, and over 0 dBFS on a float bus is not clipping. Downgrade to low (docs).

#### MB-061 — NonlinearCoupling adds about +5 to +7 dB without make-up, and ModeInject adds up to 2.72 peak x amount on top of the 0.5 body budget

**Severity:** low (finder: medium; downgraded by verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** gain-staging · **Dimension:** gain-staging-master

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/nonlinear_coupling.h:117-126](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/nonlinear_coupling.h#L117)

**Problem.** NLC computes drive = 1 + 6*velocity*amount*env (env = RMS follower of its input) and returns x + amount*(recipSqrt(x*drive) - x). For small x the stage gain is 1 + amount*(drive-1). There is no 1/drive make-up, unlike the ToneShaper drive. ModeInject (mode_inject.h:60, 126, 142) feeds 8 harmonics at amplitude 1/k with skipNormalization=true (peak up to sum 1/k = 2.72, RMS 0.87) times amount*env_. It is added to the body BEFORE NLC and the tone shaper (drum_voice.h:893) with no relation to kBodyHeadroom.

**Why wrong.** Both stages sit after the measured-strike normalisation that places the body at kBodyHeadroom 0.5 (drum_voice.h:84, 302). A timbre control (NLC 'brightening', ModeInject series) therefore also changes the level by several dB, which undoes the gain-staging plan. At amount 1, a body sample at 0.3 with env about 0.21 gives drive 2.27 and output 0.5625: +5.5 dB, and +7.1 dB in the small-signal limit. ModeInject at amount 0.2 already has an RMS (0.17) comparable to the body's PEAK budget. At amount 1 its peak reaches 2.72 x level and drives the per-voice hardClip rail (drum_voice.h:898) into hard clipping.

**Consequence.** Raising NLC (used by snare and cymbals for 'bloom') makes the pad louder as well as brighter, so loudness-matched kit design is impossible. Measured: the default-kit snare is the loudest pad at a 0.668 pre-master peak vs 0.40 for kick and toms at the same Level. Most of the ModeInject knob's range overdrives the voice into the hardClip, so it is a distortion control rather than an inject level.

**Evidence.** nonlinear_coupling.h:117 `constexpr float kDriveScale = 6.0f;` :118 `const float drive = 1.0f + kDriveScale * velocity_ * amount_ * env;` :125-126 `const float shaped = Krate::DSP::Sigmoid::recipSqrt(bodyOutput * drive); return bodyOutput + amount_ * (shaped - bodyOutput);`. sigmoid.h:193 `return x / std::sqrt(x * x + 1.0f);`. mode_inject.h:60 `frame_.partials[k].amplitude = 1.0f / static_cast<float>(harmonicIndex);`, :126 `bank_.loadFrame(frame_, f0, /*skipNormalization=*/true);`, :142 `const float s = amount_ * env_ * bank_.process();`. drum_voice.h:893-898.

**Suggested fix.** NLC: divide the shaped branch by drive (or match RMS: out = x + amount*(recipSqrt(x*drive)/drive_norm - x)) so amount changes the harmonic content, not the level. ModeInject: scale the bank output by kBodyHeadroom / (sum of 1/k), or normalise the series RMS to the body budget, so amount 1 equals the body peak. Test: a level-invariance test rendering a Membrane pad at NLC amount 0 and 1 (and ModeInject 0 / 0.5), asserting a peak difference <= 1.5 dB, and that the hardClip is never engaged at amount <= 1 for a vel-1 hit (max |pre-clip| < 1).

**Verifier notes:**
- Mechanism confirmed: nonlinear_coupling.h:107-126 has no make-up and its header (:36-38) hands peak control downstream; x = 0.3, env = 0.21 gives +5.4 dB; ModeInject (mode_inject.h:60, :126; harmonic_oscillator_bank.h:345-367 skips normalisation) peaks at 2.72 with RMS 0.87, and the prepare() comment (mode_inject.h:47-53, "then normalized") is stale. Overstated: the "+7.1 dB small-signal limit" is wrong (env follows the same signal, so drive goes to 1); the snare measurement is misattributed (NLC defaults to 0, pad_config.h:215; only the crash sets 0.35, default_kit.h:234); factory NLC 0.12-0.45 adds about +0.2 to +1.5 dB, only a few pads go high (generator :1534, :2760); NLC is a deliberate Unnatural-zone waveshaper.
- Only the ModeInject half holds. NLC: the RMS follower's attack is 30-120 ms (setVelocity, nonlinear_coupling.h:85-91), so at the strike peak drive is near 1 and the output is slightly below dry; the prior audit measured "coupling-on LOWERS peak vs off" (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:96-103); +5.5 dB applies only to a sustained ring; the snare's 0.668 peak comes from its wire noise layer (noiseLayerGain 6.2, default_kit.h:120) plus the 0.55 click. ModeInject holds: added before the tone shaper (drum_voice.h:557, 893, 1056), Level linear (:1126), amount clamped only to [0,1] (pad_config_apply.h:129-130), so it can engage the hardClip that drum_voice.h:79 and :562-565 say never engages on a musical hit; mode_inject.h:48-50 comment is stale.
- Overstated: NLC is an amplitude-dependent expander, not a flat boost (amount 1, vel 1: A = 0.5 gives +4.5 dB, A = 0.1 about +3 dB, A = 0.01 about +0.4 dB); factory amounts give about +0.3 to +1.3 dB, the Chaos cycle at 0.75-0.85 (generator :1534) about +3 dB; the snare consequence is misattributed. The ModeInject 2.72 peak cannot occur: the bank clamps to ±kOutputClamp = 2.0 (harmonic_oscillator_bank.h:92, 996), phases are random per trigger (mode_inject.h:110-113) and amplitudes ramp through the smoother (:301, :936); factory amounts 0.15-0.28 (generator :1533, :1585, :1643, :2200) stay under the rail; clipping needs an amount above about 0.5-0.6 at level 0.8, and ModeInject's amount is its level by design.

#### MB-064 — Main-bus silence flag is never set while Global Coupling > 0, and the coupling loop and limiter run forever with no voices

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** gain-staging · **Dimension:** gain-staging-master · **Also flagged by:** coupling (x2), gestalt-processor

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:693-708, 717, 739-741](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L693)

**Problem.** The main silenceFlags is 0 whenever `!couplingEngine_.isBypassed()`. isBypassed() is true only when the coupling amount is exactly 0 (sympathetic_resonance.h:370-372). For any kit with coupling > 0, the per-sample coupling loop (delay, 64-resonator engine, energy limiter) and the 4x-oversampled bus limiter run every block even after every voice and resonator has decayed, and the bus is never reported silent.

**Why wrong.** Silence flags let hosts skip downstream processing. They should reflect whether the buffer is actually silent, for example no active voice AND the coupling output below a threshold for a hold time.

**Consequence.** Idle CPU stays at the full coupling + limiter cost with no notes, and hosts cannot optimise away the track. This is wasted CPU on every coupled kit.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:739-741 `data.outputs[0].silenceFlags = (voicePool_.isAnyVoiceActive() || !couplingEngine_.isBypassed()) ? 0ULL : 3ULL;`. sympathetic_resonance.h:370-371 `return amountSmoother_.getCurrentValue() == 0.0f && couplingGain_ == 0.0f;`. processor.cpp:693 `if (!couplingEngine_.isBypassed())` runs the per-sample loop; :717 runs the limiter unconditionally.

**Suggested fix.** Track the peak of the coupling return (or the engine's active-resonator count). When no voice is active and the coupling output has been below 1e-6 for a hold of about 100 ms, skip the loop and set silenceFlags = 3. Test: load a kit with coupling 0.5, play one hit, render 10 s, and assert the last blocks report silenceFlags == 3.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: processor.cpp:739-741 keys the flag on isBypassed(), which (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/sympathetic_resonance.h:370-371) depends only on the amount; getActiveResonatorCount() (:365) exists but is not used; couplingGain_ is nonzero for any amount > 0 (:152-159); the loop at processor.cpp:693-708 runs with no short-circuit when activeCount_ is 0 (sympathetic_resonance.h:329-352). Overstated: busLimiter_.processBlock at :717 runs unconditionally whatever the coupling setting. Global Coupling defaults to 0 (plugin_ids.h:114). Low.
- Real on ordinary factory kits: tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp sets globalCoupling 0.18-0.85 on many kits (lines 1661 through 6607). specs/140-membrum-phase5-coupling/research.md:47-49 implies the flag should reflect the actual coupling output, not the bypass state. No test checks silenceFlags. The limiter part is not coupling-caused. VST3 always allows flag 0, so this is idle CPU and a missed host optimisation; low.
- Confirmed: 15 factory kits trigger it; each idle sample pays processSympatheticBankSIMD over all 64 slots (sympathetic_resonance.h:43, 329-333) plus a 64-iteration reclaim scan (:337-352). Once voices retire the coupling return is exactly zero (reclaim zeroes resonators, :341-350; the HPF tail is flushed by ScopedDenormalMode, processor.cpp:611), so the flag says "not silent" over a zero buffer. No audible defect; gating the flag alone would not remove the limiter cost. Low.

#### MB-065 — Peak meter shows one audio block's peak per UI tick with no hold: drum transients and overs are mostly missed

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** gain-staging · **Dimension:** gain-staging-master

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:1716-1724](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L1716)

**Problem.** The processor sends one MetersBlock per process() call, holding the peak of that block only (processor.cpp:790-800, 826-848), through a DataExchange queue of 4 blocks (processor.cpp:1150). The controller keeps only the LAST block of each delivery (controller.cpp:1716-1724). KitMetersView draws that value linearly, with no peak hold or decay (kit_meters_view.cpp:29-34, 52, 60).

**Why wrong.** A peak meter for percussive material must accumulate the max between UI refreshes, or hold and decay it. Otherwise it shows a random block, mostly the tail. At 64-sample blocks and 48 kHz there are about 25 audio blocks per 33 ms UI tick, but the queue holds only 4 of them and only 1 is displayed.
