Minor correction: the v2 fixture's grep hits are specs/138 tasks.md / plan.md / quickstart.md, not preset-retune. Low; the runtime consequence belongs to MB-S03.
- Confirmed: the header at :10-11 admits the "v6" name is kept only for git history; test_coupling_state.cpp:109-113 also describes a "synthetic v4" layout of 34 float64 / 9040 bytes; state_codec.h:35 ("44 float64 sound params") is stale too; specs/138 plan.md:618 promised a v2 test the dead fixture no longer backs. No ruling excuses the wrong numbers. Low.
- Confirmed: test_pad_preset.cpp:95 compares against kPadPresetBytes, so the test passes but its name is wrong; the pad blob is 4+4+4+59*8 = 484 bytes; phase2_state_v2.bin was last touched in 8d23d774 and no test TU references it; `git ls-remote --tags origin` shows membrum/v0.9.0 through v0.12.5. No runtime effect; low documentation drift, no change.

#### MB-094 — MB-S11: setActive(true) wipes every voice but keeps the coupling engine, coupling delay and energy envelope, whose resonators keep the dead voices as owners

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** lifecycle-state · **Dimension:** lifecycle-state

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:1093-1127](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L1093)

**Problem.** setActive(true) calls voicePool_.prepare(), which re-prepares and resets all 32 voices and the allocator and zeroes the metas (voice_pool.cpp:52-90), and it resets busLimiter_. It does not reset couplingEngine_, couplingDelay_ or energyEnvelope_. VoicePool::prepare does not call couplingEngine_->noteOff for the slots it wipes, so the SympatheticResonance pool still holds resonators owned by voice IDs that no longer sound. setActive(false) resets only the pad-glow publisher. Only setupProcessing re-prepares the coupling engine and delay (1081-1084), and hosts do not always call it between deactivate and activate.

**Why wrong.** An activation reset must be consistent. Either all audio state is flushed (voices, coupling resonators, coupling delay, limiter, energy limiter) or none is. Leaving the coupling engine's ownership tables pointing at reset voices breaks the 'noteOff on every voice that leaves' bookkeeping that applyKitSnapshot relies on (processor.cpp:950-961 describes exactly this orphan-ring problem).

**Consequence.** After a deactivate/activate (bypass toggles in some hosts, an offline render start, a device restart), stale sympathetic resonances and the old coupling-delay content can ring into the first blocks at a Q of up to 1000 (seconds-long at low partials) while every voice is silent. There is also double prepare cost per activation (setupProcessing and then setActive both prepare 32 voices).

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:1097 'voicePool_.prepare(sampleRate_, maxBlockSize_);' and :1104 'busLimiter_.reset();' with no coupling reset in the branch; :1117-1125 the setActive(false) branch resets only padGlowPublisher_; voice_pool.cpp:52-90 prepare resets voices with no couplingEngine_->noteOff; sympathetic_resonance.h:135-140 reset() exists.

**Suggested fix.** In setActive(true), also call couplingEngine_.reset(); couplingEngine_.setAmount(globalCoupling_.load()); couplingDelay_.reset(); energyEnvelope_ = 0. Alternatively have VoicePool::prepare call couplingEngine_->noteOff(slot) for non-Free metas. Test: ring a coupled kit, setActive(false) then setActive(true), render one block with no notes, and require the main output to be exactly 0 and couplingEngine active resonator count 0.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: setActive(true) never touches the coupling members (processor.cpp:1093-1116); VoicePool::prepare (voice_pool.cpp:106-121) never calls noteOff; active resonators keep y1s_/y2s_ and are summed by process() (sympathetic_resonance.h:312-358) until reclaimed; the coupling loop runs whenever the engine is not bypassed (processor.cpp:693-707) and silence flags stay 0 (:739-741). applyKitSnapshot (:950-967) shows the intended flush. Overstated: ownership affects neither output nor reclaim, and a reused slot clears it (noteOn calls noteOff first, :181); the leftover is capped by the -20 dBFS energy limiter. Low.
- Confirmed: these coupling members are reset only in setupProcessing (1081-1084) and applyKitSnapshot (965-967); the pool's noteOff calls (voice_pool.cpp:168, 208, 273, 390, 1042) are all on release paths; reclaim happens at the -96 dB envelope threshold (sympathetic_resonance.h:341). setActive resets the bus limiter "so a reactivation does not inherit stale ... state" (processor.cpp:1102-1104) but not the coupling. Effect needs coupling > 0 and a host that reactivates without setupProcessing; coupling gain is -46 to -26 dB. Low.
- Facts hold, mechanism and consequence overstated; recommends nit: owner IDs are read only by noteOff (sympathetic_resonance.h:264-298) and slot reuse clears them (voice_pool.cpp:247, :181); the applyKitSnapshot comment (950-961) is about a reduced coupling amount, not this case. No setDecay call exists in plugins/membrum/src, so userQ_ stays at 316 (sympathetic_resonance.h:128), about a 1 s time constant at 100 Hz, not Q 1000; the residue passes the energy limiter (processor.h:183-196), the -1 dBTP limiter and -6 dB master gain (worst case about -26 dBFS, decaying). Offline-render starts and device restarts normally go through setupProcessing, and VST3 bypass is a parameter; the double prepare runs off the audio thread.

#### MB-095 — MB-S12: The processor reports kNoTail although voices and coupling resonators ring for seconds after the last event

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** lifecycle-state · **Dimension:** lifecycle-state

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.h](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.h) (no getTailSamples override; SDK default [extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84](extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h#L84))

**Problem.** Processor does not override getTailSamples, so AudioEffect returns kNoTail (vstaudioeffect.h:84 'getTailSamples () { return kNoTail; }'). Membrum voices can ring for tens of seconds (decayTime clamp 5 s = T60 about 34.5 s; cymbal b1 0.2 + 0.02*49.8, T60 about 4.6 s per default_kit.h:241), and coupling resonators at Q up to 1000 ring after the voices.

**Why wrong.** getTailSamples tells the host how long output continues after input or events stop. Hosts use it for offline render length and for suspending processing. A ringing instrument should report kInfiniteTail, or a bounded estimate, and rely on silenceFlags (which process() already sets) for idle detection.

**Consequence.** In hosts that honour the tail for bounce/freeze length or processing suspension, cymbal and tom tails at the end of a render or after a region can be truncated.

**Evidence.** grep for getTailSamples in plugins/membrum/src: no match; extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84; processor.cpp:739-741 silenceFlags computed per block.

**Suggested fix.** Override getTailSamples to return kInfiniteTail (silenceFlags already describe true silence), or a bound such as 35 s * sampleRate. Test: Processor::getTailSamples() != kNoTail.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: Processor derives directly from AudioEffect (processor.h:40) and no getTailSamples / kInfiniteTail / kNoTail exists in plugins/membrum; silence flags are computed per block (processor.cpp:739-741). Ruinae fixed the same gap as R-190 (ruinae processor.cpp:740-749, processor_host_contract_test.cpp), Iterum returns kInfiniteTail (iterum processor.h:91), and Vorago, Profundum and Disrumpo override it with tests. T60 figures not independently verified. Low.
- Confirmed: no tail ruling in specs/*membrum*. Seraphis also keeps the default but defers it explicitly (seraphis processor.cpp:1773-1779) and forces silenceFlags = 0; Membrum does set silence flags (processor.cpp:739-741 main, :684 aux), so it has the idle detection the fix relies on. Other plugins pin their tails in tests (vorago processor.cpp:676, ruinae :743 R-190, profundum :574, disrumpo :1051 D-108). Low.
- Confirmed: ivstaudioprocessor.h:349-357 defines kNoTail as "no tail" and says hosts use the value for "offline processing, process optimization and downmix (avoiding signal cut (clicks))", which contradicts a plugin that rings for seconds. Low because accurate per-block silence flags already exist and hosts usually size instrument renders by the timeline; which hosts trust getTailSamples was not confirmed and no host was measured.

#### MB-100 — notifyBusActivation is never called in production, so the Output Bus tooltip always warns "Host must activate Aux N bus" and the FR-043 reset never runs

**Severity:** low (finder: medium; downgraded by verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** ui-wiring · **Dimension:** ui-wiring · **Also flagged by:** parallel-paths, gestalt-controller

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:923-955](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L923)

**Problem.** Controller::busActive_ is `{true}`, so only bus 0 is active (controller.h:183). The only writer is notifyBusActivation, which only tests call (grep: test_bus_activation.cpp, test_output_routing_ui.cpp). The processor's activateBus (processor.cpp:1024-1038) updates only its own busActive_ and cannot reach the controller. updateOutputBusTooltip (controller_view_sync.cpp:79-85) therefore treats every aux bus as inactive.

**Why wrong.** FR-066 asks for the warning only when the selected aux bus is really inactive, and FR-043 asks for pads on a deactivated bus to fall back to main. Neither can work without a production source of bus state. The processor would have to send it through an IMessage or the MetersBlock (the CLAUDE.md data-bridge rule says to piggyback on MetersBlock).

**Consequence.** A user who routes a pad to Aux 2 in a host that activated Aux 2 still sees the tooltip "Host must activate Aux 2 bus". The UI contradicts the routing that works. The FR-043 reset-to-main logic is dead code in shipped builds.

**Evidence.** grep notifyBusActivation: only controller.cpp:923 (definition) plus tests; controller.h:183 `std::array<bool, kMaxOutputBuses> busActive_ = {true};`; controller_view_sync.cpp:79-84 `if (busIndex >= 1 && !isBusActive(busIndex)) ... "Host must activate Aux %d bus"`.

**Suggested fix.** Add a 16-bit busActive mask to MetersBlock (processor side: from busActive_). In onDataExchangeBlocksReceived, call notifyBusActivation for each bit that changed. Alternatively, send a one-shot IMessage from activateBus. Test: processor activateBus(kOutput, 2, true), deliver a MetersBlock to the controller, and assert isBusActive(2) and an empty tooltip on the output-bus control.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: notifyBusActivation appears only at its definition (controller.cpp:923-955) and declaration (controller.h:112, whose comment at :107-111 says "This method is provided for testing"); production calls updateOutputBusTooltip at controller.cpp:888, :974 and :1280, so every aux bus always shows the warning, and the FR-043 loop (:934-949) is unreachable. Downgrade: audio routing is correct because VoicePool::processBlock gates aux writes on the processor's busActive (voice_pool.cpp:496, 550, fed from processor.cpp:665).
- Confirmed: Processor::notify (processor.cpp:1182) is the only message handler in src and MetersBlock (meters_block.h:20-31) has no bus mask, so the controller never learns bus state. specs/141 spec.md:164 and :271 (FR-066) want the warning only for a truly inactive bus; specs/139 tasks.md:233 (T046b) planned a controller-side activateBus that a separate component never receives. Every voice is also written to main, so no audio is lost: low.
- Confirmed, downgrade from medium: outputBusSelView_ is cached in verifyView (controller.cpp:1278-1280) and refreshed on bus changes, so the wrong tooltip is live, but sound, state and parameters are unaffected. The dead FR-043 reset (controller.cpp:934-949) would, if wired, call setParamNormalized with no beginEdit/performEdit and desync controller from processor; carry a bus mask on MetersBlock and either drop that reset or route it through performEdit.

#### MB-102 — Kit meter and pad glow show one audio block's peak per 30 Hz tick (last block wins, no peak hold), so drum transients and clips are mostly missed

**Severity:** low (finder: medium; downgraded by verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** ui-wiring · **Dimension:** ui-wiring · **Also flagged by:** gestalt-controller

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:1710-1738](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L1710)

**Problem.** The processor sends one MetersBlock per process() call with that block's peaks (processor.cpp:790-848). onDataExchangeBlocksReceived memcpy's every block into cachedMeters_ in a loop, so only the LAST block survives. Only that block's glow buckets are republished. The 33 ms timer pushes this single-block value into KitMetersView::setPeaks, which stores it with no hold or decay (kit_meters_view.cpp:29-34).

**Why wrong.** A peak meter has to report the maximum over the display interval, either by max-folding the received blocks or by holding with a release. With 64-512-sample host blocks, one 30 Hz tick spans many blocks, and a drum transient sits in only one or two of them.

**Consequence.** The kit meter flickers near zero while drums play, rarely shows the transient peak, and the red clip colour (>0.9) is unreliable. Pad glow also misses short hits whose peak block was not the last one delivered.

**Evidence.** controller.cpp:1717-1723 `for (... i < numBlocks ...) std::memcpy(&cachedMeters_, blocks[i].data, sizeof(MetersBlock));`; :1730-1737 glow from cachedMeters_ after the loop; kit_meters_view.cpp:31-33 setPeaks stores the value directly.

**Suggested fix.** In onDataExchangeBlocksReceived, fold max(peakL/peakR) and max glow bucket per pad across all received blocks into an accumulator. The timer consumes and resets it. Optionally add a peak-hold/decay in KitMetersView. Test: deliver three blocks with peaks 0.9, 0.1, 0.1 in one call, and assert the meter view receives 0.9.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: per-block peaks (processor.cpp:794-800), per-block glow levels (voice_pool.cpp:363-375, 486) and an unconditional overwrite in PadGlowPublisher::publish (pad_glow_publisher.h:48-60); the controller keeps the last block deliberately ("Use the most recent block (Innexus pattern); older blocks are stale", controller.cpp:1716) and the timer (:1511-1525) passes it through updateMeterViews (controller_view_sync.cpp:312-317) with no hold. No test covers it. Downgrade: display-only, and the clip colour is rarely reachable since the main bus passes the -1 dBTP limiter (~0.89) and -6 dB default master gain.
- Confirmed: the IMessage fallback also overwrites per delivery; PadGridView::pollGlow (pad_grid_view.cpp:309-329) just copies the snapshot. Spec 141 FR-044 (spec.md:252) asks for a "stereo peak+RMS display" and no RMS or hold exists. A decaying hit still shows its tail, so the meter is not dead but under-reads transients. Low.
- Confirmed, impact lower: the SDK fallback (dataexchange.cpp) makes it worse, with only 4 blocks (processor.cpp:1150), lockBlock returning nullptr when empty (137-153) and one IMessage per block (174-191), each overwriting the cache. Toms and kicks read only a few dB low; short hats and clicks (tens of ms) can be missed or under-read by 10 dB or more; at default settings the displayed peak caps near 0.45, so the > 0.9 clip colour barely applies.

#### MB-103 — Inline kit and pad browsers cycle by preset name only and keep a stale name after a project load or pad switch

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** ui-wiring · **Dimension:** ui-wiring

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/ui/preset_inline_browser_view.h:112-139](plugins/membrum/src/ui/preset_inline_browser_view.h#L112)

**Problem.** cyclePreset() rescans the preset folder on every click (file IO on the UI thread). It then finds the current preset by `p.name == currentName_`, so duplicate names (a user preset that shares a factory name, or the same name in two categories) always resolve to the first match, and prev/next loops between them. lastKitPresetName_/lastPadPresetName_ are only written by the load providers (controller.cpp:748, 771). setComponentState (a project load) does not clear them, and the pad name is one global string, not one per pad.

**Why wrong.** After a host project load the kit label still shows the last browser-loaded kit, and Next continues from that kit. After the selected pad changes, the pad label still shows the preset loaded on the previous pad, and Next loads into the new pad from there.

**Consequence.** Users see a wrong current-preset name, and cycling jumps or loops unexpectedly.

**Evidence.** preset_inline_browser_view.h:116 `auto presets = manager_->scanPresets();`, :122-125 `return p.name == currentName_;`; controller_state.cpp:64-99 setComponentState never touches lastKitPresetName_.

**Suggested fix.** Track the current PresetInfo by path, not by name. Clear the kit name in setComponentState. Keep per-pad last-pad-preset names, or clear the label on pad selection. Test: two presets with the same name in different categories; Next from the second one must reach the third.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: scanPresets clears the cache and recursively walks user and factory folders (shared preset_manager.cpp:108-127); PresetInfo::operator< compares name only (preset_info.h:30-32), so duplicates sort adjacent and Next gets stuck on the second duplicate while Prev skips the first. The names are only copied into the views at creation (controller.cpp:1213, 1226), setComponentState (controller_state.cpp:64-99) never clears them, and the pad name is one string (controller.h:407). Low: label and cycling only.
- Confirmed: duplicate names really occur because user and factory folders are merged into one list; padInlineBrowser_ is touched only by the load provider (controller.cpp:772-773), view creation (1227) and teardown (1688). No spec, comment or test treats this as intended, and no test covers InlinePresetBrowserView. The scan runs on a click on the UI thread, not a real-time violation. Low.
- Confirmed: the 20 factory kit names are unique (globbed resources/presets/Kit Presets), so the trap needs a user preset saved under a factory name: with [X(user), X(factory), Y], Next can never reach Y. No other writer or setCurrentPresetName call exists. UI display and navigation only; low.

#### MB-104 — modeToggleButton_ is write-only and never nulled; the toggle visibility is re-applied with invalid() on every timer tick

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** ui-wiring · **Dimension:** ui-wiring

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:1182, 1533](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L1182)

**Problem.** createCustomView stores modeToggleButton_ for each of the two templates (both contain the ModeToggleButton, editor.uidesc:131, 179). Nothing reads it, and neither willClose (1643-1689) nor viewWillDelete (1461-1478) clears it, so it dangles after every template swap and editor close. Separately, the poll timer calls updateMorphEnabledToggleVisibility every 33 ms, and that helper does setVisible()+invalid() unconditionally (controller_view_sync.cpp:217-218). The comment says this works around a template-swap visibility bug instead of fixing it.

**Why wrong.** Every cached raw view pointer must be nulled before its view dies. Any future reader of modeToggleButton_ (for example, to relabel the button after a kit preset changes uiMode) would get a use-after-free. Repainting every frame hides the real ordering bug and costs paint work.

**Consequence.** No crash today, because nothing reads the pointer. This is a maintenance trap plus constant 30 Hz repaints of the toggle.

**Evidence.** controller.cpp:1182 `modeToggleButton_ = view;` (only write; grep finds no read); controller.cpp:1533 `updateMorphEnabledToggleVisibility();` inside the timer lambda; controller_view_sync.cpp:217-218 `setVisible(visible); invalid();`.

**Suggested fix.** Remove modeToggleButton_, or null it in viewWillDelete/willClose and register the listener. Once the body gate is removed (see the gating finding), drop the per-tick visibility call.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: declared at controller.h:224, written only at controller.cpp:1182; the action lambda captures `view` (1173-1181); viewWillDelete nulls 10 other pointers, not this one, and no view listener is registered. CView::setVisible is a no-op when unchanged (cview.cpp:1041-1053) but invalid() -> invalidRect (cview.h:79, cview.cpp:875-881) repaints at ~30 Hz while a Membrane pad is selected; the timer comment at controller.cpp:1531-1532 claiming a no-op is contradicted by the code. Low.
- Confirmed: the comment at controller.cpp:1455-1459 says stale pointers after a template swap caused crashes before, which is why viewWillDelete exists; the helper's own comment (controller_view_sync.cpp:212-216) says the state check is skipped on purpose. No test pins it; low, no change.
- Facts correct, recommends nit: no use-after-free is possible today, since nothing reads the member, the timer stops first in willClose (1648-1652), and viewWillDelete nulls morphEnabledToggleView_ (1474) so the helper returns early (209-210). The extra invalid() is a small rect on a tick that already repaints the meter and CPU views (1525).

#### MB-108 — NoiseColor, NoiseOscillator's own parameter type, lives in core/pattern_freeze_types.h, so five Membrum headers include an Iterum Pattern Freeze header

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** shared-dsp-contract · **Dimension:** shared-dsp-contracts

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/pattern_freeze_types.h:124-136](dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/pattern_freeze_types.h#L124) (consumers plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h:15, click_layer.h:19, bodies/noise_body.h:27, exciters/noise_burst_exciter.h:31, exciters/feedback_exciter.h:29; primitives/noise_oscillator.h:18)

**Problem.** Membrum includes core/pattern_freeze_types.h only for the NoiseColor enum. That is a real dependency: NoiseOscillator::setColor takes NoiseColor, and primitives/noise_oscillator.h itself includes this header. The enum is the noise generator's public API type but is declared in a header named after Iterum's Pattern Freeze mode, together with that mode's unrelated types.

**Why wrong.** It is layer-legal (core). But a shared primitive's API type should live with the primitive (or in a neutral core header) so that changes to Pattern Freeze types do not ripple into every NoiseOscillator consumer, including Membrum and ring_modulator, noise_organism and oscillator_adapters in dsp/. Also, Membrum's NoiseLayer uses only 4 of the kNoiseColorCount = 8 colours.

**Consequence.** A maintenance trap, not an audio defect. Refactoring or renaming Pattern Freeze types breaks a drum synth's noise layer, and every edit to the header recompiles Membrum's voice.

**Evidence.** pattern_freeze_types.h:124 'enum class NoiseColor : uint8_t { White = 0, Pink, Brown, Blue, Violet, Grey, Velvet, RadioStatic };' :135 kNoiseColorCount = 8; noise_oscillator.h:18 #include <krate/dsp/core/pattern_freeze_types.h>; grep of plugins/membrum/src: 5 includes (noise_body.h:27, click_layer.h:19, feedback_exciter.h:29, noise_burst_exciter.h:31, noise_layer.h:15).

**Suggested fix.** Move NoiseColor and kNoiseColorCount into a neutral core header (e.g. core/noise_color.h). Include it from pattern_freeze_types.h for compatibility and from noise_oscillator.h. Switch the five Membrum headers to the new header. No behaviour change. The build gate covers it.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed, recommends nit: the header holds Pattern Freeze types (PatternType :27, SliceMode :56, PitchInterval :81, EnvelopeShape :161, CaptureLength :186, DryMode :215, PatternFreezeConstants :227) plus NoiseColor (:124-141); noise_oscillator.h:56 documents the dependency; Membrum uses only NoiseColor (noise_layer.h:306-309 maps 4 colours). The five direct includes are redundant because noise_oscillator.h already pulls the header in. No behaviour, audio, real-time or state impact.
- Confirmed, recommends nit: the file describes itself as "Type definitions for Pattern Freeze Mode (spec 069)" (:1-11); ring_modulator.h:21 and noise_organism.h:91 also include it only for the enum; no spec, comment or test justifies the placement. A rename would fail at compile time, the header is small and constexpr-only, and the "4 of 8 colours" remark is not a defect.
- Confirmed, no change: CaptureLength and DryMode come from the recent specs/iterum-freeze work, so the header is still being edited and every edit rebuilds Membrum's voice; clap_exciter.h:59 uses NoiseColor::White only transitively. "Renaming Pattern Freeze types breaks the noise layer" is overstated (renaming PatternType does not touch NoiseColor); build churn plus a misleading location and comment fits low.

#### MB-111 — Global proxy registrations drift from their per-pad twins (defaults and titles); Ctrl-click reset writes a different value than the per-pad default

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** duplication · **Dimension:** duplication-drift

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:288-292, 336, 347](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L288)

**Problem.** Each proxied parameter is registered twice by hand (global in kPhase2Specs and the inline registrations, per-pad in kPadParamSpecs) with no shared spec. Drift: NoiseBurst Duration proxy default 0.230769 (5 ms) vs per-pad 0.5 (8.5 ms, controller.cpp:202, pad_config.h:236). PitchEnv Start proxy default 0.070721 (about 23.6 Hz) vs per-pad 0.0 (controller.cpp:181, pad_config.h:202). PitchEnv Curve per-pad registered default 0.5 vs PadConfig 0.0 (pad_config.h:205). Titles: global kDecayId is 'Resonance' and kStrikePositionId is 'Strike Point' vs per-pad 'Decay' / 'Strike Position'. kPadParamSpecs also says stepCount 5 for the 7-entry exciter and 6-entry body lists (:168-169). That value is unused because of the special-case branch at :685-708, but it is wrong.

**Why wrong.** VST3Editor gives each bound control the parameter's defaultNormalizedValue, so the knob's reset-to-default writes the PROXY default into the selected pad. The two registrations describe the same field and must agree.

**Consequence.** Ctrl/Cmd-click on the NoiseBurst Duration knob sets 5 ms instead of the 8.5 ms per-pad default. Host parameter lists show 'Resonance' for a control the editor labels 'Decay'. An editor-reset pad differs from a fresh pad.

**Evidence.** controller.cpp:336 '{.id = kExciterNoiseBurstDurationId, ... .defaultValue = 0.230769, .unit = "ms" }' vs :202 '{.offset = kPadNoiseBurstDuration, ... .defaultValue = 0.5 }'; :347 PitchEnv Start 0.070721 vs :181 0.0; :288 STR16("Resonance") for kDecayId vs :172 "Decay"; :291 STR16("Strike Point") vs :173 "Strike Position"; :168-169 stepCount = 5 for Exciter Type / Body Model.

**Suggested fix.** Generate the global proxy registrations from kPadParamSpecs plus a small table of title/unit overrides, keyed by kProxyMappings, so default, range and step count come from one row. Test: for every kProxyMappings row, assert proxy defaultNormalizedValue == per-pad defaultNormalizedValue == the PadConfig{} field.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: every drifted value checks out (noise_burst_exciter.h:77-78 maps 0.230769 to 5 ms, 0.5 to 8.5 ms; PitchEnv Curve spec 0.5 at controller.cpp:184 vs PadConfig 0.0f; editor label "Decay" at editor.uidesc:152, 236). Only Friction Pressure has a proxy-vs-per-pad default test (test_audit_ui_controller_batch.cpp:118, :137). Disputes the Ctrl-click path: ArcKnob::onMouseDown (arc_knob.h:131-150) has no default-value handling, so only a host-side reset or generic editor writes 5 ms / 0.0707; the fix's test should exercise host reset. Low.
- Confirmed, repeats open prior finding L-10 (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:302, not marked DONE): CControl's view event listener (vstgui ccontrol.cpp:33-53) handles the Ctrl-click before ArcKnob's onMouseDown, so the reset does write 5 ms; audit finding 10 fixed the same class for Friction Pressure only (controller.cpp:337-341, correctness-audit.md:198). PitchEnv Start reaches no knob (only PitchEnvelopeDisplay, uidesc:160, 330). Refuted parts: the 'Resonance' / 'Strike Point' titles are pinned on purpose by membrum_vst_tests.cpp:116-120, and stepCount 5 is unused. Low.
- Confirmed: VST3Editor copies defaultNormalizedValue onto the control (vst3editor.cpp:287), CControl::Impl::viewOnEvent (ccontrol.cpp:33-52) performs the edit, and processParameterChanges (processor.cpp:304-305) writes it into the selected pad; plugin_ids.h:65 still says "default 5". Effect is a 3.5 ms shorter burst on NoiseBurst pads after a reset; the PitchEnv Start drift is reachable only through a host reset. Low.

#### MB-113 — Secondary shell bank copies the B1 override formula with its own 0.4 fallback instead of using the body's real damping law

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** duplication · **Dimension:** duplication-drift

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1470-1480](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1470)

**Problem.** configureSecondaryBank recomputes the body's b1 as 0.2 + n*49.8, a copy of dampingLawFromParams, and substitutes 0.4 when the pad holds the -1 sentinel. A sentinel pad's real b1 is 1/decayTime from the mapper (available in cachedMapperResult_.damping.b1), not the 20.1 s^-1 implied by 0.4.

**Why wrong.** The comment says the shell must decay at least 2.5x faster than the body it accents. For sentinel pads the comparison uses a made-up body b1, so the ratio is not the documented one. For example, decayTime 0.03 s gives a real body b1 of 33 s^-1 against a shell b1 of 50: 1.5x, not 2.5x.

**Consequence.** On sentinel pads with Coupling Strength > 0 and short decay, the shell tail can sit close to the body tail and contradict the documented intent. Edge case.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:1472-1474 'const float bodyN = std::clamp((bodyDampingB1_ >= 0.0f) ? bodyDampingB1_ : 0.4f, 0.0f, 1.0f); const float bodyB1 = 0.2f + bodyN * 49.8f;' vs membrane_mapper.h:73 'law.b1 = 0.2f + n * 49.8f;'.

**Suggested fix.** Use cachedMapperResult_.damping.b1 (the law actually pushed to the bank) as bodyB1 and delete the duplicated formula and the 0.4 fallback. Test: a sentinel pad with decay 0.05 and secondary enabled must have shell T60 <= 0.4 x body T60.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: for a sentinel pad the body law is dampingLawFromLegacy, b1 = 1/clamp(decayTime, 0.01, 5) (modal_resonator_bank.h:136-138; override only when bodyDampingB1 >= 0, membrane_mapper.h:71; sentinel default at pad_config.h:282); cachedMapperResult_ is set at drum_voice.h:220-221, before configureSecondaryBank at :396, so the fix is viable. The 2.5x ratio breaks below decayTime ~0.05 s, reachable on a Membrane (0.045 s at material = size = decay = 0, ratio ~2.26; 0.0315 s with decaySkew = 1, ratio ~1.6), but the shell never outlasts the body. Low.
- Mechanism confirmed, consequence weaker; recommends downgrade: the minimum reachable decayTime is ~0.0315 s (membrane_mapper.h:146-152, shell_mapper.h:66), so the worst ratio is ~1.58x and the comment's purpose (drum_voice.h:1464-1467, no hanging shell layer) still holds; only the 2.5x figure fails, in a corner where both tails are very short (body T60 ~0.22 s). The finding's 0.03 s example is just below the reachable range.
- Defect real, consequence smaller; recommends nit: the violating zone needs material near 0, decay <= ~0.06, secondary enabled, coupling > 0 and an untouched sentinel; plate, bell and noise-body bases start at 0.2-0.4 s (plate_mapper.h:65, bell_mapper.h:61, noise_body_mapper.h:123). Default kit pads have secondary off (default_kit.h:78) and the generator defaults bodyDampingB1 to 0.40 (membrum_preset_generator.cpp:135), so no factory kit takes the sentinel branch. Unmentioned side effect: across the normal range the fallback makes sentinel-pad shells about 2x shorter than intended (b1 ~50 instead of 25), a mild timbral deviation.

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** duplication · **Dimension:** duplication-drift

**Suggested fix.** Move one implementation to plugins/shared/src/ui/adsr_expanded_overlay.h (Krate::Plugins) with a close-callback API, port the three plugins, and cover it once in shared_tests.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed, recommends nit: all three wrap ADSRDisplay identically (`new Krate::Plugins::ADSRDisplay(displayRect, nullptr, -1)`: membrum :143, ruinae :168, innexus :151); Membrum closes through an OutlineActionButton lambda (:130-134). Corrections: the Innexus copy has no setTitle / setColors (only Ruinae :60, :66 and Membrum :50, :55), so drift is wider than stated; the Membrum header (:12-13) says the local copy is deliberate. No overlay exists in plugins/shared/src/ui; maintainability only.

The deliberate-copy reason at Membrum :12-13 ("so we can use Membrum's OutlineActionButton") no longer holds: membrum_buttons.h:26-27 just does `using Krate::Plugins::OutlineActionButton`, defined in plugins/shared/src/ui/outline_button.h:215, and Ruinae's copy includes the same shared header (:17). No runtime fault.
- Confirmed, recommends nit: Membrum's copy is live (filterEnvOverlay_, controller.cpp:1592, controller.h:277); the close-mechanism difference is a documented choice (:12-13), and the risk that a fix misses the other copies is hypothetical, with no divergent bug cited.

#### MB-117 — MB-PP-06: Applying one pad field through its selected-pad proxy ID skips the reclassify and recompute that the per-pad ID route runs, and the editor uses the proxy route

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** parallel-path · **Dimension:** parallel-paths · **Also flagged by:** test-gaps, gestalt-processor

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:178-207 vs 282-297, 334-336](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L178)

**Problem.** processParameterChanges handles the same field twice. The per-pad branch for kPadExciterType, kPadBodyModel and kPadTSPitchEnvTime writes the field, reclassifies the pad and recomputes the coupling matrix (178-207). The global proxy cases kExciterTypeId, kBodyModelId and kToneShaperPitchEnvTimeId write the same field through setPadConfigSelector / setPadConfigField and do neither (282-297, 334-336). The editor binds the global IDs (uidesc 34-38; COptionMenu ExciterType/BodyModel at 173-175 and 213-215; PitchEnvelopeDisplay time-tag at 160/330). The controller's proxy mirror writes the per-pad param with the base setter only, without performEdit (controller.cpp:866-871). So the processor never receives the per-pad ID for a GUI edit. A later recompute (Snare Buzz, Tom Resonance) does not reclassify either. The two choke routes differ as well: setPadChokeGroup versus setPadConfigField, with different clamps for > 8 (voice_pool.cpp:739 vs 643-646).

**Why wrong.** Each pad field should go through one handler whatever the ID it arrives on. Today the per-pad branch and ~55 proxy cases are two hand-written offset tables (processor.cpp:267-522 duplicates kProxyMappings, controller.cpp:84-155), and the side effects exist in only one of them.

**Consequence.** Changing a pad's body or exciter in the GUI leaves padCategories_ and the matrix stale for the session. The effect is inaudible today only because the matrix is unused (MB-PP-05). It becomes a real bug when that is fixed. The tests exercise only the per-pad route (test_coupling_integration.cpp:438, 462).

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:189-198 per-pad body: `voicePool_.setPadConfigSelector(padIdx, padOff, idx); padCategories_[...] = classifyPad(...); recomputeCouplingMatrix();` vs :290-296 proxy: `voicePool_.setPadConfigSelector(selectedPadIndex_, kPadBodyModel, idx); break;`; :334-335 `case kToneShaperPitchEnvTimeId: voicePool_.setPadConfigField(selectedPadIndex_, kPadTSPitchEnvTime, fValue); break;`; editor.uidesc:35 `<control-tag name="BodyModel" tag="201"/>`; controller.cpp:869-871 base-class setParamNormalized(padId) under suppressProxyForward_.

**Suggested fix.** Have the proxy case translate global -> padParamId(selectedPadIndex_, offset) using one shared constexpr table (the controller's kProxyMappings, moved to plugin_ids.h-level code both sides may include), then fall into the same per-pad handler. Delete the 55-case proxy switch. Test: write kBodyModelId = NoiseBody with selected pad 3, and assert classifyPad(padConfig(3)) equals the stored category for pad 3 (a test accessor), as the per-pad route does.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: the per-pad branch (processor.cpp:178-207) reclassifies and recomputes, the proxy cases (282-289, 290-297, 334-336) do not; the editor binds the global tags (editor.uidesc:34-35, menus at 173/175, 213/215); Controller::setParamNormalized (controller.cpp:862-871) and forwardGlobalToPad (987-1000) mirror without performEdit, so only the global ID reaches the processor. padCategories_ is written only at processor.cpp:115, 185/196/204, 986 and 1011; kSnareBuzzId / kTomResonanceId (411-424) recompute without reclassifying. Inaudible today: couplingMatrix_ is read only by couplingMatrixForTest() (processor.h:81). Choke side claim not verified.
- Confirmed, with a downgrade to nit (or a fold into MB-PP-05) proposed: staleness lasts until the next kit (:986-988) or pad-preset load (:1011-1012); the "Phase 5: body model change can affect pad category" comments show the reclassify was meant to run on every change; nothing on the audio path reads padCategories_ or the matrix. The choke sub-claim is cosmetic: the kChokeGroupId proxy clamps to 0..8 (processor.cpp:379-386) and setPadConfigField clamps to 0..8 (voice_pool.cpp:643-646), so the "> 8 -> 0" branch at voice_pool.cpp:739 is unreachable.
- Confirmed, downgrade to nit proposed: couplingMatrix_ is written only by recomputeFromTier1 (processor.cpp:138) and read only by the test accessor (processor.h:81); padCategories_ is read only inside recomputeCouplingMatrix (processor.cpp:141), so no sample, meter or saved byte changes. Both choke routes give the same group for any normalized input (lround(v*8) vs (int)(v*8+0.5)). The duplicated proxy table is a fair maintainability point.

#### MB-118 — MB-PP-10: The two VoicePool::processBlock overloads have drifted: only the mono one releases coupling resonators when a voice finishes naturally, and production runs the multi-bus one

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, lowered in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** parallel-path · **Dimension:** parallel-paths

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:386-396 vs 514-519](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp#L386)

**Problem.** Rendering the pool has two near-copies: processBlock(outL, outR, n) at 306-437 and the multi-bus processBlock at 443-564. When a main voice finishes naturally, the mono overload calls couplingEngine_->noteOff(slot) (389-390) and the multi-bus overload does not (514-519). The processor uses the multi-bus overload whenever more than one output bus exists, and Membrum always declares 1 + 14 aux buses (processor.cpp:96-107). The mono overload therefore runs only in tests and single-bus setups. Without the noteOff, the finished voice stays listed as an owner of its resonators (sympathetic_resonance.h:264-298) until that slot's next noteOn, which calls noteOff(voiceId) first (sympathetic_resonance.h:181). Until then the refCount stays inflated. Merges weight frequencies by refCount (sympathetic_resonance.h:199-203), so a later voice that merges into a stale resonator is pulled toward the dead voice's partial.

**Why wrong.** Two renderers of the same pool must stay behaviour-equivalent. The mono overload is the one the coupling-lifecycle comments describe, and the shipped path silently lacks the step. Each mid-function difference (aux accumulation, coupling release) is a future drift point.

**Consequence.** Resonator ownership leaks until slot reuse, which skews merged resonator frequencies (detuned sympathetic ring) and refCounts. A test written against the mono overload passes while the shipped path differs.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.cpp:386-395 `else if (meta_[slot].state == VoiceSlotState::Active) { if (couplingEngine_ != nullptr) couplingEngine_->noteOff(slot); meta_[slot].state = VoiceSlotState::Free; ... allocator_.voiceFinished(...); }` vs :514-518 `else if (meta_[slot].state == VoiceSlotState::Active) { meta_[slot].state = VoiceSlotState::Free; meta_[slot].currentLevel = 0.0f; allocator_.voiceFinished(...); }`; processor.cpp:97-107 one main plus aux outputs added in initialize; sympathetic_resonance.h:181 `noteOff(voiceId);` at the start of noteOn; :201 `float newFreq = (existingFreq * static_cast<float>(rc) + freq) / static_cast<float>(rc + 1);`.

**Suggested fix.** Collapse to one implementation: the mono overload calls the multi-bus one with auxL = auxR = nullptr and numOutputBuses = 1. Then fix the natural-finish branch once (couplingEngine_->noteOff(slot), and the allocator noteOff before voiceFinished per the voice-pool map). Test: a multi-bus processBlock with the coupling engine attached. Strike a pad with couplingAmount > 0 and render until it retires. Assert the engine holds no resonator owned by that slot (test accessor), as the mono overload already guarantees.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed, downgrade proposed: every other release path calls the engine (Quietest steal voice_pool.cpp:167-168, allocator Steal 207-208, kit switch 272-273, choke 1041-1042); process() takes the mono overload only when `numOutputBuses <= 1` (processor.cpp:633-636), else the multi-bus one (663-666). If the reused slot's pad has couplingAmount 0, noteOn is skipped (voice_pool.cpp:243-248) and the stale owner lasts longer. Nothing leaks: the reclaim pass (sympathetic_resonance.h:337-351) frees resonators below -96 dB and clears ownerVoiceIds_; merges happen only within ~0.3 Hz (header line 175), so the skew is under ~0.3 Hz.
- Confirmed: the engine is attached in production (processor.cpp:1083, setCouplingEngine); noteOff (sympathetic_resonance.h:264-298) is the only owner removal; no test exercises the multi-bus natural-finish path with the engine. The drift is the substantive point; the audible consequence is minor.
- Confirmed, impact much smaller than claimed: VoicePool::noteOff (voice_pool.cpp:283-299) does not release coupling either. Stale ownership touches only ownerVoiceIds_, voiceIds_ and refCounts_ (gain, Q, envelope untouched); merges need a partial within kMergeThresholdHz = 0.3 Hz (sympathetic_resonance.h:49, 448-458); worst-case error < 0.15 Hz (about 4 cents at 60 Hz) on a return the limiter holds at or below -20 dBFS (processor.cpp:693-703). The owner list (kMaxOwnersPerResonator = 8, line 64) clears at reclaim.

#### MB-121 — MANUAL.md describes a different engine: signal-flow order, exciter list, shell coupling, tension, air loading, meter, morph curves and RT safety disagree with the code

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, lowered in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/MANUAL.md:5, 39-62, 56, 194-196, 221, 225, 237, 241, 252-257, 263, 315, 349, 362, 393, 426, 431-432, 450, 505](plugins/membrum/MANUAL.md#L5)

**Problem.** Stale or false statements, each checked against code:
1. :5 and :39-40 list six exciters and "36 base voice fabrics". ExciterType has 7, including Clap (exciter_type.h kCount = 7), so there are 42 combinations.
2. :54-59 place the Noise and Click layers AFTER the Tone Shaper ("added in parallel" below the SVF). Code sums body + noise + click BEFORE ModeInject, NonlinearCoupling and the ToneShaper (drum_voice.h:882-896).
3. :56 "Pitch envelope updates body fundamental per-sample". The fast path retunes once per chunk of up to 2048 samples (drum_voice.h:734-745).
4. The signal flow omits the main-bus -1 dBTP TruePeakLimiter (processor.cpp:717) between coupling and master gain.
5. :194-196: Shell is called "Cylindrical-shell modes" (code: free-free bar ratios, shell_mapper.h:14), Bell "Chladni patterns" (code: Hibberts bell partials), Noise Body "40 + broadband" (code: kNoiseBodyModeCount = 64).
6. :221 gives Mallet the secondary "Burst Duration". MalletExciter reads no duration; noiseBurstDuration feeds only NoiseBurst.
7. :252-257 describe a 24-mode shell bank that "exchanges energy bidirectionally" and is "clamped to a 0.25 effective maximum". The code is feedforward only (drum_voice.h:814-843) and maps coupling over the full 0..1 range (drum_voice.h:1494-1497, audit L-7).
8. :263 "Depth scales by velocity² at note-on". The velocity² term was removed (drum_voice.h:408-421: knob * kTensionEnergyScale).
9. :241 "Rossing ... low-mode frequency depression (5% at the fundamental, tapering toward zero by mode 12)". The table holds the fundamental and RAISES (2,1), (3,1), (4,1) and (5,1) by 12-27% (membrane_modes.h:94-105).
10. :362 Morph Curve "Linear, exponential, logarithmic, S-curve". The registered StringList has 2 entries (controller.cpp:400-404).
11. :450 Meter "Peak + RMS". MetersBlock carries peaks only (meters_block.h:22-30).
12. :393 pad subcategories "HiHat" with no "Tonal". Code: Hat and Tonal (membrum_preset_config.h).
13. :349 Nonlinear Coupling "Energy-limited cross-mode coupling ... FM-like sidebands". Code is an envelope-driven recipSqrt waveshaper with no limiter (nonlinear_coupling.h:6-38).
14. :315 Drive "Alias-safe waveshaper". ReciprocalSqrt Waveshaper, no ADAA (tone_shaper.h:96-102).
15. :431-432: Snare Buzz and Tom Resonance described as audible, but they are dead (see the coupling-matrix finding). :426 says a pad's output is "mixed into other pads' excitation paths", while the code adds a SympatheticResonance return to L/R.
16. :505 zero allocations and pre-allocated variants is false (see the exciter-swap finding).
17. :237 "Legacy Decay and Material still work ... when the Phase 8A knobs are at their default position". The registered default is 0.5 while the engine default is the -1 sentinel (controller.cpp:227-228 vs pad_config.h:282-283), so returning the knob to its default makes it an explicit override.

**Why wrong.** The manual is the user contract and is published to krateaudio.com. Every item above describes behaviour the code does not have.

**Consequence.** Users are taught the wrong order (noise and click are shaped by the filter and drive), parameters that do nothing, features that do not exist (4 morph curves, an RMS meter, bidirectional shell coupling) and a sub-bass effect of air loading that is actually an upward shift. Sound-design expectations and support questions follow from this.

**Evidence.** MANUAL.md:59 `|  Noise Layer + Click Layer (added in parallel) |` below the Tone Shaper. drum_voice.h:882-883 `const float combined = bodyScratch[i] + noiseScratch[i] + clickScratch[i]; const float shaped = toneShaper_.processSample(combined);`. MANUAL.md:252 "exchanges energy bidirectionally at block rate ... stability-clamped to a 0.25 effective maximum" vs drum_voice.h:1496 `return std::clamp(couplingStrength_, 0.0f, 1.0f);`. MANUAL.md:241 vs membrane_modes.h:99 `1.0000f, 1.0000f, 1.1192f, 1.0000f, 1.2012f, ...`. controller.cpp:403-404 `appendString(STR16("Linear")); appendString(STR16("Exponential"));`.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite the Signal Flow diagram and the listed tables from the code. Add Clap and the bus limiter, fix the mode counts and body descriptions, remove "Burst Duration" from Mallet, and correct the shell coupling, tension, air loading, morph curve, meter, Drive and NLC rows. Consider a docs test that greps MANUAL.md for the exciter count and kNoiseBodyModeCount.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 4, 7, 10, 11: exciter_type.h:19-20 `Clap = 6, kCount = 7` (exciter table MANUAL.md:218-225 lists six); drum_voice.h:882-883 and :892-896 sum the layers before modeInject, NLC and the shaper (comment at :851-854); drum_voice.h:814-843 "This is feedforward (body → shell), not feedback" and :1494-1497 removed the 0.25 ceiling (L-7); controller.cpp:395-405 registers two curves, stepCount 1 (:197); meters_block.h:22-23 peaks only; diagram MANUAL.md:75-83 has no limiter. Other sub-items not re-opened. Medium fits a published manual that teaches the wrong processing.
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 7, 9, 10, 11: membrane_modes.h:98-99 holds index 0 and raises (2,1)..(5,1) by 1.1192, 1.2012, 1.2321, 1.2668. No spec, comment or test defends the manual's wording. Documentation only, no audio or state change: downgrade from medium. Items (3)-(6), (8), (12)-(17) not re-verified.
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and the missing limiter: controller registers "Clap" at controller.cpp:308; drum_voice.h:408-421 removed velocity² (N-1). Items 5, 6, 12-16 not re-derived. Downgrade: no audio, state or RT effect, and some errors self-correct in use (the menus show two curves and Clap); the real harm is the wrong mental model.

#### MB-122 — docs/index.html (published landing page) repeats false engine claims: 6 exciters, 40-mode Noise Body, bidirectional shell loop, String stretch control, RT pre-allocation

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, lowered in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/docs/index.html:7, 10, 66, 74, 75, 77, 78, 89, 93, 102, 103, 117-120](plugins/membrum/docs/index.html#L7)

**Problem.**
1. :7/:10 meta description and :66/:74 say 6 exciters and leave out Clap (code has 7).
2. :75 and :120 say Noise Body has 40 modes (code 64).
3. :117 "Shell — 32 cylindrical-shell modes" (code: free-free bar).
4. :119 "Bell — 16 Chladni-pattern bell modes with metallic damping (b3 = 0)". bell_mapper.h:53 gives brightness 0.7+0.3*material, so legacy b3 = (1-brightness)*4e-5 is non-zero below material 1.
5. :118 "String — Waveguide string body with mode-stretch control". StringMapper ignores modeStretch.
6. :78 "bidirectional energy exchange. Stability-clamped two-bank feedback loop". The code is feedforward with no return path (drum_voice.h:819-843).
7. :77 "depresses the lowest modes for realistic kick/tom sub-bass". Code raises the (m,1) modes and holds the fundamental.
8. :89 "toms ring the snare wires, kick excites the floor tom". The matrix only knows Kick->Snare and Tom->Tom, and it is not applied at all.
9. :93 "Zero allocations ... ExciterBank and BodyBank pre-allocate every variant". False (exciter_bank.h:234-235 prepare on swap -> DelayLine::resize).
10. :102 "Impulse — Single-sample velocity-scaled impulse". ImpulseExciter wraps ImpactExciter, a 0.5-15 ms Hertzian pulse (impulse_exciter.h:6-39).
11. :103 "Mallet ... velocity-controlled contact time". Contact comes from mass and the size hint (mallet_exciter.h:51-58).

**Why wrong.** The page is generated into krateaudio.com (root CLAUDE.md site rules), so these are public product claims. Each one contradicts the cited code.

**Consequence.** Public marketing and SEO copy is wrong about the instrument's feature set (it understates the exciter count) and its RT safety, and promises coupling behaviour that does not exist.

**Evidence.** index.html:74 `<strong>6 exciter types</strong> &mdash; Impulse, Mallet, Noise Burst, Friction, FM Impulse, and Feedback`. exciter_type.h: Clap = 6, kCount = 7. index.html:120 "40-mode hybrid" vs noise_body_mapper.h:73 `kNoiseBodyModeCount = 64`. index.html:78 "bidirectional energy exchange" vs drum_voice.h:815 `// This is feedforward (body → shell), not feedback.`

**Suggested fix.** Correct the listed sentences against the code and regenerate the site with tools/gen-site.js. Keep the meta description within the SEO lint limits.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 6, 10 and the pre-allocation half of 9: index.html:100 also says "one of six excitation models"; exciter_bank.h:222-223 places a ClapExciter; drum_voice.h:1489 "That loop was removed"; exciter_bank.h:206-235 emplaces and prepares the variant on swap. DelayLine::resize not opened, so "zero allocations" is plausible, not verified. Items 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11 not re-checked. Documentation only: downgrade.
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 6, 9 (up-front preparation inaccurate), 10: no spec, comment or prior ruling marks the page as intentionally stale; per root CLAUDE.md the page is the template gen-site.js publishes. Downgrade: no audio or state effect. Items 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11 not verified.
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 6, 8, 9: coupling_matrix.h:55-62 has only Kick->Snare and Tom->Tom routes; ImpactExciter holds a DelayLine `combDelay_` (impact_exciter.h:66, :356) whose prepare calls `buffer_.resize(bufferSize)` (delay_line.h:316, std::vector at :295), so variants are not all pre-allocated; tools/gen-site.js:116/:253 reads the page as the landing template. The RT allocation belongs in a separate code finding. Downgrade to low.

#### MB-123 — membrum_signal_flow.dot draws a different signal path: no bus limiter, a shell feedback edge, aux-only routing, proxies fanning out to all pads, noise and click added at the SVF

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, lowered in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/docs/membrum_signal_flow.dot:61, 121-135, 149-152, 173, 175, 231, 239, 244-245, 270-271, 292, 316, 322-323](plugins/membrum/docs/membrum_signal_flow.dot#L61)

**Problem.**
1. :61 "Global proxies fan out to all 32 pads". processor.cpp:262-281 routes each proxy to selectedPadIndex_ only.
2. :121-135 show six exciters, no Clap.
3. :173 "24 shell modes, Bidirectional energy exchange ... Stability-clamped < 0.25", and :231 draws a "shell feedback" edge back into the body. The code is feedforward with a 0..1 range.
4. :175 "Depth scaled by velocity^2" was removed (drum_voice.h:408-421).
5. :239 "per-sample fundamental". The code retunes once per chunk.
6. :244-245 add noise and click at the SVF. The code sums them before ModeInject, NLC and the whole ToneShaper.
7. :270-271 "bus = 0 -> main, bus > 0 -> aux". A voice on an aux bus is written to main AND the aux (voice_pool.cpp:483-504; spec 139 SC-008).
8. :292 "Mono sum -> matrix -> per-pad excitation". There is no per-pad excitation and the matrix is unused (processor.cpp:699-705).
9. :322-323 master gain follows the main accumulator directly. The TruePeakLimiter at -1 dBTP (processor.cpp:717) is missing.
10. :316 "Peak / RMS publisher". Peaks only.
11. :149/:151/:152: Shell "cylindrical", Bell "Chladni ... b3=0", Noise Body "40 modes".

**Why wrong.** The .dot is the published Signal Flow Diagram that MANUAL.md:90 links. It should match the code's processing order and routing.

**Consequence.** The diagram teaches wrong routing (aux pads look removed from main, which would double them in a DAW mix), hides the limiter that shapes every loud hit, and shows a feedback loop that was removed for stability.

**Evidence.** dot:270-271 `bus_select -> main_accum [label="bus = 0"]; bus_select -> aux_accum [label="bus &gt; 0"];` vs spec 139 SC-008 (a pad on aux N writes to bus N AND main). dot:231 `secondary -> body_switch [... label="shell\nfeedback"]` vs drum_voice.h:842-843 `bodyScratch[i] += secOut[i]; // mix into output (passive)`. processor.cpp:717 `busLimiter_.processBlock(outL, outR, data.numSamples);` absent from the graph.

**Suggested fix.** Redraw from processor.cpp:620-737 and drum_voice.h:774-900: add busLimiter_, remove the shell feedback edge, move noise and click before ModeInject, show main+aux duplication, mark proxies as selected-pad only, and add Clap.

**Verifier notes:**

Items 5, 10, 11 not verified. Medium fits (keeps the filed severity).
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10: gen-site.js:146, 355-357, 449 renders it to signal-flow.html, linked from gen-site.js:236 and MANUAL.md:90; default_kit.h:315 uses Clap; drum_voice.h:820-843 "passive (additive only, no return path into the body)"; dot :316 and :338 say "Peak / RMS". Nothing marks the drift as intentional. Downgrade: no runtime consequence.

A user summing main and aux in a DAW gets the pad doubled (+6 dB coherent), which MANUAL.md:374/527 does not explain either. Downgraded to low (documentation accuracy).

#### MB-124 — plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md and the membrum SKILL state ring constraints the code no longer has (Friction sustains, modeInject rings undamped), and tests are skipped on that premise

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, lowered in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md:4, 7-8, 20-21](plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md#L4); also [.claude/skills/membrum/SKILL.md:9, 26-27](.claude/skills/membrum/SKILL.md#L9)

**Problem.**
1. CLAUDE.md:20-21 and SKILL.md:26-27: "modeInject > 0 rings undamped (flat plateau); Friction sustains without note-off ... Enforced by factory round-trip + infinite-ring tests". ModeInject now has a one-pole T60 envelope ("D2: ... Without an envelope any amount > 0 rang as an undamped flat plateau", mode_inject.h:84-91, 128-143), and the voice sets T60 = 0.3 + 4.7*decay^2. FrictionExciter is a transient: A 1 ms, D 40 ms, S 0, with an explicit gate-off at 0.041*sr (friction_exciter.h:7-18, 44, 112). Any sustain is body ring only.
2. CLAUDE.md:4 and SKILL.md:9 call Membrum "the current active-development plugin". Root CLAUDE.md names Seraphis.
3. CLAUDE.md:7-8 "no update/ dir". src/update/membrum_update_config.h exists, and root CLAUDE.md requires it.

**Why wrong.** These files auto-load as load-bearing domain constraints for every agent working on Membrum, and this audit's own brief repeats them as "INTENDED". They contradict the DSP.

**Consequence.** test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:460-466 skips every Friction pad of every factory kit on the "sustains WITHOUT note-off by design" premise, so a real infinite ring on a Friction pad (body or coupling) is never caught. Agents will also preserve or "re-fix" behaviour that does not exist.

**Evidence.** friction_exciter.h:7-9 "Phase 2 uses BowExciter in transient mode only: a short ADSR envelope ramps the bow pressure up and releases within ≤ 50 ms. Sustained bowing is out of scope". friction_exciter.h:44 `autoReleaseSamples_ = static_cast<int>(0.041f * ...)`. mode_inject.h:143 `env_ *= envCoeff_;`. test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:460-466 `// Friction sustains WITHOUT note-off by design ... continue;`.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite the ring constraints from the code (Friction = 46 ms transient bow and the body rings out; ModeInject decays with T60 tied to Decay). Remove the Friction skip in the infinite-ring sweep (or justify it with a measurement). Fix the active-development and update/ lines.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed all three parts; the ring text is at CLAUDE.md:23-25 and SKILL.md:26-28. mode_inject.h:84-93 setDecaySeconds clamped [0.05, 20] s, :142-143 `amount_ * env_ * bank_.process()` / `env_ *= envCoeff_`, envCoeff_ = 10^(-3/(sr*T60)) (:150-152); drum_voice.h:331 wires `0.3f + 4.7f * decay_ * decay_` (default decayT60Sec_ 1.5 s, :161). friction_exciter.h:39-44 envelope, gate-off at :112-115, inactive at :127-130; process() ignores bodyFeedback (:124); exciter_bank.h:213-214 is the only Friction path. The skip lives in tests/unit/processor/ (not tests/unit/preset/). No infinite ring on a Friction pad was shown: downgrade to low.
- Confirmed: tests/unit/exciters/test_friction_exciter.cpp:174 already pins "bow auto-releases within 50 ms (transient mode)"; the skip comment cites "D3" and is repeated at test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:551-552. The sweep with the skip removed was not run, so an actual Friction infinite ring is unproven: downgrade.
- Confirmed: drum_voice.h:159-162 holds the amp envelope at sustain 1.0 during the gate for every exciter type, so a Friction pad's ring without note-off is the decaying body (retirement at drum_voice.h:645-647), as for any exciter; tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp has 46 "Friction" references, so the per-pad "decays to silence within 8 s" check skips many factory pads. Keeps medium (a spec-conformance finding that disables a regression sweep).

#### MB-125 — drum_voice.h comments misdescribe the signal path, pitch-envelope refresh rate, note-off damp factor and shell-coupling timing

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, lowered in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance · **Also flagged by:** gestalt-voice

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:4-19, 447-450, 663, 703-707, 802-809, 1262-1266](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L4)

**Problem.**
1. :6-8 signal path "ExciterBank -> BodyBank -> ToneShaper -> NonlinearCoupling -> amp envelope -> level" leaves out the click layer (half into the excitation, full into the output), the noise layer, ModeInject, the secondary shell bank and hardClip. It also puts NonlinearCoupling AFTER the ToneShaper, while the code runs NLC before it (:893-896).
2. :15-17 "Pitch Envelope ... runs BEFORE the body each sample". In processBlockFast it is evaluated once per chunk and the remaining chunk-1 samples are discarded (:734-745).
3. :703-707 "A 20 ms sweep at 44.1 kHz produces ~14 refresh points across a 64-sample audio block — well below any audible stair-stepping". There is one refresh per chunk = per host block up to kMaxBlockSize 2048, so a 512-sample host gives 1-2 points in 20 ms, and 2048 gives 1.
4. :447-450 "0.993 yields ~50 ms". The constant is kNoteOffDampScale = 0.997 (:64).
5. :805-807 "applied one sample late ... reads the previous-block's primary output". The code feeds the same-chunk bodyScratch (:816-817).
6. :663 "≈1.4 s at 48 kHz / 256 blocks". silentBlockCount_ counts processBlock calls, so it is host-block dependent.
7. :1262-1266 orphaned doc comment "Only Membrane supports mid-note parameter updates". updateModalParameters (:1573-1581) updates every modal body.

**Why wrong.** Comments are the design record that spec FR-040 (chain order), SC-009 (pitch glide) and the retirement logic are checked against. Item 3 states a stair-stepping guarantee the code meets only at 64-sample host blocks.

**Consequence.** Readers (and reviewers checking SC-009) are told the pitch envelope is effectively per-sample when the output really depends on host block size. A short 808 drop at 512 or 1024 samples per block is stair-stepped. The other comments hide the real chain order.

**Evidence.** drum_voice.h:7 `//   ExciterBank -> BodyBank -> ToneShaper -> UnnaturalZone::NonlinearCoupling`. :741-745 `for (int i = 1; i < chunk; ++i) (void)toneShaper_.processPitchEnvelope(); retuneFundamental(pitchHz);`. :701 `const int chunk = remaining < kMaxBlockSize ? remaining : kMaxBlockSize;`. :448 "0.993 yields ~50 ms" vs :64 `kNoteOffDampScale = 0.997f`. :816-817 `secExc[i] = bodyScratch[i] * effectiveCoupling_;`.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite the header block from the code. State the chunk-rate refresh and its block-size dependence (or sub-chunk the fast path to 64 samples so the claim holds). Fix 0.993 -> 0.997, the "one sample late" and "1.4 s" text, and delete the orphan comment. Test for item 3: an SC-009 render at host block sizes 64 and 1024 must give the same glide within ±10%.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed all seven: click into excScratch at half amplitude (:793-794), shell into bodyScratch (:842-843), noise (:855-864), then modeInject -> NLC -> toneShaper -> env*level -> hardClip (:892-898); chunk = min(remaining, 2048) (:589, :701); only the Feedback exciter takes the slow path (:620); the voice gets the whole host block (voice_pool.cpp:356, 471; processor.cpp:636, 663), and the "~14 points" claim is repeated at :615-619. The real effect (block-size-dependent glide) is a separate audio defect; as a comment finding, medium is too high.
- Confirmed all seven; the block-size dependence of the pitch refresh was not found in AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md (searched "stair|block-rate|chunk"). Comment-only: low.
- Confirmed all seven; the slow path does the same once-per-chunk refresh (:960-964, :1021-1022). Keeps medium because item 3 hides a real, untested behaviour: a 20 ms 160 -> 50 Hz sweep at 512 samples gets about 2 pitch values and at 1024-2048 collapses to one held block; the only SC-009 test (tests/unit/tone_shaper/test_pitch_envelope_808.cpp:92-141) renders through voice.process(), the per-sample path (drum_voice.h:506-509), so it never exercises the chunk path.

#### MB-126 — voice_pool.h header still describes Phase 3.0 stubs, a no-op note-off, a broadcast helper and a reserved stereo scratch that no longer match the code

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.h:39-40, 115-117, 151-153, 182-191, 231, 303-305, 349-354, 358, 383-396](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.h#L39)

**Problem.**
1. :39-40 "Phase 3.0: scaffolding only -- all methods are stubs" and :231 "Query helpers (Phase 3.0 stubs)". All methods are implemented.
2. :115-117 noteOff "bookkeeping only (FR-114)". It gates the envelope and damps the bank (cpp:291-297).
3. :151-153 setChokeGroup "Phase 3 single-pad template". Only tests call it; production uses per-pad setPadChokeGroup.
4. :182-191 forEachMainVoice "broadcasting parameter changes to every main slot". Production has no caller; parameters reach voices only via applyPadConfigToSlot at note-on.
5. :303-305 processChokeGroups "Phase 3.1 stub is a no-op" (and cpp:148-150). It is implemented.
6. :349-354 scratchR_ "reserved for a future stereo DrumVoice". It is allocated and never read; the pool pans mono itself.
7. :358 fastReleaseK_ "exp(-1 / (tau * sampleRate))". The cpp uses exp(-ln(1e6)/(0.005*sr)) per :76-83.
8. :383-396 the static_assert "budget" says the heap arrays are included, but sizeof(VoicePool) holds only two unique_ptrs, so the assert cannot catch a heap-owning member.

**Why wrong.** The header is the API contract other code and tests rely on. Each item contradicts voice_pool.cpp.

**Consequence.** Maintenance trap. Item 2 misstates audible behaviour (see the FR-114 finding), and item 4 misled the perf benchmarks into configuring voices through a path that note-on overwrites.

**Evidence.** voice_pool.h:39 `// Phase 3.0: scaffolding only -- all methods are stubs.` voice_pool.h:186-188 "broadcasting parameter changes to every main slot". grep forEachMainVoice: callers only under plugins/membrum/tests. voice_pool.cpp:148-151 `// Step 1: choke group iteration. Phase 3.3 fills this in; Phase 3.1 is a no-op stub` immediately followed by a real `processChokeGroups(midiNote);`.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite the header comments from voice_pool.cpp. Remove forEachMainVoice and scratchR_ (or document them as test-only and unused), and drop or fix the misleading static_assert rationale.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed items 1-6 and 8; item 7 refuted: noteOn (cpp:128-266), prepare (:71-121), processChokeGroups (:1004) are full bodies; noteOff (cpp:283-299) calls VP_VOICES[slot].noteOff(); setChokeGroup (cpp:595-599) and forEachMainVoice (h:192-198) have only test callers (h:173 itself says setPadChokeGroup "replaces setChokeGroup global"); scratchR_ only allocated (cpp:76); the budget (h:390-393) adds 32*sizeof(DrumVoice) (~7 MB) and a std::vector member adds only its header to sizeof. Item 7: cpp:80-82 defines tau = kFastReleaseSecs/ln(1e6), so h:358 is terse, not wrong. Low is correct.

The prior signal-path audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:288) already noted scratchR_ unused; M-9 added pan inside the pool (h:312-319). Low.

#### MB-127 — state_codec.h documents a v3 / 57-slot / 468-byte format and 'single source' save paths that the code contradicts

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.h:6-14, 35-38, 85, 120, 151-152](plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.h#L6)

**Problem.**
1. :12-14 "Current version: v3 (M-9). The plugin has not shipped ... PadSnapshot::sound carries 57 slots". The constants are version 5 and 59 slots (:60, :108-109), and releases shipped (see the version finding).
2. :35-38 "44 float64 sound params cover offsets 2-35, 42-49 and 50-51". The array has 59 slots, including 50-65 and noiseLayerGain.
3. :120 kit layout "[57 x float64 sound]" and :151-152 pad layout "[57 x float64 sound] Total: 468 bytes". It is 59 slots and 4+4+4+59*8 = 484 bytes (test_pad_preset.cpp pins 484).
4. :6-10 "Both Processor::getState/setState and the Controller kit/pad preset providers route through the same write/read helpers". The controller SAVE providers build the snapshot from parameter values (controller_state_codec.cpp:117-181) and never fill slot 57 or the -1 damping sentinel, so the "single source" claim hides the save-path divergence (extra-focus lead 1).
5. :85 "uiMode: 0=Acoustic, 1=Extended". The registered labels are Simple / Advanced (controller.cpp:556-557).

**Why wrong.** This header declares itself "the single source of truth for the persisted state layout". Its layout comments are three versions and two slots out of date.

**Consequence.** Anyone hand-parsing or migrating blobs (for example tools/convert-memkit.js or a future v1/v2 migration) will compute wrong offsets. The "same helpers" sentence hides why controller-saved presets differ from host state.

**Evidence.** state_codec.h:12 `// Current version: v3 (M-9). The plugin has not shipped`. :14 "PadSnapshot::sound carries 57 slots". :60 `std::array<double, 59> sound{};`. :108 `kBlobVersion = 5;`. :151-152 `[57 x float64 sound] // Total: 468 bytes.`

**Suggested fix.** Regenerate the layout comments from the constants (or static_assert the byte sizes: 484 per pad preset), delete the "has not shipped" sentence, and state that the controller save path builds from parameters and which slots it cannot represent.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: :60 and :100 declare 59 slots, :108-109 version 5, and the header's own slot table (:44-59) lists index 57 (noiseLayerGain) and 58 (wireCoupling), so it contradicts itself; 484 bytes is pinned by test_pad_preset.cpp:51, test_state_codec.cpp:240-243 and test_coupling_state.cpp:248-252. Item 5 is terminology only (controller.cpp:551, 1269, 1507 also say Acoustic/Extended). Item 4 is partly overstated: both paths call the same writer (processor.cpp:902; controller_state.cpp:115, :212); the divergence is upstream in buildPadSnapshotFromParams (controller_state_codec.cpp:117-181). Low.
- Confirmed items 1, 2, 3, 5; item 4 literally true (controller_state.cpp:115 writeKitBlob, :212 writePadPresetBlob) but misleading because the snapshot is built from parameter values (controller_state.cpp:202, controller_state_codec.cpp:117). No ruling makes the comments intentional. Low.
- Confirmed the stale comments, impact overstated: the codec and tests use the constants, so no silent drift; tools/convert-memkit.js only wraps an opaque blob in a .vstpreset header (convert-memkit.js:45, :62) and never reads the slot layout; the save-path divergence belongs to the extra-focus lead 1 finding. Downgrade to nit proposed.

#### MB-129 — plugin_ids.h parameter comments disagree with the registered parameters (choice counts, defaults, ranges, types, per-pad ID range)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** spec-conformance · **Dimension:** spec-conformance

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/plugin_ids.h:61, 65-66, 75-76, 78, 104, 114-116, 123, 208-210](plugins/membrum/src/plugin_ids.h#L61)

**Problem.** :61 Exciter "StringListParameter, 6 choices" (registered with 7, Clap included). :65 NoiseBurst "default 5" while the per-pad default is 0.5 norm = 8.5 ms. :66 Friction pressure "default 0.3" (code 0.0). :75-76 PitchEnv Start "default 160" and End "default 50" (code default 0.0 = 20 Hz). :78 PitchEnvCurve "StringListParameter: Exp/Lin" (now a continuous RangeParameter; :173-175 of the same file says so). :104 ChokeGroup "RangeParameter stepped [0,8]" (a StringListParameter since audit Finding 17). :114-116 coupling knobs "[0.0, 1.0]" (registered 0..100 %). :123 UI mode "{Acoustic, Extended}" (registered Simple/Advanced). :208-210 "Pad 0: 1000-1063 ... Pad 31: 2984-3047. Offsets 0-35 are active; 36-63 reserved". The stride is 128 (pad 31 = 4968-5031) and offsets 0-65 are active (pad_config.h:25, kPadActiveParamCountV12 = 66).

**Why wrong.** plugin_ids.h is the reference for host-visible IDs, and its own header says the IDs are frozen once published. Comments that state the wrong range or default are what external tools and agents copy.

**Consequence.** Maintenance trap. The per-pad range comment is the stride-64 layout of the released v0.9/v0.10 builds, which hides that the IDs moved.

**Evidence.** plugin_ids.h:61 `kExciterTypeId = 200,  // StringListParameter, 6 choices`. :209-210 `// Pad 0: 1000-1063, Pad 1: 1064-1127, ..., Pad 31: 2984-3047. // Offsets 0-35 are active`. :104 `kChokeGroupId = 252,  // RangeParameter stepped [0,8], default 0`. :123 `kUiModeId = 280,  // StringListParameter {Acoustic, Extended}`.

**Suggested fix.** Correct each comment from controller.cpp's registrations, or drop the per-ID defaults and point at kPadParamSpecs. Add a static_assert tying the comment-free layout to kPadParamStride.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: controller.cpp:302-308 appends 7 exciters; Friction pressure proxy default 0.0 (controller.cpp:341; pad_config.h:237); PitchEnv proxy defaults 0.070721 / 0.0 (controller.cpp:347-348; pad_config.h:202-203 both 0.0f); PitchEnvCurve is RangeParameter(0..1, 0.5) (controller.cpp:430-434); ChokeGroup is a StringListParameter (controller.cpp:484-489); coupling 0..100 % (511-527); UI mode Simple/Advanced (556-557); kPadParamStride = 128 (pad_config.h:25), 66 active offsets (pad_config.h:176/358). Correction: NoiseBurst "default 5" matches the global proxy default (0.230769 over 2..15 ms, controller.cpp:336) and differs only from the per-pad 0.5f (pad_config.h:236), as the finding says. Low.
- Confirmed items on exciter count, curve type, choke type, coupling range (the wire value stays normalized), UI mode labels and the stride/active range (pad 31 = 4968..5031; helpers at pad_config.h:333/358). Default-value claims at :65-66 and :75-76 not checked. Low.
- Confirmed the same set (per-pad list at controller.cpp:695 also includes Clap; pad_config.h:358 rejects offsets of 66 or more); default claims unchecked. Real IDs come from the enum values and helpers, so no runtime or host effect. The suggested static_assert has no runtime value, but fixing the comments is sound. Low.
