#### MB-134 — Dead and test-only API in production classes, including a choke setter that writes a different state than production uses

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** dead-parameter · **Dimension:** portability-quality

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.h:151-153, 192-198, 220-228, 349-354](plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.h#L151)

**Problem.** No production code calls VoicePool::setChokeGroup (it writes only the ChokeGroupTable, for all 32 pads), getChokeGroupAssignments, loadChokeGroupAssignments, forEachMainVoice or mainVoiceRef; only tests do (8, 1, 1 and 5 test files). scratchR_ is allocated in prepare and never read. Processor::editorOpen_ is read and written only by editorOpenForTest/setEditorOpenForTest, which no test calls. The processor.h:68-71 notify doc names "CouplingMatrixEdit" / "CouplingMatrixSnapshotRequest" messages that the code does not handle. RegisteredDefaultsTable (macro_mapper.h:26, std::array<float,64>, smaller than the 66-offset range) is built in processor.cpp:59-86 and never read.

**Why wrong.** Test-only setters that bypass the production path make the tests exercise a state the plugin never reaches. The choke tests set groups through setChokeGroup (table only, cfg.chokeGroup untouched), which is how the cfg/table divergence in the default-kit choke finding stays hidden. The 64-wide array next to 66 active offsets invites an out-of-bounds write the next time an offset of 64 or more is added to the table.

**Consequence.** Maintenance trap and lost coverage: a reader trusts the doc comments, and the tests miss production choke bugs.

**Evidence.** grep in plugins/membrum/src finds no caller outside voice_pool.{h,cpp} for setChokeGroup(, getChokeGroupAssignments, loadChokeGroupAssignments, forEachMainVoice, mainVoiceRef, scratchR_. voice_pool.cpp:597-598 setChokeGroup -> `chokeGroups_.setGlobal(group)` only. processor.h:87-88 and :168 editorOpen_ (grep: no other use). processor.h:68-71 notify comment vs processor.cpp:1186-1269 (handles AuditionPad, AuditionPadOff, LoadPresetState, LoadPadPreset only). macro_mapper.h:26 `std::array<float, 64> byOffset{}`; macro_mapper.cpp:39 is the only access to defaults_.

**Suggested fix.** Delete editorOpen_ and its accessors, scratchR_, the stale notify doc and the unused defaults table (or size it with kPadActiveParamCountV12 and give it a reader). Move the choke tests to setPadConfigField(pad, kPadChokeGroup, ...) and delete setChokeGroup and the raw table loaders.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: setChokeGroup (voice_pool.cpp:595-599) only calls `chokeGroups_.setGlobal(group)`, 9 test calls in 8 files; production sets choke through setPadConfigField kPadChokeGroup (voice_pool.cpp:641-646, `chokeGroups_.setEntry`) and line 741; getChokeGroupAssignments / loadChokeGroupAssignments / mainVoiceRef at voice_pool.cpp:833, 838, 43; scratchR_ (cpp:76, h:354) never read; editorOpen_ (processor.h:168) accessors (87-88) uncalled in tests; macro_mapper.h:71-74 confirms the defaults reader was removed. Limits: the runtime choke lookup (voice_pool.cpp:254, 1030) is the same table, so only cfg.chokeGroup (state save) is skipped; the 64-wide array is a latent hazard, not an OOB write today. Low.
- Confirmed, two secondary claims weaker: 24 test occurrences in 13 files (test_choke_group.cpp has 9); the largest index written is kPadTSPitchEnvCurve2 = 63 (pad_config.h:162), so no OOB today; production setters keep cfg and table in step (voice_pool.cpp:645-646, :740-741), so only a save/load divergence would go unseen. Low.
- Confirmed by grep: defaults_ appears only in comments (macro_mapper.h:71-74); every index written is a named offset below 64; the tests do exercise the runtime choke path (`chokeGroups_.lookup`, voice_pool.cpp:254, 1030) and skip only the cfg.chokeGroup write (cpp:641-646). Maintenance only; low.

#### MB-135 — Header comments state the opposite of what the code does (proxies, selected pad, blob size, filter-env law)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** anti-pattern · **Dimension:** portability-quality · **Also flagged by:** gestalt-processor

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:4-7](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L4)

**Problem.** Several current comments contradict the code they describe. processor.cpp:6-7 says "Global proxy IDs (100-252) are no-ops in the processor (controller-only proxies)", but processParameterChanges forwards about 60 of them (267-522). processor.h:135 says selectedPadIndex_ is "for state only, not used in audio", but every proxy write on the audio thread routes through it. controller.h:168 says "a 284-byte pad preset blob"; the blob is 484 bytes. controller.h:266-270 says the filter envelope uses "linear ranges (attack x500 ms...)", but pad_config_apply.h decodes norm^3. state_codec.cpp:262-266 says "Reuse the first 51 sound slots ... index 51 is intentionally excluded", and the next line copies all 59. voice_pool.h:39-40 says "scaffolding only -- all methods are stubs", and :303-305 says processChokeGroups "Phase 3.1 stub is a no-op".

**Why wrong.** These comments lead a reader to the wrong model of the threading and data flow. selectedPadIndex_ is a plain int, written on the audio thread (processor.cpp:398) and read or written on the message thread (processor.cpp:1238 in notify, :948 in applyKitSnapshot), which is a data race the "not used in audio" comment hides. The filter-env comment is the source of the linear display formatter bug recorded in the params inventory.

**Consequence.** Fixes start from false premises. The selected-pad race and the wrong filter-env display both trace back to comments that say the opposite of the code.

**Evidence.** processor.cpp:6-7 vs :267-268 `case kMaterialId: voicePool_.setPadConfigField(selectedPadIndex_, kPadMaterial, fValue);`. processor.h:135-136 `// selected pad index (for state only, not used in audio)  int selectedPadIndex_ = 0;` vs processor.cpp:398 (audio-thread write) and :1238 (message-thread read). controller.h:168 "284-byte". controller.h:266-267 "asymmetric linear ranges". state_codec.cpp:262-266 vs :272 `std::copy_n(full.sound.begin(), snap.sound.size(), ...)`. voice_pool.h:39-40, :303-305 vs voice_pool.cpp:1004-1071 (full implementation).

**Suggested fix.** Correct or delete each comment. Make selectedPadIndex_ a std::atomic<int> (relaxed) because both threads touch it.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed every cited comment: proxies forwarded at processor.cpp:268, 287, 295, 384, 436-521; selectedPadIndex_ written at :398, read in notify("LoadPresetState") at :1238, written by applyKitSnapshot at :948 on the same notify path, so the plain int is a real data race; writePadPresetBlob (state_codec.cpp:535-544) writes 12 + 472 = 484 bytes (kPadBlobVersion 5, state_codec.h:109); pad_config_apply.h:87 is a cubic decode (also controller_view_sync.cpp:243); state_codec.cpp:268-272 copies all 59. Low fits; the bigger issue is applyKitSnapshot writing engine state from notify.
- Confirmed: controller.cpp:1417 repeats the "linear ranges" text; pad_config_apply.h:91-94 decodes aN*aN*aN*500 ms while controller_param_format.cpp:291 and :372 use formatLinearMs(norm, 0, 500), so the wrong display really follows the comment. No ruling makes the comments intentional. Low; the race and the formatter bug are separate findings.
- Confirmed all quoted comments (pad_config_apply.h:91-97 decodes `aN*aN*aN*500`, `dN^3*2000`, `rN^3*2000`; state_codec.h:148 blob layout). The race's consequence is small: an aligned int cannot tear on x86 or arm64, so the harm is a stale selected pad if a pad click lands between :1238 and :948 during a kit load, after which proxy writes go to the wrong pad until the next kit-260 change; still formally undefined behaviour, so the atomic fix is valid. The claim that the comment caused the formatter bug is attribution, not verified.

#### MB-143 — Per-push gate runs 11 diagnostic cases that assert nothing (printf/WARN only), including one named 'should decay'

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, lowered in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:1616-2023](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp#L1616)

**Problem.** These cases are not hidden and contain no REQUIRE or CHECK. In test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp: "Diagnostic: dump installed Jazz Brushes snare params" (1616), "Diagnostic: minimal Membrane body at low b1 should decay" (1764), "Diagnostic: HHOpen frequency profile" (1829), "Diagnostic: single Jazz Brushes tom decay trace" (1879), "Diagnostic: hat hit dominant-frequency capture" (1915), "Diagnostic: alternating two pads on Jazz Brushes" (1949) and "Diagnostic: rapid self-hit ... tom decay trace" (1984). In tests/unit/diagnose: [diagnose_n1], [diagnose_n1_tension] and [diagnose_n1_axes] (test_body_resonant_peak.cpp:132, 185, 224; printf plus SUCCEED), and [diagnose_orch] (test_orchestral_distortion.cpp:56; printf only, it even prints "CLIPPING" without failing). The "Recipe" case also carries a dead checkPhase lambda (1691-1705).

**Why wrong.** A case that cannot fail is a tautology: it costs gate time (several render 1.2-4 s of processor audio) and reads as coverage. "minimal Membrane body at low b1 should decay" claims a behaviour it never checks.

**Consequence.** A regression in exactly the behaviours these traces were written to investigate (a tom or hat infinite ring, timpani distortion, N-1 headroom) goes green. Gate wall clock is spent on output nobody reads.

**Evidence.** test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:1814-1823: a loop of `WARN("t=" << ... << "ms peak=" << winPeak);` and the case ends with no CHECK. Tags at 1765: `"[membrum][processor][infinite_ring][regression][diag]"` (no dot). test_body_resonant_peak.cpp:178: `SUCCEED("diagnostic only");`. test_orchestral_distortion.cpp:115-120: printf `samplesNearClip > 50 ? "CLIPPING" : "clean"` with no assertion in the file.

**Suggested fix.** Either convert each case to an assertion or hide it. Convert: "minimal Membrane body at low b1 should decay" gets `CHECK(winPeak[11] < 1e-3f && winPeak[11]*10 < winPeak[0])`; "Orchestral timpani kick: bisect distortion source" gets `CHECK(samplesNearClip == 0)` per scenario; [diagnose_n1] gets `CHECK(F_strk * kBodyHeadroom <= 1.0)` per body. Hide the rest with a leading-dot tag ([.diag], [.diagnose_n1]) as test_snare_audition.cpp already does. Delete the dead checkPhase lambda.

#### MB-144 — Infinite-ring kit sweeps skip every Friction pad on a false premise and have no lower bound, so tails cut early pass

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:460-503](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp#L460)

**Problem.** runPerPadSustainTest skips every pad whose exciter is Friction because "Friction sustains WITHOUT note-off by design". FrictionExciter gates itself off about 41 ms after trigger (friction_exciter.h:44 `autoReleaseSamples_ = 0.041*sr`; :111-114 `gate(false)`), so any sustained ring on a Friction pad comes from the body or the layers, which is exactly what the sweep exists to catch. The sweep also only asserts silence by s8 and s10 < s1/100. Nothing asserts that a tail is not cut too early (the String or NoiseBody 256-block force-retire, or the per-block auto-noteOff at peak < 1e-3, voice_pool.cpp:380-384).

**Why wrong.** The CLAUDE.md constraint "Friction sustains without note-off" no longer matches the exciter code. Exempting those pads leaves a whole class of factory pads (bowed pads in the Unnatural kits) unswept for infinite ring. Decay-to-silence tests without a minimum length reward premature retirement.

**Consequence.** An infinite ring on a Friction pad, or a String or NoiseBody tail truncated at a block-size-dependent time, passes the factory-kit gate.

**Evidence.** test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:460-466: `// D3 ...: Friction sustains WITHOUT note-off by design ... if (... exciterType == Membrum::ExciterType::Friction) continue;`. friction_exciter.h:44 `autoReleaseSamples_ = static_cast<int>(0.041f * static_cast<float>(sampleRate));` and :111-114 "fire gate(false) to enter release". drum_voice.h:660-665: `if (bankSilent) { ++silentBlockCount_; if (silentBlockCount_ > 256) active_ = false; }`.

**Suggested fix.** Drop the Friction exemption, or limit it to pads whose PadConfig really sustains (modeInject > 0 with decay at maximum) and document why. Add a lower-bound check per pad: `TEST_CASE("Factory pads are not cut before their natural decay", "[membrum][processor][factory][tail]")`. Render each pad at block sizes 64 and 1024 and CHECK that the time to -60 dB below the first-window peak agrees within 10 % between them, and that it is >= the T60 implied by the pad's decay/material for modal bodies.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: the skip is at test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:460-466 and the all-kits sweep repeats the justification (:551-552). The Friction exciter in use (exciter_bank.h:186, :213-214) is transient: friction_exciter.h:38-44 (A 1 ms, D 40 ms, S 0, R 5 ms), :112-114 `gate(false)`, :127-130 `active_=false`; the header (:7-9, :15) says "Sustained bowing is out of scope". tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp gives Friction to many factory pads (1559, 3424, 3540, 3717, 4493, 4632, 5013, 5188, 5644, 5799, 5976, 6017, 6093, 6117, 6323, 6414, 6431, 6559). Only an upper bound on decay is checked (:499, :503); the auto-noteOff (voice_pool.cpp:380-384) and the block-size-dependent 256-block retire (drum_voice.h:660-665) are unguarded. Not measured whether any Friction pad fails today.
- Confirmed, downgraded: nothing else sustains Friction (only setPressure plumbing, exciter_bank.h:164-249, pad_config_apply.h:60); the amp envelope and pool auto-release are the same for every exciter. The exemption follows the documented constraint (plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md, 06-orchestralKit-fix-plan.md:222), which describes design intent, not exciter behaviour; Guiro scrapes (3424, 4493, 5644) have no claim to a sustain exemption. No pad is shown to ring forever today.
- Confirmed, downgraded to low: the rapid-hit tests strike Friction pads in only 3 kits (lines 706/712/718). The "no lower bound" half is a scope extension: per-body T60 tests exist elsewhere (tests/unit/bodies/test_*_body.cpp, body_test_helpers.h, test_tom_body_depth.cpp), and no block-size truncation was measured. The actionable part is removing the false exemption and fixing the stale CLAUDE.md and generator comments (generator 1904-1906).

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** kit-quality · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static

#### MB-146 — The pad-snapshot inverse test checks 17 of 59 slots and none of the late slots (34-58) where the hand-written maps can drift

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static

**Why wrong.** The slot-to-field map is hand-written in toPadSnapshot, applyPadSnapshot, applyPadPresetSnapshot (state_codec.cpp), kLateSlots (controller_state_codec.cpp), setPadConfigField (voice_pool.cpp) and the preset generator (extra focus lead 3). Only an exhaustive per-slot test catches a swap between two of them. Clamp differences between routes (applyPadSnapshot clamps slots 34 and up; setPadConfigField clamps no float) are also unpinned.

**Consequence.** A transposed late slot (for example noise decay and colour) or a sentinel mishandled on one path would pass every codec test while presets load wrong.

Then, for each slot with a ParamID, write sound[k] through VoicePool::setPadConfigField(offsetOf(k)) and CHECK the same field changed, which ties kLateSlots and setPadConfigField to the codec. #### MB-150 — Coupling fuzz test exercises a hand-written limiter that has drifted from the processor's

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** parallel-path · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/test_coupling_fuzz.cpp:59-76, 205-223](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/processor/test_coupling_fuzz.cpp#L59)

**Problem.** The SC-009 coupling fuzz claims to mirror "the same per-block work the Processor dispatches". It drives VoicePool's mono overload plus a local fuzzEnergyLimiter instead of Processor::process. The local limiter uses attack 0.01 and release 0.001 smoothing per sample. The processor's applyEnergyLimiter uses `envelope += (1-coeff)*(x-env)` with coeff 0.001 on attack (0.999 per-sample smoothing, near instant) and 0.9999 on release (1e-4).

**Why wrong.** A test copy of production logic proves nothing about production once it drifts. This one differs by about 100x in attack and 10x in release, skips the bus limiter, master gain and multi-bus path, and uses the bit-mask isFiniteSample (52-57) that is vacuous on macOS.

**Consequence.** Allocation and stability claims for the real coupling chain (processor.cpp:693-707) rest on a different algorithm.

**Evidence.** test_coupling_fuzz.cpp:64-71: `kAttack = 0.01f; kRelease = 0.001f; ... envelope += (absSample - envelope) * kAttack;`. processor.h:186-190: `kAttackCoeff = 0.001f; kReleaseCoeff = 0.9999f; ... energyEnvelope_ += (1.0f - coeff) * (absVal - energyEnvelope_);`.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite the fuzz to drive Membrum::Processor::process (16 output buses, global coupling 1.0, the same random note schedule) between detector.startTracking() and stopTracking(), and classify finiteness with Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite. Delete fuzzEnergyLimiter.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: test 59-76 vs processor.h:183-196; header comments (14-15, 59-61, 208) claim a mirror and cite stale processor.cpp lines (555-655, 632-647; the real chain is 693-707). The test drives VoicePool::processBlock (206), skipping the bus TruePeakLimiter, master gain, aux buses and parameter/event handling. isFiniteSample (52-57) is the forbidden bit-mask clone (also test_macro_automation_extreme.cpp:203-208). Downgrade: test gap only; the limiter is allocation-free inline arithmetic; the production attack is more aggressive, so the test is conservative; test_macro_automation_extreme.cpp:173-196 runs Processor::process under AllocationDetector.
- Confirmed: test attack about 100x slower, release 10x faster; the real chain is at processor.cpp:701-706. No ruling makes the drift intentional. The SC-007 cap is pinned through Processor::process in test_coupling_energy.cpp:148 onward; test_macro_automation_extreme.cpp:76-195 runs Processor::process under AllocationDetector without coupling. Real gap: no processor-level coupling allocation/stability fuzz plus a misleading comment; low.
- Drift real, consequence does not hold at medium: busLimiter_ is at processor.cpp:717; the bit-mask clone sits in about 40 Membrum test files under the tools/lint-finite-bitmask.js ratchet. (a) Neither limiter can allocate (processor.h:183-195); VoicePool, SympatheticResonance and DelayLine are the production classes. (b) The limiter output never feeds back into the coupling engine (processor.cpp:700-706, test 211-219), so it cannot hide a runaway. (c) The production limiter bounds more tightly. (d) What no test covers is the processor's coupling branch under allocation tracking. Downgrade to nit or low.

#### MB-154 — H-1 "safety rail (runaway/NaN only)" is not a NaN rail: hardClip is std::clamp, the bus limiter relies on it, and nothing on the output path classifies finiteness

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification; one verifier kept medium) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** prior-audit-regression · **Dimension:** prior-audit-regressions · **Source:** static

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/sigmoid.h:267-269](dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/sigmoid.h#L267)

**Problem.** The gain-staging design (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:389 and :421) says the per-voice hardClip catches runaway/NaN and the TruePeakLimiter sanitises non-finite input. In the code, hardClip is `std::clamp(x, -threshold, threshold)`, which returns NaN for NaN. TruePeakLimiter's comment says it needs no sanitising because "the per-voice hardClip bounds every voice to [-1, 1]" (true_peak_limiter.h:189-192). The only isNonFinite call in Membrum is in feedback_exciter.h:147. Inputs are not sanitised either: applyPadSnapshot copies sound[0..33] unclamped and unchecked (state_codec.cpp:167-200).

**Why wrong.** The prior fix claimed two NaN barriers, and neither exists. NaN inside the limiter makes currentGain_ NaN permanently, and the master gain and meters follow. Root CLAUDE.md requires that NaN never reach the output and that finiteness is classified via detail::isFinite.

**Consequence.** A corrupted or hand-edited preset or project with a NaN or Inf sound value, or any future NaN in a voice, poisons the main bus until the next kit load. That is persistent silence or garbage output, not one bad sample.

**Evidence.** sigmoid.h:267-268 `return std::clamp(x, -threshold, threshold);`; true_peak_limiter.h:189-192 comment; grep for isFinite/isNaN/isNonFinite in plugins/membrum/src finds only feedback_exciter.h:147 and float_guard.*; state_codec.cpp:167 `cfg.material = static_cast<float>(snap.sound[0]);` (no clamp). Probe evidence that slots 0-33 pass through unclamped: probe-results.txt:23 `decay msg/edits = 1.700/1.000`.

**Suggested fix.** Sanitise once per block on the main bus before the limiter using Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite (zero the block and reset the limiter on a hit), and reject non-finite doubles in readKitBlob / readPadPresetBlob. Correct the appendix and the limiter comment. Add a dsp_ieee_tests or plugin test that injects NaN into one voice and REQUIREs a finite main output after the next block.

**Verifier notes:**
- Core claim holds, limiter mechanism wrong; kept medium: voice output goes through hardClip at drum_voice.h:566, 885, 898, 1061; the audit doc (:389, :420-421) and true_peak_limiter.h:189-192 each rely on the other; processor.cpp:693-737 has no finiteness check. NaN enters from saved data: state_codec.cpp:167-200 unchecked, the clamps at 202-245 pass NaN, the sentinel `b1Raw < 0.0` (216-221) is false for NaN, readKitBlob (421-515) does not check the sound array. true_peak_limiter.h:193-215 does not poison currentGain_ (`tp > ceilingLin_` false, so `required = 1.0f`); NaN still reaches the output via the clamp at 256-257, sustained by voice modal state and, with coupling on, couplingDelay_ / SympatheticResonance / energy limiter (processor.cpp:698-707).
- Core claim holds, downgrade: readT (state_codec.cpp:33-55) does no finiteness check. The trigger needs a corrupted or hand-edited blob; no in-engine NaN source was shown. The limiter gain stays finite; persistence comes from voice state and the SympatheticResonance engine, flushed only on kit load (processor.cpp:950-961).
- Defect real, consequence overstated: applyPadPresetSnapshot (:284-315) also copies slots 0-33 unchecked; DrumVoice::setLevel stores unchecked (drum_voice.h:1126), so NaN in sound[4] reaches the main bus on every hit. The output is NaN only while the poisoned voice sounds, except when coupling is on (kGlobalCouplingId default 0.0, plugin_ids.h:114; bypass at sympathetic_resonance.h:370-371; y1s_ reset only in applyKitSnapshot, processor.cpp:965) or under fast-math. The plugin's writer never emits NaN; host values are normalized. Downgrade medium to low.

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** prior-audit-regression · **Dimension:** prior-audit-regressions · **Source:** static

L-10: the global proxy kExciterNoiseBurstDurationId defaults to 0.230769 (5 ms) while the per-pad spec and PadConfig default to 0.5 (8.5 ms).

**Consequence.** A noise-layer resonance above about 0.1 adds a pitched peak at the cutoff on hats and snares, the "beep" the Lowpass switch was meant to remove. On a fresh instance the NoiseBurst Duration knob shows 5 ms while the pad plays 8.5 ms.

**Evidence.** noise_layer.h:290 `return 0.3f + std::clamp(norm, 0.0f, 1.0f) * (5.0f - 0.3f);`; pad_config.h:253 `noiseLayerResonance = 0.2f`; controller.cpp:336 `.defaultValue = 0.230769` vs :202 `.defaultValue = 0.5`; pad_config.h:236 `noiseBurstDuration = 0.5f`.

**Suggested fix.** Cap the noise-layer Q at about 0.707 on the Lowpass path (or correct the comments), and align the proxy default to 0.5 or the per-pad default to 0.230769. Add both to the tracker. Tests: a lowpass noise spectrum peak no more than 1 dB above the passband at resonance 1.0; proxy default equals per-pad default (pattern of test_audit_ui_controller_batch.cpp).

**Verifier notes:**
- Both defects confirmed, framing overstated: configure() (noise_layer.h:84-86) passes Q to the SVF (svf.h:221-225, 474, Lowpass tap 555-558), forced to Lowpass at drum_voice.h:147; default 0.2 gives about +2.6 dB, norm 1.0 about +14 dB; the UI range is still Q 0.3-5 (controller_param_format.cpp:383). L-10: per-pad 0.5 at controller.cpp:202, pad_config.h:236, processor.cpp:77; plugin_ids.h:65 "default 5"; the Friction Pressure proxy was aligned (controller.cpp:337-340) but this one was not. The tracker does not mark them handled; they are unstatused like L-1, L-7, L-8, L-9. The fresh-instance consequence is mostly masked by syncGlobalProxyFromPad (controller_state.cpp:87-92, controller.cpp:961-971), and pad 0 uses Impulse (default_kit.h:46-85). Low.
- Partly true: the "Open" list is a short priority list, not exhaustive. L-6's real defect is the stale comment: resonant lowpass is used on purpose (clap.md:25 Noise Resonance 0.40 "Q≈2.18 — the clap formant"; kalimba archetype:48 0.30); capping Q near 0.707 would remove designed sounds. L-10 is mostly covered by proxy syncs (controller_state.cpp:92, :187, :273; controller.cpp:846-851); the prior audit called it "Minor default drift" (:302) and plugin_ids.h:65 documents 5 ms, so fix the per-pad default toward 0.230769.
- Valid repeat, overstated: SVF lowpass peak gain Q/sqrt(1 - 1/(4Q^2)): norm 0.1 +0.1 dB, 0.2 about +2.7 dB, default-kit 0.15-0.30 (default_kit.h:68, 117, 154, 199, 254, 285, 333) about +1.2 to +5 dB, norm 1.0 about +14 dB; a broadband hump, not the narrow bandpass "beep". The proxy knob is on screen (editor.uidesc:90, 220). NoiseBurst pads set explicit durations (default_kit.h:195, :228). What remains: resetting the proxy writes 5 ms while the pad default is 8.5 ms.

#### MB-164 — Sound-slot to parameter mapping is hand-written in five places; the FR-061 skip list twice, plus a hard-coded slot 51 in the controller (lead 3)

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification; one verifier kept medium) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** duplication · **Dimension:** gestalt-controller · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp:31-99, 263-271, 305-322](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp#L31); [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:1485-1490](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L1485)

**Problem.** The slot to field and parameter layout exists in state_codec.cpp (toPadSnapshot, applyPadSnapshot, applyPadPresetSnapshot), in controller_state_codec.cpp (kContiguousOffsets, kExciterSecOffsets, kLateSlots, kMacroOffsets plus the hand-coded sound[28..33] blocks), in VoicePool::setPadConfigField, in tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp, and inline in Controller::pushKitEnabledToGrid ("sound[51]"). The FR-061 skip list (enable 51, pan 56, choke/bus 28-29, coupling, macros) is coded again by offset in applyPadPresetSnapshotToParams. The sentinel-skip rule is also duplicated (:265-268, :313-316). Today the slots agree, per a slot-by-slot comparison in the inventory. The divergence that exists is in what each copy can represent: the controller copy cannot carry slot 57 or the -1 sentinel, which is the root of finding 1.

**Why wrong.** One layout must define the blob, the PadConfig field and the ParamID together. Otherwise every new field needs five synchronized edits, and a field without a ParamID silently falls out of the controller paths, as noiseLayerGain did.

**Consequence.** Maintenance trap: adding a slot or reordering one breaks presets with no compile error. The controller-side codec is already lossy.

**Evidence.** controller_state_codec.cpp:31-43 kContiguousOffsets, :58-93 kLateSlots (no 57); :311 `if (slot.offset == kPadEnabled || slot.offset == kPadPan) continue;`; controller.cpp:1487-1489 `// Slot 51 of PadSnapshot::sound is the per-pad enable flag ... kit.pads[...].sound[51] >= 0.5`.

**Suggested fix.** One constexpr table, `struct SlotDesc { size_t slot; int padOffset /* -1 = no param */; float PadConfig::* field; float min, max; bool sentinel; bool padPresetSkips; }`, in a header shared by state_codec, controller_state_codec, setPadConfigField and the generator. Every route iterates it. Rows with padOffset -1 are carried by a controller-side mirror. pushKitEnabledToGrid uses the table's kPadEnabled row. Add a static_assert that the table covers 0..58 once each, and a test that walks the table through all routes and compares.

**Verifier notes:**
- Duplication confirmed; kept medium as the structural cause of the lossy save path (lead 1). Tables at controller_state_codec.cpp:31-43, :46-49, :58-93 (24 rows), :96-99; slots 28-29 inline at :143-149 and :226-229. kLateSlots has no row for 57 (comment :91); PadSnapshot::sound is `std::array<double, 59>` (state_codec.h:60), so buildPadSnapshotFromParams (:116-181) leaves sound[57] at 0.0, then applyPadSnapshot clamps it to 0.1 (state_codec.cpp:243, :326). Other copies: state_codec.cpp toPadSnapshot :64 (:137, :147), applyPadSnapshot :162 (:234, :243), applyPadPresetSnapshot :276 (:326, skip :350); voice_pool.cpp:605 (:669); generator :122. No shared table or static_assert.
- Confirmed, downgrade to low: the controller codec header calls itself the "single source of truth" but only covers the controller side; generator also has "sound[58]" at :125. test_state_codec.cpp:275 checks only toPadSnapshot vs applyPadSnapshot. No slot mismatch today; the named harm is the separate lead-1 finding.
- Duplication real, no drift today: state_codec.cpp maps at :90-158, :167-254, :284-357; controller copies at :31-99, :143-156, :223-239; pan (56) simply absent from :317-357 while controller_state_codec.cpp:311 skips it; sentinel guards match (:216-221, :333-338). Counting slot 57 here would double-count finding 1. test_kit_browser_load.cpp:290-316 already guards the load direction byte for byte. Downgrade to low/nit.

#### MB-165 — Dead or stale controller code: an unused forwardGlobalToPad, a write-only modeToggleButton_, an unused ui_mode.h, and comments with wrong sizes and laws

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** anti-pattern · **Dimension:** gestalt-controller · **Source:** static

**Problem.** forwardGlobalToPad (controller.cpp:987-1001) duplicates the loop inline in setParamNormalized (:862-891) and has no caller. modeToggleButton_ is assigned (:1182) and never read or nulled. The production code never uses ui/ui_mode.h (only test_ui_mode_session_scope.cpp includes it); the controller hard-codes ">= 0.5" and 0.0. The comments contradict the code: kit blob "9036-byte ... v4 without selectedPadIndex" (it writes selectedPadIndex, v5); pad blob "284-byte" (484); filter env "asymmetric linear ranges" (cubic); formatter header "64-param stride", "ten ArcKnobs", "Selected-pad proxies are the pad-0 slot"; per-pad spec stepCount 5 for exciter and body (7 and 6 entries). Three split TUs (controller_view_sync.cpp, controller_state.cpp, controller_param_format.cpp) keep the banner "Phase 4 per-pad parameter registration + proxy logic" and the full include list of controller.cpp.

**Why wrong.** Misleading comments in this file have already caused real defects: the Membrane gate was built on a stale drum_voice.h line reference, and the save path was assumed exact.

**Suggested fix.** Delete forwardGlobalToPad and modeToggleButton_. Use UI::uiModeFromNormalized / kDefaultUiMode or delete the header. Fix the comments and the stepCount values, and trim each split TU's includes to what it uses. The compile and the existing tests cover it.

**Verifier notes:**

Kit blob writes selectedPadIndex at v5 (controller_state.cpp:115, state_codec.cpp:392, state_codec.h:123); 59 float64 slots alone are 472 bytes. Filter envelope is cubic (pad_config_apply.h:94-97); processor.cpp no longer holds those ranges (comment also at controller.cpp:1417). stepCount 5 is never read for these StringListParameters (controller.cpp:685-709). Banner copied on line 2 of the three split TUs.

#### MB-170 — Coupling Delay (global 273) is inaudible: it delays a coupling return that is itself about 60 dB down

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dead-parameter · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:425-430, 695-702](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L425)

**Problem.** kCouplingDelayId sets a 0.5..2.0 ms delay on the mono sum that feeds the coupling engine. Its effect can only be heard through the coupling return, which is inaudible (see the Global Coupling finding).

**Why wrong.** A delay that only affects a signal 60 dB below the dry sound has no perceptible effect, so the parameter is weak.

**Consequence.** Moving Coupling Delay changes level, centroid, decay and band distance by less than 0.1 dB / 1 %.

**Evidence.** Quality probe param:global=273:couplingDelay: "36/38/42: 0.0/0/0/0.0 each (not identical); live=yes". processor.cpp:429 `const float delayMs = 0.5f + clamped * 1.5f;`.

**Suggested fix.** Re-evaluate once coupling is audible. If it stays inaudible after recalibration, remove the parameter or hide it in the Advanced view. Test: with a recalibrated coupling, delay 0.5 vs 2 ms changes the comb/phase interaction measurably.

**Verifier notes:**
- Not refuted: processor.cpp:425-431 maps to 0.5..2.0 ms; read only at 695-702 on the mono sum feeding `couplingEngine_.process()`, then applyEnergyLimiter (capped at kThreshold 0.1, processor.h:183-186), added to L/R (705-706); skipped when bypassed (693). Stored and restored (890-891, 977): live but weak. param-audibility.csv:209-211 (probe source audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt:1019-1022 sets global coupling, snare buzz and tom resonance to 1.0) shows at most 0.1 dB level, 0.1 % centroid, 0.0 % decay, 0.04 dB band distance on pads 36, 38, 42. Global Coupling 0 -> 1 changes level 0.0 dB (param-audibility.csv:200-202; quality-results.txt:444). Low.
- Holds: does nothing at the default Global Coupling of 0. Level change at most 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.02 dB. Not intentional: front-panel knob (editor.uidesc:408 ArcKnob, :410 CParamDisplay); MANUAL.md:433 and :529 ("Coupling Delay > 1.5 ms for 'big room' feel") and specs/140-membrum-phase5-coupling/spec.md:39, :96 describe an audible effect. Low.
- Confirmed: plugin_ids.h:114 "default 0.0"; probe-results.txt:18 puts the coupling-only component at -60.98 dB relative to dry, total RMS change 0.00 dB. A shift of at most 1.5 ms into a return capped at -20 dBFS changes only onset timing. Symptom of the Global Coupling level finding; cross-reference it.

#### MB-172 — Noise-layer level drops about 6 dB at 192 kHz: white noise through a fixed-cutoff lowpass is not bandwidth-normalised to the sample rate

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h:264-276, 321](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/noise_layer.h#L264)

**Problem.** computeStandaloneGain corrects only for the cutoff (sqrt(fcRef/fc)). White noise of fixed per-sample variance spreads its power over 0..sr/2, so the power passed by a lowpass at a fixed cutoff scales with 1/sr. kStandaloneOutputGain = 0.243 was calibrated at one sample rate.

**Why wrong.** Level must not depend on sample rate. The noise layer carries the identity of snares, hats and cymbals.

**Consequence.** Noise-heavy pads get quieter at higher rates: crash RMS is 4.55 dB lower at 192 kHz than at 48 kHz, so mixes rendered at different rates differ.

**Evidence.** Probe srate:crash49 / snare38: "crash RMS -29.68 (48k) vs -34.23 (192k) = 4.55 dB". noise_layer.h:273-275 `const float ratio = std::clamp(std::sqrt(calibrationCutoffHz() / fc), 0.25f, 4.0f); return kStandaloneOutputGain * ratio;` (no sample-rate term).

**Suggested fix.** Multiply standaloneGain by sqrt(sr / sr_ref) (sr_ref = the calibration rate) in configure()/prepare(). Test: default-kit crash RMS(1 s) at 48 vs 192 kHz within 1 dB.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed from source and measurement: configure() (77-95) and configureRaw() (100-115) are the only setters of standaloneGain_; `sampleRate_` (324) is `[[maybe_unused]]` and used only by bloomCoef(). processWhite (noise_oscillator.h:306-309, White case 263-264) is fixed-variance uniform noise; prepare() (222-236) does not normalise. Lowpass forced at drum_voice.h:147; gain applied at drum_voice.h:548, 861, 1050. 192 vs 48 kHz is -6.02 dB for the noise layer alone. probe-results.csv:437 "srate:crash49 ... 4.55, bound <= 1 dB, bad"; snare only 0.62 dB (csv:449). The title's 6 dB is the layer-only figure; pad output drops 4.55 dB.
- Confirmed, nothing guards or documents it: NoiseLayer::prepare (noise_layer.h:39-56) passes sampleRate only to oscillator, SVF and ADSR. The only multi-rate noise test (test_noise_body.cpp:256) checks finiteness only. No ruling accepts a rate-dependent noise level; the calibration comment (noise_layer.h:312-321, gain_staging_balance_test) implies one rate. Low.
- Holds: Bandpass (default, line 47) and Lowpass are both affected; 3 dB lost at 96 kHz; Violet (processViolet, 341-351) loses more; the Kellet pink filter's fixed coefficients also shift with sr. No membrum test checks noise level across rates. Noise-heavy pads change 3-6 dB between 48, 96 and 192 kHz sessions. Low.

#### MB-176 — FM Ratio steps change level by 12 dB because StrikeNormKey omits fmRatio, so the strike gain cached for the old ratio is reused

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dead-parameter · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1394-1412](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1394)

**Problem.** measuredStrikeOutputGain re-probes only when the StrikeNormKey changes. The key holds body, exciter, material, size, decay, strikePos, modeStretch, decaySkew, airLoading, modeScatter, b1, b3, the click parameters and noiseBurstContact, but not fmRatio (or frictionPressure / feedbackAmount). An FM Ratio change alters the exciter's spectrum and therefore the body's peak, but the gain normalised for the previous ratio stays cached.

**Why wrong.** The normalisation exists so that level is independent of the timbre controls. A parameter that changes the strike peak must invalidate the cache.

**Consequence.** The FM Ratio knob behaves as a large uncontrolled level control: a 12.2 dB jump between adjacent steps on the hat. The level also depends on which ratio the voice slot was last probed with, so the same setting is louder or quieter depending on playing history.

**Evidence.** Quality param:offset=32:fmRatio: "36: 4.1/128/109/15.9 ; 38: 2.8/5/0/5.6 ; 42: 12.2/66/240/18.3, jump 12.2 dB". Context check: probe sets exciter norm 4/6 -> int(0.667*7)=4 = FMImpulse (correct). drum_voice.h:1400-1406 key fields listed, no fmRatio.

**Suggested fix.** Add fmRatio, frictionPressure, feedbackAmount and the mallet size hint to StrikeNormKey. Also move `exciterBank_.setMalletBodySizeHint(size_)` (line 340) before the probe at line 302. Test: hat with FMImpulse, sweep fmRatio in 8 steps; the peak stays within 1.5 dB of kBodyHeadroom at every step and the result is independent of step order.

**Verifier notes:**
- Stale-cache defect real, evidence and "because" do not hold: key struct at drum_voice.h:1717-1727 has no fmRatio or frictionPressure; probeStrikePeakExcited (1322-1362) drives the live exciterBank_ (trigger(1.0f) at 1338), which replays pendingFMRatioNorm_ (exciter_bank.h:146-151, 244-245; friction 164-169, 248-249); fm_impulse_exciter.h:80, 86 sets modulator frequency baseFreq*(1+3*norm). Mallet hint set at line 340, after the probe at 302. But renderParam (audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt:1070-1085, 1117-1119) builds a fresh Rig per step and queues fmRatio before the note-on (1079 vs 1080), so every step was freshly probed (kCount sentinel, drum_voice.h:1718-1719); the 12.2 dB jump is not the cache. The probe normalises at velocity 1.0 while the sweep plays at 100/127, and baseFreq / index follow velocity (fm_impulse_exciter.h:83, 90). feedbackAmount does not belong in the key: Feedback takes the setOutputGain(1.0f) branch (drum_voice.h:269-276).
- Real but smaller defect: Rig constructor (86-99) makes a new Processor per step; the 12.2 dB figure is the adjacent-step rms500Db change (1152-1153), a genuine RMS/timbre effect of FM ratio on a peak-normalised voice. "Depends on playing history" is true from the code but unmeasured. Downgrade.
- Code defect real, impact not shown (quality-results.txt:410): the probe strikes at velocity 1.0 (base 2500 Hz) while notes play at 100/127 (about 1690 Hz), and rms500 includes noise, click and tone-shaper stages the body norm does not control. The size and sign of the stale-cache error were never measured. Adding feedbackAmount does nothing; the mallet-hint ordering is a separate issue.

#### MB-177 — ModeInject level is not scaled to the body budget: the 8-harmonic series peaks at about 2.7 x amount against a 0.5 body

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dead-parameter · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/mode_inject.h:60, 126, 139-142](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/unnatural/mode_inject.h#L60)

**Problem.** Partial amplitudes are 1/k for 8 harmonics (sum about 2.72), loaded with skipNormalization=true, and the output is amount * env * bank (no headroom scaling). The result is added after the body, whose strike peak is normalised to 0.5.

**Why wrong.** A continuous amount knob should have a usable range. Here the first quarter of the range already dominates the body by several times.

**Consequence.** On the hat the step 0 -> 0.25 changes rms500 by 12.1 dB, and 0.25..1 mostly drives the nonlinear coupling and the hardClip. Fine control lives only in roughly the bottom 10 % of the knob.

**Evidence.** Quality param:offset=23:modeInjectAmount: "36: 8.7/34/3/15.8 ; 38: 10.0/83/150/12.2 ; 42: 22.9/91/37/18.7, adjacent jump 12.1 dB". mode_inject.h:60 `frame_.partials[k].amplitude = 1.0f / static_cast<float>(harmonicIndex);` and :142 `const float s = amount_ * env_ * bank_.process();`.

**Suggested fix.** Scale the injected series to the body budget (divide by the 1/k sum and multiply by kBodyHeadroom) and use a perceptual (squared) amount curve. Test: adjacent 0.25-steps of modeInject on the default hat change level by < 6 dB.

**Verifier notes:**
- Defect holds: prepare() (mode_inject.h:54-67) sets 1/k, series RMS about 0.87; the kTargetOscRms normaliser runs only when !skipNormalization (harmonic_oscillator_bank.h:345-367); process() (925-999) applies only the ±2.0 kOutputClamp (:92). Added to the 0.5 body at drum_voice.h:557, :893, :1056, then nonlinearCoupling, ToneShaper, hardClip (:566); pad_config_apply.h:129-130 only clamps to [0,1]. The comments at mode_inject.h:48-50, :124 contradict the code. Caveats: phases are randomised, so the realistic level is about 0.87 RMS; the 12.1 dB is the off -> 0.25 step. At 0.25 the injected RMS (about 0.22) is already on the order of the body peak. Low.
- Confirmed: globalAmplitude not applied, clamp at :996. No design ruling covers the level; the prior audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:342, :347) called ModeInject too weak under 1/k^2, and the switch to 1/k did not rescale. Factory and retune presets use only 0.10-0.25. "Bottom 10 %" is inferred, and "dominates by several times" is overstated on RMS.
- Confirmed: sum of squares 1.527, RMS 0.874 x amount, about -1.2 dBFS at amount 1 vs a -6 dBFS body peak; at 0.25 about -13 dBFS RMS, sustained over T60 = 0.3 + 4.7*decay^2 s (drum_voice.h:331) while a hat body decays in tens of ms. Linear amount (voice_pool.cpp:634). Not dead but over-hot and poorly scaled; "measured-dead-parameter" overstates it. Low for an Unnatural control that defaults to 0 (default_kit.h:233, pad_config.h:214).

#### MB-179 — Mode Stretch below 1.0 does nothing on Membrane: compression is clamped away

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-dead-parameter · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:129-138](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L129)

**Problem.** For modeStretch < 1, stretchDelta is negative and `r.stretch = clamp(material*0.3 + stretchDelta, 0, 1)` goes to 0. The bank can only stretch (B = stretch^2*0.01 >= 0), so the lower half of the knob (0.5..1.0) cannot compress the partials. It only removes the material-derived stretch and then saturates.

**Why wrong.** The knob range [0.5, 2.0] with 1.0 "physical" implies 0.5 compresses the overtone series. Half the knob is dead.

**Consequence.** Stretch 0.5 gives an overtone exponent of 0.998, essentially no change, while 2.0 gives 1.055. Users get no effect from the left half of the knob.

**Evidence.** Probe unnatural: "stretch 0.5 exponent 0.998, 2.0 exponent 1.055 (weak, asymmetric)", note "Membrane stretch below 1 is clamped away (membrane_mapper.h:123-138)". membrane_mapper.h:138 `r.stretch = std::clamp(params.material * 0.3f + stretchDelta, 0.0f, 1.0f);`.

**Suggested fix.** Support a signed stretch in the bank (f*sqrt(1+B*n^2) with B allowed negative down to a safe floor, or an exponent law f*n^(1+s)), or relabel the knob range. Test: on Membrane, modeStretch 0.5 vs 1.0 moves mode3/mode0 by >= 3 %.

**Verifier notes:**
- Holds: at modeStretch 0.5, r.stretch is 0 for every material. The bank cannot compress: modal_resonator_bank.h:756 clamps to [0,1], :783 B = stretch^2 * 0.01, :807 f_w = f_k * sqrt(1 + B*n^2). Value chain pad_config_apply.h:123-126, default pad_config.h:212. FR-050 (specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:235) gives range ~0.5 to ~2.0. No test covers modeStretch < 1. The other modal mappers (plate_mapper.h:61, shell_mapper.h:61, bell_mapper.h:56, noise_body_mapper.h:119) also cannot compress, but there the lower half removes a nonzero 0.333 baseline. Low.
- Confirmed: at material 0.5 the stretch hits 0 at modeStretch about 0.775, so the lower half is weak rather than fully dead. Not intentional: specs/135-membrum-drum-synth.md:177 says "Below = clustered/gong-like"; the phase-2 spec (:131), the contract (unnatural_zone_contract.md:164) and test_mode_stretch.cpp (107-110) only test 1.0 and 1.5. Low.
- Confirmed, "left half dead" slightly overstated: stretch reaches 0 at ms = 1 - 0.45*material; at material 0 the dead span is normalized 0..0.333, at 0.5 it is 0..0.15, at 1 it is 0..0.03. probe-results.csv:579-581: ratio 2.295 / 2.299 / 2.407 (about -3 cents vs +80 cents). param-audibility.csv:65 (kick, pad 36): steps 0 and 0.25 identical. MANUAL.md:346 says "< 1.0 is sparser", which no code path delivers. Single Extended-mode control, nothing unstable; low.

#### MB-182 — Main-bus silence flag is never set while coupling is on, even with no notes and a -240 dBFS output

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:739-741](plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp#L739)

**Problem.** silenceFlags = (isAnyVoiceActive() || !couplingEngine_.isBypassed()) ? 0 : 3. Any non-zero Global Coupling keeps the engine un-bypassed forever, so the flag is cleared on every block regardless of the actual output.

**Why wrong.** Hosts use silence flags to skip downstream processing. The flag should reflect whether the buffer is silent, not whether a feature is enabled.

**Consequence.** With coupling on (most factory kits set globalCoupling > 0), downstream effects never get the silence optimisation: 469 of 469 idle blocks were flagged non-silent.

**Evidence.** Probe coupling:idle silence flag: "-240 dBFS / 469 of 469" (RMS / blocks with flag cleared). processor.cpp:739-741 `data.outputs[0].silenceFlags = (voicePool_.isAnyVoiceActive() || !couplingEngine_.isBypassed()) ? 0ULL : 3ULL;`

**Suggested fix.** Flag the main bus silent when no voice is active and the coupling return plus the limiter output in this block is below a small threshold (or the coupling engine reports no active resonators). Test: coupling 1.0, no notes, 5 s: blocks after the tail have the silence flag set.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: `SympatheticResonance::isBypassed()` (sympathetic_resonance.h:370-372) is `amountSmoother_.getCurrentValue() == 0.0f && couplingGain_ == 0.0f`, depending only on the amount; setAmount (:152-155) zeroes couplingGain_ only at amount 0, and the processor sets the amount only at processor.cpp:408 and :978. `getActiveResonatorCount()` (:365, decremented at :350) exists, so the fix is cheap; the aux buses (processor.cpp:669-685) already scan their buffers. Low.
- Confirmed: with no voices and no active resonators process() returns antiMudHpf_(0) ≈ 0 (sympathetic_resonance.h:324-357), so the buffer is silent while the flag says not; no comment at :739 and no test pins the main-bus flag (grep finds only fixtures setting it to 0). A cleared flag is always safe in VST3, so this is a performance nit, not a correctness bug; key it on getActiveResonatorCount()==0 plus a drained delay line and limiter.
- Confirmed: the trigger is the normal case, since tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp sets k.opts.globalCoupling to 0.18-0.85 at 15 sites (lines 1661-6607) against a default 0.0 (:172). No audible effect, only wasted downstream CPU while idle; low stands. The energy-limiter state and the limiter's lookahead tail must also settle before flagging silent.

#### MB-184 — Documented sustain constraints do not match the engine: Friction stops after about 41 ms and modeInject decays (D2)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md:21-22](plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md#L21) (verifiers: the text sits at lines 23-24)

**Problem.** The leaf CLAUDE.md (and the task brief) state 'modeInject > 0 rings undamped (flat plateau); Friction sustains without note-off'. In code, FrictionExciter auto-releases at 0.041*sr samples (friction_exciter.h:44), and ModeInject decays with T60 = 0.3 + 4.7*decay^2 s (drum_voice.h:327-331, D2).

**Why wrong.** The domain constraints in CLAUDE.md are labelled load-bearing and are used to judge presets and tests. They must describe the engine as it is.

**Consequence.** Preset designers rely on Friction for drones and on modeInject for sustain, and get neither. The long Friction/String rings come from the String body. Agents reading CLAUDE.md treat the decay as a bug or skip valid checks.

**Evidence.** Probe tail:Friction / modeInject sustain: "Friction -240 dBFS; modeInject 0.5 -240 at 2 s; voice modeInject 0.5/1.0 last 1 s -240 dBFS". friction_exciter.h:44 `autoReleaseSamples_ = static_cast<int>(0.041f * static_cast<float>(sampleRate));`; drum_voice.h:331 `setDecaySeconds(0.3f + 4.7f * decay_ * decay_)`.

**Suggested fix.** Update plugins/membrum/CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills/membrum/SKILL.md: Friction is a 41 ms bow transient (any sustain is body ring), and modeInject decays with Decay (0.3..5 s). If a sustaining bow is wanted, implement it as a feature. Test: none (doc); the infinite-ring tests already encode the decaying behaviour.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed (line ref is CLAUDE.md:23-24): friction_exciter.h:1-18 calls it a transient struck-bow exciter ("Sustained bowing is out of scope (deferred to Phase 4)"); envelope A=1 ms/D=40 ms/S=0/R=5 ms (:39-42), gate(false) at the 0.041*sr count (:112-115), active_=false after the envelope (:127-130), zero body feedback (:124). mode_inject.h:84-93 adds the D2 decay envelope, applied per sample (:142-143), T60 one-pole (:148-153) re-armed in trigger() (:128-130), default 1.5 s (:161); CHANGELOG.md:91 records the change. Doc-only, low.
- Confirmed: .claude/skills/membrum/SKILL.md:26-27 repeats the claim; preset-retune/archetypes/singing-bowl-*.md:8 already says Friction is a ~46 ms transient and the Bell body owns the sustain; mode_inject.h:89-91 clamps T60 to [0.05, 20] s; CHANGELOG.md:90-99 records the decay as deliberate and CHANGELOG.md:461 says test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp was removed, so "Enforced by ... infinite-ring tests" is stale too. Fix the line reference to 23-25. Low.
- Confirmed: exciter_bank.h:213 emplaces only the transient FrictionExciter, so no sustaining path exists. The stale belief reaches a test: test_kit_switch_infinite_ring.cpp:460-466 skips every Friction pad in the idle-decay sweep (justified again at :551-552), so factory Friction pads never get the "silent by 8 s, geometric decay" checks (:498-503). "Designers rely on Friction for drones" is speculative. Low; also stop skipping Friction pads in the sweep.

#### MB-185 — Tabla kit: 6 near-duplicate pad pairs; pads 53/66 are copies, and 36/42 and 38/59 differ mainly in the dead Decay knob

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, downgraded on verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-kit-quality · **Dimension:** measured

**Location:** [tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:4685-4712, 4774-4777, 5006-5010, 5078-5080](tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp#L4685)

**Problem.** Pad 30 (note 66) = pads[17] with only pan changed (DATA). Pad 6 (note 42) = pads[0] with decay 0.78 -> 0.85 and tensionModAmt 0.78 -> 0.85. Both carry bodyDampingB1 0.30 / B3 0.05, so decay is dead (ENGINE, see the Decay finding). Pad 23 (note 59) = pads[2] with decay 0.58 -> 0.62, strikePosition 0.40 -> 0.42, tension 0.25 -> 0.20 and decaySkew 0.65 -> 0.62, again with explicit B1/B3. 38 vs 53/66 and 43 vs 64 are close as well.

**Why wrong.** A 32-pad factory kit should offer 32 distinct voices. The kit comment itself promises '30 distinct pads (was 10, 5 clones)'.

**Consequence.** Tabla 53 and 66 render bit-identically, and 36/42 are identical in bands, so four of the kit's pads are wasted.

**Evidence.** Quality sameness: "Tabla 53 vs 66: 0.00/1.000/1.000; Tabla 36 vs 42: 0.00/1.027/1.000; Tabla 38 vs 59: 0.25/1.004/1.115", plus 38 vs 53 0.94, 38 vs 66 0.94, 43 vs 64 1.21. Generator 5079 `pads[30] = pads[17]; pads[30].pan = 0.50;` 4775 `pads[6] = pads[0]; pads[6].decay = 0.85; pads[6].tensionModAmt = 0.85;` 4700 `pads[0].bodyDampingB1 = 0.30; pads[0].bodyDampingB3 = 0.05;`

**Suggested fix.** DATA: give pad 30 its own tuning (size/pitch) or disable it. ENGINE: fix the dead Decay so the 36/42 and 38/59 variants separate, or vary size/strikePosition/B1 instead. Test: quality sameness probe reports 0 near-duplicates for Tabla.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed with a correction: pad 30 copies pad 17 (:5079-5080; pad 17 has pan 0.52 from the tarang loop at :4930-4954), so the mono voices are identical; pad 6 = pad 0 plus decay/tensionModAmt (:4775-4777); pad 23 = pad 2 with small changes (:5007-5010). In membrane_mapper.h decay enters only via r.decayTime (:151) into dampingLawFromLegacy (:69), and :71-78 overwrite b1/b3 when the overrides are >= 0. Correction: :5078-5083 label pads 30/31 as "spare ... optional", so the "30 distinct pads" promise (:4676) is broken only by pads 6 and 23. Severity left at medium by this verifier.
- Confirmed, narrower than claimed: decay's only other voice use is the modeInject decay time (drum_voice.h:331), and pads 0/6 have no modeInject, so 36 vs 42 differ only by +0.07 tensionModAmt. Pad 2 has modeInject 0.30, so decay moves its modeInject T60 from ~1.88 s to ~2.11 s, matching 38/59's 1.115 decay ratio. The 53/66 copy is a documented placeholder; the real defect is pad 6 ("extreme gliss"). Mostly a consequence of the dead-Decay finding; downgraded.
- Confirmed, smaller impact: dampingLawFromParams (membrane_mapper.h:64-79) replaces the decayTime law with b1 = 0.2 + n*49.8, b3 = n*1e-3; 38/59 measurably differ (decay ratio 1.115, strike 0.40 vs 0.42), so that pair is "close", not identical. No crash or wrong output; two to three wasted pads in one of 20 factory kits is content quality, so low. The ENGINE half belongs to the separate dead-Decay finding.

The pedal-hat recipe (preset-retune/archetypes/pedal-hi-hat-acoustic-foot-closed-chick.md:5-17) wants a distinguishable articulation. Mitigating: both share choke group 1 (lines 1235/1249), so they never layer. Systemic hat-pair data issue; low.

The pedal is only 0.5 dB quieter, ~20 ms shorter and within 1 % in centroid, so 42 and 44 sound nearly the same. Data, not engine; low.

#### MB-195 — uidesc-inventory --check fails on Membrum's editor: 160 overlaps from FieldsetContainer frames drawn as siblings of their controls, with no allow list

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** measured-lint · **Dimension:** measured

**Problem.** Each fieldset is an empty, transparent FieldsetContainer view placed as a sibling over the same rectangle as its controls (for example line 134 FieldsetContainer Macros at 4,28,388,104, followed by sibling ArcKnobs at 8,52). uidesc-inventory reports every sibling intersection. Disrumpo and Ruinae have plugins/<p>/tests/uidesc_overlaps_allowed.json, Membrum has none.

**Why wrong.** The repo's uidesc inventory check must pass, or the deliberate overlaps must be listed with a reason (the tool's --allow mechanism).

**Suggested fix.** Either nest the controls inside each FieldsetContainer (true containment, coordinates made relative), or add plugins/membrum/tests/uidesc_overlaps_allowed.json listing the 160 frame overlaps by template and detail with the reason 'decorative fieldset frame'. Test: `node tools/uidesc-inventory.js plugins/membrum/resources/editor.uidesc --check --allow plugins/membrum/tests/uidesc_overlaps_allowed.json` exits 0.

#### MB-199 — Physics (contradicted): Air Loading is described as a low-mode frequency depression that makes the drum deeper

**Severity:** low (filed as medium, downgraded on verification) · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:membrane-modes

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/MANUAL.md:177, 239-248](plugins/membrum/MANUAL.md#L177); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:121-125, 285-291](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h#L121); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/voice_common_params.h:45-48](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/voice_common_params.h#L45); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:62-86](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h#L62)

**Problem.** The code never lowers any frequency: (0,1) and (1,1) are anchored, and (2,1)..(5,1) go UP by 11.9 / 20.1 / 23.2 / 26.7 % at airLoading = 1 (+195 to +410 cents). The documentation says the opposite. MANUAL.md:241 says 'Rossing-tabulated low-mode frequency depression (5% at the fundamental, tapering toward zero by mode 12) ... lets the lowest modes drop into realistic kick/tom sub-bass territory'. pad_config.h:286-289 says '1 -> full Rossing-curve depression ... gives a realistic Membrane deeper / less whistly character'. pad_config.h:121-123 says 'airLoading depresses the lowest Bessel modes per the tabulated kAirLoadingCurve'. voice_common_params.h:46 gives 'f_k *= (1 - airLoading * curve[k])', and :47 says scatter maps to [0, 0.15] while the bank uses 0.10. MANUAL.md:177 lists Air Loading under the Body Size macro, but MacroMapper::applyBodySize (processor/macro_mapper.cpp:160-177) moves only size, modeStretch and decay, and nothing in processor/ except the proxy at processor.cpp:469-473 writes airLoading or modeScatter. The same table row lists Mode Scatter and Tension Modulation under Complexity, but macro_mapper.cpp:206-216 touches only couplingAmount, nonlinearCoupling and modeInjectAmount. The kettledrum series is also applied on every Membrane pad (kick, snare, toms) at default 0.6.

**Why wrong.** Physically, air loading LOWERS the low-frequency modes in absolute terms, the (1,1) the most (Rossing 1992: 'air loading, which lowers the low-frequency modes, is mainly responsible for establishing the harmonic relationship'). The coded model is a deliberate ratio-space equivalent: it holds (1,1) so the Size -> f0 mapping keeps its meaning (membrane_modes.h:82-86 documents this). So the knob RAISES the overtones relative to the fundamental, and the result is brighter and more tonal, not deeper. Also, the 1 : 1.5 : 2 : 2.44 : 2.9 series is a kettledrum (closed bowl) result. Two-headed drums (snare, bass drum, toms) instead show head-coupling mode PAIRS: Rossing 1992 measured a snare with (1,1) at 275 and 344 Hz and notes that bass-drum head coupling splits (0,1) and (1,1).

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992 [paper] https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf: Air loading lowers the low-frequency modes. In two-headed drums, coupling through the enclosed air or the shell forms mode pairs: snare (1,1) at 275 and 344 Hz, and bass drum coupling splits (0,1) and (1,1). The 1:1.5:2:2.44:2.90 series is a kettledrum result.
- The Well-Tempered Timpani, ch. 3 'Air loading' [docs] https://wtt.pauken.org/chapter-3/air-loading-2: Air loading lowers the natural frequencies from those of an ideal membrane, most strongly for the lower modes.

**Consequence.** Sound designers and preset voicers follow the manual. They turn Air Loading up to make a kick or tom 'deeper' or to reach 'sub-bass', and get the opposite: the fundamental stays put and the 2nd-5th diametric overtones rise by up to 4 semitones, so the pad gets brighter and more timpani-like. They also turn the Body Size or Complexity macros expecting Air Loading, Mode Scatter or Tension Modulation to move, and those parameters do not. Every membrane kick, snare and tom gets the same kettledrum tuning by default. This contributes to membrane pads sounding alike and is a direct misdirection for voicing.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: Not covered. Research entry 10 confirmed the ratio series and noted only the mass-vs-stiffness attribution; the documentation drift and the macro-table mismatch were not reviewed. The code and docs are unchanged since then.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite MANUAL.md:239-248, pad_config.h:121-125 and 285-291, and voice_common_params.h:45-48 to describe what the code does: 'tunes the (2..5,1) overtones up toward the timpani 1:1.5:2:2.44:2.9 series; the fundamental is anchored; brighter and more pitched, not deeper'; scatter is 10 %. Fix the MANUAL.md:177-179 macro table to match macro_mapper.cpp, or wire the macros to match the table, which is a product decision. If a 'deeper' effect is wanted, add an absolute (1,1)-and-below depression as a separate term. A doc-consistency test can grep MANUAL.md for 'depression' next to Air Loading. A unit test should pin that airLoading 0 -> 1 leaves frequencies[0] and frequencies[1] unchanged and raises frequencies[2], [4], [6], [9] by the table factors.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed every code claim: membrane_mapper.h:100-108 computes `f0 * kMembraneRatios[k] * (1 + airLoading*(kAirLoadingTargetScale[k]-1))`; the table (membrane_modes.h:98-105) is 1.0 at indices 0/1 and 1.1192 / 1.2012 / 1.2321 / 1.2668 at 2/4/6/9, so nothing goes down. kAirLoadingCurve does not exist; the formula at voice_common_params.h:46 appears nowhere; the bank uses `C = scatter * 0.10f` (modal_resonator_bank.h:784, comment :770-774). Macros: applyBodySize (macro_mapper.cpp:160-178) and applyComplexity (:201-219) never write airLoading, modeScatter, tensionModAmt or secondarySize. Default 0.6 (pad_config.h:291), 0.4-0.7 in default_kit.h. preset-retune/archetypes/acoustic-maple-kick-acoustic-bass-drum.md:54 admits the upper modes scale UP. Downgraded: the defect is documentation; the DSP faithfully implements Rossing's ratios.
- Confirmed from code and from https://wtt.pauken.org/chapter-3/air-loading-2 (opened: air loading lowers natural frequencies, strongest for low modes, (1,1) by ~518 cents down to (5,1) by ~50 cents at A2). membrane_modes.h:64-69 frames the model correctly as ratio space; MANUAL.md:241's "5 % ... 12-mode" table exists nowhere in src. The kettledrum-on-two-headed-drums remark is fair.
- Doc-vs-code contradiction real; the "physics contradicted" framing is not, since membrane_modes.h:62-92 documents the anchoring and the prior audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:312) confirmed the series. default_kit.h:74-76 voices the kick with "strong air-loading for a deep kick", so the misconception has reached factory voicing. airLoading and modeScatter are written only by the proxy (processor.cpp:469), the codec, the voice pool and default_kit.

#### MB-200 — Physics (unsupported): Mode Scatter models natural head imperfection and reproduces the (0,1)/(1,1) mode splitting of a real snare head

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-unsupported · **Dimension:** research:membrane-modes

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:654-656, 784, 809-810](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L654) (comments at [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:121-125](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h#L121), [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h:74-77, 132-135, 163-165](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h#L74))

**Problem.** f_w *= 1 + C * sin(k * pi*(phi-1)), with C = scatter * 0.10 and k the bank index (membrane: sorted mode index), from MembraneMapper r.scatter = modeScatter (membrane_mapper.h:176). Mode 0 is never moved (sin 0 = 0). Every other mode becomes a single, displaced partial (up to +/-10 %, about +/-165 cents). No doublet is created. default_kit.h:132-133 claims that snare 'scatter 0.28 reproduces the (0,1)/(1,1) mode splitting of a real snare head'. Measured at airLoading = 1, relative to (1,1): scatter 0.5 moves (2,1) 1.500 -> 1.385 and (5,1) 2.900 -> 2.635; scatter 1.0 gives (2,1) 1.280, (4,1) 2.055 next to (3,1) 2.012, and (0,2) 1.260.

**Why wrong.** Real head imperfection splits each degenerate m >= 1 mode into a closely spaced DOUBLET (Euphonics: 'slightly separated in frequency', showing as double peaks), which beats. In two-headed drums the head coupling forms mode PAIRS for (0,1) and (1,1) (Rossing 1992: snare (1,1) at 275 / 344 Hz). Neither is a displacement of a single partial, and the (0,1) splitting that the snare comment cites cannot come from a term that leaves mode 0 fixed. A sinusoidal index dither of +/-10 % is a creative inharmonicity control, not a physical imperfection model.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- J. Woodhouse, Euphonics, '3.6 Tuned drums' [docs] https://euphonics.org/3-6-tuned-drums/: Any real drum departs from perfect circular symmetry, so the cos/sin mode pairs are normally slightly separated in frequency and show up as double peaks in a frequency response.
- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992 [paper] https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf: Coupling between the two heads forms mode pairs: snare (0,1)-like and (1,1)-like pairs, (1,1) at 275 and 344 Hz. Bass-drum head coupling splits (0,1) and (1,1).

**Consequence.** Scatter does not add the slow beating of split doublets that makes a real head sound alive. At moderate to high settings it also undoes the air-loading harmonicity, for example (2,1)/(1,1) 1.50 -> 1.28 at scatter 1. The default-kit settings (kick/tom 0.15, snare 0.28) shift (1,1) by +1.4 / +2.6 % and (2,1) by -1.0 / -1.9 %, a mild detune, not the claimed snare splitting. Severity is low because the knob works as a deliberate creative dither, but its comments claim a physical basis it does not have.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: Not covered for the membrane; prior research reviewed kScatterD only as a constant (the golden-ratio sine vs frac(k*phi), entry near findings.json:1514). The code is unchanged since the audit.

**Suggested fix.** Option A (physical): for each m >= 1 membrane mode, add a second bank entry, the sin member, at f*(1 + delta), with delta = scatter * ~0.02 drawn from a fixed per-mode table. Excite it with a small weight (for example 0.3 * scatter), modelling a strike off the symmetry axis, so the pair beats. Option B (minimal): keep the dither and fix the comments in default_kit.h:132-133, pad_config.h:121-125 and :287, and voice_common_params.h:47 to call it an artistic inharmonicity dither of up to 10 % that leaves mode 0 fixed. Test for A: render a membrane pad at scatter 0.5 and assert two spectral peaks within 3 % around the (1,1) frequency whose amplitude envelope beats. Test for B: assert frequencies[0] is unchanged by scatter.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: modal_resonator_bank.h:655-656 (kScatterD), :784 (C = scatter*0.10f), :810 (per-index displacement, no added entry). MembraneMapper (membrane_mapper.h:102-109, 175-176) fills 48 modes, one per (m,n), index 0 = (0,1), with no cos/sin twin (membrane_modes.h:30-46). The default_kit.h:132-133 claim is false as written; pad_config.h:287 ("15 %") and voice_common_params.h:47 ("[0, 0.15]") are stale against the 10 % code. At C = 0.028, k = 1, sin(1.941) ≈ 0.932 gives +2.6 % on (1,1). Low.
- Confirmed: the loop at modal_resonator_bank.h:786-835 writes one epsilon/radius/gain per k. Euphonics 3.6 (opened) describes double peaks from broken symmetry, i.e. a doublet; it does not mention beating. Rossing 1992 PDF not opened, so the 275/344 Hz figures are unverified; the conclusion does not depend on them. Low; supports Option B.
- Confirmed: kMembraneRatios order (membrane_modes.h:30-37): (0,1) 1.0, (1,1) 1.5933, (2,1) 2.1357, (0,2) 2.2954; sin(1.9416) = 0.932, sin(3.883) = -0.675 reproduce the quoted shifts. The false claim was copied into preset-retune/archetypes/acoustic-snare-wire-buzz.md:20 and preset-retune/recipes.json:3216. The dither itself is documented as deliberate (MANUAL.md:243, pad_config.h:121-125), but the default-kit and retune comments claim a physical effect it cannot produce; the prior audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:323) does not rule on it. Missing doublet beating would be borderline on the short snare body (b1 ~30 s^-1, T60 ~0.23 s).

#### MB-201 — Physics (contradicted): Membrane inharmonicity (Stretch) uses the stiff-string law sqrt(1 + B n^2) with n = sorted mode index + 1, on by default via material

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:membrane-modes · **Also flagged by:** research:nonlinear-coupling

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:776-807](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L776) (membrane stretch source: [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:129-138](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L129))

**Problem.** MembraneMapper sets stretch = clamp(material*0.3 + (modeStretchNorm - 1/3)), which is material*0.3 at the default modeStretch 1.0. The bank computes B = stretch^2 * 0.01 and f_w = f_k * sqrt(1 + B*(k+1)^2), with k the index into the 48 sorted membrane modes. Measured, as a multiplier on the Bessel frequency: material 0.3 (default-kit kick) gives B = 8.1e-5, mode 9 x1.004, mode 23 x1.023, mode 47 x1.089. Material 0.5 (snare) gives B = 2.25e-4: x1.011 / x1.063 / x1.232. Material 1.0 gives B = 9e-4: (1,1) x1.002, mode 9 x1.044, mode 23 x1.232, mode 47 x1.753. Because a 2-D membrane's sorted index grows as k+1 ~ j_mn^2 (index 9 <-> j 8.77, index 47 <-> j 19.6: 4.8 vs (19.6/8.77)^2 = 5.0), the coded warp behaves as sqrt(1 + B' j^4).

**Why wrong.** A stiff membrane (tension plus bending) obeys omega^2 = c^2 k^2 + kappa^2 k^4, so f_mn = f_mn,ideal * sqrt(1 + beta * j_mn^2), with the dispersion growing as the wavenumber j_mn (the mode ratio), not as the sorted mode count. Rossing 1992 confirms the effect qualitatively ('the bending stiffness of the membrane, like the stiffness of piano strings, raises the frequencies of the higher overtones') and treats it as a fine-tuning effect. The code's law gives the top modes an effective dispersion of order j^4 instead of j^2, much steeper than a stiff membrane and even steeper than a thin plate (omega ~ k^2). It is also active by default on every membrane pad through material.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- T. D. Rossing, 'Acoustics of drums', Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992 [paper] https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf: Bending stiffness of the membrane, like the stiffness of piano strings, raises the frequencies of the higher overtones. Air loading is mainly responsible for the harmonic relationship, and the other effects only fine-tune.
- S. Bilbao, Numerical Sound Synthesis, Wiley 2009, ch. 11-12 (stiff membrane / thin plate: u_tt = c^2 Lap u - kappa^2 Lap^2 u) [textbook]: Stiff-membrane dispersion omega^2 = c^2 |k|^2 + kappa^2 |k|^4: the stiffness correction depends on the spatial wavenumber |k| = j_mn/a, not on a mode count.

**Consequence.** At the default-kit materials (0.3-0.5) the top third of the membrane modes are 2-23 % sharp, enough to make the upper membrane spectrum read as slightly metallic and to detune any air-loading structure above mode ~20. At material near 1, mode 23 is +23 % and mode 47 +75 %: the membrane becomes a different, plate-like inharmonic object instead of a stiff drumhead. Because Material also drives decay and b3 brightness, this is a hidden extra axis tied to Material that pushes membrane pads toward the same bright inharmonic smear.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: Prior audit L-1 / section 3-B ('Stretch: form right, index wrong, range tiny') was judged for the stiff-string case and marked DONE in 41877a8e: index changed to k+1 and B_max raised from 0.001 to 0.01. That commit states it changed the DEFAULT timbre of all bodies because the membrane feeds material*0.3. So the code changed after the audit, and the change made this mismatch audible. The membrane-specific dispersion law was never reviewed.

**Suggested fix.** Apply the stiffness in MembraneMapper using the membrane's own wavenumber, f_k *= sqrt(1 + B_m * (kMembraneRatios[k]^2 - 1)), which keeps (0,1) exact, with B_m sized so material 1 gives a few % at mode 9. Pass stretch = 0 to the bank for the membrane, or add a bank overload that takes per-mode dispersion keys. Keep the modeStretch knob as an explicit unnatural extra. Test: for material 0.5 and modeStretch 1.0, assert getModeFrequency(k)/BesselFreq(k) == sqrt(1 + B_m*(ratio_k^2 - 1)) within 0.1 % for k = 0..47, and that (0,1) is unchanged.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: the stretch reaches the bank at note-on (membrane_body.h:36-42), on retune (drum_voice.h:1619-1625) and on the Material Morph refresh (drum_voice.h:1656-1664), all through computeModeCoefficients (modal_resonator_bank.h:272, :303); :783 B = stretch^2*0.01, :806-807 the stiff-string warp. The comment at :776-781 says "Membrum default-off", which is wrong for the membrane. Multipliers recomputed and correct; default kit materials 0.3-0.95 (default_kit.h:49, :100, :146, :189, :222, :277, :317). The stretched f_w also drives the f^2 damping (:823) and the Nyquist cull (:813). Low.
- Confirmed: membrane_body.h:41 and drum_voice.h:1624/1663 pass the stretch unchanged; k indexes the sorted Bessel zeros (membrane_modes.h:28-37, 108-115), so k+1 is a mode count. Rossing PDF could not be fetched (size limit); the stiff-membrane form omega^2 = (T/sigma)k^2 + (D/sigma)k^4 was confirmed via arXiv 1808.10576 and Bilbao. The mapper calls this "material's inherent stretch", not an Unnatural Zone effect. Low.
- Confirmed: only the intent is documented (specs/136-membrum-phase1-scaffold/spec.md:152, research.md:121-125: "slight" stretch with B = stretch^2*0.001); the prior audit (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:60, :64, :324) reviewed it only as the stiff-string case and recorded the default-timbre change as user-approved; correctness-audit.md has no Stretch entry. The "slight" intent is now exceeded (+23 % at mode 47 for the default snare). Impact low: the shifted modes are the dense upper cluster shortened by b3*f^2 damping, and (0,1)/(1,1) move <= 0.2 % at material <= 0.5.

#### MB-211 — Physics (oversimplified): Tuning compensation for the loop filters' phase delay (fundamental lands on the mapped f0)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:string-body

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/waveguide_string.h:321-341](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/waveguide_string.h#L321) (and 515-544, 199-201)

**Problem.** noteOn: D = period - 1 - 0.55*dLoss - 0.96*dDisp (:337), with empirical scale factors and no term for the in-loop DC blocker (3.5 Hz, :199-201), whose phase lead grows as 1/f^2. The dispersion term is 0 in Membrum (claim 7). Measured fundamental error against the mapped f0 = 800*0.1^size, pick 0.3: Size 0 (800 Hz) +1.2 / -2.0 / -5.3 cents for Material 1 / 0.5 / 0 at 48 kHz (-5.85 at 44.1 kHz). Size 0.5 (253 Hz) +1.8..+3.8. Size 0.7 (160 Hz) +4.4..+6.0. Size 1 (80 Hz) +11.2..+11.9 cents at all three rates. The fs-independent +12 cents at 80 Hz is the uncorrected DC-blocker lead (about -4.2 samples out of 600). retune() already uses the exact budget D = period - 1 - dLoss - dDisp - dDC (:532), and its own comment documents the noteOn error.

**Why wrong.** A loop resonates where the summed phase delay of every in-loop element equals the period at f0 (Jaffe-Smith: the damping filter's phase delay, which is S samples at low frequency, must be subtracted, and the remainder taken up by the tuning allpass). The exact budget subtracts dLoss, dDisp, dDC and the interpolator's phase delay, all evaluated at f0, with no empirical factors.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- J.O. Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Extended Karplus-Strong Algorithm' [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Extended_Karplus_Strong_Algorithm.html: The total loop delay (delay line, damping filter, stiffness allpass and tuning allpass) sets the pitch. The tuning allpass supplies the fractional remainder after the other filters' phase delays.
- J.O. Smith, Physical Audio Signal Processing, 'Fractional Delay Filtering by Linear Interpolation' [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Fractional_Delay_Filtering_Linear.html: Linear interpolation's delay is exact only at DC. The frequency-dependent delay error is what the empirical 0.55 / 0.96 factors try to absorb.

**Consequence.** Small. Large String pads (Size above 0.7) sit 6-12 cents sharp of the frequency the mapper, naturalFundamentalHz() and the pitch-envelope baseline assume. Because Size is a continuous knob and String ignores MIDI pitch, this matters only for kits tuned in Hz and for the pitch-envelope end point once claim 4 is fixed. It does not make kits sound alike.
