Downgraded because latching at note-on is the spec's design: specs/139-membrum-phase4-pads/research.md:89-93 ("Does NOT touch currently sounding voices"), specs/138-membrum-phase3-polyphony/plan.md:304, specs/139.../spec.md:182. The real gap is user-facing documentation (MANUAL.md:227 names only the exciter type) and the pan/bus inconsistency. Low.
- Documented design choice, not a defect: specs/139-membrum-phase4-pads/spec.md:353, :369, :372 (ToneShaper configured per pad at note-on, covering cutoff / drive / fold), FR-003 (:199), edge case :182; specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md FR-005 (:180) and scenarios :79/:81. The live DrumVoice setters are leftovers of the Phase-1 single-voice API. What remains is a MANUAL documentation nit; live voice updates would be a new feature against the spec.
- Mechanism real (pad_config_apply.h:30-38; per-pad IDs processor.cpp:202/214/222/232, proxies :268-521; no other path to active voices; pan read live per mix). Neither the MANUAL nor specs/135 says the other parameters latch. Impact lens: no state corruption, every edit audible from the next strike, latch-at-trigger is normal drum-machine behaviour, and the gap only shows for voices ringing longer than the inter-hit gap (Friction sustain, modeInject plateau, long Bell/Plate cymbals). Low.

#### MB-110 — Browser preset load applies every field twice by two different code paths; about 2,119 edits and 162 matrix rebuilds per kit load

**Severity:** low (filed medium; downgraded on verification) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** parallel-path · **Dimension:** duplication-drift · **Also flagged by:** parallel-paths, gestalt-controller

**Corroborated by measurement:** Probe focus2:double-apply:edits: "2119 (2112/7) / 2119 / 2119 / 162" (performEdit per-pad/global / beginEdit / endEdit / recomputeCouplingMatrix calls in the next block). controller_state.cpp:163-170 `setParamNormalized(id, clamped); beginEdit(id); performEdit(id, clamped); endEdit(id);`.

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state.cpp:146-172, 243-271](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state.cpp#L146)

**Problem.** kitPresetLoadProvider sends LoadPresetState (Processor::notify, then applyKitSnapshot, which writes every PadConfig field through State::applyPadSnapshot). It then replays the whole snapshot through setAndNotify (setParamNormalized + beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit), and that replay rewrites every field again through processParameterChanges and VoicePool::setPadConfigField. By reading the code, per pad that is 2 selectors + 5 macros + 28 contiguous + choke + bus + 4 exciter-secondary + couplingAmount + 24 late slots = 66 edits (64 when B1/B3 hold the sentinel). Over 32 pads plus 7 globals that is up to 2,119 gestures. Per pad the processor branches call recomputeCouplingMatrix 5 times (exciter :187, body :198, pitchEnvTime :206, couplingAmount :215, Complexity macro :227), plus snareBuzz :415 and tomResonance :422, for 162 rebuilds of a 32x32 table per kit load in one audio block. Per the matrix finding, nobody reads that table. The two routes encode values differently: route 1 keeps slots 0-33 unclamped and the B1/B3 sentinel and noiseLayerGain; route 2 clamps every value to [0,1] and skips the sentinel and slot 57.

**Why wrong.** R-202 / R-203 made the message the single apply path. The replay exists only to inform the host, yet it reaches the processor as real edits. Two parallel writers of the same state must produce identical results by construction, not by the values happening to agree.

**Consequence.** Every kit-browser load puts about 2,100 entries into host undo and automation history (one per parameter gesture) and writes automation in latch/write modes. It also costs a burst of 162 matrix rebuilds plus the setPadConfigField storm in one process() call. Blobs with any slot-0..33 value outside [0,1] end in a different state after a browser load than after a host load of the same bytes. Ordering between the IMessage (message thread) and the queued parameter changes (next audio block) is not guaranteed, so a second preset load or note-ons that interleave can observe a half-replayed first kit.

**Evidence.** controller_state.cpp:150-158 sendMessage("LoadPresetState"); :163-172 setAndNotify { setParamNormalized; beginEdit; performEdit; endEdit } then applySnapshot(kit, setAndNotify, ...). controller_state_codec.cpp:190-271 per-pad setter calls (2 + 5 macros + 28 + 2 + 4 + 1 + kLateSlots[24] with the sentinel skip at :265-268). processor.cpp:178-228 branches that call recomputeCouplingMatrix().

**Suggested fix.** Inform the host without re-applying. Either use restartComponent(kParamValuesChanged) after base-class setParamNormalized (no performEdit), or keep performEdit and have the processor ignore per-pad edits that equal the current cfg value. Then the snapshot has one writer. Test: count performEdit calls and recomputeCouplingMatrix calls (via a test seam) during a kit load, assert both are 0 (or bounded), and assert the final getState equals a host setState of the same blob, including a blob with an out-of-range slot-5 value.

**Verifier notes:**
- Traced and holds: route 1 is processor.cpp:1222-1240 -> applyKitSnapshot (:918-1003: voice reset, State::applyPadSnapshot at :937-942, one matrix recompute at :988, macro-cache sync at :999-1002); route 2 is controller_state.cpp:163-172 -> applyPadSnapshotToParams (controller_state_codec.cpp:183-272) and globals (:372-396), re-applied by processParameterChanges (processor.cpp:175-234). 162 rebuilds confirmed. Encoding differs: State::applyPadSnapshot clamps slots 34+ (state_codec.cpp:202-245) and slot 57 to [0.1, 16], keeps the sentinel (:218-221), leaves 0-33 unclamped; route 2 clamps to [0,1] and has no ParamID for slot 57; sendMessage is synchronous, so route 2's clamped value wins. The pad-preset path duplicates the pattern (controller_state.cpp:247-271). Deliberate per :161-162, but two writers of the same state exist.
- Mechanism correct, but deliberate, documented and pinned by a test: specs/ruinae-audit/fix-plan.md:923-924 (T1.36, R-202) explicitly keeps the performEdit mirror; tests/unit/preset/test_kit_browser_load.cpp:267-276 forwards every recorded performEdit and "Browser load leaves the processor in the same state as a host load" (:290-320) checks getState is byte-identical to host setState(B) across kits differing in noiseLayerGain, sentinel vs explicit B1/B3, macros and coupling (:195-221). The value divergence cannot be reached with a plugin-written blob (state_codec.cpp:162-200 unclamped, but every writer stays in [0,1]; MacroMapper clamps, macro_mapper.cpp:14-16).
- Real but overstated; downgrade to low: values do not differ for real presets (choke/bus rounding voice_pool.cpp:641-655, macro cache resync processor.cpp:999-1002, test_kit_browser_load.cpp:290-316); the clamping difference only affects hand-made blobs and the browser route ends in the safer state; 162 recomputes cost tens to a few hundred microseconds, not a dropout; the undo/automation flood is host-dependent, and per-parameter performEdit on an internal preset load is a common VST3 pattern (controller_state.cpp:161-162).

#### MB-133 — Mode Stretch 'Phase-1 bit-identity' relies on arithmetic that does not cancel: the default modeStretch decodes to 0.99999946

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** dsp-numerics · **Dimension:** portability-quality · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:123-138](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L123)

**Problem.** The Membrane mapper claims that when modeStretch == 1.0 "the mapper is bit-identical to the Phase 1 code path". It subtracts kUnityStretchNorm = (1.0f-0.5f)/1.5f from clamp((modeStretch-0.5f)*(1.0f/1.5f)). But the stored default is the normalised 0.333333f (pad_config.h:212, controller.cpp:189, processor.cpp:71), and pad_config_apply.h:126 decodes it as 0.5f + n*1.5f = 0.99999946. A multiply by (1/1.5) is also not the same operation as a divide by 1.5.

**Why wrong.** CLAUDE.md: "Produce a value that must be exact at a neutral point ... by a branch or a clamp, not by arithmetic that cancels in IEEE". With fast-math contraction or reassociation the residual also differs between x86 and arm64.

**Consequence.** The default stretch is material*0.3 - 3.6e-7 rather than material*0.3. That is inaudible, but the documented bit-identity (FR-055 "default-off guarantee") is false, and a test written against that claim would be platform-dependent. The same applies to the other bodies' (modeStretch-0.5)/1.5 baselines.

**Evidence.** membrane_mapper.h:126-138 "When modeStretch==1.0, the extra contribution is 0 and the mapper is bit-identical to the Phase 1 code path" + `constexpr float kUnityStretchNorm = (1.0f - 0.5f) / 1.5f; const float stretchDelta = stretchFromStretchParam - kUnityStretchNorm;`. pad_config_apply.h:126 `0.5f + std::clamp(cfg.modeStretch, 0.0f, 1.0f) * 1.5f`. Node probe (Math.fround): ms 0.999999463558197, stretchParam 0.33333298563957214, kUnity 0.3333333432674408, delta -3.5762786865234375e-7.

**Suggested fix.** Snap modeStretch to exactly 1.0 when |n - 1/3| is below a tolerance (a branch in pad_config_apply.h), or store the default as the exact double 1.0/3.0 and branch on stretchFromStretchParam near kUnityStretchNorm in the mapper. Fix the comments either way.

**Verifier notes:**
- Numbers reproduced (Math.fround: n 0.33333298563957214, modeStretch 0.999999463558197, delta -3.5762786865234375e-7); the claim at membrane_mapper.h:126-138 and pad_config_apply.h:123-124 never holds on the real PadConfig route. The mapper itself cancels exactly for an exact 1.0f input, so the defect is the normalised default (pad_config.h:212), not the subtraction. Inaudible; no test depends on it (test_mode_stretch.cpp:132 sets 1.0f directly with Approx margin 1e-6, lines 142-151; T107 at :204-238 uses a -120 dBFS tolerance). "Other bodies" is overstated: plate_mapper.h:60-62 and the bell/shell/noise mappers subtract no baseline and claim no bit-identity. Nit-level.
- Refuted: specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:240 defines FR-055 "bit-identical" as "within -120 dBFS noise floor", so 3.6e-7 is inside the specified tolerance; at exact 1.0f the mapper is exact (0.5f*fround(1/1.5) == fround(0.5/1.5) = 0.33333334); test_mode_stretch.cpp:128-153 and T107 (:194-204) use tolerances. What remains is loose comment wording.
- Confirmed but smaller: the residual comes from the truncated literal 0.333333f (pad_config.h:212) decoded at pad_config_apply.h:126; comments at membrane_mapper.h:126-135 and pad_config_apply.h:123-124 are false on the PadConfig path; the "platform-dependent test" consequence does not occur (test_mode_stretch.cpp:128-153, :204). Recommend nit/informational; the snap-to-1.0 fix is cheap.

#### MB-147 — Tests pin the wholesale rejection of state versions 1 and 2, which released builds wrote; no fixture from a released tag is loaded

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** test-gap · **Dimension:** test-gaps · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/tests/unit/state/test_state_codec.cpp:123-141](plugins/membrum/tests/unit/state/test_state_codec.cpp#L123)

**Problem.** "readKitBlob rejects every version other than kBlobVersion" asserts kResultFalse for versions 1 and 2 (and 3 and 4) with the comment "Pre-release reset". Released tags wrote exactly those versions: git show membrum/v0.9.0 has kBlobVersion = 1 and v0.10.2 has 2 ("56-slot sound array"); v0.12.0 onward has 5. The checked-in v2 fixture tests/golden/phase2_state_v2.bin (268 B, header int32 2) is referenced by no test.

**Why wrong.** Whether to migrate or reject released state is a product decision. The test encodes data loss as the expected behaviour without that decision being recorded, and nothing exercises a real blob from a shipped build: setState returns kResultFalse and the project loads at defaults.

**Consequence.** DAW projects and user presets saved with Membrum 0.9.x or 0.10.x fail to load (setState and setComponentState return kResultFalse, controller_state.cpp). The suite treats this as correct.

**Evidence.** test_state_codec.cpp:126-139: "Pre-release reset: only the single current kBlobVersion is accepted ... for (int32 badVersion : { 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, ... }) CHECK(readKitBlob(&stream, dst) == kResultFalse);". `git show membrum/v0.9.0:plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.h` line 104: `kBlobVersion = 1`. membrum/v0.10.2 line 105: `kBlobVersion = 2;  // Phase 10: 56-slot sound array`. `od` of phase2_state_v2.bin: first int32 = 2. No grep hit for "phase2_state" under plugins/membrum/tests.

**Suggested fix.** Record the decision first. If migration is chosen, add tests/golden/state_v1_v0.9.0.bin and state_v2_v0.10.2.bin generated from the tagged builds, and TEST_CASE("setState loads state written by released versions", "[state_codec][migration]") that REQUIREs kResultOk and spot-checks pad 0 material/size and pad count. If rejection is chosen, keep the test, delete the orphan phase2_state_v2.bin, and fix the "plugin has not shipped" comments. Either way the test should name the release tags it covers.

**Verifier notes:**
- Not refuted: the test pins rejection (test_state_codec.cpp:123-141); the reader has no migration branch (state_codec.cpp:431-432 `if (version != kBlobVersion) return kResultFalse;`); tags v0.9.0/v0.9.1 (state_codec.h:104) wrote 1, v0.10.2 (:105) wrote 2, v0.12.0 (:108) wrote 5; no test loads a released blob. Correction: phase2_state_v2.bin is a 268-byte April 2026 Phase-2 development fixture, not a v0.10.2 kit blob (32 pads × 56 slots). Medium fits.
- Refuted: the decision is recorded in released CHANGELOG entries, plugins/membrum/CHANGELOG.md:230-233 ([0.11.0]: "Pre-release, strict version check with no migration: state and presets saved by older builds are rejected on load") and :188-191 (v5); phase2_state_v2.bin is cited only by specs/138-membrum-phase3-polyphony/{plan,tasks,quickstart}.md. What remains is housekeeping (orphan fixture, "has not shipped" wording, test not naming tags).
- Refuted: CHANGELOG.md:327-329 (0.10.0: "Legacy v1 blobs are rejected per the existing pre-release policy"), :230-232, :188-191 record the policy, and the released reader enforced it (`git show membrum/v0.10.2:plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.cpp:395` `if (version != kBlobVersion)`). The test pins documented policy; the 268-byte fixture is not a release fixture.
- TIE-BREAK (Fable): not refuted, downgrade medium -> low. Confirmed: rejection pinned at test_state_codec.cpp:123-141, pad-preset twin :257-273, processor twin test_state_v6_migration.cpp:207-223; state_codec.cpp:431-432 with processor.cpp:911-912 and controller_state.cpp:70-71 passing the failure through; `gh release list` shows all ten Membrum tags (v0.9.0 2026-04-26 to v0.12.5 2026-11-23) as prerelease=false; tests/golden holds only phase1_default.bin (used by approval/test_phase1_regression.cpp:82) and the unused phase2_state_v2.bin (commit 8d23d774); the stated rationale is false (state_codec.h:12-13 "The plugin has not shipped", plugin_ids.h:27, :230). The skeptics are right that the rejection is recorded (CHANGELOG.md:188-191, :230-233, :327-329), so "unrecorded" is wrong; but the recorded decision rests on a "pre-release" premise that ten public releases contradict, and version rejection is not among the audit's listed intended constraints.

#### MB-157 — Finding 12 pattern reintroduced by the Finding 6 fix: grid view mutations from setComponentState / setParamNormalized bypass requestViewRefresh (and Finding 12's deferral has no test)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** prior-audit-regression · **Dimension:** prior-audit-regressions · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state.cpp:91-96](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state.cpp#L91); [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:857, 882, 903, 913](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp#L857)

**Problem.** Finding 12 routed the five view-mutating helpers through requestViewRefresh so that they apply on the UI thread or are deferred to the poll timer. The Finding 6 fix then added padGridView_->setSelectedPadIndex() in setComponentState and the kSelectedPadId branch. The existing setPadEnabled / notifyMetaChanged calls and pushKitEnabledToGrid also mutate the grid directly. Each of these calls PadGridView::invalid() (pad_grid_view.cpp:165, 176, 187) without the thread check. Finding 12's own resolution states "No new test".

**Why wrong.** Finding 12's defense-in-depth for non-compliant hosts covers only five helpers; later fixes went straight past it. Its deferral path is untested.

**Consequence.** In a host that calls setComponentState or setParamNormalized off the UI thread, the pad grid is invalidated from that thread. Low risk on compliant hosts.

**Evidence.** controller_state.cpp:95-96 `if (padGridView_ != nullptr) padGridView_->setSelectedPadIndex(selectedPadIndex_);` controller_view_sync.cpp:109-124 requestViewRefresh covers only the morph, pitch-env and filter-env helpers; correctness-audit.md:135 "No new test".

**Suggested fix.** Add a kRefreshPadGrid flag (selection plus enabled mask) and route these calls through requestViewRefresh. Add a test that calls setParamNormalized(kSelectedPadId) from a std::thread with an open editor and REQUIREs that the grid updates only after the timer drain.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: requestViewRefresh applies only on uiThreadId_ (controller_view_sync.cpp:109-115; set in didOpen, controller.cpp:1505; drained at :1522) and its flags (controller.h:327-331, applyViewRefresh controller_view_sync.cpp:117-124) have no pad-grid entry; the bypassing mutations are controller_state.cpp:91 (pushKitEnabledToGrid -> controller.cpp:1488), :95-96, controller.cpp:857, 882, 903, 913, all reaching invalid() unchecked (pad_grid_view.cpp:158-188); updateOutputBusTooltip (controller.cpp:888, controller_view_sync.cpp:84/90) likewise. "Reintroduced" is half right: the setSelectedPadIndex calls are Finding 6's, the notifyMetaChanged/setPadEnabled sites (Phase 8 / FR-065 / Phase 8F) predate it and were left out of Finding 12. Low is right.
- Refuted as a defect: correctness-audit.md §5 (Finding 12) rules the SDK tags these callbacks [UI-thread & Connected], "not a demonstrable race", so harm needs a non-compliant host; the grid calls at controller.cpp:882/903/913 come from separate features, not regressions; every call is null-guarded and skips unchanged values; the missing test is a documented decision. At most a consistency nit.
- Confirmed, narrower impact: correctness-audit.md:135/:137 confirm the five-helper scope and "defense-in-depth"; padGridView_ is non-null only while the editor is open (verifyView controller.cpp:1141, willClose :1665); the off-thread work is one store plus invalid(); the kitPresetLoadProvider call site (controller_state.cpp:183) runs on the UI thread. No audible or state consequence; recommend nit/informational.

#### MB-158 — Extra focus (2): a kit-browser load applies the kit twice; the replay costs about 163 coupling-matrix recomputes and about 2,100 host edits, and can overwrite a later load's damping sentinel

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** parallel-path · **Dimension:** gestalt-processor · **Source:** static

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp:183-271, 367-379](plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller_state_codec.cpp#L183)

**Problem.** After LoadPresetState has already applied the kit through applyKitSnapshot, the controller replays it through performEdit. Per pad, applyPadSnapshotToParams writes 2 selectors, 5 macros, 28 contiguous offsets, choke, bus, 4 exciter-secondary offsets, couplingAmount and the 24 late slots (minus the sentinel damping slots). That is about 64-66 edits per pad, roughly 2,080-2,110 for 32 pads, plus the globals at 372-379. Each edit reaches Processor::processParameterChanges. Per pad, these branches call recomputeCouplingMatrix: exciter (187), body (198), tsPitchEnvTime (206, one of the contiguous offsets), couplingAmount (215) and macroComplexity (227). That is 5 × 32 = 160, plus snareBuzz (415) and tomResonance (422) = 162, plus the one in applyKitSnapshot (988). Each recompute is a 32x32 loop, all in one audio block when the host delivers the replay at once. The values match the message route: selectors decode floor((i+0.5)/n·n) = i, and VST parameters are clamped to [0,1]. Exceptions are noiseLayerGain (no parameter) and the sentinel damping slots, which the replay skips (265-268), so the message wins for those. The two routes cross threads with no ordering. Say kit A's replay edits are still queued when kit B's message is applied, and A carries explicit damping where B has the -1 sentinel. A's queued edit then writes the explicit value over B's sentinel, and B's replay does not correct it because it skips sentinel slots.

**Why wrong.** One user action should produce one engine apply and no host-visible parameter gestures. A preset load is not an automation gesture: about 2,100 begin/perform/end triplets fill the host's undo history, and they overwrite automation lanes when the track is in write or touch mode.

**Consequence.** An audio-thread burst on every kit load; an undo history full of entries that the user's preset load created; automation written over during playback in write mode. The rare A-then-B interleave leaves B's pads with A's damping (a decay change).

**Evidence.** controller_state_codec.cpp:210-214 macros; :217-221 contiguous; :226-229 choke/bus; :235-239 exciter-secondary; :243-244 couplingAmount; :263-271 late slots with the sentinel `continue`; processor.cpp:187, 198, 206, 215, 227, 415, 422 recomputeCouplingMatrix calls; processor.cpp:1222-1239 the message route already applies everything. Counts are from reading the code, not a probe.

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the controller parameters with the base setParamNormalized only (as setComponentState does) and rely on the LoadPresetState message as the single processor apply, after making that apply audio-thread-safe (see the threading finding). Then call host restartComponent(kParamValuesChanged) so the host refreshes its view. If a replay must stay, tag it with a load sequence number and drop stale replays. Test: count performEdit calls in test_kit_browser_load (expect 0) and count recomputeCouplingMatrix calls through a test hook.

**Verifier notes:**
- Facts correct, severity too high: kitPresetLoadProvider sends LoadPresetState (controller_state.cpp:150-159), notify applies it (processor.cpp:1222-1239, recompute at :988), then applySnapshot replays 7 globals (controller_state_codec.cpp:372-385) and 32 pads (:388-392) through setParamNormalized + begin/perform/endEdit (controller_state.cpp:163-172); 64-66 edits per pad and 163 recomputes confirmed; the comment at controller_state.cpp:161-162 says the replay is deliberate. Interleave possible in principle (last point per queue, processor.cpp:163-166; sentinel skip codec :265-268). Downgrade: recomputeFromTier1 (coupling_matrix.h:42-77) is a bounded 32x32 loop, ~167k trivial ops, well under a millisecond; values match in the common case.
- Refuted: the double apply is documented design, "one preset-load path (R-202)" (controller_state.cpp:146-149, :161-162 "The edits tell the host (automation, undo, dirty flag)") per specs/ruinae-audit/fix-plan.md T1.36 (~915-930); values match (codec :190-195, setter clamp controller_state.cpp:165, sentinel skip :252-268); recompute cost is RT-safe (processor.cpp:131-143); the A-then-B interleave needs two browser loads inside one 3-10 ms block, which no human click produces; the sentinel root cause belongs to extra-focus lead (1). No measurement offered.
- Real, downgrade to low: double apply, edit counts (contiguous array at codec :31-43, 2,048-2,112 edits) and 163 recomputes confirmed; interleave path real and untested (test_kit_browser_load.cpp:290-316 only covers A, process, B, process); but no audible difference sequentially (that test asserts byte-identical state with a host setState load; macro cache synced at processor.cpp:999-1002) and the CPU burst is small.

#### MB-180 — Bell 'natural fundamental' is the nominal partial, two octaves above the lowest mode, so the pitch envelope and ModeInject target the wrong partial

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** measured-probe · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/natural_fundamental.h:41-42](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/natural_fundamental.h#L41)

**Problem.** naturalFundamentalHz returns 800*0.1^size for Bell, which bell_mapper treats as the NOMINAL (index 4, ratio 1.0). The bank's lowest mode is the hum at 0.25x. DrumVoice scales all modes by pitchHz / naturalFundamentalHz_ (retuneFundamental) and gives ModeInject naturalFundamentalHz_ (drum_voice.h:326).

**Why wrong.** For the user, the Hz value of a pitch-envelope start/end should be the pitch they hear. The bell's perceived strike pitch is debatable, but the measured mode0 is 2399 cents below the reference.

**Consequence.** A Bell pad with the pitch envelope set to 200 Hz ends with a 50 Hz hum, and ModeInject's harmonic series sits two octaves above the bell's lowest partial. Pitch-envelope values are not comparable across bodies.

**Evidence.** Probe modes:Bell fundamental / String: "Bell mode0 = 0.25 x naturalFundamentalHz (-2399 c, table normalised to the nominal)". natural_fundamental.h:42 `case BodyModelType::Bell: return 800.0f * sizeDecay;` with comment line 12 "nominal partial".

**Suggested fix.** Document that Bell pitch is the nominal, or return the hum (0.25 x) and rescale bell_mapper. Test: Bell pad with pitch env end 200 Hz, lowest audible partial within 5 cents of the documented reference.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: bell_mapper.h:38-41 places modes at f0Nominal*kBellRatios[k]; bell_modes.h:56-60 starts at 0.250 (hum) with the nominal at index 4; drum_voice.h:209-211 (ToneShaper baseline), :326 (modeInject) and retuneFundamental (:1601-1613) use this value. Every other modal body puts mode0 at ratio 1.0 (plate_modes.h:88-89, shell_modes.h:37-38); pitch-envelope params are shown in Hz (controller.cpp:347-348); MANUAL.md never mentions the nominal convention; test_natural_fundamental_hz.cpp only pins the formula. Caveat: a bell's perceived strike note sits near the prime (0.5x), so returning the hum is also debatable. Low.
- Refuted: a documented, specified convention: natural_fundamental.h:12/:42, bell_mapper.h:6-7/:34-37, specs/137-membrum-phase2-exciters-bodies/spec.md:214 ("f0_nominal = 800 · 0.1^size"), spec.md:61 and FR-024 (:201), data-model.md:412/:472, tasks.md:255 (T083). Naming a bell by its nominal is standard bell-tuning practice; the -2399 c only restates the specified table.
- Confirmed mechanism, overstated: specs/137 tasks.md:183 (T059) specifies the nominal; the strike note is near the prime (bell_modes.h:17 calls the prime the "fundamental"), so the reference sits one octave above the perceived pitch, not two, and the hum fix would be no better (use the prime if anything). Real residue: MANUAL.md:331-332 calls the pitch-envelope Hz the "fundamental". Downgrade to a documentation nit.

#### MB-188 — 909 Drum Machine: closed hat 42 and pedal hat 44 are near-duplicates (0.28 dB)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** measured-kit-quality · **Dimension:** measured · **Source:** measured

**Location:** [tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:3007-3022](tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp#L3007)

**Problem.** pads[8] = pads[6] with decay 0.07 -> 0.04 (dead under B1/B3, B3 = 0.0), noiseLayerDecay 0.07 -> 0.05, bodyDampingB1 0.65 -> 0.78. Every other field is copied (DATA, with the ENGINE dead-Decay contribution).

**Why wrong.** Pedal and closed hats should be distinguishable.

**Consequence.** bandDist 0.28 dB: the pedal hat is effectively a copy of the closed hat.

**Evidence.** Quality sameness:909 Drum Machine:closest1: "notes 42 vs 44 ... = 0.28 / 1.002 / 1.167". Generator 3020-3022 `pads[8] = pads[6]; pads[8].decay = 0.04; pads[8].noiseLayerDecay = 0.05; pads[8].bodyDampingB1 = 0.78;`

**Suggested fix.** DATA: differentiate the pedal-hat spectrum (darker noiseLayerCutoff, lower click brightness, lower level). Test: sameness bandDist >= 3 dB.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: generator :3006-3018 defines the closed hat (NoiseBurst / NoiseBody), :3020-3022 copies it; specs/membrum-audit/probes/quality-results.txt:85 gives 0.28 / 1.002 / 1.167 (inside the <3 dB, <=1.10, <=1.20 rule), the kit's only near-duplicate of 91 pairs (:84); explicit B1/B3 override the damping law (pad_config_apply.h:63-64, membrane_mapper.h:71-77, drum_voice.h:1472). Caveat: a real TR-909 has no pedal hat, and the same pattern appears in other kits (Experimental FX 0.00 dB, LinnDrum 0.29, Jazz Brushes 0.55, Vintage Wood 0.50), so this is a kit-wide data pattern. Low.
- Refuted: bandDist (audit_quality_probes.cpp.txt:21-24, :376) is a 1 s-averaged spectral distance, so decay-only variants always score as duplicates; the kit spec preset-retune/kits/07-nineOhNineKit.md:70 ("Pedal (8): clone of 6, decay 0.04 · noiseDecay 0.05 · b1 0.78") and the 909 hat archetype (lines 4, 49-52) prescribe a decay-only pedal variant, and preset-retune/01-current-state.md:50 records the pattern. The suggested spectral fix contradicts the spec; at most the decay contrast (1.167 vs ~1.4 implied) is a tuning nit.
- Confirmed: generator :3006 labels "6 closed / 8 pedal / 10 open"; kit-pads.csv:200/:202 show peak -20.08 vs -20.24 dBFS, rms500 -50.64 vs -51.04, centroid 9150.6 vs 9168.3 Hz, decayS 0.14 vs 0.12 s, all 24 bands within 0.4 dB: a tail ~20 ms (14 %) shorter, barely audible in fast patterns. One pad of one kit; low.

#### MB-197 — Physics (oversimplified): Strike-position weighting is |J_m(j_mn r0/a)|, the radial mode shape at the strike point, with r0/a = 0.9*strikePos

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:membrane-modes · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:111-118](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L111) (cull at [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:790-797](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L790), gain at [:835](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L835))

**Problem.** amplitudes[k] = |evaluateBesselJ(m_k, j_mn,k * strikePos * 0.9)|. The bank uses this directly as the mode's input gain (gain_k = amp, modal_resonator_bank.h:835) and culls modes below 1e-4 (modal_resonator_bank.h:790-797). At strikePos = 0, J_m(0) = 0 for m >= 1 (xPowM = 0), so only the six m = 0 modes (indices 0, 3, 8, 16, 27, 39) survive: a centre strike excites only axisymmetric modes. The code has no angular factor, no modal-mass (norm) factor, and no pickup / observation-point or radiation weighting. The output is the unweighted sum of the modes.

**Why wrong.** Expanding a point impulse at (r0, theta0) onto the orthogonal mode set gives modal weights psi_mn(r0, theta0) / N_mn, where psi_mn = J_m(j_mn r/a) cos(m theta) and N_mn = integral of psi^2 dA = pi a^2 J_{m+1}(j_mn)^2 for m = 0 and pi a^2 J_{m+1}(j_mn)^2 / 2 for m >= 1. The output then projects onto an observation point, or into radiation (Bilbao: excitation and observation are both inner products). (a) The cos(m theta) factor is NOT a real omission: by rotational symmetry the strike can be placed at theta0 = 0, where cos = 1, and only the cos member of each degenerate pair is excited. (b) The 1/N_mn normalisation IS missing. Measured for an ideal impulse, the rms weight per mode relative to (0,1) is too low in the code by 5.2 dB for (1,1), 6.7 dB for (2,1), 3.7 dB for (0,2), 7.8 dB for (3,1) and (1,2), 9.5 dB for (5,1) and 12.2 dB for (1,6). At strikePos 0.3 the code gives (1,1)/(0,1) = 0.451/0.897, where the physical value is 0.822/0.897. (c) There is no observation or radiation weighting: on a real drum the (0,1) monopole radiates and damps fastest, and the (m,1) dipole-and-higher family carries the pitch.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- S. Bilbao, "Modal Synthesis", CCRMA online book section, 2006 [textbook] https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~bilbao/booktop/node14.html — initial conditions or excitation are expanded onto the (usually orthogonal) modal functions through inner products, which give the weights; the output is the modal functions projected onto an observation state (in the simplest case a delta at a chosen location).
- J. Woodhouse, Euphonics, "3.6 Tuned drums" [docs] https://euphonics.org/3-6-tuned-drums/ — mode shapes vary as cos n theta or sin n theta times J_n; a centre strike excites the untuned axisymmetric modes, and the tuned modes all have a nodal line through the centre.
- N. H. Fletcher, T. D. Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., Springer 1998 [textbook] — a struck membrane's response is a normal-mode superposition; each mode's amplitude is the mode shape at the excitation point divided by its modal mass (norm).

**Consequence.** Centre-versus-edge behaviour is qualitatively right: a centre strike gives only m = 0 modes, and moving out brings in the m >= 1 modes, so Strike Position works. Two things are off. The diametric (m,1) family, which is exactly what air loading tunes into a pitch, sits 5-10 dB lower relative to the (0,1) mode than a struck ideal membrane would put it. The upper modes also carry an extra tilt of about -3 dB per octave of mode frequency. Membrane pads therefore lean on (0,1) and sound darker and more thud-like than the model implies, and the exciter, click and noise layers must supply brightness that the body should provide. This is a mild contributor to membrane pads sounding alike, not a primary one.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: Research entry 7: "nuanced" (strong). It called the radial weight physically correct and named the dropped cos(m theta) as the slight over-excitation of m >= 1. That caveat is moot, because the strike can be placed at theta = 0 without loss of generality. The real omission, the 1/N_mn modal-norm factor, which under-excites m >= 1, was not identified. The code is unchanged since the audit.

**Suggested fix.** In MembraneMapper::map, multiply each amplitude by 1/sqrt(eps_m * J_{m+1}(j_mn)^2), with eps_0 = 1 and eps_m = 1/2, normalised so the (0,1) weight is 1. Precompute this as a constexpr table kMembraneModalNormInv[48] next to kMembraneBesselZeros (values 1.00, 1.82, 2.16, 1.53, 2.46, 2.45, ...). Optionally add a fixed observation point (for example r/a = 0.5, or the radiation weighting of the (0,n) modes). Re-normalisation to kBodyHeadroom keeps the overall level. Test: for strikePos 0.3, assert amplitudes[1]/amplitudes[0] == |J_1(3.8317*0.27)|*1.82 / |J_0(2.4048*0.27)| within 1 %. Keep the existing centre-strike test (every m >= 1 amplitude < 1e-4 at strikePos 0).

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: membrane_mapper.h:111-118 with tables membrane_modes.h:40-47/:108-115; no angular, norm or observation factor (only Decay Skew at :160-173, 1.0 by default); amplitudes reach the bank unchanged via membrane_body.h:36-38, drum_voice.h:1619-1625 and :1656-1664; modal_resonator_bank.h:835 gain_k = amp, :790-797 cull below 0.0001f (:646). Hand check: J_0(0.6493) ≈ 0.897, J_1(1.0346) ≈ 0.451, norm ratio sqrt(0.2695/0.0811) ≈ 1.82 so physical ≈ 0.82. kBodyHeadroom re-normalisation is a global scale. Timbral simplification, low.
- Confirmed with literature: fetched Bilbao node14 ("expanded onto the set of modal functions ... through an inner product, giving a set of weighting coefficients"); expanding onto an unnormalised orthogonal basis means dividing by N_mn, and the point-force modal-mass factor psi(x0)psi(x)/(m_n w_n) agrees. Recomputed sqrt(N01/Nmn): 1.823 (5.22 dB) (1,1), 2.161 (6.69) (2,1), 1.526 (3.67) (0,2), 2.462 (7.82) (3,1), 2.446 (7.77) (1,2). With a fixed delta observation the factor is 1/N, a larger deficit, so the direction holds under any convention. Comment at :6-9 says Phase-1 mapping kept on purpose (FR-031): a deliberate simplification, low.
- Refuted: specs/135-membrum-drum-synth.md:616-632 specifies A_mn ~ J_m(j_mn r0/a) cos(m theta0) (Fletcher & Rossing, Kinsler); AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:312/:314 ruled it "CONFIRMED ... Correct radial mode shape". The 1/N correction depends on an unpinned observable: displacement output adds 1/omega (about -4.0 dB at the (1,1) ratio 1.593, cancelling most of +5.2 dB), and radiation weighting would favour (0,1), the opposite direction. Level re-normalised per note (drum_voice.h:283, :302, :1370-1376); balance already user-shaped by Material, damping law, Decay Skew and the filter.

#### MB-198 — Physics (oversimplified): Air loading tunes the (m,1) modes to Rossing's timpani series 1 : 1.50 : 2.00 : 2.44 : 2.90 and leaves all other modes at pure Bessel

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:membrane-modes · **Also flagged by:** research:extra:timpani-air-loading-series · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h:62-105](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h#L62) (applied at [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:100-109](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L100))

**Problem.** f_k = f0 * ratio_k * (1 + airLoading * (scale_k - 1)), with scale = 1.1192 for (2,1) [k2], 1.2012 for (3,1) [k4], 1.2321 for (4,1) [k6] and 1.2668 for (5,1) [k9], and 1.0 for every other mode: (0,1), (1,1), every (0,n), every n >= 2, and (m >= 6, 1). Measured at airLoading = 1, relative to (1,1): (2,1) 1.500, (3,1) 2.000, (4,1) 2.440, (5,1) 2.900, so the 5-mode series is exact. But (0,1) stays at 0.628, (0,2) at 1.441, (0,3) at 2.258 and (1,2) at 1.831, and the (m >= 6,1) family stays at Bessel: (6,1) [k11] 4.1316/1.5933 = 2.593, (7,1) [k14] 2.893, (8,1) [k17] 3.191. So the diametric family is NOT monotonic: (6,1) sits BELOW (5,1), and (7,1) sits 0.24 % (4 cents) under (5,1). With (1,1) = 150 Hz that puts (5,1) at 435.0 Hz and (7,1) at 434.0 Hz, a 1 Hz beat. The header comment (lines 64-67) says air loading "raises the axisymmetric (0, n) modes", but their scale is 1.0. The default PadConfig::airLoading is 0.6 (pad_config.h:291), and the default-kit kick, snare and tom use 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.6.

**Why wrong.** Rossing (1992): measured timpani (1,1), (2,1) and (3,1) are nearly 1 : 1.5 : 2, and (4,1) and (5,1) are typically 2.44 and 2.90. The family "having one to five nodal diameters" radiates partials near 2:3:4:5:6. The stiffness of the enclosed air "raises the frequencies of the axially symmetric modes, especially the (0,1) mode", and reducing the kettle volume raises (0,1), (0,2) and (0,3). Air-mass loading is largest for low modes and "small in the modes of higher frequency" (wtt.pauken.org, after Rossing et al.), so the correction should fade smoothly with mode order. It should never stop abruptly after (5,1) and fold (6,1) and (7,1) back under it. Correct form: (a) continue the (m,1) family monotonically beyond m = 5, for example (6,1) ~ 3.3-3.4 x (1,1), or at least a scale that keeps (6,1) > (5,1); (b) give (0,1), (0,2), (0,3) a scale > 1 as the comment and Rossing state, from Christian et al. 1984 (JASA 76:1336) or Fletcher & Rossing ch. 18; (c) or, as a minimum, correct the comment so it no longer claims an effect the table does not apply.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- T. D. Rossing, "Acoustics of drums", Physics Today 45(3):40-47, 1992 [paper] https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf — (1,1):(2,1):(3,1) nearly 1:1.5:2, (4,1) and (5,1) typically 2.44 and 2.90 times (1,1) (ref. 7, Rossing & Kvistad 1976); modes with one to five nodal diameters give partials near 2:3:4:5:6; air loading lowers the low-frequency modes; kettle air stiffness raises the axisymmetric modes, especially (0,1); reducing the kettle volume raises (0,1), (0,2), (0,3) and lowers (1,1)-(4,1).
- The Well-Tempered Timpani, ch. 3 "Air loading" (summarising Rossing et al. 1976-2000) [docs] https://wtt.pauken.org/chapter-3/air-loading-2 — air loading considerably decreases the frequency of the lower modes while the loading is small for higher modes; kettle air stiffness raises the concentric (0,n) modes somewhat.
- J. Woodhouse, Euphonics, "3.6 Tuned drums" [docs] https://euphonics.org/3-6-tuned-drums/ — added air mass reduces all natural frequencies, differently per mode, and does not by itself create harmonic relations; the kettle adjusts it so a few modes fall near harmonic ratios.

**Consequence.** Five modes are tuned correctly. But at the default airLoading (0.5-0.7), every membrane pad gets (6,1) and (7,1) folded back under or onto (5,1), adding a slow beat or roughness and an inharmonic cluster around 2.6-2.9 x the principal. The (0,1) mode stays at 0.63 x the principal, a strong untuned partial below the pitch partial; a timpani's kettle pushes it up. Air loading therefore produces a drum that is less tonal than the "tuned timpani" it promises. The same skeleton is used on every Membrane pad, so this contributes slightly to Membrane pads sharing one character.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: Research entries 0 and 10: "confirmed" (strong). Entry 10 noted the mass-vs-stiffness attribution nuance and the "only 5 of 48 shifted" simplification as disclosed and not an error. Neither noticed that (6,1) and (7,1) fold back under (5,1), or that the (0,n) raising described in the comment is not applied. The code is unchanged since the audit, so the confirmation of the 5-mode series still stands.

**Suggested fix.** Extend kAirLoadingTargetScale so the (m,1) family stays monotonic. For example, extrapolate Rossing's series (the 2:3:4:5:6 family gives (6,1) ~ 3.4 x (1,1), scale = 3.4*1.5933/4.1316 = 1.311, then (7,1), (8,1) tapering to 1.0 by m ~ 10, all above the previous member), or taper scale - 1 linearly from 0.2668 at m = 5 to 0 at m = 9 while enforcing f(m+1,1) > f(m,1). Give (0,1), (0,2), (0,3) a scale > 1 sourced from Fletcher & Rossing ch. 18 / Christian et al. 1984, or delete the comment's (0,n) claim. Test: at airLoading = 1, assert that f(m,1) is strictly increasing in m for m = 1..14 and that the first five ratios stay at 1.50 / 2.00 / 2.44 / 2.90 within 0.5 %. Assert that the (0,n) scales match the documented table.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: membrane_modes.h:98-105 differs from 1.0 only at k2/k4/k6/k9; mapper :100-109 applies it to all 48 modes; kMembraneBesselOrder/Radial (:40-60) put (6,1) at k11 and (7,1) at k14; at airLoading 1 (5,1) 2.900, (6,1) 2.593, (7,1) 2.893. The (0,n) claim at :64-66 contradicts the table, while :88-91 disclose n >= 2 and m >= 6 held at unity; the fold-back is not disclosed. Defaults confirmed (pad_config.h:291; default_kit.h:76/134/164). Overstatement: at 0.6, (5,1) = 2.656 and (6,1) 2.593 (still ~41 c inverted) but (7,1) 2.893 no longer "onto" (5,1); the 1 Hz beat needs airLoading near 1. Low.
- Confirmed with literature: wtt.pauken.org/chapter-3/air-loading-2 (opened) says loading is small for higher modes and places (6,1) above (5,1) in the harmonic mapping, so holding (6,1) at 1.0 while (5,1) gets 1.2668 contradicts the source. Caveats: the (0,n) raise is physically right but disclosed at :82-91 (comment misleading, not wrong); the 1.31 scale for (6,1) is an extrapolation.
- Refuted: membrane_modes.h:82-91 document the simplification ("no data beyond Rossing's five published ratios"); AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:312 accepted "only 5/48 modes shifted". At default strikePosition 0.3 (pad_config.h:192) (5,1)/(6,1)/(7,1) sit about -29/-35/-43 dB below the principal (|J_m| leading-term estimate), so any beat is inaudible; pure Bessel already holds closer pairs (kMembraneRatios[13]/[14] 4.6009/4.6099, [46]/[47]); the (0,1) raise would break the Size -> f0 anchor at :82-86. At most the :64-66 comment needs cleanup.

#### MB-203 — Physics (unsupported): Exponent P = 1.7 is 'the measured-cymbal Chladni exponent reported by Rossing & Peterson'

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-unsupported · **Dimension:** research:plate-modes · **Also flagged by:** research:extra:plate-chladni-exponent · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h:26-33](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h#L26) (also [tools/gen-plate-chladni.js:7-9, 19-20](tools/gen-plate-chladni.js#L7))

**Problem.** One global exponent P = 1.7 for every mode family, attributed to Rossing & Peterson. The (m+2n) degeneracy is split by a single factor (1 + 0.11 n), which line 33 calls "a perceptual fit". Rossing's per-family constants are not used.

**Why wrong.** The modified Chladni law in the literature is f[m,n] = C_n (m+2n)^(P_n): a separate C_n and P_n for each nodal-circle family (Wilbur & Rossing 1996), or Perrin's f = C (m + b n)^P with a fitted b. The abstract I opened gives no numeric P. The only open source with numbers (Wikipedia, citing Fletcher & Rossing p. 680 and Rossing & Fletcher pp. 73-74) says p is about 2 for flat circular plates, ranges 1.4-2.4 across cymbals, handbells and church bells, and can vary between mode families of one object. A measured 8-inch cymbal's (m,0) family fits p of about 2.2-2.4 (Brezas 2023). Because the law has a separate C_n per family, the n>=1 families start well above the n=0 family at the same (m+2n). A global C with (1+0.11n) cannot do that, which is why the coded (0,1) sits at 1.11 instead of 1.7 or more. Also, the 2026-06 audit attributed "k1 ~ 1.73, k2 ~ 1.60" to the 5pMU8 abstract URL. I re-opened that page and it contains no such numbers.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- C. Wilbur & T.D. Rossing, "Vibrational modes of cymbals and Chladni's law", ASA 132nd meeting, 5pMU8, 1996 (abstract) [paper] https://www.auditory.org/asamtgs/asa96haw/5pMU/5pMU8.html — gives f[m,n] = C_n (m+2n)^(P_n) with per-family empirical constants, fitted to about 300 modes of a 16-inch cymbal, and Perrin's f = C(m+bn)^P; no numeric exponents.
- Chladni's law (Wikipedia), citing Fletcher & Rossing p. 680 and Rossing & Fletcher pp. 73-74 [docs] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chladni%27s_law — f = C(m+2n)^p; p about 2 for flat circular plates and 1.4-2.4 for cymbals, handbells and church bells, varying by mode family within one object.
- Brezas et al., "Experimental and computational vibroacoustic study of cymbals", Forum Acusticum 2023 [paper] https://dael.euracoustics.org/confs/fa2023/data/articles/000309.pdf — (m,0) ESPI ratios 2.64 / 4.95 / 7.24 for m = 3/4/5, i.e. p of about 2.4 / 2.3 / 2.2, not 1.7.

**Consequence.** The value that sets the whole metallic spectrum rests on a citation that I could not confirm. One global P with a small kappa holds the ring families too low (see the ratio-table claim). A cymbal is not a fixed point either: the literature reports p from 1.4 to 2.4, so a single hard-coded P removes the parameter that distinguishes one cymbal or gong from another.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research[1] recommended a (m+2n)^P fit and quoted k1 ~ 1.73 / k2 ~ 1.60 from the 5pMU8 abstract, which does not contain those numbers. The fix adopted P = 1.7 from that recommendation. The code has not changed since that fix, so the unsupported attribution is still there.

**Suggested fix.** Either cite the exact table or figure that gives 1.7 (Rossing & Peterson 1982, Percussive Notes 19(3), page and figure), or drop the attribution and call P a design choice. Better: adopt the per-family form f = C_n (m+2n)^(P_n), with C_n and P_n anchored to a published data set (Leissa for flat, a measured cymbal for domed) or exposed as a "curvature" control spanning p 1.4-2.4. Test: a table test asserting that each family's fitted exponent and its C_n/C_0 offset equal the chosen published values within 2 %.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: plate_modes.h:26-28 attributes P = 1.7 to Rossing & Peterson; :29-33 add one global (1 + kappa*n), kappa 0.11; gen-plate-chladni.js:7-9/:19-25 implement (m+2n)^1.7*(1+0.11n); kPlateRatios[1] = 1.1100f is (0,1) (kPlateIndices[1], :71; table :88-92), read by plate_mapper.h:43 and noise_body_mapper.h:106. AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.findings.json:978 quotes "k1 ~= 1.73, k2 ~= 1.60" from the 5pMU8 URL; the fetched page has no such numbers; preset-retune/archetypes/crash-cymbal-cymbal.md:6 traces to the same quote. Low: documentation and model fidelity.
- Confirmed: no source supporting 1.7 found (5pMU8 abstract symbolic only; Rossing 1982 Am. J. Phys. 50:271 abstract: cymbals "require different choices of b and k" with no value; Wikipedia 1.4-2.4; two searches found no primary source). Rossing & Peterson 1982 and Perrin 1985 not readable in full, so an unseen table could still give ~1.7. Low: 1.7 is inside the reported range; the defect is the "measured" claim and the missing per-family constants.
- Refuted: plate_modes.h:25-33 call the form "a perceptual fit ... NOT an exact Leissa eigenvalue table"; :14-23 record the prior-audit §3-B origin; test_plate_body.cpp:49-50 pins the documented formula; 1.7 sits in the published 1.4-2.4 range and the Plate body also serves gongs; the comment cites Rossing & Peterson 1982/1986 and Rossing's Science of Percussion Instruments ch. 3 (plate_modes.h:8-9), which the reviewer did not open, so the attribution is unresolved, not disproved. Per-family constants are a redesign request; residual is a documentation nit.

#### MB-205 — Physics (contradicted): Default ("physical") Mode Stretch still warps the shell and bell ratios off their published series

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:shell-bell-modes · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_mapper.h:60-62](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/shell_mapper.h#L60) (also [bell_mapper.h:55-57](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/bell_mapper.h#L55); [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:783, 806-807](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L783); contrast [membrane_mapper.h:136-138](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L136))

**Problem.** PadConfig::modeStretch defaults to 0.333333, which denormalises to 1.0, documented as "physical / no stretch" (pad_config.h:212, voice_common_params.h:23). Shell and Bell map it as stretchNorm = (1.0-0.5)/1.5 = 0.3333 with NO unity-baseline subtraction. The bank then applies B = stretch^2*0.01 = 1.111e-3, f_n *= sqrt(1 + B n^2), with n = k+1. MembraneMapper subtracts kUnityStretchNorm so that 1.0 adds nothing; the shell, bell and plate mappers do not.

**Why wrong.** At the physical setting the rendered partials should be the table ratios. What actually renders at default, relative to the fundamental: shell mode 2 +2.9 c, mode 4 +14.3 c, mode 6 +33 c (18.996 instead of 18.637), mode 8 +58.5 c, mode 12 +127.5 c, mode 32 +657 c. Bell, relative to the nominal: hum -22.8 c, prime -19.9 c, tierce -15.1 c, quint -8.5 c, superquint +10 c, octave nominal +22 c, idx 9 +67.5 c, idx 15 +193 c. Church bells are tuned to within about 10 cents of their targets (Hibberts), so a hum 23 cents flat of the nominal is outside founders' tolerance. A stiff-string dispersion law sqrt(1+B n^2) on top of beam ratios also double-counts stiffness: the beam series already contains its bending dispersion.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments (1998), ch. 2 and ch. 21 [textbook] — the free-bar ratios (1, 2.756, 5.404, ...) and the tuned-bell partials are the stiffness-inclusive eigenvalue series; no additional stiff-string factor applies to them.
- Hibbert et al., "Partial Frequencies and Chladni's Law in Church Bells", Open Journal of Acoustics 4 (2014) 70-77 [paper] https://file.scirp.org/pdf/OJA_2014060315140205.pdf — upper rim partials measured to cents relative to the nominal across 2752 bells; tuning residuals are tens of cents at most.
- This audit: evaluation of the bank's warp at B = 1.111e-3 [docs] — the per-mode cent shifts listed above.
- plugins/membrum/AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md line 64 (remediation note) [docs] — "Accepted consequence (user-approved): widening B_max changes the DEFAULT timbre of all Membrum bodies, because the mappers feed a non-zero stretch at the unity default (... plate/shell/bell/noisebody stretchNorm=0.333)."

**Consequence.** Every untouched Shell and Bell pad renders a mildly stretched series. The bell's lower partials sit 8-23 cents flat of the nominal and its upper partials up to 2 semitones sharp, which is audible as a slightly "off", less bell-like strike note. The shell's upper modes drift progressively sharp. This is a fixed warp shared by every metallic body at default, so it does not differentiate kits, and the UI says "1.0 = no stretch". Body tests pass only because they allow 3 %.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: The 2026-06 audit widened B_max in the shared bank and recorded the resulting default stretch of plate, shell and bell as an "accepted consequence (user-approved)" (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:64). The code is unchanged since then, so the deviation still exists; it was accepted, not ruled physically correct.

**Suggested fix.** This is a DELIBERATE, user-approved choice (2026-06 audit line 64), so it needs a user ruling, not a silent change. If the ruling is to keep 1.0 physical: in ShellMapper and BellMapper (and PlateMapper / NoiseBodyMapper), use r.stretch = clamp(stretchNorm - kUnityStretchNorm, 0, 1), as MembraneMapper does, then re-bless the phase-1 golden and retune the affected kits. Test: render a Shell and a Bell body at modeStretch=1.0 at 96 kHz. REQUIRE the measured shell modes 2-6 within 5 cents of kShellRatios, and bell hum, prime, tierce and quint within 5 cents of 0.25, 0.5, 0.6 and 0.75 x nominal.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: pad_config.h:212 / pad_config_apply.h:123-126 give 1.0, documented "no stretch" (voice_common_params.h:23); shell_mapper.h:60-62, bell_mapper.h:55-57, plate_mapper.h:60-62 and noise_body_mapper.h:119-120 subtract no baseline, only membrane_mapper.h:136-138 does; shell_body.h:37 / bell_body.h:37 pass r.stretch through; modal_resonator_bank.h:783 B = 1.111e-3, :806-807 apply the warp on kShellRatios (shell_modes.h:37) and kBellRatios (bell_modes.h:56). Bell hum -22.8 c and shell mode 6 +33 c recomputed. The finding itself names the user-approved acceptance (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:64) and asks for a ruling. Low.
- Confirmed with literature: cent figures check by hand (shell mode 6 1.01924, bell hum 0.98694, index 9 +67.5 c, octave nominal at index 6); shell_modes.h:37-44 is the free-free Euler-Bernoulli bar series (shell_mapper.h:11-14 cites Fletcher & Rossing) and bell_modes.h:56-60 the tuned-bell table, both dispersion-inclusive, so a stiff-string factor on top has no physical basis. Hibbert 2014 not fetched; not needed. The prior "accepted consequence" does not rule the warp physically correct; the stale pad_config_apply.h:123 "bit-identity" comment is further evidence. Low.
- Refuted as new: all four mappers confirmed (Membrane still adds material*0.3, so no body is stretch-free); AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:64 names "plate/shell/bell/noisebody stretchNorm=0.333" as user-approved with the Phase-1 golden re-blessed; PRESET-RETUNE-PLAN.md:178/:199 ("Mode Stretch 0.333 = physical") and preset-retune/01-current-state.md:56 built the retune on this spectrum; kBellRatios is an idealised table (2026-06 audit line 76). Changing the default re-voices every factory kit. Only true defect left: the stale voice_common_params.h:23 comment.

#### MB-207 — Physics (unsupported): Secondary shell fundamental = head f0 x (1 - 0.75*secondarySize), default 0.625x, cited as a 'Chromaphone rule of thumb'

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-unsupported · **Dimension:** research:shell-bell-modes · **Also flagged by:** research:coupling-models · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1418-1444](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1418) (rule at [1421-1426](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1421))

**Problem.** f0_shell = max(naturalFundamentalHz_, 20) * (1 - clamp(secondarySize,0,1)*0.75), so the range is [0.25, 1.0] x the Size-only natural fundamental (Membrane 500*0.1^size, natural_fundamental.h:38). The default 0.5 gives 0.625x, which the comment cites as "Chromaphone's 'shell f0 ~0.6 f_head' rule of thumb". There are 24 beam ratios above it; b1 = max(25, 2.5*bodyB1) + (1-mat)*15.

**Why wrong.** No textbook, paper or the Chromaphone manual states a 0.6 shell/head ratio (2026-06 audit, which opened the AAS manual). The measurements that exist point the other way for the modes that were identified. Rossing's snare: complete drum (0,1) 183 Hz; shell-dominated modes (4,0) 874 Hz and (5,0) 1064 Hz, i.e. 4.8x and 5.8x the head fundamental; bare-shell (4,0) 415 Hz, 2.3x. Ring theory extrapolated down from the measured (4,0) puts the unmeasured (2,0) ovaling mode near 415/5.42 ≈ 77 Hz (0.42x) and (3,0) near 216 Hz (1.18x). So a sub-head shell fundamental is not impossible, but no source gives 0.6. Under the code's default 0.625, beam modes 3-4 land at 3.4x and 5.6x the head, which does overlap the measured shell band. Physically, shell frequencies scale with h/R^2 while the head scales with 1/R at fixed tension, so the shell/head ratio should change with Size rather than stay a constant fraction.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- T.D. Rossing, "Acoustics of drums", Physics Today 45(3) 40-47 (1992) [paper] https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v45.i3.40_1.online.pdf — snare: lowest (0,1) mode at 183 Hz (complete drum); shell modes bare (4,0) 415, (4,1) 611, (5,0) 658, (5,1) 835 Hz; complete drum, shell-dominated (4,0) 874, (5,0) 1064 Hz.
- AAS Chromaphone 3 user manual, Coupling (as opened by the 2026-06 audit) [docs] https://www.applied-acoustics.com/chromaphone-3/manual/ — states no 0.6 head/shell ratio; describes coupled resonators often tuned to the SAME fundamental.

**Consequence.** The coupled shell layer's pitch rule is folklore. It cannot place the shell's first mode above the head, and it holds the ratio constant across Size, so a small drum's shell stays as close to its head as a big one's. Audibly this is a brief accent whose pitch relation is arbitrary rather than drum-like. Its effect is limited because the layer is short (b1 >= 25 s^-1) and off by default.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 ruled this UNSUPPORTED as a named rule ("the Chromaphone rule of thumb attribution is a folk claim"). The code still carries the same comment and formula, moved from drum_voice.h:1071-1076 to 1421-1426, so the verdict still applies. This audit adds Rossing's measured shell/head ratios.

**Suggested fix.** Remove the "Chromaphone rule of thumb" attribution (drum_voice.h:1421-1423), or replace it with a sourced rule. Either (a) anchor the shell's (4,0)-equivalent at Rossing's measured ratio (about 2.3x the head (0,1) bare, 4.8x mounted) and let secondarySize span around it, or (b) derive the shell fundamental from Size with ring scaling f ∝ 1/R^2 against the head's 1/R. Test: a unit test that calls configureSecondaryBank at Size 0.2 and 0.8 and asserts the shell/head ratio rises as Size falls under (b); or, under (a), that the default puts a shell mode within 10 % of 2.3x the head fundamental.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed: drum_voice.h:1421-1426 as quoted; naturalFundamentalHz_ is Size-only (drum_voice.h:209; natural_fundamental.h:34, :38), so the ratio is a constant fraction; default secondarySize 0.5f (pad_config.h:305); modes f0*kShellRatios[k] for 24 entries (drum_voice.h:1439-1444; shell_modes.h:37-43) give 3.38x and 5.58x; damping drum_voice.h:1478-1479; layer off by default (pad_config.h:303-304). The unsourced attribution and fixed ratio are present. Low: comment and model fidelity on an off-by-default accent layer.
- Confirmed with literature: opened the Chromaphone 3 manual; it gives no shell/head ratio, only "if the objects are tuned at the same fundamental frequency, their respective motion will be synchronized" (5.3.1) and Balance as an impedance ratio (5.3.5), so the attribution is misquoted. Rossing PDF could not be opened (size), so the 183/415/874 Hz figures are unverified; not needed. The unsourced rule has spread into preset-retune/recipes.json (about 15 entries, e.g. lines 2464, 5683, 15101) and param-dictionary.json:454; fix those too. Low.
- Refuted as a physics defect: secondarySize is a per-pad user control documented at pad_config.h:300-301, PRESET-RETUNE-PLAN.md:117 and preset-retune/00-param-dictionary.md:65, set per pad by recipes (recipes.json:2462, 4751, 5887); the layer is off unless enabled (pad_config.h:294-306) and feedforward (drum_voice.h:1450-1470); the 2026-06 verdict (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.findings.json ~1003-1040) said "The 0.6 default is fine", "Largely benign"; the finding's own numbers overlap Rossing's measured band. What remains is the misattributed comment at drum_voice.h:1421-1423.

#### MB-215 — Physics (oversimplified): A linear modal bank plus enveloped noise reproduces a struck cymbal's time evolution

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:noise-body · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h:122-129, 149-150, 164-176](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/noise_body_mapper.h#L122); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:347-371](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L347); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h:235-250](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h#L235)

**Problem.** Every NoiseBody mode is a linear coupled-form resonator excited once at the strike, with decay rate b1 + b3 f^2. All modes peak at t = 0 and decay monotonically, so the lowest modes ring longest. Default-kit Cymbal (bodyDampingB1 0.020, giving b1 = 1.196 s^-1; b3 = 8e-8 s) computes to T60 = 5.57 s at 752 Hz, 2.16 s at 5 kHz and 0.75 s at 10 kHz. The comment at default_kit.h:241 says 4.6 s; b1 alone gives 5.78 s. Default-kit Hat (legacy law, b1 = 2.835, b3 = 1.2e-6) computes to 1.65 s at 1062 Hz, 0.21 s at 5 kHz and 0.056 s at 10 kHz. No inter-mode energy transfer exists inside the body. The only cascade proxy is the "bloom" on the PARALLEL noise layer (drum_voice.h:347-371): a cutoff sweep from 0.35x to a peak of (1 + 1.2*nlc)(0.45 + 0.55*vel) x base and back to 0.55x, with rise tau 140 - 90*vel ms and fall 500 ms. It is gated on NonlinearCoupling > 0 AND NoiseBody, so it is active only for the crash (nlc 0.35), not the hats. CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN.md:341 lists "No full von Karman / Ducceschi-Bilbao nonlinear modal simulation" as a deliberate exclusion.

**Why wrong.** Cymbals are "nonlinear percussion instruments". In normal use the displacement is of the order of the thickness, energy moves between modes through quadratic (curvature) nonlinearity, and a strong impact drives a chaotic regime. On thin cymbals the energy transfer appears before any pitch glide (Chaigne, Touze & Thomas 2005; Touze, Ducceschi & Bilbao 2012). Flat plates harden and curved plates soften, with frequency shifts of 16 % at amplitude = thickness (Rossing & Fletcher 1983). The measured time evolution of a 40-cm crash is NOT "everything peaks at t = 0" (F&R 20.3, Rossing & Shepherd 1983). Below 700 Hz the level falls rapidly in the first 200 ms as energy converts upward. Peaks at 700-1000 Hz build up over 10-20 ms. The 2-10 kHz band rises by >= 10 dB in the first 50 ms, and 3-5 kHz peaks 50-100 ms after the strike and dominates from 1 to 4 s. Low frequencies dominate only the late, much quieter lingering sound. The octave-band decay also depends on the stroke (crash vs ride vs soft), with a crash stroke more sustained at 16 kHz. A frequency-decreasing T60 (b1 + b3 f^2) agrees with the single-mode decay data (F&R Fig. 20.5) and with observation 5. The mid-high build-up and the early low-band drop are absent, and only partly imitated for the crash by a filter sweep on the separate noise layer.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- Fletcher & Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., 1998, Sec. 20.3 "Transient Behavior", Figs. 20.5-20.6 (data Rossing & Shepherd 1983) [textbook] https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf — (1) below about 700 Hz the level decreases rapidly in the first 200 ms, "apparently caused by the conversion of energy into modes of higher frequency"; (2) 700-1000 Hz peaks build up between 10 and 20 ms; (3) 3-5 kHz peaks about 50-100 ms after striking; (4) 3-5 kHz is the most prominent feature 1-4 s after striking; (5) low frequencies dominate the lingering sound at a much lower level; octave-band decay depends on stroke type.
- Chaigne, A., Touze, C., Thomas, O., "Nonlinear vibrations and chaos in gongs and cymbals", Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 26(5) 403-409, 2005 [paper] https://perso.ensta.fr/~touze/PDF/ChaosGong.pdf — displacement of the order of the thickness makes nonlinearity essential; energy transfer follows from quadratic nonlinearity due to curvature; the chaotic regime "sounds similar to real instruments normally excited by the strong impact of a mallet"; on thin cymbals energy transfer and mode coupling appear before pitch glide; reduced models need only 5 to 10 strongly coupled oscillators.
- Rossing, T.D. & Fletcher, N.H., "Nonlinear vibrations in plates and gongs", J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 73(1) 345-351, 1983 [paper] https://www.phys.unsw.edu.au/music/people/publications/Rossingetal1983.pdf — flat plates harden, most curved plates soften; a flat plate's frequency rises about 16 % at amplitude = thickness and 35 % at twice the thickness.
- Touze, C., Ducceschi, M., Bilbao, S., "Nonlinear plate vibrations: a modal approach with application to cymbals and gongs", Acoustics 2012 Nantes (SFA/IOA) [paper] https://www.research.ed.ac.uk/en/publications/nonlinear-plate-vibrations-a-modal-approach-with-application-to-c/ — a von Karman plate projected on its linear modes gives nonlinear coupling coefficients through the linear eigenfunctions, a tractable modal route to cymbal and gong synthesis.

**Consequence.** Hats and cymbals are brightest at the instant of the strike and darken monotonically, with the lowest NoiseBody modes (750 Hz to 1.1 kHz) outlasting the 3-5 kHz shimmer band. That is the inverse of a real crash, where the shimmer takes over after about 50 ms. The crash recovers part of the missing bloom through the parallel-layer filter sweep; the hat, ride-like and clap uses do not. Velocity scales level and (crash only) the bloom peak, but the body's spectrum does not get brighter with harder hits, as the nonlinear regime makes it in a real cymbal. NoiseBody hits therefore sound static and alike across velocities, one contributor to kit sameness on the metal pads. The stale T60 comment (4.6 s vs 5.6 s computed) misleads tuning.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research entry #2 (plate/cymbal) noted "a linear fixed-ratio modal bank omits the defining nonlinear cymbal/gong behavior (pitch glide, energy cascade)" (Fletcher 1999). The ratio table was fixed since, and CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN added the parallel-layer bloom proxy for crashes, but the body itself is still linear, so this part of the prior verdict still applies, mitigated for the crash only.

**Suggested fix.** This is a deliberate simplification (CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN.md:341), so report rather than rebuild. Cheapest physics-informed step: a few-oscillator energy-transfer term inside the body (Chaigne et al.: 5 to 10 coupled modes suffice). For example, a velocity-scaled, slowly ramped input gain on the upper NoiseBody modes (amplitude envelope rising over 20-100 ms), so 2-10 kHz builds up by about 10 dB in 50 ms, while modes under 700 Hz get extra early damping for the first 200 ms. Make the build-up depth velocity-dependent so hard hits brighten. Also correct default_kit.h:241 to "lowest-mode T60 ~ 5.6 s". Test: render the default-kit crash at 48 kHz; the 3-5 kHz band level at 75 ms exceeds its level at 5 ms by >= 6 dB; the < 700 Hz band drops by >= 10 dB between 0 and 200 ms; the velocity 1.0 vs 0.25 centroid ratio is > 1.2.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed as coded: NoiseBody is the shared linear bank (modal_resonator_bank.h:107, 367-368, 821-824; noise_body_mapper.h:95, 105-106; damping membrane_mapper.h:64-80); crash numbers recomputed (b1 1.196, f0 752 Hz, T60 5.57 s; default_kit.h:241 "~4.6 s" stale); hat matches (default_kit.h:186-208); hat nlc 0 (pad_config.h:215), so no bloom (drum_voice.h:356-371). One part wrong: for the crash, drum_voice.h:892-895 (and :558) run body + noise + click through NonlinearCoupling (unnatural/nonlinear_coupling.h:85-127, header :6-15), a velocity- and amplitude-dependent waveshaper, so the noise sweep is not the only proxy; but it is memoryless and moves no energy between modes. Low.
- Confirmed with literature: code re-read (noise_body_mapper.h:105-113/:149-150; default_kit.h:249-250; CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN.md:341); Chaigne, Touze & Thomas 2005 (PDF fetched) supports every quote ("energy transfer between modes is a consequence of quadratic nonlinearity due to curvature", 5-10 oscillators). Fletcher & Rossing Sec. 20.3 (over the fetch limit) and Rossing & Fletcher 1983 (scanned, no text) not opened; secondary sources (Wilbur/Rossing ASA abstract, Harrison & Hill 2013) agree in direction.
- Refuted as a defect: CRASH-REDESIGN-PLAN.md:339-344 rules out von Karman / Ducceschi-Bilbao and a Poirot matrix ("the bloom envelope + slow-attack NLC approximates its audible output for ~zero CPU"); :25 (T2) cites the same literature; drum_voice.h:347-355 keeps the bloom off hats and toms on purpose; archetypes gong-tam-tam...md:15 and crash-cymbal-cymbal.md:8,15 say so; AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:323 raised it and the engine route was declined. Velocity brightening exists (drum_voice.h:364-368; NLC redesign M-3/M-4, AUDIT md:263-267); hat HF T60s (0.21 s at 5 kHz) leave little room for a 50-100 ms build-up. Residual nit: the stale default_kit.h:241 comment.

#### MB-217 — Physics (oversimplified): Membrane per-mode damping is monotone in f^2, but drum-head damping is radiation-dominated and depends on mode order: (0,1) decays FASTEST

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:damping-law · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:93-109](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L93) (air-loading frequency shift), [146-152](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L146) and [177](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L177) (damping), [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/membrane_modes.h) kMembraneBesselOrder

**Problem.** The Membrane mapper applies air loading only as a frequency shift: each mode moves from its Bessel ratio toward the Rossing target (kAirLoadingTargetScale). Damping is the single law b1 + b3*f^2 for all 48 modes, so T60 decreases strictly with frequency and the (0,1) fundamental always rings longest. Example, default-kit tom at size 0.5: T60(f0 = 158 Hz) = 1.11 s, T60(2.3*f0) = 310 ms. Nothing reads kMembraneBesselOrder into the damping. decaySkew changes amplitudes only (160-173).

**Why wrong.** For an air-loaded, baffled membrane (kettledrum), calculated radiation-only T60 (Christian et al. 1984, reproduced as Table 6.1 in Packer 1993) are: (0,1) 0.06 s, (0,2) 0.2 s, (0,3) 0.1 s, (1,1) 0.8 s, (2,1) 1.8 s, (3,1) 4.6 s, (4,1) 10.5 s, (5,1) 16.2 s, (1,2) 0.2 s, (2,2) 0.8 s. The monopole-like (0,n) modes radiate efficiently and die fast; the dipole and higher (m,1) family rings long. Packer adds that measured (3,1) to (5,1) are shorter than calculated because of other losses. In the unbaffled bass drum the (0,1) survives "in no small degree". The damping therefore depends on the mode's symmetry and on air loading, not on f^2 alone. The f^2 law is the string law (Chaigne & Askenfelt) and cannot represent this.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- Packer T.A., Acoustics of the orchestral kettledrum, MSc thesis, Durham University, 1993 (Table 6.1 reproduces Christian, Davis, Tubis, Anderson, Mills, Rossing, JASA 76(5), 1984) [thesis] https://etheses.durham.ac.uk/id/eprint/5633/1/5633_3049.PDF — with the kettle as a baffle the (0,1) mode acts as a monopole and "will lose its energy quickly"; (1,1) to (4,1) decay much more slowly; Table 6.1 (tension 5360 N/m, 64 cm drum): T60 (0,1) 0.06 s, (1,1) 0.8, (2,1) 1.8, (3,1) 4.6, (4,1) 10.5, (5,1) 16.2, (0,2) 0.2, (0,3) 0.1; in the unbaffled bass drum the (0,1) is present "in no small degree".
- Chaigne A., Askenfelt A., JASA 95(2), 1994 [paper] https://www.math.kent.edu/~zheng/62262/piano_wave.pdf — b1 + b3*omega^2 is derived for, and fitted to, a string, and is "only a fair approximation" even there.

**Consequence.** At airLoading = 1 (test_per_mode_damping.cpp:622 "airLoading=1 produces the Rossing timpani series"), the model gets the harmonic (m,1) frequencies of a timpani or tuned tom right but the wrong decay order. The inharmonic (0,1) thump outlasts the (1,1)/(2,1)/(3,1) partials that carry the pitch, so the pitch sense that air loading is meant to create is masked by the thump. Every membrane pad has the same "boom, then upper modes fade first" envelope, whatever the head or air-loading setting. This contributes to toms, kicks and timpani-style pads sounding alike.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: 2026-06 research[3] cited Rossing ("snare (0,1) mode is heavily damped ... higher antisymmetric modes ring longer") as "consistent with the coded t60 spread". That reasoning was wrong: the coded law makes the (0,1) the LONGEST-ringing mode and cannot make it shorter than the (1,1). The code is unchanged, so this is a new finding against the old ruling.

**Suggested fix.** Add a per-mode radiation term to the Membrane law, keyed on the Bessel order and scaled by airLoading: rate_k = b1 + b3*f_k^2 + airLoading*bRad*g(m_k, n_k), with g large for m = 0 (monopole), about 1 for m = 1 and falling for higher m. Fit g to the Christian et al. ratios, e.g. rate(0,1)/rate(1,1) of about 13 and rate(2,1)/rate(1,1) of about 0.44. This needs a per-mode extra-rate array in the bank (setModes(..., const float* extraRate)) or a mapper-side folding into an amplitude-independent per-mode b1. Test: Membrane at airLoading = 1 with no click or noise layer. Measure per-mode T60 by band-pass at the (0,1) and (1,1) frequencies and require T60(0,1) < T60(1,1), with the ratio within 2x of 0.075. At airLoading = 0 the current law must be bit-identical.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed, not refuted: one {b1, b3} pair from dampingLawFromParams (membrane_mapper.h:64-80, :177; legacy law modal_resonator_bank.h:133-138) applied identically per mode (modal_resonator_bank.h:821-824, b3 >= 0 at :767); kMembraneBesselOrder read only for strike amplitude (mapper :115); air loading is a frequency multiplier only (:101-108, membrane_modes.h:98-105); index 0 (0,1) is always the lowest frequency (ratios >= 1.5933, scatter 0 at k = 0), hence always the longest T60; Decay Skew (:160-173, :146) gives no per-mode rate; no other per-mode damping path (drum_voice.h:1481, 1619, 1658); test_per_mode_damping.cpp:622 exists. Medium fits.
- Confirmed but overreaching: code facts re-checked (mapper :100-109, :146-152, :177; b1 >= 0.2 at modal_resonator_bank.h:766-767; :823). Packer 1993 downloaded: Table 6.1 (p.58) matches exactly; p.56 monopole quote and p.57 shorter measured (3,1)-(5,1) quoted correctly. Downgrade: the same passage (p.56) says the unbaffled bass drum keeps (0,1) "in no small degree", and Membrum's Membrane serves kick, snare and toms (default_kit.h:48, 99, 145; airLoading 0.7/0.5/0.6), two-headed unbaffled drums; airLoading is a frequency knob, not a kettle model; the bank labels the law Chaigne-Lambourg (modal_resonator_bank.h:763).
- Refuted as new / medium: plugins/membrum/preset-retune/kits/06-orchestralKit-fix-plan.md:187 (D8 "Kettledrum (0,n) radiation damping — DEFERRED") already diagnoses "damping law is global b1+b3·f², monotone in f → lowest mode always rings longest", rejects an airLoading-keyed term because it "would cut kick/tom fundamentals kit-wide 36–48%", and records a residual "~15% longer (0,1) T60 post-fix — likely acceptable" (also :55, :233, :292); this overrules the 2026-06 ruling (findings.json:1071). docs/tom-depth-implementation-plan.md:18 wants the (0,1) dominant with fundamental T60 1.5-3.0 s and overtone T60 0.15-0.5 s, the opposite of the proposed fix; the kick archetype accepts b3·f².

#### MB-218 — Physics (contradicted): Every modal strike is normalised to one fixed peak (-6 dBFS at velocity 1), whatever the body's size, material, damping or strike position

**Severity:** low (filed medium, downgraded in verification) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:strike-normalisation · **Source:** research

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:73-84, 286-306, 1322-1412, 1717-1729](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L73)

**Problem.** kBodyHeadroom = 0.5f (line 84, "-6 dBFS strike-peak budget"). For every non-Feedback, non-String body, noteOn calls bank.setOutputGain(measuredStrikeOutputGain(bank, params_, body, exciter)) (line 302). The probe (probeStrikePeakExcited, 1322-1363) triggers the live exciter and click layer at velocity 1.0, renders 30 ms through the configured bank with output gain 1, and takes the absolute peak. Then outputGain = kBodyHeadroom / peak (1386), falling back to kBodyHeadroom / getInputGainSum() only when peak <= 1e-4. The result is cached per voice slot on StrikeNormKey {body, exciter, material, size, decay, strikePos, modeStretch, decaySkew, airLoading, modeScatter, b1, b3, clickMix, clickContact, clickBright, noiseBurstContact} (1400-1411, 1717-1727). Every input in that key therefore stops changing the v=1 body peak. The header comment (73-84) documents this as deliberate: "Final loudness make-up is master gain + per-pad Level (Phase-4 tuning), NOT this budget." Measured with the existing hidden case "audit probe 07a" on the current build (48 kHz, Impulse, v 1.0, level 1.0, body only), peak dBFS: Membrane -5.96, Plate -5.94, Shell -6.67, Bell -5.98, NoiseBody -6.16. Every modal body lands within 0.7 dB of -6.02. The kit code admits the side effect: default_kit.h:456-457 says "counteract the per-voice peak normalizer that otherwise makes the floor tom the QUIETEST body of the row", and test_default_kit.cpp:277-278 says the same.

**Why wrong.** In a struck body, the radiated level at a given strike force depends on all of these. (a) Size: radiated power = radiation resistance x surface velocity squared, and below ka ~ 1 the radiation resistance of the monopole-like (0,1) / piston-like motion scales as area x (ka)^2. A larger head therefore radiates its low modes far more efficiently at the same force. (b) Strike position: per-mode excitation is the mode shape evaluated at the strike point, so a strike near the rim drives the low modes weakly and is quieter and thinner. Timpanists strike about 1/4 of the way in from the edge partly to suppress the (0,1) mode. (c) Material and damping: they set how much energy is stored and how fast it leaves.
