FR-010 also wants unfiltered white noise for hardness > 0.7; the code filters at every hardness. impact_exciter_test.cpp only checks centroid orderings.
- Context/impact lens: refutes on intent and audibility. spec.md:113 calls the formula "a perceptual balance, not a mathematically correct pink approximation"; research.md:45 (R-003) records it as "a single-pole highpass-like differentiator, NOT the Paul Kellet pink noise approximation", chosen on purpose for SC-006 golden determinism (plan.md:158, quickstart.md:61, compliance row spec.md:278). A Node probe (pink_probe.js, 20 seeds, 48 kHz) puts in-band noise 28-32 dB under the pulse, moving only 3-6 dB against white noise; above 16 kHz the SVF removes it on soft/medium hits (-67 / -47 dB) and it reaches -20 dB only on the hardest Impulse hits. The exciter only drives the modal body; the energy-cap effect is negligible.

#### MB-253 — Physics (unsupported): Shell/head damping comments cite 'Chaigne (1993) / Chaigne & Askenfelt 1993' as the source of the shell's b1 + b3*f^2 law

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-unsupported · **Dimension:** research:extra:chaigne-damping-law

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1450-1452](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1450) (also [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:111-116](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h#L111))

**Problem.** configureSecondaryBank: "Shell-like damping, following Chaigne (1993) / standard modal-synthesis form: R_k = b1 + b3*f_k^2". pad_config.h:112-114: b3 is the "perceived material: metal vs wood vs plastic -- see Aramaki/KM 2011, Chaigne & Askenfelt 1993". The secondary shell is a free-free Euler-Bernoulli beam mode set (kShellRatios) damped with b1 + b3*f^2, with f in Hz.

**Why wrong.** The cited work is A. Chaigne & A. Askenfelt, "Numerical simulations of piano strings. I", JASA 95(2):1112-1118, February 1994 (received 8 March 1993). It concerns PIANO STRINGS, not shells or drums. Its Eq. (3) gives 1/tau = b1 + b3*omega^2, with omega in rad/s, not Hz. The authors call it "a smooth law of damping which is only a fair approximation of the reality", fitted empirically to account "globally for the losses in the air and in the string material, as well as those due to the coupling to the soundboard". They chose it because damping laws that are even-order polynomials in frequency keep the finite-difference scheme stable and causal. For a solid shell or bar, the material (internal-friction) loss at a constant loss factor E2/E1 gives tau = E1/(pi*f*E2), a decay rate LINEAR in f (F&R Sec. 2.13.2, Eq. 2.42). Viscoelastic loss adds a quadratic term (Chaigne & Doutaut 1997, as summarised by Klatzky et al. 2000). For a shell the defensible form is b1 + c1*f + b3*f^2. b3*f^2 alone is the string or support-loss case (F&R: with end losses dominant, "decay time varies more nearly as 1/f^2").

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- A. Chaigne & A. Askenfelt, "Numerical simulations of piano strings. I. A physical model for a struck string using finite difference methods", JASA 95(2), 1112-1118, 1994 [paper] <https://www.math.kent.edu/~zheng/62262/piano_wave.pdf>: received 8 March 1993, published February 1994. Eq. (3): 1/tau = b1 + b3*omega^2 for a stiff damped STRING; constants fitted empirically, accounting globally for air, material and soundboard losses; "only a fair approximation"; even-order polynomials chosen for stability and causality.
- N. H. Fletcher & T. D. Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., Sec. 2.13 (Eq. 2.42, Fig. 2.15) [textbook] <https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf>: internal damping gives tau2 = E1/(pi*f*E2), so the loss rate is proportional to f when E2/E1 is frequency-independent. Air viscosity gives tau proportional to 1/sqrt(f). Only when end or support losses dominate does tau vary as about 1/f^2.
- R. L. Klatzky, D. K. Pai, E. P. Krotkov, "Perception of Material from Contact Sounds", Presence 9(4), 399-410, 2000 [paper] <https://www.cs.ubc.ca/labs/lci/papers/docs2000/pai-KlaPai00.pdf>: following Wildes & Richards, b(f) = pi*tan(phi)*f (linear in f). Chaigne & Doutaut (1997) show viscoelastic dissipation adds a quadratic term. A constant term is "usually small".

**Consequence.** Comment and provenance only: nothing audible changes. The mis-attribution does make the string-grade f^2-only law look validated for a wooden or metal shell, and it hides the missing linear (internal-friction) term that the material-perception literature says carries wood-versus-metal identity.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: research[3] cited the same 1994 paper as the origin of the form and ruled it "confirmed" for the bank. It did not flag the "1993" date or the application to a shell. The comments are unchanged since that audit, so the mis-citation still stands.

**Suggested fix.** Rewrite drum_voice.h:1450-1452 and pad_config.h:112-114 to cite "Chaigne & Askenfelt, JASA 95(2), 1994 (piano strings); Rayleigh proportional damping (standard modal-synthesis convention)". State that for shells and plates the internal-friction term is linear in f (F&R Eq. 2.42). Optionally add c1 to DampingLaw (decayRate = b1 + c1*f + b3*f^2, default c1 = 0, bit-identical). Test (dsp_processors_tests): DampingLaw{b1,0,b3} radii are unchanged; with c1 > 0, -fs*ln(R_k) equals b1 + c1*f_k + b3*f_k^2 within 1e-4 relative.

**Verifier notes.**
- Code lens: confirmed as a comment issue; downgrade. drum_voice.h:1450-1452 and pad_config.h:111-114 carry the cited wording; drum_voice.h:1478-1481 builds b1 = max(25, 2.5*bodyB1) + (1-mat)*15, b3 = mat*1e-5 on the kShellRatios modes (1428-1444); the bank applies decayRate = b1 + b3*f² in Hz, no linear term (modal_resonator_bank.h:107, 113-117, 367-368, 821-824), with the Hz convention documented on purpose. Nothing audible (the finding says so); the c1 term is a feature suggestion.
- Research lens: citation part not refuted, physics part weaker. The fetched PDF is JASA 95(2), February 1994, on piano strings: the origin of the b1 + b3·ω² form, but no shells and no material perception. Equation text was garbled, so the quoted phrases are unverified by the verifier. No 1993 Chaigne paper on drums, shells or plates was found (closest: Lambourg & Chaigne on plates, hal-00830699). Downgrade: the "/ standard modal-synthesis form" half is accurate, 1993 is the received year, Hz vs rad/s has no effect with hand-tuned coefficients, and the "defensible" linear-term form is not settled.
- Context/impact lens: refutes as reportable. AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md §3-A ruled the law "CONFIRMED, strong. Exactly Chaigne & Askenfelt (1994) string-loss form" and listed the missing linear term under "Nuances (non-bugs)" (findings.json ~1047-1074); docs/correctness-audit.md:59 settled the units. The secondary shell is short (b1 >= 25 s⁻¹, t60 <= ~0.28 s, drum_voice.h:1467-1480) and b3 = mat*1e-5 is tiny. The only residue is a 1993-vs-1994 year nit in two comments.

#### MB-255 — Physics (contradicted): The b3 ceiling (1e-3 s, 'widened empirically') and the default tom b3 (1.5e-4) damp drum-head partials far faster than measured

**Severity:** medium (final: low) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** research:extra:chaigne-damping-law

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:56-63, 75-78](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h#L56) (with [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h:128-131, 166-174](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h#L128); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:276-279](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h#L276))

**Problem.** b3 = n*1.0e-3 s (Hz convention). The comment says the ceiling was widened from 8e-5 to 4e-4 to 1e-3 to reach a ~9 dB total-energy drop for the "metallic ring -> wood thump" contract. The default toms set bodyDampingB3 = 0.15 (b3 = 1.5e-4, "Tom-depth Fix B", default_kit.h:166-174), giving T60 0.17 s at 500 Hz, 45 ms at 1 kHz and 5 ms at 3 kHz for every tom size. The default snare uses 0.4 (b3 = 4e-4): 500 Hz 53 ms, 1 kHz 16 ms. pad_config.h:279 still documents the b3 range as "1 -> 8e-5 s * rad^-2" (= 3.16e-3 in the Hz convention), which contradicts the mapper's 1e-3 Hz convention.

**Why wrong.** Bork's tom-tom measurements (F&R Table 18.8) give a 500 Hz third-octave T60 of 1.1-2.7 s, as long as or LONGER than the (01) mode's 0.8-1.05 s. Membrum's default toms decay 6-16x faster at 500 Hz (0.17 s). In Fletcher & Rossing's timpani data the high-frequency (n,1) modes also outlast the fundamental. No published drum-head or shell damping coefficient of b3 ~1e-4 to 1e-3 s (Hz) was found. The most heavily damped materials in Sterling et al.'s Rayleigh fits (wood, plastic) have b3 of about 2.6e-6 s, so the tom default is about 58x and the ceiling about 390x that. The ceiling is a perceptual design choice, documented as such in membrane_mapper.h:58-63 and default_kit.h:166-173, not a physical value.

Sources (evidence quality strong):
- N. H. Fletcher & T. D. Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments, 2nd ed., Table 18.8 (after Bork 1983) and Table 18.4 [textbook] <https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/The_Physics_of_Musical_Instruments.pdf>: 32-cm tom-tom: T60 of (01) 0.8-1.05 s; T60 in the 500 Hz third-octave band 2.5/2.7 (Ambassador), 2.5/1.4 (Diplomat), 1.1 s (Emperor). Timpani (31) and (41) modes ring 1.7-4.6 s.
- A. Sterling, N. Rewkowski, R. L. Klatzky, M. C. Lin, "Audio-Material Reconstruction for Virtualized Reality Using a Probabilistic Damping Model", IEEE TVCG 2019 [paper] <https://gamma.cs.unc.edu/ProbDampModel/data/pdm.pdf>: wood block and plastic bowl Rayleigh alpha2 = 1.3e-7 (per omega^2, on c = 2d), about 2.6e-6 s in the Hz-convention amplitude decay rate: the largest f^2 coefficient among the measured materials.

**Consequence.** Default toms keep only their fundamental after about 0.2 s; everything above about 400 Hz becomes a short click. Toms of different sizes then differ almost only in pitch, like pitched sine thumps. Real toms carry a long-ringing upper-partial body that makes them sound like drums, and the snare head likewise has almost no tonal ring. Together with claim 1, this is a direct sameness driver across the default kit and the factory kits that copy the template.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: research[3] noted that the b3 ceiling 1e-3 is about 6.3e6x Chaigne's piano value and "not literature-derived", and said "legitimate for a synth". It did not compare with measured drum T60. Tom-depth Fix B (b3 = 0.15 on toms) postdates or was not covered by that audit; the ceiling code is unchanged.

**Suggested fix.** Deliberate, documented choice (membrane_mapper.h:58-63, default_kit.h:166-173). The intent (dissolve the inharmonic "toy-like" mid cluster) is better served by the mode-class radiation term in claim 1: damp the axisymmetric (0,2), (0,3) and (2,2)-type modes, not every mode in proportion to f^2. Then lower the tom b3 to <= 1e-5. Keep the 1e-3 ceiling only as an explicitly non-physical "Unnatural" range, or cap it. Fix the pad_config.h:276-279 comment to "b3 = n*1e-3 s (Hz convention)". Test: render the default Low-Mid Tom (size 0.5) and fit band envelopes; assert T60(500 Hz third-octave) >= 0.5*T60(f0 band), following F&R Table 18.8; assert the pad_config comment constant equals the mapper constant through a shared constexpr.

**Verifier notes.**
- Code lens: confirmed; downgrade. membrane_mapper.h:75-78 (b3 = norm*1e-3), 58-63 ("widened empirically"), used by MembraneMapper::map (177); the bank's decayRate = b1 + b3*f² in Hz (modal_resonator_bank.h:107, 113-117, 821-824). Tom template (default_kit.h:143-174): b1 ≈ 2.45 s⁻¹ from the legacy path (membrane_mapper.h:148-152), b3 = 1.5e-4 → T60 ≈ 0.17 s at 500 Hz, 45 ms at 1 kHz, 5 ms at 3 kHz; snare (130-131) b1 ≈ 30.1, b3 = 4e-4 → 53 ms / 16 ms. pad_config.h:278-279 is stale. Literature not opened by this verifier. Deliberate perceptual tuning, ruled legitimate by the prior audit; only the stale comment is plainly a defect (nit).
- Research lens: not refuted. Value path verified (pad_config_apply.h:64 → drum_voice.h:191/1531 → every modal mapper); the b3 term alone caps the tom's 500 Hz T60 at 0.184 s. F&R Table 18.8 (PDF p. 517) and Table 18.4 checked and quoted correctly for a tom-tom; Sterling's alpha2 = 1.3e-7 converts to ~2.6e-6 s. Caveats: Sterling measured rigid objects (supporting evidence only); F&R 18.12 attributes some late band energy to nonlinear coupling and notes double-ply heads decay faster at high frequency; Table 18.4 shows some 300-500 Hz modes ((02), (03), (12), (22)) decay in 0.3-0.5 s, supporting a mode-class law rather than a uniform f² law.
- Context/impact lens: refutes as a physics defect. membrane_mapper.h:58-63 and default_kit.h:166-173 document the intent; plugins/membrum/docs/tom-depth-implementation-plan.md:14, 144-170 record b3 = 0.15 as rendered and measured (100-500 Hz band 0.317 → 0.164, centroid 160 → 129 Hz, fundamental kept >= 1.5 s) and warn against raising it (164-167); AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:313 and :78 re-confirmed the ceiling as "a documented non-bug". The "sameness driver" consequence has no render behind it. Remaining nit: pad_config.h:276-279.

#### MB-257 — Physics (oversimplified): Wire buzz as a linear, peak-normalised follower of the batter-body modal energy (no contact threshold, no cavity delay)

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-oversimplified · **Dimension:** research:extra:snare-wire-and-sympathetic-claims

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:1499-1515](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1499) (computeWireGainMod); [857-861, 910-918](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L857) (fast path); [1051, 1073-1081](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1051) (slow path); [542-549](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L542) (process() leaves wireGainMod_ = 1)

**Problem.** The code is in drum_voice.h:1506-1514: norm = clamp(energyEnv_ / wireEnergyPeak_, 0, 1); track = sqrt(norm); gain = 1 + wireCoupling*(track - 1). wireEnergyPeak_ is the running peak of the TOP body's modal energy since note-on. The comment says this makes the result "velocity- and gain-staging-independent (a hard hit and a soft hit both start at ~1 and relax to 0)". The gain is updated once per block (chunk) and multiplies noiseLayer * standaloneGain * noiseLayerGain from sample 0 of the hit. The single-sample process() renderer never updates it (stays 1.0, drum_voice.h:542-549), and String bodies bypass it.

**Why wrong.** In the physical models the wires are a ONE-SIDED collision against the snare-side head: a penalty/power-law contact force F = K[delta]_+^alpha (Bilbao/Torin/Chatziioannou), which only acts when the wire and head overlap. Rattling starts only when the head moves away faster than the wire tension can follow. So (a) the buzz-to-body ratio depends on strike amplitude: a soft hit gives proportionally less rattle than a hard one, and the rattle stops before the head stops ringing. (b) The snare head lags the batter head through the cavity. In Torin/Hamilton/Bilbao DAFx-14 the snares reach maximum displacement at about 6 ms and hit the membrane coherently at about 9 ms, then move chaotically. A peak-normalised sqrt(E) follower that starts at full gain at t = 0 has neither property. PLAN-wire-coupling-2026-07-13.md:10-14 documents this as a deliberate envelope-follower step up from an independent noise layer, not a collision model.

Sources (evidence quality moderate):
- A. Torin, B. Hamilton, S. Bilbao, "An Energy Conserving Finite Difference Scheme for the Simulation of Collisions in Snare Drums", DAFx-14, 2014 [paper] <https://www.pure.ed.ac.uk/ws/files/17485699/dafx14_submission_56_3.pdf>: Sec. 5.2: a pressure rise in the cavity "pushes the lower membrane downwards, together with the snares. The snares reach their maximum displacement at t = 6 ms ... At about t = 9 ms, the snares hit the membrane almost coherently ... At later times, the behaviour of the snares becomes rapidly chaotic."
- S. Bilbao, A. Torin, V. Chatziioannou, "Numerical Modeling of Collisions in Musical Instruments", Acta Acustica 2012 [paper] <https://www.ness.music.ed.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/bilbao_acustica_r2.pdf>: a power-law collision potential is used for the wire/membrane interaction. The contact force exists only under penetration, so the interaction is strongly nonlinear and amplitude-dependent.

**Consequence.** Ghost notes and rimshots get the same wire-to-body ratio from this stage: the self-normalisation removes the velocity-to-timbre cue that separates a soft snare from a hard one. The buzz also starts at the stick crack with no snare-side lag, which blurs the attack. This adds to the flattened dynamics already reported elsewhere. A lesser point: the single-sample process() renderer ignores wire coupling, so it diverges from processBlockFast/Slow for any pad with wireCoupling > 0. This is documented at drum_voice.h:542-546.

**Evidence.** Prior audit ruling: none (not covered by the 2026-06-07 audit; the feature post-dates it).

**Suggested fix.** Drive the wire gain from absolute (velocity-scaled) head amplitude, not from the peak-normalised ratio. For example: a = sqrt(energyEnv_)/kWireRef; g = smoothstep((a - aTh)/aW); gain = lerp(1, g, wireCoupling). Optionally delay the onset of the noise layer by 1-3 ms when wireCoupling > 0. Pin it with a test: render the default-kit snare (pad 2, note 38) at velocity 0.2 and 1.0, and assert that the 4-8 kHz energy relative to the 100-400 Hz energy over the first 150 ms is at least 6 dB lower at velocity 0.2. Then assert that process(), processBlockFast and processBlockSlow give the same wire envelope within a tolerance.

**Verifier notes.**
- Code lens: confirmed at low. computeWireGainMod (1506-1515) and its comment (1499-1505) are as described; wireEnergyPeak_ / wireGainMod_ reset to 0 / 1.0 at note-on and reset (425-426, 485-488), so the first chunk runs at full buzz with no onset lag. Fast path uses the previous chunk's gain (857-863) and updates once per chunk (910-919); slow path uses it per sample (1051) but updates once per whole block (1073-1082); process() never updates it (542-549). No contact threshold or batter-to-snare delay exists; PLAN-wire-coupling-2026-07-13.md:10-15 confirms the envelope-follower intent. Deliberate, off by default (wireCoupling 0 is bit-exact legacy).
- Research lens: confirmed. noteOn resets (422-426) and the rising 20 ms follower being its own running peak (917) keep the gain at 1 from t = 0. Torin/Hamilton/Bilbao DAFx-14 Sec. 5.2 quoted verbatim (pdftotext), using the positive-part collision form; Bilbao/Torin/Chatziioannou (arXiv 1405.2589) gives f = K[u]+^alpha for snares on the lower membrane (Sec. 8.4). Minor issues: 2012 is the acceptance date (published 2015); 6/9 ms come from one simulated configuration; "soft hits give proportionally less rattle" is an inference from the one-sided law (physically sound); the 6 dB test bar has no source.
- Context/impact lens: refutes. Self-normalisation is the stated design (drum_voice.h:1499-1505; plan:10-16 rules out a collision model), plan test case 4 (336-338) requires an unattenuated onset, and the process() divergence is a documented convention (plan:120-130; drum_voice.h:542-546). The velocity-to-buzz ratio is set elsewhere: NoiseLayer::trigger ignores velocity (noise_layer.h:158), so any ghost-note excess comes from there, which could be filed separately. Default wireCoupling is 0 (plan:160), only acoustic snares use 0.45 (plan:291, 304-305), and the 6-9 ms lag is masked by the stick attack and click layer.

#### MB-261 — FM Ratio's 12 dB adjacent-step jump is not the stale StrikeNormKey: the peak is normalised, but the sustained level is not, and the FM sidebands sit at fixed Hz, not the body's pitch, so they hit or miss the hat's long-ringing ~1.06 kHz mode

**Severity:** low (finder: medium; downgraded by verification) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** measured-exciter · **Dimension:** followup:strike-norm-miss-bell-pads

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/fm_impulse_exciter.h:80-86](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/exciters/fm_impulse_exciter.h#L80)

**Problem.** FMImpulse places its carrier at 400*6.25^v Hz and its modulator at carrier x (1 + 3 x fmRatioNorm) (fm_impulse_exciter.h:80-86), independent of the pad's Size or natural fundamental. Its output is a tonal burst (80 ms amplitude envelope) with sidebands |fc + k fm|. Strike normalisation (drum_voice.h:1322-1412) fixes only the early broadband PEAK. On the default-kit hat that peak comes at 0.5-7 ms. How much energy goes into the body's long-ringing modes depends on whether a sideband falls near one, and nothing normalises that energy. The tail is dominated by a 1062 Hz mode. At ratio 1.656 the lower sideband |1693-2805| = 1112 Hz lands near it, and rms500 rises by 15-18 dB against neighbouring steps.

**Why wrong.** The param-audibility probe used a fresh Processor for every step, so a stale cache cannot explain the jump (MB-176's verifiers agree), and the fresh-voice reproduction here matches it exactly. The level change is real DSP behaviour. A secondary exciter parameter that changes level by 12-18 dB between nearby settings, and changes the decay time 3x, is a modulation-coincidence artefact of a carrier that does not track the body. The SC-004 velocity-to-brightness design (fm_impulse_exciter.h:74-76) makes the same coincidence depend on velocity as well.

**Consequence.** On FMImpulse pads, FM Ratio acts as a resonance lottery rather than a timbre control. Small edits swing the loudness of the ring by up to 18 dB and the decay from 0.33 s to 1.02 s. Each step lands differently at each velocity, because the carrier moves with velocity. All 66 FMImpulse factory pads use this fixed-Hz carrier.

**Evidence.** specs/membrum-audit/probes/limiter-fm-ratio-sweep.csv: default kit pad 6 (MIDI 42), exciter forced to FMImpulse, fresh DrumVoice per step, 48 kHz. Vel 100/127 rms500 dB (voice output): ratio norm 0 -41.14, 0.25 -30.78, 0.5 -42.99. With the -6 dB master these are -47.1 / -36.8 / -49.0, an exact match for param-audibility.csv:100 ('-47.1 -36.8 -49.0'). The neutral post-chain gives the same swing (-41.58 / -30.76 / -43.52), so the cause is exciter plus body. Fine steps: 0.1875 -34.78, 0.21875 -25.72, 0.25 -30.78, 0.3125 -44.12, a 18.4 dB swing within 3/32. Peaks stay within -5.8..-16.4 dBFS (neutral normalised 0.24-0.80). Tail dominant frequency (Goertzel 100-600 ms): 1062 Hz in most steps. The sideband 1112 Hz falls near it at 0.21875 (fm 2805 Hz). Code: fm_impulse_exciter.h:80 `const float kModulatorRatio = 1.0f + 3.0f * modulatorRatioNorm_;`, :83 `const float baseFreq = 400.0f * std::pow(6.25f, velocity);`, :86 `modulator_.setFrequency(baseFreq * kModulatorRatio);`.

**Suggested fix.** Tie the FM base frequency to the body (for example baseFreq = naturalFundamentalHz_ x a velocity-dependent multiplier), or excite with an FM burst short enough to be broadband. If the level of the ring must hold, normalise an energy measure (for example RMS over 100-300 ms) in addition to the peak. Regression test: sweep fmRatio 0..1 in 1/32 steps on the default-kit hat with FMImpulse at vel 100/127, and assert that adjacent-step rms500 differences stay < 6 dB.

**Verifier notes:**
- Code confirmed: fm_impulse_exciter.h:80/83/85-86 put carrier and modulator at fixed Hz with no read of Size or naturalFundamentalHz_; the strike probe (drum_voice.h:1322-1412, 30 ms peak at velocity 1.0, lines 1329-1353) has no energy term, and StrikeNormKey has no fmRatio field (drum_voice.h:1400-1406), so the stale cache is not the cause. Downgrade to low: the swing appears only on the sparse-mode hat body (kick 36 / snare 38 stay within about 3 dB, CSV rows 68-199); the default-kit hat is NoiseBurst (default_kit.h:186-187), so FMImpulse was forced; adjacent 1/32 steps differ by at most about 9-10 dB; the single-sideband mechanism explains only the 0.2188 step (rises at 0.375, 0.5938, 0.7812-0.8438 have no sideband near 1062 Hz). The "66 FMImpulse factory pads" count could not be verified.
- Disputes the defect: the fixed-Hz, velocity-scaled carrier is the documented FR-014/FR-016/SC-004 design (fm_impulse_exciter.h:6-15, :73-76; specs/137 data-model.md §2.5), and tying it to the body would break the velocity-to-centroid contract. The CSV contradicts the sideband mechanism (line 29, norm 0.8438: no sideband near 1062 Hz yet -28.10 dB; line 36, vel 1.0: same). The configuration is synthetic (audit_limiter_probe.cpp.txt:352; no FMImpulse pad in default_kit.h); the CSV has no decay column, so "0.33 s to 1.02 s" is not supported there. What remains is the expected interaction of a tonal exciter with a sparse high-Q body.
- Not refuted, downgraded: the CSV shows an 18.4 dB swing within 3/32 and adjacent jumps up to 13.5 dB (0.84375 -28.10 vs 0.875 -41.57); param-audibility.csv:100 gives decay 0.33 / 1.02 / 0.52. Narrower than claimed: one forced pad and body type; at vel 1.0 adjacent hat steps stay at or below about 5.8 dB; the sideband explanation fits only one peak; the code follows its spec (lines 73-76); factory FMImpulse pads (mostly Bell, e.g. generator lines 895, 1333, 1365, 1495, 1931, 3086) store a fixed, by-ear fmRatio, so the effect matters only while a user edits.

#### MB-262 — Resonant tone-shaper filter and modeInject add peak gain after the strike probe, so Experimental FX Kit FM pads sit at -1.7 to -3.4 dBFS and cross the limiter on some hits (critic cause (c), confirmed for these pads)

**Severity:** low (finder: medium; downgraded by verification) · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** gain-staging · **Dimension:** followup:strike-norm-miss-bell-pads

**Location:** [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:158-165](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h#L158)

**Problem.** The strike probe normalises only the modal bank output (drum_voice.h:1322-1363). Downstream, the tone-shaper SVF Q maps res [0,1] to [0.707, 10] (tone_shaper.h:158-165) without gain compensation, and modeInject is added with random per-trigger phases (mode_inject.h trigger). Both raise the peak after normalisation. Pads that combine a mid cutoff with res 0.55 (Q about 5.8) and modeInject 0.2-0.5 run 4-6 dB hot. modeInject's random phases also make successive hits of the same pad differ by up to about 3 dB.

**Why wrong.** The voice budget (kBodyHeadroom, -6 dBFS strike peak) assumes the post-bank chain is unity on peaks. A resonant filter peaks by up to about Q at its corner, so it needs make-up or a peak-aware budget. Critic cause (c) is the explanation here, as opposed to the FM Bell pads, where (c) is under 0.7 dB.

**Consequence.** Experimental FX Kit 52 and 58 (FMImpulse/Shell, cutoff .48/.56, res .55) peak at +0.20 / -0.45 dBFS pre-limiter on the first hit and -2.63 / -1.68 on the next. Pads 40, 55 and 62 sit at -3.1 / -3.4 / -2.9 dBFS. The filter alone adds +4.6..+6.1 dB on these pads, and +6.0 dB on 909 Drum Machine 38. Single stages add more than 3 dB of peak on 61 of 383 modal factory pads. Hit-to-hit randomness keeps several of them on the edge of the limiter.

**Evidence.** specs/membrum-audit/probes/limiter-pads.csv and limiter-probe-summary.txt, peak reduction when only that stage is neutralised, as dB. Experimental FX Kit 52: dFilter 5.16, dModeInject 4.04, stale -> asis pre-limiter +0.20 -> -2.63 dBFS. EFX 58: dFilter 4.56, dModeInject 2.15, -0.45 -> -1.68. EFX 40 FMImpulse/Plate: dFilter 6.11, -3.14. EFX 55: dFilter 5.32, -3.44. EFX 62: dFilter 5.10, dModeInject 4.88, -2.86. 909 Drum Machine 38: dFilter 5.98. Rock Big Room 52 NoiseBurst/NoiseBody: dModeInject 4.41, pre-limiter -2.35 / -3.64. Caveat: deltas on pads with modeInject > 0 or noise exciters include hit-to-hit random phase, so only filter deltas on pads without modeInject (EFX 40, 55, 909 38) are clean attributions.

**Suggested fix.** Add resonance make-up (for example divide by sqrt(Q) or a measured peak law) in ToneShaper, or include the filter in the strike probe's path. Scale modeInject to the body budget, which is the existing modeInject finding. Test: render the Experimental FX 52 config 10 times on fresh voices at vel 100/127 and assert peak x panGain < 0.89 on every hit.

**Verifier notes:**
- Mechanism confirmed, consequence overstated: probeStrikePeakExcited (drum_voice.h:1322-1363) and measuredStrikeOutputGainExcited (1380-1387, kBodyHeadroom = 0.5 at :84) cover only exciter + click*0.5 into the bank; modeInject, nonlinearCoupling and toneShaper_ run after it (drum_voice.h:557-559, 893-896, 1056-1059); setFilterResonance (tone_shaper.h:158-165) and processSample (:395-460, env-swept cutoff at :454) have no make-up; ModeInject::trigger re-randomises 8 phases per hit (unnatural/mode_inject.h:107-113, added at :142). Downgrade: limiterAsis = 0 for every cited pad, and only the "stale" column crosses (EFX 52 +0.20, from the stale-hint defect, summary lines 81ff); EFX 40 has res 0.20 (Q about 2.6), its boost comes from the envelope sweep (envAmt 0.6, cutoff 0.82); EFX 55 has modeInject 0.2, not 0.
- Not a defect: kBodyHeadroom is a -6 dBFS strike-peak budget for the body that leaves overs to the -1 dBTP bus limiter and loudness make-up to master gain (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:121); resonance gain at the corner is the control's audible job, unlike the hidden drive gain fixed by M-2 (tone_shaper.h:206); factory kits are voiced with these values (PRESET-RETUNE-PLAN.md:108). limiterAsis is 0 for all 383 pads (audit_limiter_probe.cpp.txt:15-16, 247-250, threshold 0.8913); the one crossing (EFX 52 stale, hintEffectDb 2.83) belongs to the stale-hint issue; clean filter cases (EFX 40 -3.14, EFX 55 -3.44, 909 38 -12.58 dBFS) stay below the limiter even with panGain 1.17-1.28. The modeInject spread belongs to the existing modeInject finding.
- Downgraded to low: Q = 0.707 + res*9.29 (res 0.55 gives 5.82) with no compensation; quoted numbers match limiter-pads.csv and limiter-probe-summary.txt line 19 ("any single stage adds > 3 dB: 61"). Only EFX 52 (+0.20) and EFX 58 (-0.45) cross, both on the stale first hit, where the 2.83 / 1.23 dB stale/asis difference comes from modeInject's random phase; at most about 1.2 dB of gain reduction on 2 of 383 pads. The limiter is the designed owner of overs (drum_voice.h:79-80); the hot figures include +1.8 to +2.1 dB of equal-power pan gain (1.23-1.28) that is not the tone shaper. What remains is a gain-staging and preset-balance issue in mainly the Experimental FX kit.

#### MB-268 — membrum-fit keeps an eighth hand-numbered offset-to-field map that stops at offset 58: the fitter cannot reach the enable, knee, mid-pitch, curve2, pan, wire-coupling or noise-gain fields

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** duplication · **Dimension:** followup:state-field-table-design

**Location:** [tools/membrum-fit/src/refinement/bobyqa_refine.cpp:13-79](tools/membrum-fit/src/refinement/bobyqa_refine.cpp#L13) (also [tools/membrum-fit/src/main.cpp:281-282](tools/membrum-fit/src/main.cpp#L281), [291-298](tools/membrum-fit/src/main.cpp#L291))

**Problem.** fieldPtr() re-declares the PadParamOffset-to-PadConfig-member mapping as a switch on integer literals (case 2..58). The header comment says it 'Matches pad_config.h PadParamOffset enum'. It has no cases for offsets 59-65 (enabled, tsPitchEnvKneeEnabled, tsPitchEnvMidPitch, tsPitchEnvMidFraction, tsPitchEnvCurve2, pan, wireCoupling), and no index at all for noiseLayerGain. main.cpp builds the optimisable set from bare literals: {2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 15} and {50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 56, 57, 58}, where 57 means secondaryMaterial as an OFFSET. The same number 57 means noiseLayerGain as a sound SLOT in the codec.

**Why wrong.** The audit scope includes membrum-fit wherever it duplicates the plugin's parameter mapping, and this function duplicates VoicePool::setPadConfigField (voice_pool.cpp:605-699) by hand. The default branch returns nullptr, which padConfigToVector turns into 0.0f (bobyqa_refine.cpp:87-88). An index that falls outside the switch therefore becomes a silent 0, not an error. Meanwhile 57 means different things in the offset space and the slot space.

**Consequence.** Fits can never adjust the noise-layer gain, even though the snare's identity depends on it (default_kit.h:120 sets 6.2), nor the wire coupling or the three-point pitch envelope. Any future offset renumbering desyncs the fitter without a compile error.

**Evidence.** bobyqa_refine.cpp:13-17: 'indices 2..58 map the continuous float fields of PadConfig in offset order ... Matches pad_config.h PadParamOffset enum.' :20-76 is the case list, ending ':76 case 58: return &c.tensionModAmt; :77 default: return nullptr;'. :87-88 'const float* p = fieldPtr(c, indices[i]); out[i] = p ? *p : 0.0f;'. main.cpp:281-282 'rctx.optimisable = { 2 /\*material\*/, 3 /\*size\*/, 4 /\*decay\*/, 8 /\*tsFilterCutoff\*/, 9 /\*tsFilterResonance\*/, 15 /\*tsPitchEnvTime\*/ };' and :296 'for (int idx : {50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 56, 57, 58})'. pad_config.h:151-175 defines offsets 59-65 (kPadEnabled .. kPadWireCoupling), which the switch never reaches. tools/membrum-fit/src/preset_io/kit_preset_writer.cpp:19 uses State::toPadSnapshot, so the writer side is not duplicated; only the optimiser map is.

**Suggested fix.** Replace fieldPtr with a lookup into the kPadFields descriptor table from the first finding: kPadFields[rowForOffset[idx]].member, with an assert on nullptr. Replace the literal lists in main.cpp with named PadParamOffset constants. Once noiseLayerGain has an offset (Option 1 of the representation finding), add it to the optional Phase-8 set. Test: a membrum-fit unit test that, for every offset 2..kPadActiveParamCount-1 except selectors, choke and bus, gets a non-null pointer, and checks that it addresses the same member VoicePool::setPadConfigField writes.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed from source (bobyqa_refine.cpp:18-79 switch on 2..58 skipping 30/31, nullptr to 0.0f at :87-88, silently skipped at :97; pad_config.h:40-176 offsets 59-65 have no case). All 57 cases match the enum today, so there is no drift, and the silent-0 path is unreachable with current callers. Recommends nit: the small subset is deliberate (main.cpp:273 "a small, Kick-friendly subset", :283-286), and the fitter carries noiseLayerGain / wireCoupling elsewhere (gen_entry.cpp:112-113; test_render_fidelity.cpp:114-119; test_bobyqa.cpp:46 covers the Phase-8 round-trip).
- Duplication real, severity down to nit: every case matches PadParamOffset (pad_config.h:42-144, 57 = secondaryMaterial); offset vs codec slot are separate index spaces, not a mismatch; nothing selects 59..65 or noiseLayerGain (pad_config.h:261, no offset), and several of those (enabled, knee switch, pan) are poor optimisation targets; gen_entry.cpp:101-135 loads them from JSON; AGENT_GUIDE.md:307-311 lists fieldPtr as a place to update when PadConfig changes, and test_bobyqa.cpp:42-74 pins the Phase 8 cases.
- No wrong result today: the map matches pad_config.h:42-144, with 0/1 and 30/31 left out on purpose (:13-14); bobyqa_refine.h:23 documents `optimisable; // subset of [2..58]` and all callers (main.cpp:281-282, :296; test_bobyqa.cpp:32, :104-105) stay inside it. noiseLayerGain is not normalized (default 1.0, snare 6.2) and vectorToPadConfig clamps to [0,1] (bobyqa_refine.cpp:98), so it cannot belong to this optimiser. Offsets are frozen by the VST3 parameter-ID scheme (kPadBaseId + pad*stride + offset). What remains is a refactor suggestion, not a defect.

#### MB-272 — getModalEnergy() (the tension and wire-coupling driver) is not the smooth amplitude^2 its comment claims: for the magic circle, s^2 + c^2 ripples at twice the mode frequency, so a reading taken once per chunk is off by up to 31%

**Severity:** low · **Verdict:** PLAUSIBLE · **Category:** physics-contradicted · **Dimension:** followup:modal-retune-while-ringing

**Location:** [dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:482-499](dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h#L482); [plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:902-920](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L902), [1075](plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h#L1075)

**Problem.** getModalEnergy() returns sum_k (s_k^2 + c_k^2) (493-499). The comment (482-492) says 'For a Gordon-Smith phasor sin^2 + cos^2 is the mode's amplitude^2 (a smooth envelope, not an oscillating quantity)'. In the magic circle, s_n = A sin(n w) and c_n = A cos(n w + w/2): the two are half a sample off quadrature. So s^2 + c^2 = A^2 [1 - sin(w/2) sin(2 n w + w/2)]. It ripples by +/- sin(pi f/fs) at 2f around a mean of A^2, while the exact amplitude^2 is (s^2 + c^2 + eps s c)/(1 - eps^2/4). DrumVoice reads this value once at the end of each chunk (drum_voice.h:912; slow path :1075) to drive tension modulation and wire coupling. A single-sample read of a 2f ripple acts as a sampled noise term in the follower.

**Why wrong.** Vicanek 2015 (https://www.vicanek.de/articles/QuadOsc.pdf, Appendix 'Magic Circle Oscillator') states that the magic-circle outputs have 'a phase difference of 90 degrees plus half a sample'. So s^2 + c^2 is not constant along the orbit, and only the invariant form above is. The comment also cites Avanzini-Marogna-Bank for 'stored vibrational energy'. Marogna, Avanzini & Bank, 'Energy based synthesis of tension modulation in membranes', DAFx-10, Graz 2010 (opened: https://people.ece.cornell.edu/land/courses/ece5760/LABS/s2016/MarognaAvanziniBank_tension_modulation.pdf) define the membrane energy as E = T0/(2R^2) sum mu_nm^2 A_nm^2/||K_nm||^2 e^(-2t/tau) (eq. 19). That is a mode-order-weighted sum, built from kinetic and potential energies that 'oscillate in antiphase' so their total 'is a slowly decaying signal' (sec. 4.1). The bank's unweighted s^2 + c^2 is neither that energy nor ripple-free. The paper estimates energy at a decimated rate and linearly interpolates (sec. 4.2), which works only because its energy has no 2f ripple.

**Consequence.** Measured: a getModalEnergy reading at a chunk end differs from the exact amplitude^2 sum by up to 0.7% (one mode at 100 Hz) and 1.6% (48-mode membrane at f0 = 100 Hz) at 44.1 kHz, but by up to 14.2% (one mode at 2 kHz) and 31.0% (48 modes, f0 2 kHz). At 96 kHz the figures are 0.3% / 0.6% / 6.4% / 10.5%. Low-pitched membranes (tension modulation is gated to Membrane) see only a few percent. A high-pitched body with Wire Coupling (any modal body, drum_voice.h:732) gets a chunk-to-chunk wire-gain jitter. By derivation, not measured: sqrt(1 +/- 0.31) passed through a follower that keeps 1 - pow(alpha, 512) = 44% of each new reading at 512-sample chunks gives about +/-7% buzz-gain steps, and the size depends on fs and on the block size. Seraphis ContinuousBody also reads getModalEnergy (continuous_body.h:4133).

**Evidence.** modal_resonator_bank.h:484-486 '...sin^2 + cos^2 is the mode's amplitude^2 (a smooth envelope, not an oscillating quantity)'; :496-497 'energy += sinState_[k] \* sinState_[k] + cosState_[k] \* cosState_[k];'. drum_voice.h:912-914 'const float e = bodyBank_.getSharedBank().getModalEnergy(); const float a = std::pow(energyAlpha_, chunk); energyEnv_ = a \* energyEnv_ + (1.0f - a) \* e;'. Probe (specs/membrum-audit/probes/retune-probe-results.txt): 'E6 fs= 44100 f0= 2000 48 modes : ... deviates from the amplitude^2 sum by up to 31.0%'; 'E6 fs= 44100 f0= 100 1 mode : ... 0.7%'; E1 lines 'getModalEnergy ripple over a period at f2: -5.8% / +5.8% of its mean (mean/A^2 = 1.0000)' for an 816 Hz mode at 44.1 kHz (sin(pi\*816/44100) = 5.8%, as predicted).

**Suggested fix.** Add a new accessor, for example getModalAmplitudeSq() = sum (s^2 + c^2 + eps_k s c)/(1 - eps_k^2/4) using the running epsilon_. In the probe it equals the exact amplitude^2, and its mean over a cycle matches getModalEnergy's mean (mean/A^2 = 1.0000). Switch DrumVoice's tension and wire follower (drum_voice.h:912, 1075) to it. Leave getModalEnergy unchanged for Seraphis. Correct the comment at 482-492 and the 'smooth envelope' claim at drum_voice.h:902-905. Test in dsp_processors_tests: one ringing 2 kHz mode, getModalAmplitudeSq read at every sample over one period varies by < 0.1% after removing the decay.

**Verifier notes:**
- Confirmed against code: the magic-circle update s_new = R\*(s + eps\*c) + inj, c_new = R\*(c - eps\*s_new) (modal_resonator_bank.h:938-939, 959-960; modal_resonator_bank_simd.cpp:96-103, 129-130) conserves s^2 + c^2 + eps\*s\*c, so s^2 + c^2 ripples at 2f by about +/- sin(pi f/fs), matching the probe (retune-probe-results.txt line 4; lines 56-59 at 44.1 kHz; lines 67-70 at 96 kHz). drum_voice.h:912-914 and :1075-1077 read it once per chunk into energyEnv_ (alpha from :132-133, 20 ms), which drives the Membrane tension mod (:722-728) and computeWireGainMod (:917-918, :1506-1512; wireActive at :732 for any body). The ripple mean is unbiased, so the error is small post-smoothing jitter: low.
- Confirmed from source alone (the Vicanek quote could not be checked: WebFetch returned only the PDF structure and the saved PDF could not be rendered). Hand derivation: x' = x + e\*y, y' = y - e\*x' preserves x^2 + y^2 + e\*x\*y, with eps_k = 2\*sin(pi\*f/fs) (:827); 2 kHz gives 14.2% and 816 Hz 5.8%, matching the probe. energyEnv_ drives the tension retune (drum_voice.h:726, :949) and wireGainMod_ (:1512) with a block-size-dependent phase; the comments at drum_voice.h:902-905 and modal_resonator_bank.h:482-486 are wrong. Low: Membrane-only tension, modest wire jitter partly derived, nothing unstable.
- Math holds, impact inaudible: the tom case gives +/-0.8% on the fundamental (E1 "tom tension") and E6 at f0 = 100 Hz at most 1.6%; under tensionPitchMod = 1 + amt\*energyEnv_ capped at kTensionPitchModMax = 1.19 (drum_voice.h:100, 725-728) that is under about 5 cents. computeWireGainMod (drum_voice.h:1506-1515) halves the error via sqrt and scales by coupling on a noise layer (:860-863); the 31% / +/-7% case needs a 48-mode body at 2 kHz and a 512-sample block (kMaxBlockSize = 2048, :589), about +/-0.6 dB on broadband noise. Per-chunk unsmoothed steps already exist by design (:910-919) and decay steps are larger. The unweighted energy is an accepted simplification (AUDIT-signal-path-2026-06-07.md:319).

- **CA summary.** CA's line 25 says every confirmed finding is resolved. This audit agrees for Findings 1-5, 7, 8, 11, 13-16, 19 and 20, which it did not find repeated. Two of these have related new findings:
  - MB-010 notes that the Finding 7 fix covered only the FeedbackExciter follower, which was all it set out to cover.
  - MB-204 concerns the plate strike shape that replaced Finding 8's formula.

  The fixes for Findings 6, 9, 10, 12, 17 and 18 each left a sibling site behind; see the rows above.
- **SP tracker gaps.** The LOW list (SP :291-304) puts a ✅ only on L-3 and L-4. L-2, L-5, L-7, L-8, L-9 and L-12 were closed in the batch tables (SP :48-50, :134-136), and L-1 in the appendix. L-6 and L-10 were never addressed, and neither appears in the "Open" list (SP :141-205). That list also omits `confirmed[17]`. Verifiers read the "Open" list as a short priority list rather than a claim that L-6 and L-10 were done, so the tracker is incomplete, not wrong. The tracker also still marks the N-1 heading ⬜ (SP :144) under the ✅ "N-1 — DONE" line (SP :143).

### Flagged by the prior-audit dimension, but repeating no prior id

- **MB-116** (medium). `Processor::initialize` installs the default kit with `DefaultKit::apply` (processor.cpp:111). That is a third kit-install route, and it never syncs `ChokeGroupTable`, so the default hats (MIDI 42 / 44 / 46) do not choke on a fresh instance until a kit is loaded. This is the single-apply rule from R-202 / T1.36, but on a route that RA did not cover. CA Finding 23 checked the choke bookkeeping but not the table sync.
- **MB-069** (low; verifiers suggest nit). The multi-bus `VoicePool::processBlock`, which is the path real hosts use, frees a naturally finished slot without `couplingEngine_->noteOff(slot)`. The mono overload does call it (voice_pool.cpp:388-390 vs 514-519). The only effect is stale `refCounts_` in later resonator merges. It is parallel-path drift of the same kind as SP M-6, not a repeat of it.

## 8. Inventory cross-reference

Three read-only inventories cross-referenced the plugin's parameters, its enum types, and its presets, versions and docs. Each inventory gives a summary, its tables, and its full mismatch list. No builds or probes were run for these inventories.

### 8.1 Parameter-plumbing inventory: summary

Sources cross-referenced: plugin_ids.h (69 global IDs incl. kUiModeId), pad_config.h (PadParamOffset enum: 66 active offsets 0-65, plus PadConfig initialisers), controller.cpp (kProxyMappings: 60 rows at lines 85-154; kPadParamSpecs: 66 rows at lines 167-249; global addParameter registrations at lines 281-727), processor.cpp processParameterChanges (per-pad branch at lines 171-237, global switch at 240-525, buildRegisteredDefaultsTable at 58-87), voice_pool.cpp setPadConfigField (613-661) and setPadConfigSelector, dsp/pad_config_apply.h, controller_param_format.cpp, state_codec.cpp, controller_state_codec.cpp, tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp, macro_mapper.cpp, default_kit.h and editor.uidesc (inventory JSON at F:/tmp/membrum-audit/uidesc-inventory.json; script cross-check at F:/tmp/membrum-audit/xref.js).

Results:

- All 66 offsets have a spec row, an enum name, a PadConfig field and a voice-pool case.
- All 60 proxy rows agree with the processor switch (59 write the same field directly; kChokeGroupId routes through setPadChokeGroup, which updates the same cfg.chokeGroup).
- Every registered global has a processor case except kUiModeId (session-scoped by design).
- All 76 uidesc control-tag names resolve to registered IDs; the uidesc inventory reports 160 defects, all layout 'overlap' entries, none parameter-related.
- Only per-pad offset 59 (Pad Enabled) has no control in SelectedPadSimple or SelectedPadAdvanced; it is reachable only through PadGridView's glyph hit-test (editor.uidesc:117-121 comment).

The main defect classes are:

- (a) noiseLayerGain (slot 57) has no parameter and is dropped by the controller codec.
- (b) Body damping -1 sentinel vs a 0.5 registration and a 0.40 generator default.
- (c) Several defaults that disagree across PadConfig, registration, proxy, generator and comments.
- (d) Filter-envelope displays are linear while the voice decodes cubically.
- (e) Pitch-envelope values have no formatter, and the global units say Hz/ms while the voice uses 20-2000 Hz and 0-500 ms.
- (f) The registered-defaults table in the processor has no reader (macro_mapper.cpp:39 stores it, nothing reads defaults_).
- (g) Several comments in plugin_ids.h, pad_config.h, drum_voice.h and the controller are stale against the code.

The uidesc inventory undercounts bound controls: its 'bound' count omits tags bound through view attributes (PitchEnvelopeDisplay start-tag etc., XYMorphPad secondary-tag), so SelectedPadSimple shows 15 bound by the tool but 23 tags by full scan.

Extra-focus lead checks:

1. Confirmed structurally that buildPadSnapshotFromParams never writes sound[57] and that the controller reads body damping as 0.5, so saves carry the 0.5 override; the snare wire (6.2) and default pad (1.0) are lost on the controller save path. No audible or byte-level probe was run.
2. Confirmed the three hand-written slot maps and the controller/generator maps agree slot-for-slot today (59 slots; the generator's array at generator.cpp:248-291 matches state_codec.cpp:64-160), so the drift risk is the duplicated skip list and the clamp difference, not a present mismatch.
3. The lead's claim that setPadConfigField 'clamps nothing' is only partly right: it clamps choke and bus (voice_pool.cpp:641-656) and no float field (613-639, 649-650, 657-696).

### 8.5 Parameter inventory: mismatch list (28 entries)

**P-1. noiseLayerGain (PadConfig slot 57) has no parameter offset and is dropped by the controller codec; the state codec clamps it on load**

- Where: plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:261 vs plugins/membrum/src/controller/controller.cpp:167-249 (kPadParamSpecs ends at Wire Coupling; no row for slot 57) and controller_state_codec.cpp kLateSlots (no snapIndex 57 row) vs plugins/membrum/src/state/state_codec.cpp:243 and :326 (clamp to 0.1..16).
- Detail: PadConfig default noiseLayerGain = 1.0f. buildPadSnapshotFromParams (controller_state_codec.cpp:117-181) never writes sound[57], so the controller save writes 0.0, and applyPadSnapshot then clamps it to 0.1 (-20 dB on a default pad). default_kit.h:120 sets the snare to 6.2f and generator.cpp:587 writes 6.2 for the same pad; the controller path cannot represent either. Structural finding only; no audible probe was run.

**P-2. Body damping B1/B3: PadConfig sentinel -1.0 vs registered default 0.5, and the generator writes 0.40 explicitly for every pad**

- Where: pad_config.h:282-283 (-1.0f) vs controller.cpp:227-228 (defaultValue 0.5) and controller.cpp:621, 624 (proxy 0.5) vs tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:135-136 (0.40).
- Detail: The controller save path reads the registered value (0.5) through kLateSlots snapIndex 42/43 and writes an explicit override, so the -1 sentinel never survives a controller-side save (the apply path skips writing the sentinel, controller_state_codec.cpp, applyPadSnapshotToParams). Generated factory kits store 0.40 for every pad that does not override it, so no shipped pad uses the sentinel.

**P-3. tsPitchEnvCurve default: PadConfig 0.0 (fast drop) vs registration and proxy 0.5 (linear) vs generator 0.15; the processor defaults table has no entry for offset 16**

- Where: pad_config.h:205 (0.0f) vs controller.cpp:184 (0.5) and controller.cpp:431-433 (0.5) vs tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:93 (0.15) and :516; processor.cpp:58-87 (no t.byOffset[kPadTSPitchEnvCurve]).
- Detail: The voice decodes 2n-1 (pad_config_apply.h:111), so a PadConfig default pad plays curve -1 while the editor shows 0.5 (linear) until state arrives. default_kit.h templates other than toms leave the PadConfig 0.0.

**P-4. tsPitchEnvStart proxy default 0.070721 disagrees with the PadConfig/spec default 0.0 and with the plugin_ids.h comment 'default 160'**

- Where: controller.cpp:347 (proxy 0.070721) vs pad_config.h:202 (0.0f), controller.cpp:181 (0.0), processor.cpp:68 (0.0) and plugin_ids.h:75 ('20..2000 Hz, default 160').
- Detail: Per-pad default is 0.0 (= 20 Hz). The global proxy shows 0.070721 (about 23.6 Hz), and the comment says 160 Hz, which is normalised 0.4515 (default_kit.h:59 uses that value for kicks).

**P-5. tsPitchEnvEnd comment default 50 Hz vs code default 0.0 (20 Hz)**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:76 ('20..2000 Hz, default 50') vs controller.cpp:348 (defaultValue 0.0, unit Hz) and pad_config.h:203 (0.0f).
- Detail: The comment's 50 Hz is normalised 0.1990 (default_kit.h:60 uses it for kicks).

**P-6. NoiseBurst Duration: proxy default 0.230769 (5 ms) disagrees with per-pad default 0.5 (8.5 ms)**

- Where: controller.cpp:336 (proxy 0.230769) vs controller.cpp:202 (spec 0.5), pad_config.h:236 (0.5f), processor.cpp:77 (0.5).
- Detail: The proxy default matches plugin_ids.h:65 'default 5'. A fresh instance shows 5 ms on the proxy while the per-pad value is 8.5 ms.

**P-7. Exciter Friction Pressure: comment default 0.3 vs code default 0.0**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:66 ('default 0.3') vs controller.cpp:341 (0.0, with the audit-10 comment saying the proxy was aligned to 0.0), pad_config.h:237 (0.0f).
- Detail: The comment is stale. Code is consistent at 0.0.

**P-8. FM Ratio default: generator 0.5 vs PadConfig and registration 0.133333**

- Where: tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:105 (fmRatio = 0.5) vs pad_config.h:234 (0.133333f), controller.cpp:200 (0.133333).
- Detail: Generated factory pads that do not set fmRatio carry 0.5 (ratio 2.5 with the mapping 1 + 3n, drum_voice/fm_impulse_exciter.h:80) instead of the 1.4 default. Only the FMImpulse exciter is affected.

**P-9. Exciter type and body model: comment and spec disagree with the registered list**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:61 ('StringListParameter, 6 choices') vs controller.cpp:302-308 (7 entries: Impulse..Clap) and exciter_type.h:20 (kCount = 7); controller.cpp:168-169 (spec stepCount 5 for both).
- Detail: The spec stepCount is ignored for these two offsets (the branch at controller.cpp:685-708 registers 7 and 6 entries), but the table value 5 is wrong for both.

**P-10. UI Mode labels: comment says {Acoustic, Extended}; code registers {Simple, Advanced}**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:123 vs controller.cpp:556-557 (appendString Simple, Advanced).
- Detail: Comment is stale.

**P-11. Global Coupling / Snare Buzz / Tom Resonance range: comment [0.0, 1.0] vs registered plain range 0..100 %**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:114 vs controller.cpp:511-512 and :517 (RangeParameter 0.0..100.0, unit %).
- Detail: Normalised wire value is still 0..1, so the processor is correct; only the comment is wrong.

**P-12. Choke Group comment says RangeParameter; code registers a StringListParameter**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:104 ('RangeParameter stepped [0,8]') vs controller.cpp:496 (parameters.addParameter(chokeList), the audit-17 StringList with None/CG1..CG8).
- Detail: Stale comment.

**P-13. Tone Shaper PitchEnv Curve comment says StringList Exp/Lin; code registers a continuous RangeParameter**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:78 vs controller.cpp:431-433 (RangeParameter 0..1, default 0.5); plugin_ids.h:173-175 states the Phase-10 change.
- Detail: Stale comment. pad_config.h:205 has the same stale 'discrete: 0=Exp, 1=Lin' note.

**P-14. Per-pad layout comment: stride 128 and 66 active offsets, but the comment gives the stride-64 layout**

- Where: plugin_ids.h:208-210 ('Pad 0: 1000-1063 ... Pad 31: 2984-3047; Offsets 0-35 are active') vs pad_config.h:25 (kPadParamStride = 128), pad_config.h:176 (kPadActiveParamCountV12 = 66).
- Detail: With stride 128, pad 31 spans 4968-5031. pad_config.h:22 also says offsets 0-64 are active, which is stale (0-65 after wire coupling).

**P-15. Coupling Strength comment claims a 0.25 ceiling; the code maps linearly to 0..1**

- Where: pad_config.h:297-298 ('0 -> 0.25 stable range; clamped below an eigenvalue-safety ceiling in DrumVoice') vs drum_voice.h:1484-1496 (effectiveCouplingStrength returns clamp(couplingStrength_, 0, 1); comment says the ceiling was removed in audit L-7).
- Detail: Comment is stale.

**P-16. Body damping b3 scale: comments say 1 -> 8e-5 (pad_config.h:279) and 0.5 -> 4e-5 (controller.cpp:223) vs mapper n * 1.0e-3**

- Where: pad_config.h:279 and controller.cpp:223 vs dsp/bodies/membrane_mapper.h:58 and :77 (law.b3 = n * 1.0e-3f).
- Detail: Norm 0.5 gives 5e-4, not 4e-5. Code is what the voice uses. default_kit.h:250 also writes 0.00008 as a normalised value, which the 1e-3 scale turns into 8e-8 (its comment at 240-246 says this is intended).

**P-17. Global titles differ from per-pad titles for Decay and Strike Position**

- Where: controller.cpp:288 (STR16('Resonance') for kDecayId) vs controller.cpp:172 (spec 'Decay'); controller.cpp:291 (STR16('Strike Point') for kStrikePositionId) vs controller.cpp:173 (spec 'Strike Position').
- Detail: Host-visible name drift between the proxy and the per-pad parameter.

**P-18. Filter envelope displays are linear but the voice decodes them cubically**

- Where: controller_param_format.cpp:291-293 and 372-374 (linear 0..500 ms and 0..2000 ms) vs pad_config_apply.h:91-98 (aN^3 * 500, dN^3 * 2000, rN^3 * 2000).
- Detail: At norm 0.5 the editor displays 250 ms attack and 1.00 s decay/release, while the voice plays 62.5 ms and 250 ms. pad_config_apply.h:87-89 says the cubic law matches ADSRDisplay, so the formatter is the outlier.

**P-19. Pitch envelope values have no formatter; unit labels say Hz / ms while the raw normalised value is shown**

- Where: controller_param_format.cpp: no case for offsets 13-16, 61 or globals 216-219, 322 (checked the whole switch at 275-341 and 359-422); units at controller.cpp:347-349 and the PitchEnv Mid registration (STR16 'Hz').
- Detail: Voice denormalisation: 20 * 100^n Hz (pad_config_apply.h:101-106, 115-117) and norm * 500 ms (pad_config_apply.h:107). The fall-through at controller_param_format.cpp getParamStringByValue returns EditControllerEx1's default text, which shows the normalised value with the unit suffix, so the host and the knob popups disagree with the audio.

**P-20. The registered-defaults table built in the processor has no reader; the macro mapper's comment describes a removed behaviour**

- Where: processor.cpp:58-87 (buildRegisteredDefaultsTable writes 0.5/0.3/...); macro_mapper.cpp:37-39 (prepare stores into defaults_); macro_mapper.h:84 (member), macro_mapper.h:70-74 (comment: first apply writes defaults_ + delta, which the -1 sentinel design did).
- Detail: grep finds no read of defaults_ or byOffset outside the writers. The table also lacks offset 16 (tsPitchEnvCurve) and omits pitch-envelope start/end from the macro path, which is harmless because the appliers use cache deltas only.

**P-21. Pad Enabled (offset 59 / global 309): no control in either pad template**

- Where: editor.uidesc:117-121 (control-tag 309 with comment: driven by the power glyph hit-test in PadGridView, not by a bound control) vs SelectedPadSimple (129-176) and SelectedPadAdvanced (177-349): no tag 309 or 1059.
- Detail: Reachable only through PadGridView (controller.cpp:909, 1112-1133). Registered as automatable. Not an unreachable parameter, but outside the pad templates the inventory checks.

## Appendix A — Refuted findings

Each finding below was refuted by the adversarial verifiers. They are listed so nobody re-finds them. In most cases the code facts in the finding were accurate; the verifiers refuted the claim that it is a defect (a documented, spec-mandated or deliberate design) or refuted the cited consequence.

| ID | Title | File:line | Refutation reason |
|----|-------|-----------|-------------------|
| MB-040 | Velocity is applied twice: the amp envelope peaks at velocity on top of the exciter and click velocity laws | plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:163, 436-437, 1336-1338 | Mechanism is real (adsr_envelope.h:512 peak = velocity, impact_exciter.h:129 pow(v,0.6)), but it is specified: spec 136 FR-037 gives the exciter its own velocity laws and FR-038 adds envelope velocity scaling (compliance row spec.md:284, tasks.md T032). Design decision, not a defect. |
| MB-057 | Master gain sits after the -1 dBTP bus limiter: up to +11 dBFS out, and the default -6 dB 'headroom' does not reduce limiting | plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:710-737 | Ordering is real but deliberate and documented (processor.cpp:711-716, processor.h:141-143): the limiter bounds the summed voice mix to -1 dBTP before master gain; it never promised a post-master ceiling. The earlier signal-path audit records this chain as the built design. |
| MB-058 | Zero-lookahead bus limiter steps its gain in one sample: clip-like onsets, true peak not held, 80 ms ducking of tails after coincident hits | dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/true_peak_limiter.h:114-124, 246-257 | Mechanics accurate, but zero look-ahead is the documented design (true_peak_limiter.h:8-10, 17-18: keeps main and aux buses sample-aligned, instant attack acceptable for percussion), recorded in the earlier audit and pinned by a test. Sample-offset handling is a separate issue. |
| MB-063 | Strike normalisation flattens the level differences between bodies, sizes and materials: tom and kick loudness come only from the Level knob | plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:286-306, 1394-1412 | Deliberate, documented design (drum_voice.h:73-84, audit decision N-1): modal over-run is 3-18x and dominated by Size, so every alternative that keeps a size-dependent level was rejected; loudness make-up belongs to master gain and per-pad Level. |
| MB-174 | Macros override the user's direct edits: returning a macro to 0.5 subtracts its delta from a value the user set explicitly | plugins/membrum/src/processor/macro_mapper.cpp:127-144, 160-178 | Probe arithmetic is right, but specs/141-membrum-phase6-ui/spec.md:35 specifies macros as forward-only delta drivers with a stored control value; editing an underlying parameter does not snap a macro. Intended behaviour. |
| MB-181 | Steal, choke and retrigger fast release is steeper than a 5 ms fade: tau 362 us gives -6 dB in about 0.25 ms | plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:78-86 | Spec 138 FR-124 (spec.md:172) fixes exactly this coefficient and states tau about 362 us, and forbids any other curve shape (linear, cosine). The suggested fix is the shape the spec prohibits; the click criterion passes. |
| MB-196 | Build log carries two third-party CMake configure warnings (Highway CMP0111 deprecation, pffft 'MIPP not found') | CMakeLists.txt:451-460, 473-487 | Both messages are real but come from upstream sources (highway-src/CMakeLists.txt:27-29, pffft cmake/FindMIPP.cmake:23), not from the repo's CMake. They are configure-time messages, not compiler diagnostics, so the zero-warnings gate (tools/check-build-warnings.js) does not cover them; no output changes and the suggested fix would not work. |
| MB-202 | Physics (contradicted): Plate/NoiseBody mode ratios follow free circular plate (Kirchhoff/Leissa) physics | plugins/membrum/src/dsp/bodies/plate_modes.h:4-35, 70-101 (generator tools/gen-plate-chladni.js:19-25,36-40; consumers plate_mapper.h:39-43, noise_body_mapper.h:95-106) | The table is a documented Chladni power-law fit for cymbals (f = C(m+2n)^P, P = 1.7) and states it is NOT an exact Leissa eigenvalue table (plate_modes.h:29-33). The finding used the wrong reference system, and the earlier audit asked for exactly this form. |
| MB-227 | Physics (oversimplified): A band-passed white-noise burst is a realistic stand-in for the stick/beater contact transient | plugins/membrum/src/dsp/click_layer.h:41-51, 67-76, 113-134, 166-173 | Code facts accurate, but the click is a deliberate, documented perceptual layer (Cook 'Sines + Noise + Transients', click_layer.h:6-12), not a contact-force model. The cited sources measure contact force, not the radiated attack, and the velocity-to-hardness cue is carried by the selected exciter. |
| MB-228 | Physics (unsupported): Routing half the click into the body excitation is justified by the commuted-synthesis principle | plugins/membrum/src/dsp/drum_voice.h:521-534, 783-794, 1322-1353; click_layer.h:6-16 | Routing is a deliberate, documented design choice used consistently by all three renderers and normalised in the strike probe; commuted synthesis (JOS) does support putting complexity in the excitation. At most the comment wording is loose, which is not a physics defect. |
| MB-238 | Physics (oversimplified): The 'Exp' pitch-sweep curve is an exponential, analogue-style glide | plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pitch_segment_envelope.h:60-73, 103-134; dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/curve_table.h:46, 65-79; plugins/membrum/src/dsp/tone_shaper.h:286-294, 503-512; plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config_apply.h:108-111; plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:205; plugins/membrum/src/dsp/default_kit.h:478; tools/membrum_preset_generator.cpp:88-93 | Code facts correct (a power-law sweep in linear Hz), but the shape is intended and documented (pitch_segment_envelope.h:7-10); the literature claim did not hold because its main source does not say what the finding says. Only stale comments remain, and the audible severity was not borne out. |
| MB-254 | Physics (oversimplified): Material identity (metal / wood / plastic) is mapped mainly onto b3 (the f^2 term) | plugins/membrum/src/dsp/pad_config.h:111-116, 274-283 (with membrane_mapper.h:121, 148-152; modal_resonator_bank.h:133-139; shell_mapper.h:56-58) | Deliberate simplification already documented and ruled acceptable by the earlier audit; the override path (b1 0.2-50, b3 0-1e-3) lets the user reach the literature decay-rate range, and the claimed audible consequence was not measured. |
| MB-271 | A mode retuned above 0.49 fs while ringing is either cut in one sample (a click once retunes snap) or, under today's smoothing, chirps down toward DC while it fades | dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/modal_resonator_bank.h:812-819, 906-914, 342-351 | Neither consequence occurs in Membrum: snapCoefficients() has no Membrum caller (only Seraphis continuous_body.h:2860), so the click is hypothetical; with 2 ms smoothing (kSmoothingTimeMs) the chirp toward DC is inaudible. At most a design caution for a future fix. |

None.

## Appendix C — Critic gaps

The critic's gap list, verbatim.

| Kind | Detail |
|------|--------|
| uncovered-area | MIDI note-off truncation has no finding although it was measured and contradicts the spec. specs/138-membrum-phase3-polyphony/spec.md:42, :161 (FR-114) and :361 say note-off MUST be a no-op on the voice. plugins/membrum/src/voice_pool/voice_pool.cpp:283-300 now calls DrumVoice::noteOff (its comment cites 'Phase 8A.5'). The quality lane measured 180 of 185 long pads cut to a median 0.21 of their natural decay by a note-off at 100 ms (Orchestral 54: >4 s to 0.14 s). MB-012 / MB-034 / MB-107 / MB-126 only cover the sample-rate dependence and the stale header comment. Follow-up finder 'noteoff-truncation-fr114'. |
| uncovered-area | Single hits that sit on the bus limiter are unexplained for modal Bell pads. specs/membrum-audit/probes/quality-results.txt lists Glass Bell Garden 46 (FMImpulse/Bell) and 57 (Mallet/Bell), Latin Perc 46, LinnDrum CR-78 40 (FMImpulse/Bell) and World Metal 55 (Mallet/Bell) at -7.00 dBFS, the limiter ceiling. None is Feedback, Friction or String, so MB-017 / MB-019 / MB-035 do not explain them. I confirmed two candidate causes in drum_voice.h that no verified finding carries: the strike probe at :302-304 runs before exciterBank_.setMalletBodySizeHint(size_) at :340, and the probe window is 30 ms (:1327-1329) while FMImpulse runs about 80 ms and Clap 41.6 ms. Follow-up finder 'strike-norm-miss-bell-pads'. |
| unverified-claim | The quality lane labelled the tone-shaper filter rows 'ok' although its own data shows the filter barely acts. specs/membrum-audit/probes/param-audibility.csv row offset=8 (LP, env amount 0): cutoff 20 Hz vs 20 kHz moves the hat by 0.9 dB RMS (centroid still 8.3 kHz) and the snare by 0.6 dB; row offset=10 (filter env amount -1..+1) moves level by 0.07-0.15 dB. The likely cause is MB-042's coefficient glide (tone_shaper.h:83, svf.h:494-526: a one-pole on g, linear in g, so open-to-low takes many time constants on a fresh voice slot), which would make MB-042's '5 ms' consequence much too small. Nobody tested a warmed slot. Follow-up finder 'toneshaper-filter-glide'. |
| unverified-claim | Two measured anomalies have no agreed root cause. (1) MB-178 (PLAUSIBLE): 10 of 60 notes get darker when hit harder, against spec 137 SC-004 (>= 2x centroid upward); one verifier showed the noise layer, which the finding blames, cannot be the cause. (2) MB-176 (CONFIRMED/low): all three verifiers say the 12.2 dB FM Ratio adjacent-step jump cannot come from the stale StrikeNormKey the finding names, so the jump is unexplained.
